Completed: Harden df_pytest_isolation.py: foreign-token deploy-clock fails and the GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS scrub gap
Description: Two independent guard fixes inside `df_pytest_isolation.py`.\n\nFirst, the deploy-clock teardown guard's residual false-fail: `deploy_clock_guard_roots` guards the enclosing MAIN checkout as well as the worktree, and `merge_verify_breadth: full` means many worktrees run the suite concurrently, so a stamp written by worktree A's session makes worktree B's guard ERROR on a token it cannot verify — a false accusation of exactly the class task 4823 exists to fix, which 4823 deliberately left open. Decide whether a foreign token should downgrade to a warning, at minimum make the message say the writer was a concurrent session, and record the ruling (a reasoned won't-fix is an acceptable outcome).\n\nSecond, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` — git's own `-c` propagation channel, with command-line config precedence — is absent from every copy of the redirect-env scrub list, so a poisoned `core.hooksPath` / `safe.directory` / alias survives into every git call in `scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py`, including its `git commit --no-verify`. Add it to all three duplicated copies plus the test's poisoned-env fixture in one coordinated commit; the copies are pinned to each other by a strictly two-directional equality test that must not be weakened.

- Task 4823 HAS landed: df_pytest_isolation.py carries PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN_ENV='DF_PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN', CLOCK_PROVENANCE_SESSION_KEY, clock_stamp_provenance, ClockVerdict{FALSIFIED, EXTERNAL_REDEPLOY}, deploy_clock_change_report, _clock_attribution_line, _falsified_message and the token-stamping _df_deploy_clocks_unwritten. So the #4905 workstream is implementable now.
- GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is absent from all three copies: df_pytest_isolation.py::_GIT_REDIRECT_ENV (around line 2530), scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py::_GIT_REDIRECT_ENV (around line 257, with the "KNOWN GAP" paragraph in scrubbed_git_env), and the `unset` line of scripts/memory-metadata-coverage-census.sh (line 91-93). It is also absent from scripts/tests/test_reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py::POISONED_GIT_ENV.
- Measured on git 2.43.0: `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.hooksPath=/decoy/hooks'" git config --get core.hooksPath` prints /decoy/hooks. A decoy pre-commit hook at that hooksPath RUNS on `git commit` even when `-c` options are also passed. So the census wrapper's `git commit --only` (no --no-verify) runs an injected hook today. That makes a behavioural RED test possible.
- Baseline: `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/test_deploy_clock_isolation.py scripts/tests/test_reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py -q --timeout=300` gives 155 passed.

NEW FINDING THAT SHAPES WORKSTREAM #4905 (measured here, not in the task text). Most suites run under xdist (`-n auto` in escalation/fused-memory/cockpit addopts). Each xdist worker is its own pytest session, so _df_deploy_clocks_unwritten mints a DIFFERENT uuid per worker. Probe: a nested `pytest -n 2 --dist each` tree in which each worker stamps the guarded clock with its own token, with the two writes overlapping. Result: one worker reported "this run's own $DF_PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN" and the OTHER reported "from inside another pytest session". So a self-inflicted falsification under xdist already produces "foreign-token" reports from N-1 of N workers. The most common foreign token today is a SIBLING WORKER of the same run, not a concurrent run. Simply rewording the foreign message to "a CONCURRENT pytest session, not this one" would therefore be false in the common case. The fix is one token per pytest RUN. xdist already gives every worker of a run the same `config.workerinput['testrunuid']` (verified in xdist 3.8.0: workermanage.py mints it once per NodeManager; remote.py hands it to every worker). A nested non-xdist session has no `workerinput`, so it still gets a fresh token.

entry_text: Gotcha (measured 2026-10-04, task 3288): fused-memory/tests/test_harness.py::_make_test_harness builds a REAL shared UsageGate inside ReconciliationHarness.__init__. The cause is that shared/config_models.py::UsageCapConfig.enabled defaults to True, and the factory's ReconciliationConfig never disables it. A test that swaps harness.usage_gate for a mock orphans that real gate. If the test cares about gate lifecycle, shut the real gate down first (or wrap the real shutdown). When cancelling run_loop to exercise its shutdown finally, witness an await INSIDE the main try (e.g. _recover_stale_runs), not check_at_startup: the startup prologue is outside the finally.
target_text: In fused-memory/tests/test_harness.py, the `_make_test_harness(...)` helper builds a harness whose `usage_gate` is a REAL `shared.usage_gate.UsageGate` instance, not None — because the default `FusedMemoryConfig()` has `usage_cap.enabled=True`, and `ReconciliationHarness.__init__` constructs a UsageGate whenever `config.usage_cap.enabled` (harness.py ~516-518). So a test that needs a "no usage gate configured" scenario must EXPLICITLY set `harness.usage_gate = None` after construction; asserting `harness.usage_gate is None` on a fresh `_make_test_harness` harness fails. To simulate specific gate states, overwrite `harness.usage_gate = MagicMock()` and set `.active_account_name` (None = all accounts capped/auth-failed, a name = capacity available).

dark-factory has a SECOND family of AST structural guards, in `shared/tests/`, distinct from the orchestrator/tests "chokepoint guard" family documented in memory 93690770 — reach for this one when the invariant spans PACKAGES rather than living inside orchestrator/src.

THE TRIAD CONVENTION: `<name>_scan.py` (pure scanner) + `<name>_allowlist.py` (dispositioned baseline) + `test_<name>_gate.py` (assertions). Live instances: `silent_fallthrough_*`, `loop_blocking_*`, `config_dir_archival_*`. The scanner takes a `{relpath: source}` MAPPING and does no filesystem I/O, so unit tests feed synthetic modules directly; the gate test supplies real files. A single-file variant (visitor + allowlist + tests in one module) is the right size for a small site population — precedent `fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py`.

THE ENUMERATOR: `shared/tests/silent_fallthrough_scan.py::iter_first_party_files(repo_root)` yields first-party non-test source across 7 scope roots, excluding path components `mem0`/`graphiti`/`tests` and files `test_*.py`/`conftest.py`. It validates repo_root against `shared/src`+`orchestrator/src` sentinels and RAISES rather than yielding a vacuously empty scan, so you must hand it the repo root — narrowing the scope is done by FILTERING its output on a relpath prefix, never by passing a narrower root (`test_loop_blocking_gate.py:955-975` states this explicitly). Reach the root from `shared/tests/` as `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`; `shared/tests/conftest.py` appends REPO_ROOT to sys.path (append, never insert(0), or subprojects resolve as namespace packages).

TWO STANCES WORTH COPYING VERBATIM, both from `loop_blocking_scan.py`'s docstring: "an unresolvable name is silence, never a finding" — a false RED in a merge-gating whole-tree sweep "trains reviewers to bless rows unread and destroys the gate's value"; and a `SyntaxError` in one module contributes nothing and never raises, so a mid-edit file cannot turn the gate red. The dual is also true and less often stated: shipping a guard whose allowlist already contains a live unfixed instance of the defect it guards does the same damage. Always pair with a non-vacuity floor set BELOW the measured file count, whose failure message says the SWEEP is broken, not the tree (`test_loop_blocking_gate.py::TestSweepIsNotVacuous`).

CORRECTION to memory 93690770, which claims "No test in the tree uses ast.NodeVisitor/visit_Call — the convention is plain ast.walk plus hand-rolled iter_child_nodes recursion." That holds for orchestrator/tests only. `fused-memory/tests/test_gather_convention_guard.py` defines `_GatherSiteVisitor(ast.NodeVisitor)` with a parent-map for enclosing-function attribution, and `silent_fallthrough_scan.py` exports `_build_parent_map` / `_compute_qualname` / `_content_hash` / `violation_key` for reuse by sibling scanners. Verified 2026-09-19 at task/3288 base c4b3a2f033. Also note `silent_fallthrough_scan` keys findings on `(relpath, qualname, content_hash)` and NEVER on lineno, which drifts on every unrelated edit above the site.

entry_text: FalkorDB gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, task 4716): `MATCH (a)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(b) RETURN count(*)` with r UNREFERENCED counts distinct connected (a,b) node PAIRS, not edges — multi-edges between one pair collapse (dark_factory: 19,409 vs count(r) = count(DISTINCT r.uuid) = 20,491; the plan is Aggregate <- Conditional Traverse, no edge expansion). Referencing r (`count(r)`, or any `WHERE r.<prop>`) expands the edges. A `_paged_ro_query` census written as a bare-pattern count(*) is therefore LOW, and since completeness is `rows_seen >= expected_rows`, it would pass a read truncated by up to the multi-edge excess. Edge censuses must use count(r) or carry a WHERE on r.
target_text: FalkorDB gotcha (fused-memory graphiti_client): valid-edge counts must dedupe by edge ELEMENT identity (WITH DISTINCT e / count(DISTINCT e)), NOT by property tuple (RETURN DISTINCT e.uuid,e.fact,e.name). FalkorDB does not enforce property uniqueness, and redirect_node_edges copies new.uuid=old.uuid on merge, so an entity can hold multiple distinct RELATES_TO relationships sharing one (uuid,fact,name) tuple. Property-tuple RETURN DISTINCT collapses them and undercounts edge_count (the task-2084 defect: refresh_entity_summary/get_all_valid_edges reported edge_count=1 for entities with 6-9 valid edges). find_duplicate_entity_nodes already uses the correct count(DISTINCT e) pattern.

Merge-lane ratchet, the TESTS-map arm (measured 2026-09-12 at HEAD=e9d1055ed8, task 5097 planning). Complements the earlier entry on cluster TOTALS and complexipy charging; this is the rule that bites a task adding TEST coverage rather than source.

scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::test_file_measures admits an orchestrator/tests file to the baseline's `tests` map iff `imports_lane_module(source)` — i.e. it imports orchestrator.merge_queue, orchestrator.merge_lane, or any other CLUSTER_PATHS module. Consequences for a NEW test file:
- It gains a `tests` entry, which ALONE stales the committed baseline and reddens test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement (byte-identity).
- Its private_reads feed derive_totals, which sums the WHOLE current tests map (baseline 7847 over 229 entries) and _check_totals fails on any rise. _check_tests iterates BASELINE keys only and skips absent paths, so the per-file arm does NOT protect you — the totals arm does the failing. The ratchet's own seeded self-test pins a brand-new file with private_reads:1 as a total:private_reads violation.
- private_reads is deliberately RECEIVER-AGNOSTIC: any `x._foo` (non-dunder) counts, including writes (`worker._host_allocator = a`) and calls (`await worker._dispatch_item(i)`), and chains count per hop. Bare self./cls. receivers are excluded, but `self.worker._x` counts. No helper, fixture or naming trick avoids it.
- patch_targets is a UNION across all tests entries, so reusing a leaf already in the baseline's 83 is free; a brand-new leaf is a violation.

Practical upshot: a test file that imports only orchestrator.verify_runner or orchestrator.config is INVISIBLE to both gates (neither is a cluster path) and can use unrestricted private access and length. orchestrator/tests/test_host_allocator.py is the worked example — absent from the baseline, module-level imports are pytest only. Keep new merge-lane-adjacent tests lane-import-free on purpose when you can.

When you genuinely cannot test the wiring (e.g. a new config knob threaded into merge_queue.py), pyright is the available substitute: orchestrator/pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] includes both `src` and `tests`, so making the new parameter REQUIRED keyword-only turns an unwired call site into a reportCallIssue on every pre-commit and verify. Task 5097 took that route after confirming no test anywhere drives the real SpeculativeMergeWorker._dispatch_item.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha: every bodied trait assoc fn is a DefaultKind::Fn default that conformance/checker.rs::check_phase_resolve_assoc_fns compiles once PER CONFORMER via functions.rs::compile_assoc_function. A trait-static (no-self) default is ALSO compiled once more in compile_builder/traits_phase.rs as the namespaced `Trait::fn` through compile_function. So a diagnostic emitted from either compile path for one wrong default body repeats N (or N+1) times at the same trait span unless deduped. Task 5991 measured 7 reports for 3 bodies and fixed it with fn_return_check.rs::push_once_per_body (match on code plus label span and message). A self-taking default in a trait with no conformers is never compiled at all.
target_text: Measurement trap when probing reify-compiler's `compile_assoc_function` paths (trait-default bodies and structure overrides of assoc fns): a probe that declares a trait with a default body but NO conforming structure never invokes `compile_assoc_function` at all, so it measures CLEAN vacuously. This is what hid task #5371's route (4) — an assoc-fn-body constructor call falling through to the terminal first-arg fallback — until esc-5371-12 caught it. Any probe of an assoc-fn code path must include a structure that ACTUALLY CONFORMS to the trait, or the measurement proves nothing. Same caution applies to any "measured clean" claim about conformance-reached code.

Fact, measured 2026-10-01: merge-verify peak memory is NOT systematically recorded anywhere.
- The orchestrator records nothing.
- The df-verify-*.scope units are `--collect`ed at exit, so memory.peak vanishes with them.
- The only after-the-fact source is the user-journal line systemd 255 writes at scope exit ("<scope>: Consumed … CPU time, X memory peak, Y memory swap peak"). It includes the peak for only SOME scopes: 22 of 188 DF scopes and 1 of 6 reify scopes since 2026-09-30 21:00 BST. It was missing even for some of the largest legs. Treat it as a sample, not a record.

Values on leo-laptop:
- DF full-gate test leg: 13.3–14.3 GiB, against the 24G cap.
- Other DF legs: about 4.3–4.7 GiB and about 0.7 GiB.
- reify: one record of 32.0 GiB, exactly its MemoryMax. That verify passed in its normal 15.8 min, and there were no OOM kills in the kernel log. Most likely cargo page cache filling the cgroup to the limit and being reclaimed, so it says reify runs pressed against its cap, not what its anonymous memory needs.

To get real peaks, read memory.peak and memory.stat before the scope exits (suggested for task 6106 / task 5415).
target_text:
GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-11, task 5415): you CANNOT read a verify scope's cgroup memory.peak after the gate finishes, and nice is NOT a reliable verify-role discriminator. Both bite anyone instrumenting verify resource use.

(1) EPHEMERALITY. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_run_cmd spawns the scope as `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect --unit=df-verify-<slug>-<hash>-<uuid>`. `--collect` garbage-collects the unit the instant its last process exits, so the cgroup directory AND the unit's systemd MemoryPeak property are both GONE at gate end — a post-hoc read fails, it is not merely racy. Observed directly: three live df-verify scopes at one poll, two at the next. Because memory.peak is monotonic within a cgroup's lifetime, the correct technique is to POLL, carry per-scope state across ticks, and flush a terminal record using the LAST observation when a scope disappears. Live scopes are at /sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-<uid>.slice/user@<uid>.service/app.slice/df-verify-*.scope; `systemctl --user show <scope> -p MemoryPeak` also works while alive (systemd 255).

(2) ROLE ATTRIBUTION. The ROLE_BY_NICE map in scripts/cgroup-stall-ratio.py (5 merge / 15 task / 19 background) does NOT cover every leg: a live lint leg was observed at nice=0, because its outer wrapper carries no nice prefix (the `nice -n 15` is inner). The reliable key is the scope root process's cwd BASENAME from /proc/<pid>/cwd — `_merge-verify` (or DF's hash-suffixed `_merge-<hex>`) is the merge gate, `_lane-NN` is a task lane. Key on the BASENAME, not a `.worktrees/` path prefix: the warm-lane pool lives at /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/worktrees/, outside the project tree.

(3) ONE GATE IS SEVERAL SCOPES. Scopes are per-_run_cmd leg, so test / lint / type each get their own scope. A per-gate figure must group legs — join to the project's `merge_verify` events in runs.db on the [timestamp - duration_ms, timestamp] window.

(4) NO-SCOPE PROJECTS. dark_factory has verify_use_cgroup_scope off (default False; task 5206 would enable it), so DF verify shares orchestrator-dark-factory.service's cgroup with ~60 agent CLIs and that cgroup's memory.peak is NOT the verify's peak. Fall back to the merge process group (verify spawns start_new_session=True, so pgid == pid) and sum PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup — PSS, not RSS: forked xdist workers share a large copy-on-write image, so an RSS sum grossly overstates, while cgroup memory.peak charges a shared page once.

Real magnitudes for calibration, measured on the 125 GB workstation: reify merge-verify leg peak 15.87 GB, a concurrent reify task lane 36.65 GB.

entry_text: To force the except arm around `asyncio.create_task(self._some_coro(args))` in an orchestrator test (e.g. TaskWorkflow._route_review_suggestions_to_curator's scheduling-failure → SuggestionDisposition.ERROR path), replace the coroutine method with a SYNCHRONOUS `MagicMock(side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`, not `patch.object(wf, '_some_coro', side_effect=...)`: patch.object auto-builds an AsyncMock for an async target, and an AsyncMock raises its side_effect only when AWAITED, so create_task schedules it, the try never sees the error, and the router reports CURATOR. Also avoid the older trick of returning a non-coroutine, which depends on asyncio's exact TypeError (task 3415 amendment).
target_text: When mocking `asyncio.create_task` in orchestrator tests, use `patch('asyncio.create_task', side_effect=lambda coro, *, name=None: (coro.close(), mock_task)[1])` (or the explicit `def _create_task(coro, *, name=None): coro.close(); return mock_task` form). NEVER use `patch('asyncio.create_task', return_value=mock_task)` — that silently discards the coroutine argument, which CPython's GC later flags as `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '<name>' was never awaited` and `sys.unraisablehook` converts to `PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning` attributed to a different test running when GC fires (non-deterministic xdist failures). Canonical pattern: `orchestrator/tests/test_harness_watcher_supervisor.py:140-142`. The `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` filterwarnings on lines 72-73 ("error:coroutine .* was never awaited:RuntimeWarning" and "error:Exception ignored.*coroutine object:pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning") turn the warning into a test failure wherever it fires inline.

entry_text: fused-memory API quirks found 2026-09-30. get_task returns `id` as an int, while get_tasks pages return string ids, so compare with str(). update_memory and delete_memory require a `store` argument ('mem0'). In-place update_memory content amendment is refused unless agent_id starts with 'recon-stage-' or 'curator-' (Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized); to fix a wrong memory you wrote, add_memory a corrected copy, verify it, then delete_memory(store='mem0') the old one. submit_task(planning_mode=True) returns {task_id, status:'deferred'} synchronously; commit_planning(task_ids='N') then flips it to pending.
target_text: fused-memory submit_task with planning_mode=True is synchronous and curator-bypassing: returns {task_id, status: "deferred", planning_mode: True} immediately with the real task_id assigned (no tkt_<id>, no resolve_ticket poll needed). Use this for /prd decompose batches: file all cluster tasks in parallel calls, get IDs back synchronously, wire add_dependency edges, then bulk set_task_status with comma-separated IDs to flip the batch deferred → pending in one call. Different from non-planning-mode flow which returns a ticket and requires resolve_ticket. Observed working 2026-05-13 in the topology-selectors decomposition.

target_text: fused-memory planning_mode task gotcha (observed 2026-06-24): a task filed via submit_task(planning_mode=True) lands as `deferred` so the scheduler can't claim it before deps/siblings are wired — BUT a running orchestrator transiently CLAIMED such a deferred task (#4802) anyway (it showed oldStatus="in-progress" when later flipped, and a stale empty task/<id> branch at main HEAD was created with no worktree and no commits). The claim REPLACED the task's metadata blob wholesale (not a merge): the /prd-filed fields (consumer_ref, user_observable_signal, grammar_confirmed, modules, files) were wiped, leaving only the reconciler's memory_hints + branch_base_sha. Mitigation: after flipping a planning_mode task to pending, re-check get_task and restore the metadata via update_task(metadata_mode="merge") if it was clobbered (merge preserves the reconciler's memory_hints/branch_base_sha). The empty task/<id> branch is harmless (next dispatch re-creates it). Losing metadata.files defaults to []=BRE-acquires-footprint, the safe under-declaration direction.

entry_text: dark-factory fused-memory GOTCHA (measured, task 6137 planning): never put best-effort post-write work (for example an LLM judge) inline in MemoryService._execute_graphiti_write or in a durable-queue callback. DurableWriteQueue._process_item runs _execute_write under asyncio.wait_for(write_timeout), so a slow step can time out a write that has ALREADY landed and RETRY it, minting a duplicate episode. A callback that raises also retries the item, and it holds the queue semaphore while it runs. Use a tracked background task (the task_interceptor._background_tasks idiom) submitted after the identity-lock block. Also note: result.edges from add_episode is stale after the lock, because _dedup_episode_edges deletes duplicates inside it. Re-read survivors from the graph if they matter.
target_text: fused-memory concurrency discovery (verified 2026-07-06): the DurableWriteQueue's per-group_id `_group_locks` (durable_queue.py:136) serialize ONLY `_claim_next` (the claim/UPDATE-to-in_flight at :289-314), NOT `_process_item` which runs the actual `_execute_write`/add_episode (:316-335). So with workers_per_group>1, two workers each claim a different item for the same group and then run add_episode CONCURRENTLY — the queue lock does NOT serialize execution. config.yaml pins workers_per_group=1 (code default is 3), so execution is serialized today only by having one worker. Any write-time identity guarantee that must survive raising workers_per_group needs its OWN per-group lock held across add_episode+reconcile (this is why W6-α adds a separate GraphitiBackend identity lock rather than reusing the queue lock).

entry_text: Task 'Unblock whole-blob metadata repair on done tasks: update_task's done_provenance floor makes metadata_mode='replace' structurally unusable' completed. Landed in commit 987ad2cbf4860c3ae78b17cdd4f0db9aed3d6a34.
target_text:
[CONTRADICTED 2026-08-23 — READ THIS FIRST. The central claim below ("replace is structurally UNUSABLE on any done/merged task", because the write-authority floor rejects any payload containing done_provenance) DOES NOT HOLD UNIVERSALLY, and relying on it can destroy data. Mem0 6668c214-992f-4008-bede-5ffb24584502 records a first-hand probe on 2026-08-20 against task 3784 (status=done): update_task(metadata_mode='replace') was NOT refused — it returned updated=True and left metadata == {'a': 1}, destroying every other key, unrecoverably (journal.db empty; the sqlite WAL retained text columns but not the metadata BLOB). So the floor is NOT a reliable backstop on the replace path. TREAT metadata_mode='replace' AS AN UNGUARDED WHOLE-BLOB OVERWRITE: never probe it against a real task, and back the blob up before any key-retirement attempt. See also mem0 e1423e03 (2026-08-12), which frames the accurate rule as presence-keyed on done_provenance appearing in the INCOMING payload — additive writes pass, subtractive ones do not. The historical analysis below is retained as the record of what was believed on 2026-08-06.]

Gotcha (task 3697, 2026-08-06): metadata_mode='replace' is structurally UNUSABLE on any done/merged task, despite update_task's docstring calling it "the sanctioned repair path". The backend write-authority floor (sqlite_task_backend.py, ~line 2574-2591) rejects any metadata payload containing done_provenance — presence-only, no value-unchanged carve-out, evaluated BEFORE metadata_mode is resolved — and every done/merged task carries that key. This refines the older 2026-05-06 note advising migration scripts to "defensively strip done_provenance": that advice predates the three metadata modes (added 2026-06-18) and is UNSAFE under replace, where stripping the key DELETES it and only set_task_status can ever re-add it. Net effect: a whole-blob repair of a done task's metadata has no sanctioned path — merge/additive cannot delete a key (shallow {**old, **new}, no deletion sentinel) and there is no task-level metadata_delete_keys (that exists only for memories). Compounding trap: this rejection is returned as an ordinary result dict {'success': False, 'error': 'done_provenance_via_update_task'} inside a JSON-RPC SUCCESS envelope, so a client that only checks the envelope reads a refused write as an accepted one.

Description: When a task exhausts max_review_cycles with blocking issues remaining, the review loop escalates the blocking issues and returns ESCALATED without routing the accompanying `suggestion`-severity findings to ANY sink. Completed: Close the jq-vs-Rust ISO-8601 divergence in reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq (numeric TZ offset / no-TZ forms yield a quiet done_at=null)
Description: Filed from task 7236 (review point 2, reviewer_comprehensive robustness) as OUT-OF-SCOPE follow-up work. Task 7236's frozen plan design-decision #4 deliberately PINNED this divergence as accepted rather than closing it; this ticket tracks closing it, so the accepted divergence is tracked rather than only narrated.

OBSERVED (measured on task/7236, guarded green by Check 5f-f of tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh): the two loaders of the same fused-memory updatedAt field disagree on timestamp SHAPE.

- scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq uses jq's fromdateiso8601, which accepts ONLY "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" (after the filter strips a trailing .NNN millisecond suffix).
- crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs parse_iso8601_to_epoch has a split_tz arm (fused_memory_client.rs:417) accepting "Z", "+HH:MM", "-HH:MM", AND a bare no-TZ form (treated as UTC), with fractional seconds stripped in any of those positions. Its own unit tests pin all four (iso8601_plus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_minus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_no_tz_treated_as_utc).

So "2026-05-01T12:00:00+00:00" (and "2026-05-01T12:00:00", and "2026-05-01T12:00:00.000+01:00") parse to an epoch in the Rust loader and to null in the jq sidecar.

CONSEQUENCE, and why it is worth tracking rather than leaving narrated. Task 7236 made the jq conversion TOTAL (try ... catch null), which correctly stopped ONE such row from aborting the whole snapshot and taking the wrapper's exit-125 arm. But for these shapes the resulting done_at=null reproduces the ORIGINAL task-3731 silent-skip failure mode: P1's 14-day grace comparison skips a task with no done_at entirely, and the only signal is a stderr WARNING from scripts/reify-audit-predone-wrapper.sh ("done tasks with no done_at (P1 will skip them): ...") on a systemd hook path nobody is likely reading. Unreachable TODAY -- fused-memory's sqlite_task_backend.py updatedAt writer only emits ...Z -- but the catch null makes the failure permanently QUIET, which removes the pressure that would surface it if that writer ever changes.

SUGGESTED FIX (from the review): normalise the offset in the jq filter before fromdateiso8601 so it matches parse_iso8601_to_epoch's split_tz arm -- either splitting the [+-]HH:MM offset and adjusting the epoch (full parity, matching Rust's arithmetic), or at minimum handling the bare no-TZ form. A half-fix that normalises only +00:00/-00:00 to Z is worse than the documented divergence, because it makes zero offsets work while nonzero ones stay silently null.

HAZARD to respect, measured during 7236 and the reason this is not a one-liner: jq's `capture`/`match` produce EMPTY on no-match, and an empty result inside the filter's `map({...})` object construction makes the WHOLE OBJECT VANISH -- silently DROPPING the row from the snapshot. That is the exact data-loss trap that made `fromdateiso8601?` the wrong fix in 7236. Any widened parser must stay TOTAL (every input yields a value, never empty), and must keep the row present.

FILES
- scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq (the filter and its done_at DERIVATION header, which currently documents the divergence at item 3)
- tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh (Check 5f-f currently ASSERTS the divergence -- fixture row d4, "2026-05-01T12:00:00+00:00" -> done_at null. Closing the divergence must flip that assertion and its comment in the SAME diff, or the suite reds.)
- crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs (reference only -- parse_iso8601_to_epoch/split_tz is the contract to match; no change expected there)

Registration note: scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq is registered SURGICALLY via a scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt row (added by 7236), which selects tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh at task scope. Do NOT add it to scripts/…[truncated, 9259 chars total]

Description: PRD: docs/prds/v0_6/solution-set-completeness.md §3.1. Ship the solution-set completeness axis as an ADDITIVE sibling carrier in reify-ir, alongside (not inside) the landed F-result types.

WHY. SolveResult::Solved.unique is a bool, and a bool cannot distinguish five genuinely different states: proved exactly one, proved two, found one and proved nothing, found two, proved none exist. Every solver-honesty defect in this area is that type error surfacing somewhere.

DELIVER.
1. enum Completeness = Exhaustive | Partial{reason: PartialReason} | Refuted{narrowing: ConstraintNodeId}.
2. enum PartialReason = BoxBudgetExhausted | DimensionAboveEnvelope{dims} | DomainUnbounded{param} | NotIntervalRepresentable{constraint} | InnerSolveUnproven | ProbeOnly | NotAttempted.
3. SolutionSet{solutions, completeness}; an additive `completeness` field on RankedSolveResult::Ranked.
4. The C1 derived-`unique` helper: unique == (completeness == Exhaustive && solutions.len() == 1). No producer may write `unique` from any other reasoning.
5. A default `Partial{NotAttempted}` lift so every existing producer keeps behaving exactly as today until it opts in.

INVARIANTS (PRD §3.2): C1 unique is derived never asserted; C2 ProvenOptimal requires Exhaustive; C3 Refuted is a proof while Partial-with-empty-set is not, and the two must never render alike; C4 a Partial verdict may never report how many solutions exist.

Completed: Docs-truth capstone: schedule a recurring deterministic PPRDSTATUS/doc-drift sweep that escalates to L2 to book a human adjudication sitting
Description: Filed from escalation esc-6232-5. Leo's explicit instruction, 2026-08-19: "Make sure that once the detector is live, the things that are detected deterministically get some attention. Something like detection itself raises to L2, and/or have a capstone task deterministically escalate to L2 to tell me to run a session to resolve the things that have been found by the detector."

This is the RECURRING-ATTENTION half. The one-shot wiring (a non-empty PPRDSTATUS finding set raising to L2) is a hard done-criterion of the detector task itself, deliberately NOT split out, because splitting it is precisely how PDOCCOVER ended up with a landed detector (#5478, done) and a gate that is still pending (#5480) — a detector finding things and gating nothing. This task is the different, additional mechanism: a periodic sweep whose output is a booked human sitting, so findings do not merely accumulate in a log.

WHY A SITTING RATHER THAN AUTO-FILED TASKS. Leo's ruling (2026-08-19): adjudicating doc-drift findings is workflow-shaped, not task-shaped. Each finding needs a per-doc judgement that an autonomous agent should not make unsupervised — genuinely-still-active PRD vs completed plan needing a SHIPPED header vs capability manifest that must not be touched vs dated snapshot that must NOT be retroactively edited (the #6232 principle: "retroactively editing a historical snapshot destroys its value as a record"). An agent mass-stamping SHIPPED across live PRDs would be a worse outcome than the drift it fixes. Note also that the orchestrator contributes nothing here: scripts/verify.sh:1161 routes *.md to `: # no heavy checks`, so a docs-only task produces an empty plan and exits 0 — there is no gate for a docs task to pass.

SCOPE TO DECIDE FIRST (this is part of the deliverable, argue it explicitly):
  1. Cadence. Doc drift accrues on the timescale of leaves landing, not commits. Weekly or fortnightly is likely right; daily will produce an ignored alert. Justify the choice.
  2. Trigger shape. Options: (a) pure timer; (b) event-driven — sweep when a PRD's last non-terminal leaf goes terminal, which is the exact moment a PRD becomes freezable and is cheap to detect from the reconciliation path; (c) both. (b) is the more precise instrument and is worth costing before defaulting to (a).
  3. Silence discipline. The sweep must NOT escalate when the finding set is empty, and must not re-escalate the same unchanged finding set every period — otherwise it trains the L2 queue to ignore it. Some fingerprint/dedupe over the finding set is required (the escalation MCP already supports dedupe_fingerprint).
  4. What the escalation says. It should carry the finding COUNT and the doc list, and name the sitting to run, so the L2 consumer can triage without re-deriving anything.

Decide deliberately whether the L2 raise is made from the reify side via the escalation MCP endpoint (there is precedent for driving it over curl) or wired dark-factory-side, and record the choice.

entry_text: GOTCHA (fused-memory, verified on graphiti_core 0.28.2, 2026-09-30, task 4620): Graphiti EpisodicNode.created_at is NOT the time the episode becomes readable. Graphiti.add_episode takes `now = utc_now()` at the START of the call, and that becomes created_at. The node is persisted only at the END (`_process_episode_data` -> `add_nodes_and_edges_bulk`), after the LLM node/edge/attribute extraction, which can take up to the queue's write_timeout_seconds. So any `created_at > cursor` freshness filter over episodes can permanently miss an episode whose write straddles the cursor instant. mem0 differs: it stamps created_at right before its vector insert, so its lag is about zero.
target_text: FACT (dark_factory, fused-memory, verified 2026-08-04): raw Graphiti EPISODE PROSE has essentially one production consumer — MemoryConsolidator.assemble_payload (reconciliation/stages/memory_consolidator.py:684), which calls get_episodes(last_n=episode_limit) (125 sonnet / 500 opus, harness.py:326 and config/schema.py:1270-1272) and then filters by watermark to NEW episodes only. So a stale or premature-narration episode is in a stage payload for exactly ONE cycle before falling permanently out of scope. Nothing in orchestrator/, escalation/, shared/ or dashboard/ reads Graphiti episodes at all (a grep finds only unrelated uses of the word "episode" for downtime/merge episodes). The remaining consumers are ad-hoc get_episodes calls by Stage 1/2/3 agents and by interactive sessions. This bounds the blast radius of any episode-content defect and is why esc-3391-1 was ruled accepted-by-design rather than tool-worthy.

Description: Out-of-scope follow-up discovered while planning task 4137 (header count vs. focus-narrowed render array). Not filed as an escalation — it is a self-contained perf item with no blocker.

OBSERVED at base bd93e98921 by reading the source (no profiling run):

`TaskGraph` in dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx memoizes its expensive layout work with `uM_T(() => { computeTiers(tasks); partitionComponents(tasks); components.map(c => orderRows(c, tiers)) }, [tasks])`, and its highlight neighborhood with `uM_T(..., [selectedId, tasks])`.

Both dep arrays are keyed on the `tasks` REFERENCE. `tasks` originates in `TasksTab`'s `projects.map(p => ...)` callback, which computes `const projTasks = allTasks.filter(t => t.project === p.id)` and `const filtered = projTasks.filter(...)` fresh on every render — a new array instance every time. TasksTab re-renders once per second from the app-wide clock tick in app.jsx (`setInterval(() => setNow(...), 1000)`, unrelated to data polling). So these memos miss 100% of the time and the full ordering-phase layout (barycenter/transpose passes plus countCrossings inside `orderRows`, graph_layout.js) re-runs for every mounted project group every second. `PrdBox` mounts one `TaskGraph` per PRD box, multiplying this in the grouped view.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY TASK 4137: 4137 deletes two OTHER memos with the same defect (`ProjectTaskGraph`/`ProjectPrdGroups`'s `graphTasks`), but only because they were in the way of the header-count fix. It does not touch `TaskGraph`, whose memos are the expensive ones. The behaviour is identical before and after 4137.

THE FIX IDIOM ALREADY EXISTS IN THE SAME FILE: `ProjectPrdGroups` documents this exact hazard and works around it by keying its `groups`/`neighborhood`/`fullMembersByPrd` memos on the content-signature strings `filteredSig`/`allSig` rather than on the arrays. Apply the same treatment to `TaskGraph`'s two memos (a signature covering id/status/deps is sufficient for `computeTiers`/`partitionComponents`/`orderRows`/`computeNeighborhood`, which read nothing else) — or, more cheaply, memoize `projTasks`/`filtered` themselves further up so a stable reference reaches every consumer.

SUGGESTED SCOPE: dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx (+ dashboard/tests/test_tab_tasks_*.py for a structural assertion that the layout memo is signature-keyed). Note that any edit to a /static/redux asset requires bumping the shared `?v=NN` cache-buster in index.html — see dashboard/tests/_cache_buster_helpers.py::cache_buster_violation.

CAVEAT: the cost is asserted from reading the code, not measured. Confirm with a profile before investing in a large refactor; if the measured cost is negligible, closing this as won't-fix (and deleting the misleading memo comments, which claim a benefit they do not deliver) is a legitimate outcome.

entry_text: Trait-member conformance in reify is STRICT for Vector slots: type_compat.rs::implicitly_converts_to has no Vector→Vector rule beyond identity, so a conformer declaring `param axis : Vector3<Length>` against a trait requiring `Vector3<Dimensionless>` fails with DiagnosticCode::TypeMismatchForTraitMember. The dimensionless TOLERANCE in reify-core ty.rs applies only to ctor ARGUMENTS (a dimensionless vec3 passed to a Vector3<Length> param), not to trait-member declarations. So retyping a stdlib trait's vector member is a breaking change for every conformer that declares the old type, and those fixtures must migrate in the same commit.
target_text: In the Reify compiler, `type_compatible(Vector3<Length>, Vector3<dimensionless>)` is FALSE: `implicitly_converts_to` (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs) has Vector<->Tensor{rank:1} arms but NO Vector<->Vector arm coercing differing quantity slots. Per the ty.rs "Point/Vector quantity-slot convention" the quantity slot is intentionally loose, so arg-conformance for Type::Vector params must be SHAPE-based (accept any Type::Vector/Tensor{rank:1}, reject non-vectors) rather than using type_compatible — otherwise a dimensionless `vec3(0,0,1)` arg is wrongly rejected for a Vector3<Length> param.

entry_text: Rust gotcha in reify (task #6999): an io::Error built with io::Error::other(bincode_err), e.g. by CacheEntryHeader::read_from in crates/reify-eval/src/persistent_cache.rs, always has kind() == ErrorKind::Other. Its real UnexpectedEof is nested inside the boxed bincode::ErrorKind::Io, so a `matches!(e.kind(), UnexpectedEof | InvalidData)` guard on that error can never match. To classify it, downcast via e.get_ref().and_then(|s| s.downcast_ref::<bincode::ErrorKind>()) instead of calling kind().
target_text: In reify, `io::Error::other(e)` is `io::Error::new(ErrorKind::Other, e)`, so it FLATTENS the wrapped error's kind: any downstream `matches!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof | ErrorKind::InvalidData)` guard on such an error is dead code, because kind() is always Other and the real kind is nested inside the boxed source. This bit `read_entry` in crates/reify-eval/src/persistent_cache.rs, where `CacheEntryHeader::read_from` maps bincode errors via `io::Error::other` and read_entry's header arm guards on kind() — so a `.bin` truncated inside its 92-byte header returns Err instead of the documented Ok(None) miss (found by task #2980, filed as esc-2980-5). When classifying an error that crossed an `io::Error::other` boundary, inspect `e.get_ref()` and downcast, or catch Err unconditionally as the sibling body-decode arm does.

entry_text: To name a dimension in a Reify diagnostic, use reify-core's DimensionVector::diagnostic_dimension_label() (canonical name, else Display exponents; DIMENSIONLESS -> "dimensionless") or DimensionVector::diagnostic_scalar_label() ("{Name|dimensionless|dimensioned} Scalar", for an ArgRejection `got` slot). Do not hand-roll another canonical_name()-branching helper. The two forms differ on purpose, and tests in dimension.rs pin both (task 6163).
target_text: In reify-eval, `reify_ir::Value::dimension()` called on a `Value::Transform` falls into that method's catch-all arm and reports DIMENSIONLESS for EVERY transform — it does NOT inspect the translation. To get a pose's real translation dimension you must read the `Transform.translation` field (a `Value::Vector`, whose `dimension()` correctly derives from item 0). Sibling trap: `reify_core::DimensionVector::canonical_name()` (crates/reify-core/src/dimension.rs:413) deliberately excludes DIMENSIONLESS from its named-singleton table and returns `None` for it, so any user-facing dimension label must check `is_dimensionless()` BEFORE consulting `canonical_name()`. Both traps silently defeat dimension-mismatch diagnostics (found while fixing task 6099's silently-dropped dimensionless sub-pose).

entry_text: Task 7303 (2026-10-01): reify-eval `decide_morph_or_remesh` (morph_producer.rs) now treats `Some(empty BoundaryAssociation)` exactly like `None` — silent Remesh, no diagnostic, no counter (counters live in reify-mesh-morph, which normal-depends on reify-eval, so reify-eval cannot call them). MEASURED with the guard in place: `cargo test -p reify-eval --test morph_arm_e2e` (real OCCT + gmsh, fixtures/morph_box.ri) still passes all 5 tests incl. `morphed == 1`, so the real attributed gmsh producer yields a NON-EMPTY association on that box fixture. The Some(empty) case is code-reachable (kernel_real.rs:798 always wraps in Some; mesh_boundary.rs:750 skips gmsh entities whose anchor is outside match_tolerance) but has NOT been observed on any real geometry. Corollary: before the guard, that e2e's `morphed == 1` could not tell a vacuous no-op "morph" of an empty association from a real one; with the guard, a pass proves the association was non-empty.
target_text: Verified completion of task 'decide_morph_or_remesh should require a NON-EMPTY boundary association, not merely Some' against the codebase: The task is done. It landed as task 7303. In crates/reify-eval/src/morph_producer.rs, decide_morph_or_remesh now admits the morph arm only when `source.source_mesh.boundary.as_ref().filter(|b| !b.is_empty())` is Some. A Some(empty) association therefore returns MorphDecision::Remesh, the same as None. try_morph is no longer called in that case, so record_morphed() cannot fire for a no-op morph. Commits, all on the file's history: e0cf88721d5f (RED test `decide_source_with_empty_boundary_remeshes`, plus the source_with_boundary fixture now carrying a non-empty association), 33240a9b23b2 (GREEN guard), and 2c45072a16cb (2026-10-02, doc amendment). The test body in the current file was not read; the claim rests on the RED commit message and the guard code. Design choices from the fix commit: the Remesh is silent, with no new diagnostic or counter bucket, because reify-mesh-morph depends on reify-eval and a bucket would need a new MorphOutcome variant and a DiagnosticSnapshot field. rekey_boundary_association's Some(empty) contract is untouched. Reachability: the fix commit reports Some(empty) is possible from the producer API by code read only. kernel_real.rs:798 always wraps the result in Some, mesh_boundary.rs:750-751 skips entities whose anchors are out of tolerance, and engine_build.rs:9396 falls back to None only when the anchor list is empty. Whether a real .ri geometry hits this is unmeasured.

entry_text: When applying a long list of irreversible fused-memory reassign_edge calls (e.g. graph-task-conflation-census REPAIRs), a uuid retyped into the MCP call can be silently corrupted (task 6582 session 1 sent 14525eaf-9078-432f-... for ...-4332-... and hit EdgeNotFoundError, esc-6582-5). The reliable pattern: a small /tmp helper that keeps a done-log. Before each call it byte-compares the intended edge_uuid/which_end/new_endpoint_uuid with the next apply-set row. After each call it checks status=reassigned, moved=true, and old_endpoint_uuid == census from_node_uuid, then appends the row to the log. One Bash call per row (record previous + check next) keeps the overhead to 2 turns per edge.
target_text: When applying a batch of fused-memory reassign_edge calls by hand from a precomputed list (reify task 6582's Task-N conflation repairs), every uuid is retyped into each MCP call, and a one-group transcription typo happened in practice (sent 14525eaf-9078-432f-… for 14525eaf-9078-4332-…). A typo in edge_uuid or new_endpoint_uuid fails safe: EdgeNotFoundError or NodeNotFoundError is raised at the topology/node read, before any write. A swapped which_end, however, moves the WRONG end with moved=true. So after every call, check that the result's old_endpoint_uuid equals the row's from_node_uuid. Use `graph-task-conflation-census.py check-repairs` as the read-back and resumption oracle: it reads applied/pending per row, so an applied row is never re-sent.

Procedure that worked, 2026-10-02: landing a docs-only PRD commit into a busy merge lane via a solo merge carrier (task 6180).

Situation: two verifies were in flight and 3995 and 4237 were real queued entries, as confirmed by per-id marker search.

Steps:
1. Commit in a scratch worktree, so the main checkout is never dirtied. Pre-commit ran clean.
2. File the carrier with submit_task(planning_mode=True), carrying a temporary dependency on a pending task (3136) so the scheduler cannot dispatch it while pending.
3. Run `git worktree move` to .worktrees/<id> and `checkout -b task/<id>`, keeping the original branch as a backup ref.
4. Walk the status pending → in-progress (claimant_run_id interactive-carrier-<id>) → merge-deferred in back-to-back calls. Interactive in-progress claims get their worktree reaped within ~20 min.
5. Remove the temporary dependency.
6. merge_request(wait_secs=100, verified_green=False).

Result:
- It entered at position 1 (the docs-only footprint was disjoint) and went straight to verifying.
- It landed with a normal 'Merge task/6180 into main' marker, b3b4415805.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha: every bodied trait assoc fn is a DefaultKind::Fn default that conformance/checker.rs::check_phase_resolve_assoc_fns compiles once PER CONFORMER via functions.rs::compile_assoc_function. A trait-static (no-self) default is ALSO compiled once more in compile_builder/traits_phase.rs as the namespaced `Trait::fn` through compile_function. So a diagnostic emitted from either compile path for one wrong default body repeats N (or N+1) times at the same trait span unless deduped. Task 5991 measured 7 reports for 3 bodies and fixed it with fn_return_check.rs::push_once_per_body (match on code plus label span and message). A self-taking default in a trait with no conformers is never compiled at all.

Commit 79115ccc35f9 added the module crates/reify-compiler/src/fn_return_check.rs, wired from functions.rs (compile_function) and lib.rs. reconcile_fn_return compares compiled.body.result_expr.result_type with compiled.return_type, which is the declared type or the defaulted Real. A contradiction is reported as DiagnosticCode::FnReturnTypeUnannotated. For explicit Int or Scalar annotations a mismatch diagnostic is also reported. Severity is FN_RETURN_RECONCILE_SEVERITY = Warning, so the check runs in warn mode first; flipping it to Error is #7007. Commit a6d68f8e6b2b made compile_assoc_function call reconcile_fn_return with FnOwner::Conformer. Bodies that read `self` are skipped until #8118. Commit e0af13493976 added push_once_per_body to dedupe reports and a fixture, fn_return_reconciliation_tests.rs. require_bodyless_return_annotation covers bodyless trait assoc fns, so bodyless trait fns are told to annotate. Bare generic bodies (TypeParam, ScalarParam, Projection) are skipped, which is the #7008 follow-up. Fork (a) was chosen and fork (b) was deferred. entry_text: GOTCHA (task 3096): close_only only means "no task-status change". Harness._on_escalation_resolved calls event.set() on _escalation_events[task_id] for EVERY resolution, close_only and dismiss=True included, before it dispatches the action, so any closure wakes a live workflow waiting on that task id. Also, queue.submit_resolved leaves resolution_action None, and the legacy D10 mapping reads a resolved record as 'resume' (re-pend). Stamp esc.resolution_action='close_only' before submit_resolved when you mean a no-effect closure. To suppress the wake as well, you need an explicit early return at the top of the callback, like the eval-lane guard keyed on shared.eval_lane.eval_lane_provenance.
target_text: GOTCHA — `resolve_issue(action='close_only')` is documented as "task-status effect: unchanged", but that is NOT reliable when the escalation you are closing is the SOLE remaining open escalation holding a task. On 2026-08-05, closing esc-3404-5 with close_only CASCADED its member esc-3404-4 shut (`resolved_by: l2-cascade:esc-3404-5`) and RELEASED task 3404 from `blocked` to `pending`. That was actively dangerous: 3404's plan.json read 13/13 done, so a dispatch would have run straight to VERIFY/REVIEW/merge and landed a branch that was still missing recovered work. ALWAYS re-read the task's status immediately after resolving an escalation, especially when the task's plan reads complete. To hold a task afterwards, prefer `deferred` over `blocked`: `blocked` with no open escalation is the "stranded blocked" state that unblock_auto and the stranded-blocked reconciler try to heal, whereas `deferred` is a quiet park that nothing auto-dispatches.

Why task 5097 (verify_host_policy prefer_remote) stalled for 15 days, measured 2026-09-30:
- Its code was COMPLETE on branch task/5097 from 2026-09-15, but it was never reviewed or verified.
- On its third dispatch the implementer finished all 8 steps (it hit max_turns, but the work was committed). The steward resolved esc-5097-10/11/12 and fixed 16 red stub tests itself.
- The task was then requeued with reason scope_grant_lock_conflict and never re-dispatched.
- It needs 11 files locked all-or-nothing. Over 376h, all 11 were simultaneously free only ~1.2% of the time: config.py held 88%, merge_queue.py 72%.

target_text:
Task 4521 has been silently parked since 2026-08-20 on a plan-blast-radius lock conflict, and the shape of this failure is worth recognising generally. Measured from data/orchestrator/runs.db on 2026-08-25: task 4521 has exactly EIGHT events in its whole life, all on 2026-08-20, ending `task_completed {"outcome":"requeued","reason":"plan_blast_radius_lock_conflict","block_phase":"plan"}`. Nothing since.

THE MECHANISM. A task with no metadata.files is dispatched holding ONE synthetic fallback lock named `task-<id>`. Its architect then widens scope to the real file set (here 15 files). workflow.py's _plan() re-derives modules from plan["files"], fails _reconcile_scope_locks, and routes to _requeue_on_lock_conflict. From then on every scheduler tick derives the real module set and calls LockTable.try_acquire, which is ALL-OR-NOTHING at max_per_module=1 — so one held file blocks the whole task. Six of 4521's fifteen are held by live tasks (3084 holds both memory_consolidator.py and test_stage1.py; also 3127, 3672, 4012).

WHY IT IS SILENT, which is the part that makes it hard to notice. acquire_next's scored loop calls try_acquire for every candidate, but skip accounting (_skip_count) is bumped only for the single top-scored candidate. A medium-priority task among ~683 zero-dependency pending tasks is essentially never top-scored, so it accrues ZERO skips, never parks, and never appears in skip_counts/parks/pin_queue. The starvation watchdog cannot fire either: idle_secs is 259200s (72h) and its anchor _streak_starvation is IN-MEMORY, reset on every orchestrator restart, while the fleet restarts on an ~8h deploy clock — so a 72h continuous-candidacy anchor can never accumulate. (That tuning was a deliberate 2026-07-15 owner decision to stop it firing on ordinary lock contention; it is not a defect to file, and neither is rank starvation, which is separately ruled out of scope.)

DIAGNOSTIC RECIPE: for any task that looks starved, read its events from data/orchestrator/runs.db first. A single `requeued` / `plan_blast_radius_lock_conflict` row with nothing after it means the task is lock-blocked, not rank-starved — and the fix is landing whichever task holds its files, not touching the scheduler.

target_text:
NORM for an implementer RESUMING a dark-factory task after a review-driven escalation (measured on task 3790, 2026-09-02): fix the blocking finding, then STOP — the leftover non-blocking SUGGESTIONS are not yours to apply, and one of them may be un-appliable by construction.

THE SITUATION THAT KEEPS RECURRING. Three successive handlers on task 3790 each closed the blocking finding they were handed and each ended with some variant of "the N suggestions were not included in the escalation body, so they were not triaged here". The resuming agent then inherits a green tree, a complete plan, and an undischarged pile of suggestions, and has to decide whether to work them. The answer is normally NO, for two independent reasons.

REASON 1 — THERE IS ALREADY A CHANNEL. `review_state.json` carries `suggestions_routed`, and suggestions-only verdicts get routed as follow-ups by the system. Applying them by hand duplicates that channel and, worse, lands behaviour changes that no review cycle has yet seen.

REASON 2 — A SUGGESTION CAN CONTRADICT A FROZEN PLAN STEP'S LITERAL ACCEPTANCE TEXT, which is a stronger conflict than the design_decision conflicts the existing 4705/3890/4188 precedent ladder covers. Concretely on 3790: the reviewer asked to move three metadata keys into the Tier-C `x_` namespace (the premise checks out — none of `flake_debt_test` / `flake_debt_open_count` / `flake_debt_opened_at` is in `shared/src/shared/task_metadata.py::_BLESSED_METADATA_KEYS`, so every auto-filed task emits three `unknown_key` census lines). But plan step-1 PINS those exact three spellings in its own RED acceptance text. Renaming them silently falsifies a done step's recorded criteria, and it would also split the module from its sibling precedent (`chronic_flake.py`'s equally-unblessed `chronic_flake_*` keys). That is an architect amendment, not an implementer edit.

SO THE LADDER GAINS A FOURTH RUNG, below the three already recorded: DECLINE-AND-RECORD. When the finding is NON-BLOCKING and conflicts with frozen plan text, do not narrow-apply and do not silently skip — file one `escalate_info` naming each suggestion, whether you verified its premise, and why it was not actioned. Three handlers punting in a row is the failure mode this prevents.

CHECK BEFORE YOU REACH FOR report_ready_to_merge. Its preconditions are strict and a post-escalation resume usually fails two of them: review must already have returned PASS/suggestions-only ON THIS EXACT TREE (it has not — the last verdict was ISSUES_FOUND, and the blocking fix landed AFTER it), and main must be an ancestor of HEAD (measure it: `git merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD`; on 3790 the branch was 28 ahead / 16 behind, i.e. diverged, and rebasing is the merge lane's job, not yours). The correct finish is to verify green, record the triage, and end the turn so a fresh review cycle runs.

entry_text: Reify overload ladder gotcha: reify-expr's eval-side `find_matching_compiled_function` checks tier 1 (exact) UNSCREENED — it returns the first exact match immediately, before the head/wildcard tiers. The compile-side `resolve_function_overload`, by contrast, filters exact over the tier-3 survivors. So any widening of tier 1 must be made in BOTH resolvers, and must stay a subset of `reify_core::overload::slot_matches_wildcard_tier`; otherwise compile time and eval time pick different overloads (the esc-4231/esc-4093 drift class).
target_text: Reify's function-overload resolution ladder is now SINGLE-SOURCED in `crates/reify-core/src/overload.rs` as `slot_matches_wildcard_tier` (tier 3) and `slot_matches_head_tier` (tier 2). Task #5689 (merged 7f96be42b2) rewired BOTH consumers — reify-compiler's `resolve_function_overload` (type_compat.rs) and reify-expr's `find_matching_compiled_function` (lib.rs) — onto those two predicates and deleted all four private mirrors. Never re-add a per-crate copy of a tier predicate: the recurring "eval-side mirror diverged from compile-side" bug class (esc-4231-120, esc-4231-126, esc-4093-152, tasks #5685/#5686) existed only because the ladder was duplicated, and a new mirror reintroduces it. Fix or extend the shared predicate in reify-core instead.

entry_text: Stamped peer under topic pytest-xdist-serial-override — an OUTPUT-SHAPE gotcha for anyone asserting on a NESTED pytest run's text, distinct from the canonical's serial-override/fixture-loss/crash-flake modes. (1) Under `--dist loadgroup`, a test marked @pytest.mark.xdist_group('g') has its nodeid suffixed `@g` in xdist's crash line ("worker 'gw1' crashed while running 'mod.py::test_x@g'") and in -rA PASSED/FAILED summary lines, so a regex ending `::test_x'` silently misses; allow `(@[^']*)?`. (2) With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" banner goes to the dead worker's stderr and is NOT relayed by the controller, so `'Timeout' in output` is false for a thread-method kill even though the test was killed by the cap. Measured on pytest 9.0.3 / xdist 3.8.0 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0, task 5470 (tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py).
target_text:
STAMPED PEER under topic `orchestrator-xdist-worker-crash-under-load` (canonical 40d1b472). CORRECTS a load-bearing triage claim in peer 59d60997 (task 4485, topic pytest-xdist-serial-override) and in the DEEP_GATE_SCENE_TEST_TIMEOUT comment block in orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py (task 5333). Measured 2026-09-18, task 5582 planning, base main 8ef4bd385d.

THE CLAIM BEING CORRECTED. Peer 59d60997 writes: "The absence of a '+++ Timeout +++' stack dump in the log corroborates this rather than being missing output." The 5333 comment block makes the same inference and calls it a triggered falsifier: "NO `+++ Timeout +++` banner anywhere in that log, which pytest-timeout writes before its os._exit()" -> "HYPOTHESIS (unproven, and now the LEADING one): the worker is not dying of this timeout."

MEASURED, AND IT IS FALSE. A genuine pytest-timeout kill of an xdist worker emits NO banner into the MASTER's output. Probe: a throwaway `@pytest.mark.timeout(3)` test sleeping 30s beside four trivial tests, run as `pytest tests -n 2 --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0 --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread -o addopts=`. Entire captured output, verbatim:
    [gw0] node down: Not properly terminated
    worker 'gw0' crashed while running 'tests/test_probe.py::test_slow'
    1 failed, 3 passed in 5.71s
No banner, no stack dump, no traceback — for a kill that is BY CONSTRUCTION a timeout. pytest_timeout.timeout_timer writes the banner through the WORKER's own terminal writer (after suspending its capture) and then calls os._exit(1); xdist does not forward worker terminal output to the master, and os._exit skips every flush that might otherwise have carried it over the execnet channel.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TRIAGE. Banner-absence is the EXPECTED shape of a timeout kill under xdist, so it is evidence of NOTHING. Do not use it to rule the timeout mechanism in or out, in either direction. Two recorded crashes of orchestrator tests/test_merge_queue_deep_landing.py::TestStaleCasAbortLeavesTheRestAlone::test_two_consecutive_tip_fails_render_nothing_for_any_link (data/verify-logs/5440 and /4039, tasks 5440 and 4039) match the probe's signature byte for byte.

WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED, and is still the right check: peer 59d60997's OTHER test — compare the SESSION's total wall clock against the effective per-test timeout, and if the whole run is shorter than the ceiling a timeout kill is arithmetically impossible. That one is sound and needs no banner. Use it instead.

A SECOND ARITHMETIC TRAP that check does not cover: the effective per-test ceiling is NOT always the verify CLI's `--timeout=300`. A `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` marker OVERRIDES the CLI unconditionally in both directions (pytest_timeout._get_item_settings consults config._env_timeout only when the marker yielded None), so a class marked 180 really runs at 180 under a 300s verify. Recovering evidence of a bare xdist worker crash whose verify log was never persisted. Three sources survive:
(1) `<worktree>/orchestrator/.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed` holds the nodeid xdist synthesized a FAILED report for, i.e. the crashed worker's in-flight test. The file's mtime is the controller session end, not the moment of death. The entry disappears when a later run passes that test, so read it before any retry.
(2) On the implement path, the streamed `.worktrees/<id>/.task/verify/attempt-N.<pkg>.test.log` survives the raise until a later attempt with the same N overwrites it. It carries '[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated' and "worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'".
(3) Merge-lane verify logs are archived unconditionally in data/verify-logs/<task>/.
With `--max-worker-restart=0` the suite keeps running on the surviving workers after a death: task 3714's worker died at 83% and the session still finished '1 failed, 19294 passed'. So detection time is not death time.

Gotcha (dark-factory, shared/tests, task 4254) — COMPANION to the existing "re-base the sweep under tmp_path via base_dir in an AUTOUSE fixture" entry (00d9c442), covering the ONE-SHOT MARK rather than the sweep itself. `shared.config_dir` now owns the once-per-process bookkeeping (`sweep_stale_pid_dirs_once` + a process-global `_swept_prefixes: set[str]`, reset via the `reset_sweep_once_state(prefix=None)` test hook), hoisted out of the two near-verbatim twins in `usage_gate` and `startup_completion_probe`.

RULE: a test fixture must reset ONLY the prefix its own module owns — `reset_sweep_once_state(probe._PROBE_DIR_PREFIX)`, not the bare `reset_sweep_once_state()`. The bare form clears `_swept_prefixes` entirely. That matters because the mark is load-bearing PROTECTION, not just bookkeeping: `UsageGate.__init__` sweeps at construction, so the mark left behind by an earlier module is what keeps a LATER module's first gate from scandir+rmtree-ing the real system tempdir. Only `test_usage_gate.py` is autouse-guarded (`_keep_gates_off_the_real_tmp`); `test_usage_gate_exhaustive.py`, `test_usage_gate_scope_attribution.py`, `test_concurrency.py`, `test_auth_failed.py`, `test_failover_integration.py` and `test_probe_loop.py` all build gates unprotected. Clearing a prefix you do not own therefore makes whether those hit real /tmp depend on pytest COLLECTION ORDER. The one legitimate unscoped caller is `test_config_dir.py::TestSweepStalePidDirsOnce._fresh_process`, which tests the bookkeeping itself over throwaway prefixes it invents.

The migration hazard that motivated the hook: the old per-module flags were reset with `monkeypatch.setattr(..., '_probe_dir_sweep_done', False)`. Two of the three sites passed `raising=False`, so after the flag was deleted they would have SILENTLY no-opped and let the mark leak across tests; only the third would have failed loudly. Delete a module-global and migrate its reset sites in the SAME commit, or the silent pair drifts.

HOW TO MEASURE this class of thing (cheap, and it worked): a pytest plugin loaded with `-p` off PYTHONPATH that rebinds each CALLER's module-level `sweep_stale_pid_dirs` to a spy resolving `kwargs.get('base_dir') or tempfile.gettempdir()` against the real tempdir captured at import, recording and returning 0 instead of deleting. Resolve base_dir at CALL time — tests monkeypatch `gettempdir`, so a spy that only checks for `base_dir is None` reports false positives. Measured across the full `shared` suite (4936 passed): 2 real-/tmp sweeps, unchanged before and after the scoping fix — i.e. the unscoped reset was a latent blast-radius widening, not a live regression.

target_text: GOTCHA (dark-factory, 2026-08-28): every pre-existing end-to-end merge-train coalescing test pre-enqueues its singles BEFORE the worker starts, so the coalescing pass fires on the merger's STERILE FIRST ITERATION — the one state in which the old `is_idle()` gate was open. That is exactly why the whole suite stayed green while production formed zero trains for eight days. Affected: `orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue_coalesce.py::TestEndToEndWiring` and all of `orchestrator/tests/test_coalesce_integration_gate.py`'s scenarios. If you are testing anything about WHEN the coalescer runs, a sterile-start fixture proves nothing — I wrote one first and it passed identically against the pre-fix and post-fix code. To build a discriminating fixture: enqueue one warm-up single, start the worker, gate its verify (`patch('orchestrator.merge_queue.run_scoped_verification', ...)`) so its merge commit stays unadvanced, then enqueue the coalesce candidates as ONE synchronous burst of `queue.put_nowait(...)` calls — `put_nowait` never yields, so the merger cannot wake between them and all of them are buffered before it drains. Wait for a candidate's `merge_dequeued` event before releasing the gate to prove the coalesce point was reached while the warm-up was still unfinalized. Note also that with speculation depth K=1 the merger BLOCKS at `acquire_for_lookahead()` once the permit is held by an item the gated verifier cannot drain, so holding the gate too long stalls the run rather than testing it.

entry_text: `reify check` (cmd_check, crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs ~815) exits FAILURE on ANY compile-time Error diagnostic before it evaluates constraints, so it never prints per-constraint OK/INDETERMINATE lines for a file with a compile Error. A PRD signal that wants both a new compile Error and an "X still reports OK" line on the same file therefore cannot be met at the CLI. Assert the "still OK" half on the compiler surface (constraint generated) or by calling Engine::check directly on the compiled module. Also measured 2026-10-02: an ad-hoc `connect a @ point(..) -> b @ point(..)` frame_align is permanently Indeterminate because reify-expr eval_eq has no Value::Frame arm.
target_text: `reify check` cannot report per-constraint outcomes for a module that has any compile Error. cmd_check returns FAILURE right after printing compile diagnostics (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:820-826), and cmd_eval and cmd_test short-circuit the same way. So any PRD or task signal shaped "check emits compile Error X while constraint Y still reports OK" is undeliverable through the CLI. Assert the unaffected constraint at the compiler or engine surface instead, or explicitly scope a change to check's short-circuit. This was found authoring-time in the DIC PRD (B10 vs decision 5), and Leo ruled the explicit won't-fix (esc-5419-3, 2026-10-02).

entry_text: GOTCHA (task 5669 architect, measured with `pytest --setup-show` on pytest 9.0.3): within one conftest, plain autouse fixtures set up in ALPHABETICAL name order (pytest's parsefactories walks dir(module)), not declaration order. So renaming a teardown guard in orchestrator/tests/conftest.py silently moves its teardown slot. `_drain_async_mock_coroutines` tears down AFTER _drain_leaked_tasks, _function_scoped_runner and monkeypatch only because 'a' < 'f'/'l'/'m'. A rename to e.g. `_no_unawaited_...` would drain before leaked tasks are cancelled and before patches are undone. To change a guard's name safely, make the ordering explicit by fixture request instead.
target_text: Pytest-asyncio fixture-ordering gotchas measured on dark-factory's pinned toolchain (python 3.13.9, pytest 9.0.3, pytest-asyncio 1.3.0, asyncio_mode=strict), while fixing task 4412's two-arm httpx reaper. (1) DECLARATION ORDER DOES NOT DECIDE TEARDOWN ORDER between a plain `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` and a `@pytest_asyncio.fixture(autouse=True)`: pytest-asyncio 1.x async fixtures acquire an event-loop dependency that reorders them relative to plain autouse fixtures. Measured: with the sync arm declared FIRST, the SYNC arm still tore down FIRST and the async arm second — the inverse of the usual reverse-declaration-order rule. To force an async fixture to tear down BEFORE a sync one, make it REQUEST the sync one (`async def _async_arm(_sync_arm)`); requesting forces setup-first/finalize-last on the requested fixture, and this was measured to flip the order for both sync and async tests. (2) A `pytest_asyncio` autouse fixture DOES run for plain `def test_` tests, getting its own throwaway event loop — the common belief that it "only covers async tests" is false here. (3) MEASUREMENT PITFALL: you cannot spy on a conftest autouse fixture's teardown using the `monkeypatch` fixture from a test module — `monkeypatch` is function-scoped and reverts BEFORE the conftest arms finalize, yielding a misleading empty result. Patch at module-import (collection) time instead, or use a session-scoped patch. (4) A test CANNOT observe its own teardown: finalizers added via `request.addfinalizer()` in the test body and via test-module fixtures both run LIFO BEFORE conftest autouse arms (measured order: test-body finalizer, module fixture, async arm, sync arm) — so observing a teardown side effect requires a later test (co-locate the pair with `@pytest.mark.xdist_group(...)` under `--dist loadgroup`).

Reference, 2026-10-01: on leo-laptop, the wrapper /usr/local/bin/orchestrator tees every remote `orchestrator verify-merge` invocation's output to ~/verify-merge-invocations.log. That includes the orchestrator's INFO logging, e.g. 'Cold-verify shared-venv pre-provision: running …' and the 'Verification mode' lines.

It is the place to check what a REMOTE merge verify actually executed. The workstation-side verify-logs archive (data/verify-logs/<task>/attempt-N.remote-laptop.*) keeps the stderr log only for some outcomes; a pass may leave only a pass-summary JSON.

Per-scope resource usage on the laptop is in `journalctl --user` as 'df-verify-<tag>-<id>.scope: Consumed …' lines, and kernel OOM events are in `sudo journalctl -k`. Passwordless sudo works on the laptop.
target_text: Remote merge-verify writes NO durable log file on failure — diagnosability gap (DF, found 2026-06-26). When a verify FAILS on a REMOTE verify host (e.g. leo-laptop, passed=False but SSH transport OK), there is no log to `cat`: (1) the remote `VerifyRunnerPool` is constructed WITHOUT `archive_root` (merge_queue.py:894-901), unlike the LOCAL path which passes `archive_root=req.config.project_root/'data'/'verify-logs'` (merge_queue.py:910-920); (2) on `ssh_rc==0`, `RemoteRunner.run_merge_verify` returns `result_from_json(ssh_stdout)` and DISCARDS `ssh_stderr` (verify_runner.py:781-797) — remote stderr is only surfaced inside a `RunnerUnavailable` when SSH transport itself fails (`ssh_rc != 0`); (3) the remote host logs to stderr only (cli.py:159-164 "All logs go to stderr"), and the wire `MergeVerifySpec` carries no archive_root so the remote never writes a file. The substantive failure output DOES ride back inside `VerifyResult.test_output/lint_output/type_output` (verify.py:1479) and is folded into the blocked task's reason via `failure_report()` (merge_queue.py:1013-1023, format `Post-merge verification failed: <summary> [category: <cat>]\n\n<detail>`). So to triage a failed REMOTE verify you read the BLOCKED TASK's reason — there is no verify-logs/ file. Contrast: LOCAL verify archives to `<project_root>/data/verify-logs/<task_id>/attempt-{N}.{label}-{utc_ts}.log` (verify.py:_archive_merge_verify_logs, 779-856). Sibling-of task 1768 (local diagnosability gap, done).

MEASURED FACT (dark-factory, 2026-09-04, at main-descendant 6b68a87fd6): `shared/tests/` is NOT runnable against a standalone dark-factory-shared checkout, and the atomic-write anti-regrowth guard is only ONE of THREE independent reasons. Anyone scoping work off the premise "moving the atomic-write guard out of shared/tests makes shared self-contained" (task 3388's own description asserts exactly that) is working from a false premise.

The three cross-package scan roots in shared/tests, found by sweeping shared/tests/**/*.py (88 files) for sibling-tree path literals inside tuple/list nodes:

  1. test_safe_io.py — `_SRC_TREES`, the task-3223 atomic-write guard. Widened by task 3388 to six trees: shared/src, orchestrator/src, escalation/src, fused-memory/src, fused-memory/scripts, scripts.
  2. silent_fallthrough_scan.py — `_SCOPE_ROOTS` = 7 roots (orchestrator/src, fused-memory/src, dashboard/src, escalation/src, shared/src, sampler/src, scripts). LIVE and load-bearing: imported by test_silent_fallthrough_gate.py and test_config_dir_archival_gate.py.
  3. test_auth_failed.py — `_PRODUCTION_SRC_ROOTS` = ('shared/src', 'orchestrator/src').

All three HARD-FAIL rather than degrade when a sibling tree is absent, which is what makes the non-self-containedness real rather than cosmetic: silent_fallthrough_scan.iter_first_party_files raises RuntimeError from an explicit sentinel loop over ("shared/src", "orchestrator/src"); test_auth_failed executes `assert root.is_dir()`; test_safe_io's _iter_source_files does the same. Each carries a comment arguing FOR its cross-tree reach ("a guard that quietly stops scanning a tree it can no longer find is worse than no guard"), so these are deliberate designs, not oversights — do not "fix" them without a design decision.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TEST DESIGN: a guard asserting "no file in shared/tests names a sibling package's source tree as a scan root" cannot pass at this base and cannot be made to pass by relocating any single guard. The narrower invariant that IS specific to the atomic-write guard — and that the module-boundary complaint actually describes — is "no hard-asserted allowlist in shared/tests names a sibling package's SYMBOLS" (test_safe_io's _ALLOWED_RENAMERS keys orchestrator/src/orchestrator/digest.py::write_digest_entry, so deleting or renaming that orchestrator function turns shared's suite red). Files 2 and 3 scan sibling trees but pin no sibling symbols, so they do not have that property. Key any such guard on sibling file-path+qualname allowlist entries, not on bare scan-root literals.

entry_text:
Completed: [legibility census] Redundant duplicate full-suite test invocation to extract two derived metrics
Description: Agent chained two separate `timeout 2400 cargo test -p reify-eval ...` pipelines in one Bash call — one piped through grep+awk+paste to sum per-binary pass counts, a second piped through grep -c to count 'test result' lines — instead of capturing the test output once and deriving both numbers from the same capture. This doubles wall-clock cost and doubles exposure to being killed (exit 137) before either pipeline finishes.

Evidence:
- timeout 2400 cargo test -p reify-eval 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result" | awk -F'[.;]' '{print $2}' | paste -sd+ | head -3; timeout 2400 cargo test -p reify-eval 2>&1 | grep -c "^test resu

Observed in 1 sighting(s) (project: reify).
Analysis: PROBLEM. An agent ran `timeout 2400 cargo test -p reify-eval` TWICE in one Bash call to get two numbers from the same suite: piped through grep+awk+paste to sum the passed counts, then through `grep -c` to count `test result` lines. That doubles wall clock and doubles the exposure to an exit-137 kill. The root cause on the reify side is that no primitive turns ONE captured log into every count an agent asks for, so each new question becomes a new hand-rolled pipeline over a fresh run. Under the host's `skim` cargo wrapper those pipelines are also silently wrong: skim condenses output to `PASS: N | FAIL: M | SKIP: K`, so `grep '^test result'` finds nothing, and skim's 300s cap prints `Error: command timed out after 300s` and exits 0 (memory 80932c8e, 21fd3cbe, 51d94f6b).

PREMISES VERIFIED. None of the task-metadata files exist yet: `git ls-files | grep -i tally` is empty, and no commit on any ref mentions tally or 7896, so this is new work and not a duplicate.
