Reify repo: cargo test/build/clippy output is intercepted and condensed to terse summary lines instead of standard cargo/libtest output. Two independent interceptors exist: (1) a `cargo` shim wrapper (~/.local/bin/cargo, aka "skim") and (2) the Claude harness PreToolUse hook `~/.claude/hooks/skim-rewrite.sh` (rewrites `cargo test`/`cargo build` → `skim test cargo ...`). Effects: `cargo test` → `PASS: N | FAIL: M | SKIP: K` (not `test result: ok. N passed`); `cargo build`/`cargo clippy` → `BUILD OK | warnings: N | errors: N` (or `BUILD FAILED | ... errors: N` with per-error `-->` location lines). Grepping `test result:` or `running N tests` finds nothing under this wrapper — check the FAIL/errors count and exit code instead (0=green, 101=any test failure). Compiler/rustc RED-state compile diagnostics still print in full; only the successful-run summary is condensed. `-- --format pretty`, `--nocapture`, `--show-output`, and `--message-format=json|short|human` do NOT restore standard output through the wrapper — `--message-format=short` still gives concise one-line compiler errors when compilation itself fails.

Interpreting the summary: `PASS: 0 | FAIL: 0 | SKIP: 0` usually means the test-name filter matched ZERO tests (not that something broke) — verify the filter/test names (e.g. via grep on `fn .*name` in the test file) rather than assuming failure. Since no panic/assertion detail is printed for a genuine failure, TDD practice should rely on (a) the summary confirming it compiled and (b) the RED→GREEN transition after the impl lands, rather than expecting to read the failure message from this wrapper.

Confirmed bypasses to see full detail:
- Compile with `--no-run` then execute the compiled test binary directly: `target/{debug,release}/deps/<test_name>-<hash> <filter> --nocapture --test-threads=1` (for OCCT/openvdb-linked crates like reify-lsp, set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib:/snap/freecad/current/usr/lib` first; alternatively prefix with the project's own OCCT wrapper, e.g. `.cargo/run-with-occt.sh <bin> <test_name> --nocapture --test-threads=1`, which sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH automatically). Use a SUBSTRING filter, not `--exact` — in-crate tests often live in submodules (e.g. full path `engine_build::tests::<name>`), so `--exact <bare_name>` matches 0 tests.
- To find the correct/freshest test binary path, two options: (a) `ls -1t target/debug/deps/<crate>-* | grep -vE '\.(d|rlib|rmeta)$' | head -1` (or the `find ... -printf "%T@ %p\n" | sort -rn` equivalent), or (b) more reliably, run `cargo test -p <crate> --test <name> --no-run --message-format=json` and extract the `"executable":"..."` field from the JSON build output — this avoids ambiguity from stale binaries with newer mtimes than the current build.
- Redirect through a subshell to a file — the skim filter only sees the OUTER Bash tool's stdout, not an inner subshell's: `bash -c 'cargo test ... 2>&1' > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; cat /tmp/out.txt`. Piping a cold full-workspace `cargo test` through `tail` in a background task instead buffers ALL output and can itself hit the ~300s background-task ceiling — redirect to a file so output streams incrementally. A cold first full-workspace compile can also exceed the ~300s default Bash timeout — use a longer timeout + run_in_background for the first build. Separately, `cargo test -p <crate>` (all targets) can exceed the 300s wrapper cap purely on COMPILE time for crates with many integration-test binaries (e.g. reify-solver-elastic) — prefer `--lib` or running the specific prebuilt test binary.
- Prefix with `env` (e.g. `env cargo test -p <crate> --test <file> <name> 2>&1`) — the skim hook does not pattern-match `env cargo …`, so output passes through verbatim.
- Invoke cargo via its fully-qualified absolute path, e.g. `/home/leo/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p <crate> --test <name> -- --nocapture` — the hook appears to pattern-match the literal token `cargo`, not the resolved binary path, so an absolute-path invocation also returns…[truncated, 7526 chars total]

entry_text: fused-memory's MCP 'search' tool reports some failures, for example a project_id validation failure, as a NORMAL tool result: a text block containing JSON {"error": "...", "error_type": "ValidationError"}, with isError NOT set. Any consumer that treats 'not isError' as success will ingest the error document as data. A robust consumer checks for a list-valued 'results' key, as orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/briefing.py::_is_search_reply does since task 3659.
target_text: fused-memory MCP tools return their `{"error": "...", "error_type": "..."}` failure envelope on a JSON-RPC response with `isError: false`. Any client-side unwrapper that only checks `isError` (or that just reads `result.structuredContent`) will therefore hand that error dict to callers as though it were a genuine tool result. The `(payload.get("some_key") or {})` idiom on top of such a payload silently degrades to an empty default with no warning and no exception. In dark_factory this chain silently persisted a fabricated census baseline of 0 on 2026-07-24 and 2026-07-31 (task 3291). When consuming a fused-memory tool payload, assert the expected key's SHAPE and raise if absent — do not rely on `isError` and do not use `or {}` as the failure path.

The fused-memory set_task_priority_override docstring overstates what pins and reserve_now do (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py). It says 'Pin this task to the front of the queue' and, for reserve_now, 'Reserve the next worker slot'.
In fact:
- A pin gives only a first try, each scheduler tick, at all-or-nothing module-lock acquisition, with no reservation.
- reserve_now installs parks once, at the task's RAW priority, and reserves no worker slot.
Operators pin expecting movement that the code does not provide. As of 2026-09-29 no task owns the docstring fix; it was deliberately kept out of 6040 to avoid adding a fused-memory file to it.
target_text: dark-factory scheduler, measured 2026-09-28: why HIGH-tier pinned tasks starve for weeks. (1) Only the scored loop's single STRICT-TOP candidate earns skip counts and fairness parks (Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> _bump_skip_and_maybe_park). Scores are tier-dominated (config.py TIER_BASE critical 16000 vs high max 8999), so while any eligible effective-critical candidate exists a high pin can never be strict top, never parks, and its skip_count stays 0. In the 7 days to 09-28 all 390 task_skipped events went to 6 critical tasks (3542 170, 4541 79, 4023 57, 5677 41, 3620 33, 5221 10). (2) The pin loop (Scheduler._phase_select_pins) only gives a pin first try at ALL-OR-NOTHING lock acquisition on each tick. On conflict it falls through silently: no event, no skip, no park. (3) The harness calls acquire_next BEFORE sem.acquire, so at saturation (24/24) there is about one tick per freed slot (409 ticks in 7 days, of which 15 ended at select_pins). (4) The hot files are practically never free: holds alone left orchestrator config.py unheld 1.7% and verify.py 2.7% of 09-21..09-28, and harness.py/workflow.py's unheld stretches were covered by 3542's critical parks. Result: pins 3500, 3659, 5205, 5812 had their full file sets free ~0% of the week. (5) A boost_tier propagates UPSTREAM to undone deps (_compute_effective_priorities). The critical boost on OPERATOR GATE 3545 made its dep 3542 critical, and 3542 was then strict top for a month (1121 skips, 19 critical park installs 08-26..09-27), with parks on workflow.py/harness.py that were the top blocker for pins 3659 and 5677. (6) Starvation watchdog cannot fire for a high pin (dual gate needs skip>=50; idle-only gate is 30 days on an in-memory clock). (7) PSI dispatch_deferred names only the FIRST heavy candidate deferred per held tick (the first eligible heavy pin), so its per-task counts are a naming artifact, not targeting. Related tasks: 5308 (partial/empty parks, pin-loop park clearing, reserve_now at effective tier), 3821 (watchdog), 3825 (below-rank-1 counting), 3824 (durable fairness state). None as written gives a never-top-scored pin a reservation.

entry_text:
Red-on-main vectors in DF, September 2026 (measured 2026-09-28). Three of the five red-main incidents were single-parent commits made directly to main that bypassed the merge gate:
- 5230: docs commit 7938676c28
- 5425: config commit a47b5a506e
- 5878: nightly census data commit 33bc55e544

Each tripped a test that reads repo data outside its own module. The other two (5210, 5842) were environment-dependent tests. None came through a gate-verified branch.

DF's merge gate runs merge_verify_breadth "full", meaning every registered module's full suite on the merged tree. Task-lane verifies, including the pre-merge re-verify, are therefore pre-filters: changing them does not change the rate at which red reaches main. The gate-side escape paths that already exist are: the disjoint-delta skip (merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree), flake suppression, and crash-truncated sessions (5492). The lever for red-on-main is gate bypass: route automated commits through the merge queue, or run the repo guards pre-commit.
target_text: Triaging a merge-queue gate red as "pre-existing on main" vs "my regression" — the decisive measurements, in order, all cheap (used on task 3787, 2026-08-20): (1) `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- <dir-of-failing-test>` — if EMPTY, your branch contributes nothing to that module; (2) `git diff main HEAD -- <exact data/source file the test consumes>` — if EMPTY, that input is byte-identical to main, so the test is reading the same bytes on both trees; (3) re-run the failing node-ids locally in your own worktree — a DETERMINISTIC fast failure (seconds, no "[gwNN] node down", no starvation) rules out the ambient xdist-worker-death flake class and proves a real red; (4) `git log -S '<the offending literal>' main -- <file>` to name the commit that introduced it, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor <that-commit> <main-at-your-queue-time>` to prove main already carried it BEFORE you submitted. Steps 2+3 together are what upgrade "probably not mine" to proof. IMPORTANT COROLLARY: merges having landed AFTER the breaking commit does NOT mean main is green — the merge gate's effective module set can be narrower than the registry, so a red can sit in a module the gate never executed. Do not fix a red outside your granted files; escalate with the file named.

entry_text: To check that a reify binary's dynamic TBB/OCCT symbols all resolve (not just the ones a given run happens to exercise), run `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH LD_BIND_NOW=1 target/debug/reify --version`. Eager binding resolves every function symbol at load time, so a libTKernel->libtbb symbol missing from the pinned /opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin libtbb.so.12 would fail here at once. Under normal lazy binding it would only show up at the first parallel OCCT call. Measured exit 0 on 2026-10-01 (task 7439). To find which library creates threads, use an LD_PRELOAD shim that wraps pthread_create, calls dladdr on the start routine and prints backtrace_symbols_fd. gdb attach is blocked on this host by yama ptrace_scope.
target_text: GUI launch gotcha (observed 2026-09-03, litter-tray dogfood round 3): mechanism A″ (task 5192: /opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin first in each binary's RUNPATH + forced direct NEEDED libtbb.so.12) makes a BARE `target/debug/reify-gui` launch resolve the deps oneTBB 12.18 — but LD_LIBRARY_PATH beats DT_RUNPATH, and scripts/run-gui-dev.sh (line ~162) PREPENDS the snap OCCT dir to whatever LD_LIBRARY_PATH the caller already exports rather than replacing it. So a shell that has exported the CLI-recommended `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/opt/reify-deps/lib` (the OCCT-7.8-first order every dogfood brief prescribes for `reify eval`) launches a GUI that dies instantly with `target/debug/reify-gui: symbol lookup error: undefined symbol: _ZN3tbb6detail2r127get_thread_reference_vertexEPNS0_2d126wait_tree_vertex_interfaceE` (system libtbb.so.12.11 shadows the pin). Verified with ldd: no LD_LIBRARY_PATH → tbb-pin; the CLI order → /usr/lib libtbb; `/opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/opt/reify-deps/lib` → tbb-pin. The CLI binary survives the same env only because it never calls that symbol (lazy binding). FIX AT LAUNCH: `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<port> bash scripts/run-gui-dev.sh <file.ri>` (or prepend /opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin). This is what broke the ops agent's :55015 relaunch after the 2026-09-03 printer O5 landing; not a code regression (no launcher commits in that landing).

entry_text: Reify gotcha for type-arg bound checks: on the generic-fn call path, T is inferred by `unify` against compiled result_types, and geometry ctors lie — `box(..)`/`sphere(..)` bind T to `Real` and `point3(..)` to `Point3<Scalar[m]>` (measured 2026-09-30 by forcing E_FN_TYPE_ARG_CONFLICT with `fn two<T>(a: T, b: T)` + `two(box(..), true)`). Since stdlib geometry marker traits (Solid/Geometry/Transformable) are meant to be satisfied by geometry values, never reject an INFERRED builtin binding against a trait bound; only WRITTEN type args (`Housing<Bool>()`, `S : Box<Bool>`, `param c : Housing<Bool>`) are trustworthy. Also `Solid`/`Geometry`/`DatumRef` written as type names resolve to `Type::Geometry`.
target_text: Reify gotcha — `type_compatible` (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs:220) is a CALL-SITE COERCION predicate that assumes both sides carry truly-inferred types; it is NOT valid as a general conformance gate against compiled `result_type`s. Five confirmed families where a legitimate arg's result_type does not match its param type: (1) geometry AND point constructors compile to the expression compiler's numeric-fallback placeholder — `point3(0m,0m,0m)` has result_type `Scalar[m]`, not `Type::Point` (same class as the known Geometry→dimensionless-scalar GHR-γ placeholder, which is why `promote_function_call_to_structure_ref` at conformance/mod.rs:611 exists); (2) a nested list literal is the idiomatic Matrix3x3 spelling and compiles to `List<List<Real>>` — no coercion arm exists; (3) `Type::Field` args erase both slots to `Field<Real,Real>`; (4) under enum erasure a constructed variant's result_type is ALWAYS the bare `Type::Enum(n)`, never `Type::Applied` — use `enum_payload_compatible` (type_compat.rs:322) as variant_construct.rs:325 does; (5) dimensionless `Real`-typed args at DIMENSIONED `Scalar[...]` slots are idiomatic. When adding a type-conformance check, gate it on a POSITIVE allowlist of vetted param families, never a negative skip-list — a negative list opts every future `Type` variant into a false positive.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-09-14 against crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, task #6484): reify structure-instance ctor args bind BY NAME, not positionally. Task 4522 replaced the old positional binder with a two-pass scheme — "Pass 1: assign named args to their target param slot" (~expr.rs:2837), then "Pass 2: assign positional (None) args to the next param not already bound by a named arg" (~:2863). Two older memories still assert the retired positional behaviour and are now FALSE: mem0 e18a60f8-359c-46c5-9e9c-6e80212a56a6 ("positional args bind to a structure_def's Param cells in declaration order") and graphiti a641477c-28e4-4b58-b2af-1a2c0bc06ed4 ("binds arguments positionally by index"). Task #6484 existed precisely to retire this same stale claim from source comments.

GOTCHA that follows from the by-name binder: a MISSPELLED named arg is diagnosed as E_CTOR_UNKNOWN_FIELD but is STILL pushed leniently as `__arg{call_idx}` and NEVER claims a param slot (the binder's own comment: "The unknown arg is diagnosed but NOT bound to a param slot"). So the param the author meant to set silently falls back to its declared default. Writing the other params out explicitly does NOT prevent this — the mis-bind is independent of them, and with N args against a declared count of N no surplus positional exists so E_CTOR_ARITY never fires either. The severity is a single knob, CTOR_FIELD_CONFORMANCE_SEVERITY in crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/mod.rs:45, = Severity::Warning today (so it does not fail the build; slated to become Error at δ). Consequence in practice: `element_order: ElementOrdr.P2` on a ModalOptions/BucklingOptions call silently leaves element_order at its ElementOrder.P1 default, reinstating the P1 bending lock. Pinned by crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_mechanics/modal_options_validation_tests.rs::misspelled_ctor_label_is_diagnosed_but_still_leniently_appended.

entry_text:
The fused-memory set_task_priority_override docstring overstates what pins and reserve_now do (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py). It says 'Pin this task to the front of the queue' and, for reserve_now, 'Reserve the next worker slot'.
In fact:
- A pin gives only a first try, each scheduler tick, at all-or-nothing module-lock acquisition, with no reservation.
- reserve_now installs parks once, at the task's RAW priority, and reserves no worker slot.
Operators pin expecting movement that the code does not provide. As of 2026-09-29 no task owns the docstring fix; it was deliberately kept out of 6040 to avoid adding a fused-memory file to it.
target_text:
Completed: Pinned tasks never earn a reservation, so a pin on contended files never dispatches — give the head blocked pin a pin-owned reservation
Description: PROBLEM
A pin today buys exactly one thing: on each scheduler tick, the pinned task gets the first try at acquiring ALL of its module locks at once (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_select_pins). If that try fails, the pin earns nothing. No skip count, no park, no event.

Fairness parks go only to the scored loop's single strict-top candidate (::Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> ::Scheduler._bump_skip_and_maybe_park). orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::TIER_BASE makes every critical candidate outscore every high one. So a non-critical pin can never earn a park while any critical candidate is eligible, and one always is: in the 7 days to 2026-09-28, all 390 task_skipped events went to six critical tasks.

A pinned task whose footprint touches a contended file therefore dispatches only on a tick where every one of its files happens to be free of both holders and parks. Meanwhile, the files it needs free up one at a time and are taken by lower-tier scored candidates in the same tick. The pin fails exactly the class the scheduler PRD says pins exist for: plans/scheduler-dispatch-scoring-and-lock-layer-prd.md §C4 says "never top-scored — this is what the pin is for".

EVIDENCE (read-only; data/orchestrator/runs.db and .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, measured 2026-09-28)
- The scheduler ran 409 ticks in 7 days. Only 15 of them ended in select_pins.
- Pins 3500 (pinned 08-24), 3659 and 4856 (09-01), 5205 (09-19) and 5812 (09-23) went 5 to 35 days without a dispatch. 5205, 5812 and 4856 have never dispatched.

entry_text: How per-write graphiti LLM token usage is measured (shipped in task 3716): NOT by a before/after delta on the shared TokenUsageTracker and never by reset(). build_llm_client installs fused_memory.backends.llm_token_usage.AttributingTokenUsageTracker on every arm, and measure_llm_tokens(client) / GraphitiBackend.token_probe() opens a ContextVar-scoped window that counts exactly the records made by its own asyncio context, including tasks it spawns. That makes it exact under concurrent cross-group writes on the one shared _llm_client. The generic arm records via TokenRecordingOpenAIGenericClient, once per successful generate_response, matching BaseOpenAIClient. GOTCHA for parity comparisons: upstream AnthropicClient (graphiti-core 0.28.2) calls token_tracker.record BEFORE response_model validation, with cumulative totals, so on a validation retry it records the failed attempt and then re-counts it inside the next record. Its llm_calls and token counts are not comparable one-for-one with the OpenAI-shaped arms.
target_text: GOTCHA — graphiti's TokenUsageTracker is ONE cumulative instance shared across the whole GraphitiBackend (_llm_client goes to self.client and every per-group clone in _client_for), so per-write token usage cannot be read as a tracker before/after delta: concurrent cross-group writes and any other LLM use of the shared client bleed into the window. Never call tracker.reset() either. The exact approach (task 3716 plan, 2026-10-04) is context attribution: a TokenUsageTracker subclass whose record() also feeds ContextVar-scoped sinks opened per write. asyncio copies the context at Task creation, so graphiti's semaphore_gather fan-out inherits the sink and other tasks never see it. In tests, never discover such a probe with getattr on a MagicMock-backed svc.graphiti: the auto-attribute supports `async with`, and a MagicMock reaching json.dumps inside the never-raise WriteJournal.log_backend_op silently drops the row. Gate on the typed usage value instead.

entry_text: In reify, files under crates/*/tests/<harness_name>/ are `mod` submodules of a single harness test binary, so `cargo test --test <file_stem>` fails. Target the binary and filter by module path instead, e.g. `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_compilation_surface examples_smoke` or `cargo test -p reify-eval --test harness_auto_resolution auto_type_param_determinism_tests`. Also, `rustfmt --check` on a crate's lib.rs follows `mod` declarations into every module, so run it on the individual touched files to see only your own hunks.
target_text: In crates/reify-compiler/tests/, files under the harness_*/ subdirectories (e.g. harness_traits/fn_generic_call_inference_tests.rs) are NOT their own cargo test binaries — they are `#[path]`-included modules of a consolidated harness root such as tests/harness_traits.rs (task #5283 merge-gate compile-cost consolidation). To run one, use `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_traits <module_stem>::`; `--test <module_stem>` does not exist and fails with "no test target named ...".

entry_text: Reify gotcha: after task 5743, the DimensionedArgRejected readers resolve_spec_arg (shared core of resolve_length_scalar_arg + resolve_angle_scalar_arg) and resolve_density_arg in crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs are reachable only for DYNAMICALLY-typed args. Every one of their builtins (edges_at_height, extremal_by_*, faces_by_normal/edges_parallel_to/*_perpendicular_to tol, center_of_mass, moment_of_inertia) also has a compile slot in reify-compiler builtin_signatures.rs:456-513, so a bare literal already exits `reify eval` 1 via ArgTypeMismatch. body_mass_props (dynamics_ops.rs Contract B) has NO compile slot, so it is the one density position where an eval-layer severity change really flips the exit code for statically-visible source.
target_text: Reify units work — dimensioning a compiler-synthesized geometry literal is behaviour-preserving TODAY, and retyping a dimensionless MULTIPLIER is an active hazard. Two facts verified live at reify-compiler HEAD (task 5742): (1) Geometry op args are read dimension-blind: `Translate` dx/dy/dz go through `f64_arg` -> `eval_named_arg_f64` -> `Value::as_f64()` (reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs:2200-2212; reify-ir/src/value.rs:1635-1642), which returns `Some(*si_value)` for `Scalar` AND `Some(*r)` for `Real`. `sweep_revolve`'s `angle` is the same (geometry_ops.rs:2975). The real chokepoint `arg_acceptance::length_spec()`/`accept_arg` is wired ONLY to pattern spacing, mirror-plane origin, circular-pattern axis origin and arbitrary-pattern offset (see its own doc comment, arg_acceptance.rs:94-103) — NOT to Translate/Revolve slots. So changing `Value::Real(0.0)` to `Value::length(0.0)` in a compiler lowering arm changes no runtime number; write such comments in the PROSPECTIVE voice ("in anticipation of the eval-layer gate"), never as "a bare Real would be rejected". (2) THE AREA TRAP: for a scale factor inside `binop(Mul, magnitude_LENGTH, Literal(Real(-0.5)), magnitude.result_type)`, the factor must STAY a bare dimensionless `Real`. At eval `Scalar{LENGTH} x Real` takes the Scalar*Real arm and preserves LENGTH, but `Value::length(-0.5)` switches it onto the Scalar*Scalar arm yielding `Scalar{AREA}` — numerically identical through `as_f64()` (silent), yet rejected by the incoming length gate, i.e. exactly inverting the intent. Sites: `cylinder_centered` dz, `rounded_box` corner dz, `zone_profile` plus/minus_offset in reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs. docs/prds/v0_6/units-length-gate-completion.md misattributes two of these to `rounded_box` by line number; they are pinned as negative space in reify-compiler/tests/rounded_primitives_tests.rs.

entry_text: Stamped peer under topic pytest-xdist-serial-override — an OUTPUT-SHAPE gotcha for anyone asserting on a NESTED pytest run's text, distinct from the canonical's serial-override/fixture-loss/crash-flake modes. (1) Under `--dist loadgroup`, a test marked @pytest.mark.xdist_group('g') has its nodeid suffixed `@g` in xdist's crash line ("worker 'gw1' crashed while running 'mod.py::test_x@g'") and in -rA PASSED/FAILED summary lines, so a regex ending `::test_x'` silently misses; allow `(@[^']*)?`. (2) With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" banner goes to the dead worker's stderr and is NOT relayed by the controller, so `'Timeout' in output` is false for a thread-method kill even though the test was killed by the cap. Measured on pytest 9.0.3 / xdist 3.8.0 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0, task 5470 (tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py).

STAMPED PEER under topic `pytest-xdist-serial-override`, refining task 4485's discriminator (peer 59d60997). Measured 2026-09-06 on task 4188, worktree HEAD 9ac7cdbbb9.

THE REFINEMENT: task 4485 recorded a "reusable check" — compare the SESSION's total wall clock against the effective per-test timeout; if the run is shorter than the ceiling, a timeout kill is arithmetically impossible. That check SILENTLY FAILS TO DISCRIMINATE whenever the blamed test carries its own `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` marker. A marker OVERRIDES both the ini `timeout = 60` and the lane's CLI `--timeout=300`, so the effective ceiling can be far BELOW the session length even though the lane looks correctly configured. Seen here: lane ran `--timeout=300`, session lasted 3258s, but both blamed tests carry `@pytest.mark.timeout(10)` — so the arithmetic check says "kill possible" and tells you nothing.

WHAT STILL WORKS when the arithmetic check is inconclusive: grep the test log for `+++ Timeout +++`. pytest-timeout's thread method prints that stack dump BEFORE `os._exit()`, so its ABSENCE rules the timeout mechanism out regardless of ceilings. Here grep for 'Timeout' returned 0 matches over the whole log. Corollary: do NOT "fix" the blamed test by raising its `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` — that would be a band-aid on a mechanism that provably did not fire.

SECOND TELL, cheap and decisive: compare the `^FAILED ` nodeids against the `worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'` nodeids. If every FAILED nodeid is byte-identical to a crash attribution, there is NO independent failure — the FAILED line is the crash's own bookkeeping. Here lines 217/220 (crash notices) and 222/223 (FAILED) named the same two nodeids. This is exactly why `verify.py::_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash` did not route to the bounded infra retry: its veto fires on any FAILED nodeid absent from `_KNOWN_LOAD_FLAKE_NODEID_RES`, and it does not notice that the nodeid is self-attributed. Recurrence of esc-4485-1; re-filed as esc-4188-5.

BEWARE THE KILLPG RED HERRING. The two blamed tests here were `tests/test_verify.py::TestRunCmdProcessGroup::test_run_cmd_killpg_sequence_on_timeout` and `::test_run_cmd_killpg_on_cancellation` — killpg tests blamed for a worker death looks like the task-2828 REAL cross-worker-kill class (memory 16093fc0), where a test genuinely SIGKILLs a sibling worker's process group. Rule it out on two grounds rather than assuming: (1) read the test — these mock `create_subprocess_shell`, `os.getpgid` AND `os.killpg`, so no real subprocess is planted and no real signal is sent; (2) apply task 2828's own discriminator — a real cross-worker kill REPRODUCES at `-n auto` and blames the SAME test every run. Measured 12 consecutive `-n auto` runs (nproc=32): 12/12 green, plus 3 passed at `-n0` and 896 passed for test_verify.py + test_verify_runner.py together.

HOST CONTEXT that makes this class fire: loadavg 135 on 32 cores, `/proc/pressure/cpu some avg300=59.32`, `/proc/vmstat oom_kill 0` (kernel OOM ruled out — always check, it is a one-line read).

entry_text: Targeted rustfmt check gotcha in reify: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` follows `mod` declarations. Passing a crate root (lib.rs/main.rs) or a `tests/mod.rs` therefore checks the WHOLE module tree, producing hundreds of KB of pre-existing hunks from the never-formatted workspace. When checking only touched files, pass leaf module files only, and attribute any hunk to yourself only if it lies inside lines you added. Measured 2026-10-02 on gui/src-tauri (task 7274): passing src/lib.rs produced ~455KB of diff output for the reify-gui crate.
target_text: In reify, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/<crate>/src/lib.rs` (or any file that declares `mod foo;`) follows those module declarations and reports hunks for every child file, flooding the output. To check only the files you touched, filter the `Diff in <path>:<line>:` headers to those paths and compare the line numbers against `command git diff -U0` hunk ranges.

Completed: Poll only the ACTIVE tab's endpoints, using the TAB_ENDPOINTS map that already exists
Description: data.js fetches all 14 dashboard endpoints every 3000ms regardless of which tab is open, but only ONE tab is ever mounted: app.jsx's renderTab() is a switch returning a single component, and the body wrapper carries key={tab} so a tab change tears the old subtree down entirely. So the dashboard continuously fetches and parses data for twelve tabs nobody is looking at.

The mapping needed to fix this ALREADY EXISTS and is already maintained. endpoint_staleness.js::TAB_ENDPOINTS maps every tab id to the endpoints that tab actually consumes, and endpoint_staleness.test.mjs machine-checks BOTH directions - every path is a real endpointsFor() key, and every app.jsx tab id has an entry - precisely so it cannot silently drift. It says, for example, scheduler maps to a single endpoint.

Concrete saving, from live measurement 2026-09-23: sitting on the Scheduler tab currently costs about 22 MB per poll cycle across 14 endpoints; that tab needs /api/v2/dashboard/scheduler alone, 3.1 MB. The server-side cost is the real prize - 99.4% of each endpoint's wall clock is the server building the payload via MCP fan-out across 9 project roots (tasks: ttfb 3.886s of 3.910s total), on the same host as the orchestrator fleet.

THE BLOCKER, and why this is not a five-line change: app.jsx::App computes railCounts for the left-hand rail badges on EVERY tab, and it reads ACTIVE_TASKS, ORCHESTRATORS, RECON_STATE.runs, MERGE_QUEUE and ESCALATIONS to do it. So today /api/v2/dashboard/tasks - the single most expensive endpoint - is required on every tab just to render one number in a badge. Scoping the poll set without first giving the rail a cheap counts source would either blank the badges or keep the expensive endpoint polling everywhere, which forfeits most of the win.

That is what the dependency on task 5587 is for: its task snapshot unit is the natural cheap source. get_statuses (a compact id-to-status map, roughly 95% smaller than get_tasks) is the other candidate.

entry_text: Scheduler test gotcha (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py): when acquire_next has an EMPTY candidate pool, the tick ends at the empty_candidate_gate phase BEFORE the pin phase (_phase_select_pins) runs. Anything the pin phase does is therefore skipped on such a tick: pin reservation bound/release, pin_blocked, head reservation. A test that makes the only pending pin ineligible (e.g. status 'blocked') and expects the pin phase to react must keep at least one other pending candidate in the task list (e.g. a free low-priority task). Found in task 6040; the scheduler_tick event's terminal_phase field shows where a tick stopped.
target_text:
Completed: Pinned tasks never earn a reservation, so a pin on contended files never dispatches — give the head blocked pin a pin-owned reservation
Description: PROBLEM
A pin today buys exactly one thing: on each scheduler tick, the pinned task gets the first try at acquiring ALL of its module locks at once (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_select_pins). If that try fails, the pin earns nothing. No skip count, no park, no event.

Fairness parks go only to the scored loop's single strict-top candidate (::Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> ::Scheduler._bump_skip_and_maybe_park). orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::TIER_BASE makes every critical candidate outscore every high one. So a non-critical pin can never earn a park while any critical candidate is eligible, and one always is: in the 7 days to 2026-09-28, all 390 task_skipped events went to six critical tasks.

A pinned task whose footprint touches a contended file therefore dispatches only on a tick where every one of its files happens to be free of both holders and parks. Meanwhile, the files it needs free up one at a time and are taken by lower-tier scored candidates in the same tick. The pin fails exactly the class the scheduler PRD says pins exist for: plans/scheduler-dispatch-scoring-and-lock-layer-prd.md §C4 says "never top-scored — this is what the pin is for".

EVIDENCE (read-only; data/orchestrator/runs.db and .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, measured 2026-09-28)
- The scheduler ran 409 ticks in 7 days. Only 15 of them ended in select_pins.
- Pins 3500 (pinned 08-24), 3659 and 4856 (09-01), 5205 (09-19) and 5812 (09-23) went 5 to 35 days without a dispatch. 5205, 5812 and 4856 have never dispatched.
- Share of 09-21..09-28 during which each pin's FULL file set was free of other holders and foreign parks: 3500 0.00%, 3659 0.00%, 5205 0.07%, 5812 0.00%.
- Holds alone: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py was unheld 1.7% of the week, verify.py 2.7%. The unheld stretches of workflow.py and harness.py were covered by CRITICAL fairness parks owned by task 3542. 3542 is effective critical only because it inherits the boost of pinned task 3545. Those parks top-blocked pin 3659 for the whole week.
- 3500 and 3659 had to be landed by hand through merge carriers 6033 and 6024 on 2026-09-28.
- The starvation watchdog cannot see this class. Its dual gate needs skip >= 50, and pins have 0. The idle-only gate is 30 days on an in-memory clock (task 3821 owns the watchdog).

DECISIONS (made at filing; do not relitigate without new evidence)
D1 Scope — pins only. A pin reservation is granted only to a task that meets all of these:
- it is pinned in the override store;
- it passes ::Scheduler._eligible_for_dispatch;
- it is not in gated_ids;
- it is not deterministic;
- it failed try_acquire in _phase_select_pins this tick.
Non-pinned candidates keep today's rank-1-only fairness parks.

D2 Bound — only the head of the pin queue reserves. At most `pin_reservation_max_active` (default 1) tasks hold a pin reservation, namely the lowest-pin_order tasks that satisfy D1. This is the EASY-backfill head reservation, not the general below-rank-1 park installation that PRD §7 rejects. §7 measured harm from reserving for EVERY passed-over candidate: idle reservation x3.6-4.8, INV-3 gridlock of same-tier chains, and never-dispatched x1.5-3. A single operator-chosen reservation cannot gridlock with itself. Its idle cost is one task's footprint, and C7 backfill can still borrow through it. Say so in the code and docs: this is a bounded exception, not a reversal of §7.

D3 Rank — operator intent outranks automatic fairness. A pin reservation may install on a module whose active-top park is a FAIRNESS park of any tier, including critical. It installs by shadowing that park, never by destroying it. Without this the fix does nothing in exactly the observed case: critical fairness parks over the hot files (3542 historically, 5221 now). 1. set_task_status deferred FIRST (blocked → deferred was accepted).
2. update_task the description to the ruled scope.
3. resolve_issue with action='close_only', not 'resume' ('resume' would re-dispatch the task under the carry). The L1 member esc-5035-2 was cascade-dismissed ("l2-cascade").
4. Close the cockpit DecisionRecord.
No stranded-blocked refile loop followed. After the carry, deferred → done with found_on_main was accepted directly.
Carrier walk: submit_task(planning_mode) → add_dependency on the deferred real task → commit_planning → in-progress (claimant_run_id) → merge-deferred → remove_dependency. Then `git branch task/<carrier>` plus `git worktree add .worktrees/<carrier>`; this avoids `git worktree move` and its broken venv shebangs.
A queue row whose task already had a "Merge task/<id> into main" marker was a phantom. The solo carrier went straight to verifying on the laptop and landed in about 20 min. It was NOT flipped by the lane and had to be stamped merged by hand. The orchestrator had already reaped the real task's stale .worktrees/5035 and task/5035 branch by the time of cleanup.
target_text: ADDENDUM to the dark-factory carrier-task procedure for hand-carried merges from an interactive session (learned 2026-09-19, task 5668): the ORDER matters. Do NOT walk the carrier to `in-progress` before the work is done, and do NOT work in `.worktrees/<id>` on branch `task/<id>`. An `in-progress` task whose claimant_run_id is not a live orchestrator run is treated by the orchestrator's reconciler as a crashed run: within ~20 minutes it logged `[orchestrator.git_ops] Cleaned up worktree .../.worktrees/5668 and branch task/5668` and `[orchestrator.harness] Reconcile: reverted task 5668 to pending` — uncommitted work was deleted and the task became dispatchable to a factory agent. Correct sequence: file the carrier with submit_task(planning_mode=True) and LEAVE IT `deferred` for the whole working period; work in a worktree OUTSIDE `.worktrees/` (e.g. /home/leo/src/df-interactive-<slug>) on a NON-`task/` branch (interactive/<slug>); commit early; get the fresh-agent review; only when ready to submit do commit_planning → set in-progress (with claimant_run_id) → set merge-deferred back-to-back, THEN `git branch -m` to task/<id>, `git worktree move` into .worktrees/<id>, and merge_request. Related facts: `git worktree move` breaks the moved worktree's uv .venv (absolute paths) — harmless for submission because the merge lane verifies in its own _merge-* worktree, but run nothing from the moved tree; a merge commit's timestamp is when the lane BUILT the merge, not when main advanced — read the orchestrator log line `Task <id>: verify end (merge=<sha>, passed=True)` for the landing time (5668's merge commit said 19:32, main advanced at 20:00); an MCP-submitted carrier jumped from queue position 13 to the head because most older `queued` entries are ghost observability artefacts; if a carrier ever shows `pending` unexpectedly, set it `deferred` at once.

entry_text: Since task 4820, the repo-wide trailing-slash MCP URL guard (orchestrator/tests/test_mcp_post_transport.py::test_no_raw_post_builds_a_trailing_slash_mcp_url) has NO exclusion list. SWEEP_EXCLUSIONS is gone. To exempt a line that genuinely is not a fetched URL (an MCP config entry for a redirect-following client, or a display/log string), append `# mcp-url-sweep: allow <non-empty reason>` on the exact line the guard reports, which is the line where the slashed literal begins. In a multi-line call that is the literal's own line, not the call's first line. A bare or misspelled marker exempts nothing and is reported as MALFORMED. A marker on a line with no slashed URL, including the line above the hit, is reported STALE by test_every_sweep_allow_marker_earns_its_place. Markers are found as tokenize COMMENT tokens, so marker text inside a string or docstring does nothing. The policy lives in orchestrator/tests/_mcp_url_scan.py::sweep_source.
target_text: SUPERSEDES memory 8fb50fcf on marker placement (task 4820 amendment d915e0a383, 2026-10-01). Where a `# mcp-url-sweep: allow <reason>` marker may go has changed. It no longer has to sit on the exact line the guard reports. It exempts a hit when it sits on ANY line the flagged slashed-URL expression spans. The guard reports the line where the outermost expression ending in the slashed literal begins: for `base +\n '/mcp/'` that is the `base` line, and a marker on either line now works. A string running over several lines must take its marker after the closing quotes, because its reported line ends inside the string. Inside a multi-line call, only the literal's own lines count, so a marker on the call's opening line, or on the line directly above or below a hit, is still STALE. orchestrator/tests/_mcp_url_scan.py::sweep_source implements the policy from the (first_line, last_line) spans returned by _slashed_url_spans.

target_text:
Completed: Post-ZOT duplicate sweep: after a curator zero-output hang degrades dedupe to create, diff the tasks created in that window against the corpus and flag near-duplicates — the class has no live owner
Description: RULING (Leo, 2026-09-14, decision docket D5 option A; from reify esc-7459-1). Give the curator-ZOT duplicate class a live owner and a structural safeguard.

THE MECHANISM. When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout (subtype=error_empty_output, turns=0, sonnet + json-schema call shape), dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE: the caller sees a normal {status:"created"} with no signal that the dedupe check never ran. dark_factory 1743 (done, merged f8a612d8) shipped the defensive patch that stops one hung call wedging subsequent calls, and its predecessor 1550 is cancelled — so the class currently has NO live owner, and duplicates keep landing. NOTE: an earlier reify record claimed "task 1743 is unrelated GUI work"; that was a project-attribution error (reify 1743 is GUI; dark_factory 1743 is this) — cite "dark_factory 1743".

BASE RATE, five confirmed degrade windows: 2026-08-25 DUPLICATE (reify 6583 filed as a strict subset of pending 5436); 2026-09-11 DUPLICATE (reify 7416 vs 7383 at cosine 0.68, retitled SUPERSEDED and cancelled); 2026-09-12 21:07 clean (candidate resolved to exactly one task, 7480); 2026-09-13 00:56 clean (7490); 2026-09-14 01:42 clean (7517). Two of five produce duplicates; the three clean windows were each verified by search_tasks during the reify L2 watch, not assumed. Manual discipline ("search_tasks before AND after filing", procedural memory 377a4ad6) has already failed twice.

WORK. On each curator ZOT event (the circuit-breaker/escalator already files a curator_zero_output_hang escalation with the candidate title and timestamp), run a sweep: for every task created in the project within +/- N minutes of the hang, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the task itself, and if a near-duplicate scores above the curator's combine threshold, either (a) auto-file a curator ticket proposing the combine, or (b) at minimum stamp the escalation and the new task's metadata with the candidate duplicate id and score so a human sees it in the L2 record rather than discovering it later. Prefer (a) if the combine path is already idempotent. Do not delete or cancel automatically.

VERIFY. A test that simulates a ZOT (mock the LLM call to return empty output), files a candidate whose near-duplicate exists, and asserts the sweep flags the pair. Plus a control where no near-duplicate exists and nothing is flagged.
Analysis: GOAL (Leo ruling, docket D5 option A). When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout, dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE and the caller sees a normal {status:"created"}. Two of five confirmed degrade windows produced a real duplicate. Give the class a live owner: on each ZOT degrade, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the new task, and if a near-duplicate scores above a flagging threshold, stamp the new task's metadata AND file an operator-visible escalation. Never delete, cancel, or auto-combine.

entry_text: reify scheduler throughput, measured 2026-09-30 from fused-memory get_scheduler_events (scheduler_tick events): the median tick takes 272-340 s on every day from 2026-09-20 to 09-30, with a max of about 1890 s. The landed_outbox_gate phase is about 98% of each tick. Cause: dark-factory Scheduler._consult_landed_outbox calls harness._landed_dispatch_gate -> reconcile_landed_task SEQUENTIALLY for every candidate (about 935), at roughly 0.3 s each. acquire_next dispatches at most one task per tick, so reify dispatch is capped at roughly 8-11 tasks per hour. That cap is what produces 'dispatch-eligible ~3d, never top-scored (skip_count=0)' starvation-watchdog L2s, even for high-priority tasks with no deps and no lock contention. Owner: dark-factory #4900 'Scheduler tick residuals' (pending, medium); its premise that 8.2 dispatches/h is enough looks thin at this backlog. Triage such starvation L2s by tick phases, then close_only, with no priority overrides or pins.

entry_text: Option pattern-spelling facts measured 2026-09-29 (esc-6020-11 investigation, target/debug/reify 09-25 build): `some(v) =>` and `Some(v) =>` are PARSE ERRORS because tree-sitter match_pattern has no call-shaped production — NOT because some/none are keywords; grammar.js declares no `word:` rule, so tree-sitter reserves nothing and `some =>`, `none =>`, `Some =>`, `None =>`, `some { value: v } =>`, and the typo `Sme { value: v } =>` all parse and all evaluate to undef today. The GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar ~:1862) DOES @specialize some/none as ReservedWord, so `none =>` and `some { value: v }` produce error nodes in the editor; the ratified `Some { value: v }` / `None` spelling parses in BOTH grammars. The spec is internally inconsistent: §2.10 lists some/none as keywords (false for tree-sitter; `let none = 3mm` parses, though a later `none` still resolves to the Option value while `some` resolves to the let); §5.10 and §9.2.8 show `some(c) =>` and nested `some(some(x)) =>`; §15's BNF has a flat `'some' '(' IDENT ')' | 'none'` pattern production contradicting both; §3.8 says "not an enum". Nested patterns are impossible under every route (field_binding binders are bare identifiers, DCE §10). Tracked .ri corpus: ONE Option match site (tests/prd-gate/fixtures/parse_length_match_resolves.ri) vs 83 construction sites (13 `some(`, 70 `none`) in 27 files. Display already diverges: CLI prints `None`/`Some(..)`, LSP hover prints `none`/`some(..)`. All of these rewrites are #6020's docs-truth rider; the lowercase-arm ratchet flips at #6017.
target_text: Reify Option<T> gotcha (measured task 6047, 2026-08-06): `match` cannot read an Option payload in EITHER form, and one failure mode is silent. `match o { some(v) => ..., none => ... }` is a PARSE ERROR (the tree-sitter `match_pattern` production has no positional form — only variant_binding_pattern | identifier ('|' identifier)* | '_'). Binder-less `match o { some => A, none => B }` COMPILES CLEAN with zero Error and zero eval-phase diagnostics and evaluates to `undef` — for a some(x) subject just as much as for a none subject — because Option is intrinsic (Value::Option) not a Value::Enum, and eval's match-arm selection fires only on Value::Enum (gated in reify-expr/src/lib.rs:635, with an Undef catch-all at :663-670). So `reify check` reporting "All constraints satisfied" does NOT mean an Option match works; you must `reify eval` and look at the cell value. The working surface is the prelude recovery combinators (no import): unwrap_or/or_default/fallback, or_else, is_some/is_none, map_or, ok_or — declared in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/option_recovery.ri (ok_or in stdlib/result.ri), with real semantics only in the Rust intercept crates/reify-expr/src/option_recovery.rs (the .ri bodies are typecheck-only placeholders that return WRONG values). `map_or(o, dflt, |x: T| ...)` is the ONLY combinator that binds the payload to a name, so it is the replacement for a `some(c) => ...` arm. Contrast: Result<T,E> IS a real prelude enum whose Ok { value: v } / Err { error: e } named-field patterns match normally. The gap is a deliberate open design fork — docs/prds/v0_6/data-carrying-enums.md §10 and fork F4 ("Recommend Leo decide").

Task 'Coalesce-train derail strands absorbed members in merge-deferred (no re-drive to solo merge)' completed. When the retroactive merge-queue coalescing pass absorbs >=2 waiting single MergeRequests into a `coalesce-*` GroupMergeRequest and that train then DERAILS, the absorbed member tasks are orphaned permanently in `merge-deferred`. Completed, reviewed work never lands and no escalation fires.

CONSUMER: orchestrator merge worker / merger loop (`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py`).

MECHANISM (root cause):
- `_maybe_coalesce_waiting_singles` (merge_queue.py ~6552) resolves each absorbed single's ORIGINAL future as `superseded` (~6783-6787), so each workflow parks at `merge-deferred` via `workflow._handle_superseded` and EXITS.
- Members are flipped to `done` ONLY by `req.mark_member_done`, which runs ONLY on the train SUCCESS path (merge_queue.py ~4211-4248).
- On derail there is no awaiter and no re-drive: the GroupMergeRequest's future is created inside the coalescing pass (~6748) and, unlike a DECLARED train (whose tip member's workflow awaits and re-fires via `_maybe_enqueue_group_merge`), is never awaited by any workflow. The cas_failed comment "workflow re-parks the train" (merge_queue.py ~4129) encodes a false assumption for coalesced trains.
- The one-strike registry `_mark_coalesce_derailed` (~6510, called at ~6995-6999) only EXCLUDES members from the NEXT coalescing pass; it does not re-enqueue them. It is also in-memory and wiped on orchestrator restart.
- `merge-deferred` is deliberately excluded from the stranded-task reconciliation sweep (`_RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES` + the harness.py ~2024 early-return guard, PRD orchestrator-atomic-train-merge §9.8) to protect declared-train worktrees, so the self-healing safety net cannot catch these. Result: permanent silent strand, no live workflow / no queue entry / no escalation.

DERAIL PATHS that must all route through the new re-drive:
1. advance_main cas_failed -> merge_queue.py ~4128-4138 (returns `blocked`).
2. post-merge equivalence/pyright gate fail -> ~4189-4199 (returns non-done; "no member flips").
3. all-members-merge-deferred status pre-check rejects before any git work -> ~3980-4004 (member not merge-deferred, e.g. a sibling raced to in-progress).

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR (G2 user-observable signal): when a `coalesce-`prefixed GroupMergeRequest reaches any terminal NON-`done` outcome, each absorbed member that is still `merge-deferred` must be re-driven to an INDIVIDUAL solo merge — re-enqueued as a fresh per-member MergeRequest (preserving its own branch/worktree) OR flipped back to a dispatchable status so the scheduler re-runs its merge. After a simulated coalesce-derail in a fixture, assert NO absorbed member remains `merge-deferred` with no live request/workflow: each reaches `done` (solo merge) or is re-dispatched (pending/in-progress).

GUARD — double-landing: a member whose branch tip is already an ancestor of main (a partner's successful merge brought it in) must NOT be re-merged; detect via is_ancestor and flip straight to `done` with `found_on_main` provenance.

FIX SITE: the derail branch in `_merger_loop` at merge_queue.py ~6995-6999 (extend beyond `_mark_coalesce_derailed`); ensure the pre-check-rejection path (~3980-4004) also reaches it.

EVIDENCE: reify 3577+4721 (coalesce-3577-6247469e, advance_main cas_failed after ~1h post-merge verify) and 3427 (coalesce-3427-f9b6c210, rejected: member 4271 in-progress) stranded ~19h in merge-deferred on 2026-06-22, empty queue, no escalation. Found via /deb 2026-06-23. Same shape as the park-stack and degenerate-branch strand fixes: a non-terminal parked state whose only advancer dies, with the recovery sweep deliberately told to skip it — so the fix must restore a recovery edge, not weaken the sweep exclusion.

Also: GitOps.advance_main checks `merge-base --is-ancestor main <merge>` before update-ref, so a drift committed just BEFORE advance_main yields rebased_pending_reverify, never cas_failed. For a REAL cas_failed, commit the drift inside a wrapped merge_to_main (the merge is built on the drift while expected_main is stale); to land a second drift before the loop re-reads main, wrap advance_main and commit after the first real call returns. target_text:
Completed: Train landing path: any move of main under a train verify (e.g. a direct docs commit) derails the train and can strand its members until manual rescue; retry the CAS via reverify_on_rebase instead
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (interactive session, re-read of current code + runs.db). The original 2026-09-03 description claimed a moved main makes the train land an UNVERIFIED re-merged tip. That cannot happen, and the real defect is the inverse: the train DERAILS and discards its verify. The fix direction (option (a) below) is unchanged.

=== MECHANISM (verified in code) ===
`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::_do_train_merge` reads `main_sha = await git_ops.get_main_sha()` BEFORE the train verify and passes it as `expected_main=main_sha` to `_journal_landed_then_advance` WITHOUT `reverify_on_rebase=True`. If main moved during the verify, `git_ops.py::GitOps.advance_main`'s attempt loop rebases/re-merges the tip onto the new main (`rebased = True`), skips the "Reverify-on-rebase gate" (flag unset), and reaches `git update-ref refs/heads/main <rebased> <expected_main>`. `expected_main` is the stale pre-verify value, so the CAS is certain to fail → `AdvanceOutcome('cas_failed')` → `_do_train_merge` emits `train_derailed` ('Train merge advance failed: cas_failed') and returns blocked; members are re-driven as singles. The rebased sha can never land, so there is NO unverified-landing hole. The task-2154 "Correctness (amendment)" comment after the advance call ("can transparently rebase merge_commit onto a moved main and land the REBASED sha directly") describes an unreachable path whenever expected_main is passed, and it always is here. The `_await_unadvanced_predecessor` docstring states the correct behaviour ("For a TRAIN it is terminal").

Contrast: the single-branch site (`SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight`) passes `reverify_on_rebase=True`, gets `rebased_pending_reverify`, runs `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` (disjoint delta → advance with no re-verify; overlap → re-verify), re-anchors base_sha, and retries the CAS. A direct docs commit during a solo verify is therefore absorbed in ~2 min (measured 09-18, task 5578); during a train verify it costs the whole train.

=== MEASURED COST (runs.db `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, read-only, 2026-09-23) ===
train_merged 37, train_derailed 29 all-time; 5 derails are `cas_failed`: coalesce-3215 (07-31, 27 min verify lost), 3146 (07-31, 27 min), 4097 (08-16, 29 min), 4545 (09-06, 53 min), 4574 (09-16, 72 min; the mover was a direct docs commit 4 s after the train read main). Each also re-drives every member solo, and 4574's derail re-pended the tip with a stacked branch carrying the other member's commits (see memory feedback-a-lost-cas-train-derail-repends-the-tip-with-a-stacked-branch). Operational side-effect: interactive sessions are now deferring direct-to-main docs commits whenever the queue is live, because the train case is not separable from the harmless solo case.

=== FIX ===
INVARIANT (unchanged): a train never advances main to a tree no gate verified. NEW GOAL: a moved main does not discard a green train verify when the intervening delta cannot interact with the train.
Pass `reverify_on_rebase=True` at the train site and handle `'rebased_pending_reverify'` with a bounded CAS loop mirroring the single-branch one (re-read main, MAX_CAS_RETRIES). Route through `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` with the train's merge worktree; the branch-touched set MUST be the UNION of all members' diffs against the merge-base (a single member's diff is not the train's footprint): disjoint → advance the rebased sha without re-verify, overlap → re-run the post-merge verify on the rebased tip. Re-record the LandedOutbox row with the landed sha (the 2154 block becomes reachable and correct). Rewrite "DEFENSIBLE DELTAS" item 1 and the 2154 comment to state the real policy. Keep the happy path (main unmoved → one verify, one advance) byte-identic…[truncated, 15294 chars total]

entry_text: reify persistent FEA cache key composition (verified main 93b5d91a0d, task 7981): engine_eval.rs `persistent_cache_key` = compute_cache_key(node) combined with each evaluated argument Value's content_hash, so argument-value changes re-key. Realization inputs are keyed by RECIPE only (graph.rs RealizationNodeData.content_hash = id_hash ⊕ ops_hash), so a change in realization-producer code (OCCT/OpenVDB/gmsh output, native libs) never reaches the key. The shell-extract upstream node (engine_eval.rs ~:10029) uses bare compute_cache_key on an input-less node, so its key is the target string alone. Code running inside a persisted dispatch must therefore be covered by ENGINE_VERSION_HASH.
target_text: FEA compute-node cache key (reify-eval): `compute_cache_key` composes combine_all([target, value_bucket, realization_bucket, options_hash]). For the `solver::elastic_static` node, the per-call `ElasticOptions(...)` literal does NOT participate in the cache key: (1) `options_hash` is hardcoded `ContentHash(0)` (the `ElasticOptions::cacheable_hash` producer is deferred to P3.4), and (2) the γ-slice lowering in engine_eval.rs only adds direct `ValueRef` args to `value_inputs`, so a struct-literal arg contributes no value-cell hash. Consequence: neither `deterministic` nor `shell_force` currently affects cache hits — a deterministic:true request can be served a cached parallel result, so bit-stability holds only for a fresh/cold-cache solve. `compute_cache_key`'s exclusion contract intentionally requires execution-profile flags (threads/deterministic) to be filtered out of options_hash by the upstream producer.

Completed: Implement scripts/await-merge-landing.py — Monitor-based merge-landing waiter that self-re-arms before the 600s timeout_ms cap
Description: Task 7907 ([legibility census] Background Bash wait command for async merge-status polling is killed, then replacement Monitor watch needs repeated manual re-arms for the same event) was CANCELLED 2026-09-27T07:30:36Z as part of a bulk sweep of ~32 similarly-named "[legibility census]" tasks (7897-7942 range, metadata.source=legibility_census), despite carrying concrete implementation deliverables in metadata.files (scripts/await-merge-landing.py, tests/infra/test_await_merge_landing.py, tests/infra/test_await_merge_landing.sh, tests/infra/run-all-classification.manifest, CLAUDE.md) rather than being a pure documentation/census entry like its sibling tasks. Confirmed via Glob against the current reify tree: none of those deliverable files exist — the fix was never implemented, only observed and documented.

The underlying gotcha is real and recurring (sightings 2026-07-20, 2026-07-24, 2026-07-25, and again 2026-09-27 per mem0 memory 92c4a479-120b-488f-8e67-1fe39cb36901): a `run_in_background` Bash wait for an async merge-status/merge-landing event gets killed by the host's background-process sweep, and the correct replacement — the Monitor tool — has a hard `timeout_ms` cap of 600000ms (10 min) with NO `persistent` parameter (that parameter and 30-60 min timeouts existed only in earlier harness builds per stale 2026-07/08 memories). So a merge-landing wait longer than 10 minutes today requires the caller to manually re-arm Monitor with the identical watch command every time it times out — task/7182's merge needed 3 manual re-arm rounds for one event and 2 for another in the sighting that generated task 7907.

Implement scripts/await-merge-landing.py: a Monitor-based (or equivalent poll-loop-based) waiter for merge-landing / merge-status events that automatically re-arms itself before hitting the 600000ms timeout_ms cap, so a caller can issue one wait call and receive the terminal LANDED/FAILED/BLOCKED signal without manual re-arm rounds. Ground the poll on git ancestry (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> origin/main`) plus a `merge_status` call per re-arm to catch terminal states git ancestry can't see (blocked/conflict) — this mirrors the existing manual procedure already in memory (procedural_knowledge 81c30003-ab1a-4177-980a-0346c66c6522). Add tests/infra/test_await_merge_landing.sh (or .py, per the bash-to-Python migration policy in docs/notes/infra-test-bash-to-python-migration-policy.md) covering the re-arm-before-cap behavior, and document the script in CLAUDE.md alongside the existing Monitor/background-bash gotcha guidance.

This is ordinary task-planning follow-through on a Stage 1 reconciliation finding (c1dc5ff5-e476-425d-9d42-e2820f5f2be8), not a human-decision gate: the bulk cancellation swept census/documentation entries correctly but incidentally dropped this one's still-untracked implementation work.

- reify's CLAUDE.md has NO Monitor / run_in_background guidance (grep -i 'monitor|background' CLAUDE.md → 0 matches). The "existing guidance" the task refers to lives only in mem0 (92c4a479, 81c30003). The doc therefore lands as a new Landing-on-main bullet plus a Pointers-table row; precedent is 5b61a4a19c (cargo-test-tally.py's row, task 7896).
- merge_status IS callable from a stdlib script. Completed: Make REIFY_VITE_PORT user-facing: reify-gui devUrl is baked to :1420 at compile time, forcing e2e smokes to serialise across lanes
Description: Follow-up from task #7254 (amendment pass, reviewer_comprehensive suggestion 5 "robustness"). Out of scope there: #7254 held locks only for the two launcher scripts, their test, docs/debug-mcp-recipe.md, CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/reify-design/SKILL.md — the fix needs the GUI side (gui/src-tauri).

OBSERVED (measured in lane _lane-54, 2026-09-04): neither gui/test/visual/run.ts nor gui/test/visual/lib_e2e_smoke.sh mentions REIFY_VITE_PORT or 1420 anywhere (grep: zero matches in both files), so both take scripts/run-gui-dev.sh's :1420 default. Task #7254 added a vite-port preflight that refuses (exit 1, before any build) when something already answers on that port. Consequence: two warm lanes running the e2e smoke concurrently now have the second fail fast, where it previously attached to the FIRST lane's vite and asserted against another worktree's build. The refusal is correct; the new cross-lane serialisation constraint is the cost.

REIFY_VITE_PORT is not a workaround today and scripts/run-gui-dev.sh documents it as a TEST-ONLY KNOB: gui/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json pins "devUrl": "http://localhost:1420", which tauri bakes into reify-gui at COMPILE time, and nothing under gui/src-tauri/src/ reads REIFY_VITE_PORT. So overriding it moves OUR vite off :1420 while reify-gui still loads :1420 — i.e. the foreign listener that prompted the override — and the launcher reports success anyway. REIFY_GUI_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1 bypasses the check but restores that silent-wrong-vite attach, so it is not a fix either.

Work: supply the GUI-side half so REIFY_VITE_PORT can become user-facing — either a build-time devUrl override via TAURI_CONFIG, or read the env var in the Rust shell at startup. Then drop the "TEST-ONLY KNOB" warning in scripts/run-gui-dev.sh, let gui/test/visual/run.ts and lib_e2e_smoke.sh allocate a free port per run (scripts/lib_portable.sh's allocate_free_port), and remove the serialisation caveat added to docs/debug-mcp-recipe.md section 2.

Files: gui/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, gui/src-tauri/src/main.rs, scripts/run-gui-dev.sh, gui/test/visual/run.ts, gui/test/visual/lib_e2e_smoke.sh, docs/debug-mcp-recipe.md.

- scripts/run-gui-dev.sh:103-117 documents REIFY_VITE_PORT as a TEST-ONLY KNOB, defaults it to 1420 but never EXPORTS it; its occupied-port preflight (§1b, :150-173) deliberately offers only "free the port".

The config comes from the Context, which exposes `config_mut()` (lib.rs:411). target_text: Reify warm lanes: scripts/run-gui-dev.sh — the default launcher for every gui/test/visual/run_*_e2e_smoke.sh — is unusable whenever ANY process on the host holds vite's :1420, because reify-gui's devUrl is baked to http://localhost:1420 at COMPILE time (documented at run-gui-dev.sh:103-117), so REIFY_VITE_PORT relocates only vite and the GUI still loads the foreign listener; the script preflight-refuses. Seen 2026-09-10 with a long-lived personal dogfood session holding it, which made the smoke runners unrunnable in every lane at once. WORKAROUND that works and skips vite entirely: build the frontend dist (`npm --prefix gui run build`) and `cargo build -p reify-gui --bin reify-gui --features gui --release` ONCE, then drive lib_e2e_smoke.sh's e2e_smoke_run with REIFY_SMOKE_SKIP_PREBUILD=1 and REIFY_SMOKE_LAUNCHER pointed at a 4-line script that does `cd <worktree>; source scripts/lib_gui_launch.sh; gui_launch_env_pin; exec target/release/reify-gui "$1"`. REIFY_DEBUG=1/REIFY_DEBUG_PORT pass through to the release binary (main.rs:886 reads the env var), so the debug MCP listener comes up normally. Do NOT point REIFY_SMOKE_LAUNCHER at scripts/run-gui.sh directly: it re-runs `npm run build` on every launch, which rewrites gui/dist, invalidates the tauri build script and triggers a full reify-gui relink inside the readiness window.

entry_text: In orchestrator verify.py, the isolated-rerun discriminator's two call sites have OPPOSITE fail-safe directions. At merge_gate, passes_in_isolation LANDS the tree, so refusing (unconfirmable) is safe. At main_probe, passes_in_isolation only downgrades verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main to (False, '') (task-own red), and every other verdict keeps (True, main_sha), i.e. 'main is broken'. So a new refusal precondition must be scoped per site with a _RerunPolicy field, never added site-blind (task 5492 review round 1).
target_text: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py now carries a FAMILY of isolated-re-run gates that all share the same primitives (_extract_failing_test_ids, _group_node_ids_by_subproject, _scope_to_keyword -> _serial_pytest_str -> _with_pytest_timeout_str, a per-gate 300s timeout constant) but differ in fail-safe POLARITY, which is the thing to get right when adding another: confirm_main_tip_failure_is_real (task 2370) fails safe to True=file-the-alarm; _sweep_failure_reproduces_in_isolation (task 3095) is a COST pre-filter that is never a verdict and fails safe to None; confirm_merge_verify_flake_suppressible (task 3290) fails CLOSED to None=merge-stays-red; and task 3597's main-probe gate inside verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main fails safe by KEEPING today's (True, main_sha) preexisting verdict. In every case the degraded path lands on the pre-existing behaviour — the polarity flips because the surrounding verdict's meaning flips, not because the gates disagree.

Completed: Verify scopes: pass a per-role cgroup CPUWeight at the systemd-run --scope spawn (merge 100 / task 33 / background 10) so nice tiers are not defeated across cgroups
Description: PROBLEM (measured 2026-09-07/08, load-tuning session, Leo). cgroup v2 schedules in two layers: `nice` orders threads INSIDE one cgroup; BETWEEN sibling cgroups the kernel shares CPU by `cpu.weight`, and nice has no effect on that split. verify.py::_run_cmd launches a verify inside a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` (its own cgroup) when `verify_use_cgroup_scope` is true, for kill-by-cgroup on timeout. Every such scope is created at the default CPUWeight 100, the same as `orchestrator-dark-factory.service` as a whole (every agent plus every non-scoped verify). Measured per-cgroup cpu.stat over 20s under contention: df unit 8.9 cores, reify task-role verify scope 7.9, reify merge-role verify scope 7.6, i.e. an equal three-way split. The task-role scope carried `nice -n 15 ionice -c2 -n7` from shared/verify_admission.py::_NICE_TIERS and yielded NOTHING to the merge scope or to the df unit, because nice is per-cgroup. Inside the df unit the tiers DO work (merge xdist at nice 5 got 5.2 cores, task xdist at nice 15 got 2.2, background at nice 19 got 0). So the role tiering is correct in-unit and inert across scopes.

CHANGE. At the `systemd-run` argv build in verify.py::_run_cmd (the branch guarded by `use_cgroup_scope and shutil.which('systemd-run')`), add `-p CPUWeight=<w>` where w is resolved by role next to the nice prefix (verify.py::_resolve_nice_prefix is called with `role` at the two call sites; thread the weight the same way, e.g. a new optional `cpu_weight: int | None` on the spawn spec that carries `use_cgroup_scope`/`scope_tag`, None = omit the property = today's behaviour). Config: three int knobs on OrchestratorConfig, `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_merge` (default 100), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_task` (default 33), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_background` (default 10), validated 1..10000 (cgroup v2 cpu.weight range); add them to RELOADABLE_FIELDS beside `verify_admission_nice_*` (read at spawn, so green-tier is honest) and to the green list in OPERATIONS.md section "Config reload vs restart". `offline` and unknown roles get no property.

WHY THESE NUMBERS. Lower task/background rather than raise merge: reify's own cpu_governance convention is task 100 / merge 300, but a 300 merge scope would also put interactive shells (weight-100 siblings under app.slice) at a quarter share under contention. Merge at 100 keeps the merge leg at parity with each orchestrator unit and with the operator's terminals; 33 and 10 reproduce the 3:1 merge:task ratio and the nice-19 background intent. Under contention with the df unit + one reify merge scope + one reify task scope the split moves from 33/33/33 to 43/43/14. Weights are work-conserving: a lone scope still gets the whole box, so nothing slows on an idle host.

PROVEN ON THIS HOST 2026-09-08: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p CPUWeight=33 -- sh -c '...cat cpu.weight'` printed cpu.weight=33 (the cpu controller is delegated through user@1000.service/app.slice; every unit and scope currently reads 100).

ALSO IN PASSING (own-prose rule): the verify.py docstring near `_wrap_governed` that says "The live reify deployment currently sets verify_use_cgroup_scope=False" is stale, reify's yaml line ~112 has it true; correct it.

TESTS. Extend whichever test pins the systemd-run argv for the scope path (orchestrator/tests/test_harness_verify_scope_reaper.py is the likely home; grep '--collect') to assert `-p CPUWeight=<w>` appears for each role with the defaults and is ABSENT when the knob is None/role is offline; a config test for the 1..10000 validation and RELOADABLE_FIELDS membership (mirror orchestrator/tests/test_config_verify_admission_reload.py). Do not touch shared/verify_admission.py's nice tiers: the nice prefix stays, it is what orders threads inside the scope.

entry_text: 2026-09-29 diagnosis: why reify's second merge-verify host leo-laptop sits mostly idle. The laptop only takes overflow merge-queue verifies. HostAllocator.acquire (verify_runner.py) prefers local, so the laptop never verifies the head; all 80 laptop verifies since 08-01 were depth-1 speculative. K = 1 + runners = 2, and a host lease is released only in _finalize_inflight (merge_queue.py), which runs in submission order behind the head. So the laptop finishes in ~22 min, then holds a dead lease until the local head verify lands (~75 min, since the contended workstation is 3.4x slower). That caps laptop utilization at ~30% even with a deep queue. Measured 09-27T07Z to 09-29T16Z from reify runs.db heartbeats: laptop ~11% verifying, ~30% leased but finished, ~43% free while local verified a lone item (queue depth >=2 in ~60% of those, consistent with task 4929's missing host-free wakeup), ~15% both idle. Outages: 09-12 to 09-24 benched on every dispatch (uv not on PATH, fixed cf6184cfe3); 09-25T14:49Z to 09-27T06:57Z quarantined because the laptop was suspended for 41h. Owners: 4929 (wakeup, pending behind 5036), 5205 (local verify contention), 4540 (dark_factory never uses the laptop; pending on 4537).

entry_text: Reify language spec (docs/reify-language-spec.md, `where` section ~lines 1603-1621) rules that `where` blocks nest with guards composing CONJUNCTIVELY and that `else` members desugar to `where !condition`. So an else branch nested under an INACTIVE outer guard is inactive. The engine currently activates it (with on=false, Inner.ge=0.009 m) - a spec violation found by task #5935's architect (esc-5935-11). The watcher applied the spec rather than escalating: filed #7997 to fix the top-level guard composition (RED test first) and told #5935 not to mirror the bug in its new guarded-member construction paths.
target_text: Reify compiler member-shape bug confirmed at main 8f6b36cd18 (the RED for task 5424 / PRD uniform-member-access task α): a PUBLIC `param` declared inside a `where { }` guarded group is falsely denied — `let i = Inner(); i.g` emits `error: structure 'Inner' has no member 'g'` even though Inner declares `g` — while its `priv` twin IS correctly recognised as E_PRIV_MEMBER_ACCESS. Cause: template_has_member (crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs:214-218 = value_cells union ports union sub_components) does not scan guarded_groups, whereas template_member_is_priv (:234-251) does. Divergent coverage between these two lockstep predicates is the C1-iv / INV-5 no-lockstep-duplication hazard; task 5424 collapses both into one member_path::resolve_hop authority.

entry_text:
How the old merge-lane module paths stay importable after task 5036: each old file (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py etc.) does `from orchestrator.merge_lane import X`, `from orchestrator.merge_lane.X import *  # noqa: F403`, optionally `def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any: ...`, then `sys.modules[__name__] = X`.
- That keeps ONE module object, so `import`, `patch('orchestrator.merge_queue.Y')`, `patch.object(mq, ...)` and the worker's own global lookups all hit the same binding.
- Pyright keeps public names typed through the star import.
- A `__getattr__` stub makes pyright accept ANY name through that path. So the stub is kept only on the 10 aliases through which external code imports private names. orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_alias_names.py is the runtime backstop: every name reached through an alias, or imported from the façade, must exist.
- Do not put the stub under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. complexipy scores a module-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` as cognitive 1 per file, which would raise the cluster total.
target_text: MQ-refactor extraction pattern (tasks α/β/γ, merge_queue.py split): each extraction (1) creates a new orchestrator/merge_*.py with symbols moved verbatim, module logger set to logging.getLogger('orchestrator.merge_queue') (NOT the new module name, so caplog assertions keep working), and NO top-level import of merge_queue (would deadlock the shim); (2) merge_queue.py re-exports every moved name via `from orchestrator.merge_X import (...)  # noqa: F401 re-export shim`; (3) any moved function that calls a symbol the test suite monkeypatches via the string path `orchestrator.merge_queue.<name>` (co-moved sibling, staying engine function, OR bare module-level constant) must resolve it through a function-local deferred `import orchestrator.merge_queue` reach-back, NOT a direct intra-module reference. TDD steps: S1 RED module-existence+logger-name, S2 GREEN expand new module (copies coexist), S3 RED reach-back routing (patch both namespaces with contrasting values), S4 GREEN apply reach-backs, S5 RED shim-identity (getattr(mq,n) is getattr(newmod,n)), S6 GREEN delete copies + add shim import, S7 docs two-layer-model.md §7 map.

entry_text: A new STORE-WRITING escalation MCP tool (any verb that mutates a record, e.g. amend_escalation, declare_pin) also belongs in scripts/sitting/nightly_prepare.py::NIGHTLY_DENIED_TOOLS and in scripts/tests/test_sitting_nightly_prepare.py::APPLY_VERBS. That module's docstring claims the deny list names "every apply verb". No test enumerates the live tool surface against it, so a missed entry is caught only by review. Runtime safety does not depend on it, because the --permission-mode dontAsk allowlist already denies anything unlisted. This is the third registration site, after test_stages.py's _REVIEWED_STAGE_SAFE / DISALLOW_ESCALATION_READS classification.
target_text: GOTCHA for anyone adding a tool to escalation/src/escalation/server.py (verified task 3023 step-15, 2026-07-30): `create_server` backs BOTH escalation servers — the orchestrator's (data/escalations, port 8102) and the reconciliation harness's (data/reconciliation/escalations, port 8103). Recon Stage 1/2/3 agents are gated by a DENY list only (DISALLOW_ESCALATION_READS in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/cli_stage_runner.py), so every NEW tool you register ships visible and callable from all three stages by default, pointed at the RECON queue. That is how `get_task_escalations` briefly reached the stages carrying a docstring stating an empty result IS evidence of absence — re-arming the exact false positive task 3023 exists to kill. If that test fails after you add a tool, do not widen the inventory reflexively — classify it: anything that answers an existence/absence question about ORCHESTRATOR state must be denied, not blessed.

entry_text: RECIPE: deciding whether a `deferred` task with no flip trigger was retired by a task-COMBINING pass (every known pass concatenates member descriptions into the combiner). (1) Check higher-numbered tasks' metadata for x_coalesced_from / x_e3_replacement / supersedes / curator_action=combine naming the member id, and for dependency edges remapped off the member. (2) Deterministic text check: fraction of the member's 8-word shingles (title+description) found verbatim in each candidate's title+description+details; a true combiner scores ~0.7 on s8 even after amendment, noise is <0.03. Also a sentence-level check (≥1 verbatim 6-word window per member sentence) shows what was dropped or compressed. (3) Judge residue: a combiner may compress dated provenance paragraphs into 're-measure' wording — scope preserved, prose not. Coverage: the full population is reachable — get_tasks paged at page_size=200 via the fused-memory HTTP MCP client fetched all 8008 reify tasks (ids 1–8047) in one sub-agent run (~11 min); search_tasks limit=100 is only a shortlist and must be labelled as such.
