entry_text: Gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, GNU bash 5.2.21 on the dark-factory host): `bash -c 'a && b && sleep N'` execs the FINAL command of an && list in place, so `sleep N` runs as the bash pid itself, not as a child. A sleeper_spec-style test build therefore ends up as ONE process (a direct child of the verify-merge leader, leading its own session under start_new_session), not bash->sleep. Account for this when reasoning about which pid a /proc descendant walk or a pid file names.
target_text: To drive the REAL dispatch↔verify-merge CLI seam in orchestrator tests WITHOUT a 1-2h reify build: the spawned `orchestrator verify-merge` ultimately runs each module's test_command via verify.py `_run_cmd` → `create_subprocess_shell(cmd, executable='/bin/bash', start_new_session=True)` (verify.py:2185). So a crafted MergeVerifySpec whose test_command spawns a `sleep` grandchild faithfully reproduces the cargo/rustc session-escape that the stdin-watchdog (verify_cancel.fire_watchdog_kill) and cancel-verify (verify_cancel.cancel_request) must tree-kill. Observe the real subtree with verify_cancel.read_ppid_map/collect_descendants (the same funcs the production kill paths use). CLI entrypoint is the `orchestrator` console script (orchestrator.cli:main). Real EscalationQueue(tmp_path) (escalation/src/escalation/queue.py:134) drives the β born-at-L2 consumer.

Hand-carry mechanics that worked 2026-10-04 for a BLOCKED task under an open L2 (task 5035, esc-5035-3), where Leo's ruling re-scoped the task and assigned it to the interactive session:
1. set_task_status deferred FIRST (blocked → deferred was accepted).
2. update_task the description to the ruled scope.
3. resolve_issue with action='close_only', not 'resume' ('resume' would re-dispatch the task under the carry). The L1 member esc-5035-2 was cascade-dismissed ("l2-cascade").
4. Close the cockpit DecisionRecord.
No stranded-blocked refile loop followed. After the carry, deferred → done with found_on_main was accepted directly.
Carrier walk: submit_task(planning_mode) → add_dependency on the deferred real task → commit_planning → in-progress (claimant_run_id) → merge-deferred → remove_dependency. Then `git branch task/<carrier>` plus `git worktree add .worktrees/<carrier>`; this avoids `git worktree move` and its broken venv shebangs.
A queue row whose task already had a "Merge task/<id> into main" marker was a phantom. The solo carrier went straight to verifying on the laptop and landed in about 20 min. It was NOT flipped by the lane and had to be stamped merged by hand. The orchestrator had already reaped the real task's stale .worktrees/5035 and task/5035 branch by the time of cleanup.
target_text: resolve_issue(action='close_only') on the L2 that pins a BLOCKED task is not status-neutral in practice. On /unblock 5140 (2026-09-27 06:46Z), closing esc-5140-9 released the hold, and about 18s later set_task_status(done) reported oldStatus='pending', not 'blocked'. The scheduler could in principle have re-dispatched the task in that window; nothing did, and no runs.db events appeared. When the work already landed through a CARRIER (so the task's own branch is not an ancestor of main and the reconciler's automatic blocked->done flip does not fire), stamp done IMMEDIATELY after the close, in back-to-back calls.

entry_text: Rust gotcha in reify (task #6999): an io::Error built with io::Error::other(bincode_err), e.g. by CacheEntryHeader::read_from in crates/reify-eval/src/persistent_cache.rs, always has kind() == ErrorKind::Other. Its real UnexpectedEof is nested inside the boxed bincode::ErrorKind::Io, so a `matches!(e.kind(), UnexpectedEof | InvalidData)` guard on that error can never match. To classify it, downcast via e.get_ref().and_then(|s| s.downcast_ref::<bincode::ErrorKind>()) instead of calling kind().
target_text: Rust gotcha in reify's serialization layers: `io::Error::other(e)` is `io::Error::new(ErrorKind::Other, e)`, so any error produced by a `.map_err(io::Error::other)` mapping has `kind() == ErrorKind::Other` ALWAYS — the real underlying kind (e.g. `UnexpectedEof` from a truncated bincode read) is nested one level down inside the boxed source, where `kind()` cannot see it. Consequence: a downstream `matches!(e.kind(), UnexpectedEof | InvalidData)` guard on such an error is silently dead code. This produced task #6999 (`read_entry` returning Err where its rustdoc promised Ok(None)). There are ~45 `io::Error::other` sites across reify (reify-eval, reify-compute-contract, reify-shell-extract result/serialization paths); when adding a `kind()`-based guard, first check whether the error reaching it came through such a mapping. Guards on `NotFound` from raw `File::open`/`fs::metadata`/`remove_file` are unaffected — those errors come straight from the OS and are never wrapped.

entry_text: dark-factory fused-memory GOTCHA (measured, task 6137 planning): never put best-effort post-write work (for example an LLM judge) inline in MemoryService._execute_graphiti_write or in a durable-queue callback. DurableWriteQueue._process_item runs _execute_write under asyncio.wait_for(write_timeout), so a slow step can time out a write that has ALREADY landed and RETRY it, minting a duplicate episode. A callback that raises also retries the item, and it holds the queue semaphore while it runs. Use a tracked background task (the task_interceptor._background_tasks idiom) submitted after the identity-lock block. Also note: result.edges from add_episode is stale after the lock, because _dedup_episode_edges deletes duplicates inside it. Re-read survivors from the graph if they matter.
target_text: fused-memory durable_queue gotcha: DurableQueue._process_item fires an item's callback BEFORE marking it completed, and a callback EXCEPTION triggers item RETRY (durable_queue.py ~L328-332, "callback failure triggers retry instead of being silently lost"). Therefore any post-ingestion refresh_entity_summary added to _dual_write_callback (or a new post-ingest callback) MUST be best-effort/non-fatal (try/except log-and-continue, mirroring delete_entity's L891-901 neighbour-refresh loop) — otherwise a transient refresh failure poison-loops the queue item.

The fused-memory set_task_priority_override docstring overstates what pins and reserve_now do (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py). It says 'Pin this task to the front of the queue' and, for reserve_now, 'Reserve the next worker slot'.
In fact:
- A pin gives only a first try, each scheduler tick, at all-or-nothing module-lock acquisition, with no reservation.
- reserve_now installs parks once, at the task's RAW priority, and reserves no worker slot.
Operators pin expecting movement that the code does not provide. As of 2026-09-29 no task owns the docstring fix; it was deliberately kept out of 6040 to avoid adding a fused-memory file to it.
target_text: fused-memory's get_pin_queue MCP tool (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:6618) SELECTs a NAMED column list from the overrides table — task_id, boost_tier, pinned, pin_order, reserve_now, ttl_until — not SELECT *. Any column added to the overrides schema is therefore INVISIBLE through get_pin_queue until that SELECT and the returned dict are extended. This was caught at decompose of the scheduler dispatch-scoring PRD (2026-08-06): task delta's signal asserted "a source='starvation_watchdog' pin observable in get_pin_queue" while delta's module set covered only orchestrator files, making the capability binding producer-absent and the new overrides.source column a producer-orphan with no named consumer (a G1 violation). General lesson: when a leaf signal says a new persisted field is "observable in <read-path tool>", check that tool's projection — a named column list silently drops new columns.

entry_text: To tell whether a `reportMissingImports` pragma on a cross-workspace-member import is load-bearing, measure under a NARROW env as well as the all-packages one. After `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --all-packages`, every member is editable-installed in the root .venv, so the import resolves and the pragma looks vestigial. To simulate the member's own minimal env (what `uv run --directory <member>` builds on an unsynced tree), temporarily move `.venv/lib/python3.*/site-packages/_editable_impl_<other_member>.pth` aside, rerun the member's declared pyright gate, then restore the file. Measured in task 5090: shared/tests/test_task_statuses.py's orchestrator/fused_memory imports gave 0 errors under all-packages and 3 with the .pth files hidden, so those pragmas are load-bearing. Note the trap: `(root/'orchestrator').is_dir()` is true at the repo root, but pyright does NOT resolve `orchestrator.task_status` through that namespace-package partial.

MEASURED (2026-09-07, task 4357): in dark-factory's single-root uv workspace, `cd <member> && uv run <cmd>` does not merely FAIL TO INSTALL sibling members — it PRUNES ones a previous `uv sync --all-packages` had installed. There is one `.venv` per tree, so the last sync wins and workspace membership is global mutable state. Consequence: a cross-package import inside a member's tests passes or fails depending only on which uv command ran most recently, with no code change.

MEASURED BOTH WAYS on the task/4357 worktree, same tree, same test, unmodified: after `cd shared && uv sync`, `shared/tests/test_auth_failed.py`'s `import orchestrator.usage_gate` raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'orchestrator.usage_gate'`; after `uv run --all-packages`, the identical test passed. Toggling back reproduced the failure.

WHY THIS BITES VERIFY SPECIFICALLY. The configured `test_command` chain begins `cd shared && uv run pytest tests/ --timeout=300` and only later reaches `cd ../orchestrator && ...`. So shared's leg ALWAYS runs with the other six members pruned out, regardless of what cold-preprovision's `uv sync --all-packages` left behind. A cross-package import in `shared/tests/` is therefore not merely discouraged — it cannot work under verify, even though it may work in an agent's shell that happened to run `--all-packages` earlier.

THIS EXTENDS, and does not contradict, two existing entries: 54f2a288 ("`uv sync --all-packages` UNIONS every member's dev group into the one `<tree>/.venv`") and 45d56138 ("`uv run --project fused-memory` does NOT install sibling workspace packages"). The addition is the DESTRUCTIVE direction — union is not sticky, and a per-member `uv run` tears it back down.

TWO PRACTICAL RULES.
1. Never conclude "the cross-package import works" from a green run in your own shell. Re-run it under the exact verify shape (`cd <member> && uv sync` first, then the test) before believing it.
2. For a test in package A that must assert something about package B's SOURCE, read the file — `_REPO_ROOT / 'b/src/b/mod.py'` plus `ast.parse` — instead of importing B. That is venv-independent, and in this repo it is also required by the layering doctrine (`shared/` must not import `orchestrator/`, "program decision #4", cited in shared/tests/test_server_error.py, test_invocation_outcome_boundary.py and test_task_transitions.py). Task 4357 converted such a guard from `import orchestrator.usage_gate` + `hasattr` to a module-level AST bound-name scan for exactly these two reasons.

entry_text: reify gotcha: running `rustfmt --edition 2024 <file>` on a crates/*/tests/<name>.rs integration test that declares `mod common;` ALSO rewrites tests/common/*.rs (rustfmt follows out-of-line `mod` declarations), silently widening a targeted format into shared helpers. Format a new test file with `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` (nightly-only) or restore with `git checkout -- crates/<c>/tests/common/` afterwards, and always check `git status` before staging.

Each integration test compiles as a separate binary so sharing requires `tests/common/mod.rs` plus `mod common;` import (or a `#[cfg(any(test, feature="test-helpers"))]` `pub` module on the crate).

entry_text: Claude Code CLI gotcha (read statically from the 2.1.289 bundle, 2026-10-05, task 5971). Setting env CLAUDE_BASH_MAINTAIN_PROJECT_WORKING_DIR to a truthy value makes the CLI reset the Bash shell to its ORIGINAL launch cwd after EVERY Bash call, and it does so SILENTLY: no "Shell cwd was reset to <dir>" line and no telemetry event. Without the var, the CLI resets only when the cwd leaves the allowed dirs, and prints "Shell cwd was reset to <dir>" when it does. So never treat the absence of that message as proof that a `cd` persisted. Separately, measured with CLI 2.1.283: a relative or omitted `path` given to the Grep or Glob tool resolves against the drifted shell cwd, so only absolute paths are immune.

entry_text: reify gotcha: running `rustfmt --edition 2024 <file>` on a crates/*/tests/<name>.rs integration test that declares `mod common;` ALSO rewrites tests/common/*.rs (rustfmt follows out-of-line `mod` declarations), silently widening a targeted format into shared helpers. Format a new test file with `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` (nightly-only) or restore with `git checkout -- crates/<c>/tests/common/` afterwards, and always check `git status` before staging.
target_text: reify targeted-formatting gotcha: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file.rs>` RECURSES into that file's child modules, so running it on a crate root (lib.rs) formats the whole crate and reports every pre-existing hunk in every sibling file as if it were yours — measured on crates/reify-audit/src/lib.rs, which reported 200 hunks for a 20-line addition, and errors outright (`failed to resolve mod ...`) when run on a lib.rs copied to /tmp without its siblings. Add `--skip-children` for a genuinely per-file check (same lib.rs: 0 hunks before and after). This matters because CLAUDE.md's Formatting rule mandates checking only the touched files and rewriting a hunk only when it falls entirely inside your own new code — without --skip-children you cannot tell which hunks are yours. Note --skip-children also skips INLINE modules, so a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` block in your own new file is invisible to it; check that file both ways (plain to see your test module, --skip-children to isolate the file). Reliable attribution method regardless: `git show <base>:<path> > /tmp/b.rs` and diff the hunk COUNT before vs after your edit — equal counts mean you introduced none.

Scheduler gotcha: in runs.db, the event order within a single tick does NOT show that a task borrowed through a fresh park.

Scheduler._phase_select_scored (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py) runs try_acquire on candidates in score order. When a lower candidate wins, it takes that winner's locks first, and only then calls _bump_skip_and_maybe_park on the skipped top candidate. The top candidate's park is therefore laid over modules the winner already holds.

runs.db then shows task_skipped and reservation_installed for the top candidate, followed 1–2 ms later by lock_acquired for the winner. It looks like a borrow, but it is not one.

Only a park_backfill_granted event, which carries predicted_hold, admission_bound, provable_assembly_delay and park_owners, proves an EASY-backfill borrow. DF had just 6 grants ever as of 2026-10-04.

Example: on 2026-10-01, task 3096 was misread as having borrowed harness.py through task 5221's park. It had no grant event; harness.py was simply free when 3096 took it.
target_text: DISCOVERY (dark-factory scheduler, verified in runs.db 2026-09-25): a dispatched task's fairness parks are NOT cleared at dispatch unless it is the scored loop's top_id. Scheduler._phase_select_pins never calls clear_parks_for, and _phase_select_scored clears parks only for top_id. So a pinned or non-top task keeps its park for its whole run, until Scheduler.release's 'defensive' clear_parks_for removes it silently (no reservation_used, no event). While it runs, that leftover park blocks same-tier park installs by other tasks (INV-3), producing PARTIAL installs. Measured since 2026-06-23: 466 full / 74 partial / 817 empty reservation_installed. The partials are concentrated in the critical+pinned group (3620, 3541, 3542, 4541). 44 dispatches kept their own park. Detect it: a lock_acquired with no preceding reservation_used, for a task with an active park, whose scheduler_tick has terminal_phase=select_pins.

entry_text: PROCEDURE (worked 2026-09-29): closing a confusion-codebook entry whose CAUSE WAS REMOVED goes through a coding record, never a hand edit. Write a JSONL record `{"session": "<unique>", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "project": "dark_factory", "agent_class": "interactive", "corrections": [{"entry_id": "entry-cand-...", "status": "fixed", "note": "<why, non-empty>"}]}` under docs/legibility/coding-records/ and run `uv run --frozen python scripts/legibility/codebook.py apply docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml <record>.jsonl`; it flips the status and appends one dated, note-bearing sighting as the audit trail (stats line `corrections_applied=N`). STATUSES are open/partially/fixed/retired/mined-unverified; `fixed` fits a removed cause, `retired` means the entry itself is withdrawn. Corrections resolve only real ENTRY ids (`entry-cand-...`); bare `cand-...` ids are CANDIDATES the census adjudicates, and a correction naming one is counted as skipped_unknown_entry — check the id kind before drafting. `codebook.py validate` afterwards should exit 0.
target_text:
GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-09 planning task 5198): amending a confusion-codebook entry via an appended CORRECTION SIGHTING — the task-4892 precedent — is INVISIBLE to the consumer that re-ingests the entry. Do not assume the note reaches anything.

MECHANISM. scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_codebook_index is the only thing that puts codebook entries in front of the LLM trickle coder. It renders exactly one line per entry, `- {id}: {title} — {cause}`, and its own docstring states that heavy fields including `sightings` "are never included", and that "ALL entries are included, retired ones too" (a census re-observes pre-fix traces, so dropping retired entries would force spurious candidates).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both counter-intuitive:
1. A correction NOTE lives inside a sighting, so the coder never sees it. Task 4892's note-only amendment correctly annotated history for a human reader, but changed nothing about what the coder matches against. Its commit message's reasoning ("adding a merger op for a two-line doc correction would extend the §7.3 contract — disproportionate") was scoped to a case where the stale thing WAS the note.
2. `status: retired` is not rendered either, and retired entries are deliberately kept in the index. So retiring an entry does NOT stop the coder re-matching sessions to it.

Only `title` and `cause` reach the consumer. If the defect is a refuted FRAMING — an entry whose title asserts a cause that was disproved — the note-only path leaves the false assertion rendered every night, and the entry keeps self-ingesting (the census quoting its own error string back to itself as fresh sightings). Withdrawing a refuted framing requires writing `title`/`cause`.

AND THE SOLE WRITER CANNOT DO THAT TODAY. scripts/legibility/codebook.py::apply_coding_record supports exactly two ops, both pure appends: append-a-sighting-on-match and append-a-candidate. No op writes an entry field. The only field-writing transforms are census-owned (scripts/legibility/census.py::promote_candidate / reject_candidate / retire_entry), have no CLI, and are reachable only from a full census run — so they produce no committed record and are not replayable on rebase.

PRACTICE: before planning a codebook amendment, decide first WHICH FIELD carries the defect. Note-only (the 4892 shape) is right for a stale or superseded observation. A refuted title/cause needs a field write, and expressing that through the sole-writer record path means extending apply_coding_record — which is proportionate precisely when the title is what re-ingests.

entry_text: GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-10-03 for task 4155): to test that a spawn uses start_new_session=True, run a real child and check pid == os.getpgid(0) == os.getsid(0); see shared/tests/test_git_async.py::test_child_leads_its_own_session_with_no_controlling_terminal. An open('/dev/tty') -> ENXIO check alone cannot catch the bug in agent and verify shells. They have no controlling terminal, so the child gets ENXIO with or without the new session. The session-id check fails as soon as start_new_session is dropped.
target_text: GOTCHA (CPython 3.13 asyncio): a cancellation that lands while `await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(...)` is suspended after the fork (connecting pipes in _make_subprocess_transport) is handled by asyncio itself: `transp.close()` SIGKILLs only the DIRECT child, so a start_new_session child's group and grandchildren survive. `await transp._wait()` then waits for every pipe to close, so the cancelled call can HANG while a survivor holds stdout/stderr. The caller never gets a Process to group-kill. Fix pattern (task 6346, shared/src/shared/git_async.py::_spawn_session_leader): run the spawn as its own task and `await asyncio.shield(spawn)`. On BaseException, wait the spawn out with `asyncio.wait((spawn,))`, suppressing further CancelledError and never re-awaiting it, so a spawn failure cannot replace the interrupting exception. Then group-kill and reap any Process it produced, and re-raise. To reproduce deterministically in a test, condition-poll with sleep(0) until the child appears in /proc with ppid == os.getpid(), block the loop thread synchronously, then cancel.

Their stdlib wrappers in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/trajectory.ri (`profile_duration -> Time`, `peak_deviation -> Length`) therefore have bodies that contradict their declared returns. Measured 2026-10-01 as the ONLY stdlib fns a body-vs-return reconciliation fires on. Because stdlib_loader::build_stdlib_modules asserts zero Error diagnostics in stdlib, any Error-severity body/return check panics the stdlib load until these are typed (#8119, which #7007 now depends on).
target_text: Reify vacuity trap: a `compile_with_stdlib`-clean assertion can NEVER prove a stdlib function is registered as a language-level built-in. `crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs` (~line 952-968) falls ANY unknown function-call name through to a generic `CompiledExpr::FunctionCall` typed as `compiled_args.first().result_type`, emitting no undefined-name diagnostic. Measured 2026-08-26 on main-ancestor fb265292f2: `examples/topology_selectors/block_inertia.ri`, calling the entirely unregistered `moment_of_inertia`, compiled with ZERO diagnostics. The non-vacuous observable is the compiled value cell's `cell_type`: an unregistered selector yields `Type::Geometry` (the first-arg fallback), which `reify_eval::engine_eval::is_representable_cell_type` rejects and `assert_value_cell_types_representable` turns into a hard debug-build panic inside `Engine::eval`. Assert on cell_type, not on "no error diagnostics".

entry_text: Reify unit-literal scope gotcha (measured 2026-10-04, HEAD 92a94f7545): a TOP-LEVEL user `fn` body or fn-param default has NO unit registry, so the compound literal `300mm/s` errors ("compound unit expression requires a unit registry in scope") and only reify_core::units::BUILTIN_UNITS resolve there (mm cm m in deg rad kg g s K A mol cd); `200GPa`, `1N` and `5um` are "unknown unit". Compose from built-ins instead: `fn speed() -> Velocity { 300.0 * 1mm / 1s }`. Structure members (param, let, ctor args, sub blocks) and constraint defs DO have the registry, so `300mm/s` and `200GPa` work there.
target_text: Compound-unit literals (e.g. `9.81m/s^2`, `0.0001ohm*m`) only resolve when the std.units registry is in scope. entry_text: Reify gotcha: `cargo nextest run -p reify-test-support` alone is NOT equivalent coverage to the verify gate for that crate. The package-only run selects 648 tests; under verify's workspace `-p` set, feature unification enables reify-test-support's `eval-helpers` feature and the crate runs 668 tests, including the `helpers::tests::*` lib tests (measured 2026-10-03, task 5991). target_text: reify gotcha: `reify-test-support` has NO default features, so `eval-helpers` is OFF under a bare `cargo test -p reify-test-support`. Any `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "eval-helpers"))]` test in that crate is then compiled out entirely and the run reports success with ZERO tests — a false green that hides both RED and GREEN. Always pass `--features eval-helpers` when exercising gated tests in that crate. verify.sh's primary pass is `cargo nextest run --workspace` with no `--features` flag, where workspace feature unification turns `eval-helpers` on (reify-eval's dev-dep demands it), so the same test DOES run there — the divergence is between the workspace pass and narrowed `-p` selectors.

Completed: Harden the flag-marker sweep family: reject phantom project roots, add the protected-audit-record guard
Description: Two independent hardening gaps in fused-memory's orphan/flag-marker sweep family, each filed as an out-of-scope follow-up from a prior narrowly-scoped task. First: `build_known_projects_map` resolves candidate roots non-strictly, so a typo'd or unmounted root named in DASHBOARD_KNOWN_PROJECT_ROOTS is admitted as a phantom project into every registry the builder backs — the recon harness's known_projects, the server's multi-project registry, and ProjectPrefixRegistry — with no signal anywhere except the one sweep script that was taught to warn. Second: `delete_orphan_markers` lacks the `is_protected_audit_record` guard its in-cycle counterpart applies, so it can destroy deliberately-permanent audit records; an age-only rule of this shape already burned 40 cadence_check records once.

Both are latent today rather than actively firing, and both are combined here because they share `sweep_orphan_flag_markers.py` and the same 'parity/hardening gap' risk class. Neither is a mechanical patch: each requires a recorded decision — which arm to take at the builder, and whether a denylist guard alone is sufficient for a sweep whose --terminal-drain posture is the inverse of the collector the guard was designed for.
Analysis: Two independent hardening gaps. Premises verified on this branch (HEAD df5441a6f3).

WORKSTREAM 1: phantom project roots (from #4658)
- `fused_memory.models.scope::build_known_projects_map` turns each candidate into `str(Path(raw).resolve())`, and only an OSError gets it skipped. The resolve is non-strict, so a missing or typo'd root is admitted under a basename-derived id. The docstring claims "file not found ... skipped", which is false. This is still the code on main.
- Consumers that receive phantom entries:
  - `server/main.py` builds the map once and passes it to MemoryService, the harness and TicketJanitor. A phantom extra root also makes `len(map) > 1` true, which switches on multi-project mode.
  - `graphiti_client._derive_registered_graph_ids` and the fallbacks in harness and ticket_janitor all call the builder.
  - `ProjectPrefixRegistry.from_roots` repeats the resolve + `resolve_project_id_for_root` loop, so it ALREADY admits a non-directory root. It registers it with prefixes `()` and logs a WARNING from `_candidate_prefixes_for_root` ("not a directory; skipping"). That word is misleading: only the prefix scan is skipped. Existing tests pin this admission: `test_project_prefix_registry.py::TestRobustness`.
  - The sweep script's `_known_projects_coverage_issue` has its own `Path(raw).is_dir()` stat for case (i). Its end-to-end test `test_named_root_that_is_not_a_directory_is_reported_root_by_root` also pins the admission.
- DECISION: arm (b). Admit the root, and log a WARNING once per admitted phantom root in each builder call. The deciding evidence: when a project_id is unknown, `harness._project_loop` catches UnknownProjectError and calls `EventBuffer.mark_project_dead_letter`. That moves every buffered recon event for the project to dead_letter, which is a terminal, orphaned state with no replay path. On top of that, every registry is snapshotted once at process start. So under arm (a), a checkout that is merely absent at startup would lose its events and stay de-registered until restart, even after it comes back. Arm (b) costs one inert id, which now carries a WARNING. The single detection becomes a new `scope.is_phantom_project_root`. The sweep script and ProjectPrefixRegistry delegate to it.

WORKSTREAM 2: the protected-audit guard (from #5129)
- The script imports `is_protected_mirror_record` and `record_mem0_deletion_tombstones` but NOT `is_protected_audit_record`. `find_protected_markers` is mirror-only and has three consumers: the choke point in `delete_orphan_markers`, `run()`'s enumeration-scoped subtraction and report, and the absolute arm of `find_undrainable_marker…[truncated, 7319 chars total]

entry_text: reify-lsp gotcha: `DocumentState::parsed_module` (crates/reify-lsp/src/document.rs) holds its `parsed_cache` Mutex across `parse_with_stdlib` ON PURPOSE. That makes it a single-flight memo: concurrent same-version callers wait for the ONE in-flight parse of identical text and then get the same Arc. Moving the parse outside the lock with a CAS-style install cannot lower any caller's latency. A latecomer would wait a full parse P instead of the remaining P−t, and the change would add up to (N−1) duplicate parses of CPU. The real per-keystroke redundancy is elsewhere: didChange's diagnostics parse (diagnostics.rs `compute_diagnostics_with_state`) is never shared into the DocumentState cache. (Analysis from task 7272's architect pass, not a benchmark.)

reify-lsp concurrency facts, established for #7272 on 2026-10-01:

Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.
- Free-function forms `map(xs, |v| v)` / `filter(xs, |v| v > 1)` also fail; no free-function map/filter exists.
- `generate(3, |i| i)` and `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])` DO parse (both `function_call`); `xs.count` parses (bare `member_access`, no parens). So lambdas work and member access works — only method arguments are missing.

DEAD CODE this leaves behind: the `"map"`, `"filter"`, `"all"`, `"any"`, `"generate"` arms of `eval_method_call` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs (lines ~3695, ~3825, ~3714, ~3739, ~3811) are unreachable from .ri source and exercised only by Rust-level tests. crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:3798-3810 even documents a deliberate negative-count policy divergence between the free-function and METHOD forms of `generate` — a distinction no .ri program can observe.

WORK TO DECIDE/DO (triage first, this is a design question, not a mechanical fix):
(a) add an `obj.method(args)` rule to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js plus the corresponding lowering in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, so the existing evaluator arms become reachable; or
(b) expose the wanted combinators as free functions instead (the shape `generate` and `flat_map` already use) and delete or clearly mark the unreachable method arms; or
(c) accept the gap deliberately and document it, marking the unreachable arms so future readers do not assume surface coverage.

Files: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs.

Rationale for filing: leaving evaluator arms with no surface form is a silent-capability-gap — a design session reading the stdlib docs would reasonably write `xs.filter(...)` and get an opaque "invalid let" parse error rather than an unsupported-construct diagnostic.
Analysis: TRIAGE (the task asks for a design decision first).

PREMISE CHECK — the task text is partly stale. It was measured on 975cbfc301 (2026-08-21). Task 5495 μ landed afterwards (35e9259316 / dcc2f6a641, 2026-08-28) and added `namespaced_call: prec(12, seq(field('callee', $.member_access), callTail($)))` to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:2004. That rule captures EVERY `<expr>.name(args)`, so `xs.map(|v| v + 1)` now PARSES. `lower_namespaced_call` (crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs:5401) then rejects it at lowering. Measured 2026-10-01 with this lane's target/release/reify (main 107171c475):
  - `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` and `constraint xs.all(|v| v > 0)` → exit 1, "unknown qualifier `xs` in `xs.map(...)` … Reify has no method-call syntax, so this cannot be a call on a value named `xs`". So the "opaque `invalid let`" the task was filed about is GONE for identifier receivers, in let AND constraint position.

entry_text: When re-planning a reify task branch that already carries committed work, the orchestrator may have rebased it since its last verify, so the verify-passed tip SHA in runs.db (`workflow_verify` event `tip_sha`) no longer matches HEAD. To check that the content is still the verified diff, compare `git patch-id --stable` of `git diff $(git merge-base <old_tip> main) <old_tip>` against `git diff main HEAD`: identical ids mean the same diff. That is still not "verify passed on this exact tip", so plan with all steps pre-satisfied via mark_step_committed instead of calling report_ready_to_merge.
target_text: When re-planning a reify task branch that already carries committed work, check `git merge-base --is-ancestor main HEAD` BEFORE considering report_ready_to_merge — warm-lane task branches can sit long enough for a sibling task to land and restructure the same code seam, turning a green branch into a diverged one. Preflight the damage with `git merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD`, which lists conflicted paths without touching the worktree. Seen on task/6080 (2026-08-29): the branch was fully implemented and green (reify-stdlib 2167 passed / 0 failed) but sibling #6126 had merged underneath it and rewritten the same transform_log/transform_exp seam, so the branch's tests and docs contradicted landed main and the task needed a merge-and-reconcile plan rather than a merge report.

entry_text: In reify-compiler, every operand in a boolean geometry position (union/difference/... args) is ALSO value-compiled before realization lowering: a top-level geometry let / geometry-list let / geometry param emits a value cell via compile_expr_with_expected over its whole initializer (entity.rs geometry-let arm, task #4954), which runs before the realization-emission third pass. So unknown-member / priv-member / collection-sub value-level diagnostics for a boolean operand are already emitted once; a geometry-position consumer that also renders MemberPathError::to_diagnostic double-reports (measured task 5425 with `reify check`).
target_text: In reify-compiler, `compile_geometry_call` (geometry.rs:~397) returns None at the `match &expr.kind { FunctionCall => ..., _ => return None }` arm for any non-Ident/non-FunctionCall expr (MemberAccess, IndexAccess). Consequence: a boolean-op argument of the indexed cross-sub form `self.<sub>[i].<member>` never reaches the value-level `try_emit_cross_sub_geometry` (expr.rs:1562); in `resolve_boolean_arg` it falls through to the generic "argument N must be a geometry expression" fallback. This is the documented (geometry_boolean.rs:59-63) intentional scope boundary for task 3512 — indexed forms are out of scope and emit the generic diagnostic, not the cross-sub v0.1-deferred wording.

An identifier receiver (`xs.map(|v| v + 1)`, let OR constraint position) gets "unknown qualifier `xs` … Reify has no method-call syntax"; a non-identifier receiver (`[1, 2].any(...)`, `(xs).all(...)`, `self.xs.filter(...)`) gets the callee-shape message "unsupported qualified call … must be a simple `binding.Name(...)`". The old "Parse error: invalid let" is gone. PROBE GOTCHA: `constraint name: expr` is NOT valid Reify inside a structure body — it yields "invalid constraint" even for `constraint c: count(xs) > 0`; the valid form is `constraint <expr>`. #6406's "constraint position also fails" observation was an artifact of that malformed probe.

CORRECTION (verified 2026-09-14 against crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, task #6484): reify structure-instance ctor args bind BY NAME, not positionally. Task 4522 replaced the old positional binder with a two-pass scheme — "Pass 1: assign named args to their target param slot" (~expr.rs:2837), then "Pass 2: assign positional (None) args to the next param not already bound by a named arg" (~:2863). Two older memories still assert the retired positional behaviour and are now FALSE: mem0 e18a60f8-359c-46c5-9e9c-6e80212a56a6 ("positional args bind to a structure_def's Param cells in declaration order") and graphiti a641477c-28e4-4b58-b2af-1a2c0bc06ed4 ("binds arguments positionally by index"). Task #6484 existed precisely to retire this same stale claim from source comments.

GOTCHA that follows from the by-name binder: a MISSPELLED named arg is diagnosed as E_CTOR_UNKNOWN_FIELD but is STILL pushed leniently as `__arg{call_idx}` and NEVER claims a param slot (the binder's own comment: "The unknown arg is diagnosed but NOT bound to a param slot"). So the param the author meant to set silently falls back to its declared default. Writing the other params out explicitly does NOT prevent this — the mis-bind is independent of them, and with N args against a declared count of N no surplus positional exists so E_CTOR_ARITY never fires either. The severity is a single knob, CTOR_FIELD_CONFORMANCE_SEVERITY in crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/mod.rs:45, = Severity::Warning today (so it does not fail the build; slated to become Error at δ). Consequence in practice: `element_order: ElementOrdr.P2` on a ModalOptions/BucklingOptions call silently leaves element_order at its ElementOrder.P1 default, reinstating the P1 bending lock. Pinned by crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_mechanics/modal_options_validation_tests.rs::misspelled_ctor_label_is_diagnosed_but_still_leniently_appended.

entry_text: reify-compiler gotcha: a where-guarded param or let (`param x = 5mm where c`, or `where c { param x ... }`) is lowered by `compile_per_decl_guard` into `TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups[].members` / `.else_members`, NOT into `value_cells`. So any projection built only from `tmpl.value_cells` (e.g. `member_type_map_from_template` → `scope.sub_member_types`) silently misses guarded members of a child template. To ask "does the child declare name X", also scan guarded_groups, sub_components, ports, named realizations and match_arm_groups.
target_text: Reify gotcha: `template.value_cells` is NOT the complete set of a template's value cells. Guarded-group members live in a separate collection, `template.guarded_groups[*].members` / `.else_members` (crates/reify-compiler/src/types.rs:708, CompiledGuardedGroup at :1051-1068), each with its own `default_expr`. Any code that walks `value_cells` to answer "does this module do X?" silently misses anything declared inside an `if <cond> { ... }` guarded group. This is a live pre-existing gap, not hypothetical: `mint_symbolic_topology_selectors_into_values` (crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs:5937-5938) walks only `value_cells`, so a selector let inside a guarded group is never minted into the ValueMap. Other ValueMap key families also absent from `value_cells`: field cells (`__field__.*`), synthetic collection lists (`__list_{sub}__{member}`), sub-instance/keyed-member/`__self` cells, scoped child-instance cells, `__auto_pose` cells, and realization-named geometry-handle cells. No ValueMap insert anywhere is keyed off an anonymous sub-expression, though — every key is a declared or named-synthetic ValueCellId.

NORM (dark-factory, established by task 4295, 2026-08-30): a test may DERIVE from a nightly-regenerated artifact, but must never PIN its snapshots. Once task 4006 put `plans/memory-metadata-census-report.json` on an 05:00 timer that rewrites and commits it, every count in it became a moving target, and any assertion of the form `== 385` in a test is a doomed RED test no implementer can green.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVES IT. Task 4295's own description, written 2026-08-16, cited the live census as 385 distinct `metadata.kind` values, +70 vs the frozen oracle. Re-running the identical deterministic diff on 2026-08-30 gave **387, +72**. The task text was stale by the time it was planned — 14 days. entry_text: When probing a model variant with `reify eval` (e.g. a copy with an auto pinned), keep the file basename equal to the declared `module` name. Otherwise eval fails immediately with `E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH: declared module path 'X' does not match expected path 'Y' (derived from file location)`. Put each variant in its own /tmp subdirectory under the original filename. A warm lane usually already has a built `target/release/reify`; run it with LD_LIBRARY_PATH starting at /opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin.
target_text: To eval a MODIFIED copy of a Reify example (e.g. deriving the frozen-cascade half of `examples/whole_model_joint_drive.ri` by stripping its `minimize` line), the temp copy must keep the ORIGINAL FILENAME, because `reify eval` derives the expected module path from the file location and rejects a mismatch with `E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH: declared module path 'X' does not match expected path 'Y'`. Copy into a fresh directory under the same basename (`mkdir -p /tmp/jdtest && grep -v '^\s*minimize ' examples/whole_model_joint_drive.ri > /tmp/jdtest/whole_model_joint_drive.ri`) rather than renaming the file.

pytest-timeout's timeout_method="signal" DOES work inside pytest-xdist workers on this repo's pinned stack (pytest-xdist 3.8.0 / execnet 2.1.2 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0). xdist >= 3.4 starts workers with execnet's main_thread_only execmodel, so tests run on the worker's main thread and SIGALRM reaches them. Measured 2026-10-05 (task 5470 architect) on a synthetic suite at `-n 2 --dist loadgroup`, timeout=2:
- signal: failed only the test blocked on threading.Event().wait(); the worker survived and the tally was complete.
- thread (+ --max-worker-restart=0): os._exit killed the worker and later tests never ran.
The older "signal is incompatible with xdist, use thread" belief was never measured. Pick the method on that trade (signal keeps the worker alive; thread also terminates a main thread stuck in C code), not on xdist compatibility.
target_text: pytest-xdist 3.8.0 runs every worker's tests on the worker process's MAIN thread (`xdist/workermanage.py::NodeManager.__init__` uses `execnet.Group(execmodel="main_thread_only")` and forces that execmodel onto every spec). So pytest-timeout signal mode works under xdist. The orchestrator/pyproject.toml comment claiming "worker subprocesses run pytest in a thread, so signal-based interruption is no longer reliable" is stale. Verified 2026-09-28: `-n 2 --max-worker-restart=0 -o timeout_method=signal` produced 'FAILED ... Failed: Timeout (>Ns) from pytest-timeout' with a traceback, and the worker survived. shared/pyproject.toml has run `timeout_method = "signal"` since b9d39def62 (2026-04-24). fused-memory/pyproject.toml and orchestrator/pyproject.toml use "thread", and orchestrator's is pinned by `test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py::TestTimeoutConstants`. Under the thread method the timeout banner goes to worker stdout, which execnet discards, and `faulthandler_timeout=240` only fires for tests running longer than 240 s.

entry_text: GOTCHA: orchestrator `git_ops._run` (via `shared.git_async.run_git`) returns stdout `.decode().strip()`-ed, which silently corrupts any byte-exact output. A `git diff` patch whose last hunk ends in a blank context line (' \n') loses that line and `git apply` then rejects it as a corrupt patch; leading/trailing whitespace in `-z` path listings is also lost, and non-UTF-8 output raises UnicodeDecodeError out of `_run`. FIX for patches: write them with `git diff HEAD --binary --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-color --output=<tmpfile>` and read the file (see `git_ops.py::_head_diff_patch`, task 3652). Catch UnicodeDecodeError by name where a `_run` caller promises never to raise.
target_text:
GOTCHA, two of them, when feeding git output back into git inside orchestrator code (measured on task 5342 building merge_gates._branch_delta_survives, which reverse-applies a branch's own delta against a merged blob to prove work survived a rename).

(1) `orchestrator.git_ops._run` returns `stdout.decode().strip()` — it strips BOTH ends. So any caller that pipes git output into a tool requiring exact bytes must re-terminate it. `git diff ... > patchfile` via _run loses the patch's trailing newline, and `git apply` then rejects it with "error: corrupt patch at line N" — a message that points at the last hunk line and reads like a malformed diff, not like a missing newline. Fix is one line: write `patch + '\n'`. This cost a real debugging cycle; the failure surfaced only as a behavioural test going red, with no error logged, because the apply arm just returned a non-zero rc. Corollary worth knowing: `.strip()` also eats trailing whitespace on the patch's final context line, so a patch ending in a whitespace-bearing context line will not apply either. In a fail-CLOSED consumer that is merely conservative; in a fail-OPEN one it would be a silent hole.

(2) `git apply -R` locates the target file by the patch's `b/` (NEW) side, not the `a/` side and not wherever the content actually lives now. When reverse-applying a delta that SPANS a rename, stage the blob under the AFTER path, not the merged path. At the drop-guard site those differ (after=`pkg/a.py`, merged=`pkg/b.py`); staging at the merged path fails to apply silently and turns every suppression into a flag — i.e. it looks like the check is simply conservative rather than broken. Use a FRESH empty tmpdir too: with differing a/b paths, reverse-apply additionally requires the `a/` path be ABSENT, which a reused directory can violate.

USEFUL TECHNIQUE these two motivate: `git diff <revA>:<pathA> <revB>:<pathB>` (the blob-to-blob form) emits headers `a/<pathA>` `b/<pathB>`, so a delta that crosses a rename is expressible as ONE patch with no pathspec gymnastics. That is what lets a single primitive serve two call sites whose renames happen on opposite ranges (branch-side vs merge-side) without special-casing either.

entry_text: FalkorDB gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, task 4716): `MATCH (a)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(b) RETURN count(*)` with r UNREFERENCED counts distinct connected (a,b) node PAIRS, not edges — multi-edges between one pair collapse (dark_factory: 19,409 vs count(r) = count(DISTINCT r.uuid) = 20,491; the plan is Aggregate <- Conditional Traverse, no edge expansion). Referencing r (`count(r)`, or any `WHERE r.<prop>`) expands the edges. A `_paged_ro_query` census written as a bare-pattern count(*) is therefore LOW, and since completeness is `rows_seen >= expected_rows`, it would pass a read truncated by up to the multi-edge excess. Edge censuses must use count(r) or carry a WHERE on r.

GOTCHA measuring "what files did a task branch itself touch" (git 2.43, scratch-repo measurement for task 3918, 2026-10-05). Two independent errors combine.

(1) Plain `git log --name-only A..B` is MERGE-BLIND: it prints NO paths for merge commits, so a file changed only while resolving a back-merge (a conflict resolution or evil hunk) is invisible. Add `--diff-merges=dense-combined` (`--cc`). It lists a merge commit only for the paths it changed relative to EVERY parent, so a clean back-merge contributes nothing. NEVER use `-m` or `--diff-merges=first-parent`: on a back-merge the first parent is the branch, so they list everything main brought in.

(2) A WRITE-ONCE base (e.g. `TaskWorkflow._base_commit`) is too wide once the branch back-merges main or is re-cut after a quarantine: `old_base..HEAD` includes main's commits and CREDITS main-side edits as the branch's work. Re-derive the base at use time with `GitOps.merge_base_with_main(head)`.

Measured on one topology: stale base + plain log both missed the evil-merge path and credited main's edit; fresh fork + dense-combined got both right. Relevant to any consumer of a branch-touched set: the merge gate, the review diff, and implementer/debugger detection.
target_text:
MEASURED across 2026-09-08/09 (dark_factory): `base..tip` is NOT a sound oracle for "did this task deliver". Three DISTINCT false-negative/false-positive modes were measured within 24 hours, each costing an escalation cycle.

(1) COMMITS CARRIED ON ANOTHER TASK'S BRANCH — esc-4678-7 reported task 4678's "plan files were never touched by any commit". False: eight (4678)-tagged commits existed, all four declared files were touched, and the work was on main. It had landed under `Merge task/4789 into main`, so a check keyed on a task-NAMED merge found nothing.

(2) BRANCH REBASED FORWARD PAST ITS OWN LANDED WORK — esc-4369-8, same block reason. Five (4369)-tagged commits were already on main and the branch had been rebased onto a main containing them, so the `base..tip` range was empty BY CONSTRUCTION. `git diff --name-only main...task/4369` was EMPTY and `git rev-list --count main..task/4369` was 0. An architect re-plan then re-declared the already-satisfied scope, which made it read as a stalled implementation.

(3) THE INVERSE — a branch INFLATED by foreign commits: task/4502 carried 15 of task 4405's commits and 22 of task 4775's (esc-4502-8).

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS: match on commit SUBJECTS (`git log --oneline <base>..<branch> --grep=<task-id>`) or on CONTENT — run the task's own metadata.delivered_checks against main, and confirm the named symbol exists (`git grep -n <symbol> main -- <file>`). Ancestry against a recorded base distinguishes none of the three.
TWO TRAPS: a base hundreds of commits behind makes `git diff base..branch` show mostly MAIN's history (868 commits in the 4369 case), so "the diff touches many files" proves nothing either way; and the two recorded bases can DISAGREE (metadata.branch_base_sha is stale from first dispatch), so "the work predates the base" is base-dependent — the empty three-dot diff is the claim that holds regardless.
Task 5144 (pending, high) owns this class; all three instances are its subject and no fourth should be filed.

Description: Closes five related defects in the family of gates that decide whether a memory or task write falsely claims completed work: a ticket-store-misconfiguration case that gets mislabeled as an outright fabrication accusation; three false-positive classes (filing-vs-completion standard confusion, cross-repo commit misattribution, a missed negation construction) found by a 7577-episode retrospective sweep; a clause-splitting proximity-binding fix to regain recall without reintroducing a coordinated-two-id over-fire; and a PR/issue-number misparse where the gate reads a bare "#N" citation from PR/issue prose (e.g. "Merged PR #4521 into main") as a task reference and wrongly adjudicates the claim against task #N instead of recognizing it as unrelated.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on base d7e9c92abe (branch task/4853, no prior commits). Every named artifact exists: services/completion_claim_gate.py (847 lines: extract_completion_claims, _refs_in_clause, _verify_task, _verify_ticket, _verify_commit, make_commit_probe), server/tools.py::create_mcp_server closures _claim_ticket_rows / _claim_commit_presence / _completion_claim_gate / _premature_completion_block, middleware/task_interceptor.py::TaskInterceptor.get_ticket_row, reconciliation/task_filter.py (TASK_REF_RE, NEGATED_TERMINAL_RE, _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE, STRICT_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY_RE, PRESENT_TENSE_COMPLETION_RE), scripts/audit_unverified_completion_claims.py (_build_ticket_probe, _build_commit_probe, caveats), docs/unverified-completion-claim-sweep-2026-08-11/{investigation.md,report.json}. Line numbers in the task text are stale; symbols are not. Partial prior progress: task 3403 already stopped the gate importing _CLAUSE_SPLIT_RE (it uses STRICT_CLAUSE_BOUNDARY_RE) but declined the recall win; proximity binding is still open (residual noted in the gate's comment block as tkt_0RSM4JVBN05YSSP1E2ASRZ6VWH / task 4432). Baseline: the five gate-related test files pass (402 passed).

THE SIX DEFECTS AND THEIR FIXES
W6 '#N' misparse (PR/issue). task_filter.TASK_REF_RE's bare '#' arm reads 'Merged PR #4521' / 'issue #123' / 'owner/repo#12' as task refs. That regex is shared by both write gates (completion-claim gate AND the premature-completion soft-block) and 5 other consumers. Fix at the source (SPOT): the '#' arm gets (a) a fixed-width negative lookbehind per foreign-number cue word, built from a tuple constant (pr, prs, pull, request, issue, issues, gh, mr), each with and without one trailing space, and (b) (?<![\w/]) so a word-attached '#' (PR#4521, repo#12, dark_factory#2748) is not a bare task ref. 'task'/'df' arms unchanged, groups stay 1. MEASURED: with exactly this patch applied temporarily, every consumer suite (test_task_filter, test_completion_claim_gate, test_memory_eval_staleness_sweep, test_audit_duplicate_memories, test_stale_status_snapshot_edge_sweep, test_stale_priority_override_edge_sweep, test_dependency_direction_check, test_recon_premature_completion_gate) passed: 2111 passed. The gate's _EXTERNAL_TASK_REF_RE widens ':' to '[:#]' so registered 'dark_factory#2748' becomes a correctly-attributed cross-project ref instead of a writer-project task 2748.

W1 ticket store unconfigured. get_ticket_row returns None both for 'no such ticket' and for '_ticket_store is None'; _verify_ticket maps None to mismatch. That turns every tkt_ claim into a fabrication accusation while the store is unconfigured. Fix at the source: get_ticket_row RAISES a new TicketStoreNotConfiguredError (defined in task_interceptor.py) when no store is configured, so None means only 'no such ticket'. tools._claim_ticket_rows catches that type, logs one warning, and returns {} (every ref absent, so UNRESOLVABLE, so unverifiable).

W2 filing held to the completion standard (Class A, 128/172 sweep mismatches, plus live exemplars 6169-3, 5850-1, 5869-1, 4818-3, 3651-3). _verify_task requires TE…[truncated, 8876 chars total]

entry_text: dark-factory recon GOTCHA (task 6137 planning): reconciliation/context_assembler.py::ContextAssembler runs ONLY on the harness's backlog-chunk path, where run_full_cycle receives assembled_payload. Ordinary Stage 1 cycles build their payload in MemoryConsolidator.assemble_payload's time-windowed path. To put something in front of Stage 1 on EVERY full cycle, mirror graphiti_queue_health and index_health. Fetch it in harness.run_full_cycle, thread it through _configure_consolidator into a MemoryConsolidator attribute, and render it in BOTH full-cycle builders (assemble_payload and _format_assembled_payload). Register it in REQUIRED_SECTIONS only if a prompt infers something from the section's absence.
target_text: GOTCHA — Stage 1 (memory_consolidator.py) has THREE payload builders, not two: `assemble_payload` (legacy time-windowed), `_format_assembled_payload` (token-budget/assembled path), and `_assemble_remediation_payload` (remediation passes). When adding a shared section/directive builder, all three must call it. The remediation builder is routinely missed because it sits ~100 lines below the other two and is short: task 2150 introduced the gap, task 2552 fixed the missing `_build_project_root_directive()` call, and task 3839 (gate 3833) fixed the missing `_build_live_workflow_section()` call. Note `_build_task_tree_section` and `_build_task_count_census_section` are deliberately full-cycle-only — census returns '' whenever `task_count_verification is None`, which harness `_configure_consolidator` documents as always true on remediation passes — so "make all builders identical" is the wrong fix. Remediation runs DO receive `filtered_task_tree` (harness.py `_run_remediation_pass` → `_configure_consolidator(..., filtered_task_tree=remediation_tree)`), so live-workflow signals genuinely render there.

entry_text: Verified completion of task 'Compiler: un-annotated fn return types silently default to Real; nothing reconciles the declared/defaulted signature against the compiled body type' against the codebase: The un-annotated fn return type reconciliation (task #5991) is implemented in crates/reify-compiler. Commit 79115ccc35f9 added the module crates/reify-compiler/src/fn_return_check.rs, wired from functions.rs (compile_function) and lib.rs. reconcile_fn_return compares compiled.body.result_expr.result_type with compiled.return_type, which is the declared type or the defaulted Real. A contradiction is reported as DiagnosticCode::FnReturnTypeUnannotated. For explicit Int or Scalar annotations a mismatch diagnostic is also reported. Severity is FN_RETURN_RECONCILE_SEVERITY = Warning, so the check runs in warn mode first; flipping it to Error is #7007. Commit a6d68f8e6b2b made compile_assoc_function call reconcile_fn_return with FnOwner::Conformer. Bodies that read `self` are skipped until #8118. Commit e0af13493976 added push_once_per_body to dedupe reports and a fixture, fn_return_reconciliation_tests.rs. require_bodyless_return_annotation covers bodyless trait assoc fns, so bodyless trait fns are told to annotate. Bare generic bodies (TypeParam, ScalarParam, Projection) are skipped, which is the #7008 follow-up. Fork (a) was chosen and fork (b) was deferred. Caveat on PLAN STEP 4: it asked for a prose breadcrumb at the compile_function emit site. Commit 7df9fe68733e removed that note from the source and moved the rationale to the task record, which is a deviation from the step as written. The comment now only points at reconcile_fn_return. The core defect is fixed, but the breadcrumb is absent from the source. The `Real` default at functions.rs:277/679 and traits.rs:153 was not re-read directly. The grep tool returned empty results even for known symbols, so evidence comes from the git history and the file read. Latest relevant commits are e0af13493976 and 7df9fe68733e (2026-10-03).

Description: From the 2026-08-03 fallback-soundness investigation (Leo-ratified filing), anti-pattern sweep instance A — UNTRACKED at filing time (searched; closest 366/4705/936 are different surfaces). Class: silent-defaults; INV-COMP-1 breach with an INV-SF-4 knock-on.

DEFECT [verified by end-to-end probe]: a fn without a return-type annotation gets Type::dimensionless_scalar() as its signature return type — crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs:277 ("None => Type::dimensionless_scalar(), // default return type"), functions.rs:679 (conformer-fn twin), crates/reify-compiler/src/traits.rs:153 (trait assoc-fn sigs, incl. bodyless fns where no body can ever correct it). Call sites type strictly from the declared/defaulted signature (matched_fn.return_type.clone() at expr.rs:2890/:2993/:3023/:5852). The compiled body's result_expr.result_type is stored but NEVER compared to return_type — the crate has ParamDefaultTypeMismatch (params, task 4318) and the let analogue (task 4705) but no fn-return analogue.

PROBE: fn area(w: Length, h: Length) { w*h } — calls type Real; "constraint a > 5.0" passes compile (the 4490 comparison guard is defeated by the wrong Real), then evals permanently INDETERMINATE ("operator undefined for these operand kinds: Scalar of m^2"); reify check exit 0. (b) Deferred alternative (breadcrumb at the impl site): infer un-annotated return types from the body. (c) Rejected-by-default: hard-require annotations (breaking). NOT killable by the builtin-signature registry (#5068) — this is user-fn body-vs-signature reconciliation, its own seam.

Completed: OCCT binary booleans run twice: the two-shape BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse/Cut/Common constructors already Build(), and the wrapper's explicit Build() clears and reruns — fix all six sites
Description: Every binary OCCT boolean in reify runs the full algorithm TWICE. In OCCT 7.8.1 the two-shape constructors BRepAlgoAPI_Cut(S1, S2, range) / BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse(...) / BRepAlgoAPI_Common(...) call Build(theRange) in their body (BRepAlgoAPI_Cut.cxx:53-60, BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse.cxx:53-60), and BRepAlgoAPI_BooleanOperation::Build begins with an unconditional `NotDone(); Clear();` (BRepAlgoAPI_BooleanOperation.cxx:141-146) that discards the filler and recomputes everything. reify's wrapper constructs with two shapes and then calls .Build() again at all six binary sites in crates/reify-kernel-occt/cpp/occt_wrapper.cpp: boolean_fuse (:1100-1101), boolean_cut (:1114-1115), boolean_common (:1128-1129), boolean_fuse_with_history (:1358-1359), boolean_cut_with_history (:1369-1370), boolean_common_with_history (:1380-1381). Measured in the esc-5215-5 investigation (2026-09-11, standalone OCCT 7.8.1 probe, N=400 holes): 1.46 s spent in the constructor plus 1.42 s in the explicit Build. The production realization path (Engine::execute_realization_ops -> execute_with_history -> OcctRequest::ExecuteWithHistory -> boolean_*_with_history, handle.rs:1394-1402) pays this on every boolean; for designs/litter_tray/top_deck.ri the final shell-minus-holes cut is the multi-minute wait, so this roughly halves it. fuse_shape_list (:1037-1065: default constructor + SetArguments/SetTools + one Build) is already correct — mirror it.

DELIVER: rewrite the six sites as default constructor + SetArguments({left}) + SetTools({right}) + exactly one Build(); keep the IsDone() check, normalize_boolean_result and history extraction unchanged. Also make the task-5213 boolean-pass counter (t_boolean_pass_count, occt_wrapper.cpp:607) increment at the three *_with_history sites (today it counts only the plain trio, so pattern tests are blind to the production path) and update its doc in crates/reify-kernel-occt/src/lib.rs:50-73 to match. Add a regression guard that fails if a two-shape BRepAlgoAPI constructor is followed by Build() again (e.g. a tests/infra source check or a test-fixture probe) — no timing-based assertions (the build farm is heavily loaded; wall time is not a reliable test signal).

RISK TO HANDLE, NOT ASSUME AWAY: in OCCT's default destructive mode the first (discarded) pass mutates the input shapes' edges in place (adds pcurves, raises tolerances — BOPAlgo_PaveFiller_7.cxx:910-921, BOPAlgo_PaveFiller_10.cxx:62-126), so today's second pass runs on already-modified inputs. Removing the first pass may shift tolerance values or golden outputs slightly; if any golden/regression test moves, verify the new value is geometrically equivalent before re-blessing it, and say so in the commit.

WHY IT GATES 5215: with the constructor Build in place, the first half of every binary boolean can never carry a Message_ProgressRange, so it is invisible to the per-evaluation progress/cancel mechanism ruled in esc-5215-5 and cannot be cancelled.

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL: `reify check designs/litter_tray/top_deck.ri` user-CPU time (/usr/bin/time -v, same build profile, before vs after, same host) drops by roughly half, with identical mass, hole census and constraint verdicts; the OCCT suites stay green under both `cargo test` and nextest.

Description: Discharge esc-7281-4's outstanding end-to-end confirmation for task 5099 (INV-GUI-3, user path), which esc-5099-10 recorded as still unperformed when η landed.

WHAT η ALREADY PINS (do not redo): the whole chain below the live GUI is covered by automated tests on 5099's branch — engine (`commit_parameter`'s four-surface ledger, including what a fresh `load_file` re-resolves), the command layer (`set_parameter_impl` / `preview_parameter_impl`, incl. the refused-commit `RefusedParameterWrite` restore), both MCP surfaces, bridge wire names, MechanismPanel's drag/release cadence, and App wiring through the real component tree. The residual gap is exactly the Tauri IPC hop plus real DOM-event-driven component entry, which the component tests exercise against mocked bridges rather than a real webview.

WHAT TO BUILD: a smoke driver in the established `gui/test/visual` shape (`run_*_e2e_smoke.sh` + `smoke_*_e2e.mjs` + a `*.test.ts` predicate suite; copy the conventions `smokeDriverConventions.ts` and `smokeDriverGuards.mjs` enforce, and the `railLengtheningGate` trio as the closest STRUCTURAL model — note it is NOT a behavioural model: it drives `reify_set_parameter`, i.e. the AI path this task forbids). 4. REQUIRED (was "recommended" — promoted by the esc-7680-3 ruling): assert the N preview frames left the file byte-identical, and only the terminal commit wrote. This is not merely the task-1861 perf guard; it is the PROOF that the component's own RAF preview coalescer and 200 ms commit-coalesce window ran, i.e. the proof the driver entered on the user path and not below it. If assertion 4 passes, the trap below cannot have been walked into.

ADDING A TOOL TO THE reify-debug MCP — CANONICAL (consolidates 9 entries, 2026-05-05..2026-06-09, under curator gate esc-5563-1; addendum folded 2026-08-30, see end). Verified against the tree 2026-07-27. DIFFERENT TOPIC, do not merge: DRIVING the debug MCP is topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving (gate esc-5561-1).

AUTHORITY, USE IT INSTEAD OF TRUSTING THIS PROSE: `gui/src/__tests__/debugParity.test.ts` mechanically extracts the ToolDef names from the Rust source (regex over `ToolDef { name: "..." }`) and checks frontend/Rust parity. It is the executable contract; this entry only orients you. If prose and that test disagree, the test wins.

WHERE THE REGISTRY LIVES — a persistent PRD-level misdirection worth stating first. The registry is `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs`: `tool_defs() -> Vec<ToolDef>` and `dispatch_tool(state, name, params)`. It is NOT in `gui/src-tauri/src/debug.rs`, despite several PRDs (GR-016 §2.3 inventory row, mesh-morphing.md cross-ref) and task descriptions calling it "the debug.rs registry". `debug.rs` houses the unrelated `DebugBridge` used for frontend-mediated oneshot RPCs. And there is NO `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_bridge.rs` at all, despite some task metadata referencing it (confirmed absent 2026-07-27).

THE RULE: a FRONTEND-MEDIATED tool — one that reads the DOM or Solid stores rather than the OCCT engine — needs only TWO touch points:
1. a `ToolDef` entry in `tool_defs()` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs) with name, description and an object-typed JSON input_schema;
2. a handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in `gui/src/debug/bridge.ts`.
NO new Rust dispatch match-arm is required. `dispatch_tool`'s default arm — `_ => state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params).await` — already forwards any unmatched tool name to the JS bridge. Consequence worth knowing: a bridge-only handler works via `tools/call` without rebuilding the Tauri binary.

THREE EXCEPTIONS THAT DO NEED MORE:
- STATE-BOUND / ENGINE-OR-DISK tools get an explicit Rust arm, via the `run_on_engine` helper: engine_state, mesh_stats, open_file, wait_for_idle, load_fixture, the stateless morph stats.
- IMAGE-RETURNING tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must ALSO be listed in `is_image_tool()`, or `tools/call` will not strip the data-URL prefix and emit an MCP image content block.
- FRONTEND STORE FIELDS your handler reads must be added to the `DebugStores` type in `gui/src/debug/types.ts`. That type exposes only a STRUCTURAL SUBSET of the real engineStore — e.g. it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297. A field missing there is a silent read failure, not a compile error in the Rust half.

TESTS
- Rust-side, for a frontend-mediated tool, just assert the tool_defs schema (object type, required fields) — there is no Rust behaviour to test. Precedents live alongside in debug_server.rs's own test module (tool_defs_includes_set_camera, tool_defs_contains_set_test_mode, tool_defs_includes_screenshot_window, is_image_tool_recognizes_both_screenshot_variants).
- Frontend bridge unit tests go in `gui/src/__tests__/debugBridge.test.tsx` — note the `.TSX` extension. Task metadata `files` lists sometimes say `.ts`, which does not exist.
- JSDOM GOTCHA: jsdom has no layout engine, so `getBoundingClientRect()` returns width 0 under vitest. A handler that needs visibility must use CSS visibility instead — this is why the `ui_outline` handler does.

LINE NUMBERS ROT — cite symbols. The retired entries pinned dispatch_tool's default arm at "~:481"; as of 2026-07-27 it is at :1069, with tool_defs at :35, is_image_tool at :1030, dispatch_tool at :1047 and run_on_engine at :1077. Grep the symbol.

ADDENDUM (2026-08-30, folds 35275359 — this entry's own norm is to extend it rather than write another): adding a ToolDef also reds FOUR drift surfaces beyond the two-touch-point rule above, which must be updated in the SAME commit: (1) the dispatch_tool match arm itself, for a state-bound tool (or confirm the de…[truncated, 5373 chars total]

entry_text: Convention (task 5158): a committed bash wrapper that runs `uv` must not hardcode a path or trust PATH. It sources scripts/lib/resolve_uv.sh, the single copy of the UV_BIN -> PATH -> $HOME/.local/bin -> /usr/local/bin ladder. Locate the lib relative to the script itself with the fork-free idiom `case "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" in */*) d="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}";; *) d=.;; esac`, never `$(dirname ...)` (unfindable under an empty PATH) or $REPO (tests point it at a fake dir, cgl hardcodes main). Use a guarded `source "$lib" || { echo "${0##*/}: ERROR: ..." >&2; exit 127; }`, then `X="$(require_uv_bin)" || exit $?` AFTER the .env source. scripts/tests/test_resolve_uv_lib.py::test_only_the_lib_defines_the_resolver fails if any other tracked .sh defines resolve_uv_bin/require_uv_bin, and its CALLERS tuple is where a new wrapper gets wiring coverage.

Completed: Merge-gate flake suppression can launder a killed/timed-out sibling module leg: a passing re-run of another module's flake flips the joined red to PASS
Description: Follow-up found by the architect of task 5492 (merge-gate crash-truncation fix). This is OUTSIDE 5492's scope. 5492 makes the discriminator refuse suppression when the failing test_output carries an xdist worker-death marker. This is a SIBLING no-verdict hole of the same INV-1 class that 5492 does not close.

MECHANISM (by code reading at base 4e76fbd912, NOT reproduced):
- verify.py::_aggregate_results '\n'-joins per-module VerifyResults into the merge gate's single scoped result.
- Suppose one module's TEST leg was externally killed (rc<0, FailureCategory.INFRA_KILL, verdict_indeterminate) or timed out (INFRA_TIMEOUT), producing no FAILED short-summary line. Meanwhile another module completed with a genuine load flake.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_runner.py::LocalRunner.run_merge_verify calls verify.apply_merge_flake_suppression on the joined red.
- verify.py::confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict extracts only the flake's node-id, re-runs it, sees it pass, and returns passes_in_isolation.
- The hook replace()s the whole result to passed=True / merge_flake_suppressed, so the killed module's suite lands with no verdict.
Host OOM pressure plausibly produces both at once: one pytest killed while siblings run starved.

The structured signal already exists. VerifyResult.failing_leg_categories (task 3173) carries one category per failing leg, and _aggregate_results unions it across failing children. So a discriminator precondition can refuse (unconfirmable, e.g. 'leg_without_verdict:<category>') when any failing TEST leg's category produced no verdict. Decide which categories qualify: INFRA_KILL certainly; INFRA_TIMEOUT likely.

Also decide whether a failing lint/type leg should block suppression at the merge gate. Today it deliberately does not: see confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict's requires_clean_other_legs note.

Since task 5580 landed on 2026-09-21, the merge gate's isolated re-run genuinely executes and can return passes_in_isolation, so this hole is armed, not merely latent.

entry_text: Counting pytest-xdist workers of a scoped run (measured 2026-10-05, task 5469; peer of 64c791bb under topic verify-resource-measurement). Under `-q` with non-tty output xdist never prints `created: N/M workers` — TerminalDistReporter.getstatus returns only "bringing up nodes..." at verbose < 0 — so a verify-shaped `-q` log cannot prove the worker count. Reading PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER from /proc/<pid>/environ UNDER-counts (read 5 of 16): that file is the process's initial environment and xdist sets the variable after the worker starts. What worked: run the command in a named scope (`systemd-run --user --scope --unit=<u>`), and from OUTSIDE the scope (so the sampler's CPU stays out of the scope's cpu.stat) poll `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/<u>.scope/cgroup.procs` every 2 s, counting processes whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains execnet's bootstrap `exec(eval(sys.stdin.readline()))` (grep -zlsF). It read exactly 16 at PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS=16, but it is an upper bound: suites that spawn their own xdist subprocesses (scripts read 2 even when run serially with -p no:xdist). pids.peak counts threads, so it is not a worker count. Scripts: plans/verify-parallelism-trial-e1-report.md §4.
target_text: pytest/pytest-xdist terminal output under -q (measured 2026-09-25, pytest 9.0.3, xdist 3.8.0; task 5337). -q suppresses: the xdist bailout literals ('worker gwN crashed and worker restarting disabled', 'maximum crashed workers reached: N') and 'replacing crashed worker gwN' — all gated on verbose >= 0. -q keeps: '[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated'; the "worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'" FAILURES notice; the percentage progress lines (shown without a file prefix, since xdist sets terminalreporter.showfspath=False in distribution mode); and the '!!! stopping after N failures !!!' / '!!! xdist.dsession.Interrupted: ... !!!' banners. The -q-robust way to tell a truncated run from a recovered one is the FINAL progress line: pytest counts xdist's synthesized crash report toward progress and floors reported*100//collected, so an xdist bailout (triggershutdown) ends the loop normally and the progress fill IS written but reads below [100%] (measured as low as [44%]); a --max-worker-restart>0 recovery reaches [100%]. An -x/--maxfail/KeyboardInterrupt stop instead raises out of the run loop, so pytest skips the final progress fill entirely (no [NN%] on the last line) — a different signature from a bailout. Corroboration: all 17 crash-bearing logs in data/verify-logs (as of 2026-09-25) are -q legs ending at 42-99% with no bailout literal. To reproduce: build a throwaway /tmp project with one os._exit(1) test plus ~150 passing tests, run via the worktree .venv `python -m pytest -n 2 -p no:randomly -p no:cacheprovider -q` and diff against non-q output.

entry_text: reify-build-utils::find() trusts any NON-EMPTY <DEP>_LIB_DIR / <DEP>_INCLUDE_DIR override without checking for the sentinel file. Pointing GMSH_LIB_DIR at a bogus path therefore does NOT force a stub (no-has_gmsh) build: it sets has_gmsh and then fails at link time. Only an empty override counts as unset. To keep stub hosts green, write cfg-safe code by construction, for example by path-qualifying has_gmsh-only calls in files that are not gated on has_gmsh, instead of relying on a local stub build to check it.
target_text: To exercise a reify crate's `#[cfg(not(has_gmsh))]` (stub-build) code paths on a host that HAS `/opt/reify-deps`, you must temporarily suppress that crate's own `has_gmsh` emission in its `build.rs` and revert afterwards — env vars cannot do it. `reify_build_utils::find_dir_with_override` (crates/reify-build-utils/src/lib.rs:162) returns a non-empty `GMSH_LIB_DIR`/`GMSH_INCLUDE_DIR` override ON TRUST without checking the sentinel exists, so pointing them at a nonexistent path still makes `find(NativeDep::Gmsh)` succeed and still sets `has_gmsh`. This matters because `scripts/verify.sh` runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, so a warning emitted only in the stub configuration (e.g. an `unused variable` whose sole reader is `#[cfg(has_gmsh)]`) is a hard gate failure that is invisible on a gmsh-equipped host.

entry_text: In reify tests/infra/*.sh files that run under `set -euo pipefail`, a derive-from-source scrape written with grep (`grep -o`, `grep -c`) inside `$(...)` ABORTS THE WHOLE FILE when it matches nothing (grep rc 1 + pipefail), instead of failing a non-vacuity assert — so a drifted/renamed Rust symbol kills the suite silently-ish rather than reding one assertion. Write derivations with `sed -n 's/.../\1/p'` and `awk '{ n += gsub(/pat/, "&") } END { print n + 0 }'` (both exit 0 on a miss), and skip empty derived values in probe loops with `[ -n "$x" ] || continue`, since e.g. plan_for_branch "" aborts on `printf > "$FIX_B/"`. Verify by pointing the derivation at /dev/null under `set -euo pipefail`. Precedent: PDOCCOVER-DRIFT in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh (task 7987).
target_text: In reify's bash scripts running under `set -euo pipefail`, a `grep ... | head -n1 | sed ...` extraction is a latent abort: `head -n1` closes the pipe after one line, so on multi-line input `grep` dies of SIGPIPE (141) and `pipefail` propagates it, and on no-match input `grep` exits 1. Such a pipeline often appears harmless only because its enclosing function is called exclusively as `fn && ...` (or in an `if`), which suppresses errexit for the WHOLE function body — an invisible dependency that any later call outside a condition context turns into a silent mid-run abort, and which meanwhile swallows the distinction between malformed input and absent input. Prefer one `awk '/pat/ { sub(...); print; exit }' file` with no pipeline and no early-closing consumer: it exits 0 with empty output when nothing matches, so the caller's own emptiness check reports the real reason. Found and fixed in scripts/with-jcodemunch-serve.sh's SSE `data:`-line probe extraction (task #6109).
