entry_text: Reify: to probe engine build diagnostics on real OCCT without compiling a test, run the warm lane's prebuilt `target/release/reify build <file>.ri -o <out>.step` and grep its stdout/stderr. Diagnostics print as `info: ...` / `warning: ...` lines; a file without a top-of-file `module` declaration also emits W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING, which is harmless. Example: the TopologyAttributeLocalIndexReassigned tie diagnostics for `tube(...)` with a `faces(...)` binding reproduced this way in ~seconds (task #7340 planning, 2026-10-05).
target_text: Cheap way to adjudicate a Reify geometry-behaviour claim WITHOUT a rebuild (used successfully 2026-09-03 for esc-7248-3): the MAIN checkout at /home/leo/src/reify usually carries a recent `target/release/reify`. Prove it embeds the code under discussion by running `git log --oneline --since="<binary mtime>" -- <the specific source files>` and showing ZERO commits touching them — that is a far cheaper and more defensible warrant than rebuilding, and it survives a reviewer's "was your binary stale?" objection. Then run probes with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/opt/reify-deps/lib ./target/release/reify eval <probe.ri>` and filter the noisy OCCT STEP-writer banner with `grep -v "^\["`. Two .ri gotchas that cost a round-trip: the `module <name>` declaration MUST match the FILE STEM or you get `E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH`, and unary minus is not available for angle literals — write `0deg - 90deg` rather than `-90deg`. Use `reify eval` for values and `reify check` for the type/constraint surface; they disagree, and that disagreement is itself evidence (e.g. `reify check` accepts `sweep(<Curve>, <Curve>)` at exit 0 against a documented Surface-typed signature).

orchestrator/tests/_merge_lane_fakes.py gained the shared way to drive a merge lane in tests (task 5034).
- merge_through_lane(lane, queue, request, timeout=...) runs the lane, submits a single or train request through the lane's own queue, returns the MergeOutcome, and stops the lane.
- running_lane(lane) is an async context manager yielding a LaneRun. Use it for multi-submission tests. On exit it stops the lane and awaits run() unsuppressed, so a lane crash raises instead of being swallowed.
- LaneRun.outcome(request) waits on {run task, request.result}, so a lane that dies first surfaces as a crash, not as a TimeoutError.
- times_out() sits next to passes(), fails() and raises().

The reviewer had found that the first version of merge_through_lane suppressed BaseException on the run() task, which turned a crashing lane into a bare 120s TimeoutError. Do not write per-file create_task(lane.run()) / stop() lifecycles; use running_lane.

entry_text: Gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 7448): a reify gmsh-produced VolumeMesh of the 1.0x0.1x0.1 box (refine_with_size_field at uniform 0.05) carries many ORPHAN vertices (80 vertices on the x_max plane, only 20 referenced by any tet), so coordinate node-set selection must run on volume_mesh_to_solver_mesh's compacted output, not raw vm.vertices. Vertices are stored as f32, so derive expected face centroids from the mesh's own AABB (f32(0.1)/2 is 7.45e-10 off 0.05). refine_marked_elements retriangulates the WHOLE surface (classify_surfaces + create_geometry), so a remesh changes the tip-face node set even when no marked element touches that face (root-only marks: 20 -> 34 tip nodes). With the refine path's NumThreads=1 pin, the output was bit-identical across repeats.
target_text: Reify gmsh realized refine (reify-kernel-gmsh refine_volume_with_size_field, used by RealizedAdaptiveProblem::refine) re-triangulates the BOUNDARY SURFACE too (classify_surfaces + create_geometry + mesh_generate(3) under the background size field), so boundary node sets (e.g. the cantilever's coordinate-selected x_max tip face) change across every remesh even though the input surface Mesh is held fixed. Any BC/load applied per node must therefore be mesh-consistent (e.g. reify_solver_elastic::apply_patch_resultant, task 7448), not a per-node equal split.

orchestrator/tests/_merge_lane_fakes.py gained the shared way to drive a merge lane in tests (task 5034).
- merge_through_lane(lane, queue, request, timeout=...) runs the lane, submits a single or train request through the lane's own queue, returns the MergeOutcome, and stops the lane.
- running_lane(lane) is an async context manager yielding a LaneRun. Use it for multi-submission tests. On exit it stops the lane and awaits run() unsuppressed, so a lane crash raises instead of being swallowed.
- LaneRun.outcome(request) waits on {run task, request.result}, so a lane that dies first surfaces as a crash, not as a TimeoutError.
- times_out() sits next to passes(), fails() and raises().

The reviewer had found that the first version of merge_through_lane suppressed BaseException on the run() task, which turned a crashing lane into a bare 120s TimeoutError. Do not write per-file create_task(lane.run()) / stop() lifecycles; use running_lane.

Completed: pkill -f pattern textually matches its own invoking command line, self-killing the shell (exit 144) (cross-repo refile of reify #7922)
Description: CROSS-REPO REFILE. Reify legibility-census candidate #7922: an agent runs `pkill -f "<exact string>"` where <exact string> is identical to the target process's full command line; because pkill -f matches against full argv and the pkill invocation's own eval'd command line embeds that same literal pattern, pkill matches and kills its own wrapping shell/process group instead of (or in addition to) the intended target, producing exit 144 with no clear signal attribution. Dark-factory's OWN confusion-codebook (docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml) already records multiple independent sightings of this exact pattern in dark-factory sessions (pkill -f self-matching against pytest/watcher command lines), so this is a well-established, harness-wide hazard, not a reify defect. Remediation is role-prompt guidance (prefer a distinguishing marker not present in the invoking command, or `pgrep` first to confirm the target set before pkill) and/or a guard. Completed: Merge lane never un-stacks a train member whose predecessor leaves the queue without landing — the orphan's conflicts are then reported as the member's own
Description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 while resolving esc-4137-3/esc-4137-4 (steward). Task 4137's merge was blocked for reasons that had nothing to do with task 4137.

THE DEFECT. When a train is formed, an order>0 member is rebased onto its predecessor's branch tip rather than main (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::_resolve_predecessor_tip, "train-predecessor tip or main"). That is correct at formation. But if the predecessor subsequently leaves the merge queue WITHOUT LANDING, nothing un-stacks the member. The member's branch silently keeps carrying every one of the predecessor's commits, and its next merge_request therefore reports the PREDECESSOR's conflicts against main as its own.

THE SIGHTING. task/4137 (7 own commits, all dashboard) was stacked behind task/4480 at 2026-09-08 21:49 (reflog task/4137@{0} = 'rebase (finish) onto 9788a34b13'). Task 4480 then went to status=pending and left the queue, never merged; merge_status(task_id=4480) = unknown. Ten days later 4137's merge attempt reported 15 conflicts — of which 14 were 4480's fused-memory test refactor vs main's task-3895 load_script_module migration. Replaying only 4137's own delta (`git merge-tree --merge-base=9788a34b13 main <tip>`) conflicts in exactly ONE file, its own index.html cache-buster.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE BRANCH. The failure is mis-attributed by construction. The merger sees a 15-way conflict "in task 4137" and every available remedy is wrong: resolving toward main silently DROPS the absent predecessor's entire deliverable (here 786 lines of new files plus a 15-suite rewrite that exists nowhere else); combining both sides lands the predecessor's whole deliverable through the member's merge, outside the member's plan scope and file locks, and requires implementing the predecessor against a main ~2145 commits ahead. Both destructive options look locally reasonable to an agent that has not audited the branch's reflog. Only the third — un-stack — is correct, and identifying it requires noticing the stacking in the first place. Two escalation rounds were consumed on this one instance before a human-authority role took the ref rewrite.

COMPLETION CONDITION. The lane should detect, at merge_request admission time, that a branch's merge-base against main is a non-landed sibling task's branch tip, and un-stack it automatically via the operation the lane already owns — git_ops.py::materialize_member_solo(predecessor_ref=...), equivalently `git rebase --onto main <predecessor_tip> <branch>` — before attempting the merge. Escalate only if THAT rebase conflicts. Suggested shape: on dequeue, resolve the recorded train predecessor (or derive it by testing whether merge-base(branch, main) is the tip of another task's branch), check whether it is an ancestor of main, and if not, un-stack. Regression test: a member stacked on a predecessor branch that never lands merges solo on its own delta and reports only its own conflicts.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: how many other branches are currently in this state. The condition is cheap to detect in bulk (for each task branch, is merge-base(branch, main) equal to some other task/* tip that is not an ancestor of main?) and each hit is a mis-attributed merge failure waiting to happen. Task 4480 itself remains status=pending with 15 commits living only on task/4480; it is the one carrier of that work and should be scheduled before its base drifts further.

NOT A DUPLICATE (searched): 1878 (worktree-reuse rebases onto main unconditionally) is the mirror-image bug and is done; 1867/4737/4953 are merge-deferred stranding after coalescing; 4669 is a requeue rebase dropping a commit whose patch no longer applies; 2403 is a branch reset to an unrelated tip. None covers a member left stacked on a predecessor that exited the queue unlanded.

target_text: Coalesce-train non-tip members leave `task/<ID>` PERMANENTLY stale-by-rebase, so `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<ID> main` returns rc=1 forever on work that DID land. Mechanism: the train merges only the tip branch (`tip_branch=tip_req.branch`; `_do_train_merge` step (c) — the tip "by stacking, already carries all member commits") and step (b) rebases that tip onto main first, rewriting every stacked commit's SHA; the member's own ref is never advanced to the rewritten commits. rc=128 never fires for such a member either, because `GitOps._delete_branch_if_on_main` retains any branch carrying commits beyond main. The correct landing test is CONTENT, not ancestry: `git cherry main task/<ID>` → landed iff the output is NON-EMPTY and every line starts with `-`. The non-empty conjunct is required — a zero-commit branch prints nothing, so `git cherry ... | grep -q '^+' || echo landed` falsely reports it landed. In-repo authority for both the test and the conjunct: `GitOps.rebase_preserving_task_commits` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py (`bool(cherry_lines) and all(line.startswith('-') ...)`). Verified specimen 2026-08-22: task 4104 (train coalesce-4181-b2a290cd, tip merge d25b24468c) — no own merge marker, ref alive at dc82a17583, ancestry rc=1, yet all 5 commits marked `-` by git cherry.

entry_text: AMENDMENT to the task-3883 caller-census gotcha (tests/scripts/verify_command_invariants.py). Measured in task 5472, 2026-10-05: new callers can join a shared module WITHOUT any migration task, and when they do, nobody re-counts the census. Three files began calling positional_targets on 2026-10-03/04: test_member_scripts_type_gate.py, test_hook_ruff_targets_drift.py and test_hook_magicmock_test_dirs_drift.py. The docstring still said "five callers"; the real count was nine call sites across eight files. Two rules follow. (1) Take the caller list from a grep, never from the module's own count: `grep -rn 'positional_targets' tests/scripts`. (2) Count per CALL SITE, not per file. test_fallback_verify_config.py passes a value_flags set at _fleet_pytest_suite_names and none at _lint_leg_targets, and test_scripts_module_config.py::_targets passes a set only for its pytest leg, so a per-file count is ambiguous. The census also needed a third check kind beyond COVERAGE (inert to phantoms) and EXISTS (red on phantoms): EQUALS, where the extracted list is compared against a second copy such as the hook's RUFF_TARGETS array. EQUALS also turns red on a phantom. Task 5472 rewrote the census as one per-call-site table (value-flag set + check kind) so the next new caller is a one-row add.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 3883): when an N-copy extraction migrates the Nth caller onto a shared module, the count sweep in that module's prose is INCOMPLETE BY DEFAULT — the module HEADER docstring gets updated (it is the obvious prose home, and it names the copies explicitly so the omission is loud), while the counts inside the module's own FUNCTION docstrings silently rot.

MEASURED. Task 3883 brought the fifth copy of the command-parsing trio onto tests/scripts/verify_command_invariants.py. The header was correctly re-counted FOUR→FIVE, including a new paragraph calling that very drift class "the cautionary one". Three unscoped counts inside function docstrings were missed and had to be fixed in an amendment pass: anchor_split's "every anchor the four callers use", positional_targets' "one implementation serves four call sites unchanged", and — worst — positional_targets' PHANTOM CENSUS, "Measured across the four callers: THREE assert existence ... while only two of those three supply a set", which the new caller falsified on every clause at once (it asserts existence at both call sites and supplies no value_flags, making it five callers / FOUR asserting existence / two of four supplying a set).

THE CHECK is one grep over the canonical file for the OLD count word (`grep -n "four\|FOUR"`), run AFTER the header edit, not instead of it.

THE DISCRIMINATOR that makes that grep safe, and the reason a blind sed would corrupt correct history: sweep only counts in UNSCOPED present tense. Counts SCOPED to a prior task stay put — "the four task-3745 callers therefore stay on strict exact-token matching" and "before task 3745's amendment pass the literal was spelled in four files" remained four and are still true. In this file five occurrences of "four" were correct history and four were stale; the ratio is close enough to 1:1 that you must read each one.

DON'T JUST INCREMENT — RE-MEASURE. A census with internal structure ("THREE of four assert existence, two of those three supply a set") has several numbers that move independently, and the new caller's own properties decide each. Read the new caller's call sites (does it assert existence? does it pass value_flags?) before touching any of them.

RECIPROCAL CITATIONS come with the census. This one ended "the remaining exposure is root_lint's, and it is recorded on that guard's own _ruff_targets rather than papered over here". Widening it to name a second guard makes a claim ABOUT that guard's docstring which was not yet true — so the record had to be added there in the same commit. Any census clause of the form "recorded on X's own Y" obliges you to go write it at X.

NOT THE SAME as the task-3897 norm ("dated live measurements belong in exactly ONE operator doc, never restated in module docstrings"). That one governs point-in-time probe counts, whose right fix is deletion plus a pointer. A caller census is a STRUCTURAL fact about the codebase, mechanically checkable by grep at any moment, and belongs in the shared module it describes — fix it, do not delete it and point elsewhere.

entry_text: GOTCHA (measured 2026-10-02, task 4155, CPython 3.13): asyncio's Process.wait() does not return when the child exits. It returns only once every stdout/stderr pipe is closed: base_subprocess._call_connection_lost wakes the _exit_waiters, and connection_lost only fires after all pipes disconnect. So after a direct-child kill, `await proc.wait()` hangs for as long as any surviving grandchild holds an inherited pipe — e.g. df_pytest_isolation.PIPE_CLOSING_LEAKER_SRC's FOREGROUND `sleep 300` (only its background job redirects its stdio). Consequence for containment tests: if you await the interrupted call FIRST and only then assert the grandchild died, a regression makes the test HANG until pytest-timeout fires instead of failing. Instead, start the call as a task, read the leaked pid via asyncio.to_thread(read_leaked_pid, ...), cancel the task or let it time out, then poll the grandchild (zombie counts as exited) while the call is still in flight, and await the task last. shared/tests/test_git_async.py section (j) uses this shape.
target_text: asyncio's Process.wait() resolves on the child process's own exit notification via the event loop's child watcher, NOT on pipe EOF — only Process.communicate() waits for pipe EOF (reading stdout/stderr streams to completion). A whole-process-group SIGKILL on timeout is valuable for reaping orphaned grandchildren that would otherwise leak/keep running, not for unblocking a hung wait(). This was a factual inaccuracy corrected in deterministic_runner.py's _terminate_process_tree docstring during the task 2090 review pass.

entry_text: Tokio test gotcha (reify, task #6195): the FIRST poll of a freshly spawned `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` JoinHandle is almost always Pending even on an idle blocking pool, because the new pool thread has not started the work yet. A test asserting "blocking work did not run" (e.g. a saturated-pool fixture self-test) must re-poll after a settle window (reify-lsp's blocking_work::test_support self-test uses 500 ms); measured: first-poll-only stayed green when the fixture's max_blocking_threads(1) was mutated to (2). reify-lsp now exports `blocking_work::test_support::{SaturatedBlockingPool, poll_once}` behind the `test-support` feature for telling BlockingWorkPlacement::BlockingPool from CallingThread through public seams.
target_text: To test deterministically whether async code offloads to tokio's blocking pool (with no thread-name hooks or timing races), saturate the pool. Build a current_thread runtime with max_blocking_threads(1) and occupy its only blocking thread with a spawn_blocking that parks on an mpsc Receiver until released. A single poll (std::future::poll_fn) of the code under test is then Pending if and only if it went to the pool, and inline work completes regardless. Planned for reify task 6195 as reify_lsp::blocking_work::test_support::SaturatedBlockingPool.

entry_text: Fixing HostAllocator.free_host_count to count only acquirable slots (FREE and, for a remote, not quarantined; task 4929 defect 2, landed with task 5303) broke test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py::TestRedispatchSpeculativeConservation::test_speculative_redispatch_item_stays_counted_through_real_pipeline (task 2063). Its docstring used the over-count as its MECHANISM: quarantining the remote made the guard pass and acquire() fail, which parked a speculative item on _redispatch. After the fix, the only honest production route to that state is a concurrent non-loop acquirer (the drift check) winning the slot between the guard and the acquire. The test was re-mechanised on a HostAllocator subclass double (_DriftCheckTakesRemoteAllocator, injected through an allocator_cls kwarg on _inject_two_host_allocator). Lesson: when fixing a defect, grep for tests whose fixtures depend on that defect; they go red for a reason unrelated to the behaviour they guard.
target_text: HostAllocator (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_runner.py) has TWO independent ways a remote host leaves the acquirable pool, and tests must not conflate them: the shared `_quarantine` set, and a PARKED `_slots` entry left by `cancel_and_release` when the cancel RPC returns rc != 0 and every `probe_clean()` poll fails. `acquire_remote` requires BOTH `_SLOT_FREE` and non-quarantine, so `clear_quarantine` (which only does `_quarantine.discard`) cannot recover a PARKED host. To build a PARKED fixture you must acquire the host FIRST and quarantine it AFTER — seeding the quarantine up front makes `acquire_remote` refuse the host, so the cancel path is never reached and the slot never parks.

entry_text: Reify gotcha (task #7809): since #7809, an ERROR child of a `trait` body is a located parse error, `syntax error in trait body`. Before that, `lower_trait_members` dropped it silently. So a value-less trait `let x : Length` and a trait-body `port …` no longer vanish: `reify_test_support::compile_source` (which calls parse_or_panic) PANICS on them. To observe the error use `compile_source_allow_parse_errors`, where the compiler forwards it as `parse error: syntax error in trait body`. When measuring tree-sitter recovery, use the linked runtime (tree-sitter 0.24.7 per Cargo.lock), not the host `tree-sitter` CLI (0.26.x): the two recover differently. Example: the CLI shows integration_corner_cases.ri's broken trait as a source-level ERROR, while the runtime makes it a trait-body child.
target_text: Reify trait-body parsing facts (2026-09-25): tree-sitter trait_member has no port_declaration arm, and ANY non-member text in a trait body (a `port` line or pure garbage) becomes an ERROR node that ts_parser.rs::lower_trait_members drops with no diagnostic (task #7809 adds the ERROR arm). But ts_parser already routes trait members through lower_member, which HAS a port_declaration arm, MemberDecl::Port/PortDecl exist, and the GUI lezer TraitDeclaration deliberately reuses the over-permissive Block (accepts ports). traits.rs::compile_trait ends in a `_ =>` skip arm that silently drops unhandled MemberDecl kinds — a sequencing hazard for ANY new trait member kind: land the compile_trait arm with the grammar arm or it compiles clean and is unenforced. Adding RequirementKind variants forces 6 exhaustive match sites across 5 files (types.rs value_bearing_members, trait_requirements.rs collect_all_requirements, conformance/checker.rs, reify-doc-build build.rs lower_trait, reify-test-support trait_def.rs x2).

entry_text:
The fused-memory set_task_priority_override docstring overstates what pins and reserve_now do (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py). It says 'Pin this task to the front of the queue' and, for reserve_now, 'Reserve the next worker slot'.
In fact:
- A pin gives only a first try, each scheduler tick, at all-or-nothing module-lock acquisition, with no reservation.
- reserve_now installs parks once, at the task's RAW priority, and reserves no worker slot.
Operators pin expecting movement that the code does not provide. As of 2026-09-29 no task owns the docstring fix; it was deliberately kept out of 6040 to avoid adding a fused-memory file to it.
target_text: GOTCHA, operator levers for a lock-starved task holding a PARTIAL park (dark-factory, 2026-09-25): (1) request_park_eviction(task) is REFUSED by the D4 live-owner guard whenever the task is pending with deps satisfied (a reservation_force_evict_refused event is emitted, the row is consumed, nothing changes), so it cannot reset your own live task's park. (2) set_task_priority_override(reserve_now=True) widens the park, but Scheduler._phase_reserve_now installs at the task's RAW priority (coerce_tier(task['priority'])), NOT its boost_tier. And install_parks pushes a DUPLICATE (owner, rank) entry onto stacks the owner already tops. On a boost-critical task with raw priority 'high', that demotes its own rank-0 parks under rank-1 duplicates, and a same-tier critical competitor can then shadow it (verified in an in-memory ModuleLockTable sim). The safe sequence: update_task(priority=<boost tier>), then reserve_now=True, wait for the reserve_now_consumed event in runs.db, then restore the raw priority. Equal-rank duplicate entries are inert, and _remove_owner clears them together. reserve_now is consumed only on a scheduler tick, and ticks run only when a slot frees (gaps of up to 4h observed).

Completed: harness.py: gc_run_config_dir unreachable on a second cancellation in shielded finally blocks
Description: Follow-up filed from task 4431 (escalation_id agent-followup-4431), which shielded the `update_run_stage_reports` persistence call in the `finally` blocks of `ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py, shield site ~line 3560) and `ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass` (~line 5501) against a second asyncio cancellation arriving mid-write.

Residual gap, documented in task 4431's design decision 3 and in "Known residual (task 4431)" code comments at both shield sites: `await asyncio.shield(...)` protects the WRITE itself once it exists as its own Task, but the *awaiting frame* in the `finally` block is still interruptible — a second cancellation arriving while the shielded write is in flight still raises `CancelledError` at that `await asyncio.shield(...)` expression in the outer frame. That means the `gc_run_config_dir` cleanup block immediately following each shield site (harness.py ~3572-3578 for run_full_cycle, ~5512-5518 for _run_remediation_pass) remains unreachable on that path — exactly as it was BEFORE task 4431's fix, so this is not a regression, but it is a real pre-existing gap: a run's per-run recon CLI config dir is not garbage-collected when a second cancellation lands during the finally's persistence write.

Task 4431 deliberately did not fix this (see its design decision 3, verbatim): "Swallowing BaseException around the shielded await would be safe on the exception paths (an exception raised inside a finally that is already unwinding does not suppress the propagating exception), but NOT on the success path: after `return run` at ~3441, a swallow would let an outer `.cancel()` be absorbed and the task complete with a return value instead of cancelling — an uncancellable coroutine, a semantics change well beyond this task's remit." Resolving this residual requires a design that discriminates "safe to swallow because we are already unwinding due to a previous cancellation" from "the return-path completion the outer caller is legitimately trying to cancel" — that discrimination is the actual scope of this follow-up. Until it's solved, the GC block simply stays skipped on this narrow double-cancellation race, same as today.

Files: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py — both `finally` blocks (ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle and ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass).

Suggested priority: low — pre-existing behavior (not a regression from task 4431), and the blast radius is bounded to one leaked per-run config dir per occurrence of this narrow double-cancellation race.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED (worktree HEAD 6570799c7d; main d545567ca4 carries no diff to harness.py or test_harness.py): both "Known residual (task 4431)" sites are still present on main.
- run_full_cycle finally: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py ~4099-4146. It calls _flush_cycle_summaries, then ensure_future(update_run_stage_reports) with an add_done_callback(_log_stage_reports_write_failure), then `await asyncio.shield(stage_reports_write)`, then `if run.status != RunStatus.interrupted: gc_run_config_dir(...)`.
- _run_remediation_pass finally: ~6378-6434. Same shape, except the GC is unconditional (a remediation run is "Always 'failed', never 'interrupted'", per the except-CancelledError handler at ~6320).

CORRECTION to the task-4431 memory entry recorded 2026-09-03 (id 2a2b23f1): its residual note claims making harness.py's gc_run_config_dir reachable after a second cancellation "needs a BaseException swallow, which on a success path would absorb an outer .cancel() ... an uncancellable coroutine." That's not right, and it conflates two independent things. A bare `try: await asyncio.shield(write) finally: gc_run_config_dir(...)` makes the GC block reachable WITHOUT swallowing anything — gc_run_config_dir is synchronous filesystem work with no awaits, so putting it in a `finally` does not re-enable the success-path cancellation-swallow hazard. That hazard is specific to wrapping the shielded AWAIT ITSELF in `except BaseException: ...` (which WOULD absorb a second cancellation arriving on the success path and make the coroutine return a value instead of cancelling) — it has nothing to do with whether the code AFTER the shielded await runs. Task 4431's amendment pass (2026-09-05, reviewer finding, commit 9c3024bf4e) corrected harness.py's two "Known residual" comments to say the gc-reachability fix is deferred by SCOPE (this task's remit was the shield alone), not by this false technical necessity. Any future reasoning about this residual should use the corrected comments in harness.py, not the 2026-09-03 memory's framing.

SEPARATE, genuinely new discovery verified by reading cpython 3.13.9's asyncio.tasks.shield source directly in this repo's venv: asyncio.shield()'s own `_inner_done_callback` ALREADY calls `inner.exception()` even when the outer future was cancelled — specifically "to mark inner's result as retrieved" and silence the generic "Task exception was never retrieved" GC warning — but it discards the exception object without logging it anywhere. So a real exception raised inside a shield-detached Task (e.g. a DB error hitting update_run_stage_reports during a second cancellation) produces NO trace at all today: not even the generic GC warning, let alone a structured log naming the run_id. A review comment predicting "this could surface as an unretrieved-future warning" is being optimistic — it surfaces as literally nothing. Generalizes to every shield-on-cancellation-path site in harness.py (complete_run, restore_drained, update_run_stage_reports): if the shielded coroutine can raise something other than CancelledError, that failure is invisible unless the caller retrieves it first. Fix applied at the update_run_stage_reports sites (task 4431, commit 9c3024bf4e): asyncio.ensure_future() the write yourself and add_done_callback a small logger (checking task.cancelled() first, since .exception() raises CancelledError on a cancelled future) BEFORE handing the Task to asyncio.shield — your callback registers first and gets first crack at task.exception(), turning silence into a structured logger.error() line.

entry_text: In reify tests/infra/*.sh files that run under `set -euo pipefail`, a derive-from-source scrape written with grep (`grep -o`, `grep -c`) inside `$(...)` ABORTS THE WHOLE FILE when it matches nothing (grep rc 1 + pipefail), instead of failing a non-vacuity assert — so a drifted/renamed Rust symbol kills the suite silently-ish rather than reding one assertion. Write derivations with `sed -n 's/.../\1/p'` and `awk '{ n += gsub(/pat/, "&") } END { print n + 0 }'` (both exit 0 on a miss), and skip empty derived values in probe loops with `[ -n "$x" ] || continue`, since e.g. plan_for_branch "" aborts on `printf > "$FIX_B/"`. Verify by pointing the derivation at /dev/null under `set -euo pipefail`. Precedent: PDOCCOVER-DRIFT in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh (task 7987).
target_text: In reify's bash scripts running under `set -euo pipefail` (or any shell with `set -o pipefail`), `printf '%s' "$haystack" | grep -qF -- "$needle"` (or `grep -q` generally) intermittently reports a genuine MATCH as a MISS: grep -q exits the instant it matches and closes the pipe, the bash-builtin printf writer is killed by SIGPIPE, and pipefail surfaces printf's 141 exit as the pipeline's status even though grep itself exited 0. Measured at 0.14% per call (28 misses / 20000 iterations, PIPESTATUS == "141 0" on every miss) over a ~1.1KB payload — first found in tests/infra/test_occt_deps_preflight.sh (task 6493, follow-up to esc-5870-13) and reconfirmed independently at main 1d15d13083. Because the rate is uniform per call, a DIFFERENT assertion fails each run, so it masquerades as a race/infra-contention flake rather than this specific bug (~2.8% per run across ~20 such asserts in one file). Fix with the fork-free `case "$haystack" in *"$needle"*)` for literal substrings (quote the needle to keep matching literal) or a herestring `grep -qF -- "$needle" <<<"$haystack"` for genuine regexes — never with `|| true` or by disabling pipefail; both measured 0 misses / 20000. A pipeline inside a fresh `bash -c '...'` is IMMUNE (bash -c does not inherit pipefail — SHELLOPTS is not exported) — do not convert those sites blindly. Pin structurally with `declare -f <fn>` refusing `| grep`, since a 0.14%-per-call defect is not reliably caught by any bounded statistical stress loop.

entry_text: Gotcha for any PRD cite-vs-status checker: even after its SHIPPED re-stamp (edd9703fae), docs/prds/kernel-seam-contracts.md still contains "Adopt existing task **#4876** (`deferred`, high)" in its frozen AS-AUTHORED §9 body, and it must not be edited. Capability manifests (*.capability-manifest.md) are decompose-time gate artifacts whose status words are author-time evidence, and they carried 27 of 46 raw cite-status contradictions in a 2026-09-30 survey.
target_text: Reify's /prd overlay (.claude/skills/prd/project.md, sections "Code anchors in PRD prose" and "PRD terminal status") ratifies two rules: (1) PRD-family prose (the PRD .md, its .capability-manifest.md, and .yaml sidecar) must cite code by symbol/file/section-banner, never path:line, unless the document header carries an as-of commit SHA + date — and a dated/frozen snapshot must never be re-anchored once stamped, only frozen-and-superseded; (2) PRD terminal status is a closed three-value set — SHIPPED (every leaf done, cancelled tolerated alongside), SUPERSEDED (named successor), WITHDRAWN (all leaves cancelled, no successor) — the live-side vocabulary stays free-form, and decompose-mode sessions must both backfill real task IDs into decomposition leaf rows and file a mandatory PRD-close leaf (depending on every sibling leaf) whose deliverable is the terminal-status stamp itself. Detection/enforcement of drift against these rules (reify-audit --pattern PPRDSTATUS) is a separate task, #6346 — this overlay only states the authoring-time rule.

SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__ binds its landed outbox, <git_ops.project_root>/data/orchestrator/landed_outbox.json, onto the PROCESS-GLOBAL MergeProvenance via MergeProvenance.bind, and nothing ever unbinds it. In a test suite this means a LandedRow recorded by one test's lane answers a later test's MergeProvenance.lookup, for example inside workflow._recover_if_already_merged, in the same xdist worker.

It surfaced when task 5034 moved the workflow e2e helpers (_workflow_helpers.py::_build_workflow*) onto a production MergeLane. TestWipRecoveryNoAdvance recorded a write-ahead row for task '42' that was never consumed, and TestRecoverIfAlreadyMerged then got DONE instead of None. A -n0 repro of that pair gave 10 failing out of 12. To an observer it looked like a one-off e2e flake.

target_text: Gotcha for orchestrator workflow tests touching the landed-outbox journal: MergeProvenance._outbox is a PROCESS-GLOBAL set via MergeProvenance.bind(outbox). Tests must use an autouse fixture that sets MergeProvenance._outbox = None before and after each test, or a bound outbox leaks across tests. To simulate a journal hit, record a LandedRow(task_id, branch_tip_sha, advanced_sha, landed_at) into a real LandedOutbox and bind it; to simulate a miss, leave it unbound (lookup returns None fail-safe).

entry_text: reify-compiler gotcha: a where-guarded param or let (`param x = 5mm where c`, or `where c { param x ... }`) is lowered by `compile_per_decl_guard` into `TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups[].members` / `.else_members`, NOT into `value_cells`. So any projection built only from `tmpl.value_cells` (e.g. `member_type_map_from_template` → `scope.sub_member_types`) silently misses guarded members of a child template. To ask "does the child declare name X", also scan guarded_groups, sub_components, ports, named realizations and match_arm_groups.
target_text: reify-compiler gotcha: per-declaration where-clause params (`param w : Length = 5kg where flag`) are compiled through entity.rs's top-level Param arm, so check_param_default_type runs. Then `compile_per_decl_guard` MOVES the decl into `TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups`, not `value_cells`. Any pass that walks only value_cells (e.g. `param_default_cells`/`check_param_default_conformance` before task #7212) misses BOTH block-guarded and per-decl-guarded params. `guarded_groups` is a flat list: nested `where` blocks push their own entry with `parent_guard` set.

Completed: harness.py: gc_run_config_dir unreachable on a second cancellation in shielded finally blocks
Description: Follow-up filed from task 4431 (escalation_id agent-followup-4431), which shielded the `update_run_stage_reports` persistence call in the `finally` blocks of `ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py, shield site ~line 3560) and `ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass` (~line 5501) against a second asyncio cancellation arriving mid-write.

Residual gap, documented in task 4431's design decision 3 and in "Known residual (task 4431)" code comments at both shield sites: `await asyncio.shield(...)` protects the WRITE itself once it exists as its own Task, but the *awaiting frame* in the `finally` block is still interruptible — a second cancellation arriving while the shielded write is in flight still raises `CancelledError` at that `await asyncio.shield(...)` expression in the outer frame. That means the `gc_run_config_dir` cleanup block immediately following each shield site (harness.py ~3572-3578 for run_full_cycle, ~5512-5518 for _run_remediation_pass) remains unreachable on that path — exactly as it was BEFORE task 4431's fix, so this is not a regression, but it is a real pre-existing gap: a run's per-run recon CLI config dir is not garbage-collected when a second cancellation lands during the finally's persistence write.

Task 4431 deliberately did not fix this (see its design decision 3, verbatim): "Swallowing BaseException around the shielded await would be safe on the exception paths (an exception raised inside a finally that is already unwinding does not suppress the propagating exception), but NOT on the success path: after `return run` at ~3441, a swallow would let an outer `.cancel()` be absorbed and the task complete with a return value instead of cancelling — an uncancellable coroutine, a semantics change well beyond this task's remit." Resolving this residual requires a design that discriminates "safe to swallow because we are already unwinding due to a previous cancellation" from "the return-path completion the outer caller is legitimately trying to cancel" — that discrimination is the actual scope of this follow-up. Until it's solved, the GC block simply stays skipped on this narrow double-cancellation race, same as today.

Files: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py — both `finally` blocks (ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle and ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass).

Suggested priority: low — pre-existing behavior (not a regression from task 4431), and the blast radius is bounded to one leaked per-run config dir per occurrence of this narrow double-cancellation race.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED (worktree HEAD 6570799c7d; main d545567ca4 carries no diff to harness.py or test_harness.py): both "Known residual (task 4431)" sites are still present on main.
- run_full_cycle finally: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py ~4099-4146. It calls _flush_cycle_summaries, then ensure_future(update_run_stage_reports) with an add_done_callback(_log_stage_reports_write_failure), then `await asyncio.shield(stage_reports_write)`, then `if run.status != RunStatus.interrupted: gc_run_config_dir(...)`.
- _run_remediation_pass finally: ~6378-6434. Same shape, except the GC is unconditional (a remediation run is "Always 'failed', never 'interrupted'", per the except-CancelledError handler at ~6320).
- gc_run_config_dir (reconciliation/cli_stage_runner.py::gc_run_config_dir) is synchronous: shutil.rmtree with ignore_errors=True.

ROOT CAUSE: a second cancellation landing while the shielded write is in flight raises CancelledError at the `await asyncio.shield(...)` expression in the outer frame. The GC statement after it is therefore never reached.

KEY FINDING, which dissolves the "discrimination" framing in the task description: nothing needs to be swallowed. Wrapping the shielded await in try/finally with the GC in…[truncated, 7009 chars total]

reify-compiler phase ordering gotcha: in `lib.rs::compile_with_prelude_context_checked_with_config` the phases run phase_functions → phase_traits → phase_fields → phase_constraint_defs → phase_entities. All of them lower declared type names through the SAME `type_resolution` resolver, so any thread-local ambient name set (e.g. `RESOLUTION_ENUM_NAMES`, `RESOLUTION_SHADOWING_ENUM_NAMES`) that changes what a bare type name resolves to MUST be installed once around the WHOLE phase sequence in lib.rs — never inside a single phase. Installing it only in `phase_entities` (the intuitive spot, since that is where ctor params live) makes trait requirements and fn signatures disagree with structure params on the same name, and conformance/overload resolution then rejects the mismatched pair — turning a module that previously compiled with a WARNING into a hard ERROR (`TypeMismatchForTraitMember`, `no matching overload for f(Enum(X))`). Verified on task #5429/esc-5429-1; this whole-module-RAII rule is unchanged and still correct.

CORRECTED INSTALL SITE (folded in from correction e80c0bfa, task #6394, 2026-08-26 — supersedes this entry's original claim that the site is 'right after build_resolution_enums_from_cache'): the correct install site is immediately after `pre_pass::collect_decl_refs` in `lib.rs::compile_with_prelude_context_checked_with_config`. Both set inputs (`ctx.enum_defs`, `ctx.seen_entity_names`) are final from `collect_decl_refs` onward — `resolve_enum_variant_payloads` mem::takes `ctx.enum_defs` to rewrite PAYLOADS, never names — so that is the earliest sound point AND the only one that also covers `resolve_enum_variant_payloads`. The old site left enum-variant payload resolution as the ONE declared-type position that could not see the shadow set: `enum Boxed { B { f: Fit } }` lowered `f` to `Type::StructureRef("Fit")` while `fn use_fit(f: Fit)` lowered to `Type::Enum("Fit")`, failing overload resolution when the payload's match binder was passed to the fn param (PRD docs/prds/v0_6/enum-shadow-coherence.md §2 R4).

Two further non-obvious facts measured on #6394: (1) `ctx.resolution_enums` is assigned ONLY by `enums_phase::build_resolution_enums_from_cache`, which now runs AFTER the corrected install site — so it is EMPTY in anything constructed before that phase; building a module-local set from it yields an empty set (shadowing off wholesale, five `enum_ctor_param_binding_tests` red at once), not an over-broad prelude++local one. (2) `aliases_phase::phase_aliases` DOES reach `resolve_type_expr_with_aliases_kinded`, via `resolve_alias_dfs` → `type_resolution::resolve_type_alias_expr` → `resolve_parameterized_builtin_type`, whose List/Set/Map/Option arms recurse into it for every inner type arg; it is inert with respect to the shadowing override only because that DFS passes empty structure/trait/type-param sets, so the `Type::StructureRef` arm the override replaces can never fire. Do not repeat the claim that `phase_aliases` "never enters the kinded resolver".

target_text: Reify warm lanes: scripts/run-gui-dev.sh — the default launcher for every gui/test/visual/run_*_e2e_smoke.sh — is unusable whenever ANY process on the host holds vite's :1420, because reify-gui's devUrl is baked to http://localhost:1420 at COMPILE time (documented at run-gui-dev.sh:103-117), so REIFY_VITE_PORT relocates only vite and the GUI still loads the foreign listener; the script preflight-refuses. Seen 2026-09-10 with a long-lived personal dogfood session holding it, which made the smoke runners unrunnable in every lane at once. WORKAROUND that works and skips vite entirely: build the frontend dist (`npm --prefix gui run build`) and `cargo build -p reify-gui --bin reify-gui --features gui --release` ONCE, then drive lib_e2e_smoke.sh's e2e_smoke_run with REIFY_SMOKE_SKIP_PREBUILD=1 and REIFY_SMOKE_LAUNCHER pointed at a 4-line script that does `cd <worktree>; source scripts/lib_gui_launch.sh; gui_launch_env_pin; exec target/release/reify-gui "$1"`. REIFY_DEBUG=1/REIFY_DEBUG_PORT pass through to the release binary (main.rs:886 reads the env var), so the debug MCP listener comes up normally. Do NOT point REIFY_SMOKE_LAUNCHER at scripts/run-gui.sh directly: it re-runs `npm run build` on every launch, which rewrites gui/dist, invalidates the tauri build script and triggers a full reify-gui relink inside the readiness window.

entry_text: Gotcha (reify-compiler, since task 7838): the value-cell Applied-type walk (entities_phase.rs → check_applied_type_arg_bounds) covers every value cell, not only annotated ones. An un-annotated `let` gets an inferred cell_type, and its Applied type args are bound-checked as Written, so builtin args are rejected against trait bounds. Example: `let c = couple(a, 2.0)` with `a : Axis` types to `Coupling<Axis>`, which fails `P: DrivingJoint + HasMotion`. Tests that need a Coupling must build a real driving joint, e.g. `let j = prismatic(vec3(1,0,0), 0mm .. 10mm)`. Axis stand-ins no longer work. This is intended (esc-7838-3, option A).
target_text: Bound-check gap measured 2026-09-23: `check_type_param_bounds` (entity.rs ~6160-6250) `continue`s on `Type::as_name() == None` ("builtin types don't need bound checking"), and `as_name` (ty.rs ~841-849) is Some only for TypeParam/StructureRef/TraitObject/Enum. So EVERY builtin-typed type argument bypasses bound checking for every bound: `structure def Housing<T: Seal>` accepts both `Housing<Length>()` and `Housing<Bool>()` with "All constraints satisfied." Filed as #7838. The generic-fn call path (compile_builder/entities_phase.rs ~1611-1619) runs the same checker on `Q: Dimension` params and passes today ONLY because the Scalar binding is skipped by this early-out — a fix must keep `scale_q(10mm, 3.0)` green. Related: #7719 owns the kind-bound WORDING ("'X' does not implement 'Nat'") and now has a dependency edge on 6549 for its BuiltinKind recogniser. Separately, the sub use-site type-arg lowering (entity.rs ~3126-3160, duplicated at ~5398-5430) matches `Named { name, .. }` and calls bare `resolve_type_name`, so `Beam<Rate<Length>>()` becomes StructureRef("Rate") and a user alias `Stiff` becomes StructureRef("Stiff") — #7839.

entry_text: reify gotcha for scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh: callers are counted ONLY within the files discovered from the given --scope globs, and same-file callers are subtracted. So a scoped run (`--scope crates/<c>/src`) reports every pub fn of a library crate whose callers live in OTHER crates as an orphan. Only the default `crates/reify-*/src` corpus (measured 19s, 3032 pub fns, 2026-10-04) sees cross-crate production callers. A crate-local G-allow pin test should therefore assert only scope-independent facts (allowed[] membership of marked fns, absence of a marker on an unmarked fn), never orphans[] membership of a fn whose real caller is in another crate.
target_text: scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh counts callers per FILE, not per CRATE: `external = total - per_file.get(decl_path, 0)`. So a caller in a different file of the SAME crate DOES un-orphan a pub fn. A `// G-allow:` marker in crates/reify-audit/src/lib.rs asserted the opposite ("callers are intra-crate ... orphan-audit script counts only inter-crate call sites") and was wrong — the real reason that fn looked orphaned was a spurious `#[cfg(test)]` mask. To settle WHY a fn is or is not in allowed[]/orphans[], do not reason about it: patch a `print(f"PROBE {n}: {dict(hits.get(n, {}))}", file=sys.stderr)` line into the script just above `results = []` and diff the per-file hit table across two script variants. Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.
- Free-function forms `map(xs, |v| v)` / `filter(xs, |v| v > 1)` also fail; no free-function map/filter exists.
- `generate(3, |i| i)` and `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])` DO parse (both `function_call`); `xs.count` parses (bare `member_access`, no parens). So lambdas work and member access works — only method arguments are missing.

DEAD CODE this leaves behind: the `"map"`, `"filter"`, `"all"`, `"any"`, `"generate"` arms of `eval_method_call` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs (lines ~3695, ~3825, ~3714, ~3739, ~3811) are unreachable from .ri source and exercised only by Rust-level tests. crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:3798-3810 even documents a deliberate negative-count policy divergence between the free-function and METHOD forms of `generate` — a distinction no .ri program can observe.

WORK TO DECIDE/DO (triage first, this is a design question, not a mechanical fix):
(a) add an `obj.method(args)` rule to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js plus the corresponding lowering in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, so the existing evaluator arms become reachable; or
(b) expose the wanted combinators as free functions instead (the shape `generate` and `flat_map` already use) and delete or clearly mark the unreachable method arms; or
(c) accept the gap deliberately and document it, marking the unreachable arms so future readers do not assume surface coverage.

Files: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs.

Rationale for filing: leaving evaluator arms with no surface form is a silent-capability-gap — a design session reading the stdlib docs would reasonably write `xs.filter(...)` and get an opaque "invalid let" parse error rather than an unsupported-construct diagnostic.

FalkorDB fulltext gotchas, measured 2026-10-02 on FalkorDB 4.18 scratch graphs (task 3710):
(1) db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes/queryRelationships against an ABSENT index returns [] silently, with no error. That is why the missing-index defect produced no signal.
(2) While an index is UNDER CONSTRUCTION, a query returns 0 rows, NOT partial results.
(3) On a one-node graph the fulltext index is OPERATIONAL before the first CALL db.indexes() read, so a small fixture cannot observe the build window. A test needs about 50k filler nodes: a status-query-status bracket then held 14/15 times under nice -n 19 with 32 busy loops, and 10/10 at 10k-20k unloaded.
(4) DROP [FULLTEXT ]INDEX FOR (x:L) ON (x.f) removes exactly one field, but re-creating a partially-dropped fulltext index with graphiti's verbatim statement then fails ('Can not override index configuration' / 'Attribute X is already indexed').
target_text: FalkorDB fulltext was validated end-to-end for the first time WITH a live index present (2026-08-05, module v41800 / redis 8.6.2, 800 real dark_factory Entity rows on a scratch graph). Findings: the exact `CALL db.idx.fulltext.createNodeIndex(...)` DDL graphiti 0.28.2 emits is accepted; the `CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX FOR ()-[e:RELATES_TO]-() ON (e.name, e.fact, e.group_id)` edge form is accepted (and is the ONLY way — `createRelationshipIndex`/`createEdgeIndex` are not registered procedures); both `db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` and `queryRelationships` exist; RANGE + FULLTEXT + VECTOR coexist on one label. CRUCIALLY, fused-memory's hardened `build_fulltext_query` (`fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/falkor_fulltext.py`, task 3334) is STRICTLY BETTER than upstream with an index present, not merely equal: across 38 queries it rescued 6 that upstream HARD-ERRORS on (the dead-letter-9950 class, e.g. a bare `_` token leaving a dangling `|` union operator) and there were ZERO cases where hardened failed and upstream succeeded. NO write-path hazard: 13 hostile property shapes (200 KB summary, null, missing property, int, float, bool, array, emoji, control chars, vector prop) ALL wrote successfully with `indexingFailures` stuck at 0 — a non-indexable value silently no-ops rather than failing the write. Dead-letter 9950 was a QUERY-ASSEMBLY fault surfacing on the write path via `get_relevant_nodes`, not an indexing fault, and that call fires today regardless of whether an index exists — so turning indices on does not reintroduce it. One measured caveat: `graphiti_client.py:309-310`'s docstring claim that the hardening "only ever removes unparseable operands, so recall ... is unchanged" is FALSE as written — `—`, `•`, `→` and emoji are genuinely indexable terms that get dropped (practical loss is junk: 5 hits out of 800).

The escalation-watcher's `design_concern` handler PARKS items by design, which creates a structural blind spot for questions that get answered outside the watcher's view. Structural facts established 2026-08-20/21.

`skills/escalation-watcher/SKILL.md` ~lines 1011-1025, the `design_concern` (info or blocking) handler, is five steps: (1) present to the human, (2) leave the escalation pending because "the open escalation record IS the durable record", (3) create a session-only todo, (3a) file a cockpit DecisionRecord via `write-decision`, (5) "Append `<esc-id>` to the wrapper-owned exclude-file while this item is pending."

Step 5 is deliberate and defensible — it stops the watcher re-nagging a human about a question only the human can answer. Its consequence is that a parked design_concern is, by construction, no longer being RE-EXAMINED. Combined with the vacuous-predicate problem on its L1 members, nothing in the system was positioned to notice when reify's esc-6107-7 was answered on 2026-08-17 by an /unblock session that ruled, implemented, and propagated to sibling task records but never touched the escalation or the PRD.

TWO COMPLEMENTARY FAILURE MODES, one already scarred into the skill and one not:
- Step 3a exists because of esc-3223-4/-5, which kept task 3223 blocked for 11 DAYS because "the question never reached the cockpit queue the human actually reads." That is: THE ANSWER WAS NEVER REQUESTED.
- esc-6107-7 is the mirror: THE ANSWER WAS NEVER RECORDED. The question reached the human's queue fine; the answer arrived elsewhere and the record never learned.

The skill closed the first hole and left the second open. (Worth testing this framing against actual history rather than accepting it — it was formed from one incident plus one cited precedent.)

RELATED STRUCTURAL FACTS for anyone proposing edits:
- `skills/unblock/SKILL.md` is ~769 lines and already large; adding to it has real cost. Completed: test_verify_clock_stop.py: two @pytest.mark.timeout markers sit BELOW their own bounded worst case, so a slow-path run os._exit()s the xdist worker instead of failing readably
Description: Swept up from esc-4389-3 (info note filed by task 4389's agent; out of scope there, whose plan files cover orchestrator/tests/ census work only). This is arithmetic from source, not a load-dependent flake.

OBSERVED:
1. orchestrator/tests/test_verify_clock_stop.py::TestRunCmdMaxTotalSecs::test_max_total_secs_zero_means_unlimited carries @pytest.mark.timeout(10) and calls _run_cmd(..., timeout=3.0). On _run_cmd's TimeoutError path (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_run_cmd) it calls terminate_process_group(proc, pgid, grace_secs=5.0), which per shared/src/shared/proc_group.py::terminate_process_group does SIGTERM + wait grace_secs, then SIGKILL + wait grace_secs. Bounded worst case = 3.0 + 2*5.0 = 13s > the 10s marker.
2. It is the only sub-15s marker among the 9 real-subprocess tests in that file; the other 8 use 15.
3. orchestrator/pyproject.toml sets timeout_method = "thread", and the suite runs -n auto --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0. A marker breach therefore os._exit()s the worker rather than failing the test, degrading to one misattributed failure on whichever innocent test the dead worker was running.
4. The escalating agent verified empirically that a @pytest.mark.timeout marker OVERRIDES the suite's CLI --timeout=300 (a marker-timeout(2) test sleeping 6s did fire), so the 300s CLI value does not cover this.
5. Sibling test_max_total_secs_exceeded has the same shape: marker 15, _run_cmd(timeout=10.0), so its pathological bound is 10 + 10 = 20s > 15s. The escalating agent did NOT verify that path is reachable in practice.

SUGGESTED WORK: raise test_max_total_secs_zero_means_unlimited's marker from 10 to at least 15 (matching its 8 siblings, and covering the 13s bound), and adjudicate the sibling — either raise its marker above its 20s bound or record, in a comment, why the pathological path is unreachable. Same class of work as tasks 3492 and 4215 (both done), which added/adjusted timeout markers for exactly this worker-kill reason.

Note the norm in memory 9bab51bc: timeout loosening must NOT be applied as a task-scoped workaround for a blamed innocent bystander — this task is the correctly-scoped place to do it, on the merits of the arithmetic above, not to unblock any particular verify run.
Analysis: Nine real-subprocess tests use @pytest.mark.timeout of 10/15, below the 13s/20s bounded worst case of _run_cmd's terminate_process_group escalation. Replace with one derived constant (3x the 20s bound = 60).

Completed: Blast-radius requeue: a failed pending write must reach the run()-exit write-failure ledger (relaxation 2), not read as an SM-2 violation
Description: Found by the independent pre-merge review of task 3542 (θ, PRD plans/task-escalation-state-graph-prd.md). The gap is NEW with 3542's tightening.

THE GAP. 3542 tightened `_OUTCOME_ALLOWED['requeued']` to {PENDING} (shared/src/shared/task_transitions.py::_OUTCOME_ALLOWED). Spec §5's relaxation 2 says a status-write failure at exit is crash-shaped: it emits ONE store-unavailable record, never a contract violation. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._note_exit_status_write implements that ledger, but only three writers call it: _repend_for_requeue, _persist_blocked_row and the bypass reopen.

orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler.handle_blast_radius_expansion swallows a failed `set_task_status(task_id, 'pending')` (the `except RuntimeError` arm after transient retries: "keeping locks held for reconcile to recover"). It returns `False`, the same value as a SUCCESSFUL conflict requeue. workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._reconcile_scope_locks passes that bool through, and TaskWorkflow._requeue_on_lock_conflict stashes a REQUEUED report. Its three callers are _plan, the escalation-resume scope-grant path in _drive, and the replan in _execute_verify_review_loop. The row is still `in-progress`, and the ledger was never set. So orchestrator/src/orchestrator/exit_contract.py::judge_exit returns VIOLATION, not STORE_UNAVAILABLE.

CONSEQUENCE.
- Log mode (shipped default): one would-violate WARNING plus a workflow_exit_contract event per affected exit during a store outage. That pollutes task μ's soak signal (3546 step 1(a), "zero would-violate").
- Enforce mode: one blocking L1 per task, which is exactly the per-task storm spec §5 forbids.
So this must land before μ flips `workflow_exit_contract_enforce`. Until it does, μ's soak criterion should read "zero violations outside store outages".

FIX SHAPE (the implementer decides). Make the scheduler's write failure visible to the workflow: return a typed result, or raise, instead of the ambiguous bool. Then call `self._note_exit_status_write('pending', exc)` on the failure arm. Update the SchedulerProtocol stub (scheduler.py, the `handle_blast_radius_expansion` protocol signature) and every test double. Check whether a failed write must still keep the locks held (it must: see the existing comment).

RED TEST. Drive a REQUEUED exit through _plan's blast-radius conflict with the scheduler's pending write raising RuntimeError. The exit must record STORE_UNAVAILABLE (exactly one record, no violation). Today it records a VIOLATION.

Not in scope: the other known would-violate producers. The sibling task filed alongside this one covers them.

The acquire-failure branch persists metadata.files, then `set_task_status(task_id, 'pending')`. Completed: Pinned tasks never earn a reservation, so a pin on contended files never dispatches — give the head blocked pin a pin-owned reservation
Description: PROBLEM
A pin today buys exactly one thing: on each scheduler tick, the pinned task gets the first try at acquiring ALL of its module locks at once (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_select_pins). If that try fails, the pin earns nothing. No skip count, no park, no event.

Fairness parks go only to the scored loop's single strict-top candidate (::Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> ::Scheduler._bump_skip_and_maybe_park). orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py::TIER_BASE makes every critical candidate outscore every high one. So a non-critical pin can never earn a park while any critical candidate is eligible, and one always is: in the 7 days to 2026-09-28, all 390 task_skipped events went to six critical tasks.

A pinned task whose footprint touches a contended file therefore dispatches only on a tick where every one of its files happens to be free of both holders and parks. Meanwhile, the files it needs free up one at a time and are taken by lower-tier scored candidates in the same tick. The pin fails exactly the class the scheduler PRD says pins exist for: plans/scheduler-dispatch-scoring-and-lock-layer-prd.md §C4 says "never top-scored — this is what the pin is for".

EVIDENCE (read-only; data/orchestrator/runs.db and .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, measured 2026-09-28)
- The scheduler ran 409 ticks in 7 days. Only 15 of them ended in select_pins.
- Pins 3500 (pinned 08-24), 3659 and 4856 (09-01), 5205 (09-19) and 5812 (09-23) went 5 to 35 days without a dispatch. 5205, 5812 and 4856 have never dispatched.
- Share of 09-21..09-28 during which each pin's FULL file set was free of other holders and foreign parks: 3500 0.00%, 3659 0.00%, 5205 0.07%, 5812 0.00%.
- Holds alone: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py was unheld 1.7% of the week, verify.py 2.7%. The unheld stretches of workflow.py and harness.py were covered by CRITICAL fairness parks owned by task 3542. 3542 is effective critical only because it inherits the boost of pinned task 3545. Those parks top-blocked pin 3659 for the whole week.
- 3500 and 3659 had to be landed by hand through merge carriers 6033 and 6024 on 2026-09-28.
- The starvation watchdog cannot see this class. Its dual gate needs skip >= 50, and pins have 0. The idle-only gate is 30 days on an in-memory clock (task 3821 owns the watchdog).

DECISIONS (made at filing; do not relitigate without new evidence)
D1 Scope — pins only. A pin reservation is granted only to a task that meets all of these:
- it is pinned in the override store;
- it passes ::Scheduler._eligible_for_dispatch;
- it is not in gated_ids;
- it is not deterministic;
- it failed try_acquire in _phase_select_pins this tick.
Non-pinned candidates keep today's rank-1-only fairness parks.

D2 Bound — only the head of the pin queue reserves. At most `pin_reservation_max_active` (default 1) tasks hold a pin reservation, namely the lowest-pin_order tasks that satisfy D1. This is the EASY-backfill head reservation, not the general below-rank-1 park installation that PRD §7 rejects. §7 measured harm from reserving for EVERY passed-over candidate: idle reservation x3.6-4.8, INV-3 gridlock of same-tier chains, and never-dispatched x1.5-3. A single operator-chosen reservation cannot gridlock with itself. Its idle cost is one task's footprint, and C7 backfill can still borrow through it. Say so in the code and docs: this is a bounded exception, not a reversal of §7.

D3 Rank — operator intent outranks automatic fairness. A pin reservation may install on a module whose active-top park is a FAIRNESS park of any tier, including critical. It installs by shadowing that park, never by destroying it. Without this the fix does nothing in exactly the observed case: critical fairness parks over the hot files (3542 historically, 5221 now). entry_text: In reify-compiler, every operand in a boolean geometry position (union/difference/... args) is ALSO value-compiled before realization lowering: a top-level geometry let / geometry-list let / geometry param emits a value cell via compile_expr_with_expected over its whole initializer (entity.rs geometry-let arm, task #4954), which runs before the realization-emission third pass. So unknown-member / priv-member / collection-sub value-level diagnostics for a boolean operand are already emitted once; a geometry-position consumer that also renders MemberPathError::to_diagnostic double-reports (measured task 5425 with `reify check`).
target_text: In reify-compiler, a geometry `let` is compiled by TWO required passes that share one `&mut Vec<Diagnostic>`: the value-cell pass (`compile_expr`, where `check_builtin_arg_types` is wired at expr.rs:3392) and the realization pass (entity.rs:3851 -> `compile_geometry_call` -> the argument walk at geometry.rs:1417). Gotcha for shell wrappers that source a sibling lib (task 5158): locate it with fork-free parameter expansion `case "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" in */*) d="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}";; *) d=.;; esac`, never `$(dirname ...)` or `$REPO`.
- dirname: the uv-wrapper tests run under an EMPTY PATH, so `$(dirname ...)` yields "" and the source silently becomes /lib/....
- $REPO: fused-memory/scripts/cgl_eta_auto_apply.sh hardcodes REPO to the MAIN checkout, so a worktree would source main's copy.
- `${0##*/}` is the fork-free basename for ERROR prefixes, and `$0` inside `$(...)` is still the caller's path.
target_text: Convention (task 5158): a committed bash wrapper that runs `uv` must not hardcode a path or trust PATH. It sources scripts/lib/resolve_uv.sh, the single copy of the UV_BIN -> PATH -> $HOME/.local/bin -> /usr/local/bin ladder. Locate the lib relative to the script itself with the fork-free idiom `case "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" in */*) d="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}";; *) d=.;; esac`, never `$(dirname ...)` (unfindable under an empty PATH) or $REPO (tests point it at a fake dir, cgl hardcodes main). Use a guarded `source "$lib" || { echo "${0##*/}: ERROR: ..." >&2; exit 127; }`, then `X="$(require_uv_bin)" || exit $?` AFTER the .env source. scripts/tests/test_resolve_uv_lib.py::test_only_the_lib_defines_the_resolver fails if any other tracked .sh defines resolve_uv_bin/require_uv_bin, and its CALLERS tuple is where a new wrapper gets wiring coverage.

entry_text: Reify GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar), as of 2026-10-01 before task 7092 lands: LetDeclaration has NO `pub`/`priv`/`aux` prefix, although grammar.js `let_declaration` has `optional(choice('pub','priv')) optional('aux') 'let'`. As a result `aux let x = 1mm`, `pub let …` and `priv let …` each produce 1 error node in the editor, while the compiler parses all three (`priv let` then gets the semantic error E_PRIV_REDUNDANT). Task 7092 widens it. A cheap way to prototype a grammar change with no tracked-file churn: copy reify.grammar to gui/src/editor/zzProbe.grammar, run `npx lezer-generator` with `-o src/editor/zzProbeParser.js` (the generated file imports ./highlight, so it must sit in the same directory), import both parsers in a throwaway vitest file to diff error counts across the corpus, then delete all the probe files.
target_text: Gotcha: the GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar) accepts `aux` only before `sub`, not before `let`, even though tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js accepts `aux let`. Any `.ri` under examples/ or tests/prd-gate/fixtures/ that gui/src/__tests__/reifyGrammarCorpus.test.ts pins in EXPECTED_CLEAN will fail the drift ledger as a 'grammar regressed' error if it gains an `aux let`. entry_text: To test a Rust binary's behaviour on a closed stdout deterministically in reify, create the pipe with `std::io::pipe()` (stable since 1.87; toolchain is 1.96.0), `drop(reader)` BEFORE spawning, and pass the `PipeWriter` as `.stdout(writer)`. The child's first write then always meets no reader. Don't use `Stdio::piped()` and drop `ChildStdout` afterwards: that races the child's write into the pipe buffer and can flake to exit 0. Expected outcomes: a stock Rust binary exits 101 with the 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe' panic, because the runtime ignores SIGPIPE before main. After a `libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` reset, `ExitStatusExt::signal() == Some(libc::SIGPIPE)` (python returncode -13). The python `os.pipe(); os.close(r)` driver reproduces the same thing outside cargo (task 7906).

Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (escalation-watcher, esc-7906-3, option C). The census sighting's `head --short` was the host skim-hook flattening artifact (see dark-factory 5955), NOT a reify bug. BUT there is a REAL reify-cli defect, and it is this task's scope now: with stdout wired to a closed pipe, reify panics and exits 101 with 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)'. Watcher reproduced it on main: target/debug/reify --version into a pre-closed pipe gives rc=101 and a panic at std/src/io/stdio.rs. Nothing in crates/reify-cli handles SIGPIPE. FIX: restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE at the top of reify-cli's main(), in a small sigpipe module (unix-only, no-op elsewhere). Files: crates/reify-cli/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs,src/sigpipe.rs}, Cargo.lock, tests/harness_cli_surface.rs, tests/harness_cli_surface/cli_broken_pipe.rs. Write two RED tests first: `reify --version` and `reify cache stats` into a closed pipe must NOT exit 101 or print a panic. The reify-audit binaries have the same exposure; that follow-up is filed separately.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION ---
Agent piped a Rust binary's stdout into `head --short` (not a valid head option); head exited immediately on the bad flag, closing the pipe, and the upstream Rust process then panicked on SIGPIPE ('failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe') while still writing. The panic trace is the visually dominant part of the output, obscuring the actual root cause (the unrecognized head flag) printed just above it.

Evidence:
- head: unrecognized option '--short'
...thread 'main' (4068124) panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)

Observed in 1 sighting(s) (project: reify).
Analysis: PREMISE VERIFIED on this branch (task/7906 == main 1cdfa6bdb9, no prior commits): with stdout wired to a pipe whose read end was closed before spawn, the prebuilt target/debug/reify exits rc=101 for BOTH `reify --version` and `REIFY_CACHE_DIR=<empty tmp> reify cache stats`, with stderr "thread 'main' panicked at .../library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9: failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)". Measured with a python os.pipe()/close(r) driver. On a normal (open) stdout both commands write ZERO bytes to stderr.

ROOT CAUSE: the Rust runtime sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN before main, so write(2) to a reader-less pipe returns EPIPE and println! panics. Nothing in crates/reify-cli touches SIGPIPE (Grep for sigpipe/SIG_DFL across crates/ finds only a test comment). The stable toolchain is pinned at 1.96.0 (rust-toolchain.toml); `-Zon-broken-pipe=kill` and the old `#[unix_sigpipe]` attribute are nightly-only, so the fix is a `libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` call as the first statement of main() (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:115).

- New leaf module crates/reify-cli/src/sigpipe.rs exposing one fn `restore_default()` (unix: the unsafe libc call with a `// SAFETY:` note; non-unix: no-op). main.rs gains `mod sigpipe;` beside `mod cache; mod dev; mod mcp_context;` and calls `sigpipe::restore_default();` before `std::env::args()`.

How the old merge-lane module paths stay importable after task 5036: each old file (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py etc.) does `from orchestrator.merge_lane import X`, `from orchestrator.merge_lane.X import *  # noqa: F403`, optionally `def __getattr__(name: str) -> Any: ...`, then `sys.modules[__name__] = X`.
- That keeps ONE module object, so `import`, `patch('orchestrator.merge_queue.Y')`, `patch.object(mq, ...)` and the worker's own global lookups all hit the same binding.
- Pyright keeps public names typed through the star import.
- A `__getattr__` stub makes pyright accept ANY name through that path. So the stub is kept only on the 10 aliases through which external code imports private names. orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_alias_names.py is the runtime backstop: every name reached through an alias, or imported from the façade, must exist.
- Do not put the stub under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. complexipy scores a module-level `if TYPE_CHECKING:` as cognitive 1 per file, which would raise the cluster total.
target_text:
Rebase hazard created by task 5036 (merge lane moved into orchestrator/merge_lane/): git cannot follow the move while the old path survives as a modified alias file. A branch that edited orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py, or any moved satellite, before 5036 landed gets a modify/modify conflict on the OLD path.
- Resolving it by keeping the branch's full old file would create a second, divergent copy of the worker next to merge_lane/worker.py, and the old import path would stop being the same module object.
- Correct resolution: port the branch's hunks into the new merge_lane/<module>.py, then take main's alias file as-is. The hunks usually apply by offset (`patch -p1 --fuzz=3` after rewriting the path in the diff).
- Task 5618 was the in-flight holder when 5036 landed, and its details carry this instruction.

target_text: DASHBOARD DEADLINE-RACE FLAKES (task 6079, measured 2026-09-30). The shape: a fan-out test gives a HEALTHY project and a slow project (slow_ports={port: 0.5}) ONE shared per_call_timeout=0.05, then asserts the healthy one read. Its cold MockTransport MCP handshake (3 posts) takes about 6.6ms idle, so a loaded xdist worker stalled for more than 50ms turns it None. That is correct production behaviour, and a synchronous time.sleep(0.06) in the healthy handler reproduces the red deterministically. Fix without widening any value by running the unchanged scenario on an idle-autojump virtual clock. Use an asyncio.SelectorEventLoop subclass whose time() reads a counter, plus a selectors.DefaultSelector subclass whose select(timeout>0) adds timeout to that counter and polls with select(0). Drive it with asyncio.Runner(loop_factory=...) from a sync test. Host stalls can then never expire a deadline, and timer order stays exact. It works on CPython 3.13 and 3.14 and under pytest-asyncio 1.3 auto mode beside async tests. Task 6079 adds it as dashboard/tests/_virtual_clock_helpers.py::run_on_virtual_clock. It fits in-loop scenarios only; real sockets or executor threads race the jump. The same latent race is in test_task_runtime.py (2 tests), test_merge_halt.py and test_merge_queue_data.py, filed as ticket tkt_0RV862T8K2BDD34QKN2KXZ2DDY.

entry_text: Gotcha in reify capability-manifest delivered_checks: kind 'grep' runs `git grep` over file CONTENT, so a pattern that is a fixture's basename (e.g. pattern 'member_geom_let_instance' with paths [fixtures dir]) never matches unless the file body contains that string, and many .ri fixtures have no `module <basename>` line. Task 5432's 'fixtures-committed-and-probed' check is unsatisfiable for exactly this reason (measured 2026-10-01). Anchor such checks on a string that really occurs in the fixture body, or use kind: manual.
target_text: DELIVERED-CHECK grep semantics, and the authoring anti-pattern that follows (root cause of esc-5761-2, 2026-09-10). dark-factory runs a kind=grep delivered_check as, verbatim from orchestrator/src/orchestrator/delivered_checks.py:152, `git -C <project_root> grep -E -e <pattern> <ref> -- <paths>`; rc>=2 is ERRORED, rc==0 is matched, then delivered = matched if expect=='present' else not matched. It is therefore a CASE-SENSITIVE POSIX-extended regex over FILE CONTENT at the committed ref — there is no -i, and shared/src/shared/capability_manifest.py's DeliveredCheckMeta has no case-insensitivity field at all, so case-insensitivity cannot be requested from a manifest. ANTI-PATTERN: task 5760's check "corpus-and-compile-gate" used pattern `INDEX` against examples/best_practices/INDEX.md — the author echoed the FILENAME. That file's prose has only ever used lowercase "index"; `git log -G` with uppercase INDEX over that path is EMPTY across the file's whole history, so the check FAILED from the day it was authored and had blocked dependent task 5761 ever since. It was never a regression. Never derive a grep pattern from a filename; pick a string that is quoted verbatim in the file AND names the capability being asserted (here: best_practices_index_matches_corpus_directory, the bidirectional INDEX-to-corpus invariant in examples_smoke.rs).
