Completed: Verify scopes: pass a per-role cgroup CPUWeight at the systemd-run --scope spawn (merge 100 / task 33 / background 10) so nice tiers are not defeated across cgroups
Description: PROBLEM (measured 2026-09-07/08, load-tuning session, Leo). cgroup v2 schedules in two layers: `nice` orders threads INSIDE one cgroup; BETWEEN sibling cgroups the kernel shares CPU by `cpu.weight`, and nice has no effect on that split. verify.py::_run_cmd launches a verify inside a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` (its own cgroup) when `verify_use_cgroup_scope` is true, for kill-by-cgroup on timeout. Every such scope is created at the default CPUWeight 100, the same as `orchestrator-dark-factory.service` as a whole (every agent plus every non-scoped verify). Measured per-cgroup cpu.stat over 20s under contention: df unit 8.9 cores, reify task-role verify scope 7.9, reify merge-role verify scope 7.6, i.e. an equal three-way split. The task-role scope carried `nice -n 15 ionice -c2 -n7` from shared/verify_admission.py::_NICE_TIERS and yielded NOTHING to the merge scope or to the df unit, because nice is per-cgroup. Inside the df unit the tiers DO work (merge xdist at nice 5 got 5.2 cores, task xdist at nice 15 got 2.2, background at nice 19 got 0). So the role tiering is correct in-unit and inert across scopes.

CHANGE. At the `systemd-run` argv build in verify.py::_run_cmd (the branch guarded by `use_cgroup_scope and shutil.which('systemd-run')`), add `-p CPUWeight=<w>` where w is resolved by role next to the nice prefix (verify.py::_resolve_nice_prefix is called with `role` at the two call sites; thread the weight the same way, e.g. a new optional `cpu_weight: int | None` on the spawn spec that carries `use_cgroup_scope`/`scope_tag`, None = omit the property = today's behaviour). Config: three int knobs on OrchestratorConfig, `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_merge` (default 100), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_task` (default 33), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_background` (default 10), validated 1..10000 (cgroup v2 cpu.weight range); add them to RELOADABLE_FIELDS beside `verify_admission_nice_*` (read at spawn, so green-tier is honest) and to the green list in OPERATIONS.md section "Config reload vs restart". `offline` and unknown roles get no property.

WHY THESE NUMBERS. Lower task/background rather than raise merge: reify's own cpu_governance convention is task 100 / merge 300, but a 300 merge scope would also put interactive shells (weight-100 siblings under app.slice) at a quarter share under contention. Merge at 100 keeps the merge leg at parity with each orchestrator unit and with the operator's terminals; 33 and 10 reproduce the 3:1 merge:task ratio and the nice-19 background intent. Under contention with the df unit + one reify merge scope + one reify task scope the split moves from 33/33/33 to 43/43/14. Weights are work-conserving: a lone scope still gets the whole box, so nothing slows on an idle host.

PROVEN ON THIS HOST 2026-09-08: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p CPUWeight=33 -- sh -c '...cat cpu.weight'` printed cpu.weight=33 (the cpu controller is delegated through user@1000.service/app.slice; every unit and scope currently reads 100).

ALSO IN PASSING (own-prose rule): the verify.py docstring near `_wrap_governed` that says "The live reify deployment currently sets verify_use_cgroup_scope=False" is stale, reify's yaml line ~112 has it true; correct it.

TESTS. Extend whichever test pins the systemd-run argv for the scope path (orchestrator/tests/test_harness_verify_scope_reaper.py is the likely home; grep '--collect') to assert `-p CPUWeight=<w>` appears for each role with the defaults and is ABSENT when the knob is None/role is offline; a config test for the 1..10000 validation and RELOADABLE_FIELDS membership (mirror orchestrator/tests/test_config_verify_admission_reload.py). Do not touch shared/verify_admission.py's nice tiers: the nice prefix stays, it is what orders threads inside the scope.

Scheduler gotcha: in runs.db, the event order within a single tick does NOT show that a task borrowed through a fresh park.

Scheduler._phase_select_scored (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py) runs try_acquire on candidates in score order. When a lower candidate wins, it takes that winner's locks first, and only then calls _bump_skip_and_maybe_park on the skipped top candidate. The top candidate's park is therefore laid over modules the winner already holds.

runs.db then shows task_skipped and reservation_installed for the top candidate, followed 1–2 ms later by lock_acquired for the winner. It looks like a borrow, but it is not one.

Only a park_backfill_granted event, which carries predicted_hold, admission_bound, provable_assembly_delay and park_owners, proves an EASY-backfill borrow. DF had just 6 grants ever as of 2026-10-04.

Example: on 2026-10-01, task 3096 was misread as having borrowed harness.py through task 5221's park. It had no grant event; harness.py was simply free when 3096 took it.

entry_text:
GOTCHA measuring "what files did a task branch itself touch" (git 2.43, scratch-repo measurement for task 3918, 2026-10-05). Two independent errors combine.

(1) Plain `git log --name-only A..B` is MERGE-BLIND: it prints NO paths for merge commits, so a file changed only while resolving a back-merge (a conflict resolution or evil hunk) is invisible. Add `--diff-merges=dense-combined` (`--cc`). It lists a merge commit only for the paths it changed relative to EVERY parent, so a clean back-merge contributes nothing. NEVER use `-m` or `--diff-merges=first-parent`: on a back-merge the first parent is the branch, so they list everything main brought in.

(2) A WRITE-ONCE base (e.g. `TaskWorkflow._base_commit`) is too wide once the branch back-merges main or is re-cut after a quarantine: `old_base..HEAD` includes main's commits and CREDITS main-side edits as the branch's work. Re-derive the base at use time with `GitOps.merge_base_with_main(head)`.

Measured on one topology: stale base + plain log both missed the evil-merge path and credited main's edit; fresh fork + dense-combined got both right. Relevant to any consumer of a branch-touched set: the merge gate, the review diff, and implementer/debugger detection.
target_text:
The merge_gates PLAN_FILES_NOT_TOUCHED misfire has a THIRD specimen shape, measured 2026-08-20 on task 3513 and combined into task 3918: the QUARANTINED-LANE (wrong-range) shape, which is materially worse than the already-landed shape esc-3604-13 documents.

esc-3604-13 models the defect as the gate reading an EMPTY base..HEAD (after a task lands, a later rebase of task/<id> onto post-landing main drops every commit as upstream, parking the ref on one of main's own merge commits at 0 commits ahead). On 3513 the range was NOT empty. GitOps.quarantine_worktree renames task/<id> to task/<id>-<lane_start_ts> and recreates task/<id> at a main tip, but the gate's stored `base` stays at the ORIGINAL pre-quarantine base. Measured: base=d58590e7e32a ("Merge task/3769 into main"), HEAD=task/3513@84ca41b199 => the range spans MAIN'S OWN HISTORY, 142 commits touching 62 files, entirely other tasks' work.

WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN AN EMPTY RANGE: because the range is full of foreign commits, declared plan files that unrelated tasks happened to touch get SILENTLY CREDITED as delivered, and only the remainder is reported. The gate reported exactly 2 of 4 declared files (pytest_markers.py, test_pytest_marker_deselection.py) while crediting verify.py and verify_plan.py — which unrelated tasks had touched in that window. The 2-of-4 split is a coincidence of main traffic, not a measurement of the task. The resulting escalation (esc-3513-4) therefore reads as a plausible, SPECIFIC scope-narrowing finding ("the architect declared these files but no commit on the branch touched them") rather than as the measurement error it is — far more likely to be actioned wrongly than an all-files-missing report would be.

Anchors (repo HEAD ca0978adca): merge_gates.py:109 PLAN_FILES_NOT_TOUCHED_REASON_PREFIX; :1333 _check_plan_files_touched_in_branch; :1445 the not_touched.append accumulation; :118 CROSS_REPO_DELIVERABLE_REASON_PREFIX, the in-file carve-out precedent whose docstring already reasons about a branch that "is legitimately EMPTY".

THREE SIBLING MECHANISMS, ONE GATE — keep them distinct: (1) single-ref / wrong-ref-of-two (task 3560, tkt_0RS82XDT4WMAZHPA9H5P1KVAG5); (2) already-landed / mixed-stack empty range (tasks 3604, 3779, 3717, 3572); (3) quarantined lane with a stale base spanning main. A fix that only special-cases an EMPTY base..HEAD still gets shape (3) wrong — that is the specific test case task 3918 needs.

HOW TO APPLY when triaging a "Plan files not touched by branch" escalation: never take it at face value. Measure the range it actually used — `git rev-list --count <base>..<branch>` and `git diff --name-only <base>..<branch>` — and check whether those commits belong to this task at all. A PARTIAL not-touched list is a red flag for shape (3), not evidence of partial delivery.

entry_text: LIVE soundness hole in overload resolution (measured 2026-09-29, target/debug/reify 09-25 build; fixture tests/prd-gate/fixtures/getar_wildcard_headed_arg_silent.ri): crates/reify-core/src/overload.rs `slot_matches_wildcard_tier` carries the D4 disjunct `|| type_carries_type_param(arg_ty)`, so ANY argument whose static type contains a TypeParam anywhere (e.g. the leaky Applied{Result,[T,E]} that `or_else(Ok{value:5mm}, Ok{value:6mm})` yields) matches EVERY candidate parameter — `fn fl(x: Length)` called `fl(or_else(Ok{5mm},Ok{6mm}))` checks clean and evaluates `W.v = Result::Ok`. Tier 3 is the only gate (tier 2 narrows to a bare TypeParam only). Owned by leaf β (task 8014) of the generic-enum-type-arg-retention PRD: β must NARROW tier 3 so a headed arg needs heads_unifiable, otherwise δ (construction emitting Applied with placeholders) would widen the hole to every partly-bound construction. Also: slot_matches_wildcard_tier now has a third consumer (TraitMethodCall in expr.rs, landed after 2026-09-25) and task 5992's "two independent implementations" premise was superseded by task 5689's shared module.
target_text: In crates/reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs, generic-overload resolution and unify() must distinguish a bare TypeParam arg from a HEADED arg carrying nested erased type params (e.g. Applied{"Result",[TypeParam,TypeParam]} leaking out of a chained combinator call like or_else(parse_length_r(x), parse_length_r(y)), since parse_length_r types as a headless Type::Enum("Result") — deliberate, per reify-eval's value_type_kind_matches which only matches Value::Enum against Type::Enum, not Type::Applied). Only a genuinely bare TypeParam should wildcard-match in the head-exact tier (a headed leaky arg must instead be discriminated via heads_unifiable, else two generic overloads sharing arity — e.g. two `fallback` overloads over Option vs Result — become spuriously "ambiguous function call: N candidates"). Separately, unify() must treat an erased (TypeParam) binding as PROVISIONAL — yielding to a concrete binding rather than hard-conflicting — else a leaky erased binding at one arg spuriously conflicts with real concrete info at another arg (was misfiring as E_FALLBACK_TYPE). Two differing CONCRETE bindings, or two differing ERASED bindings, still correctly conflict. Fixed in commit b83df134ea (task #4038 δ resolver fix, esc-4038-2); 4 regression tests added: overload_chained_result_leaky_arg_resolves_to_result_overload, overload_bare_type_param_arg_still_resolves, unify_erased_type_param_binding_yields_to_concrete, unify_two_distinct_erased_params_still_conflict.

entry_text: In reify, files under crates/*/tests/<harness_name>/ are `mod` submodules of a single harness test binary, so `cargo test --test <file_stem>` fails. Target the binary and filter by module path instead, e.g. `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_compilation_surface examples_smoke` or `cargo test -p reify-eval --test harness_auto_resolution auto_type_param_determinism_tests`. Also, `rustfmt --check` on a crate's lib.rs follows `mod` declarations into every module, so run it on the individual touched files to see only your own hunks.
target_text: Reify C1 consolidated test harnesses: files under crates/<crate>/tests/harness_<subsystem>/ are `#[path]` modules of a single harness_<subsystem> test BINARY, not test targets of their own — so `cargo test -p <crate> --test <filename>` fails with `error: no test target named ...`. The runnable form is a module-path filter: `cargo test -p reify-syntax --test harness_syntax fn_body_semicolon_ambiguity_corpus::`. When adding a file to such a harness, the explicit `#[path = "harness_x/file.rs"] mod file;` attribute is REQUIRED: in an integration-test crate root a bare `mod file;` resolves to the sibling tests/file.rs, not the subdir. If a crate has no root for your subsystem prefix yet, seed a fresh harness_<prefix>.rs (harness_engine.rs #5056 precedent) rather than adding a standalone top-level test binary.

entry_text: Targeted rustfmt check gotcha in reify: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file>` follows `mod` declarations. Passing a crate root (lib.rs/main.rs) or a `tests/mod.rs` therefore checks the WHOLE module tree, producing hundreds of KB of pre-existing hunks from the never-formatted workspace. When checking only touched files, pass leaf module files only, and attribute any hunk to yourself only if it lies inside lines you added. Measured 2026-10-02 on gui/src-tauri (task 7274): passing src/lib.rs produced ~455KB of diff output for the reify-gui crate.
target_text: Reify rustfmt gotcha (no fmt gate): `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <crate>/src/lib.rs` follows `mod` declarations into EVERY child module file, so on a lib.rs it reports hundreds of pre-existing hunks in files you never touched. Filter its output by the touched file paths (`grep 'Diff in' | grep -E '<your files>'`). To apply only the hunks lying wholly inside your own code in a file that also carries main's code, intersect `rustfmt --emit stdout` hunks with the added-line set from `git diff -U0 main HEAD -- <file>` (difflib opcodes; apply a hunk only if every source line is branch-added). Used in task 7543.

target_text:
CLASS GOTCHA (second confirmed instance, 2026-08-31): a test gated on COMMITTED REPO STATE rather than a fixture goes red on every in-flight worktree at once when that state changes, and reads as a branch regression on whichever unlucky task is verifying at the time. Check the merge-base BEFORE debugging it as your own defect.

The diagnostic move, in order — all cheap, all decisive:
1. `git diff --no-ext-diff --quiet main HEAD -- <implicated files>`. If they are byte-identical to main, your branch cannot be the cause.
2. Confirm no TRANSITIVE import path: exec_module the failing test files and match sys.modules against the modules your branch touches. Absence of a direct import is not enough on its own; this closes it.
3. `git log` the DATA file the test reads, not just the test. That is where the change usually is.

TWO INSTANCES NOW, with different mechanisms — which is what makes this a class rather than a one-off:
(a) LIVE-CORPUS instance: test_every_tracked_extension_is_allowlisted self-audits against `git ls-files`, so committing a file with a new extension reddens every worktree. See the existing memory 0e4e5ade-b758-4c13-b1ae-24c419e9935a for the cross-repo fix (CODE_EXTENSIONS in two packages + both test copies + reify's shell script must all agree).
(b) COMMITTED-ARTIFACT instance: fused-memory/tests/test_census_memory_metadata.py and test_memory_eval_retrieval_probe.py read plans/memory-metadata-coverage-history.json. Commit bd092bab74 (author "Test", message "baseline") overwrote it with the stub {"baseline": true}; load_coverage_history (fused-memory/scripts/census_memory_metadata.py:1194) correctly refuses schema_version None, and 4 tests went red on main and on every branch inheriting it. Tracked as ticket tkt_0RT3EGJ8B7V90J97CM0TKVJ1K6 / escalation esc-3949-12.

WHAT (b) ADDS BEYOND (a): the trigger need not be anyone's task at all. Synthetic/harness-authored commits ("Test" author, stub payloads like {"baseline": true} / {"regenerated": true}) can clobber committed plans/ artifacts, so the causing commit may match no task and no plan — do not assume a human or an agent branch produced it.

DO NOT relax the guard to make such tests pass. In (b) the schema_version check exists precisely to refuse misreading an unknown schema; weakening it trades a loud failure for a silent misread. Fix the artifact, or make the test fixture-backed so a clobbered artifact fails at one obvious place instead of scattering reds across unrelated tasks.

entry_text:
Completed: reify-cli panics (exit 101, 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe') when stdout is a closed pipe — restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (escalation-watcher, esc-7906-3, option C). The census sighting's `head --short` was the host skim-hook flattening artifact (see dark-factory 5955), NOT a reify bug. BUT there is a REAL reify-cli defect, and it is this task's scope now: with stdout wired to a closed pipe, reify panics and exits 101 with 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)'. Watcher reproduced it on main: target/debug/reify --version into a pre-closed pipe gives rc=101 and a panic at std/src/io/stdio.rs. Nothing in crates/reify-cli handles SIGPIPE. FIX: restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE at the top of reify-cli's main(), in a small sigpipe module (unix-only, no-op elsewhere). Files: crates/reify-cli/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs,src/sigpipe.rs}, Cargo.lock, tests/harness_cli_surface.rs, tests/harness_cli_surface/cli_broken_pipe.rs. Write two RED tests first: `reify --version` and `reify cache stats` into a closed pipe must NOT exit 101 or print a panic. The reify-audit binaries have the same exposure; that follow-up is filed separately.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION ---
Agent piped a Rust binary's stdout into `head --short` (not a valid head option); head exited immediately on the bad flag, closing the pipe, and the upstream Rust process then panicked on SIGPIPE ('failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe') while still writing. The panic trace is the visually dominant part of the output, obscuring the actual root cause (the unrecognized head flag) printed just above it.

Evidence:
- head: unrecognized option '--short'
...thread 'main' (4068124) panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)

Observed in 1 sighting(s) (project: reify).
Analysis: PREMISE VERIFIED on this branch (task/7906 == main 1cdfa6bdb9, no prior commits): with stdout wired to a pipe whose read end was closed before spawn, the prebuilt target/debug/reify exits rc=101 for BOTH `reify --version` and `REIFY_CACHE_DIR=<empty tmp> reify cache stats`, with stderr "thread 'main' panicked at .../library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9: failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)". The stable toolchain is pinned at 1.96.0 (rust-toolchain.toml); `-Zon-broken-pipe=kill` and the old `#[unix_sigpipe]` attribute are nightly-only, so the fix is a `libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` call as the first statement of main() (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:115).

- Tests go in a NEW member of the existing harness `crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli_surface.rs` (seam rule: consumes no tests/common helpers), file `tests/harness_cli_surface/cli_broken_pipe.rs`, declared `#[cfg(unix)]` → `#[path = ...]` → `mod cli_broken_pipe;` (rpath_smoke's ordering). entry_text: Reify gotcha: `cargo nextest run -p reify-test-support` alone is NOT equivalent coverage to the verify gate for that crate. The package-only run selects 648 tests; under verify's workspace `-p` set, feature unification enables reify-test-support's `eval-helpers` feature and the crate runs 668 tests, including the `helpers::tests::*` lib tests (measured 2026-10-03, task 5991). To re-check reify-test-support after a fix, keep verify's full `-p` list and narrow with `-E 'package(reify-test-support)'`.
target_text: In reify-test-support, unit tests gated `#[cfg(feature = "eval-helpers")]` inside `src/*.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` DO run in the merge gate, and are not silently compiled out: `cargo nextest run --workspace` unifies features, and reify-eval's dev-dep `reify-test-support = { features = ["eval-helpers"] }` turns the feature on for reify-test-support's own lib test target. Standalone, run them with `cargo test -p reify-test-support --features eval-helpers --lib`. A bare `cargo test -p reify-test-support` compiles those tests OUT (eval-helpers is not a default feature), so a green run there proves nothing about them.

Hand-carry mechanics that worked 2026-10-04 for a BLOCKED task under an open L2 (task 5035, esc-5035-3), where Leo's ruling re-scoped the task and assigned it to the interactive session:
1. set_task_status deferred FIRST (blocked → deferred was accepted).
2. update_task the description to the ruled scope.
3. resolve_issue with action='close_only', not 'resume' ('resume' would re-dispatch the task under the carry). The L1 member esc-5035-2 was cascade-dismissed ("l2-cascade").
4. Close the cockpit DecisionRecord.
No stranded-blocked refile loop followed. After the carry, deferred → done with found_on_main was accepted directly.
Carrier walk: submit_task(planning_mode) → add_dependency on the deferred real task → commit_planning → in-progress (claimant_run_id) → merge-deferred → remove_dependency. Then `git branch task/<carrier>` plus `git worktree add .worktrees/<carrier>`; this avoids `git worktree move` and its broken venv shebangs.
A queue row whose task already had a "Merge task/<id> into main" marker was a phantom. The solo carrier went straight to verifying on the laptop and landed in about 20 min. It was NOT flipped by the lane and had to be stamped merged by hand. The orchestrator had already reaped the real task's stale .worktrees/5035 and task/5035 branch by the time of cleanup.
target_text:
Procedure, verified 2026-09-30: hand-carrying a REAL task that is held 'deferred' (to guard it from dispatch) into the merge queue.

What does not work:
- Table A forbids deferred → in-progress for actor 'human' (error illegal_transition).
- Going deferred → pending → in-progress races the scheduler once the task's dependencies are satisfied.

What works, on both dark_factory and reify:
1. Use a CARRIER task. submit_task(planning_mode=True), then add_dependency(carrier → the deferred real task), then commit_planning(carrier). The carrier's pending step is undispatchable because its dependency is not done.
2. set in-progress with claimant_run_id, then merge-deferred.
3. `git branch -m` to task/<carrier>, then `git worktree move` into .worktrees/<carrier>.
4. merge_request under the carrier id.

reify carrier 8084 for task 7269 used exactly this.

After landing:
- a SOLO carrier stays merge-deferred, so stamp it done kind=merged with the marker sha;
- stamp the real task found_on_main.

Note: on reify, hooks/pre-commit exits immediately on non-main branches, so commits on a reify task branch are cheap. Only main commits run the full workspace verify.

READING DARK-FACTORY merge_heartbeat EVENTS FOR PAST QUEUE OCCUPANCY: two traps, measured for task 6021 on 2026-10-01. This complements the 'MEASURING DARK-FACTORY MERGE-GATE THROUGHPUT' memory.

(1) The heartbeat's `depth` does NOT mean runnable work existed. It counts every non-terminal registry entry, stale ones included. Measured: for 49-57 min stretches, depth was 2-18, but verify_in_progress was null and occupancy.inflight_total was 0. head_of_line was either 4792 ('queued', age about 110 h) or 5590's blocked first request, still 'queued' after 5590 had landed (task 3860). To judge whether runnable work was waiting, use verify_in_progress, occupancy.inflight_total, and the queue_depth field on merge_queued events.

(2) The heartbeat is SUPPRESSED when depth == 0 (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::SpeculativeMergeWorker._maybe_log_queue_heartbeat). A heartbeat silence much longer than its ~5-min interval therefore means the pipeline was empty. Example: 33 min of silence on 2026-09-30, 09:09-09:42Z.

Related gotchas:
- merge_verify's duration is in json data.duration_ms; the events.duration_ms column is NULL for it.
- A laptop-runner merge verify lands only after a local parity verify, about 30-40 min after the laptop pass.
target_text: Measured facts about the merge queue, window 2026-09-01 → 09-18 (plans/verify-merge-queue-policy-study-2026-09-18/measure-merge.md). Dark Factory: one serial gate busy 74% of wall time, wait p50 18 min / p90 154 min, 2.40 merge episodes and 1.37 gate runs per landing; tasks landing in one episode had a median merge leg of 1.49 h vs 25.85 h for multi-episode tasks. Outcome mix of 485 episodes: landed 41%, superseded into a train 28% (median re-entry gap 47.6 h), blocked_red 15% (74 reds = 69.8 h = 25% of all gate wall; a DF red costs p50 53 min vs reify's 21 min because DF's gate does not fail fast), needs_rebase bounce 6%, worker_shutdown 4.7%, conflict-at-dispatch 3.3%. Reify: two verify hosts at 28% utilisation, wait p50 0 min, zero train/coalesce events in 17 days — there is no reify merge queue to reorder. P(textual conflict or needs-rebase) rises with base age from 0% at 0–5 commits behind to 28% (DF) / 48% (reify) at 61+, holding footprint fixed; P(red on the merged tree) does NOT rise with base age. Main advances ~38 commits/day, so merge-queue wait contributes only ~2% (DF) / ~1% (reify) of accrued base age — drift is a task-duration effect, not a merge-order effect. Gate duration barely depends on footprint (CV 0.28) under merge_verify_breadth=full, so shortest-gate-first has nothing to sort on. 21% of DF waiting episodes were overtaken by a strictly lower-priority episode; metadata.merge_lane='high' is set on 11 of 5,545 DF tasks. Measurement traps: merge_queued/merge_dequeued.queue_depth reads the drained asyncio inbox and is always 0 (task 5622); merge_heartbeat depth/head_of_line is contaminated by never-retired entries on 12–17% of rows (task 3860); merge_attempt rows with outcome main_health_red and a probe_host are main-health PROBES outside any dequeue window and inflate outcome censuses; merge_finalized.landed_via_chain is None everywhere because deep chains are not enabled — not a defect; the PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS A/B inside the window confounds any cross-date DF gate-duration comparison.

entry_text: FalkorDB planner gotcha, cosine leg (measured 2026-10-03, task 6238, after γ/task 3708 provisioned per-property indices). graphiti_core edge_similarity_search's `MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH DISTINCT e,n,m, cos AS score ...` plans as Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan [e] on the RELATES_TO.group_id index. That is one index scan per Entity node: 825 ms on dark_factory (21.7k edges) and a 1000 ms 'Query timed out' on reify (26.8k edges). Edge-first with late endpoint binding avoids it: `MATCH ()-[e:RELATES_TO]->() WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH e, cos AS score WHERE score > $min WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m WHERE n:Entity AND m:Entity ...`. It ran in 52-60 ms on dark_factory and 92-108 ms on reify. Node cosine (Node By Index Scan) was fine at 85-135 ms. Rule: in GRAPH.EXPLAIN, any *Scan operator that has children is re-executed per row.

entry_text: The unblock_auto dry-run proposal for Task 5671 (2026-09-28) misread rebase committer dates as landing times. It said three amend commits "landed at 07:34Z after the pass", but 07:34Z was when the branch was rebased. The pre-rebase tip that passed full verify at 07:32Z was itself the amended code, with a byte-identical patch. When reading a branch timeline, use author dates and the reflog (`git reflog show --date=iso task/<id>`), not committer dates, which a rebase rewrites.
target_text: A "correction" to a commit DATE in an escalation triage note may be an AUTHOR-vs-COMMIT date confusion, not an error. On esc-4545-2 the architect dated 650a173d0f as 2026-08-17 and called the gap to the manifest commit "11 days"; the interactive triage note "corrected" this to 2026-08-19 / "13 days" and framed the architect as mistaken (while noting the error was in the architect's favour). `git log -1 --format='author=%ad commit=%cd' --date=iso 650a173d0f` returns author=2026-08-17 19:04:28 +0100, commit=2026-08-19 00:49:52 +0100 — both parties were right on different fields. `git log --diff-filter=A` and most default log output show the AUTHOR date; a rebase or delayed merge separates the two by days. Before recording a date discrepancy as someone's mistake, print both fields. This matters because a reader who catches the discrepancy can be tempted to discard the whole argument with it.

entry_text: Cancelling a spawned_from parent BEFORE its child raises a blocking reconciler scope_violation ('Task N orphaned: parent P cancelled') on the still-live child within seconds, even when the child is cancelled moments later. Seen 2026-09-30 as esc-6497-1 and esc-6548-1. Cancel children first. If it happens anyway, close with resolve_issue(action='close_only', resolution_class='moot-terminal-subject'). Before cancelling a parent whose child stays live, re-point the child's metadata.spawned_from at the surviving task (done for #6371: 6134 → 6934, with spawned_from_original and spawned_from_repointed keys).
target_text: Before CANCELLING a parent task, disposition its spawned follow-ups FIRST — cancelling the parent orphans every agent-followup child and files one BLOCKING scope_violation escalation per child. Violated this on 2026-09-16 cancelling task 6938: it immediately orphaned #7571 and #7613 and produced esc-7571-2 and esc-7613-2, both blocking, minutes later. The children were fine (pending and dispatchable, and 6938's own cancellation record named both as the intended homes for its surviving content), so the escalations were pure self-inflicted triage. TWO COROLLARIES learned in the cleanup. First, when the orphaning is DELIBERATE, do NOT rewrite the children's `metadata.spawned_from` to silence the detector: the cancelled parent IS their true historical parent, and falsifying provenance to quiet an alarm is worse than the alarm. Instead write the explanation into the parent's cancellation record naming each child by id, so the lineage stays readable, and close the orphan escalations against that. Second, the orphan detector's own recommendation in these cases was `expand_scope (keep)`, which was correct — an administrative/hollowed-out cancellation almost never retracts the children's findings.

entry_text: Attributing a file deletion to its owning task: `git log --diff-filter=D -- <path>` can return a "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" commit whose NNNN is a stale lane label, not the task that owns the change. Measured example: d4f413bdf3, subject "(task 1933)", deleted reify-compiler's parse_signatures.rs, analysis_signatures.rs and signatures_common.rs, but it sits on task/6001's branch (merge 87b744b189). Decide ownership by range membership, `git log --format=%h <merge>^1..<merge>^2 | grep <sha>`, never by the subject's task number.
target_text: The warm-lane GC's "chore: save WIP before warm-lane reclaim (task NNNN)" auto-save commits can cite the WRONG task id — apparently the lane's previous occupant rather than the branch's actual task. Observed on branch task/5360, whose tip commit 057fa90721 is labelled "task 1933" but contains only that task's own `crates/reify-eval/src/unfold.rs` work. Consequence: `git log --grep=<task-id>` silently misses such commits, so provenance sweeps must also inspect the branch tip directly. Verify the diff's content before assuming cross-task contamination.

Description: PRD: docs/prds/v0_6/solution-set-completeness.md §3.1. Ship the solution-set completeness axis as an ADDITIVE sibling carrier in reify-ir, alongside (not inside) the landed F-result types.

WHY. SolveResult::Solved.unique is a bool, and a bool cannot distinguish five genuinely different states: proved exactly one, proved two, found one and proved nothing, found two, proved none exist. Every solver-honesty defect in this area is that type error surfacing somewhere.

DELIVER.
1. enum Completeness = Exhaustive | Partial{reason: PartialReason} | Refuted{narrowing: ConstraintNodeId}.
2. enum PartialReason = BoxBudgetExhausted | DimensionAboveEnvelope{dims} | DomainUnbounded{param} | NotIntervalRepresentable{constraint} | InnerSolveUnproven | ProbeOnly | NotAttempted.
3. SolutionSet{solutions, completeness}; an additive `completeness` field on RankedSolveResult::Ranked.
4. The C1 derived-`unique` helper: unique == (completeness == Exhaustive && solutions.len() == 1). No producer may write `unique` from any other reasoning.
5. A default `Partial{NotAttempted}` lift so every existing producer keeps behaving exactly as today until it opts in.

INVARIANTS (PRD §3.2): C1 unique is derived never asserted; C2 ProvenOptimal requires Exhaustive; C3 Refuted is a proof while Partial-with-empty-set is not, and the two must never render alike; C4 a Partial verdict may never report how many solutions exist.

CORRECTION to memory 897461ee (pytest-timeout inversion band, task 5147). Its rule "Do NOT simply DELETE a slow test's marker" gives a stale reason: it says the ini default is 60. The ini timeout in orchestrator/pyproject.toml is now 540 (task 5442), and verify passes --timeout=300. Deleting an in-band marker would leave a test at 540s locally and 300s under verify. The advice still holds, for different reasons:
(a) The offline-lane modules' test_every_composing_caller_carries_a_timeout_override REQUIRES markers on some tests and checks their values.
(b) Pending task 5529 plans to run every EXPLICIT marker in signal mode (a clean failure) while unmarked tests keep the thread-mode worker kill.
(c) The ini default has moved 60 -> 300 -> 540, so do not size a heavy test by it.
So migrate an in-band marker to the name `@pytest.mark.timeout(VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT)`. Never use an expression: the guard resolves it to None ("no opinion") and the marker escapes the sweep. The one exception: a module whose module-level pytestmark already sets a budget >= 300. There, delete the decorator, because a per-test decorator overrides the module mark and would narrow it. test_marker_registration_drift.py is an example, with WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT = 540. Measured by task 5149's architect, 2026-10-02, base 2d56f6e406.

RESOLUTION of the pytest-timeout inversion-band gotcha (memory 458d79ad-39aa-48a5-b87d-bf7ba2570111, task 5147) — LANDED 2026-09-07. Read this WITH that entry, which carries the mechanism and census; this one records only what changed, because that entry's closing claim that "nothing checks a per-test marker's VALUE" is now FALSE and it could not be amended in place (content_amend is restricted to recon-stage-/curator- agents).

WHAT TO WRITE when an orchestrator test needs more than the 60s ini default:
    from _orch_helpers import VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT
    @pytest.mark.timeout(VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT)
The only other sanctioned option is N <= 60, a DELIBERATE tight bound for a test asserting something happens FAST. Anything strictly between the two inverts.
Do NOT simply DELETE a slow test's marker — the ini default is 60, so removal leaves it worse off under a bare local `pytest` than the bug being fixed. That is why the named instance was RAISED to 300 rather than dropped.

WHERE THE RATIONALE LIVES, singly: the `VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT = 300` comment block in `orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py`, beside PYPROJECT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT and WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT. The guard, the amended pyproject comment and the fixed call site all POINT there rather than restating it. Follow that convention when you touch any of them.

WHY IT IS A LITERAL 300 and deliberately NOT `5 * PYPROJECT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` despite equalling it today: the quantity is the VERIFY CLI BUDGET, and the ini default is the OTHER EDGE of the band, not a scale factor. Deriving one edge from the other would let a tightened ini default drag the constant DOWN in silence — `timeout = 20` would shrink it to 100 — collapsing the band toward nothing while a ratio assertion stayed green as an identity. Same hazard and same resolution as WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT deliberately not borrowing HEAVY_BARRIER_TEST_TIMEOUT's 300. A literal instead needs an EXECUTABLE link: a drift test re-reads orchestrator/orchestrator.yaml's test_command at runtime. GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this instance: when two constants happen to be equal, derive one from the other ONLY if the causal story actually runs that way; coincidental equality is how a silent shrink gets a green test.

THE GUARD: `orchestrator/tests/test_timeout_marker_inversion_guard.py`. AST-sweeps all FOUR binding forms — function/method decorator, class decorator, module-level `pytestmark`, class-level `pytestmark` — which is precisely the gap the pre-existing guards left (test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py reads MODULE-LEVEL marks only, for a different per-file family invariant). Unresolvable arguments resolve to None = "no opinion", never "too small", so it is a FLOOR and never manufactures false offenders.

IT IS A RATCHET, NOT A SWEEP — and this is the part to respect if you touch it. 61 pre-existing in-band sites across 19 modules are grandfathered in `_GRANDFATHERED`, keyed by (module, qualname): per-SITE and NOT a per-file count, because a count nets to zero when one marker is added and another removed in the same file, leaving a hole in a guard whose whole purpose is catching accidental additions. Entries may only ever be REMOVED; a stale-entry twin test fails on any entry that no longer names a real in-band site, so the list cannot rot into a permanent blanket exemption. The 61 were NOT migrated in 5147 on purpose: they live in the hottest files in the repo (test_merge_queue.py and its deep_* siblings, test_crash_recovery.py), so rewriting ~20 files at once would have taken locks on nearly everything in-flight fleet tasks were editing and risked destabilising the very verify path the task existed to de-flake. Red-on-main vectors in DF, September 2026 (measured 2026-09-28). Three of the five red-main incidents were single-parent commits made directly to main that bypassed the merge gate:
- 5230: docs commit 7938676c28
- 5425: config commit a47b5a506e
- 5878: nightly census data commit 33bc55e544

Each tripped a test that reads repo data outside its own module. The other two (5210, 5842) were environment-dependent tests. None came through a gate-verified branch.

DF's merge gate runs merge_verify_breadth "full", meaning every registered module's full suite on the merged tree. Task-lane verifies, including the pre-merge re-verify, are therefore pre-filters: changing them does not change the rate at which red reaches main. The gate-side escape paths that already exist are: the disjoint-delta skip (merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree), flake suppression, and crash-truncated sessions (5492). The lever for red-on-main is gate bypass: route automated commits through the merge queue, or run the repo guards pre-commit.

Do not let a probe-environment artifact be reported as a second main-red — check whether the failing test depends on a resolved environment before attributing it to the change under test.

entry_text: Task 'Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source' completed. Landed in commit 095e5f6da2ed90ae832f87620426a3c03cfada83.
target_text: reify's tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule: `member_access` (tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:1583) is `object '.' identifier` with no callTail, and the only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (bare identifier) and `trait_method_call` (qualified callee). So `xs.map(|v| ...)`, `xs.filter(...)`, `xs.all(...)` — and any `obj.method(args)` — are parse errors in every position (let AND constraint), for any element type. `xs.count` parses only because it is a bare member access. Consequently the `map`/`filter`/`all`/`any`/`generate` arms of `eval_method_call` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~3695-3845) are unreachable from .ri source and are exercised only by Rust tests. Lambdas themselves parse fine in free-function argument position (`generate(3, |i| i)`, `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])`). Measured on HEAD 975cbfc301; filed as a follow-up from task #5385 (esc-5385-1).

entry_text: fused-memory's MCP 'search' tool reports some failures, for example a project_id validation failure, as a NORMAL tool result: a text block containing JSON {"error": "...", "error_type": "ValidationError"}, with isError NOT set. Any consumer that treats 'not isError' as success will ingest the error document as data. A robust consumer checks for a list-valued 'results' key, as orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/briefing.py::_is_search_reply does since task 3659.
target_text: A client calling fused-memory MCP tools must check THREE distinct failure shapes or it will count failed writes as landed: (1) a JSON-RPC `{"error": ...}` envelope; (2) an in-tool exception, which `@mcp_tool_errors()` converts to a 200 carrying `{"error": ...}` / `success: False` in the payload; and (3) a FastMCP-level failure — argument validation, an unknown or renamed tool — which bypasses that decorator entirely and surfaces only as `result.isError: true` inside a 200. Checking (1) and (2) alone is the common bug: a renamed tool or a wrong wire param then reads as a successful write forever. Precedents that get it right: `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py:3817` (isError) plus `extract_rejection` (payload), and `scripts/consume_redispatch_requests.py`. Related trap: if a tool's text content block is not JSON, an unwrapping client typically returns a `{'_raw': <text>}` stand-in — that too is usually an error string, not a success.

Completed: Unblock whole-blob metadata repair on done tasks: update_task's done_provenance floor makes metadata_mode='replace' structurally unusable
Description: Split out of task 3697 (esc-3697-4) by the steward on 2026-08-06. 3697 is rescoped to ship its documentation + tested migration script; THIS task provides the write path 3697 needs, then executes the live migration 3697 could not.

OBSERVED, first-hand code reads (not inferred):

1. sqlite_task_backend.py:2575-2591 — update_task raises DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError
   for ANY metadata payload that parses to a dict containing 'done_provenance'. The check
   is PRESENCE-ONLY: no value-unchanged carve-out, no metadata_mode carve-out. It fires
   before _resolve_metadata_mode, before ensure_connected(), before the row SELECT.

2. _merge_metadata has no deletion sentinel (merge is shallow {**old, **new}), and there is
   no task-level metadata_delete_keys — that API exists only for MEMORIES
   (memory_service.py / update_memory). backend.set_task_status
   (sqlite_task_backend.py:1938-1947) accepts no metadata argument.

3. The privileged non-protocol seam stamp_audit_metadata (sqlite_task_backend.py:2835,
   added by task 2201) also hardcodes _merge_metadata(mode='merge'), so it cannot retire a
   key either, and it is not reachable over MCP.

4. Single enforcement point: the interceptor does NOT pre-check independently — it catches
   the backend exception at task_interceptor.py:4366 and converts via .to_error_dict().
   Task 2203 deliberately deleted the duplicate guard copies. So a fix has ONE code site,
   not several.

CONSEQUENCE (the generalization worth fixing): every done/merged task carries
done_provenance, so metadata_mode='replace' is structurally unusable on ALL of them — while
task_backend_protocol.py:209 and server/tools.py:5956 both document replace mode as
"the sanctioned repair path". That doc claim and this floor are in direct tension. Any
task needing a key RETIRED (not just added) from a done task's metadata is currently
unfixable through public API.

CANDIDATE DESIGNS (architect decides; do not assume):
  (A) Identical-passthrough carve-out — permit a payload whose done_provenance is
      byte-identical to the stored value, on the reasoning that an unchanged passthrough is
      not a write of that key. Smallest change, preserves the floor's actual intent
      (set_task_status remains the only thing that can CHANGE done_provenance), and unblocks
      whole-blob repair on every done task. Must compare against the STORED value read under
      the same txn, not trust the caller.
  (B) Task-level metadata_delete_keys on update_task, mirroring the memories API. Most
      general, largest blast radius, and needs its own write-authority thinking (deleting
      done_provenance must stay forbidden).
  (C) Widen the privileged stamp_audit_metadata seam to accept a mode/deletion argument and
      expose a narrow operator-only path. Follows the existing 2201 precedent.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, also reconcile the docstrings at task_backend_protocol.py:209 and
server/tools.py:5956 so "the sanctioned repair path" is either true or qualified.

migrate_task_metadata_to_x_namespace.py lands with 3697 — it is dry-run-by-default,

Completed: Merge lane never un-stacks a train member whose predecessor leaves the queue without landing — the orphan's conflicts are then reported as the member's own
Description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 while resolving esc-4137-3/esc-4137-4 (steward). Task 4137's merge was blocked for reasons that had nothing to do with task 4137.

THE DEFECT. When a train is formed, an order>0 member is rebased onto its predecessor's branch tip rather than main (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::_resolve_predecessor_tip, "train-predecessor tip or main"). That is correct at formation. But if the predecessor subsequently leaves the merge queue WITHOUT LANDING, nothing un-stacks the member. The member's branch silently keeps carrying every one of the predecessor's commits, and its next merge_request therefore reports the PREDECESSOR's conflicts against main as its own.

THE SIGHTING. task/4137 (7 own commits, all dashboard) was stacked behind task/4480 at 2026-09-08 21:49 (reflog task/4137@{0} = 'rebase (finish) onto 9788a34b13'). Task 4480 then went to status=pending and left the queue, never merged; merge_status(task_id=4480) = unknown. Ten days later 4137's merge attempt reported 15 conflicts — of which 14 were 4480's fused-memory test refactor vs main's task-3895 load_script_module migration. Replaying only 4137's own delta (`git merge-tree --merge-base=9788a34b13 main <tip>`) conflicts in exactly ONE file, its own index.html cache-buster.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE BRANCH. The failure is mis-attributed by construction. The merger sees a 15-way conflict "in task 4137" and every available remedy is wrong: resolving toward main silently DROPS the absent predecessor's entire deliverable (here 786 lines of new files plus a 15-suite rewrite that exists nowhere else); combining both sides lands the predecessor's whole deliverable through the member's merge, outside the member's plan scope and file locks, and requires implementing the predecessor against a main ~2145 commits ahead. Both destructive options look locally reasonable to an agent that has not audited the branch's reflog. Only the third — un-stack — is correct, and identifying it requires noticing the stacking in the first place. Two escalation rounds were consumed on this one instance before a human-authority role took the ref rewrite.

COMPLETION CONDITION. The lane should detect, at merge_request admission time, that a branch's merge-base against main is a non-landed sibling task's branch tip, and un-stack it automatically via the operation the lane already owns — git_ops.py::materialize_member_solo(predecessor_ref=...), equivalently `git rebase --onto main <predecessor_tip> <branch>` — before attempting the merge. Escalate only if THAT rebase conflicts. Suggested shape: on dequeue, resolve the recorded train predecessor (or derive it by testing whether merge-base(branch, main) is the tip of another task's branch), check whether it is an ancestor of main, and if not, un-stack. Regression test: a member stacked on a predecessor branch that never lands merges solo on its own delta and reports only its own conflicts.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: how many other branches are currently in this state. The condition is cheap to detect in bulk (for each task branch, is merge-base(branch, main) equal to some other task/* tip that is not an ancestor of main?) and each hit is a mis-attributed merge failure waiting to happen. Task 4480 itself remains status=pending with 15 commits living only on task/4480; it is the one carrier of that work and should be scheduled before its base drifts further.

NOT A DUPLICATE (searched): 1878 (worktree-reuse rebases onto main unconditionally) is the mirror-image bug and is done; 1867/4737/4953 are merge-deferred stranding after coalescing; 4669 is a requeue rebase dropping a commit whose patch no longer applies; 2403 is a branch reset to an unrelated tip. None covers a member left stacked on a predecessor that exited the queue unlanded.

AUDIT PROCEDURE + MEASURED POPULATION for the "task branch rebased onto an unlanded sibling tip" defect (dark-factory, 2026-09-07, task 4818 steward). Extends the esc-4818-6 root-cause note and memory 3ab43a5b; supersedes the population figure of 14.

THE CONCLUSIVE PROBE is the reflog onto-target audit, NOT a conventional-commit-scope heuristic. For each `refs/heads/task/*`, extract every distinct `rebase (finish) ... onto <sha>` from the branch reflog and test `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main`. Any rc=1 means that branch was replayed onto a base that is not on main.

MEASURED: 828 task branches; only 386 still have reflog (442 pruned, so every count here is a FLOOR); 59 of 386 (15.3%) have at least one non-main onto-target. The scope heuristic found 14 — a strict undercount, because it only fires when a commit subject happens to name another task id.

THE FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS YOU MUST RULE OUT, and the discriminator. A non-main onto-target could in principle be the branch's OWN earlier commit (a benign amend/autosquash rebase). Discriminate with `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/task/ --contains <sha>`: if the only branch containing it is the branch itself, benign; if a DIFFERENT task branch contains it, contamination; if nothing contains it, it was orphaned by a later rebase (still real). Run on all 59: ZERO were benign self-amends. Reporting 59 without this check would have been unsound, and it is cheap.

CONTAMINATION CHAINS, so do not assume one hop. task/4347 was itself rebased onto d160001242 ("resolve: merge main into task/4369"); 4347's tip then contaminated BOTH task/4818 and task/4788.

WHY SHA PROBES LIE HERE (the trap that sank the first investigation): after a rebase the same patch exists under two shas, so `merge-base --is-ancestor` between them returns rc=1 "unrelated" while `git patch-id --stable` returns an identical id. Measured on the specimen: 29a73af3e0 and ace4d81f98 both hash to af201b5c9ac6aed4d58036612867285f836778a2. MATCH BY PATCH-ID OR SUBJECT, NEVER BY SHA ACROSS A REBASE.

MECHANISM (read, not guessed): `GitOps.rebase_onto_main` runs a bare `git rebase <target>` with no validation of target. Three call sites pass a non-main base — `stack_train_branches` (onto `task/<sibling>`, deliberate for merge trains), `create_worktree`'s requeue path via `_resolve_predecessor_tip` (existence check only), and `_bounce_conflicting_suffix_items` (a speculative frozen staging tip). `GitOps.is_ancestor` exists and is used ~40 places but at ZERO rebase call sites.

FRAMING THAT MATTERS: stacking onto a predecessor is INTENDED for merge trains, so "never rebase onto non-main" is the wrong fix. The defect is the missing lifecycle — `metadata['train']` is never cleared anywhere in the orchestrator package (zero hits for pop/del/None), so a requeue re-stacks onto a long-dead predecessor indefinitely, and nothing ever un-stacks a branch. Prefer an explicit opt-in parameter so intentional stacking sites must name themselves and every other caller is guarded by default.

REMEDY for an affected branch: plain `git rebase main` (do NOT pass --reapply-cherry-picks) — git drops the duplicates by patch-id. On task/4818 that was five `warning: skipped previously applied commit` lines, zero conflicts. Verify with `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` matching the plan's declared files.

DISTINCT POPULATION, do not conflate: a separate sweep found 25 branches touching files outside their plan's declared `files`, but those are mostly shared test helpers (conftest.py, _orch_helpers.py, _fm_helpers.py) — ordinary scope drift, not commit injection.

Tracked as ticket tkt_0RTBRY6P6K2HPACA0XF05E498M (high).

entry_text: GOTCHA (escalation tests): the `serve_escalation_mcp` factory in escalation/tests/conftest.py drives its readiness handshake with `asyncio.run(...)`, so calling it from inside an `@pytest.mark.asyncio` test body raises `RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop`. Start the server from a SYNC fixture (e.g. `@pytest.fixture def served(tmp_path, serve_escalation_mcp): return serve_escalation_mcp(tmp_path / 'esc')`) and let the async test take that fixture — the pattern test_escalation_http_helper.py and escalation/tests/test_server_eval_lane.py use.
target_text: To drive the REAL escalation FastMCP server chokepoint (e.g. `resolve_issue`) from within a dashboard FastAPI route test, use a SYNC test that runs the async archive builder via `asyncio.run(...)`, NOT an async test. Starlette's sync `TestClient` (the `client` conftest fixture) runs the app lifespan on its own anyio portal loop in a separate thread; an async test would already hold a running loop in the main thread and conflict. Pattern (dashboard/tests/test_escalation_lifecycle_gate.py, task 2662): `queue = EscalationQueue(base/'data'/'escalations'); server = create_server(queue, startup_sweep=False); arch = asyncio.run(build_archive(queue, server))` then use the sync `client`. Note `resolve_issue` is a sync `def` tool, so `tool = await server.get_tool('resolve_issue'); tool.fn(...)` returns directly (only `get_tool` is awaited). Tests that DON'T need TestClient (record-level / aggregator-only) can just be async and await the builder directly, since dashboard pyproject sets `asyncio_mode = "auto"`.

entry_text: PRECISE MECHANISM + FIX for the slow nested-pytest probe (refines memories aa61611b / fa1896ee; measured 2026-10-01, pytest 9.0.3, task 5146). `pytest <tmp_path>/probe.py -c orchestrator/pyproject.toml` sets confcutdir to the inifile's dir, and `PytestPluginManager._is_in_confcutdir(p)` is literally `p not in confcutdir.parents`. So /tmp and every dir under it count as "inside" (only `/` is excluded). Two effects follow. (1) `Session.collect` roots the tree at `<Dir tmp>` and runs pytest_ignore_collect plus a stat on every entry of the fleet-shared /tmp: ~72k entries, 31k Dir nodes, 128s of a 131s run at loadavg ~475, versus 0.00s collection with the fix. (2) Any conftest.py in /tmp, /tmp/pytest-of-leo, … gets IMPORTED into the probe, which is a contamination hazard. FIX: pass `--confcutdir=<probe's own dir>` (with the probe in a subdir of tmp_path). This bounds both conftest discovery and the collection root. The probe can stay in tmp_path, with no in-repo scratch dir to clean up. A control arm whose inifile sits beside the probe never had the problem, because its confcutdir already equals the probe dir.
target_text: In the dark-factory monorepo, spawning a nested `pytest --collect-only` subprocess bound to a subproject config via `-c <path>/pyproject.toml` is extremely slow (15-25s+, CPU-bound in pytest's conftest/collection machinery) when the target test-file argument shares no close common ancestor with the config file's directory (e.g. a file under system /tmp, which is exactly what pytest's `tmp_path` fixture produces) — pytest falls back to a wide collection sweep. Fix: create the throwaway probe file inside the target subproject tree instead (e.g. `tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=<subproject>/tests)`), which keeps collection near-instant (~0.1-0.5s). See cockpit/tests/test_smoke_marker_config.py (task 2446) for the pattern of a behavioral pytest-collection guard test that avoids this trap.

target_text: FastMCP 3.x stdio MCP servers (orchestrator's plan_tools/verdict_tools) make a SYNCHRONOUS network call on startup: server.run(transport='stdio') defaults show_banner=True, and run_stdio_async->log_server_banner->check_for_newer_version does an httpx.get to pypi.org (2s timeout, 12h cache in ~/.local/share/fastmcp/) BEFORE serving stdio. Under cold cache / network pressure / concurrent load this delays the MCP initialize handshake past the CLI's MCP_TIMEOUT (30s), so the Claude Code CLI silently DROPS the server and the agent reaches turn 1 with those tools absent (intermittent, non-blocking). Investigated as task 2942 (plan-tools unreachable, 3rd reproduction). Fix: pass show_banner=False to server.run() and/or set FASTMCP_SHOW_SERVER_BANNER=false + FASTMCP_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=off in the launch dict env — either fully eliminates the network call (log_server_banner is the only caller of check_for_newer_version).

entry_text: GOTCHA (task 3096): close_only only means "no task-status change". Harness._on_escalation_resolved calls event.set() on _escalation_events[task_id] for EVERY resolution, close_only and dismiss=True included, before it dispatches the action, so any closure wakes a live workflow waiting on that task id. Also, queue.submit_resolved leaves resolution_action None, and the legacy D10 mapping reads a resolved record as 'resume' (re-pend). Stamp esc.resolution_action='close_only' before submit_resolved when you mean a no-effect closure. To suppress the wake as well, you need an explicit early return at the top of the callback, like the eval-lane guard keyed on shared.eval_lane.eval_lane_provenance.

target_text:
Completed: ts_parser: add an external seeding hook for Lowering::import_bindings (mirror parse_with_prelude_enums) so std.prelude + pub import re-exported qualifiers are not rejected at parse time
Description: Follow-up filed by task #5495 (stdlib-namespace μ, qualified-ref grammar production). Raised as suggestion #4 of #5495's cycle-2 code review (ISSUES_FOUND, 0 blocking / 6 suggestions, 2026-08-13) and deliberately DEFERRED there rather than implemented — see #5495's plan design decision "suggestion #4 is DEFERRED to ν/ι".

WHAT: task #5495 added `Lowering::import_bindings: HashSet<String>` in `crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs` (~line 162), populated only by `collect_import_bindings` (~line 559) walking the CURRENT FILE's own import declarations. `lower_namespaced_call` (~line 4473) rejects any qualified call `pp.Foo()` whose qualifier `pp` is not in that set.

THE GAP: unlike the sibling `known_enums` field, which has an external seeding path via the public `parse_with_prelude_enums(source, module_path, prelude_enum_names)` entry point (ts_parser.rs ~line 54), `import_bindings` has NO seeding hook — `with_prelude_enums` initialises it to `HashSet::new()` unconditionally. So a qualifier that a file does NOT import directly, but which is visible to it through `import std.prelude` (stdlib-namespace PRD §4 D-4 / §10 Q1) or through a `pub import` re-export (resolution-unification μ, consumed by stdlib-namespace ι), will be REJECTED at parse time with "unknown qualifier `X`".

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, NOT FIXED: `std.prelude` is task ι's deliverable and qualified resolution is task ν's (#5505); neither had landed when μ was written. Adding the constructor in μ would have shipped an API with no caller, whose correct signature depends on decisions ι has not yet made. The guard fails CLOSED (a rejected qualifier yields a loud, specific diagnostic, never silence), so widening the binding set later unwinds nothing.

SUGGESTED WORK: mirror the enum precedent — add a `with_prelude_bindings` / `parse_with_prelude_bindings` seed alongside `with_prelude_enums`, wired from whichever of ι / ν first needs it. If that owner concludes the seeding belongs at the resolution layer rather than the parse layer, closing this as won't-fix with that reasoning recorded is an acceptable outcome; the point is that the constraint is tracked rather than rediscovered.

FILES: crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax/namespaced_ref_lowering_tests.rs
RELATED: #5505 (ν, qualified resolution over DefEnv keying) — the most likely consumer. PRD docs/prds/v0_6/stdlib-namespace.md §4 D-4, §10 Q1.
Analysis: PREMISE CHECK (base 091e927d26).
- The field the task calls `Lowering::import_bindings` now exists as `namespace_bindings: HashSet<String>` (ts_parser.rs:174), alongside `entity_bindings: HashMap<String, ImportKind>` (:186). Both are filled only by `collect_import_bindings` (:867) during `lower_source_file`'s first pass (:596-598). `with_prelude_enums` (:208) seeds only `known_enums` and initialises both binding maps empty. `lower_namespaced_call` (:5403) rejects any `q.Name(...)` whose `q` is not in `namespace_bindings` (:5434), with the message "unknown qualifier `q` ... declare one as `import <path> as q`".
- The test file has moved. The task names `tests/harness_syntax/namespaced_ref_lowering_tests.rs`, but task #7040 moved it to `crates/reify-syntax/tests/harness_syntax_lowering/namespaced_ref_lowering_tests.rs` (955 lines). The harness unit is at 5113 of the 20000-line kLOC cap, so the new tests can go into that existing file. No new test file is needed, which matters because reify-syntax is a consolidatable crate.

Completed: Graphiti BM25 edge search times out on every provisioned graph: FalkorDB plans graphiti's `{uuid: rel.uuid}` join as a per-row Entity label scan
Description: Discovered 2026-10-03 (~03:40-03:50Z) by task 3711's architect (FalkorDB index provisioning ζ, PRD docs/prds/falkordb-index-provisioning.md). Task 3708 (γ, merged 2026-10-02 11:42Z) provisioned fulltext + per-property range indices on every registered graph; fused-memory.service last restarted 2026-10-02 22:51 BST. Since then Graphiti search is failing, and this blocks task 3711's primary signal.

OBSERVATIONS (all read-only: MCP search, or `docker exec docker-falkordb-1 redis-cli GRAPH.RO_QUERY / GRAPH.EXPLAIN`):
1. MCP search(stores=['graphiti'], limit=5) failed with ResponseError 'Query timed out' 3/3: dark_factory 'task 3127', dark_factory 'FalkorDB fulltext index provisioning', reify 'rustfmt gate'.
2. fused-memory.service journal since the 22:51 BST restart: 13,217 lines matching 'timed out' (graphiti_core.driver.falkordb_driver ERROR 'Error executing FalkorDB query: Query timed out').
3. GRAPH.CONFIG: TIMEOUT 1000, TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 0, TIMEOUT_MAX 0.
4. Bare `CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO','3127') YIELD relationship, score RETURN count(relationship)` on dark_factory: 3 rows in 0.72 ms. So BM25 itself serves.
5. graphiti_core's own join (graphiti_core/search/search_utils.py::edge_fulltext_search, FalkorDB branch): `CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO','3127') YIELD relationship AS rel, score MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN ['dark_factory'] RETURN e.uuid, score LIMIT 10` returned 'Query timed out' on all 3 runs. Token 'index' timed out the same way. On reify, token 'cargo' (140 fulltext rows) also timed out.
6. GRAPH.EXPLAIN of that query: ProcedureCall -> Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan [e:RELATES_TO] -> Filter -> Project -> Limit. That is a full Entity label scan per yielded row.
7. The same join with a token that yields 0 fulltext rows took 13.9 ms.
8. A rewritten join, `... YIELD relationship AS e, score WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m WHERE e.group_id IN ['dark_factory'] RETURN e.uuid, n.uuid, m.uuid, score LIMIT 10`, took 6.5 ms on dark_factory.
9. The cosine-leg shape (`MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN [...] WITH e, (2 - vec.cosineDistance(e.fact_embedding, v))/2 AS score ...`) took 736 ms on dark_factory. That is under the 1000 ms read TIMEOUT, but close to it.
10. Open L2 esc-durable-write-dead-letter-2 (root_cause 'infra-outage:fused-memory-graphiti-falkordb-query-timeout-dead-letters-add-memory', filed 2026-10-02 14:02Z) records add_memory_graphiti writes dead-lettering on 'Query timed out'.

Hypothesis: before γ, no RELATES_TO fulltext index existed, so queryRelationships yielded 0 rows and the join never ran. Now that BM25 serves, the `{uuid: rel.uuid}` property-map join runs as a per-row label scan, overruns the 1000 ms read TIMEOUT, and fails the whole Graphiti search. The same join inside add_episode's edge-dedup searches would plausibly also explain the write dead-letters.

WORK: make Graphiti's FalkorDB fulltext edge search finish well inside the read TIMEOUT. Also audit the node and community fulltext paths, and any other `{uuid: x.uuid}` re-match that follows a YIELD. graphiti_core checks `driver.search_interface` before its built-in Cypher, and fused-memory already overrides build_fulltext_query in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/graphiti_client.py. One candidate fix is to bind the yielded relationship directly (startNode/endNode) rather than re-matching by uuid. Add a live-FalkorDB regression test: a scratch graph with production indices and at least one matching edge, asserting search returns rows within budget. Build it with fused-memory/tests/_falkor_index_live.py. Do NOT drop the provisioned indices as a mitigation without an operator ruling, because that reverts γ. Once l…[truncated, 11612 chars total]
target_text: The Graphiti "Task N" entity-conflation defect behind esc-3375-1 has a three-link root cause, verified in code on 2026-08-05. (1) `_MultiTenantFalkorDriver.build_indices_and_constraints` is a `pass` stub at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/graphiti_client.py:291, and the ONLY index builder `_ensure_indices` (:474) calls exactly that overridden method, then logs "Ensured indices" — so no fulltext index has ever been built on ANY graph in the FalkorDB instance. (2) A missing FalkorDB fulltext index makes `db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes` return zero rows SILENTLY with no exception, so the BM25 leg of NODE_HYBRID_SEARCH_RRF is dead and candidate retrieval degrades to embedding-only. (3) gpt-4o-mini then picks a numerically adjacent sibling from ~800 `Task N` nodes sitting at 0.94-0.99 mutual cosine (only 0.046 separates rank 2 from rank 20), handed bare name strings with no summary and no attributes because `entity_types` is always None. Graphiti's DETERMINISTIC dedup layer is NOT at fault: `Task 3331` vs `Task 3330` scores Jaccard 0.333 against a 0.90 threshold, so it correctly abstains and the LLM decides. The index regression came from commit 723ec915c3 (2026-04-02), which made `clone()` return the suppressed subclass to stop a CREATE INDEX storm and silently turned `_ensure_indices` into a no-op in the same diff.

entry_text: GOTCHA (pytest, measured 2026-10-03 for task 5328 on the dark-factory host): an AUTOUSE fixture that requests `tmp_path` is expensive at suite scale. Over 4000 trivial tests it took 4.5s to 37.0s, because each tmp_path creation rescans basetemp for numbered dirs (O(n^2)). A session-scoped `tmp_path_factory.mktemp(...)` parent plus a per-test `tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=parent)` cost 4.5s to 7.4s. Use the latter when an autouse fixture needs a private per-test dir.
target_text:
GOTCHA (fused-memory tests, measured task 4310): a shared pytest fixture that creates a scratch DIRECTORY must not create it under the test's own `tmp_path` — use `tmp_path_factory.mktemp(...)` instead.

MEASURED. Task 4310 added a conftest factory fixture `neutralise_store_mutation_preflight` that redirects `store_mutation_preflight.resolve_history_dir` to a scratch dir so a guarded script's REAL fail-closed capability probe passes hermetically. First implementation did `scratch = tmp_path / 'mem0-history-scratch'; scratch.mkdir()`. That turned THREE unrelated tests in tests/test_audit_duplicate_memories.py red — `TestRunWiring::test_no_metrics_writes_nothing`, `TestRunLivenessRecurrenceWiring::test_no_metrics_still_writes_no_artifact`, `TestEmitMetricsArtifact::test_malformed_metric_leaves_no_directory_and_no_partial_artifact` — all of which assert `list(tmp_path.iterdir()) == []`. Failure text: `assert [PosixPath('.../test_no_metrics_writes_nothing0/mem0-history-scratch')] == []`.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS. The broken tests have NOTHING to do with the fixture's subject matter, so the failure reads as an unrelated regression from whatever else the commit touched. This class of "writes nothing / leaves no directory / no partial artifact" assertion is common in this repo's script suites, so a `tmp_path`-creating autouse-adjacent fixture is disproportionately likely to collide with one.

FIX. Request `tmp_path_factory` (session-scoped, so a function-scoped fixture may depend on it) and call `tmp_path_factory.mktemp('name')`. That yields a unique directory under the session base directory, a SIBLING of the test's `tmp_path` rather than a child, so the redirect is invisible to any assertion about `tmp_path` contents.

GENERAL RULE: a fixture that needs scratch filesystem space and is consumed by suites it does not own should allocate OUTSIDE `tmp_path`. `tmp_path` belongs to the test, and the test may be asserting on its exact contents.

HOW TO ROOT-CAUSE a fused-memory "Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?" AFTER THE FACT — measured 2026-09-19 (task 5688, legibility census 2026-09-20 §1.3, which had listed this cause as unverified).

REFINES two existing entries (2a20cfb9 and d32c6d7d, both 2026-06-16) rather than restating them: they establish the symptom string, that the drop is per-server (:8102 keeps working), and that HTTP re-connects on the next call. What follows is the diagnostic they lack, plus the shape of the hole.

THE MECHANISM. `scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py::fused_memory_liveness_pass` is a Type=oneshot unit on a 60s timer. Three consecutive non-healthy `_fused_memory_liveness_verdict()` readings and it calls `restart_unit("fused-memory.service")`. The restart is AUTOMATIC — no operator is involved, so there is no sign-off to withhold and no human to go looking for. On 2026-09-19 the journal reads: 19:26:54 BST `liveness verdict 'wedged' (streak 3/3); restarting`; 19:26:54 `Stopping`; 19:27:41 SIGTERM serviced; 19:27:56 `Consumed ...` then immediately `Starting`; 19:28:36 `Started`. Port 8002 was therefore UNBOUND for 40 seconds, 19:27:56 → 19:28:36, and the two failing add_memory calls (19:28:07, 19:28:17) sit inside it, with a SUCCESSFUL write at 19:27:50 before and successful escalation calls at 19:28:47/53 after.

TWO HALVES, OPPOSITE SYMPTOMS — this is the part that misleads. While the loop is wedged the process is up and the socket stays BOUND, so a client HANGS until its own timeout. Once the unit has deactivated the socket is GONE, so the connect is REFUSED in milliseconds (the failing calls returned in 0.3s and 0.7s). A sub-second "Unable to connect" is the second half. It is NOT a backing-store timeout — the request never reached the server process, so FalkorDB/Qdrant are the wrong place to look — and the error string is emitted by the harness's own MCP HTTP client, so nothing in this repo can retry or annotate it. Nor is it worktree-specific: port 8002 is host-global and .mcp.json points every client at the same URL.

THE PROCEDURE.
1. `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service --since "<T-5min>" --until "<T+5min>" -o short-iso --no-pager` — `--user` is MANDATORY; system scope prints "-- No entries --" and looks exactly like an absence of evidence.
2. Pipe it to `scripts/fm_wedge_forensics.py` (stdlib-only, safe to run while fm is down) and read the reported intervals; task 5688 adds a `port down` interval specifically so a failed call's timestamp can be tested for containment in one command.
3. `journalctl --user -u orchestrator-watchdog.service` over the same window gives the restart DECISION (the verdict and streak), which the fused-memory journal by construction does not carry.

THE CLOCK-FILE TRAP. `data/fused-memory/last_liveness_restart_fused_memory.json` (liveness tier) and `last_redeploy_fused_memory.json` (staleness tier) each hold only the MOST RECENT restart. They answer "was it restarted just now?" and cannot answer "was it down at time T" — a later restart silently overwrites the one you are investigating. The 2026-09-20 census read exactly this file and concluded the nearest restart was 30 minutes away; the journal shows one 90 seconds away. Use the journal for any question about a past instant.

entry_text: The merge-lane ratchet (orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json) measures two populations differently. CLUSTER paths (listed under 'files', e.g. orchestrator/tests/conftest.py, merge_queue.py) are ratcheted on cognitive, lines, prose_lines, function_local_imports and reexport_names, so any added line needs --authorize-raise. Every other .py under orchestrator/tests is ratcheted only on private_reads and patch_targets (the 'tests' section). Adding a test or a comment to a non-cluster test file therefore needs no authorization, as long as it reads no private names and adds no patch targets. Measured 2026-09-29.
target_text: Merge-lane ratchet, measured by scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py: ANY file under orchestrator/tests that imports a cluster module (git_ops, merge_queue, …) is swept for private_reads. A NEW such test file contributes to the summed total:private_reads, so it must keep `obj._attr` attribute accesses at 0 or the ratchet reddens. A name import like `from orchestrator.git_ops import _run` is NOT counted, because only ast.Attribute nodes are, and self/cls receivers are exempt. The regenerated baseline also gains one tests-map entry per new lane-importing test file, so a later `--write-baseline` adds those entries.

entry_text: Gotcha (reify-compiler, since task 7838): the value-cell Applied-type walk (entities_phase.rs → check_applied_type_arg_bounds) covers every value cell, not only annotated ones. An un-annotated `let` gets an inferred cell_type, and its Applied type args are bound-checked as Written, so builtin args are rejected against trait bounds. Example: `let c = couple(a, 2.0)` with `a : Axis` types to `Coupling<Axis>`, which fails `P: DrivingJoint + HasMotion`. Tests that need a Coupling must build a real driving joint, e.g. `let j = prismatic(vec3(1,0,0), 0mm .. 10mm)`. Axis stand-ins no longer work. This is intended (esc-7838-3, option A).

Compound-scheme finding (Jev trial 2026-09-29, exploratory, no new API calls): combining the gpt-4o-mini judge (G) and Jev (J).

- For contradiction labelling, no compound beats Jev alone. G almost never catches a contradiction J misses, so requiring G's agreement only loses catches, and accepting either one only adds false alarms.
- For file-or-store, "store only if BOTH G and J say no match; J sets the label" loses the fewest true links:
  - round 3: 16/211 vs J 20 and G 50; 11/211 with G at 4,000 chars;
  - round 2: 5/132 vs 10 and 27.
  - It may let more misfiles through (3–5 of 8 RELATED pairs vs 1–4). That is unmeasurable at n=8 per population, and Leo ruled misfiles the worse error.
- Lowest-risk architecture: G keeps placement and file-or-store; J only sets the label (restated/amended/contested). It runs concurrently at ~USD 0.0002/write and keeps 37 of J's 41 catches.
- Details: data/write-triage-jev-trial-2026-09-29/results/compound.md.

entry_text: OCCT 7.8 STEPCAFControl_Writer writes DIRECTION components at 12 significant digits (e.g. 0.866025403784), so a non-axis-aligned occurrence rotation round-trips with ~2e-13 error (measured Rx(30deg): 1.9e-13); axis-aligned rotations and mm->m translations round-trip to ~1e-17. Use >=1e-9 tolerance for STEP placement round-trip assertions. Also: libgmsh from /opt/reify-deps loads libTKXCAF/TKLCAF.so.7.9 beside system OCCT 7.8 in every reify-kernel-occt harness test binary (harness_occt, harness_step_export both NEED libgmsh.so.4.15).
target_text: OCCT runtime linkage in reify (measured 2026-09-11 with LD_DEBUG=bindings,libs on the release `reify check examples/perforated_plate.ri`): the reify binary directly NEEDs libgmsh.so.4.15 plus 16 libTK*.so.7.8 from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; libgmsh (RPATH $ORIGIN/.:$ORIGIN/../lib) pulls 19 libTK*.so.7.9 from /opt/reify-deps/lib, and a third wave loads 10 more 7.8 libs — essentially the whole OCCT module graph is loaded twice. crates/reify-build-utils never lists /opt/reify-deps for OCCT, so reify's own wrapper can only compile against system 7.8. No copy uses symbol versioning, DT_SYMBOLIC or hidden visibility, and DT_FLAGS_1=NOW resolves everything eagerly: of bindings from 7.9 callers, 47,101 resolve into 7.8 and 15,137 into 7.9 (the latter only where 7.8 has no rival symbol), because 7.8 is loaded first. Reify never runs booleans through gmsh — gmsh only receives plain mesh data via its C API — so a Message_ProgressIndicator subclass compiled against 7.8 headers is safe. The 7.8/7.9 progress and BOP headers differ only by a clang-format reflow. Guard task: 7440.
