Completed: Post-ZOT duplicate sweep: after a curator zero-output hang degrades dedupe to create, diff the tasks created in that window against the corpus and flag near-duplicates — the class has no live owner
Description: RULING (Leo, 2026-09-14, decision docket D5 option A; from reify esc-7459-1). Give the curator-ZOT duplicate class a live owner and a structural safeguard.

THE MECHANISM. When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout (subtype=error_empty_output, turns=0, sonnet + json-schema call shape), dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE: the caller sees a normal {status:"created"} with no signal that the dedupe check never ran. dark_factory 1743 (done, merged f8a612d8) shipped the defensive patch that stops one hung call wedging subsequent calls, and its predecessor 1550 is cancelled — so the class currently has NO live owner, and duplicates keep landing. NOTE: an earlier reify record claimed "task 1743 is unrelated GUI work"; that was a project-attribution error (reify 1743 is GUI; dark_factory 1743 is this) — cite "dark_factory 1743".

BASE RATE, five confirmed degrade windows: 2026-08-25 DUPLICATE (reify 6583 filed as a strict subset of pending 5436); 2026-09-11 DUPLICATE (reify 7416 vs 7383 at cosine 0.68, retitled SUPERSEDED and cancelled); 2026-09-12 21:07 clean (candidate resolved to exactly one task, 7480); 2026-09-13 00:56 clean (7490); 2026-09-14 01:42 clean (7517). Two of five produce duplicates; the three clean windows were each verified by search_tasks during the reify L2 watch, not assumed. Manual discipline ("search_tasks before AND after filing", procedural memory 377a4ad6) has already failed twice.

WORK. On each curator ZOT event (the circuit-breaker/escalator already files a curator_zero_output_hang escalation with the candidate title and timestamp), run a sweep: for every task created in the project within +/- N minutes of the hang, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the task itself, and if a near-duplicate scores above the curator's combine threshold, either (a) auto-file a curator ticket proposing the combine, or (b) at minimum stamp the escalation and the new task's metadata with the candidate duplicate id and score so a human sees it in the L2 record rather than discovering it later. Prefer (a) if the combine path is already idempotent. Do not delete or cancel automatically.

VERIFY. A test that simulates a ZOT (mock the LLM call to return empty output), files a candidate whose near-duplicate exists, and asserts the sweep flags the pair. Plus a control where no near-duplicate exists and nothing is flagged.
Analysis: GOAL (Leo ruling, docket D5 option A). When the task-curator's LLM call hangs with zero output until the 180s timeout, dedupe silently DEGRADES TO CREATE and the caller sees a normal {status:"created"}. Two of five confirmed degrade windows produced a real duplicate. Give the class a live owner: on each ZOT degrade, run the curator's own dedupe query against the corpus EXCLUDING the new task, and if a near-duplicate scores above a flagging threshold, stamp the new task's metadata AND file an operator-visible escalation. Never delete, cancel, or auto-combine.

target_text: GOTCHA — graphiti's TokenUsageTracker is a single CUMULATIVE instance shared across the whole GraphitiBackend: `_llm_client` (one OpenAIClient) is handed to `self.client` AND to every per-group Graphiti clone in `_client_for()` (graphiti_client.py:422-428, :592-598), and `Graphiti.token_tracker` just forwards to `llm_client.token_tracker`. Completed: Poll only the ACTIVE tab's endpoints, using the TAB_ENDPOINTS map that already exists
Description: data.js fetches all 14 dashboard endpoints every 3000ms regardless of which tab is open, but only ONE tab is ever mounted: app.jsx's renderTab() is a switch returning a single component, and the body wrapper carries key={tab} so a tab change tears the old subtree down entirely. So the dashboard continuously fetches and parses data for twelve tabs nobody is looking at.

The mapping needed to fix this ALREADY EXISTS and is already maintained. endpoint_staleness.js::TAB_ENDPOINTS maps every tab id to the endpoints that tab actually consumes, and endpoint_staleness.test.mjs machine-checks BOTH directions - every path is a real endpointsFor() key, and every app.jsx tab id has an entry - precisely so it cannot silently drift. It says, for example, scheduler maps to a single endpoint.

Concrete saving, from live measurement 2026-09-23: sitting on the Scheduler tab currently costs about 22 MB per poll cycle across 14 endpoints; that tab needs /api/v2/dashboard/scheduler alone, 3.1 MB. The server-side cost is the real prize - 99.4% of each endpoint's wall clock is the server building the payload via MCP fan-out across 9 project roots (tasks: ttfb 3.886s of 3.910s total), on the same host as the orchestrator fleet.

THE BLOCKER, and why this is not a five-line change: app.jsx::App computes railCounts for the left-hand rail badges on EVERY tab, and it reads ACTIVE_TASKS, ORCHESTRATORS, RECON_STATE.runs, MERGE_QUEUE and ESCALATIONS to do it. So today /api/v2/dashboard/tasks - the single most expensive endpoint - is required on every tab just to render one number in a badge. Scoping the poll set without first giving the rail a cheap counts source would either blank the badges or keep the expensive endpoint polling everywhere, which forfeits most of the win.

That is what the dependency on task 5587 is for: its task snapshot unit is the natural cheap source. get_statuses (a compact id-to-status map, roughly 95% smaller than get_tasks) is the other candidate.

entry_text: DESIGN GOTCHA (task 5232, measured 2026-10-02 at HEAD 13a9caaca2): never write a checked-in-corpus sweep in shared/tests asserting that every kind='path' delivered_check's paths EXIST on main. It contradicts the task-3500 authoring lint. shared/src/shared/delivered_check_polarity.py::_lint_path_check rejects an expect='present' path check as 'vacuous_present' when its paths already exist, so every correctly-authored adopter names a missing path at the moment its sidecar is committed. At HEAD, 6 of the 7 tracked kind='path' checks (owners 4681, 6181, 6184, 6185, 6188, 6190, all pending) named missing paths. The analogy to TestCheckedInScriptCheckTargets fails: a script target is the CHECKER, and a missing one is a silent ERRORED hold, while path entries are the SUBJECT. A missing path is the normal pre-delivery state and evaluates FAIL, which feeds the visible delivered_fail streak. Telling "permanently red" apart from "not yet delivered" needs owning-task status, so it belongs in a tasks.db-aware scripts/ audit, not the shared suite.
target_text:
RATIONALE RECORD for task 3500's central design call (landed 2026-08-29), written to a Mem0-backed category on purpose: the conclusion alone is useless without it, and decisions_and_rationale distils reasoning away.

THE CALL: evaluating a delivered_check against a tree yields a BIT, not a VERDICT — so the same rule cannot be both an authoring gate and a corpus sweep. 3500 split them.

WHY. "expect: present and it matches" is simultaneously (a) the SUCCESS state of a landed producer and (b) a never-fires vacuous gate on a live one. Nothing in the descriptor distinguishes them. MEASURED: applying the authoring-time 2x2 to the checked-in corpus with the reference tree set to main-today flags 313/548 descriptors (57%) — 287 present/match, 203 present/nomatch, 32 absent/match, 26 absent/nomatch. The overwhelming majority of those 313 are correctly delivered work. The fold-in (esc-4545-2) had reported 104/538 (19%) and framed the 2x2 as "checkable with nothing but the manifest and git — no commit-ordering premise"; re-running it showed the reference tree is load-bearing, and that discrepancy is methodological, not corpus growth (52 vs 50 manifest files). Filed as esc-3500-1.

THE RESOLUTION THAT MADE IT TRACTABLE: at AUTHORING time the reference tree is free. commit_planning runs BEFORE the task is implemented, so HEAD at that moment IS the pre-task tree and "already green" is decisive with no history and no status. Only the RETROACTIVE sweep cannot recover it — and there the missing input is the producer's STATUS, which turns the bit into a disposition (present+nomatch is a defect on a done task, the normal forward-looking majority on a pending one). Status lives in .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, which is why the sweep is scripts/audit_delivered_checks.py and not a pytest gate.

THE THIRD PLACE THE SAME QUESTION LANDS, and why it got a THIRD answer: shared/tests/test_capability_manifest.py must run in any checkout, so it can read neither tasks.db nor a status. It therefore sweeps ONLY the STRUCTURAL codes (self_referential, comment_only, filename_shaped) — statements about a descriptor's SHAPE, which stay true whatever tree they are measured against — and deliberately leaves the vacuity direction alone. It is a frozen-allowlist RATCHET, not a gate, because the measured live structural debt (5 self-reference, 5 comment-only, 1 filename-only) sits in plans/ and docs/prds/ manifests outside that task's lock scope; a hard gate there would have been permanently-red and therefore ignored.

OPTIONS REJECTED, with reasons: (1) one status-blind rule everywhere — rejected on the 57% false-positive rate above; (2) the prior plan's {pre-state, still, unchanged, old, legacy, before} NAME-TOKEN vocabulary — strictly dominated and deleted entirely, because it guessed author intent from English and needed hand-tuned exclusions (installed/stillness/threshold/preflight-state-machine) to avoid false rejects on a hard-blocking gate, whereas the non-vacuity rule MEASURES the repo and subsumes the same cases; (3) adding kind='path' for MODE 3 — deferred purely on blast radius (closed Literals plus every mechanical-kind tuple in the fleet), not merit, and filed as a follow-up.

CAVEAT DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED: the corpus ratchet's allowlist is pre-existing debt the task could not repair in-scope, and the audit sweep's exit code deliberately ignores `superseded`, `inert` and `unevaluable` rows. Both are choices to keep a detector green enough to be read, not claims that those rows are fine.

App.tsx's effect calls mechanismStore.refresh(), whose produce() does a wholesale `s.descriptors = newDescriptors`, and MechanismPanel's <For> keys rows by object identity, so value-identical descriptors still remount every JointRow (confirmed in jsdom: same element false, isConnected false). target_text: Reify GUI gotcha: assigning a freshly fetched array into a Solid store wholesale (e.g. `s.descriptors = fetched` inside produce) gives <For> new object references on every refresh, so it remounts every row and detaches any <input> the user is holding mid-gesture. Write fetched lists with `setState('list', reconcile(fetched, { key: '<id field>' }))`. Nested objects without that key are matched by position and keep their DOM identity. mechanismStore.refresh was fixed this way in task 7680 and is pinned by MechanismPanel.test.tsx (l).

  1. orchestrator/tests/conftest.py:998 — TaskSteward, inside the canonical `make_steward` fixture-factory.

Site 3 is a THIRD steward-construction idiom that the 3461 -> 3514 -> 3551 consolidation lineage never examined. It was added by task 2488 roughly four weeks before 3647 (see commits 285fab9499, 65b0d61d3e), i.e. AFTER task 3514 folded the last two factories onto `make_steward`, so it postdates every consolidation pass and no prior task's reviewer suggestion mentions it.

WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY FOLD TODAY. `_build_steward_for_triage(config: OrchestratorConfig, worktree: Path, *, task_id='42')` takes a REAL `OrchestratorConfig` (supplied by that module's `config` fixture) and pre-initializes a real on-disk meta-root via `_artifacts_for(worktree).init(...)` so `_pre_triage_suggestions`'s "meta-root missing" diagnostic branch never fires. `make_steward` builds `MagicMock(spec_set=pydantic_spec(OrchestratorConfig))` and exposes no `config=` passthrough, so folding requires new factory surface.

Description: PRD: docs/prds/v0_6/solution-set-completeness.md §3.1. Ship the solution-set completeness axis as an ADDITIVE sibling carrier in reify-ir, alongside (not inside) the landed F-result types.

WHY. SolveResult::Solved.unique is a bool, and a bool cannot distinguish five genuinely different states: proved exactly one, proved two, found one and proved nothing, found two, proved none exist. Every solver-honesty defect in this area is that type error surfacing somewhere.

DELIVER.
1. enum Completeness = Exhaustive | Partial{reason: PartialReason} | Refuted{narrowing: ConstraintNodeId}.
2. enum PartialReason = BoxBudgetExhausted | DimensionAboveEnvelope{dims} | DomainUnbounded{param} | NotIntervalRepresentable{constraint} | InnerSolveUnproven | ProbeOnly | NotAttempted.
3. SolutionSet{solutions, completeness}; an additive `completeness` field on RankedSolveResult::Ranked.
4. The C1 derived-`unique` helper: unique == (completeness == Exhaustive && solutions.len() == 1). No producer may write `unique` from any other reasoning.
5. A default `Partial{NotAttempted}` lift so every existing producer keeps behaving exactly as today until it opts in.

INVARIANTS (PRD §3.2): C1 unique is derived never asserted; C2 ProvenOptimal requires Exhaustive; C3 Refuted is a proof while Partial-with-empty-set is not, and the two must never render alike; C4 a Partial verdict may never report how many solutions exist.

ADDITIVE-ONLY IS FORCED, NOT PREFERRED. F-result invariant I1 freezes SolveResult and ConstraintSolver::solve(). The production matches in engine_eval.rs / engine_edit.rs / concurrent.rs destructure `Solved { values, unique }` WITHOUT `..`, so adding a field to Solved would not compile. A sibling carrier is the only back-compatible shape.

SolveAllResult{solutions, complete} in reify-constraints/src/cpsat.rs (landed by PRD 2 β #5468) already states the doctrine correctly in its own doc: an empty set with complete:true is a PROOF of unsatisfiability, an empty set with complete:false proves nothing, and every honesty claim is conjoined with the flag rather than asserted. This task promotes that discipline out of cpsat.rs and makes it the law for every driver.

SIGNAL (intermediate): unlocks β, γ and ι. Back-compat is the checkable property — BT13: SolveResult and ConstraintSolver::solve() byte-identical, and every producer that does not opt in reports Partial{NotAttempted} and behaves exactly as today.

entry_text: Counting pytest-xdist workers of a scoped run (measured 2026-10-05, task 5469; peer of 64c791bb under topic verify-resource-measurement). Under `-q` with non-tty output xdist never prints `created: N/M workers` — TerminalDistReporter.getstatus returns only "bringing up nodes..." at verbose < 0 — so a verify-shaped `-q` log cannot prove the worker count. Reading PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER from /proc/<pid>/environ UNDER-counts (read 5 of 16): that file is the process's initial environment and xdist sets the variable after the worker starts. What worked: run the command in a named scope (`systemd-run --user --scope --unit=<u>`), and from OUTSIDE the scope (so the sampler's CPU stays out of the scope's cpu.stat) poll `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/<u>.scope/cgroup.procs` every 2 s, counting processes whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains execnet's bootstrap `exec(eval(sys.stdin.readline()))` (grep -zlsF). It read exactly 16 at PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS=16, but it is an upper bound: suites that spawn their own xdist subprocesses (scripts read 2 even when run serially with -p no:xdist). pids.peak counts threads, so it is not a worker count. Scripts: plans/verify-parallelism-trial-e1-report.md §4.

STAMPED PEER under topic `orchestrator-xdist-worker-crash-under-load` — the bailout literal that the canonical entry and peer 59d60997 both quote is ABSENT from dark-factory's own verify logs. Measured 2026-09-08 on task 5082, HEAD 9de4890ba9.

THE TRAP. Canonical 40d1b472 and peer 59d60997 both cite `xdist: worker gwN crashed and worker restarting disabled` as a signature you can read out of a verify log. You cannot — not from a module-scoped verify log. All SEVEN module-scoped configs (shared/, escalation/, orchestrator/, fused-memory/, dashboard/, sampler/, cockpit/ `orchestrator.yaml`) run `pytest tests/ --tb=short -q --timeout=300`, and BOTH of xdist's emission paths for that message are gated on `config.option.verbose >= 0` (`dsession.py::report_line` and `dsession.py::pytest_terminal_summary`). Under `-q` the line is emitted nowhere. Checking `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` addopts is what makes this easy to get wrong: addopts carry `-n auto --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0` and no `-q`, so the effective verbosity is set by the module config's test_command, not by the file people look at.

TWO TELLS THAT YOU ARE READING `-q` OUTPUT, both visible with no extra tooling: xdist's `getstatus()` (dsession.py:504) falls back to the literal `bringing up nodes...` (it appears TWICE at the top of the log, in place of pytest's session header and `created: N/N workers`), and pytest drops the `===` bars from the final tally, so it reads `1 failed, 6676 passed, 8 warnings in 1592.00s` rather than `==== 1 failed ... ====`. Reproduced byte-for-byte in a throwaway 6-test project on pytest 9.0.3 / xdist 3.8.0.

WHAT SURVIVES `-q`, AND IS THE DISCRIMINATOR TO USE. The crash attribution itself does: `[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated`, the FAILURES-section body `worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'`, and the fabricated `FAILED <nodeid>` summary line. So the canonical's bystander triage still works. What you lose is the ability to tell a TRUNCATED session from a COMPLETE one via the bailout literal — and `replacing crashed worker gwN` (the recovering-path line) is suppressed by the same gate, so its absence proves nothing either. Use the FINAL PROGRESS PERCENTAGE instead: reproduced both ways under `-q`, a `--max-worker-restart=0` bailout run's last progress line stays below `[100%]` (observed `[ 83%]`) while a `--max-worker-restart=1` recovering run still reaches `[100%]`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR verify.py AS SHIPPED BY TASK 5082. `_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash` works on real `-q` output (verified True on the specimen, so facet 1's routing to the bounded infra retry is live). `_is_worker_death_truncated_session` keys on the bailout literal and therefore returns False on every module-scoped verify log — facet 2 and its four consumers (cause-hint rung 0, the test-leg note, aggregation carry-through, the report caveat) are INERT on this project today. Fail-safe, but silent. Filed as esc-5082-5 (design_concern); the detection signal was left unchanged rather than widened by a debug pass.

SPECIMEN, useful as a fixture: `.worktrees/5082/.task/verify/attempt-2.orchestrator.test.log` — gw7 died, the log ends at `[ 32%]` reporting `1 failed, 6676 passed` where the suite collects 20717 (`--collect-only`), i.e. ~14040 tests never ran, and the named victim passes in isolation (1 passed in 19.23s). This is the same understated-damage shape peer 59d60997 measured at 1%; the count check it recommends (compare reported items against the suite's real size) remains the reliable manual test and does not depend on verbosity.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06 on task 4176): TWO facts about pytest-timeout under xdist that existing memory does NOT cover. The known part — thread method os._exit()s the worker, shows as 'node down' — is already recorded; these two are the parts that mislead a debugger.

1. A @pytest.mark.timeout(N) MARKER CLAMPS DOWN a LARGER --timeout on the command line. pytest_timeout.py:388-410 `_get_item_settings` resolves the marker FIRST and falls back to `item.config._env_timeout` (the --timeout value) only when the marker is None. Precedence is marker-wins, NOT max-wins. Orchestrator verify runs `uv run --directory orchestrator pytest tests/ --tb=short -q --timeout=300`, so every test gets 300s EXCEPT any carrying a marker below that. Measured case: test_aiosqlite_leak_isolation.py::test_a_thread_exception_actually_fails_a_test_under_this_projects_inifile carries @pytest.mark.timeout(120) and therefore ran with a budget 2.5x TIGHTER than the rest of the same run — while being one of the suite's most load-sensitive tests (it spawns two full pytest subprocesses; measured 15.42s/30.74s/31.46s across three isolated runs, a 2x spread from ambient load alone). Every such marker was authored as an UPWARD opt-out from the ini's `timeout = 60`; that intent silently inverts under a harness that raises the run-level budget. When auditing timeouts, compare each marker against the HARNESS --timeout, not just against the ini default.

2. A worker death TRUNCATES the run, so the pass count in a red verify log is NOT the suite. orchestrator/pyproject.toml pairs `timeout_method = "thread"` with `--max-worker-restart=0` (the latter deliberately, to avoid a restart/re-collect/re-die hang — see its comment). Consequence: os._exit() of one worker ENDS the session. Measured on the same run: the red log read "1 failed, 728 passed, 1 skipped in 209.67s" while a clean re-run of the identical command read "19622 passed, 17 skipped in 953.70s". The red run recorded 3.7% of the suite. "728 passed / 209.67s" reads like a completed fast suite and is neither — do not conclude from a red verify log that the other tests passed, and do not use its duration as a suite baseline.

Corollary for diagnosis: pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" stack dump is written to `item.config.get_terminal_writer()` INSIDE the xdist worker, which is not forwarded to the controller. So the one artifact naming the cause is absent from the controller log BY CONSTRUCTION; its absence is not evidence against a timeout reading.

REMEDY CONSTRAINT: do not answer any of this by raising the number. plans/flake-ledger-prd.md:221 — "do not widen a timeout as a fix for anything" — with the task-1836 precedent where a 10s->30s widening masked a real SIGHUP bug for a day. The sanctioned verdict vocabulary is `passes_in_isolation`; record the evidence and leave the diagnosis to a de-flake task.

Which fused-memory writers can hit a memory_metadata.enforce rejection, and what happens to it (traced 2026-10-02):
- Deterministic code writers set only constant keys, so they cannot produce a fatal violation. This covers the recon harness markers, scope-freshness snapshots, stall and flag markers, the cycle-summary mirror, the standing-decision and flag-suppression Mem0 mirrors (which swallow failures at DEBUG), the override audit write and the orchestrator workflow memory writes.
- add_episode extraction bypasses the vocabulary seam completely. _execute_mem0_classify_and_add calls mem0.add directly.
- Every replay path also bypasses the seam: replay_dead_letters → _execute_mem0_write, recover_mem0_intents, replay_to_graphiti. So a fatal-invalid row that was already queued would land unvalidated on replay.
- The real exposure is LLM-authored metadata: recon stages, which run as claude CLI subprocesses over MCP, plus task roles, stewards, curator sittings and interactive sessions. Each sees the rejection as a tool result on the same call. Nothing makes it retry, and if it doesn't, the memory is gone with no durable record.
- consolidate_memories already hard-rejects a malformed topic slug whatever enforce says (server/consolidation.py::validate_consolidate_args).
- Latent silent-loss path: shared/mcp_post.py::check_mcp_post_response, the orchestrator's raw MCP POST checker, inspects only the HTTP status and the JSON-RPC error member. A tool-level {'error','error_type'} dict inside a successful JSON-RPC result reads as success. Today's orchestrator payloads cannot trip enforce, but any future fatal key would be lost without an orchestrator-side log.
- sweep_toolcall_xml_leak deletes a record before re-adding it, so under enforce a rejected re-add loses the original (the script reports it as content-lost).

- orchestrator/tests/test_session_hooks.py:23 — `import pytest  # pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]`

So the interpreter/venv situation there is demonstrably not identical to tests/scripts/, and the verdict must be re-measured rather than carried over.

THE ARGUMENT THAT MOTIVATED 4516, for whoever picks this up: pytest is a declared dev dependency of every module that runs these suites and resolves from the .venv that the pyright venvPath/venv keys pin — never from extraPaths. If it fails to resolve, the ENVIRONMENT is broken (typically an un-synced worktree, where pyright prints `venv .venv subdirectory not found in venv path` and silently falls back to an ambient interpreter, making every other diagnostic in that run a measurement of the wrong interpreter). A reportMissingImports suppression on that line converts a real env fault into silence. The remedy for an unresolved pytest is `uv sync --all-packages`, never a pragma.

HOW TO MEASURE IT HONESTLY (this is the part task 4516 found easy to get wrong): run the orchestrator module's OWN declared type_check_command from the repo root, in a worktree that has been cold-synced, with the ambient venv suppressed — `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV PATH="/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:$HOME/.local/bin" uv sync --all-packages` first, then the declared command. An agent Bash session otherwise inherits VIRTUAL_ENV from the MAIN checkout, which is precisely the confound these class-(b) pragmas are about, so a measurement taken under it proves nothing. Strip the two pragmas, re-run, and compare error counts. If the count is unchanged, they are vestigial and should be deleted; if it rises, they are load-bearing and should stay.

ALSO WORTH RE-MEASURING IN THE SAME PASS (observed by the same grep, verdict likewise NOT measured): pyright-form pragmas on non-pytest imports at shared/tests/test_task_statuses.py:147,158,167; fused-memory/tests/test_cgl_eta_finalize_gate.py:49; dashboard/tests/test_costs_data.py:1565. IF ANY TURN OUT VESTIGIAL, the durable fix is the guard shape task 4516 shipped at tests/scripts/test_no_vestigial_import_pragmas.py — it derives its search roots from the pyright config at test time rather than hardcoding a file list, so it cannot go stale the way the prose 4516 had to rewrite did. STAMPED PEER under topic `guard-tests-grep-code-not-prose` (canonical 091af6df). That canonical answers "what may my guard grep" (code structure, never prose). This peer answers the adjacent question task 4516 ran into: HOW DO I KEEP THE GUARD ITSELF FROM BECOMING THE STALE THING IT POLICES — plus one concrete self-reference hazard.

CONTEXT. Task 3456 added `scripts` to the root `[tool.pyright] extraPaths`, which made tests/scripts/'s flat scripts/ imports resolve statically. Every `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` on those imports became vestigial at that moment. TWELVE survived four months; task 4793 then added THIRTEEN MORE of the identical class a week after 4516 was filed to delete them. Nothing detects this: pyright's `reportUnnecessaryTypeIgnoreComment` is set nowhere in the repo (grepped: zero hits) and is off under `typeCheckingMode = "basic"`.

(1) DERIVE THE GUARD'S ROOTS FROM CONFIG AT TEST TIME, NEVER HARDCODE THE FILE LIST. A guard spelled "these 8 files must not contain this string" reproduces the very failure it polices one level up: it freezes one day's measurement as permanent truth, goes stale silently the moment the config changes, and needs hand-editing for every new test file. Reading `[tool.pyright] extraPaths` with `tomllib` and asserting "no pragma-carrying import RESOLVES on these roots" tracks the MECHANISM instead of a snapshot of its consequences — a future extraPaths entry that makes some pragma vestigial turns the guard red automatically and names the pragma to delete, while a genuinely unresolvable import keeps it green and its suppression allowed. It also self-corrected a misclassification in the task text: `setup_host_parsing.py` was filed as a flat scripts/ import but lives in tests/scripts/, and a resolvability check against real roots reaches the right verdict without depending on the classification being right.

(2) A GUARD THAT FORBIDS A TOKEN MUST NOT ITSELF CONTAIN THAT TOKEN. Build it from parts — `_RULE = 'reportMissingImports'; _PRAGMA = f'pyright: ignore[{_RULE}]'`. The operator-facing way to audit this class of invariant by hand is a repo-wide grep for the literal, and a literal in the guard plants a permanent false positive in every such audit, including the one used to verify the guard's own cleanup. Cheap, and it removes a real recurring confusion.

(3) GATE ON "PARSES AS AN IMPORT", NOT ON A BACKTICK/QUOTING HEURISTIC — this is the canonical's code-not-prose rule applied to a case where the two are interleaved in the same directory. Split the line on the first `#`, `ast.parse` the code part, keep it only if it yields a single `ast.Import`/`ast.ImportFrom`. That makes the three backtick-quoted PROSE mentions of the pragma in the same directory correctly invisible, as a property of what the line IS. A backtick heuristic is incidental to how those three happen to be written today and stops working the moment one is reworded. Two parsing details that matter: dedent before parsing (pragma sites include function-body imports), and close a parenthesised `from X import (` opening line with a placeholder name — it is a real import statement that does not parse standalone.

(4) SPLIT BY REASON, NOT BY SYNTAX. 4516's pragmas were vestigial for two DIFFERENT reasons with two DIFFERENT remedies: class (a) static resolution via extraPaths (remedy: restore the extraPaths entries, never re-add a pragma) and class (b) `import pytest`, which is about INTERPRETER/venv selection and never touches extraPaths at all (remedy: `uv sync --all-packages`, because an unresolved pytest means a broken environment the gate must report LOUDLY). One blanket "no pragma anywhere" assertion would collapse that, hand readers the wrong remedy, and forbid legitimate future suppressions. Two guards also make the TDD measurement verifiable per class — red on exactly 5 and exactly 20 — so a miscount is caught before any deletion.

(5) DELETING THE PRAGMA IS THE SMALLER HALF; THE STALE PROSE THAT JUSTIFIED IT I…[truncated, 4679 chars total]

Completed: State in confusion-reduction PRD §7.1 whether a codebook sighting `note` is human-provenance-only or machine-read signal
Description: Documentation-only correction. Records the actual readership of the confusion-codebook sighting `note` field so future legibility tasks stop being justified on a re-derivation path that does not exist.

ORIGIN: info-note esc-4892-3 (filed against task 4892, severity=info, category=risk_identified), confirmed independently by task 4892's steward at branch tip bf67d958da.

THE FALSE BELIEF. Task 4892's own WHY-IT-MATTERS asserted: "the codebook is the corpus the periodic-census verifier, the trickle-coder digest passes and reconciliation match NEW sightings against. A present-tense 'omits --system-prompt-file' entry can lead a future census pass to re-derive an already-fixed defect as live." That mechanism does not exist. The `note` field is write-only with respect to every automated consumer.

RE-MEASURED (steward, independently of the filer, at bf67d958da):
- `note` is WRITTEN by scripts/legibility/codebook.py::_build_sighting (schema-declared at the entry- and candidate-sighting shapes) and REQUESTED from the LLM by scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_prompt.
- scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_codebook_index is the only seam putting codebook content into an LLM prompt. Read in full: it emits `- {id}: {title} — {one-line cause}` per entry and nothing else. Sightings — and therefore notes — are never included; its own docstring says so.
- The census miner reaches the LLM through that same seam (census.py::mine_to_saturation -> coder.code_digests -> build_codebook_index).
- census.py::compute_matrix reads only origin_phase/manifested_phase. census.py::_cluster_description reads only len(sightings). census_trigger.py::codebook_signal reads only sighting `date` and candidate `first_seen`. digest.py never loads the codebook.
- Grep for `note` across scripts/legibility/*.py returns writes, schema declarations, and unrelated prose ("cost note") — no reader.

So a note's only readers are humans and agents skimming the raw YAML, which skills/census/SKILL.md:27 does direct ("Skim docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml for recent sightings/candidates dates").

FIX 1 (load-bearing). In plans/confusion-reduction-prd.md §7.1, state explicitly which of the two the `note` field is:
  (a) human-readable provenance only — the measured status quo, requiring no code change; or
  (b) intended machine-read signal — in which case the wiring does not exist today and the PRD should say that plainly rather than implying it works.
Prefer (a) unless there is a ratified intent to the contrary; option (b) implies follow-on work that should be filed separately, not assumed. Whichever is chosen, the point is that a reader can no longer infer a census feedback loop that isn't wired.

FIX 2 (cheap, same class, discretionary). scripts/legibility/codebook.py:551 carries a comment asserting "every consumer afterwards (the matrix path, build_codebook_index) reads ENTRY sightings." build_codebook_index does NOT read sightings — only id/title/cause, per the measurement above. The comment's CONCLUSION is unaffected and still correct (the sighting belongs on the entry, not the promoted candidate: the matrix path genuinely does read entry sightings, and candidates are absent from build_codebook_index entirely — see census.py:758). Only the parenthetical over-claims. Correct it to name the matrix path alone, or reword to "the consumers that read sightings at all". Do not restructure the surrounding logic — the code is right; one clause of the comment is not.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is itself an instance of the codebook entry `guards-assert-unverified-diagnoses` — a plausible mechanism asserted without verification, then inherited by downstream work. Task 4892 was prioritized partly on it. Leaving the PRD silent lets the same belief regenerate.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-09 planning task 5198): amending a confusion-codebook entry via an appended CORRECTION SIGHTING — the task-4892 precedent — is INVISIBLE to the consumer that re-ingests the entry. Do not assume the note reaches anything.

MECHANISM. scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_codebook_index is the only thing that puts codebook entries in front of the LLM trickle coder. It renders exactly one line per entry, `- {id}: {title} — {cause}`, and its own docstring states that heavy fields including `sightings` "are never included", and that "ALL entries are included, retired ones too" (a census re-observes pre-fix traces, so dropping retired entries would force spurious candidates).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both counter-intuitive:
1. A correction NOTE lives inside a sighting, so the coder never sees it. Task 4892's note-only amendment correctly annotated history for a human reader, but changed nothing about what the coder matches against. Its commit message's reasoning ("adding a merger op for a two-line doc correction would extend the §7.3 contract — disproportionate") was scoped to a case where the stale thing WAS the note.
2. `status: retired` is not rendered either, and retired entries are deliberately kept in the index. So retiring an entry does NOT stop the coder re-matching sessions to it.

Only `title` and `cause` reach the consumer. If the defect is a refuted FRAMING — an entry whose title asserts a cause that was disproved — the note-only path leaves the false assertion rendered every night, and the entry keeps self-ingesting (the census quoting its own error string back to itself as fresh sightings). Withdrawing a refuted framing requires writing `title`/`cause`.

AND THE SOLE WRITER CANNOT DO THAT TODAY. scripts/legibility/codebook.py::apply_coding_record supports exactly two ops, both pure appends: append-a-sighting-on-match and append-a-candidate. No op writes an entry field. The only field-writing transforms are census-owned (scripts/legibility/census.py::promote_candidate / reject_candidate / retire_entry), have no CLI, and are reachable only from a full census run — so they produce no committed record and are not replayable on rebase.

PRACTICE: before planning a codebook amendment, decide first WHICH FIELD carries the defect. Note-only (the 4892 shape) is right for a stale or superseded observation. A refuted title/cause needs a field write, and expressing that through the sole-writer record path means extending apply_coding_record — which is proportionate precisely when the title is what re-ingests.

CORRECTION to canonical PTODO entry 35e0187a (topic ptodo-phantom-tracking-phrases), case (3). That entry warns "A cite you added later goes terminal (done/cancelled) -> it becomes an orphaned High-severity finding." For the phantom-tracking lane on a NON-MARKER prose line that is FALSE, and the fear it creates is the very thing the 2026-08-20 curator correction was trying to remove.

Read from source at crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs (verified 2026-08-27 on task 6810): scan_file computes has_canon = has_canonical_cite(line) per PHYSICAL LINE (~line 897), and arm (6) is "else if phantom_phrase(line) && !has_canon" (~line 993) with NO else branch. So once you add a same-line #NNNN, arm (6) is skipped and NOTHING is pushed, provided no earlier arm matches; for a plain prose comment that is exactly the case, since arm (3) needs the TODO/FIXME/HACK marker regex (find_comment_marker, ptodo.rs:52-59) and arms (4) stub-macro and (5) allow(dead_code) are .rs-ONLY. No LineClass::Cited is emitted, so the cite never reaches the beta liveness lane and can NEVER become orphaned or unknown-id. This agrees with entry 9b3fe0a9 (a bare #NNNN cite in ordinary prose is not a marker and is therefore never scanned) and generalises it to the phantom-tracking arm specifically.

PRACTICAL UPSHOT: citing a real live task on a phantom-phrase prose line is a strictly safe, terminal fix with no orphaning risk to weigh. Case (3) of 35e0187a applies only when the line ALSO carries a real TODO/FIXME/HACK marker, or (.rs only) a stub macro or allow(dead_code) deferral, which routes the cite into the liveness lane. The flip side is that the discharged claim is never re-checked: when the cited task completes, the "tracked separately as #NNNN" sentence silently goes stale. Filed as a low-priority follow-up from task 6810 (escalation id agent-followup-6810, ticket tkt_0RSY04VQQ9JESXRC7ZFKSY628J) to decide whether arm (6) should gain an else pushing LineClass::Cited, or whether PRD section 8.3 should record this as a second deliberate divergence.

PLACEMENT GOTCHA worth keeping: because has_canon is per-line with no above-line lookback for arm (6), a wrapped comment sentence can strand the phrase on a continuation line away from its cite. Task 6810's fixture had "// OWNED BY #6653 (...)" on line 15 and the bare fragment "// tolerance hides is tracked separately." on line 17; the #6653 two lines up did not protect it. Fix by pulling the whole sentence onto ONE line that carries the cite, so a future re-wrap cannot re-open the regression.

entry_text: reify-eval: `Engine::evaluate_let_bindings` (engine_eval.rs) is no longer part of eval()'s initial pass. The initial pass is `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified` → `build_combined_param_let_graph`. evaluate_let_bindings is only called by three RE-eval passes over already-diagnosed templates: after sub-elaboration (when the template has subs), the per-scope solver Solved arm, and the merged-cluster per-member loop. Fix = unified topological eval over params∪lets dispatched by kind. target_text:
Completed: Close the jq-vs-Rust ISO-8601 divergence in reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq (numeric TZ offset / no-TZ forms yield a quiet done_at=null)
Description: Filed from task 7236 (review point 2, reviewer_comprehensive robustness) as OUT-OF-SCOPE follow-up work. Task 7236's frozen plan design-decision #4 deliberately PINNED this divergence as accepted rather than closing it; this ticket tracks closing it, so the accepted divergence is tracked rather than only narrated.

OBSERVED (measured on task/7236, guarded green by Check 5f-f of tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh): the two loaders of the same fused-memory updatedAt field disagree on timestamp SHAPE.

- scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq uses jq's fromdateiso8601, which accepts ONLY "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" (after the filter strips a trailing .NNN millisecond suffix).
- crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs parse_iso8601_to_epoch has a split_tz arm (fused_memory_client.rs:417) accepting "Z", "+HH:MM", "-HH:MM", AND a bare no-TZ form (treated as UTC), with fractional seconds stripped in any of those positions. Its own unit tests pin all four (iso8601_plus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_minus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_no_tz_treated_as_utc).

So "2026-05-01T12:00:00+00:00" (and "2026-05-01T12:00:00", and "2026-05-01T12:00:00.000+01:00") parse to an epoch in the Rust loader and to null in the jq sidecar.

CONSEQUENCE, and why it is worth tracking rather than leaving narrated. Task 7236 made the jq conversion TOTAL (try ... catch null), which correctly stopped ONE such row from aborting the whole snapshot and taking the wrapper's exit-125 arm. But for these shapes the resulting done_at=null reproduces the ORIGINAL task-3731 silent-skip failure mode: P1's 14-day grace comparison skips a task with no done_at entirely, and the only signal is a stderr WARNING from scripts/reify-audit-predone-wrapper.sh ("done tasks with no done_at (P1 will skip them): ...") on a systemd hook path nobody is likely reading. Unreachable TODAY -- fused-memory's sqlite_task_backend.py updatedAt writer only emits ...Z -- but the catch null makes the failure permanently QUIET, which removes the pressure that would surface it if that writer ever changes.

SUGGESTED FIX (from the review): normalise the offset in the jq filter before fromdateiso8601 so it matches parse_iso8601_to_epoch's split_tz arm -- either splitting the [+-]HH:MM offset and adjusting the epoch (full parity, matching Rust's arithmetic), or at minimum handling the bare no-TZ form. A half-fix that normalises only +00:00/-00:00 to Z is worse than the documented divergence, because it makes zero offsets work while nonzero ones stay silently null.

HAZARD to respect, measured during 7236 and the reason this is not a one-liner: jq's `capture`/`match` produce EMPTY on no-match, and an empty result inside the filter's `map({...})` object construction makes the WHOLE OBJECT VANISH -- silently DROPPING the row from the snapshot. That is the exact data-loss trap that made `fromdateiso8601?` the wrong fix in 7236. Any widened parser must stay TOTAL (every input yields a value, never empty), and must keep the row present.

FILES
- scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq (the filter and its done_at DERIVATION header, which currently documents the divergence at item 3)
- tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh (Check 5f-f currently ASSERTS the divergence -- fixture row d4, "2026-05-01T12:00:00+00:00" -> done_at null. Closing the divergence must flip that assertion and its comment in the SAME diff, or the suite reds.)
- crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs (reference only -- parse_iso8601_to_epoch/split_tz is the contract to match; no change expected there)

Registration note: scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq is registered SURGICALLY via a scripts/verify-pipeline-infra-tests.txt row (added by 7236), which selects tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh at task scope. Do NOT add it to scripts/…[truncated, 9259 chars total]

GOTCHA — `orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py` takes ~215 SECONDS to run (measured 2026-09-15: 214.48s, 215 tests passed, on base f7f6c8f89a). At the Bash tool's 120000ms DEFAULT timeout it is SIGTERM'd mid-gate (exit 143) and reads as a hang. Pass an explicit `timeout` of at least 600000ms. The module is xdist_group-pinned and does whole-tree scans, so its cost is structural, not incidental.

Any task editing a merge-lane cluster path must budget against TWO independent zero-slack axes, not one. Measured on that same base, both EQUAL to the committed baseline (`check_against_baseline` reports 0 violations, i.e. no headroom anywhere):
- `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py` — lines 21572, prose_lines 12288, cognitive 2132, function_local_imports 16, reexport_names 60. `lines` is the RAW physical count (`len(source.splitlines())`, blanks included) and `prose_lines` is the union of docstring-spanned lines and tokenize COMMENT lines — so a rewritten comment must occupy EXACTLY the line count of the one it replaces, and a new kwarg must stay on its existing line. `orchestrator/pyproject.toml` ignores E501, so no wrap is ever needed.
- The DERIVED `total:private_reads` — 7212 summed across 231 lane-importing test files. `derive_totals` sums the WHOLE current `tests` map and `_check_totals` fails on any rise, so ONE new private attribute access — read, write OR call, receiver-agnostic — in ANY lane-importing test file reddens the gate. This is what makes a brand-new white-box test file importing `orchestrator.merge_queue` un-GREENable: it also adds a `tests` entry, which independently breaks `test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement` (a byte-identity comparison against the committed baseline).

Completed: Merge drop-guard inherits the PRECEDING task's plan targets from a reused _merge-verify worktree — "Merge commit is missing plan target files" cites files that were never the task's
Description: Two instances observed on 2026-08-29 during the reify stranded-branch recovery, with an IDENTICAL blocking message and OPPOSITE correct dispositions. Anyone treating the message as authoritative would either land a fragment or withdraw a finished branch.

INSTANCE A - reify task 4388. Guard cited gui/src/__tests__/viewport/channelTags.test.ts and its companion source file. Those files belong to reify task 6185, are on main, and were never on task/4388. The branch WAS independently partial (metadata.files declares 13 paths, the branch touches 2, coverage 0.15 - the clear outlier in a sweep of 68 branches where the next lowest is 0.50), so it was correctly withdrawn - but NOT for the reason the guard gave. The guard's own citation was a red herring.

INSTANCE B - reify task 5405. Guard cited 8 files belonging to THREE other tasks (reify 5951, 5867, 5718), all of which landed during that session. Measured: none of the 8 is in 5405's metadata.files (17 paths, all reify-audit/PDIAG); git cat-file -e fails for all 8 against the branch, so it never contained them; all 8 POSTDATE the branch's merge-base 6e2faf178f, so a correct merge takes them from the main side unmodified and the merged TREE contains them. merge-tree against main is CLEAN. Delivery coverage 17/17. Resubmitted unchanged and it merged.

LIKELY MECHANISM (hypothesis, not yet confirmed in code). The guard appears to consult a .task/plan.json that PERSISTS in a reused _merge-verify worktree and accumulates targets across successive tasks, then asserts those targets appear in the MERGE COMMIT DIFF. For a file that neither parent changed relative to the other, a merge commit's combined diff is silent - the same semantics that make `git show --stat <merge> -- <path>` print nothing. So the guard cannot distinguish "the branch dropped planned work" from "the branch never owned this file and main supplied it".

WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE. The existing family all concern targets that genuinely ARE the task's own: 990 and 1068 (_check_plan_targets_in_tree correctness and the amend-orphaned-commit false positive, both done); 1587, 3004 and 3110 (path normalization, external-repo paths, and post-declaration renames in _check_plan_files_touched_in_branch, all done); 3918 (pending - the base..HEAD range failing to measure the task's own contribution, in wrong-branch / mixed-stack / quarantined-lane shapes). This report is a distinct FOREIGN-PLAN shape: the cited targets were never this task's at all, and arrive from another task's state. If it is in fact a manifestation of 3918's third shape or of a plan-artifact lifecycle bug rather than a gate bug, say so and fold it in rather than fixing it twice.

SUGGESTED PROBE, in order:
1. Determine whether the guard reads the plan from the MERGE WORKTREE on disk or from the task record. If from disk, that is the bug - a reused worktree carries the previous task's plan.
2. Determine whether _merge-verify (or any reused _merge-* worktree) is cleaned of .task/ between tasks.
3. Determine whether the guard should test the merged TREE for the targets (git ls-tree / cat-file -e against the merge commit) instead of the merge commit's combined DIFF, which is silent for a file neither parent changed.

ACCEPTANCE. A regression test that reproduces a merge where a planned-target path exists in the merged tree but is absent from the merge commit's combined diff, and asserts the guard does NOT block. Plus a test that a plan.json left behind by a previous task in a reused merge worktree cannot influence the current task's target set.

PROVENANCE. Recorded by reify recovery session 4 (2026-08-29) in /home/leo/.claude/fleet/recovery/reify-ledger.json under key MERGE_GUARD_DEFECT_missing_plan_target_files, with the full per-instance evidence. Filed by se…[truncated, 9827 chars total]

GOTCHA (claude CLI 2.1.284, measured 2026-09-29, task 3995): the CLI does not treat the `.credentials.json` that shared.config_dir.TaskConfigDir.write_credentials writes ({claudeAiOauth: {accessToken}} only) as a login. With that file holding even a VALID token and no CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, `claude -p` reports 'Not logged in' at zero cost. With CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set, the env token is used even when the file is garbage, empty or half-written, and a garbage env token fails with 401 over a valid file. So a per-call env token is what picks the account, and concurrent rewrites of one shared config dir's credentials file are harmless. Pinned by shared/tests/test_config_dir_credentials_live.py (-m integration). To probe accounts cheaply, a failing CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN_* returns at cost 0; on this date only D/F/G authenticated.

entry_text: escalation/src/escalation/server.py::merge_cancel on a PENDING waiter cancels the merge even mid-verify: it fully retires the entry and reaps the in-flight merge worktree, so cancelling a 'verifying'/'gate'/'finalizing' entry throws away a running, possibly green verify. Only a 'queued' entry is free to cancel. The raw worker state 'gate_reverify' surfaces as merge_status state 'gate' (via server.py::_map_live_state).
target_text:
MEASURED 2026-09-09 (dark_factory, filed as task 5248): mcp__escalation__merge_cancel CANNOT cancel a queued or verifying merge request once its submitter's bounded wait has returned.

merge_cancel only acts on a request that still has a live waiter in the worker's `_waiters` map, and a waiter exists only while some caller is blocked inside `merge_request`. The documented protocol — which this repo's own skills mandate — is to submit with a bounded wait_secs (100) and then POLL merge_status. So every request that actually queues outlives its waiter and becomes UNCANCELLABLE through the MCP surface.

Live reproduction, with the two surfaces disagreeing about the same id:
  merge_status(task_id=5118) -> {state:'verifying', request_id:'mr-602bf437', position:0}
  merge_cancel('mr-602bf437') -> {cancelled:false, state:'unknown', reason:"No in-flight waiter..."}
while get_merge_queue reported that same entry as state=verifying, waiter_alive=true, and a pytest was genuinely running in its merge worktree.

The reasons merge_cancel's own error offers were each ruled out: not already-finalized (a live pytest was in its merge worktree), not never-submitted (position 0 with an owned worktree), not a server restart (the orchestrator process had been up ~40h continuously).

TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) an operator facing a congested or wedged queue has NO working MCP-surface lever — cannot reprioritise (task 5246) and cannot cancel (this). (2) get_merge_queue's `waiter_alive: true` disagrees with merge_cancel's "no waiter" for the same entry; one of those readings is lying to the operator, which is what makes the failure surprising and is worth fixing independently.

entry_text: Dark-factory's scheduler has NO dispatch gate on open escalations (no has_open_escalation check in scheduler.py): a PENDING task whose escalation is still open can be dispatched. To hold a pending task while a human rules, set its status to `deferred` (the only status that parks). As of 2026-09-29 a defer triggers reconciliation that APPENDS a generated 'resolution for: <title>' query to metadata.memory_hints (it no longer wipes the authored hints); restore the original hints set after deferring.
target_text: Task-status norm (Leo, 2026-06-08): a task that will be ready to run once its dependencies land should be `pending`, NOT `deferred` — the orchestrator scheduler respects deps and won't dispatch until they clear, so parking a dep-waiting task in `deferred` just quarantines it from the scheduler (it never auto-runs even after deps land). Reserve `deferred` ONLY for a genuine non-dependency gate: premise-unmet / orphan-producer with no consumer (G1); an explicit human decision/unblock gate; a bookmark/forward-stub awaiting an external trigger; manual/external (sudo-only, cross-repo dep); or deliberate scheduler-quarantine of a pathological task. If a task is deferred but its real blocker is an UNFILED task, the fix is to file the blocker + add a dependency edge + set pending — not leave it deferred. Applied this session: flipped 16 deferred→pending after verifying their deps were satisfied.

entry_text: In a $15-budget focused review, five parallel sonnet general-purpose subagents (one per cluster of about 10 merges) used about $8 of it in 18 minutes. Budget for subagent fan-out at about $1.6 per seat, or use fewer, narrower seats, so enough is left for triage and task filing.
target_text: Lessons about running a multi-agent investigation, from the 2026-09-19 dark-factory orchestrator-suite study (lead on a Fable-class model; seats on sonnet/opus/fable). (1) A cheap decisive scout by the lead beat the whole brief: the one surviving full junit report showed per-test time was FLAT (median 1.44 s), and an 80-second A/B of one trivial test with the whole suite collected vs only its own file collected (0.65 s vs 0.048 s) found the cause before any seat launched — check for an existing artefact (the merge path already wrote --junitxml) before paying for a measurement. (2) A direct look at the production process beat a regression on confounded history: an era regression argued the per-test floor was ≤26% of suite CPU; py-spy on a live worker and then paired whole-leg CPU totals showed ~88%. The lead wrongly conceded to the regression for an hour; reconcile contradictory seats with a direct measurement, not by averaging their arguments. (3) The separate adversarial critic pass again overturned more of the LEAD's claims than anyone's: it found a thread race in the prototype fix (iterated WeakSet: 170 RuntimeErrors in 8,139 drains on CPython 3.13.9), bounded the throughput claim with a closed-loop model (×1.3-2, not ×4 — the merge gate binds next), and reconciled two seats' incompatible CPU figures. (4) A per-file correlation is structurally blind to a cost that is socialised through a global autouse fixture — a 'negative result' (reach-in density r=0.095) and the real finding were both true. (5) Put 'do this yourself — do not spawn sub-agents' in every seat brief: one sonnet seat spawned its own forks and spent ~500k tokens on a job budgeted at ~100k. (6) A long-running seat that reports interim results is worth keeping alive: the crash-debugging seat only reproduced the hang on its 8th full-suite run (1 in 9), and the captured stack refuted its own earlier leading hypothesis. (7) Seats flagged an apparent prompt injection when a harness system-notice about commit attribution appeared attached to tool output mid-run; declining to act on it was correct and cost nothing.

entry_text:
Convention for PRD predicate gates in dark-factory (established by plans/write-triage-link-healing-prd.md D9, 2026-10-01): any gate task that later tasks depend on must ALSO carry a metadata.delivered_checks entry of kind 'script' that re-runs the same predicate.

Why: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::_deps_satisfied treats a dependency as satisfied when its status is in TERMINAL_STATUSES, which includes cancelled. Cancelling a gate to clear its hold would otherwise silently release everything behind it. A dependency on a task you may not edit has the same hole: a cancelled 3169 would dispatch its dependents. The fix there is an intermediate deterministic 'flip live' gate whose delivered_check asserts the real condition (write_triage.enabled true in the committed config).

Rules for the check itself:
- delivered_checks of kind 'script' run `<project_root>/<script> <args>` against the WORKING CHECKOUT.
- A check must FAIL on today's tree; the non-vacuity lint at commit_planning enforces this.
- scripts/check_write_triage_readiness_gate.py is generic: `--report NAME PATH`, `--require NAME PATH OP VALUE`, `--subcheck`, and its exit code is the contract. It can serve any PRD's gates.
target_text: GOTCHA (PRD gate design, verified 2026-09-23 against orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::_deps_satisfied): cancelling a dependency does NOT reliably release its dependents when that dependency carries metadata.delivered_checks. A cancelled task is terminal and satisfies the status check, but the delivered-check arm of _deps_satisfied runs against main for a cancelled dep exactly as for a done one ("the check trusts the state of main, not the status label"). So a plan like "if the reranker gate fails, cancel the integrate leaf so the downstream matrix leaf proceeds" withholds the downstream leaf instead: its grep for `def rerank_candidates` in a file that never landed returns rc 1 → FAILED (not ERRORED), the streak reaches grace_cycles (3), a born-at-L2 dependency_capability escalation fires and the dependent goes BLOCKED — the opposite of the intent. Correct fail-branch order: (1) remove_dependency(dependent, dep) FIRST, (2) then set the dep cancelled, (3) then cancel the gate. Also make the downstream leaf self-discovering (run the arm iff the module is on main, else record skipped) rather than reading instructions from task metadata written after dispatch. Written into plans/write-triage-flip-readiness-prd.md D3 and gate Γ2 (task 5804)'s before_done.args; caught by the fresh pre-commit review seat, not by the author.

A NEW such test file contributes to the summed total:private_reads, so it must keep `obj._attr` attribute accesses at 0 or the ratchet reddens. A name import like `from orchestrator.git_ops import _run` is NOT counted, because only ast.Attribute nodes are, and self/cls receivers are exempt. target_text:
Merge-lane ratchet, the TESTS-map arm (measured 2026-09-12 at HEAD=e9d1055ed8, task 5097 planning). Complements the earlier entry on cluster TOTALS and complexipy charging; this is the rule that bites a task adding TEST coverage rather than source.

scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::test_file_measures admits an orchestrator/tests file to the baseline's `tests` map iff `imports_lane_module(source)` — i.e. it imports orchestrator.merge_queue, orchestrator.merge_lane, or any other CLUSTER_PATHS module. Consequences for a NEW test file:
- It gains a `tests` entry, which ALONE stales the committed baseline and reddens test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement (byte-identity).
- Its private_reads feed derive_totals, which sums the WHOLE current tests map (baseline 7847 over 229 entries) and _check_totals fails on any rise. _check_tests iterates BASELINE keys only and skips absent paths, so the per-file arm does NOT protect you — the totals arm does the failing. The ratchet's own seeded self-test pins a brand-new file with private_reads:1 as a total:private_reads violation.
- private_reads is deliberately RECEIVER-AGNOSTIC: any `x._foo` (non-dunder) counts, including writes (`worker._host_allocator = a`) and calls (`await worker._dispatch_item(i)`), and chains count per hop. Bare self./cls. receivers are excluded, but `self.worker._x` counts. No helper, fixture or naming trick avoids it.
- patch_targets is a UNION across all tests entries, so reusing a leaf already in the baseline's 83 is free; a brand-new leaf is a violation.

Practical upshot: a test file that imports only orchestrator.verify_runner or orchestrator.config is INVISIBLE to both gates (neither is a cluster path) and can use unrestricted private access and length. orchestrator/tests/test_host_allocator.py is the worked example — absent from the baseline, module-level imports are pytest only. Keep new merge-lane-adjacent tests lane-import-free on purpose when you can.

When you genuinely cannot test the wiring (e.g. a new config knob threaded into merge_queue.py), pyright is the available substitute: orchestrator/pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] includes both `src` and `tests`, so making the new parameter REQUIRED keyword-only turns an unwired call site into a reportCallIssue on every pre-commit and verify. Task 5097 took that route after confirming no test anywhere drives the real SpeculativeMergeWorker._dispatch_item.

Also measured: merge_queue.py sits at EXACTLY its frozen lines=21572 / prose_lines=12288 / cognitive=2132, so a task that adds no cluster file has ZERO line slack there and must make every comment/docstring edit line-count-preserving (E501 is ignored in orchestrator/pyproject.toml, so a long line needs no wrap). Such a task raises no measure and must therefore NOT regenerate the baseline — regeneration is only correct for a commit that legitimately changes a measure (e.g. ζ1's new package directory).

entry_text: Convention (reify, 2026-09-30) for task-record provenance on members retired into a coarser combiner task, mirroring the E3 A/B shape. A deferred member carries: x_backlog_sweep_arm='retired', x_backlog_sweep='<sweep date>', x_replacement='<delivering task id as a string>', and x_flip_condition naming the exact condition that flips it back to pending. A member CANCELLED because its combiner is done also carries superseded_by='<combiner>' and x_cancel_reason, and its x_flip_condition is overwritten to 'None: cancelled … Reopen only if #<combiner>'s landed work is reverted'. entry_text: CONVENTION (dark_factory, task 5466): a recon/Stage-1 detector that files a recurring L1 'blocking' escalation and folds repeats by content fingerprint must call escalation/dedupe.py::file_or_fold_l1(queue, *, project_id, subject, category, finding_category, agent_role, summary, detail, log, log_label). target_text: Reconciliation already has a sanctioned escalation-fold path that the gate-backlog filer bypasses. `escalation/src/escalation/dedupe.py::submit_or_dedupe` (:318-360) handles the enabled/category gates, `find_dedupe_parent` lookup, and a TOCTOU guard that falls through to `queue.submit()` if the parent was archived mid-flight (so a finding is never dropped), delegating the mutation to `attach_dedupe_child` — pending-only (never resurrects an archived record), per-id flock-serialized, atomically rewritten, and it bumps `dedupe_count` plus promotes (never demotes) severity. target_text:
GOTCHA — editing a knob in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml can turn the orchestrator UNIT suite red on main, and there is currently no pre-merge gate that catches it.

WHY: orchestrator/tests/conftest.py's AUTOUSE `_isolate_orch_config` (:235) pins ORCH_CONFIG_PATH to the canonical absolute top-level dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml so tests load the OPERATIONAL config deterministically. Its docstring names this as deliberate and calls out `lock_depth` and `merge_verify_breadth` as "the operational values every test relies on" (task 2719 retired the old orchestrator/config.yaml symlink in favour of this absolute pin). Consequence, measured 2026-08-07: `OrchestratorConfig(project_root='/tmp').lock_depth` returns 12 — the repo's operational value — even though the declared pydantic field default is 2 and defaults.yaml ships 4. A test fixture that constructs OrchestratorConfig(...) directly and passes no override still gets the operator's value.

CONCRETE INSTANCE: commit 094d634465 ("config(locks): lock_depth 4 -> 12 — make dark-factory module locks file-granular") turned 3 tests in orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_status_on_resume.py red for EVERY lane. Their fixtures use 'a/b/c/d/e.py' and 'a/b/c/d/f.py', which files_to_modules collapses to one module ('a/b/c/d') only at depth <= 4; at 12 they stay distinct, so the tests' self-validating "same module, different file" precondition became unconstructible and fired.

BEFORE retuning a config knob: run the orchestrator suite at the proposed value and sweep for tests encoding assumptions about the old one. Also grep the yaml's own prose — 094d634465 left dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml:306-307 still documenting "the effective lock_depth of 4", contradicting line 59.

DO NOT "fix" such a break by pinning the old value in a test's config fixture: that opts the test out of the operational value _isolate_orch_config deliberately makes authoritative. Either deepen/adjust the fixture data to be valid at the new value, or decide the behaviour under test is now vacuous and rethink the assertion. Pinning is acceptable only as an explicit, commented exception to the contract.

TRIAGE NOTE: a lane whose diff does not touch the config, the test, or their inputs is NOT the cause. Verify with `git diff --quiet <merge-base>..HEAD -- <path>` per input file; if every input is byte-identical to main, the failure reproduces on main and belongs to a separate task.

entry_text: For a compile-RED TDD step that touches several integration-test binaries at once, use `cargo check --keep-going -p <crate> --test a --test b --test c` to see the errors of every binary. Both `cargo test` and `cargo test --no-fail-fast` stop after the FIRST binary that fails to compile, so they report only one file's errors. Measured in reify task #7292 (reify-solver-elastic tests/).
target_text: When a plan step says "run the whole crate — `cargo test -p reify-eval`" to catch collateral breakage, treat that literally as expensive, not just the `--lib` build: `-p reify-eval` (all targets) compiles+links ~250 separate integration-test binaries under `crates/reify-eval/tests/*.rs`, which can run long enough to hit a session usage-limit interruption (observed on task #7210, 2026-09-03 — a backgrounded full run was silently lost mid-compile when the session got interrupted, confirming CLAUDE.md's warning that abandoned background work is not recoverable). A cheaper, still-rigorous substitute when the touched functions are crate-private: (1) `grep -rn "unsupported law type" --include="*.rs" .` (or whatever string/symbol the change touches) repo-wide to confirm the function has zero external references — proves the blast radius is contained to the one file; (2) `grep -rl <touched-symbol-or-related-type> crates/reify-eval/tests/*.rs` to find the handful of integration-test files that plausibly exercise the changed path through the public trampoline, and run only those via `cargo test -p reify-eval --test <file1> --test <file2> ...` (multiple `--test` flags in one invocation); (3) combine with a full `--lib` run (covers every in-crate unit test, including the touched file's own inline `#[cfg(test)]` module) and, if a sibling fixture-consuming crate exists (e.g. `reify-eval-fea-tests`, which `include!`s the same shared test fixtures), its full suite too. This combination gives equivalent confidence to the full `-p reify-eval` run at a small fraction of the cost/time.

entry_text: VACUOUS-TEST-GUARD, two shapes measured in task 5134 (orchestrator/tests). (1) AN UNRELATED FAIL-OPEN PRODUCES THE ABSENCE. TestBuildAgentEnvCpuGovern::test_governance_disabled_by_default_no_df_agent_cpu_govern left exec_path='' and worktree unset. CpuGovernConfig.agent_env fails open on an unresolvable path, so DF_AGENT_CPU_GOVERN stayed absent even with enabled=True, and the flag the test names never got a say. Repair: make the precondition hold (a resolvable governor under tmp_path), then assert a positive control (enabled=True yields the key) before the absence. (2) THE COUNT IS READ BEFORE THE SCHEDULED CALLBACK CAN RUN. Scheduler._maybe_fire_park_stop_trip schedules its callback with asyncio.ensure_future, and set_task_status never yields. So a trip that really fires reads callback_count==0 unless the test does `await asyncio.sleep(0)` first: measured fired=0 without the yield and 1 with it. Every 'does not fire' test on that path passed even with its guard deleted. Repair: yield before counting, plus a control arm that does trip (resume() then fresh transitions, or the threshold-th transition) and asserts ==1.
target_text: TESTING GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-10-01, task 5134): a NEGATIVE assertion on a callback that production code schedules via asyncio.ensure_future ("callback did not fire", e.g. `callback_count[0] == 0`) is vacuous unless the test yields first. Scheduler._maybe_fire_park_stop_trip ensure_future's on_park_stop_trip and set_task_status never awaits afterwards (and an AsyncMock-patched mcp_call never suspends), so a trip that DOES fire is still counted 0. Probe: threshold 3, 4 blocked transitions → fired=0 without `await asyncio.sleep(0)`, fired=1 with it (is_paused was True both times, because the pause latch is synchronous). FIX: `await asyncio.sleep(0)` before reading the count, plus a positive control arm in the same test (drive the trip for real, yield, assert it fired once) so the zero is proven observable. Found in test_scheduler.py TestParkStopTrip ×2 and TestParkStopDisabled.

entry_text: reify-compiler gotcha: per-declaration where-clause params (`param w : Length = 5kg where flag`) are compiled through entity.rs's top-level Param arm, so check_param_default_type runs. Then `compile_per_decl_guard` MOVES the decl into `TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups`, not `value_cells`. Any pass that walks only value_cells (e.g. `param_default_cells`/`check_param_default_conformance` before task #7212) misses BOTH block-guarded and per-decl-guarded params. `guarded_groups` is a flat list: nested `where` blocks push their own entry with `parent_guard` set.
target_text: Reify guarded-block params take two distinct compile paths: block-form `where cond { param x }` routes through compile_guarded_members (guards.rs), which rebuilds the ValueCellDecl; per-decl `param x where cond` routes through compile_per_decl_guard using the decl already built at the structure-body site (entity.rs). To test block-form guarded-member ValueCellDecl construction (e.g. priv visibility), you MUST use the block form — the per-decl form bypasses compile_guarded_members entirely. Port members surface in template.ports[].members with composite id.member ("port.param"); guarded members in template.guarded_groups[].members with plain id.member.

entry_text: Reify compiler: expression compilation (compile_expr / CompilationScope in crates/reify-compiler/src/scope.rs) carries NO TypeAliasRegistry or structure/trait name sets, so any type annotation resolved inside an expression (e.g. a lambda param `|p : T|`) can only resolve builtins (incl. parameterized builtins via resolve_type_expr_with_aliases with an empty context) and ambient enums — user aliases/structures/traits stay UnresolvedType (tracked by #6893). Also: before #6871, `.x/.y/.z` failed on EVERY Point3 value (not just lambda params) because datum_projection.rs's table had no Type::Point arm.
target_text: In reify-compiler, `resolve_type_name` (type_resolution.rs:616) is NAME-ONLY (`&str -> Option<Type>`) and has no arm for ANY parameterized builtin — `Point3`, `Vector3`, `Field`, `List`, `Scalar<Q>`, etc. all miss. So any annotation site that matches `TypeExprKind::Named { name, .. }` and calls `resolve_type_name(name)` silently DROPS the `<...>` type args and then reports the type as unresolved. The canonical full resolver is `resolve_type_expr_with_aliases_kinded` (type_resolution.rs:1687), used correctly by `compile_function` (functions.rs:93-137). Two sites carried this defect: the lambda-param arm in expr.rs (~5395, task #6871) and `resolve_field_type_name` (functions.rs:771), which resolves `field def F : D -> C` domain/codomain and turns `Point3<Length>` into `Type::StructureRef("Point3")` plus a warning (relevant to #6543). When adding or reviewing a type-annotation position, check which resolver it uses.

entry_text: In `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._run_merge_phase` the Phase 1 pre-merge re-verify (`run_scoped_verification(..., role='task')`) is the only task-role verify outside `_run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry`, and it passes no task_id or attempt_id. Whatever it returns, the loop still submits to the merge queue (with pre_rebased=False on a failure or timeout), and the queue's own merge verify is the real gate. Only a RAISED VerifyInfraError bypasses that path: it escapes run() and blocks the task as infra_issue, and the detection log says 'Task None'. This is how Task 4237 (2026-09-26) and Task 5671 (2026-09-28) blocked. Task 6039 owns the fix. Separately, the main-tip sweep (`run_main_tip_sweep`, background role) swallows the same raise as 'unexpected error ... returning the no signal sentinel' and persists nothing.
target_text: Orchestrator verify retry architecture (task 2365): the task-path debugfix loop (_verify_debugfix_loop in workflow.py) ONLY auto-retries verification via the VerifyInfraError exception path (_run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry, bounded exponential backoff, keeps task in-progress). A *returned* failed VerifyResult — even an INFRA_TRANSIENT_CATEGORIES one like env_transient or pytest_internalerror — does NOT trigger a whole-suite retry; it flows to the preexisting-break probe, signature-repeat guard, then the DEBUGGER. So to make a transient verify signal retry WITHOUT burning debugger iterations, raise VerifyInfraError (any phase string, errno may be None) rather than adding a FailureCategory. CONVENTION — cite code by SYMBOL, never by `file:line`. CANONICAL (curator gate 6022, 2026-08-20).

THE RULE: in comments, doc prose, tests and memories, reference code by a stable anchor — function/method/type name, named block, match arm, or §-section title — not by a line number or line range. Line numbers rot silently on any edit above the target, nothing validates them, and the comment becomes actively misleading rather than merely unhelpful. Cite docs by section name, not line range. Keep `esc-<id>` anchors, task ids and PRD paths verbatim: those are already drift-immune.

THIS IS NOT ADVISORY, IT IS MEASURED. Every audit that has looked found most cites already stale: 80 of ~103 stdlib cites wrong (one past EOF, one naming a deleted file, one on a blank line); 6 of 7 spot-checked targets stale with drifts up to 76 lines; 8 of 10 sampled wrong at #5856's start, one by 71 lines. Self-cites rot fastest — only 2 of 11 still accurate. Cites routinely go stale WITHIN THE SAME DIFF that introduced them, because the paired impl commit shifts the code being cited.

UNPOLICED EVERYWHERE, including stdlib/*.ri — NOT enforced by any guard test. [CORRECTED 2026-09-20, task #5801 investigation, recorded at abd8dbbe-0d23-43cf-88ba-dcd369b43454: crates/reify-compiler/tests/stdlib_citation_hygiene.rs is ABSENT from main (`git ls-tree -r main`), as is harness_stdlib_hygiene.rs. A green test run is NOT evidence your cites are fresh.] This is exactly why the convention keeps being rediscovered.

TWO REFINEMENTS worth knowing before you "fix" a stale cite:
- Converting `path:line` to a symbol: VERIFY the replacement handle actually greps in the target repo first. A multi-line call or a since-refactored assignment makes a plausible verbatim literal resolve to zero hits — that swaps a stale number for a stale literal, which is STRICTLY WORSE because it no longer looks stale.
- In a doc that deliberately mixes dated-evidence anchors with forward-looking pointers, make the classes distinguishable PER CITE: a cite carrying a line number is part of the dated record; a bare symbol is a forward-looking pointer. Then any single cite can be classified in isolation.
- When you must keep an in-file line cite, make the edit line-count-neutral (rewrap within existing comment lines) so other self-cites do not shift, then re-verify against the POST-edit file.

entry_text: DASHBOARD SPA (task 5594, 2026-09-30): to read a Datum the server serves NESTED inside a payload that data.js registers as PLAIN (PERFORMANCE[project].cards, like TASKS_SNAPSHOT / BURNDOWN_BY_PROJECT), use static/redux/datum.js::servedDatum(served, endpointKey, absentReason, receipts). It stamps the endpoint's receipt onto a copy: no receipt gives 'not yet fetched', a non-Datum gives absentReason. Then render through Pip/DatumReading with a field-reading format (c => fmtMs(c.ttc.p50)); never branch on state in tab code. The endpoint MUST also emit a top-level served_at: without it datumView's server gap is 0 and a weeks-old as_of badges as seconds. Gotcha when touching tabs.jsx: dashboard/tests/test_datum_components.py pins EXACT per-file site counts in _PIP_SITES (tabs.jsx 11) and _STAT_TILE_SITES (tabs.jsx 30). Changing an existing <Pip>'s datum source is free; adding or removing a <Pip>/<ST> site arrives red unless that table changes.
target_text: Dashboard SPA gotcha (found planning task 5594): a Datum served NESTED in a payload (PERFORMANCE / TASKS_SNAPSHOT / BURNDOWN_BY_PROJECT style) only ages correctly if the payload also carries a top-level `served_at`. data.js copies body.served_at into the endpoint receipt, and datum.js::displayedAgeMs treats a missing _served_at as ZERO server gap. So a stale Datum whose as_of is 20 days old silently badges as a few seconds when the handler forgets `{**shaped, 'served_at': now.isoformat()}` (the api/burndown.py idiom). Also as of 2026-09-30, endpoint_staleness.js::formatAge had no day unit (20 days renders '480h'); task 5594 adds one.
