entry_text:
GOTCHA measuring "what files did a task branch itself touch" (git 2.43, scratch-repo measurement for task 3918, 2026-10-05). Two independent errors combine.

(1) Plain `git log --name-only A..B` is MERGE-BLIND: it prints NO paths for merge commits, so a file changed only while resolving a back-merge (a conflict resolution or evil hunk) is invisible. Add `--diff-merges=dense-combined` (`--cc`). It lists a merge commit only for the paths it changed relative to EVERY parent, so a clean back-merge contributes nothing. NEVER use `-m` or `--diff-merges=first-parent`: on a back-merge the first parent is the branch, so they list everything main brought in.

(2) A WRITE-ONCE base (e.g. `TaskWorkflow._base_commit`) is too wide once the branch back-merges main or is re-cut after a quarantine: `old_base..HEAD` includes main's commits and CREDITS main-side edits as the branch's work. Re-derive the base at use time with `GitOps.merge_base_with_main(head)`.

Measured on one topology: stale base + plain log both missed the evil-merge path and credited main's edit; fresh fork + dense-combined got both right. Relevant to any consumer of a branch-touched set: the merge gate, the review diff, and implementer/debugger detection.
target_text: Git-diagnostic gotcha (hit during task 2060 /unblock triage): `git diff main..HEAD --stat` (TWO-dot) on a task branch whose base is stale is MISLEADING — it compares tip-of-main directly against tip-of-branch, so everything main ADDED since the branch's base shows up as "deletions". For task 2060 this rendered as 2917 deletions across 16 unrelated files (fused-memory stages, warm-lane tests, etc.), which looked alarming but was purely main having advanced 51 commits past the base. The REAL per-task diff is `git diff main...HEAD` (THREE-dot, against the merge-base): it was surgical (merge_queue.py +96, one test file). Always use three-dot (or `git diff <base>..HEAD`) to read a task's own changes when the branch base may be stale.

entry_text: Gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, task 7448): a reify gmsh-produced VolumeMesh of the 1.0x0.1x0.1 box (refine_with_size_field at uniform 0.05) carries many ORPHAN vertices (80 vertices on the x_max plane, only 20 referenced by any tet), so coordinate node-set selection must run on volume_mesh_to_solver_mesh's compacted output, not raw vm.vertices. Vertices are stored as f32, so derive expected face centroids from the mesh's own AABB (f32(0.1)/2 is 7.45e-10 off 0.05). refine_marked_elements retriangulates the WHOLE surface (classify_surfaces + create_geometry), so a remesh changes the tip-face node set even when no marked element touches that face (root-only marks: 20 -> 34 tip nodes). With the refine path's NumThreads=1 pin, the output was bit-identical across repeats.
target_text: Reify FEA solver gotcha (task 5008): a realized gmsh tet VolumeMesh can carry orphan vertices (surface nodes with no incident tet). Such a node cannot be handled by merely excluding it from BC node selection — the CG solver's Jacobi preconditioner (reify-solver-elastic/src/solver.rs extract_diag_jacobi, ~L683) UNCONDITIONALLY panics on any K row with a missing/zero diagonal, and assemble_global_stiffness sizes K at 3*n_nodes (n_nodes = coords.len()), so an orphan yields an empty row that trips the preconditioner regardless of BCs (panic relocates from dirichlet.rs:273 to solver.rs:710). The only robust fix is to COMPACT orphan (tet-unreferenced) vertices out of the solve mesh (reify-eval volume_mesh_to_solver_mesh) and renumber connectivity, so every solve DOF has a non-zero assembled diagonal. Use a STABLE ascending remap so it is a no-op for orphan-free meshes.

AUTHORITATIVE — reify #precision vs achieved facet deviation. This is the ADJUDICATED result of curator gate 6060 / esc-6060-1, ruled by Leo 2026-08-10 on 388 measured points. It SUPERSEDES three older entries that are each partly wrong and remain live only because a Mem0-consolidation hold is in force: 35147204 and 7fca1441 (Side A — right about the phenomenon, WRONG about the mechanism and overstating the swing) and 52d9bf5a (Side B — arithmetically correct but its conclusion is FALSE, because the data table it was given had the 0.44/0.46/0.60mm rows dropped in transfer, so it never saw two of the three off-trend points). If you retrieve any of those three, prefer this entry.

THE CORRECT STATEMENT. Achieved sampled facet-chord deviation is a STAIRCASE in requested #precision — neither a sawtooth nor near-linear. Treads follow an upper envelope at ~2.075x the request, punctuated by narrow PERIODIC DOWNWARD TEETH at ~0.758x, plus a third branch at ~1.49x for d/R < 2.5e-4. Teeth are NOT isolated anomalies: near 0.65mm they recur with period ~0.022mm and width ~8.5um (~39% duty cycle); near 0.30mm the period tightens to ~0.006mm. Transitions are brutal — 0.5955mm gives 1.223e-3 m and 0.5960mm gives 4.541e-4 m, a 2.69x change in achieved deviation for a 0.08% change in the request. Exactly scale-invariant in d/R. Deterministic and reproducible digit-for-digit across binaries and machines.

WHAT EACH SIDE GOT WRONG. Side A's "never interpolate a precision sweep, and verify both neighbours" guidance is CORRECT and survives. But its mechanism cite is wrong twice over: occt_wrapper.cpp's tessellate_shape contains only the three-line mesher call and no integer arithmetic, and the "OCCT meshes each EDGE into an integer segment count" framing is falsified by a control — the same sweep on cylinder(1000mm,2000mm), whose curved face IS edge-segment-quantised, is perfectly smooth at ratio 0.493-0.500 with ZERO teeth. Side A's "~3x swing" is really 2.74x, and its "TWO isolated teeth" is a large undercount caused by sampling a 0.05mm grid. Side B's "NOT a sawtooth" and especially "do not assume large swings between adjacent values" are FALSE and unsafe; only its 2.074x ratio arithmetic over its own 8 points was sound.

THE REAL MECHANISM (verified at OCCT V7_9_3 source AND by 388/388 branch prediction) is a TWO-LADDER PHASE COLLISION on the sphere face, not per-edge quantisation. Interior surface nodes get step 0.7*ArcAngularStep quantised by a truncating divide (BRepMesh_SphereRangeSplitter.cxx:25-27, literal "0.7 *"), while the seam meridian EDGE is tessellated at HALF the requested deflection (BRepMesh_CurveTessellator.cxx:74, "0.5 * myDEdge->GetDeflection()"). The 1.015% mismatch between 0.70000 and 0.70711 makes the two ladders drift in and out of phase over the same V-range, and the branch is selected entirely by m-nV. See Mem0 d284d7b2 for the full derivation, cfb0f4bb for the raw measurement.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE, and note the architecture is moving: #precision does NOT upper-bound achieved deviation (exceeded up to 2.106x). Leo has REJECTED making it one by scaling — see the E+F+D decision — so treat #precision as a NOMINAL control and use a RepresentationWithin assertion when you need a guarantee. Until measure-and-refine machinery lands, choose a value whose UPPER envelope clears the bound (~2.09 * precision <= bound, with margin) rather than hand-sweeping neighbours: teeth only ever move deviation DOWN, so bounding the treads bounds everything, and near 0.30mm the tooth period (~0.006mm) is finer than a +/-0.01mm neighbour probe can resolve anyway. 0.3mm is genuinely safe against a 1e-3 bound (tread 6.202e-4, 1.61x margin, whole neighbourhood clears); 0.50mm clears ONLY because it sits on a 4.5um-wide tooth whose tread value ~1.03e-3 violates — a true knife-edge.

entry_text: Reify decl-level match blocks (`match kind { Hex => sub head : HexHead, _ => sub head : DefaultHead }`) do NOT support a bare `_` wildcard arm at compile time. MEASURED 2026-09-30 with `reify eval`: it errors "match-arm pattern '_' is not a variant of enum 'Kind'" plus "non-exhaustive match". The parser lowers `_` to the pattern string "_", but entity.rs compile_match_arm_decl_group has no wildcard handling. Only the EXPRESSION-form match treats bare `_` as a catch-all. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RV8QPD0JZDHVCH6PQ0PCHDB9Z was filed from task 5967.
target_text:
Reify's two `match` compilation paths enforce match-arm variant-name validity asymmetrically (confirmed by source read, main @56a277fae0): the DECL form (crates/reify-compiler/src/entity.rs:5277-5290) validates every arm pattern against the discriminant enum's variants and emits "match-arm pattern '

' is not a variant of enum ''", while the EXPRESSION form (crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs:5278-5293, `lower_simple_pattern`) performs NO such check and lowers `MatchPattern::Variant(n)` straight to IR. A typo'd variant on the expression path therefore compiles to an unconditionally-false guard and surfaces only as a confusing downstream "non-exhaustive match" naming the wrong problem. Wildcard status on both paths is decided by WHOLE-pattern text (`pattern_text == "_"` at ts_parser.rs:4412 and :4548), so `_` in an or-pattern slot (`A | _`) lowers to `Variant("_")`, not `Wildcard`.

entry_text: reify gotcha: running `rustfmt --edition 2024 <file>` on a crates/*/tests/<name>.rs integration test that declares `mod common;` ALSO rewrites tests/common/*.rs (rustfmt follows out-of-line `mod` declarations), silently widening a targeted format into shared helpers. Format a new test file with `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` (nightly-only) or restore with `git checkout -- crates/<c>/tests/common/` afterwards, and always check `git status` before staging.
target_text: rustfmt RECURSES into `mod` declarations, which silently poisons the standard reify "compare rustfmt hunk counts against the merge base" check (canonical recipe: memory 3ff5c531-8807-403c-b86e-47015ade6689) whenever the file you touched is a module ROOT — lib.rs, main.rs, mod.rs, or any file containing `mod foo;`. rustfmt resolves those submodules relative to the checked file's own directory and reports each hunk under the SUBMODULE's path, not the root's. So `git show <base>:crates/X/src/lib.rs > /tmp/base.rs; rustfmt --edition 2024 --check /tmp/base.rs` gives a FALSE-CLEAN baseline: the submodules do not exist in /tmp, their hunks silently vanish, and the count is not comparable to the working-tree run, which does descend. Observed on task 5094: the /tmp baseline copy of crates/reify-ast/src/lib.rs reported 0 hunks while the in-tree run of the same file reported hunks in lib.rs, ast.rs AND decl.rs. `--skip-children` is NOT a way out — rustfmt 1.9.0-stable rejects it with "Unrecognized option: 'skip-children'" (and note it exits non-zero, so a `| grep -c` pipeline reports a meaningless 0 rather than failing loudly). Two working fixes: (a) materialise the whole sibling module set into the scratch dir before checking — `for f in $(git ls-tree --name-only <base> crates/X/src/); do git show "<base>:$f" > /tmp/base/$(basename $f); done` — then run rustfmt on /tmp/base/lib.rs; or (b) skip counting entirely and filter hunk path+line, keeping only hunks whose path is the file you edited AND whose line falls inside your added range: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <file> 2>&1 | grep -oE '<file>\.rs:[0-9]+' | awk -F: '$2>START && $2<END'`. This is the same transitive-descent behaviour already noted for `#[path]`-declared C1 harness roots (memory f8b9de2e); the new part is that it also invalidates the /tmp baseline comparison, which is what CLAUDE.md's "rewrite a hunk only when it falls entirely inside your own new code" rule depends on.

Completed: check-harness-baseline-registration.sh: a no-arg invocation reports a vacuous green pass over an empty candidate set
Description: Found while implementing task 7040 (harness_syntax lowering split); OUT OF SCOPE there, which was confined to crates/reify-syntax/tests/**.

FILE: scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh, input-dispatch block at ~lines 213-224.

OBSERVED. The documented dispatch is "positional args, else newline-separated stdin", implemented as an unredirected `while IFS= read -r _line` loop, so a no-argument caller falls through to stdin. Two bad outcomes in non-interactive contexts:

(1) With a socket/pipe stdin that never reaches EOF (e.g. a backgrounded agent-harness shell) the script HANGS. Measured: blocked 17+ min in WCHAN unix_stream_data_wait, State S, no children, /proc/<pid>/fd/0 -> socket:[3626119811].

(2) With `< /dev/null` it returns instantly having read ZERO paths, prints `HARNESS_BASELINE_REG PASS` / `HARNESS_BASELINE_REG SUMMARY added=0 violations=0`, exit 0. Indistinguishable from a real pass, but nothing was checked. This produced misleading verification evidence during task 7040; the correct form `bash scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git` on the identical tree reported `added=15 violations=0`.

Hypothesis (not established here): some CI/agent call site may invoke it with no args and be getting a vacuous pass. Grepping repo-resident and dark-factory-side call sites (scripts/verify.sh, hooks/, orchestrator config) is part of the work.

SUGGESTED WORK (small, defensive): make the empty-input case self-announcing instead of silently green. In order of preference: (a) when the candidate list is empty and no positional args were given, emit a distinguishable marker (e.g. `... added=0 violations=0 input=empty`) or a stderr hint naming --from-git; (b) refuse a no-arg invocation on a non-TTY stdin with a nonzero exit and usage text; (c) at minimum document the trap in the script header beside the existing dispatch comment. Leave --from-git and the positional form behaviourally unchanged — both are correct today.

Not urgent: scoped-verify callers appear to pass input explicitly and no bad merge is known to have resulted. Priority low.

Operational workaround captured as mem0 procedural_knowledge ddb5db45-c2d4-4797-9a97-293b70cae841; this task is the code fix.
Analysis: Call sites (verify.sh) already use --from-git. Existing tests (Sections J, P2) pin exact stdout and silent stderr for empty stdin, so options (a)/(b) would require editing out-of-scope tests; apply option (c): header documentation of the trap.

2026-09-29 diagnosis: why reify's second merge-verify host leo-laptop sits mostly idle. The laptop only takes overflow merge-queue verifies. HostAllocator.acquire (verify_runner.py) prefers local, so the laptop never verifies the head; all 80 laptop verifies since 08-01 were depth-1 speculative. K = 1 + runners = 2, and a host lease is released only in _finalize_inflight (merge_queue.py), which runs in submission order behind the head. So the laptop finishes in ~22 min, then holds a dead lease until the local head verify lands (~75 min, since the contended workstation is 3.4x slower). That caps laptop utilization at ~30% even with a deep queue. Measured 09-27T07Z to 09-29T16Z from reify runs.db heartbeats: laptop ~11% verifying, ~30% leased but finished, ~43% free while local verified a lone item (queue depth >=2 in ~60% of those, consistent with task 4929's missing host-free wakeup), ~15% both idle. Outages: 09-12 to 09-24 benched on every dispatch (uv not on PATH, fixed cf6184cfe3); 09-25T14:49Z to 09-27T06:57Z quarantined because the laptop was suspended for 41h. Owners: 4929 (wakeup, pending behind 5036), 5205 (local verify contention), 4540 (dark_factory never uses the laptop; pending on 4537).

ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-29 /deb, reify merge queue): the second verify host sits idle not because it is benched but because the DISPATCHER NEVER ASKS. Two distinct defects in _verifier_loop, filed as DF 3276 and 3277.

(1) DF 3276 — DISPATCH-FILL early-break tests the WRONG PREDICATE. merge_queue.py:12471-12481 breaks the fill loop on `allocator.free_host_count() == 0 or (not is_from_verifier_queue and not self._redispatch)`. The comment says the hazard is blocking on `_verifier_queue.get()` when the QUEUE is empty after a cascade; the predicate actually tests that `_redispatch` is empty. So when an item is dispatched from _redispatch (cascade-remerge or RU re-dispatch) and _redispatch then drains, the fill ends even though _verifier_queue holds ready items and a host slot is free. The guard also looks REDUNDANT: falling through takes get_nowait() (dispatches immediately) or the QueueEmpty branch, which races a PERSISTENT getter against running verifies and cannot block indefinitely.

(2) DF 3277 — no re-fill while parked in FINALIZE-HEAD. Once fill_done is set the loop blocks in `await self._finalize_inflight(head)` for the whole head verify (20 min - 2 h on reify). The ONLY mid-verify re-fill path is the asyncio.wait fill-ahead race at merge_queue.py:12323-12341, reachable ONLY via the QueueEmpty branch. Net asymmetry: the loop CAN wake for a newly-arriving queue ITEM (when idle) but NEVER for a newly-available HOST. So a host freed / un-quarantined mid-verify is stranded until the head completes.

MEASURED COST (reify, 7 days to 2026-07-30): of 1409 merge-queue heartbeats with depth>=2 and 2 hosts configured, 53% showed only ONE host busy, 37% two, 9% zero. The second host ran just 28 of 228 completed merge-verifies (12%).

DECISIVE EVIDENCE that this is "never asked", not "acquire failed": tasks 5568/5196 sat in state `awaiting_verify` (the _verifier_queue state) and NOT `awaiting_host` (the _redispatch state, merge_queue.py:9958-9979), so _dispatch_item was never CALLED for them. target_text: Cross-language (Rust producer ↔ TS consumer) wire-contract guards in reify's GUI: a vitest test that READS Rust source at test time is scope-safe exactly where it already lives, and needs no fixture relocation. `scripts/verify.sh`'s scope arm (~line 1259, verified on main 2026-09-12) classifies `gui/src-tauri/*` as `rust=1; gui=1`, so a lone edit to `gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs` fires BOTH the Rust arm and the GUI/vitest arm under `--scope staged/branch` — which is the direction that matters, since the thing you are guarding against is someone changing the Rust producer. (Contrast the fixture-PLACEMENT case in memory a73df79d: a file read by both sides must live under `gui/src-tauri/`, because every other `gui/*` path is `gui=1, rust=0`.) The shape used by task 6723 for `ConstraintData.status`: a vitest-free helper under `gui/src/__tests__/` with NO `.test.` segment (so vitest's default include does not collect it; `toolDefNames.ts` is the precedent), exporting a PURE function over a source STRING plus a thin `readFileSync` resolver — the purity is what lets the helper's own unit pins work off synthetic Rust string literals with no on-disk fixture. Two non-obvious requirements: the extractor must NOT normalise (casing is the signal being detected), and it must THROW on an empty/partial/ambiguous match, because the characteristic failure of a source-scraping guard is going vacuous — rename the Rust enum and a lenient extractor returns an empty map, the fixture builds with `undefined`, and the guard passes while asserting nothing.

  "The Reify DSL uses positional-call form exclusively — field labels like

   positional args (see crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs).  To set
   `shell_force` (position 8) we must supply all preceding defaults explicitly"

   positional binding preserves existing callers that omit it)."
The underlying fact is not false — declaration order genuinely still governs UNLABELLED args — but the framing "positional binding" is the retired wording, and the "same rationale as PointLoad" cross-reference now dangles: #6484's commit bf6988e76d rewrote PointLoad's rationale in this same file (:325-340) to the by-name explanation, so Gravity cites a rationale that no longer reads as it did. Bring it in line with the PointLoad wording immediately above it.

target_text:
THE HIGH MERGE LANE IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE MCP SURFACE. Verified on dark-factory main @ 5bd7fd8489 (2026-08-20).

The merge queue has two lanes (`MERGE_LANES = ('high','normal')`, orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py:415-417) and the lane is NOT a parameter on any tool. `MergeRequest.lane` defaults to `'normal'` (merge_types.py:35) and exactly ONE of the six MergeRequest construction sites in the repo ever sets it: workflow.py:10306, `lane=lane_for_task_metadata(self.task.get('metadata'))`. The other five all take the normal default — escalation/src/escalation/server.py:2330 (the `merge_request` MCP tool), merge_queue.py:5603, merge_queue.py:14388 (GroupMergeRequest), workflow.py:1711 (GroupMergeRequest), stranded_verified_green.py:323.

CONSEQUENCE: `merge_request` (server.py:2025-2033) has no lane/priority parameter and omits `lane=` when it builds its MergeRequest, so EVERY merge submitted through the MCP — /merge-queue, /unblock, /do, an interactive session, the escalation-watcher — lands in the normal lane, and does so SILENTLY, REGARDLESS of the task's `metadata.merge_lane`. The queued/attached response shape (server.py:2094-2100) carries no lane field, so the submitter cannot even observe the downgrade.

The high lane is therefore reachable only from the orchestrator's own in-process VERIFY→MERGE submission. fused-memory exposes no merge tool at all (`merge_lane` has zero hits in fused-memory/src); the entire merge surface (merge_request/merge_status/merge_cancel/get_merge_queue/halt_merge_queue) lives on the escalation MCP.

TO VERIFY WHICH LANE AN ITEM ACTUALLY GOT: `get_merge_queue` returns `worker.snapshot()`, whose per-item shape DOES include `lane` (merge_queue.py:12491, 12508). That is the only lane observability that exists today.

Filed as task 4531 (add an explicit lane parameter to merge_request + honour metadata.merge_lane as fallback).

entry_text: reify: `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps` is already hermetic. With CARGO_HOME pointed at an empty mktemp -d it returns rc=0 in about 170ms and leaves CARGO_HOME empty, because nothing is resolved, fetched or written to Cargo.lock. Only the full-resolve form (no --no-deps) needs `--locked --offline` to avoid rewriting Cargo.lock and fetching from the network. Measured 2026-10-03 on task 7316's lane: a bare full-resolve read on a cold CARGO_HOME fetched for 13s and succeeded, while `--locked --offline` failed with rc=101 in 227ms.
target_text: To test cargo offline/network behavior in reify's infra tests, redirect CARGO_HOME to an empty mktemp -d — never set CARGO_NET_OFFLINE or pass --offline from the test, which forces the behavior under test from outside and makes the assertion tautologically green regardless of the code change. RUSTUP_HOME is independent of CARGO_HOME, so the toolchain still resolves and cargo fails for the intended offline-resolution reason. Measured in a reify worktree: `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --locked --offline` (== --frozen) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to plain --locked on a warm cache (2741207 bytes, cmp clean), and fails in ~0.4s on a cold CARGO_HOME with "no matching package named `serde` found ... offline mode".

entry_text: On fused-memory main as of 2026-10-01 (f3aa08d619), TaskCurator degrades to action='create' on a zero-output hang (ZOT) at THREE sites, not two: (1) curate()'s breaker short-circuit, (2) curate()'s `except CuratorFailureError` branch, and (3) curate_batch_prepared's OWN breaker gate, which never calls curate(). The justification 'llm-error-escalated' covers EVERY CuratorFailureError, so it cannot tell a ZOT apart from other failures; use exc.zero_output_timeout or a structured flag. Also, no `curator.*` config leaf is in fused_memory/config/reload.py::RELOADABLE_FIELDS, so curator knobs take effect only after a fused-memory restart, not via reload_config.
target_text: The TaskCurator's zero-output-timeout (ZOT) circuit breaker installed by task 1743 is INERT for the pattern escalations repeatedly cite it as mitigating, and any triage note claiming "a circuit-breaker watchdog will short-circuit further curator LLM calls if this recurs" is FALSE as filed. Mechanism: _record_zero_output_timeout opens the breaker only at zero_output_breaker_threshold=2 CONSECUTIVE ZOTs, while _reset_zero_output_breaker() fires on ANY successful call. Curator zero-output events recur hours apart with ~35 successful calls per day in between, so the counter is always reset before a second one lands. It has never opened (0 "zero-output-breaker OPEN" lines in the retained journal). There is also NO retry — a single timeout degrades straight to action='create'. Tracked as task 3995 part C. First reported via escalation esc-task-curator-14 (2026-08-10, memory b19e3519 — consolidated into this entry 2026-08-20). IMPORTANT: task 4143 (pending) documents the OPPOSITE-direction defect on the same breaker — _reset_zero_output_breaker has exactly one call site (task_curator.py:1336, inside curate() after a successful single-item _call_llm), so a successful multi-item BATCH call never resets it, meaning two size-1 ZOTs arbitrarily far apart can open the breaker and disable dedupe for 600s. 3995C and 4143 push the same mechanism in opposite directions and must be adjudicated TOGETHER before either is dispatched.

entry_text: Gotcha for corpus-repair work that amends Mem0 records in place with update_memory and then checks for duplicate corrections by re-running the census searches: a content amend RE-EMBEDS the record, so an amended target can newly rank for a query where the pre-mutation census did not find it. A check of the form "every id in (after-search hits minus census hits) must not carry the correction marker" therefore fails on correct data unless the amended target ids are also subtracted — the question is whether a NEW record carries the marker, not whether a target moved in the ranking. Measured in task 6060 (2026-09-29): 2 of 5 amended targets surfaced as new hits for a query they had not matched before. The same run showed a sandboxed implementer reaching update_memory and get_memory_by_id over HTTP on :8002 through scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py::FusedMemoryClient under a curator- identity the task text sanctioned, after a zero-UUID probe returned MemoryNotFound.
target_text:
`update_memory` has TWO independently gated arms — `content_amend` (rewrite a record's text in place; re-embeds, point id survives) and `metadata_patch` (patch/delete metadata keys; no re-embed) — each behind an agent_id-prefix allowlist read live off config per call, plus a `mem0_update.enabled` kill switch that outranks both. Since 2026-08-12 the schema default for BOTH arms is `['recon-stage-', 'curator-']` (config/schema.py Mem0UpdateConfig; resolver in server/mem0_update_authz.py, every fallback fail-closed). An ordinary interactive agent_id is refused with error_type=Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized.

THE SANCTIONED PATH TO AMEND A MEMORY IS THE `/curate-fused-memories` SKILL, whose sitting legitimately adopts `agent_id='curator-<slug>'`. That is what the prefix was minted for (Leo's ruling (b) on esc-3524-1). Do NOT instead write a superseding duplicate record — that was tried on 2026-08-24 and is strictly worse: it leaves the wrong text in the corpus alongside the correction.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS SAFE, and it is load-bearing: `agent_id` is SELF-REPORTED, and the resolver's own docstring says the gate is "a misuse deterrent for cooperating callers ... not a security boundary." So adopting `curator-` is legitimate ONLY while actually executing a sanctioned curation sitting, or at an operator's explicit direction. It is NOT legitimate to adopt it because you hit Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized mid-way through unrelated work and want past it — renaming yourself to clear a gate is self-authorization for a silent-rewrite primitive. In that case stop, leave the record alone, and ask an operator.

PRACTICAL NOTES: authorization is checked BEFORE any record lookup, so `update_memory` against a nonexistent uuid is a zero-mutation authority probe — a MemoryNotFound reply means the arms are held, Mem0UpdateNotAuthorized means they are not. Pass `reason` on every amend; it is the audit trail. `metadata_patch` is separately validated against the Mem0 metadata vocabulary at the service seam (an off-vocabulary topic spelling, or a second canonical for a topic already taken, is refused there), and `metadata_delete_keys` removes a key outright. Note also that ~20 content amends in an hour trips `mem0_update.storm_threshold`, which ESCALATES but never blocks, by design.

target_text: The escalation MCP server (http://127.0.0.1:8100/mcp, the `escalation` entry in reify's tracked .mcp.json) is STATEFUL streamable-HTTP, unlike the fused-memory curl pattern in scripts/reify-audit-predone-wrapper.sh: a bare JSON-RPC `tools/call` POST returns HTTP 400 "Bad Request: Missing session ID" (measured 2026-09-27). entry_text: Convex hull / Minkowski availability in reify's native deps (verified 2026-09-30): manifold3d 0.3.0 (a pure re-export of manifold-csg 0.3.0) exposes Manifold::hull(), Manifold::batch_hull(&[Manifold]), Manifold::hull_pts(&[[f64;3]]), minkowski_sum() and minkowski_difference(), with egress via to_mesh_f64() -> (vert_props, n_props, tri_indices_u64). OCCT 7.8 has NO 3D convex-hull API, and no workspace crate has a hull implementation (no chull/quickhull/parry crate in the cargo registry). ManifoldKernel::execute handles only Union/Difference/Intersection and returns STUB_MSG for every other GeometryOp via a wildcard arm.
target_text: Reify: the Manifold kernel is UNREACHABLE from `reify eval` / `reify check` / `reify build`, for two independent reasons — and the common guess ("the #kernel pragma is ignored") is WRONG. (1) Module-level `#kernel(manifold)` IS accepted and honoured: `manifold` is in `KNOWN_V02_KERNELS` (crates/reify-compiler/src/module_pragmas.rs:52) and is threaded to the dispatcher via `.with_prefer_kernel(module.kernel_pragma.as_deref())`; only BLOCK-level `#kernel` is discarded with a warning (:159-178). (2) The real blockers are that `manifold_capability_descriptor()` (crates/reify-kernel-manifold/src/register.rs:112-119) declares ONLY three entries — (BooleanUnion|BooleanDifference|BooleanIntersection, Mesh) — so no query op (e.g. GeometryQuery::Distance) is dispatchable to Manifold at all; and all four reify-cli engine constructions (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:902, 1136, 1501, 2174) use the SINGULAR `Engine::with_registered_kernel`, which picks via `pick_lexmin_brep_kernel()` and loads exactly one BRep-capable kernel — Manifold is Mesh-only and never wins. The plural `with_registered_kernels` that would load it has no reify-cli caller. There is no `REIFY_KERNEL` env var anywhere in crates/. Consequence: any OCCT-vs-Manifold comparison must be written as a `GeometryKernel`-level pair test in `crates/reify-kernel-conformance` (the only crate dev-depping both kernels), never as a `.ri` fixture. Also note `ManifoldKernel::execute` implements only the three booleans and returns STUB_MSG for every primitive op, so a Manifold box must be OCCT-tessellated and `ingest_mesh`-ed; `manifold3d` is at 0.3 (not 0.2 as several in-repo comments still claim) and does expose an unused `Manifold::cube(x,y,z,center)`.

entry_text: Three reify tasks carry mis-authored delivered_checks of the MODE-3 shape: a file-existence capability written as kind=grep over file contents, where the pattern is the declared file's own name. They were found by replaying dark-factory task 3500's new authoring lint on 2026-09-28. Task 5511 has pattern 'extrusion_2020' for examples/best_practices/extrusion_2020.ri. Task 6763 and task 6907 have pattern 'divergence-baseline' for a .txt baseline file, whose content will not contain its own name. Such a check goes green only if some other file happens to mention the name, so it can wedge dependents with a DEP_CAPABILITY_NOT_DELIVERED block after the producer lands. target_text:
NORM for /prd capability-manifest sidecars: before filing a batch, verify every `kind: grep` delivered_check is DISCRIMINATING — an `expect: absent` check must currently MATCH (false now, required-true only after the leaf lands), and an `expect: present` check must currently NOT match. A check that is already in its expected state is green-by-construction and proves nothing about delivery.

Cheap verification loop (run from project_root before `submit_task`):
  git grep -cE '<pattern>' -- <paths>
and confirm the hit/no-hit polarity is the OPPOSITE of the declared `expect`.

Two practical rules that fell out of doing this on 2026-08-19:
- Prefer `expect: absent` checks over files that EXIST TODAY (e.g. "fn tool_defs is gone from debug_server.rs") to `expect: present` checks over files the leaf will CREATE — a present-check on a not-yet-existing path risks a harness error rather than a clean FAIL.
- A `kind: script` check whose script IS the leaf's deliverable is necessary-not-sufficient; pair it with a discriminating grep, never let it stand alone (the convention the merge-gate-compile-cost sidecar already documents).

Use `kind: manual` with an explicit `reason` for anything that is a before/after delta over a COMPILED listing (`cargo nextest list`) or that requires mutating and reverting the tree (observing a guard's rejection) — neither is a property of the committed tree, so no grep or committed script can express it. Manual checks are recorded but excluded from the dispatch gate by design.

Validate the finished sidecar before filing:
  cd ~/src/dark-factory && PYTHONPATH=shared/src .venv/bin/python -c "from shared.capability_manifest import load_capability_manifest; load_capability_manifest('<abs path>')"
(dark-factory's .venv has pydantic; the system python3 does not.) `commit_planning` then stamps task_ids in place and yaml.dump-rewrites the file, DROPPING all YAML comments — so keep the prose rationale in the `.md` twin, not in the sidecar header.

target_text: PSI dispatch-gate hold behaviour measured from data/orchestrator/runs.db on 2026-09-08 (14 days): scheduler_tick cadence is ~150-165 s median in both dark-factory and reify (p90 322-474 s), and the dispatch_deferred event is emitted once per tick on the first heavy skip, so hold episodes must be cut at a multiple of the tick interval (2.5x) rather than a fixed seconds gap — a 120 s cut falsely makes every hold a separate episode. Cut properly: reify's cpu_some_avg10 holds (threshold 70) were 86% single-tick, values clustered at 70-73, longest episode 5 ticks; dark-factory's mem_full_avg10 holds 82% single-tick, longest 4; dark-factory had ZERO cpu holds at the stock 85 (178 deferrals, all mem_full/mem_some/io). Interpretation: a hold costs one ~2.5-minute deferral of NEW dispatch, and ~60 agents cost ~1 core in total, so the gate's CPU leverage is small and hold/release hysteresis on it would only lengthen cheap blips — the expensive latching on this host is reify's jobserver reservoir (hours), not the gate. This is why the harmonisation PRD adopted no gate hysteresis. The runqueue ratio (procs_running/nproc) is the discriminating host CPU signal: 2.4x quiet vs 7.1x busy in task 3590's samples, 4.25x median during the 2026-09-07 saturation vs 1.1-1.9x after the fanout cuts; a live unit-cgroup read at moderate load gave cpu-some avg10 36.6 / avg300 40.9, so a 40 own-pressure threshold has no basis on the unit population and the PRD ships that arm off until calibrated on the slice population.

entry_text: PRECISE MECHANISM + FIX for the slow nested-pytest probe (refines memories aa61611b / fa1896ee; measured 2026-10-01, pytest 9.0.3, task 5146). `pytest <tmp_path>/probe.py -c orchestrator/pyproject.toml` sets confcutdir to the inifile's dir, and `PytestPluginManager._is_in_confcutdir(p)` is literally `p not in confcutdir.parents`. So /tmp and every dir under it count as "inside" (only `/` is excluded). Two effects follow. (1) `Session.collect` roots the tree at `<Dir tmp>` and runs pytest_ignore_collect plus a stat on every entry of the fleet-shared /tmp: ~72k entries, 31k Dir nodes, 128s of a 131s run at loadavg ~475, versus 0.00s collection with the fix. (2) Any conftest.py in /tmp, /tmp/pytest-of-leo, … gets IMPORTED into the probe, which is a contamination hazard. FIX: pass `--confcutdir=<probe's own dir>` (with the probe in a subdir of tmp_path). This bounds both conftest discovery and the collection root. The probe can stay in tmp_path, with no in-repo scratch dir to clean up. A control arm whose inifile sits beside the probe never had the problem, because its confcutdir already equals the probe dir.
target_text: When writing a real-pytest-subprocess config probe, put the throwaway probe dir OUTSIDE the package's `tests/` dir — `tests/conftest.py` applies to subdirectories, so every xdist worker imports the full package. Measured 2026-08-03 on a 1-item probe at -n 32: 43.38s with the probe under `fused-memory/tests/`, 12.93s with it outside. `<package>/.pytest-tmp/` is the right home: already gitignored (.gitignore:76 covers the sub-project spelling), dot-prefixed so pytest's norecursedirs skips it, and still close enough to the `-c` pyproject that rootdir resolution stays instant (a system /tmp path makes pytest walk from the filesystem root).

entry_text: Reify compiler: expression compilation (compile_expr / CompilationScope in crates/reify-compiler/src/scope.rs) carries NO TypeAliasRegistry or structure/trait name sets, so any type annotation resolved inside an expression (e.g. a lambda param `|p : T|`) can only resolve builtins (incl. parameterized builtins via resolve_type_expr_with_aliases with an empty context) and ambient enums — user aliases/structures/traits stay UnresolvedType (tracked by #6893). Also: before #6871, `.x/.y/.z` failed on EVERY Point3 value (not just lambda params) because datum_projection.rs's table had no Type::Point arm.
target_text: Reify compiler limitations on fn signatures (as of 2026-05-11 main): (1) fn_param grammar at tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:83-87 is `seq(name, ':', type)` with NO default-value slot — `param: T = expr` does not parse; (2) compile_function at crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs:11-15 hardcodes `empty_structs: HashSet<String>` and `empty_traits: HashSet<String>` passed to resolve_type_expr_with_aliases, because "functions are compiled before the trait/structure registries are built". Net effect: fn signatures CANNOT reference any user-defined trait/structure name (including stdlib types like ElasticMaterial, ElasticOptions, ElasticResult, Solid) — they resolve to Type::Real with an "unresolved type" Error diagnostic. Anyone filing a task that adds a fn declaration to the stdlib must either use builtin-only types in the signature OR depend on task 3440 (resolve stdlib trait/structure names in fn signatures, two-pass compile).

WHERE THE REGISTRY LIVES — a persistent PRD-level misdirection worth stating first. The registry is `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs`: `tool_defs() -> Vec<ToolDef>` and `dispatch_tool(state, name, params)`. It is NOT in `gui/src-tauri/src/debug.rs`, despite several PRDs (GR-016 §2.3 inventory row, mesh-morphing.md cross-ref) and task descriptions calling it "the debug.rs registry". `debug.rs` houses the unrelated `DebugBridge` used for frontend-mediated oneshot RPCs. And there is NO `gui/src-tauri/src/debug_bridge.rs` at all, despite some task metadata referencing it (confirmed absent 2026-07-27).

THE RULE: a FRONTEND-MEDIATED tool — one that reads the DOM or Solid stores rather than the OCCT engine — needs only TWO touch points:
1. a `ToolDef` entry in `tool_defs()` (gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs) with name, description and an object-typed JSON input_schema;
2. a handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in `gui/src/debug/bridge.ts`.
NO new Rust dispatch match-arm is required. `dispatch_tool`'s default arm — `_ => state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params).await` — already forwards any unmatched tool name to the JS bridge. Consequence worth knowing: a bridge-only handler works via `tools/call` without rebuilding the Tauri binary.

- STATE-BOUND / ENGINE-OR-DISK tools get an explicit Rust arm, via the `run_on_engine` helper: engine_state, mesh_stats, open_file, wait_for_idle, load_fixture, the stateless morph stats.
- IMAGE-RETURNING tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must ALSO be listed in `is_image_tool()`, or `tools/call` will not strip the data-URL prefix and emit an MCP image content block.
- FRONTEND STORE FIELDS your handler reads must be added to the `DebugStores` type in `gui/src/debug/types.ts`. That type exposes only a STRUCTURAL SUBSET of the real engineStore — e.g. it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297. A field missing there is a silent read failure, not a compile error in the Rust half.

TESTS
- Rust-side, for a frontend-mediated tool, just assert the tool_defs schema (object type, required fields) — there is no Rust behaviour to test. Precedents live alongside in debug_server.rs's own test module (tool_defs_includes_set_camera, tool_defs_contains_set_test_mode, tool_defs_includes_screenshot_window, is_image_tool_recognizes_both_screenshot_variants).

entry_text: Reify unit-literal scope gotcha (measured 2026-10-04, HEAD 92a94f7545): a TOP-LEVEL user `fn` body or fn-param default has NO unit registry, so the compound literal `300mm/s` errors ("compound unit expression requires a unit registry in scope") and only reify_core::units::BUILTIN_UNITS resolve there (mm cm m in deg rad kg g s K A mol cd); `200GPa`, `1N` and `5um` are "unknown unit". Compose from built-ins instead: `fn speed() -> Velocity { 300.0 * 1mm / 1s }`. Structure members (param, let, ctor args, sub blocks) and constraint defs DO have the registry, so `300mm/s` and `200GPa` work there.
target_text: In `.ri` sources, the corpus-standard way to write a unit-carrying value where a compound-unit literal (`300mm/s`, `1000N`) would fail is the compositional `<scalar> * <unit-literal>` form: `300.0 * 1mm / 1s`, `5000.0 * 1mm / (1s * 1s)`, `1000.0 * 1N`. Compound-unit literals route through `resolve_unit_expr` against the module's `UnitRegistry` and fail in registry-less scopes (`crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/units.ri:141-148`, `examples/integration_corner_cases.ri:29-35`); the compositional form resolves regardless of registry state and its `result_type` matches the declared dimension exactly. Established precedent: `STANDARD_GRAVITY() = 9.80665 * 1m / (1s * 1s)`, `SPEED_OF_LIGHT() = 299792458.0 * 1m / 1s`, `critical_load(result, 1000.0 * 1N)` (`buckling_column_p2.ri:84`).

RESOLUTION of the pytest-timeout inversion-band gotcha (memory 458d79ad-39aa-48a5-b87d-bf7ba2570111, task 5147) — LANDED 2026-09-07. Read this WITH that entry, which carries the mechanism and census; this one records only what changed, because that entry's closing claim that "nothing checks a per-test marker's VALUE" is now FALSE and it could not be amended in place (content_amend is restricted to recon-stage-/curator- agents).

WHAT TO WRITE when an orchestrator test needs more than the 60s ini default:
    from _orch_helpers import VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT
    @pytest.mark.timeout(VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT)
The only other sanctioned option is N <= 60, a DELIBERATE tight bound for a test asserting something happens FAST. Anything strictly between the two inverts.
Do NOT simply DELETE a slow test's marker — the ini default is 60, so removal leaves it worse off under a bare local `pytest` than the bug being fixed. That is why the named instance was RAISED to 300 rather than dropped.

WHERE THE RATIONALE LIVES, singly: the `VERIFY_CLI_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT = 300` comment block in `orchestrator/tests/_orch_helpers.py`, beside PYPROJECT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT and WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT. The guard, the amended pyproject comment and the fixed call site all POINT there rather than restating it. Follow that convention when you touch any of them.

WHY IT IS A LITERAL 300 and deliberately NOT `5 * PYPROJECT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` despite equalling it today: the quantity is the VERIFY CLI BUDGET, and the ini default is the OTHER EDGE of the band, not a scale factor. Deriving one edge from the other would let a tightened ini default drag the constant DOWN in silence — `timeout = 20` would shrink it to 100 — collapsing the band toward nothing while a ratio assertion stayed green as an identity. Same hazard and same resolution as WHOLE_TREE_SCAN_TEST_TIMEOUT deliberately not borrowing HEAVY_BARRIER_TEST_TIMEOUT's 300. A literal instead needs an EXECUTABLE link: a drift test re-reads orchestrator/orchestrator.yaml's test_command at runtime. GENERAL LESSON, worth more than this instance: when two constants happen to be equal, derive one from the other ONLY if the causal story actually runs that way; coincidental equality is how a silent shrink gets a green test.

THE GUARD: `orchestrator/tests/test_timeout_marker_inversion_guard.py`. AST-sweeps all FOUR binding forms — function/method decorator, class decorator, module-level `pytestmark`, class-level `pytestmark` — which is precisely the gap the pre-existing guards left (test_whole_tree_scan_timeout_guard.py reads MODULE-LEVEL marks only, for a different per-file family invariant). Unresolvable arguments resolve to None = "no opinion", never "too small", so it is a FLOOR and never manufactures false offenders.

IT IS A RATCHET, NOT A SWEEP — and this is the part to respect if you touch it. 61 pre-existing in-band sites across 19 modules are grandfathered in `_GRANDFATHERED`, keyed by (module, qualname): per-SITE and NOT a per-file count, because a count nets to zero when one marker is added and another removed in the same file, leaving a hole in a guard whose whole purpose is catching accidental additions. Entries may only ever be REMOVED; a stale-entry twin test fails on any entry that no longer names a real in-band site, so the list cannot rot into a permanent blanket exemption. The 61 were NOT migrated in 5147 on purpose: they live in the hottest files in the repo (test_merge_queue.py and its deep_* siblings, test_crash_recovery.py), so rewriting ~20 files at once would have taken locks on nearly everything in-flight fleet tasks were editing and risked destabilising the very verify path the task existed to de-flake. entry_text: To assert an orchestrator conftest fixture's runtime effect from tests/scripts/ (which never collects orchestrator/tests/conftest.py), load the conftest with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under a UNIQUE module name (never 'conftest'), take getattr(fixture, '__wrapped__', fixture) (pytest 9 FixtureFunctionDefinition), and call it with the test's own monkeypatch/tmp_path. Executing that conftest has import-time side effects: it inserts five sys.path entries (orchestrator/tests at the front), setdefaults ORCH_DEBUG_ASSERTS, sets worker._DEBUG_ASSERTS and patches AsyncMockMixin. Contain the first two with monkeypatch.setattr(sys, 'path', [*sys.path]) and monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_DEBUG_ASSERTS', ...) before exec_module. Worked example: tests/scripts/test_config_retune_gate_decision.py::_exec_orchestrator_conftest (task 3886); full tests/scripts/ stayed green with it.
target_text: To assert what a pytest autouse fixture DOES at runtime from a test in ANOTHER package — distinct from asserting it is merely registered, which is memory e5ebdf0d — load the owning conftest by path with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` plus `exec_module` under a UNIQUE module name (never the bare name `conftest`; sibling conftests collide in `sys.modules`), then resolve `fn = getattr(mod._fixture, '__wrapped__', mod._fixture)` and call it with a real `monkeypatch` and `tmp_path`, asserting the side effect it left. Measured on task 3886 under pytest 9.0.3: `__wrapped__` is present on `FixtureFunctionDefinition`. Two things keep it non-vacuous — call `monkeypatch.delenv(VAR, raising=False)` FIRST so an ambient value cannot pass the assertion for you, and guard with `if hasattr(r, '__next__'): next(r)` so a later conversion to a yield-fixture does not silently no-op it. Exec'ing `orchestrator/tests/conftest.py` this way inserts 5 sys.path entries but was measured NOT to shadow imports for the rest of a tests/scripts session (full suite stayed green with it present). THE LESSON THAT MOTIVATED IT: a guard claiming to protect a conftest fixture's contract, but which only loads config through the production loader, actually tests pydantic-settings LAYER PRECEDENCE and not the fixture — it stays green under the exact fixture edit it claims to catch. Validate such a guard by mutating the FIXTURE, not the data it points at.

entry_text: Three reify tasks carry mis-authored delivered_checks of the MODE-3 shape: a file-existence capability written as kind=grep over file contents, where the pattern is the declared file's own name. A delivered_check CAN PASS GREEN WHILE THE CAPABILITY ITS DEPENDENTS NEED IS ABSENT — two live instances found on reify in one session, 2026-09-21. Treat "dep is done" as unverified until you read the check itself.

INSTANCE 1, a check that tests the wrong thing. `registry-threads-real-dependent-cells` in docs/prds/v0_6/discrete-cost-minimisation.capability-manifest.yaml is an UNSCOPED whole-file grep for `dependent_cells:\s*Vec::new\(\)` over crates/reify-constraints/src/registry.rs with `expect: absent`. Its single match is at registry.rs:1424, inside the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` that opens at line 1371 — task 5467's OWN test fixture. The production site threads the real fold at registry.rs:666 (`dependent_cells: sub_dependent_cells`). Byte-identical on current main and on the cited sha, so this was mis-scoped since 5467 landed, not drift. It falsely blocked FOUR critical tasks (5469, 6077, 6207, 6431) for ~20h. Fix filed as task #7739. LESSON: an `expect: absent` grep over a whole file asserts a global negative that any future test fixture can break; prefer a POSITIVE assertion on the production symbol.

INSTANCE 2, a check that cannot observe the omission. Task #5436's delivered_checks were three greps — `world_frame`, `E_POSE_CYCLE`, `fn build_dependent_cells`. A #5436 that ships §7.1.2-7.1.3 (.world_frame member, in_frame builtin, staged placement eval) and quietly skips §7.1.5 (the carried-frame member read) passes all three GREEN while leaving dependent task #6683 exactly as stranded as if nothing had been built. Closed 2026-09-21 by adding a fourth check `carried-frame-cross-sub-geometry-read` (grep `cross_sub` on crates/reify-eval/tests, expect present).

GENERAL RULE: when re-pointing a dependency onto a task, read that task's delivered_checks and confirm at least one is bound to the specific capability the dependent needs. Otherwise the edge is decorative and the strand just moves.

Completed: Negative-assertion tests that pass for the wrong reason when a config default flips: invisible to both the AST ratchet and the adversarial-config sweep
Description: Filed by task 4481's implementer as out-of-scope follow-up work. No escalation record; discovered by inspection while executing task 4481's steps 8-10.

BACKGROUND. Task 4481 swept orchestrator/tests for tests that depend on an UNDECLARED config key's package code default, using two detectors: a committed AST ratchet (static) and a scratch adversarial-config harness (dynamic — a test green with the real yaml and red under a yaml that perturbs every undeclared key is depending on a code default by definition).

THE GAP. Both detectors are blind to a test whose assertion is NEGATIVE — "this env var is absent", "this callback did not fire", "this flag was not injected". When the root key flips, the behaviour under test is disabled, the negative assertion becomes trivially true, and the test PASSES. It passes for the wrong reason: it is no longer exercising anything. The dynamic harness cannot see it (it only reports failures), and the AST ratchet cannot see it (there is no equality-against-a-default to match).

MEASURED INSTANCES (all observed green under the adversarial config during task 4481, each in a class whose sibling POSITIVE tests went red from the same single root key, which is what makes the reading concrete rather than speculative):
- orchestrator/tests/test_verify_admission_pytest_n.py::TestPytestNWiring::test_merge_role_excluded_from_dash_n_injection and ::test_env_recovery_rerun_is_not_dash_n_injected — both assert '-n 16' is NOT present; root key verify_admission_enabled, which when false means nothing is ever injected for any role.
- orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_e2e.py::TestBuildAgentEnvCpuGovern::test_governance_disabled_by_default_no_df_agent_cpu_govern — asserts DF_AGENT_CPU_GOVERN absent; survives cpu_governance.enabled being flipped to true because the exec-path resolution then fails open.

DETECTING (not repairing) dark-factory tests that depend on package code defaults: perturb the WHOLE config at once, then diff against a baseline. The repair idiom is already known (@pytest.mark.usefixtures('code_default_config') on the one test); this is how to FIND every site in one run instead of one key at a time.

METHOD, measured working on task 4481 at main tip 13ff3d630f. Load OrchestratorConfig with ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at an absent path to get package defaults, walk every leaf field (390 at that SHA), subtract the keys already declared in dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml (41) — the remaining ~349 are the landmine surface. Write a non-default value for each into a COPY of the operational yaml: bool -> negate, int -> +7 then +1 then -1, float -> +0.25 then +0.01. Keep each perturbation ONLY if OrchestratorConfig() still validates with it, applied incrementally — several fields carry pydantic bounds or model validators (steward_max_timeouts_per_escalation <= 5, steward_max_empty_outputs_per_escalation <= 4, sccache.enabled requires a non-empty backend_env), and a naive bulk perturbation dies with a ValidationError. That yields ~254 perturbed and ~2 unperturbable. Skip str and list fields — they are enums/paths/model-names and mostly unsafe to perturb blindly, which is why this technique needs the AST complement below.

Then cp the yaml aside, `trap` the restore on EXIT/INT/TERM, swap the adversarial copy in (the autouse _isolate_orch_config hardcodes REPO_ROOT/dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, so you must swap the FILE — setting ORCH_CONFIG_PATH externally does nothing), run the suite, restore, then run the SAME file set unperturbed. THE AUTHORITATIVE RESULT IS THE SET DIFFERENCE adversarial MINUS baseline, never the raw adversarial list: on task 4481 the raw counts were 79 vs 3 failures, and those 3 were pre-existing main-reds that would have been mis-attributed as landmines. Measured net: 76 tests / 12 files, in ~5 minutes per run under -n 8.

TWO CLASSES, NEEDING TWO DETECTORS. The dynamic sweep finds tests that merely EXERCISE default-only behaviour and assert no config literal at all (e.g. flipping verify_admission_enabled disables a code path so an xdist flag is never injected — surfacing as `assert '-n 16' in 'pytest tests/'`, with no config assertion anywhere to grep for). It MISSES str/list defaults you declined to perturb. A complementary AST scan finds those: flag a test iff it binds a name to a BARE OrchestratorConfig(), is not isolated, and asserts that name's attribute path == a literal equal to the package default. Validate such a scanner against a KNOWN red — on 4481 it independently rediscovered task 3886's exemplar (test_verify.py merge_config_only_full_gate_globs == [], a list default the perturbation could not reach).

TRIAGE PER TEST, NEVER PER FILE. The natural heuristic — "files containing a bare OrchestratorConfig() that never mention code_default_config" — is wrong and drops the worst offenders, because a file that uses the hatch ANYWHERE is excluded while still harbouring unhatched landmines elsewhere. On 4481 it excluded exactly test_config.py (15 landmine tests, the largest single concentration) and test_verify.py (the motivating exemplar itself).

Any such scanner must treat the two ad-hoc idioms as valid isolation or it will false-positive: monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', '') (154 live uses) and monkeypatch.delenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', raising=False) (29), versus only 26 uses of the sanctioned mark.

Jev (TypeSafe jev-1.13.0) measured behaviour on write-triage inputs (2026-09-29 trial, ~1,600 calls):

- Reliability: 0 errors, 0 retries, no parse failures (typed output). gpt-4o-mini fails open on a truncated candidate uuid ~1% of the time.
- Latency: p50 0.26 s / p95 0.37 s for an 11-question request at N=5; 0.41 / 0.52 s for 41 questions at N=20. gpt-4o-mini is 0.87–0.96 / 1.06–1.26 s.
- Cost and size (input tokens only, at USD 0.042/Mtok):
  - full fan-out at 1,200-char elision: ~8k tokens (USD 0.00034/write) at N=5, ~30k (USD 0.00126) at N=20;
  - a per-pair relation question at 4,000 chars: ~2.5k tokens.
- A 20-slate fits Jev's budgets when each candidate is placed in its own question's instructions and the state holds only the new entry, because the 32k cap applies to the state plus the longest single question. This corrects the earlier concern that a 20-slate exceeds the state cap.
- Its `match` choice over the slate is order-sensitive: reversing or shuffling the slate changes the pick in 12–19% of writes, though misfile rates are unchanged. Re-asking in the same order gives the same pick 97–99% of the time.
- The `none` option works on true distractors (18/18 stored at N=5, 17/18 at N=20), but P(none) is ~0 on real fixture slates.
- As a slate orderer, fixture canonical at rank 1 was 28/84 (cosine 16, bge 32).
target_text: Jev (TypeSafe AI, typesafe.ai; researched 2026-09-22/23 for esc-3169-1 at Leo's request): a non-autoregressive "System One" model released in limited early access 2026-09-15 ($40M seed led by DCVC; founders Diogo Almeida, Erik Gafni, Sasha Sheng; no technical report or weights). API: POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone with a `state` (text/JSON) plus typed `questions`: `noul` (yes/no → probability), `choice` (one of up to 255 options → top choice + full distribution + confidence), `score` (rubric). No text generation. Budgets: 64k tokens per request, 32k for state + longest question. Price $0.042/M input, output free; latency 70–500 ms (third parties measure ~370–440 ms). Stated weaknesses: negation, indirect reasoning, "context rot" with irrelevant state, option-order sensitivity; all benchmarks self-reported (the 193.6x/444.6x figures are against frontier models; one independent test measured ~16% in a pipeline). Python SDK typesafe-sdk, Pydantic AI and Cloudflare Workers AI integrations. RELEVANCE VERDICT for the write-triage problem: it bears on exactly one sub-problem — the judge's output contract (a `choice` over the slate is option (a), a candidate-bound verdict, by output type) and latency — and not on retrieval recall, the fixture gaps, or the topic guard. Against gpt-4o-mini the input-price gain is ~3.6x, not a discriminator; a 20-candidate slate at the corpus's worst case (~60k tokens) exceeds the 32k state cap. The same binding is available from gpt-4o-mini structured output (task 5794) or a local cross-encoder with no vendor and no order sensitivity, so Jev has to beat those on the fixture, not the status quo. Adding it as a third judge provider arm touches seven functions (_KNOWN_PROVIDERS, resolve_judge_provider, _provider_credentials, _call_llm, build_judge_prompt, parse_judge_verdict, tests) plus the LLMConfig.provider literal. Filed as task 5809 (ν), DEFERRED, promoted only by gate Γ3's fail branch when the residual is the judge and a key exists.

LLM call:
- shared/cli_invoke.py::invoke_with_cap_retry runs the Claude CLI over OAuth and strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env returns 401, so the CLI is the only working route to an Anthropic model today.
- Pattern: call it with output_schema, no tools, no MCP servers, and shared/neutral_cwd.py::neutral_cli_cwd. Precedents are middleware/path_scope_adjudicator.py::PathScopeAdjudicator and reconciliation/judge.py::Judge._call_judge_cli; fused-memory/scripts/probe_schema_max_turns.py is a standalone-script precedent.
- The structured output may arrive as a JSON string; handle both.

Escalations:
- middleware/_folded_escalation.py::file_folded_escalation(project_root, anchor_task_id=…) files into a project's queue from any process.
- It folds every new record into the open escalation under the same anchor. Give each storm condition its own anchor, registered in fused-memory/tests/test_folded_escalation.py::TestNoTwoFilersShareAnAnchor, or a later storm is silently absorbed.

target_text: fused-memory declares BOTH `openai>=1.91.0` and `anthropic>=0.52.0` in pyproject.toml, but only OPENAI_API_KEY is actually set in the dark-factory deployment — CLAUDE.md states ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is deliberately NOT needed because agents use OAuth. entry_text: Merge-lane ratchet, measured by scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py: ANY file under orchestrator/tests that imports a cluster module (git_ops, merge_queue, …) is swept for private_reads. A NEW such test file contributes to the summed total:private_reads, so it must keep `obj._attr` attribute accesses at 0 or the ratchet reddens. A name import like `from orchestrator.git_ops import _run` is NOT counted, because only ast.Attribute nodes are, and self/cls receivers are exempt. Because test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement demands baseline == fresh measurement, ANY count change in a swept file (even a decrease) forces a baseline regeneration, so new tests are cheapest in a non-swept file.

Verified at reify c09a26b5b1: the pool path buffers each member's stdout+stderr to its own workdir file and REPLAYS it in Phase 3 in discovered order under its own header (`_ra_emit_sanitized "$_H2_WORKDIR/${i}.out"`, run_all.sh:1770-1810); the legacy serial path (:1838-1852) emits the same framing inline. A PASS close may carry a trailing ` [flaky: passed on serial retry]` suffix (:1792) and a retried member's block contains `--- attempt 1 (concurrent pool) ---` / `--- attempt 2 (serial retry) ---` delimiters, deliberately shaped NOT to match `^--- Running: ` so the one-header-per-discovered-test contract holds. Gotcha that makes this load-bearing: DF's verify_classify guard-3 host-infra detectors are handed the WHOLE aggregated run_all output, so a PASSING suite that EXECUTES a real emitter (e.g. reify test_lane_x_flock.sh Tests 13/15 and test_test_run_semaphore.sh HG-2, which print genuine column-0 `failed to acquire ... within 0s/1s` lines) mislabels the whole run SEMAPHORE_TIMEOUT. Line-anchoring cannot separate those from production lines — they are byte-identical — only the enclosing PASS attestation can. Any DF parser scoping by these markers must require the OPEN and CLOSE suite names to MATCH, so a suite that replays a run_all transcript cannot close (and thus swallow) an outer block; every ambiguous shape must degrade to whole-output behaviour.

entry_text: GOTCHA (fused-memory tests): two throwaway repos built with tests/_fm_helpers.py::_init_git_repo in the same second get the SAME commit sha. The helper always commits an identical seed.txt with a fixed author and message, so tree, parent, identity and timestamp all match. Any test that needs "this sha exists in repo B but not in repo A" (e.g. a cross-repo commit-probe test) then passes vacuously. Fix without touching the helper: mkdir the second repo first and write a per-repo file (e.g. repo-name.txt) before calling _init_git_repo, so `git add -A` commits a different tree, and assert the two shas differ. Task 4853 hit this in its make_registry_commit_probe tests; the plan's suggested 'git init + --allow-empty commit' fixture has the same flaw.
target_text: Gotcha when writing orchestrator tests that must simulate a rebase orphaning a commit and replaying it as a DIFFERENT sha: `git reset --hard <base>` followed by re-committing identical content and an identical message can produce the SAME sha, because a git commit hash depends on tree + parent + author/committer identity and timestamp, and a fast test run reuses the same one-second timestamp. Such a test goes vacuously green (the "orphan" is still reachable). Use the `git switch -c tmpbase <base>` + unrelated commit + `git rebase --onto tmpbase <base>` technique from orchestrator/tests/test_reconcile_done_step_commits.py:1002 instead — the different parent chain guarantees new shas — and assert the original really is orphaned with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <orig> HEAD` returning non-zero.

entry_text: reify-test-support's value-cell lookup family (crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs, re-exported at the crate root) returns the full ValueCellDecl, so tests needing cell_type/kind/visibility need not hand-roll `templates[0].value_cells.iter().find(|vc| vc.id.member == ..)`. Pick by what you hold: get_value_cell(module, name) for the first template, get_value_cell_in(module, template, name) for a named template, get_value_cell_of(&template, name) for a template you already hold, and try_get_value_cell_of(&template, name) -> Option to assert absence (it still panics on an ambiguous member). The get_let_expr* siblings return only default_expr and panic on a defaultless cell (task #6973).
target_text: reify-test-support value-cell lookup naming (task #6973): the suffix encodes the argument shape across both families — bare `get_value_cell(module, cell)` / `get_let_expr(module, cell)` = module's FIRST template; `_in(module, template_name, cell)` = named template in a module; `_in_template(&TopologyTemplate, cell)` = a template you already hold (e.g. from compile_first_template). `try_get_value_cell_in_template` is the tolerant Option variant and THE single ambiguity-guarded walk; its rustdoc is the one home of the ambiguity contract. Do not add an `_of` or other suffix for the held-template shape.

entry_text: ASYNCIO TEST GOTCHA (task 6079, measured on CPython 3.13.9, 20 runs per cell). To show a host stall expiring a deadline on a REAL loop, run `async with asyncio.timeout(0.05): time.sleep(0.1); await asyncio.sleep(0)`. Do not expect a TimeoutError from it: the body returns normally 20/20. The resumed task step is queued ahead of the newly-due timeout callback, so the task leaves the timeout context before the callback runs. A timed post-stall wait such as `await asyncio.sleep(0.001)` makes the loop process the overdue timer first and raises TimeoutError 20/20. Use that form whenever a test needs to discriminate real-clock from virtual-clock behaviour (see dashboard/tests/test_virtual_clock_helpers.py).
target_text: DASHBOARD DEADLINE-RACE FLAKES (task 6079, measured 2026-09-30). The shape: a fan-out test gives a HEALTHY project and a slow project (slow_ports={port: 0.5}) ONE shared per_call_timeout=0.05, then asserts the healthy one read. Its cold MockTransport MCP handshake (3 posts) takes about 6.6ms idle, so a loaded xdist worker stalled for more than 50ms turns it None. That is correct production behaviour, and a synchronous time.sleep(0.06) in the healthy handler reproduces the red deterministically. Fix without widening any value by running the unchanged scenario on an idle-autojump virtual clock. Use an asyncio.SelectorEventLoop subclass whose time() reads a counter, plus a selectors.DefaultSelector subclass whose select(timeout>0) adds timeout to that counter and polls with select(0). Drive it with asyncio.Runner(loop_factory=...) from a sync test. Host stalls can then never expire a deadline, and timer order stays exact. It works on CPython 3.13 and 3.14 and under pytest-asyncio 1.3 auto mode beside async tests. Task 6079 adds it as dashboard/tests/_virtual_clock_helpers.py::run_on_virtual_clock. It fits in-loop scenarios only; real sockets or executor threads race the jump. The same latent race is in test_task_runtime.py (2 tests), test_merge_halt.py and test_merge_queue_data.py, filed as ticket tkt_0RV862T8K2BDD34QKN2KXZ2DDY.

entry_text: Reify merge-gate trap (task 7981): crates/reify-eval/src/engine_hash_algo.rs no longer has CONTRIBUTORS_RELATIVE. It was replaced by WORKSPACE_CRATE_COVERAGE, which has one row per workspace PATH crate in reify-eval's dependency closure: Coverage::Hashed(paths) or NotHashed(NotHashedBecause::{UpstreamOfPersistentKey, RealizationProducer, NotOnAPersistedDispatchPath}). The ENGINE_VERSION_HASH computation itself is now engine_hash_algo::engine_version_hash_for(manifest_dir); build.rs only prints its result. Two traps follow. (1) Adding a dependency that pulls a new workspace path crate into reify-eval's closure fails engine_hash_tests::every_path_crate_in_the_engine_hash_closure_is_classified until you add a row. (2) Adding a 4th entry to compute_persist::PERSISTABLE_TARGETS fails persisted_target_sources_cover_exactly_the_persistable_targets until you list its source files in engine_hash_tests.rs's PERSISTED_TARGET_SOURCES.
target_text:
Reify merge-gate trap: adding a Cargo dependency to ANY crate reachable from reify-eval — including indirect ones like reify-compiler, which is a normal dep of reify-eval — requires regenerating the checked-in closure manifest crates/reify-eval/engine_hash_closure.txt in the SAME branch, or tests/infra/test_engine_hash_closure.sh fails the merge gate with "FAIL: manifest is a superset of the live closure (no member missing)".

The non-obvious hop: you can red this guard without touching reify-eval at all. Task 5337 added `stacker` to crates/reify-compiler/Cargo.toml and that alone pulled FOUR new names into reify-eval's closure — `stacker`, its `psm` dep, plus `ar_archive_writer` and `object` reached via cc's BUILD-dep chain (the closure is `-e no-dev`, so build-deps count; only dev-deps are excluded). Budget for transitive build-dep fan-out, not just the crate you named.

Fix is mechanical: regenerate the manifest's data section with the canonical command documented verbatim in the manifest header and duplicated in the guard (the two MUST stay byte-identical for the superset check to be meaningful):
  cargo tree -p reify-eval -e no-dev --prefix none --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --frozen -f '{p}' | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u
Preserve the header comment block; append names in sorted position. Never REMOVE a name — the manifest is required to be a superset (⊇) of the live closure, and over-approximation is the deliberately-sanctioned safe direction (G6).

Why the guard is not noise: ENGINE_VERSION_HASH narrows its Cargo.lock contribution to only the resolved (name, version) pins of the crate NAMES in this manifest. A real closure member MISSING from the manifest means a later version bump of that crate would NOT invalidate the persistent FEA cache — silent under-invalidation producing stale, possibly-incorrect FEA results.

Expect and accept a one-time FEA cache invalidation after the edit: ENGINE_VERSION_HASH changes, which is exactly the intended behaviour when the shipped engine's dependency closure genuinely changes. No golden-hash test breaks — compose_engine_version_hash_pins_fixed_input_to_exact_hex_literal pins a SYNTHETIC fixed input, not the live closure.

Cheap pre-merge self-check (seconds, no compile — cargo tree --frozen is resolve-only): run `bash tests/infra/test_engine_hash_closure.sh` locally on any branch that touches a Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock, rather than discovering the drift in post-merge verify.

entry_text: Host load profile, from data/load-samples.db (metric runqueue_ratio = runnable tasks per core; 5 s cadence; populated since 2026-09-20; PSI avg10 only, no loadavg column). In 2026-09-25..28 the median was about 2.9 and p90 about 7.2 on the 32-core host. Bursts of 15-37 runnable per core (about 500-1100 runnable tasks) lasting 1-3 minutes recur every 30-60 minutes around the clock. CPU PSI some avg10 sits at a median of about 56%, so PSI does not distinguish the moments crashes happen. What causes the bursts has NOT been measured. The sampler's `verify_concurrency` and `verify_rss_total_bytes` metrics are dead (always 0.0); use runs.db phase intervals as a proxy.
target_text: CPU PSI `some` avg10 has no stable admission threshold on this saturated 32-core host, because the variable SATURATES: its whole distribution slides upward with load rather than spreading out, so it tracks load instead of discriminating it. Two 1 Hz samples on the same host three days apart barely overlap — 2026-07-31 at load ~85: min 5.5 / med 46.3 / p90 60.8 / max 68.9 (n=720); 2026-08-03 at load ~190: min 62.2 / med 66.8 / p90 71.2 / max 74.1 (n=229). Fraction of ticks a gate would HOLD, quiet-day vs busy-day: threshold 55 -> 22.2%/100%, 60 -> 13.9%/100%, 65 -> 1.9%/68.1%, 70 -> 0.0%/13.5%, 75 -> 0%/0%. Every value below 62 is a total gate on a busy day; every value above 69 is dead on a quiet one. The shipped PsiAdmissionConfig default of 85.0 has NEVER fired here (observed max 74.1). Also note CPU PSI `full` is ALWAYS 0.00 by kernel definition (something is always runnable), so only `some` is usable for CPU at all. The runqueue ratio is the right control variable instead: 2.4x cores on the quiet sample vs 7.1x on the busy one — ~3x separation where CPU PSI gives ~1.4x.

entry_text: In reify tests/infra/*.sh files that run under `set -euo pipefail`, a derive-from-source scrape written with grep (`grep -o`, `grep -c`) inside `$(...)` ABORTS THE WHOLE FILE when it matches nothing (grep rc 1 + pipefail), instead of failing a non-vacuity assert — so a drifted/renamed Rust symbol kills the suite silently-ish rather than reding one assertion. Write derivations with `sed -n 's/.../\1/p'` and `awk '{ n += gsub(/pat/, "&") } END { print n + 0 }'` (both exit 0 on a miss), and skip empty derived values in probe loops with `[ -n "$x" ] || continue`, since e.g. plan_for_branch "" aborts on `printf > "$FIX_B/"`. Verify by pointing the derivation at /dev/null under `set -euo pipefail`. Precedent: PDOCCOVER-DRIFT in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh (task 7987).
target_text: In tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh (all `set -euo pipefail`), a TOP-LEVEL capture whose pipeline ends in a possibly-non-matching grep — e.g. `NLINE="$(printf '%s\n' "$PLAN" | grep -E "(^| )cargo nextest run " | head -1)"` — ABORTS the whole file at that line when the grep misses (pipefail makes the substitution nonzero; set -e kills the script), with no per-assert diagnostic and no test_summary. This silently kills every later test in the file AND makes downstream `if [ "$NEXTEST_AVAILABLE" -eq 1 ]` / `-n` guards dead code, since the abort happens BEFORE the guard. It bites on hosts without cargo-nextest, where verify.sh gracefully emits `cargo test` instead of `cargo nextest run` (scripts/verify.sh:1377) — latent on the merge-gate host, which has nextest. Fix: append `|| true` (the idiom already used by the surrounding captures, e.g. test_verify_retry_subset.sh:75/:354/:419). Captures inside `bash -c '…'` assert bodies are NOT affected (that subshell has no set -e). Surveyed 2026-07-26 at d34278cffc: ~23 unguarded sites across test_verify_role_prio.sh (12), _semaphore_wiring (4), _offline_partition (2), _semaphore_e2e (2), _compile_gate/_retry_failed_only/_test_threads (1 each).

entry_text: reify persistent FEA cache key composition (verified main 93b5d91a0d, task 7981): engine_eval.rs `persistent_cache_key` = compute_cache_key(node) combined with each evaluated argument Value's content_hash, so argument-value changes re-key. Realization inputs are keyed by RECIPE only (graph.rs RealizationNodeData.content_hash = id_hash ⊕ ops_hash), so a change in realization-producer code (OCCT/OpenVDB/gmsh output, native libs) never reaches the key. The shell-extract upstream node (engine_eval.rs ~:10029) uses bare compute_cache_key on an input-less node, so its key is the target string alone. Code running inside a persisted dispatch must therefore be covered by ENGINE_VERSION_HASH.
target_text: In reify-eval, a ComputeNode's at-rest `node.cache_key` is NOT the bare `compute_cache_key(node, graph)` — both @optimized dispatch sites in engine_eval.rs store `Engine::persistent_cache_key`, which folds the order-dependent `ContentHash::combine_all` over the ORDERED full `arg_values` list. `compute_cache_key`'s value bucket is deliberately order-blind AND (since #6661) duplicate-collapsing, so argument POSITION and multiplicity are carried only by that outer fold. When reasoning about whether two designs get distinct cache keys, read persistent_cache_key, not compute_cache_key.

entry_text: A pyright pragma is vestigial only if BOTH type gates agree. A green run of a member's declared gate (`uv run --directory <member> pyright src/ tests/`) is not enough. Task verify scopes that gate to the changed files: verify_cmd.py::promote_cwd_to_project and strip_cwd render it as `uv run --project <member> pyright <member>/tests/x.py`, run from the REPO ROOT, so it reads the ROOT pyproject's [tool.pyright]. Measured in task 5090: fused-memory/tests/test_cgl_eta_finalize_gate.py imports the fused-memory/scripts module `cgl_eta_finalize_gate`. That path is in fused-memory's own extraPaths ("scripts") but not in the root's. Removing its `# pyright: ignore[reportMissingImports]` passed the declared gate (0 errors) and failed scoped verify with 1 reportMissingImports. So before calling a pragma vestigial, re-run the scoped root-cwd form as well: `uv run --project <member> pyright <member>/tests/<file>.py` from the repo root.
target_text: fused-memory's pyright is intentionally scoped: `fused-memory/pyproject.toml` has `[tool.pyright] include = ["src", "tests"]` — so `fused-memory/scripts/*.py` is NOT type-checked by the project's pyright gate. When run from the repo root (wrong CWD/config), pyright reports `Import "escalation.queue" could not be resolved (reportMissingImports)` for scripts in `fused-memory/scripts/` — but the identical error fires on the ALREADY-MERGED `backfill_recon_escalations.py`, so it's an invocation-context artifact, not a real verification failure. From `fused-memory/`'s context, `escalation` resolves via `extraPaths = [..., "../escalation/src"]` and the workspace dep `escalation = { workspace = true }`.
