orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::_main_probe_failure_is_isolated_flake IS NOT A DEBUGGER SUPPRESSOR, and the docstring of ::_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash misleads a reader into thinking it is. Established 2026-09-21; the misleading prose is still on main.

THE DOCSTRING CLAIM: "The opposite-direction case — a load flake co-occurring with the crash, whose ``FAILED`` line defeats this veto — is deliberately NOT fixed by exempting named tests here: no test is exempt. See ``_main_probe_failure_is_isolated_flake`` (task 3597) for the downstream confirm gate that catches it instead."

WHY IT DOES NOT CATCH IT.
- The gate lives inside ::verify_failure_is_preexisting_on_main, the broken-main CONTAGION GUARD, which workflow.py::WorkflowEngine._verify_debugfix_loop calls before invoking the DEBUGGER.
- It is reachable in principle on the task lane: junit production is gated `role == 'merge'` and full breadth, role='task' is a literal at workflow.py::_run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry, and the multi-module aggregate is None iff every child is — so failing_test_ids is always None there and the task-mu early-return fork is NOT taken. (plans/flake-ledger-prd.md §3.2's "this gate is unreachable" verdict is true for MERGE-role callers only.)
- But it only fires when the MAIN PROBE is ALSO red with a MATCHING (category, normalised cause_hint) signature. For a one-off branch crash against a green main, the caller returns early at `if main_result.passed: return False, ''` and the gate is never called.
- And when it DOES fire it returns "not inherited", which sends the task TO the debugger. Its purpose is to prevent a FALSE "main is broken" verdict, not to prevent a debugger invocation.

IT ALSO LEAVES NO DURABLE TRACE: it never sets VerifyResult.flake_suppression, so it never writes a flake_occurrence row. Its only observable output is a WARNING containing "passed on isolated re-run on the main probe" — and there are ZERO hits for that string across journald and /var/log/syslog plus four rotations. Coverage is non-contiguous, so read that as SUPPORTED, not PROVEN.

This is the one genuine defect esc-5580-4 surfaced. It was not fixed under the 2026-09-21 ruling (Leo actioned only tasks 5089 and 5741), so the misleading citation remains in the docstring.

entry_text: Stamped peer under topic pytest-xdist-serial-override — an OUTPUT-SHAPE gotcha for anyone asserting on a NESTED pytest run's text, distinct from the canonical's serial-override/fixture-loss/crash-flake modes. (1) Under `--dist loadgroup`, a test marked @pytest.mark.xdist_group('g') has its nodeid suffixed `@g` in xdist's crash line ("worker 'gw1' crashed while running 'mod.py::test_x@g'") and in -rA PASSED/FAILED summary lines, so a regex ending `::test_x'` silently misses; allow `(@[^']*)?`. (2) With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" banner goes to the dead worker's stderr and is NOT relayed by the controller, so `'Timeout' in output` is false for a thread-method kill even though the test was killed by the cap. Measured on pytest 9.0.3 / xdist 3.8.0 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0, task 5470 (tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py).

Orchestrator/fused-memory pytest-xdist gotcha (canonical, merges bbe45a4f's 6 prior entries + 6d203bd5 + 0ebfcaa7): orchestrator/pyproject.toml and fused-memory/pyproject.toml hardcode `-n auto --dist loadgroup --max-worker-restart=0` in [tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts. Passing `-p no:xdist` on the CLI to force serial execution FAILS with "unrecognized arguments: -n --dist --max-worker-restart=0" — pytest parses addopts AFTER the plugin is disabled, so xdist's own CLI options are no longer registered to consume those flags.

IMPORTANT nuance (corrects a prior contradiction between two merged entries): BOTH cross-file selection styles can spuriously report "no tests ran" (or "file or directory not found") under `--dist loadgroup`, even though the tests collect fine — this is a pytest-xdist + custom-reporter quirk, not reliably avoided by switching between styles: (a) multiple fully-qualified `path::Class::test` node IDs spanning files, and (b) a cross-file `-k "name_a or name_b"` keyword filter spanning multiple test files. Do NOT treat "switch from node-IDs to -k" or "switch from -k to node-IDs" as a dependable fix — either selection style can fail depending on collection/grouping, and one entry's "use -k instead" previously contradicted another's "use node-ID instead."

The ONE reliably robust workaround is `-n0`, which cleanly overrides addopts' `-n auto` (last `-n` wins) and forces serial execution without touching plugin registration (~1s startup for a single in-process test; xdist still pays ~27-30s worker-pool startup even for one selected test under the default distributed mode — expected overhead, not a hang/regression). Example: `python -m pytest tests/<file>::<Class>::<test> -n0`. Note the Bash tool's cwd can drift between calls — prefix pytest invocations with an explicit `cd <pkg-dir> &&`. Contrast: the escalation/ package has NO forced xdist in its addopts, so targeted runs there are fast and accept `-p no:xdist` / normal flags without issue.

SECOND, DISTINCT `-p no:xdist` failure mode: silent FIXTURE loss (task 3875). The above covers `-p no:xdist` erroring with "unrecognized arguments: -n --dist" when addopts still carries `-n auto`. This is the OTHER case: pairing `-p no:xdist` with `-o addopts=` clears addopts so that error does NOT fire, but unregistering the plugin also removes its FIXTURES. `worker_id` is supplied solely by pytest-xdist, so every test requesting it ERRORs at setup ("fixture 'worker_id' not found") and no assertion body runs. `orchestrator.verify._serial_pytest_str` appends exactly `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` for the offline-deep lane's red-path confirm re-run — that is how 14 fused-memory tests across 5 files were reported "failing" and mis-attributed to an unrelated suspect commit.

FIXED ON MAIN 2026-08-24 for fused-memory — task 3875 landed at main 7169009858 (until then this entry described the remedy only prospectively). `worker_id` IS now defined in the SUBPROJECT test-root conftest, fused-memory/tests/conftest.py (the lane runs `cd fused-memory && pytest tests/`, so rootdir is the subproject and the repo-root conftest.py is never loaded), session-scoped to match xdist's own scope, and delegates to `resolve_xdist_worker_id` in fused-memory/tests/_fm_helpers.py, which calls `xdist.plugin.get_xdist_worker_id` through a FUNCTION-LOCAL import — the xdist MODULE stays importable when only the PLUGIN is unregistered, so delegation works in exactly the broken case and cannot drift from xdist's semantics when xdist is healthy. Regression guard: fused-memory/tests/test_worker_id_fixture.py, whose `test_worker_id_survives_the_lanes_serial_confirm_rerun` spawns a NESTED pytest under the lane's exact `-p no:xdist -o addopts=` flags — an in-process assertion cannot catch this class of bug, because the outer run already holds the fixture the child lacks.

SCOPE OF THAT FIX — fused-memory ONLY. The fixture lives in fused-memory's own test-root conftest, not a shared/repo-root one (the repo-root con…[truncated, 6528 chars total]

Tier 3 is the only gate (tier 2 narrows to a bare TypeParam only). Owned by leaf β (task 8014) of the generic-enum-type-arg-retention PRD: β must NARROW tier 3 so a headed arg needs heads_unifiable, otherwise δ (construction emitting Applied with placeholders) would widen the hole to every partly-bound construction. target_text: MEASURED 2026-10-02 (task 8014 β architect, scratch build, reverted afterwards): this narrowing of reify-core `slot_matches_wildcard_tier`'s arg-side disjunct is behaviour-safe on main. Evidence: across 7687 reify-core/expr/compiler tests, only 2 failed, both pins of the S-4 hole (`slot_matches_wildcard_tier_accepts_a_type_param_carrying_arg`, reify-expr `headed_type_param_arg_resolves_a_non_generic_concrete_candidate`). entry_text: The merge-lane ratchet (orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json) measures two populations differently. CLUSTER paths (listed under 'files', e.g. orchestrator/tests/conftest.py, merge_queue.py) are ratcheted on cognitive, lines, prose_lines, function_local_imports and reexport_names, so any added line needs --authorize-raise. Every other .py under orchestrator/tests is ratcheted only on private_reads and patch_targets (the 'tests' section). Adding a test or a comment to a non-cluster test file therefore needs no authorization, as long as it reads no private names and adds no patch targets. Measured 2026-09-29.
target_text:
Merge-lane ratchet property (measured 2026-09-22 on HEAD ea47bfb5ec, task 5034/delta): DELETING a file that is a CLUSTER_PATHS member is coupled into a single commit by three separate mechanisms, and doing it in stages breaks the instrument rather than the gate.

(1) scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::CLUSTER_PATHS lists some members as LITERAL paths and one as a glob. Its own comment states the asymmetry: "a glob matching nothing is NOT a failure; a literal matching nothing is." So `git rm`-ing a literal member without editing CLUSTER_PATHS makes the instrument exit 2 (MetricsError / incomplete enumeration), which is categorically different from exit 1 "the tree regressed" — you get a broken instrument, not a ratchet violation.

(2) scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::_require_matching_params RAISES whenever the committed baseline's params.cluster_paths differs from live CLUSTER_PATHS, with the message "a path can never leave the cluster and take its frozen numbers with it." So the CLUSTER_PATHS edit forces a baseline regeneration in the same commit.

(3) orchestrator/tests/test_merge_lane_ratchet.py also hardcodes the test-tree members in `_APPENDIX_A_TESTS` and asserts they are a subset of CLUSTER_PATHS, plus a prose comment naming the count ("exactly the 3 that live there"). Both must be edited too.

Correct order inside the one commit: edit CLUSTER_PATHS and _APPENDIX_A_TESTS, delete the file, THEN run `python scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py --write-baseline orchestrator/tests/merge_lane_ratchet_baseline.json` last. A removal LOWERS totals, so the write gate accepts without --authorize-raise.

RELATED AND SEPARATELY BINDING: test_merge_lane_ratchet.py:3388::test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement asserts BYTE EQUALITY between the committed baseline and a fresh measurement, and the baseline's `tests` section carries per-file patch_targets/private_reads for all 235 lane-importing files under orchestrator/tests. So editing ANY of those 235 test files — not just a cluster path — requires regenerating the baseline in that same commit. A commit that only LOWERS measures still fails without regeneration; "the ratchet only fails on a rise" is false. This matches the steward ruling recorded on esc-4211-7 (2026-09-13).

entry_text: Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, main 7da9051b0e): explicit sub type-args and type-param defaults never reach the compiler as Type::Applied or Type::Error. entity.rs's two sub type-arg arms (~3281, ~5674) and convert_type_params' default arm (type_resolution.rs ~4518) match `Named { name, .. }`, which drops nested args, so `Box<SealA>` becomes StructureRef("Box") and `List<Real>` becomes StructureRef("List"). Any unknown name falls back to StructureRef(name) with no diagnostic unless the type param has a bound. A quick way to probe compile+eval behaviour without building tests is the warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify check|eval <file.ri>`.
target_text: Fact (2026-06-14, Reify compiler): Structure type-arguments are SILENTLY DROPPED today. When a TypeExprKind::Named{name, type_args} resolves to a user-defined structure, resolve_type_with_aliases returns Type::StructureRef(name) (type_resolution.rs:659-660, returned at :1358-1365) WITHOUT examining type_args — no error, no warning. So Coupling<Prismatic> and Coupling<Revolute> are the same Type today. Separately, associated-type projection is rejected for two base shapes in resolve_qualified_assoc_type: a base WITH type args (:818-827) and a type-PARAM base (:832-845, with a comment 'PRD §3.5 adds no associated-type-projection Type variant' at :830). And assoc-type bindings cannot reference the structure's type-params: collect_structure_assoc_type_bindings hardcodes empty_params (crates/reify-compiler/src/conformance/checker.rs:910), so `type MotionValue = P::MotionValue` fails to resolve. These three are exactly what the type-args/projection substrate PRD (4601-4606) fixes.

entry_text: To force the except arm around `asyncio.create_task(self._some_coro(args))` in an orchestrator test (e.g. TaskWorkflow._route_review_suggestions_to_curator's scheduling-failure → SuggestionDisposition.ERROR path), replace the coroutine method with a SYNCHRONOUS `MagicMock(side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`, not `patch.object(wf, '_some_coro', side_effect=...)`: patch.object auto-builds an AsyncMock for an async target, and an AsyncMock raises its side_effect only when AWAITED, so create_task schedules it, the try never sees the error, and the router reports CURATOR. Also avoid the older trick of returning a non-coroutine, which depends on asyncio's exact TypeError (task 3415 amendment).
target_text: Test gotcha (dark_factory, task 3550): patching `asyncio.create_task` in a test — e.g. `patch('asyncio.create_task', return_value=MagicMock())` to stop a real server task from starting — leaves the coroutine argument BUILT BUT NEVER SCHEDULED OR AWAITED. When it is garbage-collected it raises an *unraisable* exception ("Exception ignored in: <coroutine object X>"), which pytest surfaces as PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning attributed to whatever test happens to be running in that xdist worker when the GC fires — a spurious failure in a completely unrelated FILE, and order-dependent (passes in isolation, passes if the offending file is scheduled last). FIX: capture the coroutine via `side_effect=` instead of `return_value=` and call `coro.close()` after the call under test; close() on a never-started coroutine retires it cleanly. This is the INVERSE of the leaked-background-task class already covered by the conftest cancel+drain reapers (_reap_leaked_merge_workers etc.): those tasks ARE scheduled and outlive the loop, and are fixed by cancel/drain — here create_task itself is mocked out, so no task ever exists and a reaper cannot see it. Tell them apart by whether create_task is patched.

entry_text: Reify compiler: when you add or widen a builtin classification family slice (e.g. in orientation_signatures.rs / units.rs), you must also do three things in crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs. Add the slice to the `is_known_builtin` union. Add it to the test module's `ALL_FAMILY_SLICES` table. Remove its names from `EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES`. Otherwise the name is silently double-owned (family + "unclaimed" manifest), and `eval_deferred_names_are_disjoint_from_every_registered_family` cannot detect it. Task #6082's ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES missed this; task 6306 fixes it.
target_text: Reify: adding a new stdlib builtin touches FOUR sites, and `crates/reify-compiler/src/builtin_signatures.rs` is NOT one of them despite the name — that module is the per-argument dimension SLOT table (`builtin_arg_slots`/`check_builtin_arg_types`), whose `ExpectedArg` enum has only `Scalar`/`Int` variants and so cannot gate a composite Point3/Vec3 arg, and whose header forbids new ANGLE slots by binding seam decree. The real per-family registries are the sibling `<family>_signatures.rs` modules (orientation_, relation_, joint_, math_). For an orientation/transform/frame builtin: (1) add the name to `ORIENTATION_TYPED_FN_NAMES` + the result-type arm in orientation_signatures.rs — membership alone then supplies call-site typing (expr.rs `NoUserFunctions` ladder) AND `is_known_builtin` (suppresses the UnresolvedFunction warning); (2) bump the hand-written independent `EXPECTED_NAMES` fixture and its "exactly the N" count test in the same file; (3) add the eval arm in reify-stdlib, choosing the module by PRODUCED VALUE KIND — every `Type::Transform(3)` producer lives in `geometry.rs::eval_geometry`, never `orientation.rs`, and the `diagnose` disjointness tests enforce it; (4) docs/reify-stdlib-reference.md (convention only — no doc-coverage gate exists).

entry_text: reify gotcha (measured 2026-09-30, main 778339a7e1): `self.<datum>` (self.x/.frame/.xy_plane…) lowers to MethodCall{ValueRef(<Entity>.__self : StructureRef)} which pure reify_expr::eval_expr short-circuits to Undef; Engine::eval patches it only via a post-pass (engine_eval.rs ~5954, geometry_ops rewrite_self_datum_projections) that re-evaluates ONLY cells textually containing self.<datum>, never their consumers, and runs BEFORE the post-solve evaluate_let_bindings re-run (which clobbers them back to Undef when the template has a solved `auto`); eval_cached never runs it. Symptoms: `let f = frame_at(p, self.x, self.z); let o = f.origin` → o undef; `let fr = self.frame; fr.origin` → undef. Task 6100's plan moves self-datum eval into reify-expr (identity-frame delegation) and deletes the post-pass.
target_text: Reify eval gotcha (root-caused under task #6100): the geometric-relations eta self-datum post-pass in `Engine::eval` (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs ~:4771-4821) rewrites and re-commits ONLY the Let cells whose expression syntactically CONTAINS a `self.<datum>` node. Any cell that merely READS such a cell was already evaluated in the main Param+Let walk while the producer still held `Value::Undef`, and is never re-evaluated — so it keeps a stale Undef forever. This is why `let f = frame_at(p, self.x, self.z)` yields a real Frame while `let fo = f.origin` yields undef. It is the same bug class task #4707 fixed for guarded members (engine_eval.rs:5396-5432 "downstream cone"); the canonical fix is to seed `Engine::re_eval_post_walk_mints_per_template` (:9518) with the flipped cell ids rather than hand-rolling a topo walk.

Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.
- Free-function forms `map(xs, |v| v)` / `filter(xs, |v| v > 1)` also fail; no free-function map/filter exists.
- `generate(3, |i| i)` and `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])` DO parse (both `function_call`); `xs.count` parses (bare `member_access`, no parens). So lambdas work and member access works — only method arguments are missing.

DEAD CODE this leaves behind: the `"map"`, `"filter"`, `"all"`, `"any"`, `"generate"` arms of `eval_method_call` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs (lines ~3695, ~3825, ~3714, ~3739, ~3811) are unreachable from .ri source and exercised only by Rust-level tests. crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:3798-3810 even documents a deliberate negative-count policy divergence between the free-function and METHOD forms of `generate` — a distinction no .ri program can observe.

WORK TO DECIDE/DO (triage first, this is a design question, not a mechanical fix):
(a) add an `obj.method(args)` rule to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js plus the corresponding lowering in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, so the existing evaluator arms become reachable; or
(b) expose the wanted combinators as free functions instead (the shape `generate` and `flat_map` already use) and delete or clearly mark the unreachable method arms; or
(c) accept the gap deliberately and document it, marking the unreachable arms so future readers do not assume surface coverage.

Files: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs.

Rationale for filing: leaving evaluator arms with no surface form is a silent-capability-gap — a design session reading the stdlib docs would reasonably write `xs.filter(...)` and get an opaque "invalid let" parse error rather than an unsupported-construct diagnostic.
Analysis: TRIAGE (the task asks for a design decision first).

SECOND HAZARD IN THE SAME AREA: `SqliteTaskBackend.get_tasks(<any project_root>)` AUTO-CREATES `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db` and returns `{"tasks": []}` without raising, and `EscalationQueue.__init__` does `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on its queue_dir. entry_text: Workspace-member pyright gotcha (task 5267, measured 2026-10-03): a member's module type_check_command `uv run --directory <m> pyright src/ tests/` passes EXPLICIT CLI targets, which override [tool.pyright] include. So widening include alone (e.g. adding "scripts") reaches only BARE `pyright` runs (hooks/project-checks, the fleet chain, editors), never the merge-verify type leg that runs that command verbatim under merge_verify_breadth "full". That is how fused-memory/scripts quietly accumulated 19 pyright errors. Both homes now name scripts/ for fused-memory and orchestrator. tests/scripts/test_member_scripts_type_gate.py discovers every member that has [tool.pyright] and scripts/*.py, and fails if either gate misses a script or an exclude/ignore carves one out. When adding a new checked directory to a member, edit BOTH include and the module type_check_command.
target_text:
PACKAGE-LEVEL `fused-memory/scripts/` IS A FOURTH pyright-scope disagreement, distinct from the three in memory 3a0c41f6 (which are all about the REPO-ROOT `scripts/` tree). Measured 2026-09-13 on task/2900 at HEAD 5daa563333, worktree .worktrees/2900:

* `uv run --directory fused-memory pyright src/ tests/` (the module's OWN declared type_check_command, fused-memory/orchestrator.yaml:20) → 0 errors, 2 warnings. 3m45s.
* `uv run --directory fused-memory pyright scripts/backfill_entity_standing_decision.py` → 1 error (reportArgumentType), same venv, same pyright 1.1.408. 16s.

MECHANISM (measured, not inferred): fused-memory/pyproject.toml `[tool.pyright] include = ["src", "tests"]` and `extraPaths = [..., "scripts", ...]`. So a scripts/ module imported by a test is ANALYZED (its types are real, not Unknown) but its diagnostics are NOT REPORTED unless the file is named on the command line. Verify's FILE_SCOPED path does name it whenever the diff touches it, so the module gate is red while the module's own declared command is green.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYONE EDITING fused-memory/scripts/: the self-verification an implementer naturally runs — the declared type_check_command — cannot see the file it just wrote. Task 2900's implementer commit message records "uv run pyright in fused-memory reports 0 errors" and verify attempt-1 then failed on exactly one error in the script; both statements were true. Run `uv run --directory fused-memory pyright scripts/<file>.py` explicitly after any fused-memory/scripts/ edit.

Note the direction is OPPOSITE to memory 06f6ae15 ("treat isolated-pyright errors on scripts/ as environment artifacts"): that entry is about repo-root scripts/ before task 3456. For a fused-memory/scripts/ file whose imports all resolve, an isolated scoped run is the AUTHORITATIVE one — it is what verify runs. Remedy direction, per 3a0c41f6's rule: widen the package `include` to cover scripts, never narrow what verify checks.

entry_text: FalkorDB gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, task 4716): `MATCH (a)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(b) RETURN count(*)` with r UNREFERENCED counts distinct connected (a,b) node PAIRS, not edges — multi-edges between one pair collapse (dark_factory: 19,409 vs count(r) = count(DISTINCT r.uuid) = 20,491; the plan is Aggregate <- Conditional Traverse, no edge expansion). Referencing r (`count(r)`, or any `WHERE r.<prop>`) expands the edges. A `_paged_ro_query` census written as a bare-pattern count(*) is therefore LOW, and since completeness is `rows_seen >= expected_rows`, it would pass a read truncated by up to the multi-edge excess. Edge censuses must use count(r) or carry a WHERE on r.
target_text: As of task 4340, fused-memory has a reusable paginated-read primitive: `_paged_ro_query(graph, page_template, census_cypher, *, params, page_size, resultset_size, max_pages) -> PagedRead` in fused_memory/backends/graphiti_client.py. Use it instead of open-coding SKIP/LIMIT for any new whole-graph FalkorDB read. It returns a frozen PagedRead(rows, complete, rows_seen, expected_rows, reason) and fails CLOSED on four independent paths, each logging a WARNING naming the numbers: page_size >= resultset_size (refuses outright, returns NO rows), max_pages exhausted on a still-full page, census probe unusable, and rows_seen < expected_rows. Callers supply a page template with ORDER BY over a TOTAL row order plus SKIP/LIMIT placeholders, and a census cypher with an IDENTICAL MATCH/WHERE returning count(*). enumerate_all_valid_edges and enumerate_entity_nodes are the two worked examples; get_all_valid_edges and list_entity_nodes are back-compat shims over them that WARN (deliberately never raise) on an incomplete read.

entry_text: reify tests/infra/nextest_absent_lib.sh (nx_run) gives nested suites a throwaway HOME with CARGO_HOME unset, so their cargo registry cache is COLD. Any hermetic `cargo metadata --locked --offline` read inside a suite nested by test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh fails (measured 126 ms, 'no matching package named serde ... offline'). A bare non-offline read instead silently downloads the registry into the throwaway HOME (measured 12.6 s, ~718 MB). H7's 'HOME still small' check runs BEFORE the S-rows, so it does not catch that fetch.
target_text: tests/infra/nextest_absent_lib.sh simulates cargo-nextest absence by mirroring ONE directory (the mirror source: $CARGO_HOME/bin, else $HOME/.cargo/bin) into a symlink farm minus cargo-nextest, then dropping that directory from PATH. It therefore only hides cargo-nextest from that single directory — a cargo-nextest reachable via any other PATH entry stays resolvable and the simulation silently degrades to nextest=1. Since task 5602 the mirror-source element is matched PHYSICALLY (cd + pwd -P), so alternate spellings of the same dir (trailing slash, doubled separator, symlink) are filtered; a genuinely different directory is not. When writing an ad-hoc probe against this lib, do not build a synthetic ambient PATH out of a fresh symlink dir that itself contains cargo-nextest — the harness will correctly fail H1/H4 and it looks like a lib bug. Simulate a modified toolchain by pointing CARGO_HOME at a fake home whose bin/ mirrors the real one instead.

entry_text: Reify gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, main 7da9051b0e): explicit sub type-args and type-param defaults never reach the compiler as Type::Applied or Type::Error. entity.rs's two sub type-arg arms (~3281, ~5674) and convert_type_params' default arm (type_resolution.rs ~4518) match `Named { name, .. }`, which drops nested args, so `Box<SealA>` becomes StructureRef("Box") and `List<Real>` becomes StructureRef("List"). Any unknown name falls back to StructureRef(name) with no diagnostic unless the type param has a bound. A quick way to probe compile+eval behaviour without building tests is the warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify check|eval <file.ri>`.
target_text: Reify compiler: a type-parameter default (`<T = X>` on alias/structure/fn/trait/constraint/enum) is lowered by convert_type_params (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_resolution.rs), NOT by the full type resolver — builtins only, else Type::StructureRef(X). It becomes user-visible through parametric-alias default substitution: `type Picked<T = E> = T` + bare `param a: Picked` gives a's cell type the StructureRef default (probe 2026-10-01: enum default E → 'no matching overload ... candidates: f(Enum(E))'). Fast probe: write a .ri with that shape and run target/debug/reify check.

entry_text: To tell whether a `reportMissingImports` pragma on a cross-workspace-member import is load-bearing, measure under a NARROW env as well as the all-packages one. After `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV uv sync --all-packages`, every member is editable-installed in the root .venv, so the import resolves and the pragma looks vestigial. To simulate the member's own minimal env (what `uv run --directory <member>` builds on an unsynced tree), temporarily move `.venv/lib/python3.*/site-packages/_editable_impl_<other_member>.pth` aside, rerun the member's declared pyright gate, then restore the file. Measured in task 5090: shared/tests/test_task_statuses.py's orchestrator/fused_memory imports gave 0 errors under all-packages and 3 with the .pth files hidden, so those pragmas are load-bearing. Note the trap: `(root/'orchestrator').is_dir()` is true at the repo root, but pyright does NOT resolve `orchestrator.task_status` through that namespace-package partial.
target_text:
Placing a doc-contract guard that must import a workspace member under `tests/scripts/` WORKS, and the way to prove importability is a throwaway test file there — never `python -c "import <member>"`.

MEASURED on task 5374 (2026-09-17, worktree .worktrees/5374): `tests/scripts/test_shadow_ruling_doc_contract.py` does a module-level `from escalation.shadow_ruling import ...` and runs green under the directory's own `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/` gate — 1972 passed / 2 skipped for the full directory — even though `shared`'s pyproject declares no `escalation` dependency. The repo-root `conftest.py` appends every subproject's `src/` to `sys.path` and pre-imports the packages, so the venv's contents are not the binding constraint UNDER PYTEST. The import resolved to the worktree's own tree, not the main checkout.

THE FALSE-NEGATIVE TRAP: probing with a bare `python -c "import escalation"` reports a FALSE SUCCESS. The repo root is on `sys.path`, so the bare subproject directory `escalation/` matches as an empty namespace package and the import "works" while importing nothing. Probe with a throwaway test file under `tests/scripts/` instead, so the conftest applies.

WHY IT MATTERS: the alternative — putting such a guard in the member's own `tests/` — is what you pick if you believe the import is impossible, and it costs you the cheaper suite, the directory where every comparable SKILL.md guard already lives, and the directory the `SKILLS_CONSUMING_TESTS` inventory's other entries point at. Task 5374's plan recorded this as an explicit correction of an earlier decision made on the false premise.

entry_text: Since task 4015 (spawn-claude.sh `sanitize_env` in the `$inner` payload), a spawned claude's environment carries ONLY CLAUDE_SPAWN_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_SPAWN_OWNER_PPID, CLAUDE_SPAWN_WM_TITLE, CLAUDE_SPAWN_RESULT_FILE (plus CLAUDE_SPAWN_PARENT_ID when set). There is NO CLAUDE_SPAWN_TITLE/ROLE/PROJECT/TASK_ID/ESCALATION_ID/PROMPT; those are passed only as one-off prefixes on the `python3 ... launching` call. Verified 2026-10-04 via /proc/<pid>/environ on 5 live spawned sessions. So session_hooks tests that put CLAUDE_SPAWN_TITLE/ROLE in a hook's env model a shape production does not produce; in production the hook's title comes from the persisted record.title.
target_text: In skills/spawn/spawn-claude.sh, only 4 CLAUDE_SPAWN_* vars are actually spliced into `inner` (the payload that execs the real spawned `claude` process) and thus reach a spawned session's real env: CLAUDE_SPAWN_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_SPAWN_PARENT_ID, CLAUDE_SPAWN_RESULT_FILE, CLAUDE_SPAWN_WM_TITLE (via spawn_id_export/parent_id_export/result_export/wm_title_export, all prefixed onto `inner` right before `cd $q_cwd && claude ...`). CLAUDE_SPAWN_TITLE, CLAUDE_SPAWN_PROMPT, CLAUDE_SPAWN_CWD, and CLAUDE_SPAWN_LAUNCHER_PID are exported only around the separate short-lived `python3 "$SESSION_REGISTRY_PY" launching` command-substitution subprocess (lines ~122-128) and never reach the spawned claude session's own process env. This matters for any test/fixture trying to be hermetic against a real fleet-spawned launching context (e.g. orchestrator/tests/test_session_hooks.py's `_clear_claude_spawn_env` autouse fixture, task 2643): only those 4 vars can realistically leak into `os.environ` inside a spawned session; clearing the others is inert defense-in-depth, not a fix for an observed leak.

entry_text: Historical base rate for the MODE-3 delivered_check shape in dark-factory (a filename-existence intent written as kind=grep over file CONTENTS, where the pattern is the declared file's own name): 14 of about 758 grep expect=present checks in tasks.db, measured 2026-09-28. 13 of the 14 were on done tasks and went green on main only through coincidental mentions: the script's own usage text or docstring (5 cases), a sibling script's prose, an importer, or README text. The belief that 'a module rarely mentions its own name' is FALSE for scripts, so such checks usually pass by luck, and they fail when nothing mentions the file. Example: the check of pending task 4681 (reclaim-orphaned-worktrees-predicate over scripts/) fails on main. kind='path' (task 4743) is the right shape for file existence.
target_text: When authoring a `metadata.delivered_checks` entry of `kind=grep`, remember it searches file CONTENT, never filenames — a check whose `pattern` is a module/file name with `expect=present` is near-guaranteed to be vacuously false, because a test module does not normally mention its own name in its body. Verified instance: task 3536's check `pattern='test_workflow_merge_gating_strand', expect=present, paths=['orchestrator/tests/']` reported DEP_CAPABILITY_NOT_DELIVERED and blocked task 3537 with a `critical` escalation even though `orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_merge_gating_strand.py` had fully landed on main. Pick a pattern that is a CONTENT string inside the deliverable (e.g. a class name such as `TestNoStrandExitProperty`) and confirm it goes 0 -> 1 across the task by grepping the dep's own `branch_base_sha`. This is a third distinct mis-authoring mode alongside `expect=absent` greps that match the fix's own docstring (task 3534) or a deliberate residual counter (task 3618); task 3500 tracks validating checks against the tree at authoring time.

Fact, verified 2026-09-30 on leo-laptop, Ubuntu 24.04 with systemd 255:
- `systemd-run --user --scope` works from a NON-interactive ssh session. Linger=no, but the ssh session starts the user manager.
- A dashed-prefix drop-in such as ~/.config/systemd/user/df-verify-<tag>-.scope.d/memory-max.conf applies to TRANSIENT scopes whose names start with that prefix. A probe scope's cgroup memory.max/memory.swap.max reflected MemoryMax/MemorySwapMax exactly.
- The laptop has 60 GiB RAM and 135 GiB swap, so a MemoryMax without MemorySwapMax=0 would swap-thrash instead of killing.
- DF verify scopes land in app.slice under user@1000.service. The scope tags were computed with the laptop's code (orchestrator.verify._scope_tag_for): 'dark-factory-c889f090' and 'reify-4ae45bbd'.
target_text: cgroup v2 / systemd facts verified on the dark-factory host 2026-09-08, load-bearing for task 3394 (per-project slice topology) and the load-throttle-harmonisation PRD. (1) Every orchestrator-*.service unit and every df-verify-* transient scope sits directly under user@1000.service/app.slice at cpu.weight 100 with cpu.max=max; the cpu controller is delegated through app.slice (cgroup.subtree_control has cpu memory pids). (2) A cgroup's cpu.pressure covers its whole subtree: app.slice read 62 while its children read 46 (df unit), 6 (reify unit), 54 (a reify verify scope), and user@1000.service read 63 ~ host 64. (3) systemd derives a slice's parent from its name by stripping the last dash segment: `systemd-run --user --scope --slice=df-prd-probe.slice` created df.slice/df-prd.slice/df-prd-probe.slice under user@1000.service, i.e. `df.slice` lands as a SIBLING of app.slice, not inside it; project ids with underscores (fused_memory.project_id: dark_factory, reify) avoid spurious nesting, whereas verify.py::_scope_tag_for (dash-sanitised basename plus a hash, used for df-verify-<tag>-<uuid>.scope names) would make systemd derive bogus parents and must not be used for slice names. (4) A fresh slice or scope has NO cpu.weight file until some CPU property is set on it; `systemctl --user set-property --runtime <slice> CPUWeight=250` vivified it and read back; `systemd-run --user --scope -p CPUWeight=33` reads back cpu.weight=33 (both harmless probes, cleaned up). (5) Per-process runqueue wait is readable from /proc/<pid>/schedstat (fields run_ns, wait_ns); the committed scripts/cgroup-stall-ratio.py reports wait/(run+wait) per (cgroup bucket, family, nice) and is the honest "who is starved" signal — ps pcpu is a lifetime average that missed 8-10 cores of short-lived fork churn (~1100 forks/s under test load), while per-cgroup cpu.stat usage_usec deltas are exact. (6) The deterministic runner spawns before_done scripts with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, so a script that calls the orchestrator's own escalation MCP over HTTP (reload_config single-shot tools/call with Accept: application/json, text/event-stream) does not deadlock the loop; scripts/merge-deep-set-cap.sh and scripts/merge-pytest-n-ab-switch.sh are the pattern.

entry_text:
Completed: Close the jq-vs-Rust ISO-8601 divergence in reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq (numeric TZ offset / no-TZ forms yield a quiet done_at=null)
Description: Filed from task 7236 (review point 2, reviewer_comprehensive robustness) as OUT-OF-SCOPE follow-up work. Task 7236's frozen plan design-decision #4 deliberately PINNED this divergence as accepted rather than closing it; this ticket tracks closing it, so the accepted divergence is tracked rather than only narrated.

OBSERVED (measured on task/7236, guarded green by Check 5f-f of tests/infra/test_reify_audit_predone_wrapper.sh): the two loaders of the same fused-memory updatedAt field disagree on timestamp SHAPE.

- scripts/reify-audit-snapshot-filter.jq uses jq's fromdateiso8601, which accepts ONLY "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" (after the filter strips a trailing .NNN millisecond suffix).
- crates/reify-audit/src/fused_memory_client.rs parse_iso8601_to_epoch has a split_tz arm (fused_memory_client.rs:417) accepting "Z", "+HH:MM", "-HH:MM", AND a bare no-TZ form (treated as UTC), with fractional seconds stripped in any of those positions. Its own unit tests pin all four (iso8601_plus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_minus_offset_equivalent_to_utc, iso8601_no_tz_treated_as_utc).

So "2026-05-01T12:00:00+00:00" (and "2026-05-01T12:00:00", and "2026-05-01T12:00:00.000+01:00") parse to an epoch in the Rust loader and to null in the jq sidecar.

CONSEQUENCE, and why it is worth tracking rather than leaving narrated. Task 7236 made the jq conversion TOTAL (try ... catch null), which correctly stopped ONE such row from aborting the whole snapshot and taking the wrapper's exit-125 arm. Description: PROBLEM (measured 2026-09-07/08, load-tuning session, Leo). cgroup v2 schedules in two layers: `nice` orders threads INSIDE one cgroup; BETWEEN sibling cgroups the kernel shares CPU by `cpu.weight`, and nice has no effect on that split. verify.py::_run_cmd launches a verify inside a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` (its own cgroup) when `verify_use_cgroup_scope` is true, for kill-by-cgroup on timeout. Every such scope is created at the default CPUWeight 100, the same as `orchestrator-dark-factory.service` as a whole (every agent plus every non-scoped verify). Measured per-cgroup cpu.stat over 20s under contention: df unit 8.9 cores, reify task-role verify scope 7.9, reify merge-role verify scope 7.6, i.e. an equal three-way split. The task-role scope carried `nice -n 15 ionice -c2 -n7` from shared/verify_admission.py::_NICE_TIERS and yielded NOTHING to the merge scope or to the df unit, because nice is per-cgroup. Inside the df unit the tiers DO work (merge xdist at nice 5 got 5.2 cores, task xdist at nice 15 got 2.2, background at nice 19 got 0). So the role tiering is correct in-unit and inert across scopes.

CHANGE. At the `systemd-run` argv build in verify.py::_run_cmd (the branch guarded by `use_cgroup_scope and shutil.which('systemd-run')`), add `-p CPUWeight=<w>` where w is resolved by role next to the nice prefix (verify.py::_resolve_nice_prefix is called with `role` at the two call sites; thread the weight the same way, e.g. a new optional `cpu_weight: int | None` on the spawn spec that carries `use_cgroup_scope`/`scope_tag`, None = omit the property = today's behaviour). Config: three int knobs on OrchestratorConfig, `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_merge` (default 100), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_task` (default 33), `verify_cgroup_cpu_weight_background` (default 10), validated 1..10000 (cgroup v2 cpu.weight range); add them to RELOADABLE_FIELDS beside `verify_admission_nice_*` (read at spawn, so green-tier is honest) and to the green list in OPERATIONS.md section "Config reload vs restart". `offline` and unknown roles get no property.

WHY THESE NUMBERS. Lower task/background rather than raise merge: reify's own cpu_governance convention is task 100 / merge 300, but a 300 merge scope would also put interactive shells (weight-100 siblings under app.slice) at a quarter share under contention. Merge at 100 keeps the merge leg at parity with each orchestrator unit and with the operator's terminals; 33 and 10 reproduce the 3:1 merge:task ratio and the nice-19 background intent. Under contention with the df unit + one reify merge scope + one reify task scope the split moves from 33/33/33 to 43/43/14. Weights are work-conserving: a lone scope still gets the whole box, so nothing slows on an idle host.

PROVEN ON THIS HOST 2026-09-08: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect -p CPUWeight=33 -- sh -c '...cat cpu.weight'` printed cpu.weight=33 (the cpu controller is delegated through user@1000.service/app.slice; every unit and scope currently reads 100).

Claude CLI 2.1.287 permission mechanics (measured 2026-10-02, task 4344 architect, headless --print with --json-schema):
(1) StructuredOutput survives a non-empty registry filter such as `--tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash`.
(2) Under `--permission-mode dontAsk` with NO allow rules, Read/Grep inside cwd are allowed, while Read/Grep outside cwd (e.g. /etc/hostname) are denied.
(3) Adding a bare `Read` allow rule lets Read reach /etc/hostname.
(4) `Bash(git log:*)` under dontAsk permitted `git log -1 --output=/tmp/x.txt`, which WROTE the file. A git-scoped Bash allow rule is therefore not read-only.
target_text: Headless Claude CLI sandbox scoping (discovered 2026-08-03 during the reify census recovery, verified empirically): a headless `claude -p` session sandboxes file/Bash tool access to the tree of its inherited cwd — reads of any other repo are permission-denied non-interactively, and a conscientious agent then reports "could not verify / sandbox restricts access to <cwd> only". The fix is `claude -p --add-dir <other_root> [<more_roots>]` (variadic; verified working: with --add-dir /home/leo/src/reify a headless session run from dark-factory reads reify files fine). IMPLICATION for any harness code that shells out to headless claude to inspect a DIFFERENT project than its own cwd (census verify, cross-repo checks, dispatched investigations): without --add-dir the model doesn't error — it produces well-formed negative answers, so a fail-closed caller silently converts an access problem into mass negative verdicts. During the census this rejected 19 of the first 20 clusters before being caught; the detection tell was every rejection reason sharing the same could-not-observe wording.

READING DARK-FACTORY merge_heartbeat EVENTS FOR PAST QUEUE OCCUPANCY: two traps, measured for task 6021 on 2026-10-01. This complements the 'MEASURING DARK-FACTORY MERGE-GATE THROUGHPUT' memory.

(1) The heartbeat's `depth` does NOT mean runnable work existed. It counts every non-terminal registry entry, stale ones included. Measured: for 49-57 min stretches, depth was 2-18, but verify_in_progress was null and occupancy.inflight_total was 0. head_of_line was either 4792 ('queued', age about 110 h) or 5590's blocked first request, still 'queued' after 5590 had landed (task 3860). To judge whether runnable work was waiting, use verify_in_progress, occupancy.inflight_total, and the queue_depth field on merge_queued events.

(2) The heartbeat is SUPPRESSED when depth == 0 (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::SpeculativeMergeWorker._maybe_log_queue_heartbeat). A heartbeat silence much longer than its ~5-min interval therefore means the pipeline was empty. Example: 33 min of silence on 2026-09-30, 09:09-09:42Z.

Related gotchas:
- merge_verify's duration is in json data.duration_ms; the events.duration_ms column is NULL for it.
- A laptop-runner merge verify lands only after a local parity verify, about 30-40 min after the laptop pass.

entry_text: Option pattern-spelling facts measured 2026-09-29 (esc-6020-11 investigation, target/debug/reify 09-25 build): `some(v) =>` and `Some(v) =>` are PARSE ERRORS because tree-sitter match_pattern has no call-shaped production — NOT because some/none are keywords; grammar.js declares no `word:` rule, so tree-sitter reserves nothing and `some =>`, `none =>`, `Some =>`, `None =>`, `some { value: v } =>`, and the typo `Sme { value: v } =>` all parse and all evaluate to undef today. The GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar ~:1862) DOES @specialize some/none as ReservedWord, so `none =>` and `some { value: v }` produce error nodes in the editor; the ratified `Some { value: v }` / `None` spelling parses in BOTH grammars. The spec is internally inconsistent: §2.10 lists some/none as keywords (false for tree-sitter; `let none = 3mm` parses, though a later `none` still resolves to the Option value while `some` resolves to the let); §5.10 and §9.2.8 show `some(c) =>` and nested `some(some(x)) =>`; §15's BNF has a flat `'some' '(' IDENT ')' | 'none'` pattern production contradicting both; §3.8 says "not an enum". Nested patterns are impossible under every route (field_binding binders are bare identifiers, DCE §10). Tracked .ri corpus: ONE Option match site (tests/prd-gate/fixtures/parse_length_match_resolves.ri) vs 83 construction sites (13 `some(`, 70 `none`) in 27 files. Display already diverges: CLI prints `None`/`Some(..)`, LSP hover prints `none`/`some(..)`. All of these rewrites are #6020's docs-truth rider; the lowercase-arm ratchet flips at #6017.
target_text: Open language-design question as of 2026-09-29 (reify esc-6020-11, data-carrying-enums PRD fork F4, 'Recommend Leo decide'): how `match` destructures Option<T>. The spec's `some(c) =>` does not parse (some/none are keywords excluded from match_pattern). Task 6020's architect chose route (ii) `Some { value: v }` / `None` (parses today, mirrors Result's Ok { value }, consistent with Leo's F3 ruling of 2026-05-27 that enum payloads are named-field only) with the wart that construction is lowercase some(x). Route (i) positional some(x)/none reintroduces the positional form F3 excluded. Task 6020 was set DEFERRED by the L2 watcher pending the ruling; Leo delegated it to a spawned fable /team session (brief ~/.claude/spawn-briefs/esc-6020-11-option-match.md) to investigate, discuss with him, then action his conclusions and resolve the escalation.

The non-blocking DONE arm first runs `_apply_amendment_delta_scope` (only when used_ctx is set) and then `_suppress_resettled_suggestions`, and after that routes through `_route_review_suggestions_to_curator`.
- ITEM 5 is live: `_route_review_suggestions_to_curator` stamps every ticket with ONE batch hash (`review_suggestion_payload_hash(suggestions)`) as metadata.suggestion_hash. fused-memory task_interceptor.py::_check_escalation_idempotency matches on (escalation_id, suggestion_hash), and _process_add_tickets_batch_prepared resolves a hit as 'combined'/idempotency_hit, so once the first ticket of a batch creates a task, later tickets of that batch fold away. orchestrator/agents/triage.py::suggestion_hash already exists as the per-suggestion R4 key used by the steward triage path.

STEWARD RECOVERY PROCEDURE (dark-factory, verified 2026-09-07, esc-4821-3 / esc-4821-4): when a `review_issues` escalation's summary advertises N suggestions but its body contains only blocking issues, the suggestions are NOT lost — read them off disk at `<worktree_base>/.task-meta/<task_id>/reviews/*.json`. Do not ask for them to be re-surfaced.

WHERE THEY LIVE. `.task-meta/<task_id>/reviews/reviewer_comprehensive.json` (and siblings per reviewer) holds the FULL verdict: every issue with severity/location/category/description/suggested_fix. Earlier rounds are archived alongside as `reviews-cycle-1/`, `reviews-cycle-2/`, … Measured on task 4821: the artifact carried verdict=ISSUES_FOUND with Counter({'suggestion': 6, 'blocking': 1}) while the escalation body carried only the 1 blocking issue.

WHY THE RECORD LOOKS TRUNCATED — it is built that way, it is not corruption. `workflow.py::_escalate_review_issues` sets `detail = reviews.format_for_replan()`, and `artifacts.py::ReviewAggregation.format_for_replan` iterates `self.blocking_issues` ONLY (docstring: "Format blocking issues for the architect to address"). The summary's count comes from a SEPARATE `len(reviews.suggestions)`. Summary and body are derived from different collections with nothing coupling them, so the summary can promise content the body structurally cannot hold.

THE GENERAL SMELL, worth recognizing anywhere: a summary string and a detail body computed from two different collections, with no assertion tying them together. The failure is silent and actively misleading — a reader trusts the count and concludes the content must be there. When you write a summary that names a count, derive it from the same collection you rendered, or assert the correspondence.

ALSO TRUE AND SEPARATELY FILED: on the cycles-exhausted branch (`if review_cycle >= max_review_cycles: _escalate_review_issues(reviews); return ESCALATED`) there is NO `_route_review_suggestions_to_curator` call, unlike the DONE path. So on that path suggestions reach no consumer at all and survive only as the on-disk artifact. The amendment path does not save them either: `_scope_post_amendment_verdict` routes only the OUT-OF-DELTA complement, deliberately keeping in-delta suggestions in the verdict — exactly the ones that then hit this branch. Filed as tkt_0RTBP5ERMYGG8BM77X63W9V1WQ against orchestrator/.

PRACTICAL UPSHOT for a steward: an incomplete-looking escalation body is a prompt to go read the artifact, not a dead end. Check `.task-meta/<id>/reviews/` before declaring anything untriageable.

entry_text: Gotcha (socket-activated user units, verified 2026-09-29): (1) First migration of a running service onto a newly installed .socket needs only an ordinary `systemctl --user restart <service>` - systemd orders the old process's stop before the socket's start, and the new process gets LISTEN_FDS. (2) Changing an ACTIVE socket's ListenStream set needs `systemctl --user stop <service>` then `systemctl --user start <x>.socket <service>` - a combined `restart <x>.socket <service>` fails with 'Socket service <service> already active, refusing'. (3) In ExecStopPost, `systemctl --user list-jobs <unit>` shows TYPE `restart` during a restart, `stop` during a stop, and no job during a crash awaiting auto-restart - that is what scripts/stop-socket-unless-restarting.sh keys on.

3. Attribution is cross-crate: the failure surfaces under `-p reify-test-support`, not under the crate you edited. Under verify.sh's narrowed / affected-crate passes that reads as an unrelated crate breaking. When adding any test anywhere in the workspace that touches a temp dir, expect this gate to fire out of reify-test-support.

Completed: reify-cli panics (exit 101, 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe') when stdout is a closed pipe — restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (escalation-watcher, esc-7906-3, option C). The census sighting's `head --short` was the host skim-hook flattening artifact (see dark-factory 5955), NOT a reify bug. BUT there is a REAL reify-cli defect, and it is this task's scope now: with stdout wired to a closed pipe, reify panics and exits 101 with 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)'. Watcher reproduced it on main: target/debug/reify --version into a pre-closed pipe gives rc=101 and a panic at std/src/io/stdio.rs. Nothing in crates/reify-cli handles SIGPIPE. FIX: restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE at the top of reify-cli's main(), in a small sigpipe module (unix-only, no-op elsewhere). Files: crates/reify-cli/{Cargo.toml,src/main.rs,src/sigpipe.rs}, Cargo.lock, tests/harness_cli_surface.rs, tests/harness_cli_surface/cli_broken_pipe.rs. Write two RED tests first: `reify --version` and `reify cache stats` into a closed pipe must NOT exit 101 or print a panic. The reify-audit binaries have the same exposure; that follow-up is filed separately.

--- ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION ---
Agent piped a Rust binary's stdout into `head --short` (not a valid head option); head exited immediately on the bad flag, closing the pipe, and the upstream Rust process then panicked on SIGPIPE ('failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe') while still writing. The panic trace is the visually dominant part of the output, obscuring the actual root cause (the unrecognized head flag) printed just above it.

Evidence:
- head: unrecognized option '--short'
...thread 'main' (4068124) panicked at library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9:
failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)

Observed in 1 sighting(s) (project: reify).
Analysis: PREMISE VERIFIED on this branch (task/7906 == main 1cdfa6bdb9, no prior commits): with stdout wired to a pipe whose read end was closed before spawn, the prebuilt target/debug/reify exits rc=101 for BOTH `reify --version` and `REIFY_CACHE_DIR=<empty tmp> reify cache stats`, with stderr "thread 'main' panicked at .../library/std/src/io/stdio.rs:1165:9: failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)". Measured with a python os.pipe()/close(r) driver. On a normal (open) stdout both commands write ZERO bytes to stderr.

ROOT CAUSE: the Rust runtime sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN before main, so write(2) to a reader-less pipe returns EPIPE and println! panics. Nothing in crates/reify-cli touches SIGPIPE (Grep for sigpipe/SIG_DFL across crates/ finds only a test comment). The stable toolchain is pinned at 1.96.0 (rust-toolchain.toml); `-Zon-broken-pipe=kill` and the old `#[unix_sigpipe]` attribute are nightly-only, so the fix is a `libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` call as the first statement of main() (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs:115).

SHAPE:
- New leaf module crates/reify-cli/src/sigpipe.rs exposing one fn `restore_default()` (unix: the unsafe libc call with a `// SAFETY:` note; non-unix: no-op). main.rs gains `mod sigpipe;` beside `mod cache; mod dev; mod mcp_context;` and calls `sigpipe::restore_default();` before `std::env::args()`.
- libc enters reify-cli as `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] libc = "0.2"` (reify-fdm precedent, crates/reify-fdm/Cargo.toml:29-30). libc 0.2.186 is the ONLY locked libc, so Cargo.lock changes by exactly one `"libc",` line in reify-cli's dependency array.
- Tests go in a NEW member of the existing harness `crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli_surface.rs` (seam rule: consumes no tests/common helpers), file `tests/harness_cli_surface/cli_broken_pipe.rs`, declared `#[cfg(unix)]` → `#[path = ...]` → `mod cli_broken_pipe;` (rpath_smoke's ordering). A standalone crates/reify-cli/tests/*.rs is blocked by scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh, so the harness member is the sanctioned shape. harness_cli_surface is ~5.3k lines against a 20k cap.

1. Use a CARRIER task. submit_task(planning_mode=True), then add_dependency(carrier → the deferred real task), then commit_planning(carrier). The carrier's pending step is undispatchable because its dependency is not done.
2. set in-progress with claimant_run_id, then merge-deferred.
3. `git branch -m` to task/<carrier>, then `git worktree move` into .worktrees/<carrier>.
4. merge_request under the carrier id.

reify carrier 8084 for task 7269 used exactly this.

After landing:
- a SOLO carrier stays merge-deferred, so stamp it done kind=merged with the marker sha;
- stamp the real task found_on_main.

Note: on reify, hooks/pre-commit exits immediately on non-main branches, so commits on a reify task branch are cheap. Only main commits run the full workspace verify.

entry_text: Reify decl-level match blocks (`match kind { Hex => sub head : HexHead, _ => sub head : DefaultHead }`) do NOT support a bare `_` wildcard arm at compile time. MEASURED 2026-09-30 with `reify eval`: it errors "match-arm pattern '_' is not a variant of enum 'Kind'" plus "non-exhaustive match". The parser lowers `_` to the pattern string "_", but entity.rs compile_match_arm_decl_group has no wildcard handling. Only the EXPRESSION-form match treats bare `_` as a catch-all. Follow-up ticket tkt_0RV8QPD0JZDHVCH6PQ0PCHDB9Z was filed from task 5967.
target_text: Reify match patterns: `_` is a catch-all wildcard ONLY as an entire match pattern (bare `match k { _ => ... }`), never inside an or-pattern slot (`A | _` or `_ | A`) — there it lowers to an ordinary Identifier/MatchPattern::Variant("_"), not a WildcardPattern. Cause: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:1289-1293 makes `'_'` a sibling of the WHOLE or-production, and both lowering sites in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs (:3468/:3482 `lower_match_arm`, :3618 `lower_match_arm_decl_arm`) decide wildcard by WHOLE-pattern text (`if pattern_text == "_"`). MEASURED 2026-08-02 with `reify eval`: `match k { A | _ => 1mm }` -> `error: non-exhaustive match on 'Kind': missing variant(s) B, C`; `match k { _ | A => 1mm }` -> `Parse error: syntax error`; decl form `match kind { Hex | _ => sub head : DefaultHead }` -> `error: match-arm pattern '_' is not a variant of enum 'Kind'`; bare `match k { _ => 1mm }` DOES evaluate clean. `_` is also a legal BINDABLE ordinary name in Reify (`let _ = 3mm` evaluates to `F._ = 0.003 m`), so it cannot simply be reserved as a keyword. Do NOT "fix" the GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar) to emit WildcardPattern in an or-slot — task #5958 made exactly that change (commit 7b08b457f5) and had to revert it (66262ce122); the anti-recurrence note now lives on the MatchPattern rule in reify.grammar. Whether `A | _` SHOULD become legal catch-all sugar is an open language-design question, tracked as task #5967.

Completed: Merge drop-guard inherits the PRECEDING task's plan targets from a reused _merge-verify worktree — "Merge commit is missing plan target files" cites files that were never the task's
Description: Two instances observed on 2026-08-29 during the reify stranded-branch recovery, with an IDENTICAL blocking message and OPPOSITE correct dispositions. Anyone treating the message as authoritative would either land a fragment or withdraw a finished branch.

INSTANCE A - reify task 4388. Guard cited gui/src/__tests__/viewport/channelTags.test.ts and its companion source file. Those files belong to reify task 6185, are on main, and were never on task/4388. The branch WAS independently partial (metadata.files declares 13 paths, the branch touches 2, coverage 0.15 - the clear outlier in a sweep of 68 branches where the next lowest is 0.50), so it was correctly withdrawn - but NOT for the reason the guard gave. The guard's own citation was a red herring.

INSTANCE B - reify task 5405. Guard cited 8 files belonging to THREE other tasks (reify 5951, 5867, 5718), all of which landed during that session. Measured: none of the 8 is in 5405's metadata.files (17 paths, all reify-audit/PDIAG); git cat-file -e fails for all 8 against the branch, so it never contained them; all 8 POSTDATE the branch's merge-base 6e2faf178f, so a correct merge takes them from the main side unmodified and the merged TREE contains them. merge-tree against main is CLEAN. Delivery coverage 17/17. Resubmitted unchanged and it merged.

LIKELY MECHANISM (hypothesis, not yet confirmed in code). The guard appears to consult a .task/plan.json that PERSISTS in a reused _merge-verify worktree and accumulates targets across successive tasks, then asserts those targets appear in the MERGE COMMIT DIFF. For a file that neither parent changed relative to the other, a merge commit's combined diff is silent - the same semantics that make `git show --stat <merge> -- <path>` print nothing. So the guard cannot distinguish "the branch dropped planned work" from "the branch never owned this file and main supplied it".

WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE. The existing family all concern targets that genuinely ARE the task's own: 990 and 1068 (_check_plan_targets_in_tree correctness and the amend-orphaned-commit false positive, both done); 1587, 3004 and 3110 (path normalization, external-repo paths, and post-declaration renames in _check_plan_files_touched_in_branch, all done); 3918 (pending - the base..HEAD range failing to measure the task's own contribution, in wrong-branch / mixed-stack / quarantined-lane shapes). This report is a distinct FOREIGN-PLAN shape: the cited targets were never this task's at all, and arrive from another task's state. If it is in fact a manifestation of 3918's third shape or of a plan-artifact lifecycle bug rather than a gate bug, say so and fold it in rather than fixing it twice.

SUGGESTED PROBE, in order:
1. Determine whether the guard reads the plan from the MERGE WORKTREE on disk or from the task record. If from disk, that is the bug - a reused worktree carries the previous task's plan.
2. Determine whether _merge-verify (or any reused _merge-* worktree) is cleaned of .task/ between tasks.
3. Determine whether the guard should test the merged TREE for the targets (git ls-tree / cat-file -e against the merge commit) instead of the merge commit's combined DIFF, which is silent for a file neither parent changed.

ACCEPTANCE. A regression test that reproduces a merge where a planned-target path exists in the merged tree but is absent from the merge commit's combined diff, and asserts the guard does NOT block. Plus a test that a plan.json left behind by a previous task in a reused merge worktree cannot influence the current task's target set.

PROVENANCE. Recorded by reify recovery session 4 (2026-08-29) in /home/leo/.claude/fleet/recovery/reify-ledger.json under key MERGE_GUARD_DEFECT_missing_plan_target_files, with the full per-instance evidence. Filed by se…[truncated, 9827 chars total]

target_text: reify type aliases: `CompiledTypeAlias.type_expr` is populated UNCONDITIONALLY for every user-declared alias — both `TypeAliasEntry` construction sites (crates/reify-compiler/src/type_resolution.rs:3676 and :3713) set `Some(decl.type_expr.clone())` regardless of `type_params`, and `into_compiled` (:76-85) carries it verbatim. The `type_params.is_empty() => None` narrowing at :107-111 is ONLY in `from_compiled_for_prelude`, which builds registry entries for prelude-seeded aliases, and those are never re-exported (:194) so they never reach consumers. MERGE-LANE RATCHET, THE GAMING SHAPE A REVIEWER WILL CATCH (measured task 5024, γ1, reviewer suggestion "metric-gaming"): `private_reads` in scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py counts EVERY `ast.Attribute` whose attr starts with one underscore, on ANY receiver — it has no idea whether the attribute belongs to production or was invented by the test itself on a MagicMock. So renaming a test-local slot (`git_ops._stub_advanced_sha` → `git_ops.stub_advanced_sha`, 6 sites) drops the measure by 6 while removing exactly zero coupling to lane internals. It reads as migration progress in the baseline diff and is not.

THE TEST TO APPLY BEFORE MIGRATING ANY private read: grep the production module for the attribute name. Zero hits means the leading underscore was never signalling a production internal, and the honest move is to DELETE the slot, not rename it — the value is the test's own, so it belongs in a local or a class constant passed straight to the kwarg the helper actually reads (here `advanced_sha=`, since task 1997 retired the `GitOps._last_advanced_sha` side channel). That also narrows its lifetime (heuristic 5) instead of parking it on a mock that outlives the call. A nonzero hit count means it IS production coupling and needs a real seam or a recorded residual.

Two corollaries measured in the same pass. (1) Deleting a stash usually orphans its plumbing: `_make_git_ops(last_advanced_sha=...)` had no consumer left, and one caller's local constant turned out never to have reached the helper at all (the call omits `advanced_sha=`, so production's `advanced_sha = advanced_sha or merge_commit_fallback` made the fallback the real subject) — ruff F841 is what surfaces that. (2) Restoring a deleted class-hierarchy assertion costs the ratchet NOTHING if you reach the symbol by `from orchestrator.merge_queue import _WipHaltMixin` (an ImportFrom node) rather than `mq._WipHaltMixin` (an Attribute node, +1 private read). Same fact, same test, one spelling is free and the other raises the measure above baseline.

harness.py ~:9145 captures `task_metadata = (assignment.task.get('metadata') or {})` — the DISPATCH-TIME snapshot, the same dict object as TaskWorkflow.self.task['metadata']. Then at ~:9309-9315:

    await self.scheduler.update_task(

_reconcile_scope_locks persists the refined metadata.files BACKEND-ONLY and never refreshes self.task['metadata'], so that snapshot keeps its pre-plan `files` for the whole run. target_text: Pattern for live-smoke-verifying an MCP connection-capability header end-to-end: (1) start create_server(queue, startup_sweep=False).run_http_async(...) on a free port in a daemon thread, polling raw TCP connect for readiness instead of sleeping; (2) seed pending records directly via EscalationQueue.submit() (bypasses MCP tools); (3) build the exact production mcp_config via the real config-building function (e.g. McpLifecycle.mcp_config_json) rather than hand-rolling one, so the smoke proves the production code path; (4) drive a real `claude` CLI agent via invoke_agent(..., mcp_config=..., allowed_tools=[only the tools under test], output_schema=...) restricted to just the tools being verified; (5) treat the agent's structured_output as corroborating evidence only — the actual assertion must re-read the underlying store (e.g. queue.get(id)) as ground truth, since a misbehaving/hallucinating agent could self-report a false pass.

entry_text: Gotcha (socket-activated user units, verified 2026-09-29): (1) First migration of a running service onto a newly installed .socket needs only an ordinary `systemctl --user restart <service>` - systemd orders the old process's stop before the socket's start, and the new process gets LISTEN_FDS. (2) Changing an ACTIVE socket's ListenStream set needs `systemctl --user stop <service>` then `systemctl --user start <x>.socket <service>` - a combined `restart <x>.socket <service>` fails with 'Socket service <service> already active, refusing'. (3) In ExecStopPost, `systemctl --user list-jobs <unit>` shows TYPE `restart` during a restart, `stop` during a stop, and no job during a crash awaiting auto-restart - that is what scripts/stop-socket-unless-restarting.sh keys on.

GOTCHA (verified 2026-09-16, task 5544): `fused-memory.service` is a systemd --USER unit. A system-scope `journalctl -u fused-memory.service` returns `-- No entries --` AND EXITS 0 — it looks exactly like "the logs are gone" rather than "you asked the wrong journal". Every read must be `journalctl --user -u fused-memory.service ...`. `systemctl is-active fused-memory.service` lies the same way (reports `inactive` while the unit is active); use `systemctl --user`. This is the same scope the orchestrator watchdog uses (`scripts/orchestrator-watchdog.py` shells `systemctl --user`), so its restart lines and fm's own lines are in the SAME user journal.

Retention measured that day: the user journal reached back to 2026-08-24 (~3 weeks), so incident windows weeks old are still readable.

PAIR THIS WITH THE EXISTING LOAD WARNING (memory a398ae1a, 2026-08-19: twelve concurrent journalctl scans of this same unit burned 906% CPU on a 4.5 GB journal, 7-23 min each, driving host load to ~127). Both halves bite together: an unbounded `--since` over several days does NOT finish inside the Bash tool's 120000ms default timeout — measured twice in task 5544, where `--since "2026-09-06"` and `--since "2026-09-13"` both had to be backgrounded and were still running minutes later. PRACTICE: bound the window to the minutes you actually need (`--since`/`--until` on the same day), add `-o short-iso --no-pager`, and extract once to a file and grep that rather than re-streaming the unit per question.

entry_text: To test a Rust binary's behaviour on a closed stdout deterministically in reify, create the pipe with `std::io::pipe()` (stable since 1.87; toolchain is 1.96.0), `drop(reader)` BEFORE spawning, and pass the `PipeWriter` as `.stdout(writer)`. The child's first write then always meets no reader. Don't use `Stdio::piped()` and drop `ChildStdout` afterwards: that races the child's write into the pipe buffer and can flake to exit 0. Expected outcomes: a stock Rust binary exits 101 with the 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe' panic, because the runtime ignores SIGPIPE before main. After a `libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` reset, `ExitStatusExt::signal() == Some(libc::SIGPIPE)` (python returncode -13). The python `os.pipe(); os.close(r)` driver reproduces the same thing outside cargo (task 7906).
target_text: reify-cli panicked with exit 101 'failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe' when stdout is a closed pipe (verified 2026-09-27 on main: target/debug/reify --version into a pre-closed pipe). There was no SIGPIPE handling in crates/reify-cli. Task 7906 was rescoped to restore SIG_DFL for SIGPIPE at the top of main(); task 7955 covers the same exposure in the reify-audit binaries.

entry_text: faer 0.24 dense `gevd_real` (QZ) panics in reify DEBUG builds with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' at faer-0.24.0/src/linalg/gevd/qz_real/mod.rs:2287. Cause: aggressive_early_deflation sets `kwbot = kwtop.wrapping_sub(1)` (line 2222) when the deflation window starts at row 0, then computes `ihi - kwbot`. That wraps to the correct LAPACK value in release, but the generic QZ is monomorphised in reify-solver-elastic, which keeps dev overflow-checks on, so root `[profile.dev.package."*"]` overflow-checks=false does NOT help. Cheap reproducer: solve_eigen_dense on K=tridiag(-1,2,-1) n=136 with B tridiagonal (diag +1 for i<n/2, -0.5 after, off-diagonals 0.2). It passes with `cargo test --config 'profile.dev.package."reify-solver-elastic".overflow-checks=false'`. Task #7602 plans that profile override as the guard.
target_text: faer 0.24's generic dense QZ (`gevd_real`, used by reify's `solve_eigen_dense`) relies on usize wrapping in aggressive early deflation (qz_real/mod.rs:2222/2287). It panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in any crate compiled with overflow-checks on, e.g. on an indefinite-B 136-DOF pencil. Since task 7602, the root Cargo.toml sets `overflow-checks = false` in `[profile.dev.package.reify-solver-elastic]` for this reason. Do not re-enable it. A new crate that monomorphises gevd_real needs the same override. Tripwire test: `dense_solve_completes_on_the_indefinite_136dof_pencil`.

Wrap everything after `worker_task = asyncio.create_task(worker.run())` in `try:`. Put `await worker.stop()` plus a `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` join in its `finally:`, INSIDE `with patch(...)`. target_text:
GOTCHA (measured task 5066, 2026-09-14): a static guard can be scoped BY THE SYMBOL A CALL SITE USES, so migrating call sites to a better helper silently OPTS THE ENCLOSING TEST INTO that guard. The migration's blast radius is therefore not just the lines you edit — it is every guard keyed on the NEW symbol's name. This is a different mechanism from the file-glob scope gotcha in memory 0983aa97 (guards with different rglob patterns); here the scan sees the file either way, and what changes is whether the METHOD matches the guard's predicate.

THE CASE. Task 5066 migrated 15 gate barriers in orchestrator/tests/ from raw `asyncio.wait_for(gate_x.wait(), timeout=15.0)` to `wait_responsive(..., timeout=MERGE_GATE_BARRIER_TIMEOUT, label=...)`. Unrelated-looking guard `test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py::TestLoudWaitMigrationRatchet::test_migrated_methods_stop_worker_in_finally` went red naming five methods that the migration had not otherwise touched. Its helper `_unguarded_worker_teardown_methods` is explicitly "deliberately scoped to methods that call `wait_responsive`" — the module has ~25 pre-existing straight-line teardown sites it ignores, because its job is to stop the MIGRATED set from regressing. Adopting the symbol is what enrolled those five.

WHY THE GUARD WAS RIGHT AND THE FIX IS FORWARD, NOT BACK. `wait_responsive` gives up by raising `_pytest.outcomes.Failed` (a BaseException subclass), so a straight-line body skips `worker.stop()` and leaks a live merge worker plus its run task into pytest-asyncio teardown — the documented mechanism (task 4219) by which ONE red test cascades into unrelated failures elsewhere in the session. The five methods had that exposure all along; the migration merely made it VISIBLE. Reverting the migration would have re-hidden it. The fix is to complete the migration: wrap the `with patch(...)` body in `try:` / `finally:` with the stop+join INSIDE the patch block (the shape test_merge_speculation.py::_stop_worker blesses), and drop any redundant manual stop on a give-up path — the guard requires EVERY worker-stop call to sit in a crediting `finally:` whose `try:` encloses EVERY `wait_responsive` call, so one stray straight-line stop keeps the method red.

THE CHEAP PRE-CHECK, before a symbol-adoption migration: grep the test tree for the symbol you are ADOPTING, not just the one you are replacing, and read any guard that mentions it. `grep -rn "wait_responsive" orchestrator/tests/ | grep -i "guard\|ratchet\|offender"` would have surfaced this in one command, before the 42-minute whole-suite run did.

GENERAL SHAPE WORTH REMEMBERING: a well-built repo guard that is "deliberately scoped to sites using X" turns adopting X into a contract, not just an improvement. That is good design — it ratchets — but it means a mechanical-looking migration can carry real obligations. Budget for them in the same task; do not assume a nominal-preserving swap is behaviour-free.

target_text: Reify `// G-allow:` markers: never cite the CURRENT task's `#NNNN` in a marker body. `crates/reify-audit/tests/g_allow_repo_wide_hard_gate.rs` Test B is live (not `#[ignore]`d) and asserts ZERO `g-allow-orphaned` from `ptodo::check()` over the real repo — and a cite to a task whose status is done/cancelled is a Severity::High `g-allow-orphaned`. entry_text: Gotcha: the GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar) accepts `aux` only before `sub`, not before `let`, even though tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js accepts `aux let`. Any `.ri` under examples/ or tests/prd-gate/fixtures/ that gui/src/__tests__/reifyGrammarCorpus.test.ts pins in EXPECTED_CLEAN will fail the drift ledger as a 'grammar regressed' error if it gains an `aux let`. On a geometry let, `aux` only sets default viewport visibility (realization_is_aux -> default_visible), so a plain `let` is a safe substitute in such fixtures.
target_text: Reify GUI Lezer grammar (gui/src/editor/reify.grammar), as of 2026-10-01 before task 7092 lands: LetDeclaration has NO `pub`/`priv`/`aux` prefix, although grammar.js `let_declaration` has `optional(choice('pub','priv')) optional('aux') 'let'`. As a result `aux let x = 1mm`, `pub let …` and `priv let …` each produce 1 error node in the editor, while the compiler parses all three (`priv let` then gets the semantic error E_PRIV_REDUNDANT). Task 7092 widens it. A cheap way to prototype a grammar change with no tracked-file churn: copy reify.grammar to gui/src/editor/zzProbe.grammar, run `npx lezer-generator` with `-o src/editor/zzProbeParser.js` (the generated file imports ./highlight, so it must sit in the same directory), import both parsers in a throwaway vitest file to diff error counts across the corpus, then delete all the probe files.
