entry_text: Workspace layering for test-support code shared across packages (measured 2026-10-04, task 5402). shared/tests cannot import orchestrator. shared is the bottom layer and its pyproject has no pythonpath to orchestrator/src. fused-memory/tests CAN import orchestrator, because fused-memory/pyproject.toml sets pythonpath = ["src", "../orchestrator/src"]. So any helper all three suites must share has to live in shared/src/shared/, and shared src modules stay pytest-free by convention (see shared/src/shared/testing_reify_layout.py). Pytest runtime differs by package: shared uses timeout_method="signal" with NO xdist, while orchestrator and fused-memory use thread + -n auto + --max-worker-restart=0. All three verify test_commands pass --timeout=300.
target_text: Cross-package test helpers belong in shared/src/shared/<module>.py, NOT shared/tests/: the wheel packages only src/shared, shared/tests has no __init__.py, and both orchestrator and fused-memory already declare dark-factory-shared as a workspace dep and wire ../shared/src onto sys.path in their own tests/conftest.py (so it resolves even under `uv run --directory <pkg>`, where the ROOT conftest is never loaded). Precedent: shared/src/shared/testing.py is a pure pytest helper imported from fused-memory/tests/. Two constraints when adding such a module: do NOT re-export it from shared/__init__.py (shared/tests/test_public_api.py asserts shared.__all__ equals a hardcoded union and goes red), and do NOT import pytest at module level (pytest is a dev-group dep, not a [project] dep) — expose pure functions returning skip-reason strings and let each call site build its own pytest.skip/skipif.

entry_text: Giving shared.usage_gate.UsageGate.invoke_slot a new keyword that shared.cli_invoke.invoke_with_cap_retry forwards breaks four hand-written invoke_slot test doubles that don't take **kwargs, and they live in two packages. In shared: shared/tests/test_cli_invoke_sandbox_wrap.py (_FakeGate.invoke_slot). In orchestrator: orchestrator/tests/test_dry_run_unblock.py (_ForcedCapUsageGate.invoke_slot), plus `_attach_invoke_slot._cm` in BOTH orchestrator/tests/test_steward.py and orchestrator/tests/test_invoke.py. The shared suite stays green, so this only shows up on a full orchestrator run. Task 6042's `park=` keyword updated only the first two, and 25 steward/invoke tests failed with "_cm() got an unexpected keyword argument". Put all four files in the task's scope up front.
target_text: Regression pattern: when a task changes a shared API signature (e.g. task 2856/β added a `scope` kwarg to `UsageGate.invoke_slot`, and cli_invoke.invoke_with_cap_retry now calls `invoke_slot(scope=scope)`), file-scoped per-attempt verifies only run the touched file's tests and therefore MISS fake/mock test doubles in OTHER test files that hardcode the old signature. β updated 2 of the invoke_slot fake factories but left 5 others red on main (shared/tests/test_cli_invoke_sandbox_wrap.py, test_liveness_boundary_gate.py; orchestrator/tests/test_dry_run_unblock.py, test_steward.py::_attach_invoke_slot, test_invoke.py). These stayed hidden until a downstream task's (2857/γ) FULL-suite merge gate ran. Fix pattern: give every fake `invoke_slot` additive back-compat (`scope=None` on defs, `*_a, **_kw` on lambdas). Guidance: when changing a shared/mocked signature, grep the whole repo for all test doubles of that symbol (`def invoke_slot`, `invoke_slot =`, `side_effect=lambda`) and run the full cross-package suite, not just the file-scoped verify.

target_text: Gotcha found in fused-memory/scripts/bake_off_storage_shape.py (task 4004): a provenance block can record fixture sha256 digests that NOTHING ever compares — `fetch_cache_provenance` stored `fixture_digests(...)` while every read of the provenance dict only touched corpus_fingerprints, search_limit, guard_threshold and embedder_model, so a stale cache replayed clean. entry_text: dark_factory merge lane, measured 2026-10-03 by the task-5302 architect (read-only: runs.db, git, journal). The 2026-08-12 (mr-763d254b/task 3956) and 2026-08-28 (mr-4ee12a75/task 3122, mr-627b607f) non-empty reads of snapshot()['two_layer_invariants'] were NOT detector false positives. They are a genuine INV-3 gap. Main moves under an in-flight head (e.g. a human direct commit). The head then lands REBASED (rebased_pending_reverify / gate_retry), and that landing branch in merge_lane/worker.py never calls _record_dead_base for the head's pre-rebase merge commit. The successor, built on that orphaned commit at depth 0, passes INV-3's dead-base checks and verifies on a base that never reaches main. IMPORTANT REFINEMENT to the 2026-08-21 claim that the red main "blocks every merge reaching the post-merge gate" — that was TOO STRONG and is now falsified. Attempt 1 (mr-831c3587) was blocked citing fused-memory's test_it_reuses_the_bake_offs_cell_renderer as "not present on main". Attempt 2 (mr-42afb0b5), submitted a day later, LANDED — while that test was STILL failing on main (re-measured 2026-08-22 on main at 38e4f123d2: 1 failed in 18.61s). In between, six other merges landed, one of which (c63e902c79, task 4458) touched 7 fused-memory files.

So the mis-attribution was a TIMING artifact of the per-main-sha failing-id baseline, not a standing repo-wide gate: a merge that hits the gate before the baseline for that main sha has recorded a given failure gets it charged as "new", i.e. as a BRANCH_BUG; once later merges seed the baseline, the same failure is recognised as pre-existing and no longer blocks. The underlying baseline defect is still real (a red main should be reported as red, not charged to an innocent branch) and remains filed as task 4583, but its blast radius is a window, not the whole queue. Practical rule: a merge blocked on a test your diff cannot touch may simply be EARLY relative to the baseline — re-measure the test on bare main, and a plain resubmit later can succeed with nothing changed.

Second attempt profile, for anyone sizing this gate: queue empty, position 0, no two_layer_invariants violations, retries_total 0; verify ran ~39 min of unscoped all-module (test + lint + type) work before finalizing. That is normal, not a wedge.

entry_text: When an interactive session's escalation MCP client has given up but the orchestrator is running, do NOT take merge-queue's direct-merge fallback (it races the merge worker). Call the tools over HTTP with a tiny script using mcp.client.streamable_http.streamablehttp_client + ClientSession against http://127.0.0.1:8102/mcp (merge_request with wait_secs=100, then poll merge_status by request_id). Same trick reaches fused-memory on 8002 (e.g. add_memory) when the session's fused-memory client is disconnected.
target_text: The escalation MCP can be disconnected from a specific Claude Code session even while an escalation.watcher process is running on the host for a different project (e.g. reify). When the merge-queue skill probes for the escalation MCP and finds it unreachable, the correct fallback is direct merge (`git merge --no-ff`) — not waiting or retrying. Saw this 2026-04-26 in dark-factory: merge_request was a deferred MCP tool that disconnected mid-session while reify's escalation.watcher was still active. Direct-merge fallback is safe when no orchestrator process for *this* project is running (check pgrep -af 'orchestrator.*harness' for the relevant project root).

entry_text: Reify verify triage gotcha: if every command in .task/verify/attempt-N.summary.json has rc=1 with duration_secs of a few ms, and the type step (whose command is literally `true`) also failed, with logs reading only "Command failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files", then the orchestrator's spawner hit EMFILE before verify.sh ever ran. That is no evidence about the branch. Do not edit code. Re-run the checks from `./scripts/verify.sh <test|lint> --scope branch --include-infra --print-plan` directly (e.g. cargo clippy/nextest -p <crate>) to confirm green, and file escalate_info with category=infra_issue (observed on task 6504, 2026-10-04).
target_text: A dark-factory verify failure whose .task/verify/attempt-N.*.log files contain only "Command failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files", with summary.json durations of about 1 ms (even for the literal `true` type command), means the orchestrator process could not spawn the commands at all. The code was never exercised, so nothing in the branch needs fixing. Look at the orchestrator's RLIMIT_NOFILE: the reify orchestrator python runs with soft limit 1024. Re-verify by hand, but note that `verify.sh test` can sit for a long time in test_slot_starvation admission. Running the touched crates' `cargo test` binaries directly confirms green faster.

entry_text: fused-memory TargetedReconciler journal-row convention (targeted.py, tasks 4903/4977/5273): every add_run_action row names target = the system written to ('taskmaster', 'escalation', 'memory', ...) and operation = the call actually made ('set_task_status', 'update_task', 'set_task_claimant', 'submit'). Write symmetric 'write' (landed) / 'skip' (refused or raised, with detail.error from _write_error_code or str(e)[:200]) rows, and for the cancelled-parent sweep set detail.type EQUAL to the returned action type ('descendant_cancelled'/'descendant_blocked'/'descendant_escalated'). A second write on the same path gets its own operation (and a distinct detail.type like 'unblock_metadata_stamp' / 'unblock_claimant_clear') so existing set_task_status query cardinalities don't change. An absent optional escalation package stays journal-silent (degraded env, not a failure).
target_text:
Completed: TargetedReconciler: clear the stale claimant on dependent-unblock, and journal the L1 escalation sweep
Description: Two robustness gaps in TargetedReconciler, both confined to reconciliation/targeted.py and its test file. _unblock_dependent re-pends a blocked dependent without first clearing its stale claimant_run_id/heartbeat_at, so a task this sweep 'unblocks' can sit pending-but-undispatchable until the heartbeat TTL expires — the orchestrator's equivalent sweep already clears the claimant for exactly this reason. And _sweep_escalate_l1, the only sync member of the cancelled-parent dispatch triad, files a real L1 escalation without emitting any journal row, leaving two of three branches auditable via get_run_actions and one not.

This task closes both: a claimant-clearing write with a deliberate, test-pinned failure policy on the unblock path, and a journal row plus the async/run_id threading that emitting one requires on the escalate path.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on base aeb23fbadd (worktree HEAD == main, no branch commits):
- fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/targeted.py::TargetedReconciler._unblock_dependent exists. The order is: interceptor-wired guard -> _unblock_veto_reason -> escalation-pin veto -> live status re-read (TOCTOU guard) -> set_task_status('pending') -> 'write'/'skip' journal row -> metadata stamp (update_task, metadata_mode='merge'), which records but never downgrades (metadata_stamp='rejected'|'failed', journal 'write'/'skip' under operation='update_task', type='unblock_metadata_stamp'). No claimant clear exists.
- TaskInterceptor.set_task_claimant (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/task_interceptor.py::TaskInterceptor.set_task_claimant) is a public, reachable method on the self.task_interceptor the reconciler already holds. It is tri-state: explicit None clears the column to NULL. It takes no write-lock and passes no gates; it delegates to sqlite_task_backend.py::SqliteTaskBackend.set_task_claimant. On success that returns {'id', 'message'}; it raises TaskmasterError on an unknown id, and returns a message-only dict as a fail-safe when the claimant columns are absent. The routing question is therefore settled: call it through the interceptor, which is the same object every other sweep write uses. No new wiring is needed.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked clears via set_task_claimant(tid, claimant_run_id=None, heartbeat_at=None) IMMEDIATELY BEFORE set_task_status(tid,'pending'), best-effort, never blocking the flip. Its stated reason for clear-BEFORE-flip: a concurrent dispatch right after the task goes pending can never have its fresh stamp clobbered by a late-landing clear.
- Task 4977 HAS landed on main (commits 9b0ae53944 / 2ce07b0c01 are ancestors of HEAD). run_id is threaded into _sweep_cancel_orphan and _sweep_block_orphan, both of which emit symmetric write/skip rows: target='taskmaster', operation='set_task_status'|'update_task', and detail.type EQUAL to the returned action type ('descendant_cancelled' / 'descendant_blocked'). The SEQUENCING WARNING in the task is therefore resolved: build directly on 4977's convention.

entry_text: Counting tests from a captured cargo-nextest log (measured on nextest 0.9.136, 2026-10-01, task 7896): `grep '^test result'` double-counts in two ways. (a) With `--no-capture`, each nextest TEST prints its own UNINDENTED libtest line, e.g. `test result: ok. 1 passed; ... 2 filtered out`. (b) A failing test's replayed stdout carries an INDENTED `    test result: FAILED. ...` line. For a nextest capture, trust only the `Summary [..] N tests run: X passed (k slow), F failed, T timed out, S skipped` line; a partial run shows as `N/M tests run`. A `Starting N tests across M binaries` header with no Summary line means the run was killed.
target_text: Empirically verified facts about the installed cargo-nextest 0.9.136, useful for any future nextest-config or failure-capture work in reify: (1) No --junit CLI flag exists on `cargo nextest run`/`list`; JUnit output is config-file-only via `[profile.<name>.junit]\npath = "..."` in nextest.toml, resolved by nextest to `<target-dir>/nextest/<profile-name>/<path>`. (2) A JUnit `<testcase name="...">`'s bare name attribute (e.g. `cache::tests::foo`, never package/binary-prefixed) is exactly what nextest's own `-E 'test(=<id>)'` exact-match filterset matches — a package-prefixed id like `reify-config::cache::tests::foo` matches ZERO tests ("no tests to run"). (3) Failing testcases carry a `<failure>` or `<error>` child element; passing ones are empty. (4) nextest's default is FAIL-FAST (not documented prominently) — without an explicit `--no-fail-fast`, tests scheduled after an early failure are not run at all (not even attributed as "skipped" — nextest prints "N tests were not run due to test failure"), so any manifest/capture mechanism needing the COMPLETE failed set must pass --no-fail-fast explicitly. (5) `cargo nextest run` exits 100 (not 1) when the run completes cleanly but ≥1 test failed; any other exit code (124 from an outer timeout wrapper, a signal, etc.) means the run did not complete cleanly and its JUnit report cannot be trusted as complete. Reminder: bypass the cargo/rustc skim condensation hook for exploratory `cargo nextest` invocations with `env cargo nextest ...` (plain `cargo nextest run --help` gets silently rewritten into the skim wrapper's own usage text).

entry_text: faer 0.24's generic dense QZ (`gevd_real`, used by reify's `solve_eigen_dense`) relies on usize wrapping in aggressive early deflation (qz_real/mod.rs:2222/2287). It panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow" in any crate compiled with overflow-checks on, e.g. on an indefinite-B 136-DOF pencil. Since task 7602, the root Cargo.toml sets `overflow-checks = false` in `[profile.dev.package.reify-solver-elastic]` for this reason. Do not re-enable it. A new crate that monomorphises gevd_real needs the same override. Tripwire test: `dense_solve_completes_on_the_indefinite_136dof_pencil`.
target_text: faer 0.24 dense `gevd_real` (QZ) panics in reify DEBUG builds with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' at faer-0.24.0/src/linalg/gevd/qz_real/mod.rs:2287. Cause: aggressive_early_deflation sets `kwbot = kwtop.wrapping_sub(1)` (line 2222) when the deflation window starts at row 0, then computes `ihi - kwbot`. That wraps to the correct LAPACK value in release, but the generic QZ is monomorphised in reify-solver-elastic, which keeps dev overflow-checks on, so root `[profile.dev.package."*"]` overflow-checks=false does NOT help. Cheap reproducer: solve_eigen_dense on K=tridiag(-1,2,-1) n=136 with B tridiagonal (diag +1 for i<n/2, -0.5 after, off-diagonals 0.2). It passes with `cargo test --config 'profile.dev.package."reify-solver-elastic".overflow-checks=false'`. Task #7602 plans that profile override as the guard.

entry_text: Kernel linkage facts for the production `reify` binary (verified 2026-09-28 on main 5340545275): reify-cli/src/main.rs force-links OCCT, Manifold (unconditional) and OpenVDB (cfg has_openvdb) via `extern crate` so their inventory capability descriptors survive the linker. Gmsh is NOT force-linked — it reaches the CLI only FUNCTIONALLY through reify-solver-elastic's real FEA meshing calls → reify-eval → reify-cli; if the elastic solver ever drops its direct reify_kernel_gmsh calls for a pure-Rust mesher, Gmsh's GeometryKernel capability silently stops shipping with no compile error. Fidget has no path at all (see the #8010 decision). reify-config lists all five kernel crates but ONLY as [dev-dependencies] for tests/kernel_name_consistency.rs (task 3139 / esc-3123-85) — its production library is adapter-free, so a Cargo.toml grep that hits reify-config is not evidence of production linkage. Also: `sweep(profile, path)` → OCCT make_pipe is a thin BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe with NO auto-orientation of the profile to the path's start tangent (an in-plane profile sweeps to a silent zero), whereas `pipe(path, radius)` builds an oriented circle at the start frame first — a likely source of 'sweep produced a twisted/zero solid' reports that are not kernel bugs.
target_text: reify-eval's "gmsh-build-free" invariant (task 4743, reify-eval/Cargo.toml:140-165) is about SYMBOL NAMING, not about libgmsh being absent from the link graph. Production reify-eval already reaches libgmsh unconditionally: sweep_classifier.rs:786 calls reify_solver_elastic::mesh_swept_profile_2d, whose mesher.rs:435/457/525 call reify_kernel_gmsh::mesh_profile_2d::mesh_plane_2d with no cfg gate (reify-solver-elastic normal-deps reify-kernel-gmsh and its build.rs does not re-derive has_gmsh). The OCCT-only kernel_count/registry-size assertions stay green because the linker pulls only the needed rlib archive members and register.rs's inventory::submit! CGU is not among them. So calling another gmsh-reaching reify-solver-elastic function from reify-eval adds no new linkage risk; naming a reify_kernel_gmsh::* symbol directly is what pulls the register CGU and breaks those assertions. To use a gmsh type from reify-eval, re-export it from reify-solver-elastic instead.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, task 4484): an agent-authored ledger, gate, or plan step that requires a TASK ID for filed follow-up work is UNSATISFIABLE by an agent at filing time. `submit_task` is two-phase and returns `{"ticket": "tkt_..."}` only; the curator decides create/combine/drop asynchronously; and the agent operating instructions explicitly forbid calling `resolve_ticket`. So no task id exists when the agent writes the record.

DISTINCT from the existing `resolve-ticket-timeout-discriminator` topic, which is about how to interpret a resolve_ticket TIMEOUT. This is about the id-AVAILABILITY contract for agent-side records: the id is simply not available yet, timeout or not.

MEASURED. Task 4484's plan step-9 said "backfill their ids into the justifications (flipping `to_file` -> `filed`)", and the gate it targeted (`shared/tests/test_loop_blocking_gate.py::TestAllowlistHygiene::test_filed_entries_name_their_task`) asserts `re.search(r'\b\d{3,5}\b', justification)` on every `filed` row. Eleven `submit_task` calls returned eleven tickets and zero task ids, so flipping the rows would either turn the gate red or bless a row pointing at a decision the curator had not made.

PRACTICE when you hit this shape:
1. Keep the pre-filing disposition (`to_file`, `pending`, whatever the vocabulary calls it) and record the TICKET id in the row. A ticket is durable and greppable; it is a real pointer, just not a task pointer.
2. State the reason ONCE — in a module docstring or schema comment — rather than repeating it per row; INV-9 (one-fact-one-home) applies to the explanation as much as to the data.
3. Name "flip to `filed` with the task id when the ticket resolves" as explicit follow-up work in the artifact, so the intermediate state is a recorded step and not drift.
4. File an `escalate_info` recording the deviation (task-3890 precedent): the plan text stays frozen in plan.json, so a reviewer diffing plan against code otherwise reads it as an oversight.

FOR PLAN AUTHORS: do not write a step that requires an agent to record a task id for work it files itself. Write "record the ticket id" instead, or make the gate accept either shape.

entry_text: In reify-compiler, every operand in a boolean geometry position (union/difference/... args) is ALSO value-compiled before realization lowering: a top-level geometry let / geometry-list let / geometry param emits a value cell via compile_expr_with_expected over its whole initializer (entity.rs geometry-let arm, task #4954), which runs before the realization-emission third pass. So unknown-member / priv-member / collection-sub value-level diagnostics for a boolean operand are already emitted once; a geometry-position consumer that also renders MemberPathError::to_diagnostic double-reports (measured task 5425 with `reify check`).
target_text: Reify compiles geometry and values in two disjoint worlds, and this is why geometry constructors silently yield Undef in any value-position expression (lambda bodies, list literals). Geometry world: `is_geometry_let` (reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:202) gates `compile_geometry_call` (geometry.rs:1096), producing `Vec<CompiledGeometryOp>` in a `RealizationDecl` referenced by `GeomRef::Step/Sub`, executed by the kernel; `Value::GeometryHandle` is minted only AFTER the build by `post_process_geometry_handle_cells` (reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:9479) or symbolically by `mint_symbolic_geometry_handles_into_values` (engine_eval.rs). Value world: `compile_expr` -> `CompiledExpr` -> `reify_expr::eval_expr`, a pure evaluator with no kernel and no realization context. In value position a geometry call hits the ladder arm `is_geometry_function(name) => Type::dimensionless_scalar()` (expr.rs:3346) and at eval time falls through `reify_stdlib::eval_builtin` to its terminal `Value::Undef` (reify-stdlib/src/lib.rs:301) with no diagnostic. Corollary: geometry can never be constructed at expression-eval time; bridging requires compile-time lowering into a RealizationDecl. Sibling geometry lets are resolved by AST RE-INLINING via `geometry_lets: HashMap<&str, &reify_ast::Expr>` (entity.rs:3769) with a `visiting` cycle guard, not by value references.

Completed: harness.py: gc_run_config_dir unreachable on a second cancellation in shielded finally blocks
Description: Follow-up filed from task 4431 (escalation_id agent-followup-4431), which shielded the `update_run_stage_reports` persistence call in the `finally` blocks of `ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle` (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py, shield site ~line 3560) and `ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass` (~line 5501) against a second asyncio cancellation arriving mid-write.

Residual gap, documented in task 4431's design decision 3 and in "Known residual (task 4431)" code comments at both shield sites: `await asyncio.shield(...)` protects the WRITE itself once it exists as its own Task, but the *awaiting frame* in the `finally` block is still interruptible — a second cancellation arriving while the shielded write is in flight still raises `CancelledError` at that `await asyncio.shield(...)` expression in the outer frame. That means the `gc_run_config_dir` cleanup block immediately following each shield site (harness.py ~3572-3578 for run_full_cycle, ~5512-5518 for _run_remediation_pass) remains unreachable on that path — exactly as it was BEFORE task 4431's fix, so this is not a regression, but it is a real pre-existing gap: a run's per-run recon CLI config dir is not garbage-collected when a second cancellation lands during the finally's persistence write.

Task 4431 deliberately did not fix this (see its design decision 3, verbatim): "Swallowing BaseException around the shielded await would be safe on the exception paths (an exception raised inside a finally that is already unwinding does not suppress the propagating exception), but NOT on the success path: after `return run` at ~3441, a swallow would let an outer `.cancel()` be absorbed and the task complete with a return value instead of cancelling — an uncancellable coroutine, a semantics change well beyond this task's remit." Resolving this residual requires a design that discriminates "safe to swallow because we are already unwinding due to a previous cancellation" from "the return-path completion the outer caller is legitimately trying to cancel" — that discrimination is the actual scope of this follow-up. Until it's solved, the GC block simply stays skipped on this narrow double-cancellation race, same as today.

Files: fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/harness.py — both `finally` blocks (ReconciliationHarness.run_full_cycle and ReconciliationHarness._run_remediation_pass).

Suggested priority: low — pre-existing behavior (not a regression from task 4431), and the blast radius is bounded to one leaked per-run config dir per occurrence of this narrow double-cancellation race.

CORRECTION to the task-4431 residual note (memory 2a2b23f1): code after `await asyncio.shield(w)` in a cleanup `finally` can be made reachable on a second cancellation WITHOUT any BaseException swallow. Wrap it as `try: await asyncio.shield(w)` with `finally: <synchronous cleanup>`. The cleanup runs and the CancelledError still propagates, so the coroutine stays cancellable even on a success-path `return`.

Measured on CPython 3.13.9 for both the double-cancel path and a success-path cancel: cleanup ran, and task.cancelled() was True. No "already unwinding vs success path" discrimination is needed. It is only safe if the finally's cleanup has no awaits. Task 5128 plans this for harness.py's gc_run_config_dir tail via a shared ReconciliationHarness._persist_stage_reports_then_gc_config_dir helper.

entry_text: scan_memory_content CANNOT find ordinary text. Its custom needles are only a store-side prefilter; every candidate is then re-verified with the shared tool-call-leak detector (fused_memory.utils.toolcall_xml_leak), which is the authoritative verdict. Measured 2026-09-28: needles like 'omitting entities' / 'DeclaredReferentConflict' returned scanned=6, matches=0 for dark_factory and 0/0 for every other project although four matching records exist. 'scanned' counts prefilter candidates, not corpus size. For a literal-text hunt use search(query=..., stores=['mem0'], limit=15) per project and filter the results client-side; that is how the four 'omit entities' records were located.
target_text:
`scan_memory_content` cannot be used as a general literal-substring search over Mem0, despite accepting a `needles` argument. It re-verifies EVERY store-side prefilter hit with the shared tool-call-XML-leak detector (`fused_memory.utils.toolcall_xml_leak`), and that detector is the authoritative verdict — so a custom needle returns `matches: []` no matter what the text actually contains, while `scanned` reports the prefilter hit count.

Observed 2026-08-05: `scan_memory_content(project_id='dark_factory', needles=['task/task/'], filters={'category':'procedural_knowledge'})` returned `matches: []` with `scanned: 6`. The empty match list was an artifact of the wrong detector; the 6 was the real prefilter hit count. Reading that as "no entries contain this string" would have been wrong.

STILL LIVE 2026-08-19, AND NOW POSITIVE-CONTROL VALIDATED (recon run c7f6e323-9861-4efe-a432-a67f75499541, Stage 1). The 2026-08-05 observation above could not, on its own, fully exclude the innocent explanation "the string genuinely is not in any record". This run closed that hole with a control: a needle was chosen that was verbatim the FIRST LINE of a record the same session had just read by id AND successfully amended — `needles=['VERIFIED MEM0 TOMBSTONE COVERAGE MAP']`, present in memory c641fb28-bb73-4cf1-afdb-992816b6f9b3. Result: `scanned: 1, matches: []`. The prefilter found the record; the verdict layer discarded it. A string that is CERTAIN to be present returns zero. That is conclusive, and it rules out the innocent explanation for the earlier observations too.

THE TRAP IS THE TOOL'S OWN ADVERTISED PURPOSE. Its docstring sells it as the deterministic answer for exactly the case where "search cannot find a string because it carries no semantic signal" — UUIDs, run_ids, memory ids, identifiers. That is precisely the use case it silently fails, and it fails in the worst direction: a clean, confident, plausible-looking zero rather than an error. Two ways to catch it in the moment: (a) `scanned > 0` with `matches: []` is by itself suspicious — the prefilter found candidates that the verdict layer then threw away; (b) always run a positive control with a needle you have independently proven is present, per the standing repo norm on probes that return a convincing false zero (mem0 62855a62-d626-4e33-97d0-9f0c81a1b7ac).

Only the built-in leak sentinels (call with `needles` omitted, or `exhaustive=True`) behave as documented.

For literal substring search over Mem0 content, query Qdrant directly instead — `http://localhost:6333`, collection `fused_<project_id>` (e.g. `fused_dark_factory`). Point lookups by id work via `POST /collections/<c>/points` with `{"ids":[...], "with_payload": true}`, which also confirms whether cited memory uuids still exist. When you only need a handful of records and can phrase a topical query, `search(stores=['mem0'], categories=[...], limit=25)` and filtering client-side is usually cheaper than standing up a direct Qdrant call.

SIBLING ENTRY carrying the same caveat from a different angle (phrase derivation for topic-guard clusters, measured 2026-08-08: four on-topic needles returned 0 matches over 53 scanned records): mem0 5b7d246e-ca5a-4bdd-a93b-2f0592585164. Three independent observations across 2026-08-05, 08-08 and 08-19 now agree, so this is a stable property of the tool and not a transient.

entry_text: When re-planning a reify task branch that has diverged from main, preview the conflicts without touching the lane with `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main HEAD` (git 2.43). Exit 1 means conflicts: the first line is the merged tree OID, and the conflicted paths follow. Hunks can be read via `git ls-tree -r <oid> <path>` plus `git cat-file -p <blob>`. A conflict where main edited PROSE inside a section the branch MOVED to another file resolves textually to the branch side, but git cannot carry main's edit to the destination file. Port it by hand, as task 6956 did with #7063's helpers.rs wording moving into harness_doc_chunks/module_compile.rs.
target_text: In a reify worktree, use `git merge-tree --write-tree <branch> main` to detect merge conflicts against main WITHOUT touching the working tree — it prints the conflicted paths and CONFLICT lines to stderr and exits 0. This is the safe way for a planning/architect agent on a diverged task branch to size a re-merge, since reify prohibits `git stash` (refs/stash is one host-wide ref shared by every lane) and a real trial merge would dirty the lane. Caveat: it only reports TEXTUAL conflicts — a clean auto-merge can still be semantically broken when both sides added contradictory tests for the same behaviour (e.g. task 5743's "polygon coords are NOT gated" vs main's 5661 "polygon gate rejects every coordinate"), so always diff the two sides' test names for the shared subject too.

pytest-timeout's timeout_method="signal" DOES work inside pytest-xdist workers on this repo's pinned stack (pytest-xdist 3.8.0 / execnet 2.1.2 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0). xdist >= 3.4 starts workers with execnet's main_thread_only execmodel, so tests run on the worker's main thread and SIGALRM reaches them. Measured 2026-10-05 (task 5470 architect) on a synthetic suite at `-n 2 --dist loadgroup`, timeout=2:
- signal: failed only the test blocked on threading.Event().wait(); the worker survived and the tally was complete.
- thread (+ --max-worker-restart=0): os._exit killed the worker and later tests never ran.
The older "signal is incompatible with xdist, use thread" belief was never measured. Pick the method on that trade (signal keeps the worker alive; thread also terminates a main thread stuck in C code), not on xdist compatibility.
target_text: orchestrator/pyproject.toml under xdist: addopts = "-n auto --dist loadgroup"; timeout_method changed signal→thread (signal mode is unreliable inside xdist worker subprocesses); pytest-xdist>=3.0 added to [dependency-groups].dev. Tests that need to stay on a single worker get @pytest.mark.xdist_group('<name>'): two such groups in the repo as of 2026-05-15 — 'cargo_scope_cache' (TestDiscoverWorkspaceCrates + TestFilesToCrates in test_cargo_scope.py, shares module-level discover_workspace_crates cache via _clear_cache) and 'fixed_mcp_port' (three tests in test_stale_escalation_cleanup.py that hard-code harness.mcp.url = 'http://localhost:9999'). Suite went from ~10min serial to ~13s parallel (2272 orchestrator tests).

Reify builtin-signature registry (docs/prds/v0_6/builtin-signature-registry.md), seam files established by leaf α / task #6001: each later τ family migration must EXTEND two existing one-call-site seams, never scatter `reify_builtins::` calls. (1) `crates/reify-compiler/src/builtin_registry.rs` — `registry_result_type(name, &[Type]) -> Option<Type>`, the compiler's SINGLE entry into the row table; `expr.rs` has exactly one ladder arm calling it, and the module is deliberately NOT glob-re-exported from lib.rs. Arg TYPES cross the boundary, not `CompiledExpr`s, because reify-builtins deps reify-core only. (2) `crates/reify-stdlib/src/registry_dispatch.rs` — `dispatch(EvalBuiltinId, &[Value])`, an exhaustive match with NO `_` arm, wired as the first arm of `eval_builtin`'s chain. The seams are deliberately ASYMMETRIC: the compiler side resolves via `name_group(name)` (arity-INSENSITIVE, answering only for single-row groups) because the legacy family arms it replaced gated on name only and switching to argc-keyed `lookup` would silently re-route mis-arity calls through the terminal first-arg fallback; the eval side uses `lookup(name, argc)` because eval dispatch genuinely is argc-keyed. Also established by α and meant to be extended, not restated: `units.rs::registry_row_names_are_disjoint_from_legacy_families` and `reify-builtins/tests/i_reg_1_seed_string_dispatch_gate.rs` both derive their name lists from `reify_builtins::rows()`, so a new τ's rows are auto-covered with zero edits in either place.

entry_text: To pin a FalkorDB query's PLAN SHAPE in a test, use falkordb-py's `await graph.explain(cypher, params)` (drop graphiti's `routing_` param first): it returns `ExecutionPlan.structured_plan`, an Operation tree (`.name`, `.args`, `.children`). Assert that no operator whose name ends in 'Scan' has children, because such an operator re-runs once per input row. Always pair this with a negative control that EXPLAINs stock graphiti's Cypher, captured from `object.__new__(FalkorDriver)` with a recording execute_query, on the same provisioned graph. Reference helpers: fused-memory/tests/test_falkor_edge_search_integration.py::non_leaf_scans / issued_by_stock_graphiti (task 6238). This works on structured data with no plan-text parsing, and it can tell plans apart at test scale even where wall-clock cannot.
target_text: FalkorDB planner gotcha, cosine leg (measured 2026-10-03, task 6238, after γ/task 3708 provisioned per-property indices). graphiti_core edge_similarity_search's `MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH DISTINCT e,n,m, cos AS score ...` plans as Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan [e] on the RELATES_TO.group_id index. That is one index scan per Entity node: 825 ms on dark_factory (21.7k edges) and a 1000 ms 'Query timed out' on reify (26.8k edges). Edge-first with late endpoint binding avoids it: `MATCH ()-[e:RELATES_TO]->() WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH e, cos AS score WHERE score > $min WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m WHERE n:Entity AND m:Entity ...`. It ran in 52-60 ms on dark_factory and 92-108 ms on reify. Node cosine (Node By Index Scan) was fine at 85-135 ms. Rule: in GRAPH.EXPLAIN, any *Scan operator that has children is re-executed per row.

entry_text: Gotcha (task 5066): migrating any gate or result wait to `wait_responsive` in a merge-queue timing-corpus test module (the 10 modules listed in orchestrator/tests/test_merge_queue_wait_budget_guard.py::_MERGE_QUEUE_TIMING_CORPUS) pulls that method under the esc-3980-4 teardown guard, which now runs corpus-wide (TestMergeQueueTimingCorpus::test_no_unledgered_unguarded_worker_teardown), not just in concurrent_verify. Wrap everything after `worker_task = asyncio.create_task(worker.run())` in `try:`. Put `await worker.stop()` plus a `contextlib.suppress(Exception)` join in its `finally:`, INSIDE `with patch(...)`. Keep the module's existing join timeout. Never add a `_UNGUARDED_WORKER_TEARDOWN_DEBT` entry to pass.
target_text: Adopting `_orch_helpers.wait_responsive` in a merge-pipeline test REQUIRES pairing it with a try/finally that runs `worker.stop()` plus the worker_task join (task 3980 amendment esc-3980-4, documented at orchestrator/tests/test_merge_speculation.py:1972-2003). `wait_responsive` gives up by raising `_pytest.outcomes.Failed`, so on a straight-line body a give-up — like any mid-body `assert` — skips `stop()` and leaks a live SpeculativeMergeWorker plus its run task into pytest-asyncio teardown, which is how one red test cascaded into unrelated failures elsewhere in the session. Put the `finally` INSIDE the `with patch(...)` block so the worker unwinds against the fakes, not real git ops; `stop()` is safe there even with an unreleased gate because it cancels in-flight verify tasks rather than awaiting them.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 (main 2128c3692c, reproduced independently twice): a reify `auto` param pinned ONLY by a one-sided inequality resolves to the edge of a hardcoded default domain, silently, exit 0. `constraint length >= 8mm` on a Length auto resolves to 10 METRES; the mirror `<= 12mm` resolves to 0.000001 m (1 micron). Two-sided bounds (`>= 8mm` AND `<= 12mm`) correctly resolve to 0.01 m, the analytic Chebyshev centre of [8,12].

MECHANISM: build_centrality_objective synthesises Maximize(min_j slack_j), which is MONOTONE in a parameter pinned from only one side, so its argmax is a box edge. The box is default_bounds_for's hardcoded domain (LENGTH -> (1e-6, 10.0); ANGLE -> (-TAU, TAU); else (-1e6, 1e6)), and build_auto_param_list always passes bounds:None so constraint-derived bounds never narrow it. Only Ge/Gt/Le/Lt contribute slack terms — Eq/Ne contribute none, which is why an equality-only auto gets no synthetic objective and resolves exactly.

WHY THIS MATTERED: it is the behaviour the old cmd_build "solver-free posture" comment cited as its reason NOT to wire the solver. Wiring the solver into `check` without addressing it would make `reify check` print "All constraints satisfied." on a 10-metre tolerance — strictly WORSE than today's INDETERMINATE. Leo ruled that a one-sided-only auto is UNDERDETERMINED and must be refused with a coded diagnostic naming the missing bound, never resolved to a box edge. Owned by task #6692. Fixtures: tests/prd-gate/fixtures/driver_parity_one_sided_auto.ri and driver_parity_two_sided_auto.ri (the latter is the discriminating negative case that stops the refusal being implemented as a blanket "inequality-pinned auto is refused").

Measuring a reify-compiler change's blast radius on the .ri corpus:
1. Build a debug `reify` at HEAD (`RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo build -p reify-cli --bin reify`, ~6 min cold, ~1.5 min after a compiler-only edit) and copy it out.
2. Apply the change, rebuild, copy again, then revert.
3. Run `reify check <file>` for every `git ls-files '*.ri'` (xargs -P 8, `timeout 120`), keeping only `^(error|warning)` lines plus the exit code per file, and `diff -r` the two output dirs. It takes ~3 min per binary for ~760 files.
Watch out: the module name must match the file stem, or E_MODULE_PATH_MISMATCH pollutes ad-hoc probes. A few designs/prd-gate fixtures time out or panic identically in every build.
target_text: Reify architect technique for MEASURING a compiler change's blast radius before planning: apply a throwaway prototype in the task lane and rebuild only debug `reify` with the lane's seed env — `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_HOME=/tmp/reify-agent-cargo-home cargo build -p reify-cli --bin reify` (the seeded target/ was built with exactly these; any mismatch, e.g. default CARGO_INCREMENTAL, rebuilds the whole workspace). Measured ~3m20s for a reify-compiler edit under load ~100, and `cargo nextest run -p reify-compiler` with the same env ~4m build + ~5m run. Snapshot the HEAD binary first, run `reify check` over `git ls-files '*.ri'` with both (xargs -P6, timeout ~90s) and diff outputs: expect noise from /tmp/reify_step_* STEP-file names and tests/prd-gate/fixtures/pnrg_envelope_pipe.ri (~60s, times out under load). Afterwards `git checkout` the prototype files and `rm target/debug/reify && cp <snapshot> target/debug/reify` (break the hardlink); leave target/release/reify untouched because target/.reify-bin-sha certifies the RELEASE binary against HEAD (scripts/reify-bin-freshness.sh prefers release).

VERIFIED PRE-FLIP FINDING for dark_factory's write_triage judge, established 2026-08-27 against main while triaging esc-3169-1 (the write_triage_enabled flip gate). The judge is shown up to judge_candidate_count candidates (config.yaml: 5) and the prompt deliberately RENDERS their ids, but its output contract carries no candidate identity and the attach always targets the band's top-1 — so a verdict reasoned about candidate #3 is applied to candidate #1, and in the contested case stamps the contested flag on a canonical the entry never contradicted. EVIDENCE: write_triage_judge.py parse_judge_verdict(raw: str) -> str returns a bare string; the token candidate_id appears NOWHERE in that module; tools.py:3392 attaches to triage_decision.canonical_id. WHICH READING APPLIES IS SETTLED BY THE CODE'S OWN DOCSTRING: build_judge_prompt says "Candidate ids ARE rendered, because the model must be able to say which candidate it means" — so the module renders ids for a purpose its output contract cannot serve, and the alternative reading (that the verdict is intended relative to the band winner) would require contradicting that docstring. The fix that matches declared intent is to add candidate_id to the judge's JSON contract, validate it against the slate in parse_judge_verdict, and thread it through BandDecision. target_text: reify-solver-elastic gauge/convergence testing gotcha: the catenoid-tube fixtures used to calibrate form_find.rs's surfaces-path convergence criterion (crates/reify-solver-elastic/tests/tensegrity_gamma_membrane_form_find.rs build_catenoid_tube, at 16x3 / 32x6 / 8x2) are surfaces of revolution whose free nodes are all structurally identical, so their free-row norms of D are UNIFORM — measured max_row/min_row = 1.000 exactly. Any test that tries to discriminate between residual normalization schemes (ratio-of-maxes vs per-row) on these meshes is therefore VACUOUS: both schemes compute the same number there, agreeing to 10 significant digits. To get non-uniform free-row norms, add hoop cables on the free ring and make ONE of them stiff (e.g. q=30 against the others' 0.3 at n_theta=16, n_axial=2, sigma=1); measured row-norm spread then tracks the stiff q roughly linearly (q=3 -> 3.9x, q=30 -> 33.9x, q=300 -> 334x). Grading sigma per-triangle instead does NOT work — even a 10:1 sigma jump collapses triangles and the solve fails with DegenerateTriangle.

entry_text: To check that a reify binary's dynamic TBB/OCCT symbols all resolve (not just the ones a given run happens to exercise), run `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH LD_BIND_NOW=1 target/debug/reify --version`. Eager binding resolves every function symbol at load time, so a libTKernel->libtbb symbol missing from the pinned /opt/reify-deps/tbb-pin libtbb.so.12 would fail here at once. Under normal lazy binding it would only show up at the first parallel OCCT call. Measured exit 0 on 2026-10-01 (task 7439). To find which library creates threads, use an LD_PRELOAD shim that wraps pthread_create, calls dladdr on the start routine and prints backtrace_symbols_fd. gdb attach is blocked on this host by yama ptrace_scope.
target_text: TBB linkage gotcha (task 5192): The OCCT-style version-pin trick (cargo:rustc-link-lib=dylib:+verbatim=libtbb.so.X.Y) CANNOT surgically fix libtbb resolution the way it fixes OCCT. GNU ld records DT_NEEDED from the linked library's DT_SONAME, not the -l:+verbatim filename. TBB in /opt/reify-deps ships a MAJOR-ONLY SONAME (libtbb.so.12) for BOTH deps 12.18 and system 12.11 — proof: libopenvdb.so (built against deps libtbb.so.12.18) has NEEDED=libtbb.so.12. So verbatim-linking libtbb.so.12.18 still yields NEEDED=libtbb.so.12 (unchanged). OCCT's pin works ONLY because OCCT's SONAME is fully-versioned (libTKernel.so.7.8). Separately, reify_build_utils::read_soname_version(deps,"tbb") returns "12" (immediate target of libtbb.so → libtbb.so.12), not "12.18". Also, reify-kernel-openvdb's wrapper.o has 22 UNDEFINED tbb symbols (incl. tbb::detail::r1::get_thread_reference_vertex) from header-only meshToLevelSet/volumeToMesh templates, so dropping -ltbb breaks the link. Surgical fix requires new infra (a tbb-only symlink dir prepended to RUNPATH, or post-build patchelf --replace-needed).

entry_text: jcodemunch get_layer_violations gotchas (measured 2026-10-01 at 1.108.55 against local/reify-4ae45bbd). (1) Calling the wheel's `jcodemunch_mcp.tools.get_layer_violations.get_layer_violations()` directly from Python, outside a server, does NOT load the project's .jcodemunch.jsonc: it returns layer_count=0 with "No layer rules defined". target_text: jcodemunch-mcp serve (v1.108.27) returns its get_changed_symbols / get_dead_code_v2 / get_untested_symbols tool results as a custom MUNCH/1 text encoding inside `content[0].text` — NOT JSON — so reify-audit's fused_memory_client-style `serde_json::from_str(content[0].text)` will fail on them. MUNCH/1 is self-describing: a `@N=string` ref/intern table, a scalar line ending in `__stypes=` then `__tables=<prefix>:<table>:<cols|>:<types|>` (comma-joined for multiple tables), then CSV data rows prefixed by the table's letter; unquoted fields may be `@N` (intern ref) or `@N<suffix>` (ref+literal); quoted `"..."` fields are literals that can contain commas. get_layer_violations, by contrast, returns plain JSON in content[0].text. A decoder must branch on the `#MUNCH/` prefix. Reference: crates/reify-audit/tests/fixtures/jcodemunch/README.md and the L-CLIENT plan (task 4103).

entry_text: reify-test-support value-cell lookup naming (task #6973): the suffix encodes the argument shape across both families — bare `get_value_cell(module, cell)` / `get_let_expr(module, cell)` = module's FIRST template; `_in(module, template_name, cell)` = named template in a module; `_in_template(&TopologyTemplate, cell)` = a template you already hold (e.g. from compile_first_template). `try_get_value_cell_in_template` is the tolerant Option variant and THE single ambiguity-guarded walk; its rustdoc is the one home of the ambiguity contract. Do not add an `_of` or other suffix for the held-template shape.
target_text: reify-test-support's value-cell lookup family (crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs, re-exported at the crate root) returns the full ValueCellDecl, so tests needing cell_type/kind/visibility need not hand-roll `templates[0].value_cells.iter().find(|vc| vc.id.member == ..)`. Pick by what you hold: get_value_cell(module, name) for the first template, get_value_cell_in(module, template, name) for a named template, get_value_cell_of(&template, name) for a template you already hold, and try_get_value_cell_of(&template, name) -> Option to assert absence (it still panics on an ambiguous member). The get_let_expr* siblings return only default_expr and panic on a defaultless cell (task #6973).

entry_text: Gotcha (reify-compiler, since task 7838): the value-cell Applied-type walk (entities_phase.rs → check_applied_type_arg_bounds) covers every value cell, not only annotated ones. An un-annotated `let` gets an inferred cell_type, and its Applied type args are bound-checked as Written, so builtin args are rejected against trait bounds. Example: `let c = couple(a, 2.0)` with `a : Axis` types to `Coupling<Axis>`, which fails `P: DrivingJoint + HasMotion`. Tests that need a Coupling must build a real driving joint, e.g. `let j = prismatic(vec3(1,0,0), 0mm .. 10mm)`. Axis stand-ins no longer work. This is intended (esc-7838-3, option A).
target_text: In reify's compiler, `Type::Applied` arity and type-arg bound checking is NOT done at type-resolution time: `entities_phase` runs a post-compilation walk over every template value_cell's `cell_type`, calling `check_applied_type_arg_bounds` on each `Type::Applied` node. Consequence for any resolution path: producing `Type::Applied` earns those diagnostics for free, while a path that resolves an applied name to a bare `StructureRef`/`TraitObject` silently disables them (no node to inspect, no diagnostic, and `N<A>` == `N<B>`). That is why `resolve_entity_name_with_shadowing` intercepts structure-with-args before the bare-name fallthrough.

entry_text: Reify compiler: when you add or widen a builtin classification family slice (e.g. in orientation_signatures.rs / units.rs), you must also do three things in crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs. Add the slice to the `is_known_builtin` union. Add it to the test module's `ALL_FAMILY_SLICES` table. Remove its names from `EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES`. Otherwise the name is silently double-owned (family + "unclaimed" manifest), and `eval_deferred_names_are_disjoint_from_every_registered_family` cannot detect it. Task #6082's ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES missed this; task 6306 fixes it.
target_text: Reify has TWO independently-authored `crates/reify-compiler/src/orientation_signatures.rs` files that collide: task #5344's (landed on main, `ORIENTATION_TYPED_FN_NAMES`, 18 orientation/frame/transform CONSTRUCTOR names, includes orient_euler, explicitly disclaims the four decomposers via `is_orientation_typed_fn_rejects_the_four_decomposers`) and task #6082's on branch task/6082 (`ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES` = [orient_euler, orient_to_euler]). entry_text: To assert an orchestrator conftest fixture's runtime effect from tests/scripts/ (which never collects orchestrator/tests/conftest.py), load the conftest with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under a UNIQUE module name (never 'conftest'), take getattr(fixture, '__wrapped__', fixture) (pytest 9 FixtureFunctionDefinition), and call it with the test's own monkeypatch/tmp_path. Executing that conftest has import-time side effects: it inserts five sys.path entries (orchestrator/tests at the front), setdefaults ORCH_DEBUG_ASSERTS, sets worker._DEBUG_ASSERTS and patches AsyncMockMixin. Contain the first two with monkeypatch.setattr(sys, 'path', [*sys.path]) and monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_DEBUG_ASSERTS', ...) before exec_module. Worked example: tests/scripts/test_config_retune_gate_decision.py::_exec_orchestrator_conftest (task 3886); full tests/scripts/ stayed green with it.

Completed: Train landing path: any move of main under a train verify (e.g. a direct docs commit) derails the train and can strand its members until manual rescue; retry the CAS via reverify_on_rebase instead
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (interactive session, re-read of current code + runs.db). The original 2026-09-03 description claimed a moved main makes the train land an UNVERIFIED re-merged tip. That cannot happen, and the real defect is the inverse: the train DERAILS and discards its verify. The fix direction (option (a) below) is unchanged.

=== MECHANISM (verified in code) ===
`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::_do_train_merge` reads `main_sha = await git_ops.get_main_sha()` BEFORE the train verify and passes it as `expected_main=main_sha` to `_journal_landed_then_advance` WITHOUT `reverify_on_rebase=True`. If main moved during the verify, `git_ops.py::GitOps.advance_main`'s attempt loop rebases/re-merges the tip onto the new main (`rebased = True`), skips the "Reverify-on-rebase gate" (flag unset), and reaches `git update-ref refs/heads/main <rebased> <expected_main>`. `expected_main` is the stale pre-verify value, so the CAS is certain to fail → `AdvanceOutcome('cas_failed')` → `_do_train_merge` emits `train_derailed` ('Train merge advance failed: cas_failed') and returns blocked; members are re-driven as singles. The rebased sha can never land, so there is NO unverified-landing hole. The task-2154 "Correctness (amendment)" comment after the advance call ("can transparently rebase merge_commit onto a moved main and land the REBASED sha directly") describes an unreachable path whenever expected_main is passed, and it always is here. The `_await_unadvanced_predecessor` docstring states the correct behaviour ("For a TRAIN it is terminal").

Contrast: the single-branch site (`SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight`) passes `reverify_on_rebase=True`, gets `rebased_pending_reverify`, runs `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` (disjoint delta → advance with no re-verify; overlap → re-verify), re-anchors base_sha, and retries the CAS. A direct docs commit during a solo verify is therefore absorbed in ~2 min (measured 09-18, task 5578); during a train verify it costs the whole train.

=== MEASURED COST (runs.db `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, read-only, 2026-09-23) ===
train_merged 37, train_derailed 29 all-time; 5 derails are `cas_failed`: coalesce-3215 (07-31, 27 min verify lost), 3146 (07-31, 27 min), 4097 (08-16, 29 min), 4545 (09-06, 53 min), 4574 (09-16, 72 min; the mover was a direct docs commit 4 s after the train read main). Each also re-drives every member solo, and 4574's derail re-pended the tip with a stacked branch carrying the other member's commits (see memory feedback-a-lost-cas-train-derail-repends-the-tip-with-a-stacked-branch). Operational side-effect: interactive sessions are now deferring direct-to-main docs commits whenever the queue is live, because the train case is not separable from the harmless solo case.

=== FIX ===
INVARIANT (unchanged): a train never advances main to a tree no gate verified. NEW GOAL: a moved main does not discard a green train verify when the intervening delta cannot interact with the train.
Pass `reverify_on_rebase=True` at the train site and handle `'rebased_pending_reverify'` with a bounded CAS loop mirroring the single-branch one (re-read main, MAX_CAS_RETRIES). Route through `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` with the train's merge worktree; the branch-touched set MUST be the UNION of all members' diffs against the merge-base (a single member's diff is not the train's footprint): disjoint → advance the rebased sha without re-verify, overlap → re-run the post-merge verify on the rebased tip. Re-record the LandedOutbox row with the landed sha (the 2154 block becomes reachable and correct). Rewrite "DEFENSIBLE DELTAS" item 1 and the 2154 comment to state the real policy. Keep the happy path (main unmoved → one verify, one advance) byte-identic…[truncated, 15294 chars total]

Observed a full coalesce-train derail-and-redrive cycle on task 3543's merge (2026-08-17). merge_request returned status "queued" (mr-85a71e32, position 24 of 25); polling by request_id later returned state "superseded" with superseded_by "coalesce-3543-c255a1c1". Per the merge-queue contract a coalesce-* id names the TRAIN, not a request, and resolves through none of merge_status's tiers — it must not be polled by request_id. The canonical ancestry check then read rc=1 (branch ref present, commits genuinely not on main), which means "not landed YET", not a stale record, and under rc=1 the tip-marker and task-status landing signals are NOT consultable (they apply only under rc=128-with-empty-marker). Shortly afterwards get_merge_queue showed the train gone and task 3543 re-enqueued as a FRESH solo request mr-525db4c5 at position 16 — i.e. _redrive_coalesce_members had auto-re-pended the unlanded member. Correct handling throughout was to keep polling the branch handle and never resubmit, since the re-drive already had. Useful incidental: the train id encodes the tip task id as coalesce-<TIP_ID>-<hex>, so `coalesce-3543-...` meant 3543 was the train's tip and would therefore carry its own "Merge task/3543 into main" marker if the train landed.

[SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-23 (recon Stage 1, run cd53b227-18ac-4432-b22f-2b5ac0913cf2) — DO NOT APPLY THE "rc=1 ⇒ landing signals NOT consultable" RULE AS STATED ABOVE.] That sentence generalises a rule that was true of THIS incident but is false in general, and following it makes you report "not landed" about work that HAS landed. Two corrections:

(1) WHY IT HELD HERE: task 3543 was the train's TIP (`coalesce-3543-...`), and a tip that has not yet landed genuinely is not on main — so rc=1 correctly meant "not landed YET" in this specific case. The reading was right; the generalisation is not.

(2) WHERE IT FAILS: for a NON-TIP member of a coalesce train, `git merge-base --is-ancestor task/<ID> main` returns rc=1 PERMANENTLY on work that DID land. The train merges only the tip branch and rebases it onto main first, rewriting every stacked commit's SHA; the member's own ref is never advanced, and rc=128 never fires either because a branch carrying commits beyond main is retained rather than deleted. The correct landing test for such a member is CONTENT, not ancestry: `git cherry main task/<ID>` → landed iff the output is NON-EMPTY and every line begins with `-`. Full mechanism, the required non-empty conjunct, and the in-repo authority (`GitOps.rebase_preserving_task_commits`) are in Mem0 c71cd6fc-1416-4420-93da-c483798d2040; live specimen is task 4104 (train coalesce-4181-b2a290cd, tip merge d25b24468c).

(3) THE DOC IS ALREADY FIXED: skills/merge-queue/SKILL.md rule 3 carried this same false "consultable only under rc=128-with-empty-marker, not under rc=1" text and was corrected by dark_factory task 4612 (status done, done_provenance kind=found_on_main, commit 2d4720660d2815368aa113e6c51a24da54d03f61). Rule 2's landing signals ARE now consultable under rc=1 when the flow was entered via the `coalesce-*` arm; the restriction survives only on the non-coalesce path, where a permanent rc=1 does still mean not-landed. The sibling gap in skills/unblock/SKILL.md is tracked by task 4630 (pending) and was not fixed by 4612.

entry_text: How per-write graphiti LLM token usage is measured (shipped in task 3716): NOT by a before/after delta on the shared TokenUsageTracker and never by reset(). build_llm_client installs fused_memory.backends.llm_token_usage.AttributingTokenUsageTracker on every arm, and measure_llm_tokens(client) / GraphitiBackend.token_probe() opens a ContextVar-scoped window that counts exactly the records made by its own asyncio context, including tasks it spawns. That makes it exact under concurrent cross-group writes on the one shared _llm_client. The generic arm records via TokenRecordingOpenAIGenericClient, once per successful generate_response, matching BaseOpenAIClient. GOTCHA for parity comparisons: upstream AnthropicClient (graphiti-core 0.28.2) calls token_tracker.record BEFORE response_model validation, with cumulative totals, so on a validation retry it records the failed attempt and then re-counts it inside the next record. Its llm_calls and token counts are not comparable one-for-one with the OpenAI-shaped arms.
target_text: GOTCHA — graphiti's TokenUsageTracker is a single CUMULATIVE instance shared across the whole GraphitiBackend: `_llm_client` (one OpenAIClient) is handed to `self.client` AND to every per-group Graphiti clone in `_client_for()` (graphiti_client.py:422-428, :592-598), and `Graphiti.token_tracker` just forwards to `llm_client.token_tracker`. So per-write token usage MUST be read as a before/after delta — never `tracker.reset()`, which would destroy a concurrent write's accounting. Deltas also need an explicit exclusive/shared attribution flag, because DurableWriteQueue runs concurrent add_episode calls and overlapping measurement windows silently absorb each other's tokens.

WHERE FINDING→MEMORY CITATIONS ACTUALLY LIVE (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06 while planning task 5151). If you need to answer "which findings cite memory X", the corpus is the reconciliation journal's `runs.stage_reports` JSON blob in `data/reconciliation/reconciliation.db` — NOT Mem0 payloads and NOT `recon_report_state.db`. Measured side by side: runs.stage_reports = 29,119 findings / 7,318 distinct cited memories / 3,303 multi-cited / max 43 citers; recon_report_state.db = 254 findings / 323 cited (it TTL-evicts at 300s and calls delete_run at run quiescence); a full scroll of 68,673 Qdrant points across 5 fused_* collections = only 21 citing records / 52 cited. `citation_repair.py`'s module docstring states the same thing in prose ("the ONLY durable home of a closed run's findings") — believe it.

QUERY SHAPE, with cost. The cited ids are embedded in a JSON TEXT column so no index on them is possible. `SELECT id, project_id, status FROM runs WHERE stage_reports LIKE '%<uuid>%'` over the live 116MB / 22,917-row table measured **0.102s** — cheap enough for a delete-time gate. But the LIKE result is a strict SUPERSET: findings quote uuids in `description`/`suggested_action` prose constantly, so you must narrow it by parsing each row's `stage_reports` → `StageReport.items_flagged` → finding dict → `cited_memories` (list of `{'memory_id','store'}`). Never treat the LIKE hit as the answer.

DO NOT PROJECT-SCOPE THE SCAN. Measured: the most-cited memory in the corpus (43 citers, 14 runs) returns **0 rows** under a `project_id='dark_factory'` filter — all its citers are in other projects. Scoping by the caller's project silently misses the entire hazard. (Scoping is also not a speedup: 0.143s scoped vs 0.102s unscoped, since neither uses an index.) `citation_repair`'s `caller_project_id` confinement is not a counterexample — that module WRITES to the blob; a read-only scan is safe at the widest scope.

FINDING LIVENESS HAS NO `retracted` OR `superseded_by` KEY — do not invent one. Verified absent tree-wide. Retraction (`recon_report.py::delete_finding`) is documented in-run-only so a retracted finding never reaches the durable blob, and `citation_repair` rewrites a repointed citation in place so the old id vanishes from `cited_memories`; both are handled structurally by ABSENCE. The two markers that do exist are the owning run's status (`RunStatus.rolled_back` / `circuit_breaker` = not live; `failed` and `interrupted` ARE still live — interrupted runs are re-adopted and resumed) and the finding's own `resolution_status`, whose measured values are: flagged_for_stage2 52, partially_fixed 42, human_operator_required 40, unresolved 23, fixed 10, resolved 9, deferred 7, informational 5, noted 4.

Measured 2026-10-04 with `./target/debug/reify eval`: `unwrap_or(<some(0.03 m/s)>, 0mm/s)` evaluates to 0.03 m/s and `is_some(..)` to true, so both are usable for DSL-level Option assertions in e2e tests.
target_text: Reify Option<T> gotcha (measured task 6047, 2026-08-06): `match` cannot read an Option payload in EITHER form, and one failure mode is silent. `match o { some(v) => ..., none => ... }` is a PARSE ERROR (the tree-sitter `match_pattern` production has no positional form — only variant_binding_pattern | identifier ('|' identifier)* | '_'). Binder-less `match o { some => A, none => B }` COMPILES CLEAN with zero Error and zero eval-phase diagnostics and evaluates to `undef` — for a some(x) subject just as much as for a none subject — because Option is intrinsic (Value::Option) not a Value::Enum, and eval's match-arm selection fires only on Value::Enum (gated in reify-expr/src/lib.rs:635, with an Undef catch-all at :663-670). So `reify check` reporting "All constraints satisfied" does NOT mean an Option match works; you must `reify eval` and look at the cell value. The working surface is the prelude recovery combinators (no import): unwrap_or/or_default/fallback, or_else, is_some/is_none, map_or, ok_or — declared in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/option_recovery.ri (ok_or in stdlib/result.ri), with real semantics only in the Rust intercept crates/reify-expr/src/option_recovery.rs (the .ri bodies are typecheck-only placeholders that return WRONG values). `map_or(o, dflt, |x: T| ...)` is the ONLY combinator that binds the payload to a name, so it is the replacement for a `some(c) => ...` arm. Contrast: Result<T,E> IS a real prelude enum whose Ok { value: v } / Err { error: e } named-field patterns match normally. The gap is a deliberate open design fork — docs/prds/v0_6/data-carrying-enums.md §10 and fork F4 ("Recommend Leo decide").

reify GOTCHA (verified 2026-10-04, main 92a94f7545): relate_solve.rs `self_anchor_member` classifies ANY zero-arg `MethodCall` on a `StructureRef`-typed receiver as the scope's `self` anchor, so a new synthesized member lowered as a MethodCall on a sub ref (e.g. `a.world_frame`, which lowers to `MethodCall(ValueRef("

.a","__self"))`) is silently mis-grounded if it ever reaches a relate operand. Reject such members before `solve_scopes` and exclude them in `self_anchor_member`. Separately, `StructureInstanceData` has ~216 non-test struct-literal construction sites. Add per-instance data through a reserved overlay key with typed accessors (the `@@source_span` precedent in reify-ir value.rs), not through a new struct field.
target_text: In reify's relate path (crates/reify-eval/src/relate_solve.rs), a `self.*` operand is invisible to `operand_refs`: `ground(sub)`/`fix(sub)` desugar at compile time to `fasten(sub.frame, self.frame)`, and `self.frame` lowers to a no-arg `MethodCall` on a `StructureRef` receiver that `decode_operand` returns None for (only `<sub>.<member>` IndexAccess operands decode). So any pass that walks `operand_refs` to reason about a relation's operands under-counts such a relation by one, and it reaches `static_relation_residuals` with a single datum operand, tripping that function's arity guard and returning an EMPTY row vector. An empty row vector there has two distinct causes — unmodelled name/operand-kind combination, or fewer than two comparable datum operands — and `reify_constraints::relate_solve::comparable_datum_operands` is the public discriminator to read rather than guessing.

THE SHARED MAIN CHECKOUT'S CURRENT BRANCH IS NOT A CONSTANT, and the session-start gitStatus snapshot goes stale. Measured 2026-09-22: the snapshot said `Current branch: main` with 7 dirty tracked files; ~40 minutes later another live session had committed those files onto a NEW branch `task/df-whole-tree-drift` and left /home/leo/src/dark-factory checked out on it. A `git commit --only docs/task-authoring.md` — the documented safe-under-contention form — therefore landed on THAT session's branch tip instead of main.

RULE: re-read the branch in the same command as any commit into /home/leo/src/dark-factory (`git status -sb`, or `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`). Never infer it from the system-prompt snapshot, from an earlier status call, or from "it's the main checkout so it's on main". This is distinct from, and additional to, the known shared-index hazards (bare `git commit` sweeping another session's staged WIP; `cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`; the pyright pre-commit widening the race window).

REPAIR THAT WORKED, without disturbing the other session (their tree was tracked-clean because they had just committed):
  git branch _keep <my-sha>                   # preserve the commit FIRST
  git reset --soft <their-sha>                # move the branch ref back; tree untouched
  git restore --staged --worktree <my-path>   # un-apply only my file
  git branch task/<carrier> $(git rev-parse main)
  git worktree add <path OUTSIDE .worktrees/> task/<carrier>
  git cherry-pick _keep && git branch -D _keep
Use `reset --soft` plus a per-path `restore`, NEVER `reset --hard` — a hard reset in someone else's active checkout would wipe any tracked edit they made in the interval. Verify afterwards that their branch is back at their sha and the tree is tracked-clean.

YOU CANNOT CHECK OUT `main` TO FIX THIS: it is checked out in that one working tree, and switching it yanks the rug from the other session. Land the commit via a carrier branch through the merge queue instead.

CHOOSING THE CARRIER TASK ID: do NOT reuse a `pending` task's id for a docs/amendment branch — the scheduler can dispatch it onto `task/<id>` and the merge would mark real implementation work as delivered by a docs-only commit. File a dedicated carrier with `submit_task(planning_mode=True)` so it lands `deferred` and the scheduler cannot claim it, and build it in a worktree OUTSIDE `.worktrees/` so the reconciler cannot reap it. Worked example 2026-09-22: carrier dark_factory 5772 for docs/task-authoring.md §10, branch task/5772, merged via mr-3b984d97 as commit 924dd7a407.

AFTER THE MERGE LANDS, the merge worker has already flipped the carrier task to `done` itself — a follow-up `set_task_status(status='done', done_provenance={kind:'merged', commit:<sha>})` returns `{success:true, no_op:true, done_provenance_repaired:true}`. That is the expected success shape, not a failure: the status call was a no-op and only the provenance was stamped. The carrier's worktree may also already have been reclaimed (`git worktree remove` answers "is not a working tree"), which is likewise normal.

target_text: Discovery (jun18): the dark-factory test `orchestrator/tests/test_repend_state_machine.py::test_b4_l2_park_members_deferred_sweep_quiescent` encodes a deliberate invariant — park→`deferred` was chosen specifically so parked tasks fall OUTSIDE `_RECONCILE_SWEEP_STATUSES={'in-progress','blocked'}` and the stranded-blocked reconcile sweep never re-files them. Critically, in the L2-cluster-park flow the member L1 escalations are DISMISSED by the cascade, so after park the members have NO open escalation — only the `deferred` status keeps them sweep-quiescent. This makes a naive `park='blocked'` flip provably wrong: parked tasks would become `blocked` + no-open-escalation → reconcile Fix #1b files `stranded_blocked` → the auto-watcher resolves it with `action='resume'` → re-pend, and the dispatch loop returns. For `blocked` to be sweep-quiescent the holding escalation MUST stay OPEN (Fix #1b skips a blocked task that has an open escalation). Also confirmed: "blocking"-severity escalations are born L1; only critical/urgent (BORN_AT_L2_SEVERITIES) are born L2, and agent-role criticals are downgraded to blocking — so L1→L2 promotion is the auto-watcher's (an LLM) judgement, not deterministic code, and `promote_to_l2` is clustering-shaped (needs member_ids/root_cause/options).

MEASUREMENT UPDATE to the whole-source-tree AST scan census (memory f99f3bc0) and to the consolidation norm's straggler list (memory 5c202334): shared/tests/test_auth_failed.py IS NO LONGER A STRAGGLER, and task 5094's premise for it is stale.

WHAT THE PRIOR RECORDS SAY. The 2026-09-04 census lists `test_auth_failed.py::TestFabricatingForkHasNoProductionCallers` (its own `_PRODUCTION_SRC_ROOTS` walk) at 3.26s + 2.91s call, one of four independent whole-tree read+parse passes costing ~57s of the shared suite. The norm memory names task 5094 as "the open follow-up folding two remaining stragglers (test_safe_io.py 11.11s, test_auth_failed.py 7.41s)" onto `silent_fallthrough_scan.parse_first_party_tree`.

WHAT CHANGED (task 4357, commit 94267f2797, measured 2026-09-20 in .worktrees/4357). The class was renamed to `TestSingleResetsParserOwnership` and its scan was both WIDENED and made ~18x cheaper in the same edit, by applying exactly the technique the census itself recommended — "a raw source-substring prefilter is EXACT here, because [the names] are identifiers and the scan only matches ast.Name.id / ast.Attribute.attr, which are literal source substrings by construction":

  before: 188 files in 2 roots, all parsed          -> 1.84s
  after:  426 files in 7 roots, 2 parsed            -> 0.10s

  in-suite, `pytest tests/test_auth_failed.py --durations`:
  the scan is now the 2nd-slowest item at 0.10s call; whole module 39 passed in 0.80s.

The roots also went from the hardcoded `('shared/src','orchestrator/src')` to `_REPO_ROOT.glob('*/src')` — all seven uv workspace members. NOTE for anyone reusing that glob: pathlib's `*` does NOT cross a path separator, so `glob('*/src')` cannot wander into fixture src trees nested under tests. This is the OPPOSITE of the git-pathspec trap recorded in memory 63055270 ("git's wildmatch lets `*` cross slashes, so a `*/src/*` pathspec also matches orchestrator/tests/fixtures/atomic_train/crate_a/src/"). Verified by printing the matched roots: exactly cockpit/src, dashboard/src, escalation/src, fused-memory/src, orchestrator/src, sampler/src, shared/src.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TASK 5094. Folding this file onto the shared parsed-tree provider would now make it SLOWER, not faster: the provider parses the whole first-party tree (461 files, ~5.68s per the census; the 2026-09-13 amendment measures 11.01s for 573 files and +666.8 MB RSS to retain the trees), whereas this guard needs 2 files and 0.10s. A prefilterable identifier-only guard is a case where the "consolidate onto the shared provider" norm should NOT be applied — re-measure before folding it. test_safe_io.py (11.11s) is unaffected by this and remains a genuine straggler.

GENERALISATION WORTH REUSING: when a tree-walking guard matches only IDENTIFIERS, a substring prefilter is exact by construction, and it can make scanning the WHOLE repo cheaper than parsing a hand-picked subset — so widening such a guard's coverage and cutting its cost are not a trade-off.

entry_text: Gotcha, verified 2026-10-05 for task 4701 on CPython 3.13.9 under -X dev -W error. Raising pytest.fail (a Failed, which is a BaseException) inside a monkeypatched subprocess.Popen.__init__ comes out of `await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(...)` cleanly. It emits no ResourceWarning or unraisable warning, and production `except Exception` handlers do not catch it. That makes Popen.__init__ a test seam that no name binding can bypass for 'forbid this spawn' guards. A recording-only probe over the full orchestrator suite found zero agent-CLI (claude/codex/gemini/pi) spawns in 24,267 tests: every invocation test mocks at or above asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, which shadows a Popen-level guard.
target_text:
In orchestrator/tests, patching `orchestrator.agents.invoke.asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` mutates the GLOBAL asyncio module attribute (invoke.py does `import asyncio` and calls it off the module), so a spy that delegates to the real spawner must capture `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` into a local BEFORE entering the patch context or it recurses infinitely. Existing mocked tests avoid this only because they use `side_effect=fake_exec` returning a MagicMock, never delegating to the real spawner. Related: shared/tests is NOT on the orchestrator suite's sys.path (conftest.py adds orchestrator/tests, orchestrator/src, shared/src, escalation/src only), so real-process test helpers like `_pgid_gone_within`/`_kill_group` from shared/tests/test_proc_group.py must be mirrored locally rather than imported.

Additional gotcha for tests that DO delegate to the real spawner (task 3224's TestRunSubprocessLocalCancellation.test_cancellation_reaps_real_process_group): because the patch is on the global asyncio module attribute, it also intercepts every OTHER subprocess spawned anywhere in the same worker process for the duration of the `with patch(...)` block — including this suite's background git-subprocess workers that conftest.py's `_reap_leaked_merge_workers` exists to reap. A spy that unconditionally appends every spawned proc to a list and then trusts `spawned[0]` as "the one I launched" is flaky: an unrelated concurrent spawn landing first makes the test poll/kill the wrong process group. Fix: filter the spy by the actual argv the test passed (e.g. `if args[:2] == ('sleep', '30'): spawned.append(proc)`) and assert exactly one match before deriving pgid, rather than indexing spawned[0] unconditionally.

entry_text: Before carrying a branch that /team or subagent seats committed to, read the seats' raw commit messages (git log --format=%B main..<branch>). On 2026-09-28 a sonnet seat wrote two commits with the Co-Authored-By trailer fused into the subject line, because there was no blank line before it. A branch nobody else has fetched can be reworded without changing any tree: git commit-tree <old>^{tree} -p <parent> -m <subject> -m <trailer> for each commit, then git update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <new> <old-tip>, where passing the old tip makes it a compare-and-swap. Confirm git diff --quiet <old-tip> HEAD afterwards. No interactive rebase is needed.
target_text: Gotcha (Claude Code Bash tool, 2026-09-16): a `git commit -m "<multi-line message>"` inside a long compound command that got moved to the background (it exceeded the 120s foreground timeout while chained with a slow pytest run) was committed with the whole message flattened onto ONE line. The Co-Authored-By trailer therefore wasn't a real trailer (solar-challenge commit 9e668f0, now on main, not rewritten). To avoid it, commit in its own short foreground command before any slow step, or pass the message via `git commit -F <file>` or a heredoc. Then check with `git cat-file -p HEAD` before submitting to the merge queue.
