NORM (dark-factory, task 4890): a session-scoped AUTOUSE fixture that each test root's conftest binds its OWN copy of must be IDEMPOTENT, or a session collecting two roots breaks it. `_df_fleet_dir_redirect` (df_pytest_isolation.py) was bound by conftest.py, scripts/tests/conftest.py and orchestrator/tests/conftest.py; each instance unconditionally mktemp'd a fresh dir and overwrote ORCH_FLEET_DIR, so the root whose fixture ran FIRST yielded a path the env var no longer held, and its per-root identity assertion failed (task 4398).

THE FIX SHAPE, which generalizes: make adoption a PURE HELPER defined ON TOP of the soundness rule the tests already assert — adopt an existing value exactly when `<rule>_violation_reason(value, basetemp) is None`, else create. Defining adoption as "already passes the very rule the tests assert" makes it safe by construction rather than by a second, drifting copy of the check. An ADOPTING instance must touch neither os.environ nor teardown: overwriting strands the owning instance and popping strips a value it still needs.

THE TRAP WHEN REPRODUCING IT: each root's session fixture instantiates LAZILY at first use, so a root whose identity test runs right after its own fixture ALWAYS passes. The failure needs the interleave — root A's fixture, then root B's overwrite, THEN a root-A test. A `-k`-narrowed run collapses that and shows green even with the bug present. Reproduce with the real file ORDER (e.g. `pytest scripts/tests/test_drain_check.py tests/scripts/test_fleet_dir_isolation.py scripts/tests/test_restart_all_orchestrators.py`), and note the repo's own gating test_command runs BOTH roots in ONE session (scripts/orchestrator.yaml), which is what makes this class of bug reachable in CI at all.

VERIFY BY MUTANT, not by a green run: disable adoption (`adopted = None`) and confirm the failure reproduces verbatim before trusting the fix. Here it printed `fleet-dir0 != fleet-dir1` under one basetemp — exactly what 4398 recorded.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha: every bodied trait assoc fn is a DefaultKind::Fn default that conformance/checker.rs::check_phase_resolve_assoc_fns compiles once PER CONFORMER via functions.rs::compile_assoc_function. A trait-static (no-self) default is ALSO compiled once more in compile_builder/traits_phase.rs as the namespaced `Trait::fn` through compile_function. So a diagnostic emitted from either compile path for one wrong default body repeats N (or N+1) times at the same trait span unless deduped. Task 5991 measured 7 reports for 3 bodies and fixed it with fn_return_check.rs::push_once_per_body (match on code plus label span and message). A self-taking default in a trait with no conformers is never compiled at all.
target_text: Reify compiler (task #5991): a fn body's result type is now reconciled against its return type by crates/reify-compiler/src/fn_return_check.rs (warn-mode FnReturnTypeMismatch / FnReturnTypeUnannotated, severity from FN_RETURN_RECONCILE_SEVERITY). Gotcha for test authors: a deliberately mismatched trivial fn fixture (e.g. `fn f(x: Real) -> Int { x }`, `-> Length { 1.0 }`, or an un-annotated `fn f() { 10mm }`) now carries a Warning, so assert Error-severity-only rather than zero total diagnostics. Code-verified fact (2026-09-29): a write-triage `contested` outcome triggers NO adjudication.

- tools.py stamps CONTESTED_METADATA_KEY (x_contested) on the attached child. The stamping site's own comment says there is no gate, no escalation and no operator surface. The contradicted parent is left unchanged and nothing is scheduled to settle it. reconciliation/consolidation_gate.py keys on a different key.
- The only reader is server/grouped_read.py::is_contested_child. A contested child is never suppressed: it stays a full top-level search hit, and appears in the parent's digest list marked contested. A plain `amended` child is folded under its parent as a 240-char digest, which is the esc-5712 buried-correction shape.
- So the practical benefit of better contradiction detection is read-side visibility of the correction to the next agent. It is zero while write_triage.enabled is off.
- The cost of a false `contested` is reader clutter plus a misleading "disputed" marker, not queue load.

entry_text: CORRECTION to memory d9d3afde-6570-47a6-a07d-8382ca06570a and to task 5145's description: AsyncMock is NOT a MagicMock subclass. Measured on CPython 3.13.9: issubclass(AsyncMock, MagicMock) is False; the MRO is AsyncMock -> AsyncMockMixin -> AsyncMagicMixin -> MagicMixin -> Mock. It gets __fspath__ from the shared MagicMixin, whose __fspath__ is f'{type(self).__name__}/{mock name}/{id}'. So the leading path component is always the mock's own class name. Among the public unittest.mock classes, those that are PathLike, with their leading component: MagicMock -> 'MagicMock', AsyncMock -> 'AsyncMock', NonCallableMagicMock -> 'NonCallableMagicMock', ThreadingMock (3.13+) -> 'ThreadingMock'. Mock, NonCallableMock and PropertyMock raise TypeError from os.fspath. The repr FILE shape is likewise '<ClassName ...>', so a '<MagicMock*' ignore pattern also misses '<AsyncMock ...>' files.
target_text:
[CORRECTED 2026-09-06 by d9d3afde-6570-47a6-a07d-8382ca06570a: "os.fspath(mock) always starts with a literal 'MagicMock' path component" is FALSE for AsyncMock — os.fspath(AsyncMock()) starts with "AsyncMock" instead, a shape dark-factory's .gitignore does not cover. The rest of this entry remains valid.]

A unittest.mock.MagicMock is a fully valid os.PathLike[str]: it supports __fspath__ as a configured magic method whose default return is a genuine str derived from the mock's repr, so os.fspath(mock) always starts with a literal "MagicMock" path component. Consequence: production code that coerces one with Path() and then calls mkdir() materialises a REAL directory tree under the process CWD. No type-level check can reject a mock while accepting a legitimate relative path (isinstance(os.fspath(m), str) is True), so the fix belongs in the test that introduces the mock, not in the write primitive. Two distinct residue shapes exist and are often confused: the os.fspath() shape is a plain directory named MagicMock/ (no angle bracket), while the str(mock)/repr shape is a file named "<MagicMock name='...' id='...'>". .gitignore's long-standing "<MagicMock*" pattern only matches the second, which is why a MagicMock/ directory once reached a commit. orchestrator/tests/conftest.py's autouse _no_mock_derived_stray_dirs guard now fails (and cleans up) on the directory shape only.

Commit 50f674a40d ("feat(5594): GREEN - performance cards bind the wall-clock cutoff") deleted `_WINDOW_SQL` and `_project_cutoffs` from dashboard/src/dashboard/data/performance.py. Its message names this task: "also the lexical-date defect task 5155 was filed for". `git merge-base --is-ancestor 50f674a40d HEAD` succeeds, and grep finds no `_project_cutoffs`/`_WINDOW_SQL` anywhere in performance.py. The boundary-day regression part 1 asks for is also on main: test_performance.py::TestCardsShareTheWallClockWindow. Its fixture row a4 is completed at CARDS_NOW - 7d - 30m = 2026-09-23T11:30:00+00:00. That is the cutoff's own calendar date, 30 minutes before the cutoff instant 2026-09-23T12:00:00+00:00. Under the old lexical defect, '2026-09-23T11:30...' >= '2026-09-23 12:00:00' is TRUE ('T' 0x54 > ' ' 0x20 at index 10), so a4 would be over-included. Each family test pins a4's exclusion: completion_paths count==3, escalation_rates total_tasks==3, loop_histograms sums==2, time_centiles count==2. These pass on the base (25 passed in the clock/guard/wall-clock subset). Part 1 therefore needs no code and no new test.

`import ast` and `from collections.abc import Iterator` in test_performance.py are used ONLY by that block. No other file in the repo references these names.

APPROACH: move the guard into dashboard/tests/test_clock_discipline.py and reshape it to match that file's existing checker idiom.
- Detection becomes `find_sql_datetime_violations(source) -> list[tuple[int, str]]`, returning (lineno, whitespace-collapsed excerpt) like `find_clock_violations`.

  - upper-case and spaced spellings.
- It deliberately does NOT match the legitimate `date(completed_at)` / `strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:00', ...)` bucketing the data layer uses (costs.py, escalation_analytics.py, metrics.py, write_journal.py, burndown.py, performance.py), and does not match Python `datetime(...)` constructor calls, which are Call nodes, not string literals.

entry_text: Task 'eigensolve: shift-invert Lanczos is inaccurate on non-identity-B pencils (SPD B and buckling B = -K_g): use a B/K-inner-product operator and verify generalized residuals' completed. Landed in commit 091e927d26bda08abeeedbff2e9406497c00e18e.
target_text: Verified 2026-09-29 (reify esc-7260-4): shift-invert Lanczos in crates/reify-solver-elastic/src/eigensolve.rs feeds CompositeShiftInvertOp = (K - sigma*B)^-1 B to faer partial_self_adjoint_eigen, which assumes the Euclidean inner product; that is invalid whenever B is not a multiple of the identity (buckling B = -K_g, modal B = M), and `converged` only means n_modes values were returned (no residual check). Main already takes this path at sigma=0 above n = max(64, 2*n_modes), so buckling modes 2+ and modal-with-mass eigenvalues can be silently wrong (136-DOF column: lambda2 6.143e-2 vs dense 5.373e-2; lambda1 correct). The operator is self-adjoint in the K inner product for every sigma, so Cholesky symmetrisation L^T (K-sigma B)^-1 B L^-T keeps faer's Lanczos (consistent with the PRD's 'convergence diagnostic, NOT a Krylov rewrite' ruling). Owner: #7602.

entry_text: When re-planning a reify task branch that has diverged from main, preview the conflicts without touching the lane with `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main HEAD` (git 2.43). Exit 1 means conflicts: the first line is the merged tree OID, and the conflicted paths follow. Hunks can be read via `git ls-tree -r <oid> <path>` plus `git cat-file -p <blob>`. A conflict where main edited PROSE inside a section the branch MOVED to another file resolves textually to the branch side, but git cannot carry main's edit to the destination file. Port it by hand, as task 6956 did with #7063's helpers.rs wording moving into harness_doc_chunks/module_compile.rs.
target_text: Merging main into a reify task branch that MOVED a section to a new file: git reports a conflict in the old file, where main edited prose that the branch deleted. Taking the branch side (empty) is correct but not enough, because git cannot carry an edit across a move. To find main's edit, diff the base and main parts of each diff3 hunk (`git merge --no-commit`, then compare the `|||||||` and `=======` regions). Then port it by hand into the section's new home, or confirm the new home carries no such text. Task 6956 hit this: #7063 removed `parse_errors_as_diagnostics` from a doc that had moved to harness_doc_chunks/module_compile.rs.

And ptodo's repo-wide G-allow liveness hard gate (crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs extract_g_allow_owner_cites) flags any `#NNNN` cite of a done/cancelled task as g-allow-orphaned (High) unless a paren group containing `done`/`cancelled` directly follows the cite — write terminal cites as `#NNNN (done)`.
target_text: G-allow marker placement gotcha (scripts/audit-orphan-producers.sh): the orphan audit only inspects the SINGLE line immediately above a `pub fn` (regex `//\s*G-allow:\s*(.+)` on lines[idx-1]). So a `// G-allow:` marker must sit directly above the `pub fn`/`pub(crate) fn`, BELOW any `#[allow(...)]`/`#[cfg(...)]` attribute, with the reason + citation + `#NNNN` task all on that one line. The PRD engine-integration-norm §6.1 two-line example form would FAIL detection. Also: the audit's allowed[] list contains only ZERO-caller fns — a fn that has callers plus a G-allow marker appears in neither orphans[] nor allowed[], so pin-tests asserting "present in allowed[]" must target genuine orphans only.

Root cause found 2026-10-01 for task #5312 (FEA-selector-migration Bmig2), step 8.
What fails: switching FixedSupport(target: "root") to the typed face(body, "root") turned #6662's two instance-reuse tests red (crates/reify-eval-fea-tests/tests/instance_scope_optimized_dispatch_e2e.rs). With the legacy String target, identical at both scopes, reuse had fired.
Why: at TEMPLATE scope, an Undef geometry let is retried with a symbolic geometry-handle mint and try_eval_symbolic_topology_selector, at four sites in engine_eval.rs (~:8549/:8761/:10319/:10835). entry_text: RECIPE (used 2026-09-29 for review/briefing.yaml, task #8009; precedent #7949): landing a docs-only change through the reify MERGE QUEUE under the temporary 2026-09-26 SOP. (1) submit_task with planning_mode=True — it lands directly in `deferred` so the scheduler never dispatches it; title it 'HAND-LANDED DOCS VEHICLE — DO NOT DISPATCH'. (2) `git worktree add -b task/<id> /home/leo/src/reify-docs-<id> main` — a SIBLING path, never under .worktrees/. (3) Copy the file in, `git commit --no-verify -F <msgfile>` on the task branch (fine there; the queue runs the full gate), then `git checkout -- <file>` in project_root FIRST so project_root carries no overlapping WIP (an overlap halts the whole queue as wip_halted). (4) merge_request(task_id, branch, worktree, wait_secs=20). (5) Watch landing with a Monitor polling `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> main` (30-min expiry, re-arm; detect only, never mutate inside a Monitor). GOTCHA: the merge worker does NOT flip a planning-mode vehicle to done on landing — #8009 stayed `deferred` after 7fe20f64f5 landed; set_task_status done with done_provenance {kind: merged, commit: <merge sha>} by hand, then `git worktree remove` + `git branch -d`. Observed timing: queued behind one in-flight verify, then a full-gate verify of its own, ≈75 min end to end.

Add the slice to the `is_known_builtin` union. Add it to the test module's `ALL_FAMILY_SLICES` table. Remove its names from `EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES`. target_text: GOTCHA (verified by direct reproduction, 2026-08-06): Python's subprocess.run(..., timeout=N) calls process.kill() on the DIRECT CHILD ONLY. If that child is a bash script currently executing a COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — `verdict="$(some_function)"` — the forked subshell SURVIVES the kill and is reparented to `systemd --user` (PPID 2036 on this host). It then runs to completion on its own, however long that takes. Reproduced twice: SIGKILLing the main shell of scripts/restart-all-orchestrators.sh left the `$(drain_await_fresh ...)` subshell alive under PPID 2036, still polling. CONSEQUENCE FOR TEST DESIGN: "the test kills the child on timeout" is NOT containment for a bash script. Spawn with start_new_session=True and os.killpg(os.getpgid(p.pid), SIGKILL) on timeout, AND structure the script so no long wait lives inside a command substitution. See [[a-wait-a-test-interrupts-must-not-live-in-a-command-substitution]].

FLEET-WIDE FACT (verified 2026-07-25): there is NO docs-only fast path at merge role in ANY dark-factory-targeted project. `verify_plan.derive_verify_plan` short-circuits to `ScopeKind.TRIVIAL` when a diff contains no `.py`/`.rs` file (`verify_plan.py:707`), but that applies only at `role='task'`. At merge role, INV-1 (task 2883) intercepts it: `verify.py:5499` (global/no-module_configs branch) and `:5321` (module_configs branch) escalate the would-be trivial pass to the FULL GLOBAL GATE whenever any global command exists, emitting `trivial_pass_escalated(resolution='full_gate')`; with no global command it returns a loud `merge_no_evidence` FAIL (`_merge_no_evidence_fail`, `verify.py:1953`) rather than passing. Rationale: the merge verdict is ADOPTABLE (reused downstream as green evidence), so it must never be stamped from zero evidence. `skip_verify` was retired outright (task 1724/ο — `merge_queue.py:12899`, "unconditionally False on every success path"), so the merge queue has no docs bypass at any layer.

CONSEQUENCE: any project SOP, memory, or doc asserting "the merge queue is the fast path for docs" is stale by construction. Worth sweeping other projects' /prd and docs flows for that premise — it was true before INV-1 landed and is silently false now.

COMPOUNDING (reify case, but the shape generalizes): INV-1 stacks with (a) per-project never-narrow merge contracts — reify's `scripts/verify.sh:778` forces `--scope all` and `:602` forces `--profile both` whenever the orchestrator stamps `DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge` — and (b) `verify.py:4041`, which forces `is_cold=True` for every merge verify because merge worktrees are created fresh. Net: a docs-only merge costs a full cold debug+release workspace build. reify budgets `merge_verify_cold_command_timeout_secs: 10800` (3h) for it.

entry_text: VACUOUS-TEST-GUARD, two shapes measured in task 5134 (orchestrator/tests). (1) AN UNRELATED FAIL-OPEN PRODUCES THE ABSENCE. TestBuildAgentEnvCpuGovern::test_governance_disabled_by_default_no_df_agent_cpu_govern left exec_path='' and worktree unset. CpuGovernConfig.agent_env fails open on an unresolvable path, so DF_AGENT_CPU_GOVERN stayed absent even with enabled=True, and the flag the test names never got a say. Repair: make the precondition hold (a resolvable governor under tmp_path), then assert a positive control (enabled=True yields the key) before the absence. (2) THE COUNT IS READ BEFORE THE SCHEDULED CALLBACK CAN RUN. Scheduler._maybe_fire_park_stop_trip schedules its callback with asyncio.ensure_future, and set_task_status never yields. So a trip that really fires reads callback_count==0 unless the test does `await asyncio.sleep(0)` first: measured fired=0 without the yield and 1 with it. Every 'does not fire' test on that path passed even with its guard deleted. Repair: yield before counting, plus a control arm that does trip (resume() then fresh transitions, or the threshold-th transition) and asserts ==1.
target_text:
VACUOUS-TEST-GUARD, a new shape: A TEST THAT WAS NON-VACUOUS WHEN WRITTEN GOES VACUOUS WHEN AN UPSTREAM FAST PATH IS ADDED. Distinct from the peers under this topic, which all describe tests that were vacuous from birth. Here the coverage ROTS: the test still exercises a real path, just no longer the one its docstring names.

SIGHTING (dark-factory task 4360, dashboard/tests/test_burndown_data.py, TestCollectSnapshotPaginatesTheTaskRead). `collect_snapshot` originally issued a paginated task read directly; four tests stubbed `mcp_tool_call` and asserted on the paginated behaviour. A later commit in the SAME task inserted a size probe upstream (`_fetch_snapshot_tasks` issues one ordinary UNPAGINATED read first and only falls back to the paginated walk when that is rejected). Three of the four stubs were updated to reject the probe (`if 'page_size' not in args: return {'error': 'response too large'}`); the fourth — the class's declared POSITIVE CONTROL for fetch_tasks's empty-tree carve-out — was missed. Its stub answered EVERY request successfully, so the probe succeeded, the paginated path was never entered, and the carve-out it existed to protect never executed. Measured: mutating the carve-out to `if False:` left it green.

WHY IT SURVIVES REVIEW. The test is not obviously wrong at any single line — its stub is well-formed, its assertions are real, and it passes. What changed is a call site it does not mention. Diff review sees "3 stubs updated" as complete because the 4th stub needed no edit to keep PASSING; only to keep TESTING. Grep for the new discriminator (`page_size`) across the test module, not for edits.

THE RULE. Adding an early-exit / probe / cache / fast path to a function under test SILENTLY RETIRES every existing test whose double satisfies the fast path. That change is not test-neutral even when every test stays green — treat the green suite as evidence of nothing. Re-run the topic's universal mutation test against the SLOW path specifically after adding a fast path.

THE REPAIR, and it is two parts. (1) Make the stub reject the fast path. (2) Assert the slow path was REACHED — here `assert any('page_size' in c for c in calls)` — so the control cannot silently go vacuous again the next time the read shape changes. Part (2) is the load-bearing half: without it the test is one upstream refactor away from the same failure, and the next author gets no signal.

target_text:
Completed: refine_volume_with_size_field is pinned to single-threaded meshing because gmsh 4.15.2's PostView background field deadlocks under multi-threaded HXT — revisit the pin
Description: Task 7447 replaced refine_volume_with_size_field's 0-D corner-anchor sizing with a PostView background size field. That fixed the structural defect (the size field's interior now reaches gmsh), but measurement during 7447 found the PostView field DEADLOCKS gmshModelMeshGenerate(3) whenever gmsh meshes multi-threaded.

7447 shipped the conservative mitigation: General.NumThreads is pinned to 1 on the background-field path regardless of MeshingOptions::threads. This task revisits that pin. It is NOT a bug report against 7447 — the pin is correct and deliberate; this is the deferred half.

MEASURED IN 7447 (libgmsh 4.15.2, mesher_poison_recovery binary at c1cabbb73c, --test-threads=1, only the MeshingOptions at the two refine call sites varied):
  NumThreads=1 (deterministic:true) -> 5 passed, 41.07s
  threads: Some(1)                  -> 5 passed, 17.58s
  threads: Some(2)                  -> 5 passed, 24.37s
  threads: Some(8)                  -> HANG, SIGKILLed at 100s
  threads: Some(32) (= nproc)       -> HANG, SIGKILLed at 100s

The hang is a true block, not slowness: >10 minutes with process CPU frozen at 00:00:40 across 2.5 minutes wall clock, RSS flat at 33 MB, all 35 threads in futex_do_wait. It is not confined to the failure path — the valid unit cube hangs as well as the deliberately unmeshable open triangle, and WHICH one hangs varies with thread count (8 -> one, 32 -> the other), consistent with a race rather than a fixed ordering. Mesh.MaxNumThreads3D = 1 with General.NumThreads = 32 does NOT avoid it, so pinning only the 3D HXT stage is not sufficient. eprintln probes localized the stall to inside init::mesh_generate_with_recovery: the whole install path (view_add -> view_add_list_data -> field_add -> field_set_number -> field_set_as_background_mesh -> size-source option writes -> clamp writes) completes, and control never returns from mesh_generate.

HYPOTHESIS, UNVERIFIED (no gmsh-side thread stacks were obtainable — ptrace is refused in the orchestrator sandbox, so gdb could not attach): gmsh 4.15.2's PostView-backed background field is not safe to evaluate concurrently from many mesher threads, and a meshing stage blocks on a lock or a lazily-built octree inside field evaluation.

SCOPE — any of these, in increasing cost:
1. Re-measure on a newer libgmsh. If the deadlock is fixed upstream, lift the pin to a version-gated clamp and restore parallel remeshing. Cheapest and most likely to pay off.
2. Bisect the safe thread ceiling. 1 and 2 are measured-green, 8 and 32 measured-hanging; 3..7 are UNMEASURED. If a stable ceiling exists it would recover some parallelism without an upstream fix. Treat a bisected ceiling with suspicion — a race's safe ceiling is load-dependent and may not hold on other hosts.
3. Reach the same size field through a mechanism that is not PostView — a Structured field, a MathEval field, or a non-HXT Mesh.Algorithm3D. Largest change; would need its own byte-layout/interior-reach coverage equivalent to what 7447 landed.

VALUE / URGENCY: production impact is zero today — the only production caller, RealizedAdaptiveProblem in crates/reify-eval/src/compute_targets/elastic_static.rs, already passes deterministic:true (NumThreads=1). The cost is that adaptive remeshing cannot use meshing parallelism. Priority is medium, not high, for exactly that reason: this is recovering lost performance headroom, not fixing a live defect.

DO NOT "fix" this by removing the pin without re-measuring the table above. The pin is the only thing standing between a caller and an unbounded hang with no error and no timeout.

ENTRY POINTS: the pin and its rationale comment live at the General.NumThreads write in crates/reify-kernel-gmsh/src/refine_volume.rs; the multi-threaded coverage that would red if the pin were lifted prema…[truncated, 10302 chars total]

entry_text: reify-eval: `Engine::evaluate_let_bindings` (engine_eval.rs) is no longer part of eval()'s initial pass. The initial pass is `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified` → `build_combined_param_let_graph`. evaluate_let_bindings is only called by three RE-eval passes over already-diagnosed templates: after sub-elaboration (when the template has subs), the per-scope solver Solved arm, and the merged-cluster per-member loop. Any diagnostic emitted inside it is therefore duplicated per re-eval pass. This is how task #5819's twice-emitted "circular let-binding dependency in template T" arose.
target_text: reify-eval's `Engine::eval` elaborates sub-components in two SEPARATE module-wide loops: Phase A (engine_eval.rs:4943-5126, `evaluate_params_and_lets_unified`) evaluates every template's params/lets, then Phase B (engine_eval.rs:5130-5410) elaborates subs in PLAIN DECLARATION ORDER with no topological sort, forwarding `sub.args` RAW to `unfold.rs::elaborate_child_params_only`. Phase A's dependency graph (`build_combined_param_let_graph`, :517-624) is built only from `template.value_cells`, so a read of `ValueCellId("Top.mid","p")` creates no ordering edge — a parent `let` sourced from `self.<sub>.<member>` is therefore still Undef when Phase B evaluates a sibling sub's constructor args. The post-sub `evaluate_let_bindings` at :5396 fixes the parent let but nothing re-elaborates the child, and there is no fixpoint. Discriminator measured on task #6586: a DIRECT `Bar(length: self.leaf.doubled)` arg WORKS; only an intervening parent `let` is stale.

GOTCHA (measured 2026-09-04, task 5078 architect): a task whose fix removes an INV-8 loop-blocking call site is COUPLED to task 4484's ledger and cannot be planned before 4484 lands.

MECHANISM. Task 4484 introduces the triad shared/tests/loop_blocking_{scan,allowlist}.py + test_loop_blocking_gate.py. The allowlist carries one row per audited site keyed (relpath, qualname, content_hash). Fixing a site — e.g. wrapping an inline read_text in asyncio.to_thread — makes that site vanish from the caller-side scan, so reconcile_against_allowlist (Counter subtraction) reports the surviving row as STALE and TestRatchet::test_no_stale_blessings hard-asserts stale == []. shared/tests is the FIRST segment of this repo's test_command (cd shared && uv run pytest tests/), so a landed fix that leaves its row behind turns verify RED for every subsequent task in the repo until someone edits the allowlist. The fix is always a DELETION of the row, never a re-bless, and it must ship in the SAME commit as the code change.

WHY IT BITES THE ARCHITECT. As of main b4c963862a the triad exists only on branch task/4484 (status merge-deferred — verified and queued, not landed); `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms it is not on main, and plans/inv8-caller-side-census-2026-09-03.md is likewise absent. A follow-up task filed BY 4484 (5078, 4201, 3778 and the other step-9 tickets) therefore names a ledger file that does not exist on its own base. Because plan.json is IMMUTABLE, there is no way to write a plan that deletes the row only if 4484 has landed by execution time: planning without the deletion guarantees the repo-wide RED above, and planning with it breaks on a nonexistent file today.

PRACTICE. If your task's description says "flip/delete the ledger row in shared/tests/loop_blocking_allowlist.py" and that file is not on your base branch, do NOT plan the code fix alone — report_blocking_dependency on 4484 and let the orchestrator re-queue you after it merges. Verify with: git ls-files -- shared/tests/loop_blocking_allowlist.py (empty output = not on your base).

entry_text: PEER under topic `new-git-ref-creation-denied-in-worktree`: REF DELETION IS DENIED EVEN UNDER THE LANE'S OWN `task/` NAMESPACE, so an agent cannot clean up the safety branch it is allowed to create. Measured 2026-10-03, task 3508, worktree .worktrees/3508. `git branch task/3508-pre-rebase-backup HEAD` succeeded, consistent with peer 244b4ab3. But `git branch -D task/3508-pre-rebase-backup` failed with rc=1: "could not delete reference ...: Unable to create '/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.git/packed-refs.lock': Permission denied". Deleting a ref has to lock packed-refs, which is the same sandbox denial as the non-fatal stderr in 6db26169, but here it is FATAL. Practice: do not plan "delete the backup branch" as an agent step; hand it off with escalate_info(category='cleanup_needed'). Note that a squash-style rebase leaves the old per-step plan.json commit SHAs reachable ONLY from that backup branch. Related recovery for a CONFLICTED `git rebase --continue` in a worktree: rerere cannot write `.git/rr-cache` (Permission denied). One continue died with "commit died of signal 11" (the commit had in fact landed), and the next failed with "could not remove CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" while a stale 0-byte `.git/worktrees/<id>/MERGE_RR.lock` remained. Fix: `rm -f $GD/MERGE_RR.lock $GD/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, then `git -c rerere.enabled=false rebase --continue` (GD=$(git rev-parse --git-dir)), and check `git log` before redoing anything.
target_text:
PEER under topic `new-git-ref-creation-denied-in-worktree` — THE DENIAL IS NAMESPACE-SCOPED, NOT BLANKET. This CORRECTS the over-broad claim in memory e56d3fa4 ("there is no ref-based parking spot", "the usual safety-branch move is unavailable"). A safety branch IS available in a task worktree — you just have to create it under the lane's own `task/` namespace.

MEASURED 2026-09-14, task 5033, worktree .worktrees/5033, before a 23-commit rebase:
- DENIED: `git branch -f backup/5033-prerebase-abeea023 HEAD` -> `fatal: cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/backup/5033-prerebase-abeea023': Unable to create '/home/leo/src/dark-factory/.git/refs/heads/backup/...lock': Permission denied`. Same shape as e56d3fa4's `backup-x` sighting.
- ALLOWED: `git branch -f task/5033-prerebase-backup HEAD` -> succeeded; `git rev-parse --short task/5033-prerebase-backup` returned the pre-rebase tip, and the ref survived the whole rebase and was still readable afterwards.
- NOT a unix-permission effect: `ls -ld` on both `.git/refs/heads` and `.git/refs/heads/task` shows `drwxrwxr-x leo leo` in both cases.

Hypothesis (NOT measured): the agent sandbox allows ref writes under the lane's own `refs/heads/task/` prefix — the same prefix that makes ordinary `git commit` on `task/<id>` work — and denies the rest of `refs/heads/`. The competing "creating a new SUBDIRECTORY under refs/heads is what is denied" reading is weakened by e56d3fa4's own sighting, where `backup-x` needed no new directory and was still denied.

PRACTICE: before rewriting history in a task worktree, park the tip as `git branch -f task/<id>-prerebase-backup HEAD`. It costs nothing, and it beats the tree-hash-comparison fallback e56d3fa4 recommends because you can actually `git reset --hard` back to it. Keep e56d3fa4's fallback for the case where even the `task/` write is refused. Unrelated and expected throughout such a session: `Unable to create '.../.git/packed-refs.lock': Permission denied` on stderr while the operation still succeeds — see memory 6db26169 and the segfault entry 76016562, and check `git rev-parse HEAD` before believing any git `error:` line in a worktree.

entry_text: Reify gotcha: TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups is stored child-before-parent — guards::compile_block_guard allocates the outer __guard_N first but pushes nested groups (via compile_guarded_members) BEFORE pushing the outer group, and a nested group's guard_expr is AND(ValueRef(<entity>.__guard_<parent>), inner). Any single-pass evaluator of guarded groups outside the engine must reorder parent-first (walk parent_guard). Also: when the outer guard is false, a nested group's guard is false, so the nested ELSE branch is active (engine behaviour, measured 2026-09-29).
target_text: In reify-compiler, `TopologyTemplate::guarded_groups` is populated in POST-order (a nested group appears at a LOWER index than its parent): for a nested `where`/`else`, the inner group (`__guard_1`) sits at index 0 and the enclosing outer group (`__guard_0`) at index 1. Guard ValueCells `__guard_N` are allocated in the OPPOSITE order — PRE-order — by `compile_block_guard`. Locate a group by matching `guard_value_cell` (a `ValueCellId` whose `.member` is `__guard_N`), never by vec position — an index-based assertion over a nested fixture silently asserts the opposite of what it reads. `CompiledGuardedGroup` has no span field; the robust lookup is via `CompilationScope.names`, whose entries are `(ValueCellId, Type, Option<ValueCellId>)` where the third slot is the member's innermost guard cell (filled by `compile_block_guard`'s `register_guarded` sweep), then `guarded_groups.iter().find(|g| g.guard_value_cell == cell)`. Measured on task #5665.

entry_text: Reify CP-SAT completeness gotcha (verified on main 92a94f7545, 2026-10-04): since #5469, CpSatSolver reaches users through SolverRegistry::production()'s CrossDomain DiscreteFirstFallback, so OptimalityStatus::ProvenOptimal is on the production ranked path. CpSat's RankedSolveResult::Ranked carries at most RANKED_CANDIDATE_CAP = 16 candidates (cpsat.rs), so mapping its `complete` flag straight to Completeness::Exhaustive would falsely claim that every solution is in the carried set. Re-expressing CP-SAT under the completeness axis (task #6903) needs the cap reconciled, not a flag copy.
target_text: reify solver telemetry: three false premises that will poison any RED test asserting them (all verified 2026-08-26, main 2128c3692c; recorded as FORBIDDEN ASSERTIONS in docs/prds/v0_6/solver-legibility-telemetry.md §12). (1) `ProvenOptimal` IS UNREACHABLE IN PRODUCTION — `SolverRegistry::production()` leaves the Logical slot None and CP-SAT, the only solver that emits ProvenOptimal, is unregistered (#5469 pending). EVERY production objective solve returns `BestFound`. Any surface or test asserting "proven optimal" is asserting something the system cannot produce. (2) NO ITERATION COUNT ESCAPES reify-constraints — the only iteration telemetry is `SolveMeta { iter_limited: bool }`, which is PRIVATE and one bit wide; termination_reason, n_params, max_iters and initially_feasible go only to `tracing::debug!`. A signal asserting "shows the iteration count" needs new plumbing. There is no `ConvergenceStatus` type anywhere in the repo. (3) `candidates[1..]` FROM solve_ranked ARE NOT DEDUPLICATED — solver.rs warns explicitly that for a single-basin objective they may be K near-identical repeats, not distinct alternative designs. Any surface showing "alternatives" must dedupe by resolved-value fingerprint first. Related: the engine seam consumes only candidates[0] and discards every objective_score — the largest single telemetry drop in the stack.

entry_text:
Completed: State in confusion-reduction PRD §7.1 whether a codebook sighting `note` is human-provenance-only or machine-read signal
Description: Documentation-only correction. Records the actual readership of the confusion-codebook sighting `note` field so future legibility tasks stop being justified on a re-derivation path that does not exist.

ORIGIN: info-note esc-4892-3 (filed against task 4892, severity=info, category=risk_identified), confirmed independently by task 4892's steward at branch tip bf67d958da.

THE FALSE BELIEF. Task 4892's own WHY-IT-MATTERS asserted: "the codebook is the corpus the periodic-census verifier, the trickle-coder digest passes and reconciliation match NEW sightings against. A present-tense 'omits --system-prompt-file' entry can lead a future census pass to re-derive an already-fixed defect as live." That mechanism does not exist. The `note` field is write-only with respect to every automated consumer.

RE-MEASURED (steward, independently of the filer, at bf67d958da):
- `note` is WRITTEN by scripts/legibility/codebook.py::_build_sighting (schema-declared at the entry- and candidate-sighting shapes) and REQUESTED from the LLM by scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_prompt.
- scripts/legibility/coder.py::build_codebook_index is the only seam putting codebook content into an LLM prompt. Read in full: it emits `- {id}: {title} — {one-line cause}` per entry and nothing else. Sightings — and therefore notes — are never included; its own docstring says so.
- The census miner reaches the LLM through that same seam (census.py::mine_to_saturation -> coder.code_digests -> build_codebook_index).
- census.py::compute_matrix reads only origin_phase/manifested_phase. census.py::_cluster_description reads only len(sightings). census_trigger.py::codebook_signal reads only sighting `date` and candidate `first_seen`. digest.py never loads the codebook.
- Grep for `note` across scripts/legibility/*.py returns writes, schema declarations, and unrelated prose ("cost note") — no reader.

So a note's only readers are humans and agents skimming the raw YAML, which skills/census/SKILL.md:27 does direct ("Skim docs/legibility/confusion-codebook.yaml for recent sightings/candidates dates").

Recovering evidence of a bare xdist worker crash whose verify log was never persisted. Three sources survive:
(1) `<worktree>/orchestrator/.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed` holds the nodeid xdist synthesized a FAILED report for, i.e. the crashed worker's in-flight test. The file's mtime is the controller session end, not the moment of death. The entry disappears when a later run passes that test, so read it before any retry.
(2) On the implement path, the streamed `.worktrees/<id>/.task/verify/attempt-N.<pkg>.test.log` survives the raise until a later attempt with the same N overwrites it. It carries '[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated' and "worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'".
(3) Merge-lane verify logs are archived unconditionally in data/verify-logs/<task>/.
With `--max-worker-restart=0` the suite keeps running on the surviving workers after a death: task 3714's worker died at 83% and the session still finished '1 failed, 19294 passed'. So detection time is not death time.
target_text:
THE xdist-WORKER-CRASH CLASS IS NEARLY UNOBSERVABLE ON THE TASK LANE, measured 2026-09-21. This is the mechanical explanation for why the class has re-emerged in a NEW SHAPE six times across tasks 2365, 2619, 3000, 4066, 5333 and 5580: the system cannot see it, by policy, on both branches of its own outcome.

THREE CHANNELS LOSE IT.
1. Reclassified as infra: the `raise VerifyInfraError(phase='xdist_worker_crash')` in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py::run_verification PRECEDES both ::_persist_attempt_logs and ::_archive_attempt_log in the same function, and _run_cmd's streamed worktree log is the only complete copy — it dies with the lane.
2. Left as test_failure (what actually happens today): orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_categories.py::CATEGORY_POLICY sets TEST_FAILURE archive=False, and verify.py::_archive_attempt_log early-returns on a non-archivable category. Its docstring states the intent: it excludes "categories where the debugger can self-correct (compile errors, known test failures, timeouts)".
3. The flake ledger: all 368 flake_occurrence rows carry call_site='merge_gate'. ZERO task-lane rows, because no task-verify call site is registered (that is task 5089).

THE MERGE LANE SURVIVES ONLY BY A DIFFERENT PATH: verify.py::_archive_merge_verify_logs archives UNCONDITIONALLY on `not passed` and never consults CATEGORY_POLICY. Census confirming the asymmetry: 0 of 212 archived task-lane test logs carry a crash literal, against 12 of 219 merge-lane.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FUTURE ANALYSIS: no archive-derived or ledger-derived frequency for the task lane can be correct. This invalidated BOTH the escalation's "~7 observations" AND a seat's confident "zero task-lane occurrences" negative result, which was purely an artefact of searching data/verify-logs/ for a category that is never written there. A seat's positive control (the same grep finds 12 real crashes) does NOT cover this, because those 12 arrive by the unconditional merge-lane path.

WHAT DOES SURVIVE: a one-line cause hint in the daemon journal, of the form "Verification failed: test_failure — FAILED <nodeid>". That is enough to COUNT occurrences but nowhere near enough to diagnose them. Use the escalation corpus (data/escalations/**) plus runs.db::invocations, or journald, for any frequency figure on this class — and label it a floor.

entry_text: Stamped peer under topic pytest-xdist-serial-override — an OUTPUT-SHAPE gotcha for anyone asserting on a NESTED pytest run's text, distinct from the canonical's serial-override/fixture-loss/crash-flake modes. (1) Under `--dist loadgroup`, a test marked @pytest.mark.xdist_group('g') has its nodeid suffixed `@g` in xdist's crash line ("worker 'gw1' crashed while running 'mod.py::test_x@g'") and in -rA PASSED/FAILED summary lines, so a regex ending `::test_x'` silently misses; allow `(@[^']*)?`. (2) With timeout_method=thread, pytest-timeout's "+++ Timeout +++" banner goes to the dead worker's stderr and is NOT relayed by the controller, so `'Timeout' in output` is false for a thread-method kill even though the test was killed by the cap. Measured on pytest 9.0.3 / xdist 3.8.0 / pytest-timeout 2.4.0, task 5470 (tests/scripts/test_timeout_method_policy.py).
target_text:
FOURTH distinct pytest-xdist failure mode, stamped peer under topic `pytest-xdist-serial-override` (canonical 8bb3eb15 documents three: (1) `-p no:xdist` "unrecognized arguments", (2) silent `worker_id` fixture loss, (3) worker crash under load as a flake). This one is different from all three: the workers never run a test at all — they disagree at COLLECTION, and the run aborts before any assertion executes.

SYMPTOM. The suite dies with N cryptic errors, one per worker, naming no failing test and showing no traceback:
  ERROR gw0..gw7 - Different tests were collected between gw6 and gwN
  7 errors in 7.19s
Zero tests run. It reads as broken test infrastructure or a bad xdist config, so the natural first move — chasing xdist settings, or blaming the branch's own changes — is wrong.

CAUSE. pytest-xdist requires byte-identical collected test IDs across every worker process. Any parametrize id that is not a pure function of the parameter VALUE therefore breaks it. Measured 2026-09-01, task 3778 lane: the sole differing line across all seven workers was
  test_toolcall_markup.py::TestMarkupOverrideLifecycle::test_never_raises_and_fails_closed_on_any_other_input[<object object at 0x7341dc4bc730>]
— a `@pytest.mark.parametrize(..., ids=repr)` list ending in a bare `object()`. `repr(object())` embeds the heap address, which differs per worker process. Fix (already on main as 08c0c0dde8, task 3578): give the sentinel an explicit stable id, `pytest.param(object(), id='<bare object()>')`.

GENERALISATION: same break from an id built on `id()`, `uuid4()`, `time()`, a `repr()` of any object without `__repr__`, or unstabilised set/dict iteration order. If a parametrize case's id is not determined solely by its value, pin it with an explicit `pytest.param(..., id=...)`. SERIAL RUNS NEVER CATCH THIS — with one process there is nothing to disagree with — so it can sit latent in a suite that looks green locally.

DIAGNOSTIC, read-only, two commands, seconds:
  uv run pytest tests/ -n0 -q                                  # serial: mismatch cannot occur,
                                                               # abort vanishes, real failures surface
  uv run pytest tests/ -n auto --ignore=tests/<suspect>.py      # confirms the abort is that one file
Task 3778 measured: serial -> "1 failed, 4319 passed, 12 skipped"; `-n auto` minus the suspect file -> "1 failed, 4192 passed, ZERO collection errors". That pair simultaneously pins the abort to one file and proves nothing else in the suite is broken. (This is the canonical entry's blessed `-n0` override doing double duty as a diagnostic, not just a speed workaround.)

CROSS-TOPIC LINK — the reason this matters beyond xdist. In task 3778 this abort was a SYMPTOM OF LANE STALENESS, firing alongside three lock-charter drift-guard assertion failures from the same cause (lane 3242 commits behind main; both fixes already on main). The stale-lane entries under topic `lock-charter-drift-guard-checkout-depth` (peers 1c415ab2, 19cf6c33) describe that condition ONLY as assertion failures on the two named drift tests — they do not mention a collection abort, which names no test and mentions no lock charter, and so is easily misattributed to infrastructure. If a long-lived lane shows this abort, check whether main already carries a fix before touching anything; the remedy there is a rebase, not a cherry-pick.

COMPLEMENT to memory 86123d1c, which covers context-dependent de-literalisation from task 4948. Measured on task 5209, 2026-10-02.

The simple case: every raw envelope-literal hit sits in a comment or in a non-raw string or docstring. Then a WHOLE-FILE replace is enough:
1. Replace chr(60)+'/' with backslash-x3c+'/'.
2. Replace chr(60)+'parameter' with backslash-x3c+'parameter'.
3. Assert ast.dump(ast.parse(old)) == ast.dump(ast.parse(new)) before writing.
The assertion proves runtime byte-identity in one check. Comments are not in the AST, and the escape decodes to an identical constant value.

If a hit sits inside a raw string or bytes literal, or in a position the replacement would break, the ast.dump comparison differs or ast.parse raises. That tells you to fall back to 86123d1c's token-level method for that line only.

Dry-run on base 5a217969e4: escalation/tests/test_markup_middleware_registration.py, fused-memory/tests/test_toolcall_xml_leak.py and scripts/tests/test_scan_task_toolcall_leaks.py (1, 1 and 15 lines) all came out AST-identical, with no residue.
target_text:
EXTENSION to memory 01d46aad (de-literalising a file that holds raw MCP envelope sentinels), measured on task 4948, 2026-09-23. Two additions.

(1) GOTCHA: running a sentinel guard in RED, which TDD requires, puts the raw literals back into your context. The guard's failure message prints its hits dict, whose KEYS are the raw needles, and pytest's assertion introspection prints them again. A `git diff` of the rewrite also shows the removed raw lines. Pipe both through a filter that replaces chr(60), e.g. `| python -c "import sys; sys.stdout.write(sys.stdin.read().replace(chr(60), '‹'))"`.

(2) A whole-file str.replace cannot express one needle needing DIFFERENT replacements by context:
- a quoted pattern= literal becomes an expression;
- prose gets the \x3c escape;
- a literal that is the second half of an IMPLICIT string concatenation needs an explicit '+', otherwise it is a SyntaxError.

What worked:
- Redact each line by substituting marker tokens for the runtime-imported needles.
- Match each target line by its EXPECTED REDACTED text; markers are safe to type.
- Substitute at the token level (a redacted quoted token becomes closer_for('content'), INVOKE_CLOSER, and so on).
- For each substitution, assert ast.literal_eval(unredacted old token) == eval(new expression).
- Finally, assert that every decoded docstring (ast.get_docstring over all def/class nodes plus the module) is unchanged between old and new source.

This proves byte-identity per substitution and never types a raw needle. The shape is described in task 4948's step-2 commit (ae245392ca) message.

DISCOVERY 2026-08-27: flipping write_triage.enabled would NOT reduce the rate at which memory-consolidation human gates are filed, contrary to the intuition that server-side write triage supersedes the duplicate problem. Three independent reasons, any one sufficient:

(1) THE STAGE-1 SURVEY SURFACE IS UNGROUPED. The scheduled path, reconciliation/stages/memory_consolidator.py::MemoryConsolidator.assemble_payload, calls `self.memory.mem0.get_all(scope, limit=...)` — a bare Mem0 scroll with no parent_id awareness — and renders it into the "New Mem0 Memories Since Last Reconciliation" block the prompt tells the LLM to scan for duplicates. The backlog path uses MemoryService.search, which is ALSO ungrouped. server/grouped_read.py's own LAYERING CONSTRAINT docstring says the child-suppression filter is called ONLY from the MCP tool wrappers and that MemoryService.search is deliberately NOT touched — precisely so children stay visible to reconciliation/mem0_dedup.py and the near-duplicate write guard. Grouping applies to the `search` and `get_memory_by_id` MCP tools only; get_memories_by_metadata and count_memories_by_metadata do no grouping. So a sighting child arrives in Stage 1's payload as an ordinary peer row.

(2) TRIAGE IS ADD-ONLY AND RETROACTIVELY INERT. server/write_triage.py: triage issues no update_memory and no delete_memory, never edits a canonical. The existing duplicate population that generates today's gates carries no parent_id and is untouched by the flip.

(3) THE GATE KEYS ON A DIFFERENT SHAPE ENTIRELY. reconciliation/consolidation_gate.py::render_end_state_brief ratifies Option C — N short single-claim peers sharing one metadata.topic — and states explicitly that retained ids are "never given parent_id". evaluate_closure reads a metadata.topic scroll and never reads parent_id at all. Triage's parent/child links and the gate's topic clusters are orthogonal shapes. Corroborating scale: the corpus holds 11 child records total (1 sighting, 10 amendment) against thousands of records.

THEREFORE the gate rate is independent of the write path, and any fix must be on the reconciliation/filing side.

Scheduler._phase_select_pins never calls clear_parks_for, and _phase_select_scored clears parks only for top_id. So a pinned or non-top task keeps its park for its whole run, until Scheduler.release's 'defensive' clear_parks_for removes it silently (no reservation_used, no event). While it runs, that leftover park blocks same-tier park installs by other tasks (INV-3), producing PARTIAL installs. The partials are concentrated in the critical+pinned group (3620, 3541, 3542, 4541). 44 dispatches kept their own park. Detect it: a lock_acquired with no preceding reservation_used, for a task with an active park, whose scheduler_tick has terminal_phase=select_pins.

entry_text: GOTCHA (task 4935, 2026-09-29): a capability-manifest sidecar can still bind a delivered_check to a task after a human ruling moved that check to ANOTHER task. The only record of the move may be an `x_*` metadata key on the producer. Measured case: 5034 carries `x_reachback_guard_check_moved_to: "5446"` (ruling esc-5025-2), while plans/merge-lane-quality-prd's δ block still binds `reachback-patch-guard-retired` to 5034. So before hand-stamping a sidecar check with update_task, read the producer's x_* metadata and its description for a moved-check or suspended-step marker. update_task runs no polarity lint and no such check. scripts/audit_delivered_checks.py's `unwired_live_gate` disposition keys on (task_id, name), so it keeps listing a moved check as a false positive until the sidecar block is re-homed.
target_text: GOTCHA — a capability-manifest sidecar stamped with `task_id` is NOT proof the task carries `metadata.delivered_checks`. In fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/manifest_stamping.py the stamp is TWO separate steps: step 4 writes task_id into the sidecar and commits it to disk (atomic write-to-temp + os.replace), and only then does step 5 copy mechanical delivered_checks onto each task via update_task. Step 5's per-label body is individually guarded TWICE — an `except Exception` that logs 'failed to build/write delivered_checks' and continues, plus an `interceptor_write_succeeded(resp)` branch logging 'rejected delivered_checks write' (update_task rejects by RETURNING a structured error dict, it does not raise). So a label whose step-5 write failed leaves a stamped sidecar beside a task that never carried delivered_checks at all. Any tool inferring expected delivered_checks from a sidecar (e.g. scripts/audit_combine_gate_marker_loss.py) must state this assumption: grep the fused-memory log for those two strings before treating such a gap as damage. Note also the real mechanical-kind filter is `check.kind not in ('grep','script')` — BOTH grep and script are copied and only 'manual' is dropped; a grep-only filter under-counts.

Convention for PRD predicate gates in dark-factory (established by plans/write-triage-link-healing-prd.md D9, 2026-10-01): any gate task that later tasks depend on must ALSO carry a metadata.delivered_checks entry of kind 'script' that re-runs the same predicate.

Why: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::_deps_satisfied treats a dependency as satisfied when its status is in TERMINAL_STATUSES, which includes cancelled. Cancelling a gate to clear its hold would otherwise silently release everything behind it. A dependency on a task you may not edit has the same hole: a cancelled 3169 would dispatch its dependents. The fix there is an intermediate deterministic 'flip live' gate whose delivered_check asserts the real condition (write_triage.enabled true in the committed config).

Rules for the check itself:
- delivered_checks of kind 'script' run `<project_root>/<script> <args>` against the WORKING CHECKOUT.
- A check must FAIL on today's tree; the non-vacuity lint at commit_planning enforces this.
- scripts/check_write_triage_readiness_gate.py is generic: `--report NAME PATH`, `--require NAME PATH OP VALUE`, `--subcheck`, and its exit code is the contract. It can serve any PRD's gates.
target_text: Scheduler dep-gate asymmetry discovered while authoring capability-delivered-checks PRD (2026-07-13): _deps_satisfied (orchestrator/scheduler.py ~:2964) treats ANY local dep with status in TERMINAL_STATUSES as satisfied — so a locally CANCELLED dep counts as satisfied and the dependent dispatches, unlike cross-project external deps where cancelled triggers immediate escalation (dependency_discovered). This is why the delivered-check gate (task 2580) deliberately covers ALL terminal-status local deps carrying metadata.delivered_checks, done AND cancelled: a scope-cut cancel today silently unblocks dependents built on the cancelled work's premise.

entry_text: To force the except arm around `asyncio.create_task(self._some_coro(args))` in an orchestrator test (e.g. TaskWorkflow._route_review_suggestions_to_curator's scheduling-failure → SuggestionDisposition.ERROR path), replace the coroutine method with a SYNCHRONOUS `MagicMock(side_effect=RuntimeError(...))`, not `patch.object(wf, '_some_coro', side_effect=...)`: patch.object auto-builds an AsyncMock for an async target, and an AsyncMock raises its side_effect only when AWAITED, so create_task schedules it, the try never sees the error, and the router reports CURATOR. Also avoid the older trick of returning a non-coroutine, which depends on asyncio's exact TypeError (task 3415 amendment).
target_text: unittest.mock.patch auto-upgrades to AsyncMock when target is a coroutine function. AsyncMock AWAITS the side_effect call result. So if you write `side_effect=async_callable`, MagicMock-style logic calls it, gets a coroutine, AsyncMock awaits → gets the inner async callable's return (still a coroutine if the side_effect itself returned an async result). Symptom seen 2026-05-06 in test_burndown_data: "Unexpected fetch_statuses result <class 'coroutine'>" plus "coroutine never awaited" RuntimeWarnings. Fix: side_effect for AsyncMock-patched targets must be a SYNC callable that returns the value directly. AsyncMock wraps the awaiting itself.

Claude CLI 2.1.287 permission mechanics (measured 2026-10-02, task 4344 architect, headless --print with --json-schema):
(1) StructuredOutput survives a non-empty registry filter such as `--tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash`.
(2) Under `--permission-mode dontAsk` with NO allow rules, Read/Grep inside cwd are allowed, while Read/Grep outside cwd (e.g. /etc/hostname) are denied.
(3) Adding a bare `Read` allow rule lets Read reach /etc/hostname.
(4) `Bash(git log:*)` under dontAsk permitted `git log -1 --output=/tmp/x.txt`, which WROTE the file. A git-scoped Bash allow rule is therefore not read-only.
target_text: Gotcha — the headless `claude -p` CLI SANDBOXES its tool access to the subprocess's cwd tree. A caller that wants the model to read some other tree must set subprocess.run(cwd=<that tree>); absolute paths in the prompt are NOT sufficient, and non-interactively there is no permission prompt to approve, so every Read/Bash is silently denied. Proven 2026-08-03 (task 3577, fleet session census-reify-3386101): scripts/legibility/census.py verified /home/leo/src/reify from a dark-factory cwd and, because its verify seam fails CLOSED per cluster, presented as a silent mass rejection of every cluster rather than an error — a fail-closed default plus a mis-rooted subprocess is indistinguishable from honest rejection. Fixed by threading a keyword-only `cwd` (default None = inherit) through coder._invoke_cli into subprocess.run, bound via the existing functools.partial seam in _build_stage_invokes. Complements (does not contradict) the separate cwd-keyed CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md auto-load cost note: a NO-TOOLS classifier wants a neutral empty scratch cwd, while a TOOL-USING invocation must be rooted in the tree it has to read.

entry_text: Reify: a user `structure def`'s runtime Value::StructureInstance is built at FOUR independent sites, so any change to what an instance carries must cover all of them: (1) reify-expr eval_structure_instance_ctor (lowered in reify-compiler expr.rs from the authoritative template for entity-scope ctors, and from build_structure_def_skeleton templates for fn-body ctors); (2) engine_eval.rs plain-sub collapse (writes ValueCellId(parent, sub) and the "{parent}.{sub}"/__self alias); (3) engine_eval.rs keyed-sub per-key collapse; (4) unfold.rs nested-sub collapse. The three engine collapses gather fields from child_template.value_cells scoped cells only. Sub elaboration (unfold.rs elaborate_child_instance_nested) does NOT evaluate the child template's guarded_groups at all, so `Test.s.g` scoped cells never exist for where-guarded members (measured 2026-09-29, task #5935).
target_text: In reify, a `sub` instance is ALREADY materialized at runtime as a `Value::StructureInstance` stored at `ValueCellId::new("<scope>", "<sub>")` — the exact cell a `ValueRef(<scope>.<sub>) : StructureRef(..)` read resolves — plus a `__self` alias at `ValueCellId::new("<scope>.<sub>", "__self")`. Two sites build it: the "COLLAPSED instance value" block in crates/reify-eval/src/unfold.rs (~:780-800, instance scope) and its mirror SIR-α block in crates/reify-eval/src/engine_eval.rs (template scope). Do not assume subs are only flattened per-member value cells — both representations coexist, and the per-member cells (`<Struct>.<member>` / `<scope>.<sub>.<member>`) serve `self.<sub>.<member>` reads while the collapsed instance serves whole-value uses (bare `k`, trait-method receivers, member chains).

Completed: TargetedReconciler: clear the stale claimant on dependent-unblock, and journal the L1 escalation sweep
Description: Two robustness gaps in TargetedReconciler, both confined to reconciliation/targeted.py and its test file. _unblock_dependent re-pends a blocked dependent without first clearing its stale claimant_run_id/heartbeat_at, so a task this sweep 'unblocks' can sit pending-but-undispatchable until the heartbeat TTL expires — the orchestrator's equivalent sweep already clears the claimant for exactly this reason. And _sweep_escalate_l1, the only sync member of the cancelled-parent dispatch triad, files a real L1 escalation without emitting any journal row, leaving two of three branches auditable via get_run_actions and one not.

This task closes both: a claimant-clearing write with a deliberate, test-pinned failure policy on the unblock path, and a journal row plus the async/run_id threading that emitting one requires on the escalate path.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED on base aeb23fbadd (worktree HEAD == main, no branch commits):
- fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/targeted.py::TargetedReconciler._unblock_dependent exists. The order is: interceptor-wired guard -> _unblock_veto_reason -> escalation-pin veto -> live status re-read (TOCTOU guard) -> set_task_status('pending') -> 'write'/'skip' journal row -> metadata stamp (update_task, metadata_mode='merge'), which records but never downgrades (metadata_stamp='rejected'|'failed', journal 'write'/'skip' under operation='update_task', type='unblock_metadata_stamp'). No claimant clear exists.
- TaskInterceptor.set_task_claimant (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/middleware/task_interceptor.py::TaskInterceptor.set_task_claimant) is a public, reachable method on the self.task_interceptor the reconciler already holds. It is tri-state: explicit None clears the column to NULL. It takes no write-lock and passes no gates; it delegates to sqlite_task_backend.py::SqliteTaskBackend.set_task_claimant. On success that returns {'id', 'message'}; it raises TaskmasterError on an unknown id, and returns a message-only dict as a fail-safe when the claimant columns are absent. The routing question is therefore settled: call it through the interceptor, which is the same object every other sweep write uses. No new wiring is needed.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler._phase_redispatch_stranded_blocked clears via set_task_claimant(tid, claimant_run_id=None, heartbeat_at=None) IMMEDIATELY BEFORE set_task_status(tid,'pending'), best-effort, never blocking the flip. Its stated reason for clear-BEFORE-flip: a concurrent dispatch right after the task goes pending can never have its fresh stamp clobbered by a late-landing clear.
- Task 4977 HAS landed on main (commits 9b0ae53944 / 2ce07b0c01 are ancestors of HEAD). run_id is threaded into _sweep_cancel_orphan and _sweep_block_orphan, both of which emit symmetric write/skip rows: target='taskmaster', operation='set_task_status'|'update_task', and detail.type EQUAL to the returned action type ('descendant_cancelled' / 'descendant_blocked'). That equality is pinned by TestSweepCancelledDescendants::test_status_write_exception_leaves_skip_row ("journal type to match the action vocabulary"). _sweep_escalate_l1 is still a sync `def` with no run_id, called without await at targeted.py::_sweep_cancelled_descendants, and it emits no journal row. The SEQUENCING WARNING in the task is therefore resolved: build directly on 4977's convention.
- Baselines: `uv run --directory fused-memory pytest tests/test_targeted.py -q` gives 229 passed. `cd shared && uv run pytest tests/test_loop_blocking_gate.py -q` gives 131 passed. The loop-blocking scanner keys on (relpath, qualname, sha of the CALL node), and it does not resolve obj.method calls (queue.submit) or cross-package constructors. Making _sweep_escalate_l1 async should therefore add no finding. The existing targeted.py rows are keyed on the is_orchestrator_live_for call and a decl…[truncated, 7887 chars total]

entry_text: Write-triage judge wording × model interaction (measured 2026-09-30, 359 hand links + 84 reify slates): the production JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT ('prefer amends', 'same situation at different times is not a conflict') caps EVERY model at ≤ 27/111 contradictions labelled contests — Opus and gpt-6-astra included — so a stronger judge alone is not a lever. The policy wording (contests = wrong/outdated/different, prefer-amends removed) is the lever jointly with the model; on gpt-4o-mini alone it only swaps 61 misses for 60 false alarms. Known cost of the policy wording: 7 of gpt-6.1-sol's 13 false `contested` on the reify slates were plain restatements (rated SAME), hence task 6149 (ψ) adds a restatement guard to the clause. Rater-family caveat: the raters are Opus; in the 26 pairs where Opus and Astra disagree on contested the raters side with Opus 19 times, so do not rank Opus above Sol on that truth — the cleaner cross-vendor evidence is that Sonnet (37–39 errors) and Haiku (44) do worse than Sol (28) and Terra-low (33).
target_text: Stronger judge models for write triage, measured 2026-09-30 (exploratory; both hand-link populations were used in the Jev trial). Relation task, 359 hand links, 4,000-char fields, three-rater consensus truth (111 CORRECTS): contested-decision errors — gpt-4o-mini production wording 99, gpt-4o-mini policy wording 102, Opus-high policy 22, Opus-low 24, Sol-6.1-low 28, Terra-low 33, Astra-high policy 34, Terra-none 37, Sonnet-low 37, Haiku 44, Luna-low 50, Luna-none 66. Under the PRODUCTION wording even Opus/Astra catch only 25–27/111 contradictions (the prompt says prefer amends). Conclusion: the judge model is a lever for labels, but only jointly with the policy wording (contests = wrong/outdated/different, prefer-amends removed); every policy-wording arm beats both gpt-4o-mini arms at paired p < 0.001. Placement/recall on the 84-case reify slate task did NOT measurably improve over the shipped 1,200-char judge (paired p ≥ 0.07). The policy wording costs 7–13 agreeing attaches per ~82 shown as contested (vs 1–3 today; 16 for gpt-4o-mini under the same wording). Practical shortlist: Sol 6.1 low (~$0.006/write at N=5, p50 3.2 s), Terra none (1.9 s, same price, fewer false contested, fewer contradictions caught), Luna low (half of today's label errors at today's price). Completed: Remove the now-obsolete parse-error prepend from reify-test-support's compile_source_with_stdlib_allow_parse_errors (it doubles every parse diagnostic)
Description: Discovered while planning task #5392 (fn-body separator misparse, INV-SF-7 parse-is-value-faithful). Out of scope for #5392, which fixed the one test it broke surgically instead.

BACKGROUND. `reify_test_support::compile_source_with_stdlib_allow_parse_errors` (crates/reify-test-support/src/helpers.rs:354-363) prepends `parse_errors_as_diagnostics(&parsed)` — one bare `Diagnostic::error` per `ParseError` — and THEN calls `reify_compiler::compile_with_stdlib`. Completed: Train landing path: any move of main under a train verify (e.g. a direct docs commit) derails the train and can strand its members until manual rescue; retry the CAS via reverify_on_rebase instead
Description: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-09-23 (interactive session, re-read of current code + runs.db). The original 2026-09-03 description claimed a moved main makes the train land an UNVERIFIED re-merged tip. That cannot happen, and the real defect is the inverse: the train DERAILS and discards its verify. The fix direction (option (a) below) is unchanged.

=== MECHANISM (verified in code) ===
`orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_queue.py::_do_train_merge` reads `main_sha = await git_ops.get_main_sha()` BEFORE the train verify and passes it as `expected_main=main_sha` to `_journal_landed_then_advance` WITHOUT `reverify_on_rebase=True`. If main moved during the verify, `git_ops.py::GitOps.advance_main`'s attempt loop rebases/re-merges the tip onto the new main (`rebased = True`), skips the "Reverify-on-rebase gate" (flag unset), and reaches `git update-ref refs/heads/main <rebased> <expected_main>`. `expected_main` is the stale pre-verify value, so the CAS is certain to fail → `AdvanceOutcome('cas_failed')` → `_do_train_merge` emits `train_derailed` ('Train merge advance failed: cas_failed') and returns blocked; members are re-driven as singles. The rebased sha can never land, so there is NO unverified-landing hole. The task-2154 "Correctness (amendment)" comment after the advance call ("can transparently rebase merge_commit onto a moved main and land the REBASED sha directly") describes an unreachable path whenever expected_main is passed, and it always is here. The `_await_unadvanced_predecessor` docstring states the correct behaviour ("For a TRAIN it is terminal").

Contrast: the single-branch site (`SpeculativeMergeWorker._finalize_inflight`) passes `reverify_on_rebase=True`, gets `rebased_pending_reverify`, runs `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` (disjoint delta → advance with no re-verify; overlap → re-verify), re-anchors base_sha, and retries the CAS. A direct docs commit during a solo verify is therefore absorbed in ~2 min (measured 09-18, task 5578); during a train verify it costs the whole train.

=== MEASURED COST (runs.db `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, read-only, 2026-09-23) ===
train_merged 37, train_derailed 29 all-time; 5 derails are `cas_failed`: coalesce-3215 (07-31, 27 min verify lost), 3146 (07-31, 27 min), 4097 (08-16, 29 min), 4545 (09-06, 53 min), 4574 (09-16, 72 min; the mover was a direct docs commit 4 s after the train read main). Each also re-drives every member solo, and 4574's derail re-pended the tip with a stacked branch carrying the other member's commits (see memory feedback-a-lost-cas-train-derail-repends-the-tip-with-a-stacked-branch). Operational side-effect: interactive sessions are now deferring direct-to-main docs commits whenever the queue is live, because the train case is not separable from the harmless solo case.

=== FIX ===
INVARIANT (unchanged): a train never advances main to a tree no gate verified. NEW GOAL: a moved main does not discard a green train verify when the intervening delta cannot interact with the train.
Pass `reverify_on_rebase=True` at the train site and handle `'rebased_pending_reverify'` with a bounded CAS loop mirroring the single-branch one (re-read main, MAX_CAS_RETRIES). Route through `merge_gates.py::_reverify_rebased_tree` with the train's merge worktree; the branch-touched set MUST be the UNION of all members' diffs against the merge-base (a single member's diff is not the train's footprint): disjoint → advance the rebased sha without re-verify, overlap → re-run the post-merge verify on the rebased tip. Re-record the LandedOutbox row with the landed sha (the 2154 block becomes reachable and correct). Rewrite "DEFENSIBLE DELTAS" item 1 and the 2154 comment to state the real policy. Keep the happy path (main unmoved → one verify, one advance) byte-identic…[truncated, 15294 chars total]

Completed: Merge lane never un-stacks a train member whose predecessor leaves the queue without landing — the orphan's conflicts are then reported as the member's own
Description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 while resolving esc-4137-3/esc-4137-4 (steward). Task 4137's merge was blocked for reasons that had nothing to do with task 4137.

THE DEFECT. When a train is formed, an order>0 member is rebased onto its predecessor's branch tip rather than main (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::_resolve_predecessor_tip, "train-predecessor tip or main"). That is correct at formation. But if the predecessor subsequently leaves the merge queue WITHOUT LANDING, nothing un-stacks the member. The member's branch silently keeps carrying every one of the predecessor's commits, and its next merge_request therefore reports the PREDECESSOR's conflicts against main as its own.

THE SIGHTING. task/4137 (7 own commits, all dashboard) was stacked behind task/4480 at 2026-09-08 21:49 (reflog task/4137@{0} = 'rebase (finish) onto 9788a34b13'). Task 4480 then went to status=pending and left the queue, never merged; merge_status(task_id=4480) = unknown. Ten days later 4137's merge attempt reported 15 conflicts — of which 14 were 4480's fused-memory test refactor vs main's task-3895 load_script_module migration. Replaying only 4137's own delta (`git merge-tree --merge-base=9788a34b13 main <tip>`) conflicts in exactly ONE file, its own index.html cache-buster.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE BRANCH. The failure is mis-attributed by construction. The merger sees a 15-way conflict "in task 4137" and every available remedy is wrong: resolving toward main silently DROPS the absent predecessor's entire deliverable (here 786 lines of new files plus a 15-suite rewrite that exists nowhere else); combining both sides lands the predecessor's whole deliverable through the member's merge, outside the member's plan scope and file locks, and requires implementing the predecessor against a main ~2145 commits ahead. Both destructive options look locally reasonable to an agent that has not audited the branch's reflog. Only the third — un-stack — is correct, and identifying it requires noticing the stacking in the first place. Two escalation rounds were consumed on this one instance before a human-authority role took the ref rewrite.

COMPLETION CONDITION. The lane should detect, at merge_request admission time, that a branch's merge-base against main is a non-landed sibling task's branch tip, and un-stack it automatically via the operation the lane already owns — git_ops.py::materialize_member_solo(predecessor_ref=...), equivalently `git rebase --onto main <predecessor_tip> <branch>` — before attempting the merge. Escalate only if THAT rebase conflicts. Suggested shape: on dequeue, resolve the recorded train predecessor (or derive it by testing whether merge-base(branch, main) is the tip of another task's branch), check whether it is an ancestor of main, and if not, un-stack. Regression test: a member stacked on a predecessor branch that never lands merges solo on its own delta and reports only its own conflicts.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: how many other branches are currently in this state. The condition is cheap to detect in bulk (for each task branch, is merge-base(branch, main) equal to some other task/* tip that is not an ancestor of main?) and each hit is a mis-attributed merge failure waiting to happen. Task 4480 itself remains status=pending with 15 commits living only on task/4480; it is the one carrier of that work and should be scheduled before its base drifts further.

NOT A DUPLICATE (searched): 1878 (worktree-reuse rebases onto main unconditionally) is the mirror-image bug and is done; 1867/4737/4953 are merge-deferred stranding after coalescing; 4669 is a requeue rebase dropping a commit whose patch no longer applies; 2403 is a branch reset to an unrelated tip. None covers a member left stacked on a predecessor that exited the queue unlanded.

CORRECTION + EXTENSION to the 2026-07-28 norm "No test in dark-factory asserts on CLAUDE.md *content* ... CLAUDE.md doc tasks are impl-only with no meta-test" (mem0 0615a402-7ac2-492c-b87d-20c00c20cb08). That was true when written and is now FALSE. Verified in-tree 2026-09-10 while planning task 5330.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. Task 3959 landed `tests/scripts/test_package_source_lookup_convention.py`, which does assert on CLAUDE.md content — and does it one step past a string mirror: it extracts the command from a `<!-- package-source-lookup:begin -->` / `:end` HTML-comment marker pair wrapping a labelled inline-code bullet, then EXECUTES it, so the recipe is certified to still work rather than merely to still be spelled the same way. Its sibling `tests/scripts/test_contributing_lint_command_drift.py` (task 3558) is the older half of the pattern (`_documented_lint_command`), mirroring a CONFIG value where there is one to mirror. Both live in `tests/scripts/`, which carries its own module config and so runs under FULL_SUITE and merge-role `merge_verify_breadth: full`. `tests/scripts/conftest.py` records a no-cross-import convention between guard files, so each carries its own extractor by design — 3959 copied 3558's rather than importing it. Non-negotiable in that extractor: every failure is a loud AssertionError naming the marker literal; a silent `''`/None return would turn the execution assertion vacuously green, which is strictly worse than no guard.

SO: a CLAUDE.md recipe CAN be TDD'd, and the marker-plus-execute shape is the house way to do it.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, and is the real constraint. The same 2026-07-28 entry's cost argument is unchanged and load-bearing: CLAUDE.md is auto-loaded into EVERY agent call from cwd, and `fused-memory/tests/test_config_schema.py` records that filing-project CLAUDE.md growth eroded the path-scope adjudicator's budget floor until it hit `error_max_budget_usd` and became a silent no-op. Combined with the 2026-07-22 "operator-facing knowledge goes to the checked-in doc set, not CLAUDE.md" norm, the usable rule is: CLAUDE.md may gain a short AGENT-SESSION recipe (a marked, copy-pasteable command plus the trap it avoids) but never a REFERENCE TABLE. Carry the command, never the data it prints — a data table is bulk billed on every call AND a second copy free to rot.

CHOOSING THE CHANNEL for a legibility-census remediation. The dominant precedent (tasks 4964, 4273, 4578) is a guidance constant in `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/roles.py` spliced into the eight unpinned role prompts, plus an `orchestrator/tests/test_roles_*.py` splice-contract module. Two questions decide whether that is right: (1) REACH — check the codebook sighting's `manifested_phase`; `ops`/interactive sessions are never handed a role prompt, so roles.py cannot reach them and CLAUDE.md can. (2) SCOPE — roles.py prompts serve every project the factory operates and their existing constants are harness-generic (tool-call rejections, background waits); a fact about THIS repo's files or stores does not belong there. Repo-specific + ops-manifested ⇒ CLAUDE.md; harness-generic + dispatched-agent-manifested ⇒ roles.py.
