FalkorDB fulltext gotchas, measured 2026-10-02 on FalkorDB 4.18 scratch graphs (task 3710):
(1) db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes/queryRelationships against an ABSENT index returns [] silently, with no error. That is why the missing-index defect produced no signal.
(2) While an index is UNDER CONSTRUCTION, a query returns 0 rows, NOT partial results.
(3) On a one-node graph the fulltext index is OPERATIONAL before the first CALL db.indexes() read, so a small fixture cannot observe the build window. A test needs about 50k filler nodes: a status-query-status bracket then held 14/15 times under nice -n 19 with 32 busy loops, and 10/10 at 10k-20k unloaded.
(4) DROP [FULLTEXT ]INDEX FOR (x:L) ON (x.f) removes exactly one field, but re-creating a partially-dropped fulltext index with graphiti's verbatim statement then fails ('Can not override index configuration' / 'Attribute X is already indexed').
target_text: FalkorDB gotcha, verified 2026-10-04 on throwaway graphs: `DROP FULLTEXT INDEX FOR ()-[e:RELATES_TO]-() ON (e.name, e.fact, e.group_id)` deletes only ONE property's fulltext index ('Indices deleted: 1'), leaving the others. Removing a multi-property relationship fulltext index needs one DROP statement per property: ON (e.name), then ON (e.fact), then ON (e.group_id). Range indexes on the same relationship are untouched, and afterwards db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships returns 0 rows. Also: FalkorDB's GRAPH.SLOWLOG does not record queries that hit the TIMEOUT, so timed-out queries must be found in client logs.

entry_text: 2026-09-29 diagnosis: why reify's second merge-verify host leo-laptop sits mostly idle. The laptop only takes overflow merge-queue verifies. HostAllocator.acquire (verify_runner.py) prefers local, so the laptop never verifies the head; all 80 laptop verifies since 08-01 were depth-1 speculative. K = 1 + runners = 2, and a host lease is released only in _finalize_inflight (merge_queue.py), which runs in submission order behind the head. So the laptop finishes in ~22 min, then holds a dead lease until the local head verify lands (~75 min, since the contended workstation is 3.4x slower). That caps laptop utilization at ~30% even with a deep queue. Measured 09-27T07Z to 09-29T16Z from reify runs.db heartbeats: laptop ~11% verifying, ~30% leased but finished, ~43% free while local verified a lone item (queue depth >=2 in ~60% of those, consistent with task 4929's missing host-free wakeup), ~15% both idle. Outages: 09-12 to 09-24 benched on every dispatch (uv not on PATH, fixed cf6184cfe3); 09-25T14:49Z to 09-27T06:57Z quarantined because the laptop was suspended for 41h. Owners: 4929 (wakeup, pending behind 5036), 5205 (local verify contention), 4540 (dark_factory never uses the laptop; pending on 4537).

target_text: Adding a new reify debug-MCP tool: the five same-diff registration obligations (verified 2026-08-26 against gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs). A PURE READ must follow the demand_dispatch_json shape, NOT engine_state_json — the latter routes through build_gui_state_full_scene and RE-TESSELLATES, so a "status" tool built on it would perturb the very thing it reports. Completed: Harden df_pytest_isolation.py: foreign-token deploy-clock fails and the GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS scrub gap
Description: Two independent guard fixes inside `df_pytest_isolation.py`.\n\nFirst, the deploy-clock teardown guard's residual false-fail: `deploy_clock_guard_roots` guards the enclosing MAIN checkout as well as the worktree, and `merge_verify_breadth: full` means many worktrees run the suite concurrently, so a stamp written by worktree A's session makes worktree B's guard ERROR on a token it cannot verify — a false accusation of exactly the class task 4823 exists to fix, which 4823 deliberately left open. Decide whether a foreign token should downgrade to a warning, at minimum make the message say the writer was a concurrent session, and record the ruling (a reasoned won't-fix is an acceptable outcome).\n\nSecond, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` — git's own `-c` propagation channel, with command-line config precedence — is absent from every copy of the redirect-env scrub list, so a poisoned `core.hooksPath` / `safe.directory` / alias survives into every git call in `scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py`, including its `git commit --no-verify`. Add it to all three duplicated copies plus the test's poisoned-env fixture in one coordinated commit; the copies are pinned to each other by a strictly two-directional equality test that must not be weakened.
Analysis: PREMISES VERIFIED (2026-10-03, worktree tip 7cdda17ab4):
- Task 4823 HAS landed: df_pytest_isolation.py carries PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN_ENV='DF_PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN', CLOCK_PROVENANCE_SESSION_KEY, clock_stamp_provenance, ClockVerdict{FALSIFIED, EXTERNAL_REDEPLOY}, deploy_clock_change_report, _clock_attribution_line, _falsified_message and the token-stamping _df_deploy_clocks_unwritten. So the #4905 workstream is implementable now.
- GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS is absent from all three copies: df_pytest_isolation.py::_GIT_REDIRECT_ENV (around line 2530), scripts/reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py::_GIT_REDIRECT_ENV (around line 257, with the "KNOWN GAP" paragraph in scrubbed_git_env), and the `unset` line of scripts/memory-metadata-coverage-census.sh (line 91-93). It is also absent from scripts/tests/test_reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py::POISONED_GIT_ENV.
- Measured on git 2.43.0: `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.hooksPath=/decoy/hooks'" git config --get core.hooksPath` prints /decoy/hooks. A decoy pre-commit hook at that hooksPath RUNS on `git commit` even when `-c` options are also passed. So the census wrapper's `git commit --only` (no --no-verify) runs an injected hook today. That makes a behavioural RED test possible.
- Baseline: `uv run --project shared pytest tests/scripts/test_deploy_clock_isolation.py scripts/tests/test_reclaim_orphaned_worktrees.py -q --timeout=300` gives 155 passed.

NEW FINDING THAT SHAPES WORKSTREAM #4905 (measured here, not in the task text). Most suites run under xdist (`-n auto` in escalation/fused-memory/cockpit addopts). Each xdist worker is its own pytest session, so _df_deploy_clocks_unwritten mints a DIFFERENT uuid per worker. Probe: a nested `pytest -n 2 --dist each` tree in which each worker stamps the guarded clock with its own token, with the two writes overlapping. Result: one worker reported "this run's own $DF_PYTEST_SESSION_TOKEN" and the OTHER reported "from inside another pytest session". So a self-inflicted falsification under xdist already produces "foreign-token" reports from N-1 of N workers. The most common foreign token today is a SIBLING WORKER of the same run, not a concurrent run. Simply rewording the foreign message to "a CONCURRENT pytest session, not this one" would therefore be false in the common case. The fix is one token per pytest RUN. xdist already gives every worker of a run the same `config.workerinput['testrunuid']` (verified in xdist 3.8.0: workermanage.py mints it once per NodeManager; remote.py hands it to every worker). A nested non-xdist session has no `workerinput`, so it still gets a fresh token.

entry_text: GOTCHA (measured 2026-10-01): `git check-ignore -z --stdin` exits 128 if ANY input path is outside the repo (absolute like /etc/hosts or ../x), yet stdout still carries a PARTIAL echo of earlier ignored entries — so a caller must check returncode (0=some ignored, 1=none) before trusting stdout. It echoes each input path verbatim (absolute/./nested), and without --no-index a tracked file matching an ignore rule is NOT reported as ignored.
target_text:
GOTCHA — `git check-ignore` semantics when calling it PROGRAMMATICALLY (complements the gitignore-verification-methodology entry, which covers the `-v` provenance/precedence side). Validated empirically in a scratch repo 2026-08-04 for task 3611's submit-time lint:
(1) By DEFAULT check-ignore consults the INDEX, so a TRACKED file that also matches an ignore rule is NOT reported as ignored (exit 1). That is usually the semantic you want ("can this path ever be committed?"). Passing `--no-index` inverts it and yields a false positive on every tracked path matching a broad rule — only use it to debug why a path became tracked.
(2) Batch mode: `git check-ignore -z --stdin` with NUL-delimited input prints ONLY the ignored subset, NUL-delimited. So "are ALL these paths ignored?" is `len(printed) == len(probed)`; exit 0 means at least one matched, exit 1 means none did.
(3) Exit 128 (fatal on stderr) for BOTH "cwd is not a git repository" AND "path is outside repository at <root>" — an absolute path belonging to another repo aborts the WHOLE batch, not just that entry. Treat 128 as an explicit fail-open sentinel distinct from "nothing ignored"; collapsing the two hides a git failure as a clean result.
(4) The path need not exist on disk — check-ignore evaluates the path string against the rules, which is what makes it usable as a declaration-only lint on files a task has not created yet.

entry_text: Task 'eigensolve: shift-invert Lanczos is inaccurate on non-identity-B pencils (SPD B and buckling B = -K_g): use a B/K-inner-product operator and verify generalized residuals' completed. Landed in commit 091e927d26bda08abeeedbff2e9406497c00e18e.
target_text:
Completed: eigensolve: shift-invert Lanczos is inaccurate on non-identity-B pencils (SPD B and buckling B = -K_g): use a B/K-inner-product operator and verify generalized residuals
Description: lanczos_shift_invert drives faer's partial_self_adjoint_eigen with CompositeShiftInvertOp = (K - sigma*B)^-1 B. That operator is self-adjoint only in the B (or K) inner product, not the Euclidean one. Symmetric Euclidean Lanczos on it therefore returns poor eigenvectors and inaccurate or spurious eigenvalues whenever B is not a multiple of I, yet reports converged=true. Fix the operator or the inner product, and add a post-solve generalized-residual check so a non-eigenpair can never report converged=true.
Analysis: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in source and by a scratch prototype, since deleted): `lanczos_shift_invert` hands faer's `partial_self_adjoint_eigen` the operator A = (K − σB)⁻¹B (`CompositeShiftInvertOp`). faer assumes that operator is Euclidean-symmetric; A is symmetric only when B = cI. faer's lock test (operator/eigen/mod.rs, `residual[j] <= tol`) is the ABSOLUTE Krylov estimate |β·s_j|. It never re-applies the operator, so garbage Ritz pairs are reported as converged.

FIX — the MATH. Let W = K − τB be SPD with W = G·Gᵀ. Then W·A = (K − τB)(K − σB)⁻¹B = B + (σ − τ)·B(K − σB)⁻¹B, which is symmetric. So S = G⁻¹[B + (σ − τ)·B(K − σB)⁻¹B]G⁻ᵀ is Euclidean-symmetric and has the same eigenvalues μ = 1/(λ − σ). Eigenvectors are recovered as φ = G⁻ᵀy. Two arms:
- (i) K − σB is SPD. This includes σ = 0, where it is K itself. Take τ = σ, W = K − σB, S = G⁻¹BG⁻ᵀ. One factorization, and K itself need NOT be SPD (free-free modal with σ < 0 keeps working).
- (ii) K − σB is indefinite. Take τ = 0, W = K, S = G_K⁻¹[B + σB(K − σB)⁻¹B]G_K⁻ᵀ, with (K − σB)⁻¹ applied through the existing sparse LU. This arm needs K SPD, which is the PRD §6 amendment's "K inner product".

B = cI keeps TODAY's Euclidean operator, byte-for-byte. PRD §6 amendment: C1/BT1 stand for B = cI and are waived for B ≠ cI.

FAER SPLIT FACTOR. `faer::sparse::linalg::solvers::Llt` keeps its L factor private, so G⁻¹ and G⁻ᵀ cannot be applied separately through it. The low-level API does expose them:
- Build: `sparse::linalg::cholesky::factorize_symbolic_cholesky(A.symbolic(), Side::Lower, Default, Default)` → `SymbolicCholesky`, then `sym.factorize_numeric_llt(&mut vals, A, Side::Lower, Default, par, stack, Default)`.
- Apply: the factorization is A = PᵀLLᵀP, so G = PᵀL. G⁻¹x = L⁻¹(Px) and G⁻ᵀy = Pᵀ(L⁻ᵀy).
- Simplicial arm: `triangular_solve::solve_lower_triangular_in_place` / `solve_lower_triangular_transpose_in_place` on `SparseColMatRef::new(s.factor(), vals)`.
- Supernodal arm: `supernodal::SupernodalLltRef::{l_solve_with_conj, l_transpose_solve_with_conj}`.
- faer picks supernodal only when flops / nnz(L) > 40 (`CHOLESKY_SUPERNODAL_RATIO_FACTOR`). A tridiagonal, a 10³ 3-D Laplacian and bandwidth-60 banded matrices all stayed SIMPLICIAL. A banded n=300, bandwidth-100 matrix goes SUPERNODAL (measured).
- Measured ‖G⁻¹AG⁻ᵀx − x‖/‖x‖ = 3.8e-16 to 5.8e-16 on both arms.

PROTOTYPE MEASUREMENTS (scratch test, faer 0.24, debug profile). "Euclidean" is today's operator, "symmetrized" is S above. relgap is the relative eigenvalue gap vs `solve_eigen_dense`. genres is the Euclidean generalized residual ‖Kφ − λBφ‖/‖Kφ‖. ρ is the recomputed operator residual ‖Sy − μy‖/(|μ|·‖y‖).
- (A) K = tridiag(−1,2,−1), n = 80; B = diag(1 + i/80); n_modes = 2; tol = 1e-10; σ ∈ {0, 5e-4, 0.05, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5}.
  - Euclidean reproduces the task's numbers exactly: genres 3.58e-1 / 3.27e-1 / 8.46e-2 / 1.73e-2 / 7.48e-3 / 9.26e-3; relgap 1.8e-2 to 4.8e-4; ρ 0.23 to 3.5.
  - Symmetrized: relgap ≤ 1.3e-12, genres ≤ 1.4e-13, ρ ≤ 1.5e-14. Dense residual ≤ 2.3e-12.
- (B) K = tridiag, n = 136; B indefinite tridiagonal (diag +1 on the first half, −0.5 on the second, off-diagonal 0.2); n_modes = 3; σ ∈ {0, 1e-3, 0.02, −0.02, 0.2, −0.3}.
  - Euclidean: relgap up to 15, genres ≈ 1, and at σ = 1e-3 a spurious λ = −0.002…[truncated, 9652 chars total]

entry_text: Three reify tasks carry mis-authored delivered_checks of the MODE-3 shape: a file-existence capability written as kind=grep over file contents, where the pattern is the declared file's own name. They were found by replaying dark-factory task 3500's new authoring lint on 2026-09-28. Task 5511 has pattern 'extrusion_2020' for examples/best_practices/extrusion_2020.ri. Task 6763 and task 6907 have pattern 'divergence-baseline' for a .txt baseline file, whose content will not contain its own name. Such a check goes green only if some other file happens to mention the name, so it can wedge dependents with a DEP_CAPABILITY_NOT_DELIVERED block after the producer lands. Rewrite each as kind='path' (supported since dark-factory task 4743) with the file path and expect=present. The dark-factory lint does not re-check tasks that are already filed.
target_text: A DELIVERED_CHECK CAN BE VACUOUS IN THREE DISTINCT WAYS (reify, measured 2026-08-30 across all 825 check entries). (1) GREEN AT DECOMPOSE TIME: the pattern already matched at the task's own metadata.branch_base_sha, so it asserts nothing that task delivered — 35 of 67 expect:present checks on done tasks were in this state. Many are LEGITIMATE deliberate premise pins (names ending "-substrate", "-exists-today", "-already-implemented"); the suspect ones are those whose NAME claims the task's own deliverable. Task 5750's 'row-9b-premise-corrected' was one, re-pointed 2026-08-30 to the marker 5750 actually landed ("PRD boundary row 9b — RESOLUTION RECORDED"), verified rc=0 on main AND rc=1 at branch_base — that second probe is what proves non-vacuity. CAUTION when probing at a historical sha: probe the path VALID AT THAT REF, else a renamed-since path returns rc=1 for the wrong reason and falsely reads as non-vacuous. (2) INVALID REGEX: task 5627's 'rejection-mechanism-observed-firing' uses pattern `Type::Scalar { dimension } => dimension.is_dimensionless()`; the unescaped braces are an invalid ERE interval so git grep exits 128, the runner reads that as not-matched, and expect:absent passes UNCONDITIONALLY — a gate that can never fail. (3) expect:absent bare tokens false-RED on mere COMMENTS mentioning the token.

GOTCHA — reify-audit's PTODO ratchet (test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh) has a "phantom-tracking" heuristic (crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs §8.3, PHANTOM_PHRASES ~line 1719) that flags ANY source line — including plain `///` doc comments, not just TODO/FIXME/HACK markers — containing one of four phantom phrases ("tracked separately", "tracked as a follow-up", "tracked in project memory", "follow-up task will") with no canonical `#NNNN` cite on that SAME line, as a Medium-severity structural finding. The check fires per-LINE, independent of the TODO/FIXME/HACK marker regex and with NO above-line lookback: in a multi-line `//` comment block, a properly-cited `TODO(#NNNN)` on one line does NOT protect a later line in the same block that happens to contain a phantom phrase without its own same-line cite. Because crates/reify-audit/ptodo-baseline.txt is committed empty (zero-residual-state policy), ANY new PTODO-pattern fingerprint fails the ratchet and blocks merge.

Confirmed trigger in the wild: a doc comment using "Tracked separately from `other_field`" (added by task 4636 in engine_build.rs) tripped this heuristic on an otherwise unrelated code comment.

FIX POLICY — RATIFIED 2026-08-20 (curator gate 5821). Choose by whether a real follow-up actually exists:
1. A REAL, live, non-terminal follow-up exists → CITE IT: `#NNNN` on the same line. This is the primary fix. It is also what the project's hard convention requires for every TODO/FIXME/HACK marker, todo!()/unimplemented!() stub, and blocker #[ignore] (CLAUDE.md "TODO citation convention"; grammar in docs/prds/reify-audit-ptodo-detector.md §8). Rewording away a genuine pointer destroys information and is the wrong fix here.
2. NO real follow-up exists — the phrase is incidental prose and no citation would be meaningful → REWORD (comment-only, no logic change): "Distinct from X" / "Not the same set as X" instead of "Tracked separately from X".
3. A cite you added later goes terminal (done/cancelled) → it becomes an `orphaned` High-severity finding. Re-point it at a live task, or, if no follow-up remains, reword per (2). Cited != tracked.
Escape hatch for a legitimate pattern string that is neither: append `// ptodo:allow — reason`.

To debug/find the exact offending fingerprint: run `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB target/release/ptodo-baseline-gen --project-root $PWD` and inspect the `path :: kind :: text` output.

entry_text: DESIGN GOTCHA (task 5232, measured 2026-10-02 at HEAD 13a9caaca2): never write a checked-in-corpus sweep in shared/tests asserting that every kind='path' delivered_check's paths EXIST on main. It contradicts the task-3500 authoring lint. shared/src/shared/delivered_check_polarity.py::_lint_path_check rejects an expect='present' path check as 'vacuous_present' when its paths already exist, so every correctly-authored adopter names a missing path at the moment its sidecar is committed. At HEAD, 6 of the 7 tracked kind='path' checks (owners 4681, 6181, 6184, 6185, 6188, 6190, all pending) named missing paths. The analogy to TestCheckedInScriptCheckTargets fails: a script target is the CHECKER, and a missing one is a silent ERRORED hold, while path entries are the SUBJECT. A missing path is the normal pre-delivery state and evaluates FAIL, which feeds the visible delivered_fail streak. Telling "permanently red" apart from "not yet delivered" needs owning-task status, so it belongs in a tasks.db-aware scripts/ audit, not the shared suite.
target_text: Auditing delivered_checks / capability-manifest descriptors: the REFERENCE TREE is load-bearing and picking the wrong one inverts the result. A delivered_check is a forward-looking producer gate, so it is SUPPOSED to fail when written and pass after its producer lands. Evaluating the (expect x matches) 2x2 against MAIN TODAY therefore misreads every successfully-delivered done check as "vacuous" — measured on dark_factory at HEAD f38463508e (52 manifests, 548 verdict-PASS kind=grep descriptors) that flags 313/548 (57%), versus 104/538 (19%) when evaluated against each manifest's own authoring tree. Rules of thumb: (1) at AUTHORING time the reference tree is free — HEAD is the pre-task tree, so a vacuity gate there needs no git history at all; (2) retroactively you cannot recover the authoring tree without a commit-ordering premise, so a retroactive sweep must be STATUS-AWARE (present+no-match is a defect on a done task and healthy on a pending one), which means tasks.db and therefore scripts/, not the shared test suite; (3) never assert a corpus-wide vacuity count in a pytest gate — it is un-greenable and the population drifts.

entry_text:
Convention for PRD predicate gates in dark-factory (established by plans/write-triage-link-healing-prd.md D9, 2026-10-01): any gate task that later tasks depend on must ALSO carry a metadata.delivered_checks entry of kind 'script' that re-runs the same predicate.

Why: orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::_deps_satisfied treats a dependency as satisfied when its status is in TERMINAL_STATUSES, which includes cancelled. Cancelling a gate to clear its hold would otherwise silently release everything behind it. A dependency on a task you may not edit has the same hole: a cancelled 3169 would dispatch its dependents. The fix there is an intermediate deterministic 'flip live' gate whose delivered_check asserts the real condition (write_triage.enabled true in the committed config).

Rules for the check itself:
- delivered_checks of kind 'script' run `<project_root>/<script> <args>` against the WORKING CHECKOUT.
- A check must FAIL on today's tree; the non-vacuity lint at commit_planning enforces this.
- scripts/check_write_triage_readiness_gate.py is generic: `--report NAME PATH`, `--require NAME PATH OP VALUE`, `--subcheck`, and its exit code is the contract. It can serve any PRD's gates.
target_text:
metadata.delivered_checks has three consumers in the orchestrator (mapped 2026-09-18):
(1) Scheduler._compute_delivered_check_cache / _deps_satisfied. Every TERMINAL local dep (done OR cancelled) carrying delivered_checks must pass against committed main before its dependents dispatch. That is what holds dependents of a pure gate that closed on `resume`: deterministic_runner never consults delivered_checks. Only DELIVERED results are cached (key: dep, main sha, descriptor digest); FAILED re-runs every tick.
(2) Harness._delivered_checks_withhold. The mark-done gate at the train-member-merged seam; it reverts a member to pending when a check fails or errors.
(3) landing_evidence._delivered_checks_differential. UPGRADE-ONLY positive evidence: the check must be FALSE at the parent, TRUE at the citation sha and TRUE at main. A check already true before the branch gives no signal.
Consequences: a pure gate's check must be producible by the operator (e.g. give a fallback row), and a normal task's check must not be pre-satisfied by upstream work.

entry_text: Gotcha for corpus-repair work that amends Mem0 records in place with update_memory and then checks for duplicate corrections by re-running the census searches: a content amend RE-EMBEDS the record, so an amended target can newly rank for a query where the pre-mutation census did not find it. A check of the form "every id in (after-search hits minus census hits) must not carry the correction marker" therefore fails on correct data unless the amended target ids are also subtracted — the question is whether a NEW record carries the marker, not whether a target moved in the ranking. Measured in task 6060 (2026-09-29): 2 of 5 amended targets surfaced as new hits for a query they had not matched before. The same run showed a sandboxed implementer reaching update_memory and get_memory_by_id over HTTP on :8002 through scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py::FusedMemoryClient under a curator- identity the task text sanctioned, after a zero-UUID probe returned MemoryNotFound.
target_text:
CAPABILITY GAP EVIDENCE (filed 2026-07-27 as dark_factory task 3088, dep-edged onto decision task 3055): fused-memory's Mem0 surface is add-only + delete-only, with no way to amend content or patch metadata while preserving the Qdrant point id. This is the shared root cause of two costly, repeatedly-observed failure patterns.

(1) SURVIVORS CANNOT BE TOPIC-TAGGED, so the deterministic scroll cannot enumerate them. `get_memories_by_metadata(topic=...)` only finds records tagged AT WRITE TIME. When a consolidation identifies pre-canonical survivors it cannot tag them, so rediscovery depends entirely on semantic search — whose top-N cutoff silently drops low-similarity matches. On the reify docs-prd-landing cluster this produced FOUR successive false closure claims (a 7-id sweep missed 4; a 4-survivor addendum missed a 5th; the human gate enumerated 8 and missed 6 more). Falsification stub 6fa72085 documented its own inability to be updated in place, and a separate note (a390babf) existed solely to record that the stub could not be corrected — two entries of pure scaffolding standing in for one missing tool call.

(2) CURATOR-GATE AMENDMENT DEADLOCK. Correcting one clause of an otherwise-good entry requires delete + re-add, which mints a NEW uuid and breaks every inbound pointer. At reify gate 5541 this forced re-issuing the canonical SOP under a new id (166f5106 -> 9b01e961) purely to fold in three residues, leaving stale uuid pointers in sibling entries. It also makes a minimal correction disproportionately expensive, biasing curators toward delete-everything or leave-everything rather than the correct surgical fix.

DESIGN NOTES for 3088: a metadata-only patch must NOT re-embed (so tagging a survivor is cheap and does not perturb ranking), while a content amend must. Metadata merge must be non-destructive shallow-merge by default — the same correction already made for update_task in task 1827, where whole-blob REPLACE silently destroyed sibling keys. Recon Stage 1 (memory_consolidator) is the consumer that needs it every cycle, so the authorization model must cover it. Because in-place content amendment is a silent-rewrite primitive, writes should be journalled and attributable (agent_id + reason) so it does not become a way to rewrite history without a trace.

Also worth noting as a project norm: reify's CLAUDE.md already tells agents NOT to cite Mem0 uuids because they churn on every consolidation round — that norm exists precisely because this tool is missing.

entry_text: To prove a pyright rule is actually live in a workspace member's [tool.pyright] table, rather than just reading the key with tomllib, run `python -m pyright --outputjson -p <member_dir> <tmp_file>` and assert on the rule's diagnostics. Pyright applies that table's settings to an explicitly-named file even when the file is outside the table's `include`, and filesAnalyzed == 1 confirms the check was not vacuous. Each probe takes about 1.5s. Pattern: tests/scripts/test_pyright_unnecessary_ignore_opt_in.py (task 5086), which derives <member_dir> from the module's declared `uv run --directory <x> pyright` type_check_command via verify_command_invariants.anchor_split.
target_text: Workspace-member pyright gotcha (task 5267, measured 2026-10-03): a member's module type_check_command `uv run --directory <m> pyright src/ tests/` passes EXPLICIT CLI targets, which override [tool.pyright] include. So widening include alone (e.g. adding "scripts") reaches only BARE `pyright` runs (hooks/project-checks, the fleet chain, editors), never the merge-verify type leg that runs that command verbatim under merge_verify_breadth "full". That is how fused-memory/scripts quietly accumulated 19 pyright errors. Both homes now name scripts/ for fused-memory and orchestrator. tests/scripts/test_member_scripts_type_gate.py discovers every member that has [tool.pyright] and scripts/*.py, and fails if either gate misses a script or an exclude/ignore carves one out. When adding a new checked directory to a member, edit BOTH include and the module type_check_command.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, main 15634a417f): inside a trait INSTANCE assoc-fn body, every `self.member` / bare member read types as dimensionless Real, regardless of the member's declared type. Cause: crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs compile_assoc_function builds its body scope without set_template_registry, so expr.rs member_access_on_structure_like hits its registry-miss permissive fallback for the StructureRef(conformer) receiver. E.g. `fn lateral_area(self) -> Scalar<Area> { pi * diameter * length }` compiles its body to Real. Any static check on assoc-fn body types (comparison guards, body-vs-return reconciliation) will false-positive or false-negative there. Tracked as #8118; sibling #7855 is the same erase-to-Real class for trait-typed fn params.
target_text: Reify trait associated-fn instance dispatch (task ζ/3941): the `self` receiver is bound by passing the receiver object as the first arg to a UserFunctionCall (Design A), NOT by inlining. A `sub pin : Pin` Ident evaluates to a `Value::StructureInstance` at `ValueCellId(parent, sub_name)` (materialized by task 3540 SIR-α), and member access on a `Type::StructureRef`-typed value compiles to `CompiledExprKind::IndexAccess(obj, Literal(String(member)))` which evals via `Value::StructureInstance.fields.get(k)` (reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~1095). So `self.diameter` inside an assoc-fn body works with zero new evaluator entry point. Key naming constraint: a CompiledFunction's body references params/lets via `ValueCellId(func.name, ...)`, and eval binds args under the same `func.name`, so a function MUST be compiled under the exact name it is registered/called by — you cannot rename a CompiledFunction after compilation without rewriting its body's ValueCellIds. Trait-static fns (task η) follow this by cloning+renaming the FnDef BEFORE compiling (trait_static_fn_symbol = "Trait::method"); instance fns need a per-conformer symbol compiled the same way.

- An opus/high seat was the best choice for code-mechanism tracing.

entry_text: GOTCHA (merge-lane tests that pin a _disjoint_skip_blockers SKIP, measured task 5070 2026-10-03): a lane-scene OrchestratorConfig resolves merge_verify_breadth='full' (the live dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml is layered in; the Field default 'scoped' is not what the test sees), so P1 forces a re-verify and any mutation that empties the overlap delta SURVIVES. GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-09-06, task 4924): when a task has been BLOCKED for a while and you are resuming it just to re-submit the merge, "my branch is unchanged and was verified green" is NOT sufficient. Main moves underneath you, and the thing most likely to bite is a newly-landed lint/debt checker whose baseline is OPT-OUT and SHRINK-ONLY — new files are deliberately NOT grandfathered, so a test file you wrote before that checker existed can fail a gate that did not exist at your merge-base.

CONCRETE INSTANCE. Task 4924 sat blocked ~1 day on unrelated main breakage (the 5088 fleet-pause test drift). While it waited, task 4246 landed `fused-memory/scripts/check_bare_magicmock_config.py`, adding Rule B (bare-dataclass-double) and Rule C (wall-clock-deadline) with SHRINK-ONLY debt baselines. 4924's diff adds a NEW 284-line test file (`orchestrator/tests/test_citation_gate_positive_arm.py`) plus 93 lines appended to a `fused-memory/tests/` file — squarely in that checker's scan scope, and written weeks before the checker existed.

THE CHEAP PRE-FLIGHT, ~4 tool calls, before re-submitting a long-blocked merge:
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..main -- <each of your files>` — per-file main-side churn. Zero on every file means no textual/semantic conflict risk (and is much more informative than a bare `git merge-tree` pass).
2. `git merge-tree --write-tree main HEAD` — rc=0 is a clean speculative merge, computed in-memory with NO worktree mutation. Safe to run on a clean tree; does not touch refs.
3. Diff main against your merge-base for NEW gate scripts (`git show --stat <merge-commit>`), extract them with `git show main:<path> > /tmp/x.py`, and RUN them against YOUR new files. They are typically stdlib-only and take seconds.
4. Only then re-submit.

In 4924's case all four came back clean (rc=0 on the checker), which converted "probably fine" into a measured claim.

SECOND GOTCHA, same sitting: check `merge_status(task_id=...)` BEFORE submitting. On resume-after-escalation the orchestrator had ALREADY re-queued 4924 (`mr-81d83706`, enqueued 4 minutes into the resume cycle, position 7, queue not halted) — even though the escalation handler's written resolution said "re-submit the merge request". The handler's instruction was authored before that auto-resubmission existed. Blindly following it would have added a redundant entry. Compare `enqueued_at` against the resume timestamp in `iterations.jsonl` to tell a FRESH auto-resubmission from a STALE leftover of the blocked attempt.

THIRD, and the one that silently corrupts a verification: an agent Bash session in a worktree typically inherits the MAIN checkout's `VIRTUAL_ENV`, so a bare `python -m pytest` tests MAIN's first-party source, not the worktree code you are about to merge. Run `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV ./.venv/bin/python -m pytest ...` from the worktree, and PROVE which tree you hit by printing provenance first: `env -u VIRTUAL_ENV ./.venv/bin/python -c 'import shared; print(shared.__file__)'` must print a path under `.worktrees/<id>/`. Without that line a green run is not evidence about your branch at all.

entry_text: Trait-member conformance in reify is STRICT for Vector slots: type_compat.rs::implicitly_converts_to has no Vector→Vector rule beyond identity, so a conformer declaring `param axis : Vector3<Length>` against a trait requiring `Vector3<Dimensionless>` fails with DiagnosticCode::TypeMismatchForTraitMember. The dimensionless TOLERANCE in reify-core ty.rs applies only to ctor ARGUMENTS (a dimensionless vec3 passed to a Vector3<Length> param), not to trait-member declarations. So retyping a stdlib trait's vector member is a breaking change for every conformer that declares the old type, and those fixtures must migrate in the same commit.
target_text: In reify, the compiler ENFORCES trait→struct param-type consistency: a `structure def S : SomeTrait` whose `param x : T` type differs from the trait's `param x : U` emits a type-mismatch diagnostic (covered by conformance/mod.rs test `check_phase_check_members_against_requirements_emits_type_mismatch_for_wrong_member_type`). Consequence: tightening a stdlib trait param's type (e.g. tolerancing.ri GeometricTolerance.feature Real→Geometry) is a breaking change that forces EVERY implementing struct — including inline test fixtures in crates/reify-compiler/tests/tolerancing_tests.rs (TestTolMMC/RFS/LMC/Zero/Neg, TestFlat, MyFlat) — to be migrated in the same crate to keep `cargo test -p reify-compiler` green.

target_text: gmsh 4.15.2 deadlocks inside gmshModelMeshGenerate(3) when a PostView background mesh-size field is evaluated from many mesher threads. The threshold is fixture-dependent, so a single measurement does not generalise: on a clean process meshing a unit cube, General.NumThreads=8 completes in ~4s while 32 hangs indefinitely; in tests/mesher_poison_recovery.rs, whose gmsh has already been through a finalize/initialize recovery cycle, 8 already hangs. It is a true block, not slowness (CPU time frozen, all threads in futex_do_wait), and Mesh.MaxNumThreads3D=1 does not avoid it. reify's fix (task #7447) pins General.NumThreads=1 unconditionally in refine_volume_with_size_field. Consequence for test authors: a regression guard for this must ask for a thread count measured to hang ON ITS OWN FIXTURE — copying a count that hangs a different binary silently yields a test that is green on both sides of the fix.

entry_text: Before carrying a branch that /team or subagent seats committed to, read the seats' raw commit messages (git log --format=%B main..<branch>). On 2026-09-28 a sonnet seat wrote two commits with the Co-Authored-By trailer fused into the subject line, because there was no blank line before it. A branch nobody else has fetched can be reworded without changing any tree: git commit-tree <old>^{tree} -p <parent> -m <subject> -m <trailer> for each commit, then git update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <new> <old-tip>, where passing the old tip makes it a compare-and-swap. Confirm git diff --quiet <old-tip> HEAD afterwards. No interactive rebase is needed.
target_text:

body

Co-Authored-By: ..."`. In one session, 2 of 4 such commits kept their layout and 2 SUCCEEDED as a single 700-900-char subject line with the trailer inside it. The two that flattened had `git status --short &&` in the same chain; the cause was not diagnosed. DETECT after every commit: `command git log -1 --format=%B HEAD | wc -l` (2 means flattened). REPAIR without `rebase -i`: write each message to /tmp with a plain heredoc, then `new=$(git commit-tree "<old>^{tree}" -p <parent> -F msg)` for each flattened commit in order (chain -p through the new SHAs). Then run `git reset --soft <newest>`, confirm `git diff --stat <old-tip> HEAD` is empty, and re-call mark_step_done with the new SHAs.

The judge is shown up to judge_candidate_count candidates (config.yaml: 5) and the prompt deliberately RENDERS their ids, but its output contract carries no candidate identity and the attach always targets the band's top-1 — so a verdict reasoned about candidate #3 is applied to candidate #1, and in the contested case stamps the contested flag on a canonical the entry never contradicted. entry_text: Gotcha (socket-activated user units, verified 2026-09-29): (1) First migration of a running service onto a newly installed .socket needs only an ordinary `systemctl --user restart <service>` - systemd orders the old process's stop before the socket's start, and the new process gets LISTEN_FDS. (2) Changing an ACTIVE socket's ListenStream set needs `systemctl --user stop <service>` then `systemctl --user start <x>.socket <service>` - a combined `restart <x>.socket <service>` fails with 'Socket service <service> already active, refusing'. (3) In ExecStopPost, `systemctl --user list-jobs <unit>` shows TYPE `restart` during a restart, `stop` during a stop, and no job during a crash awaiting auto-restart - that is what scripts/stop-socket-unless-restarting.sh keys on.
target_text: systemd socket activation with this repo's launch shape: ExecStart is `uv run ...`, which spawns Python as a child, so LISTEN_PID names the uv parent and fd 3 is passed through uv to Python intact - the adopter must accept LISTEN_PID == getppid() (shared/src/shared/systemd_listeners.py does). uvicorn 0.44's Config(fd=...) path hardcodes AF_UNIX via socket.fromfd, so pass the socket to Server.serve(sockets=[socket.socket(fileno=3)]) instead (family auto-detected). A test can hand a child a real listener on fd 3 with Popen(close_fds=False, preexec_fn=lambda: os.dup2(fd, 3)) - close_fds=True runs after preexec_fn and would close it.

/team routing lessons from the 2026-09-28 pin-starvation study.
- An opus/high seat was the best choice for code-mechanism tracing.
- A sonnet/medium seat got a control-flow ORDERING question backwards. It claimed the harness semaphore gates Scheduler.acquire_next, but harness.py calls acquire_next BEFORE sem.acquire, so an on-deck task is picked and holds its locks while waiting for a slot. Route ordering and concurrency questions to high effort.
- A sonnet/high forensic seat produced correct interval reconstructions but two presentation errors: it read PSI dispatch_deferred per-task counts as targeting (they are a naming artifact: only the first deferred heavy candidate is named per held tick), and it labelled a top blocker '100%' when it meant the module was blocked all week by rotating owners. Check a seat's derived labels, not just its numbers.
target_text: dark-factory scheduler, measured 2026-09-28: why HIGH-tier pinned tasks starve for weeks. (1) Only the scored loop's single STRICT-TOP candidate earns skip counts and fairness parks (Scheduler._phase_select_scored -> _bump_skip_and_maybe_park). Scores are tier-dominated (config.py TIER_BASE critical 16000 vs high max 8999), so while any eligible effective-critical candidate exists a high pin can never be strict top, never parks, and its skip_count stays 0. In the 7 days to 09-28 all 390 task_skipped events went to 6 critical tasks (3542 170, 4541 79, 4023 57, 5677 41, 3620 33, 5221 10). (2) The pin loop (Scheduler._phase_select_pins) only gives a pin first try at ALL-OR-NOTHING lock acquisition on each tick. On conflict it falls through silently: no event, no skip, no park. (3) The harness calls acquire_next BEFORE sem.acquire, so at saturation (24/24) there is about one tick per freed slot (409 ticks in 7 days, of which 15 ended at select_pins). (4) The hot files are practically never free: holds alone left orchestrator config.py unheld 1.7% and verify.py 2.7% of 09-21..09-28, and harness.py/workflow.py's unheld stretches were covered by 3542's critical parks. Result: pins 3500, 3659, 5205, 5812 had their full file sets free ~0% of the week. (5) A boost_tier propagates UPSTREAM to undone deps (_compute_effective_priorities). The critical boost on OPERATOR GATE 3545 made its dep 3542 critical, and 3542 was then strict top for a month (1121 skips, 19 critical park installs 08-26..09-27), with parks on workflow.py/harness.py that were the top blocker for pins 3659 and 5677. (6) Starvation watchdog cannot fire for a high pin (dual gate needs skip>=50; idle-only gate is 30 days on an in-memory clock). (7) PSI dispatch_deferred names only the FIRST heavy candidate deferred per held tick (the first eligible heavy pin), so its per-task counts are a naming artifact, not targeting. Related tasks: 5308 (partial/empty parks, pin-loop park clearing, reserve_now at effective tier), 3821 (watchdog), 3825 (below-rank-1 counting), 3824 (durable fairness state). None as written gives a never-top-scored pin a reservation.

entry_text: Merge-lane ratchet test sweep scope (scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::imports_lane_module_in_tree, read 2026-10-03 for task 5341): a test file is measured, and its private_reads/patch_targets pinned per file, ONLY if it DIRECTLY imports a CLUSTER_PATHS module (e.g. orchestrator.git_ops, lane_lifecycle, warm_lane_pool, offline_lane, merge_*) or orchestrator.merge_lane.*. A test file that gets GitOps/harness objects through helpers imported from another test module (e.g. `from test_harness_terminal_lane_record_reclaim import _make_pool_harness`) is not swept. Because test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement demands baseline == fresh measurement, ANY count change in a swept file (even a decrease) forces a baseline regeneration, so new tests are cheapest in a non-swept file.

Merge-lane ratchet, the TESTS-map arm (measured 2026-09-12 at HEAD=e9d1055ed8, task 5097 planning). Complements the earlier entry on cluster TOTALS and complexipy charging; this is the rule that bites a task adding TEST coverage rather than source.

scripts/merge_lane_metrics.py::test_file_measures admits an orchestrator/tests file to the baseline's `tests` map iff `imports_lane_module(source)` — i.e. it imports orchestrator.merge_queue, orchestrator.merge_lane, or any other CLUSTER_PATHS module. Consequences for a NEW test file:
- It gains a `tests` entry, which ALONE stales the committed baseline and reddens test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement (byte-identity).
- Its private_reads feed derive_totals, which sums the WHOLE current tests map (baseline 7847 over 229 entries) and _check_totals fails on any rise. _check_tests iterates BASELINE keys only and skips absent paths, so the per-file arm does NOT protect you — the totals arm does the failing. The ratchet's own seeded self-test pins a brand-new file with private_reads:1 as a total:private_reads violation.
- private_reads is deliberately RECEIVER-AGNOSTIC: any `x._foo` (non-dunder) counts, including writes (`worker._host_allocator = a`) and calls (`await worker._dispatch_item(i)`), and chains count per hop. Bare self./cls. receivers are excluded, but `self.worker._x` counts. No helper, fixture or naming trick avoids it.
- patch_targets is a UNION across all tests entries, so reusing a leaf already in the baseline's 83 is free; a brand-new leaf is a violation.

Practical upshot: a test file that imports only orchestrator.verify_runner or orchestrator.config is INVISIBLE to both gates (neither is a cluster path) and can use unrestricted private access and length. orchestrator/tests/test_host_allocator.py is the worked example — absent from the baseline, module-level imports are pytest only. Keep new merge-lane-adjacent tests lane-import-free on purpose when you can.

When you genuinely cannot test the wiring (e.g. a new config knob threaded into merge_queue.py), pyright is the available substitute: orchestrator/pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] includes both `src` and `tests`, so making the new parameter REQUIRED keyword-only turns an unwired call site into a reportCallIssue on every pre-commit and verify. Task 5097 took that route after confirming no test anywhere drives the real SpeculativeMergeWorker._dispatch_item.

Also measured: merge_queue.py sits at EXACTLY its frozen lines=21572 / prose_lines=12288 / cognitive=2132, so a task that adds no cluster file has ZERO line slack there and must make every comment/docstring edit line-count-preserving (E501 is ignored in orchestrator/pyproject.toml, so a long line needs no wrap). Such a task raises no measure and must therefore NOT regenerate the baseline — regeneration is only correct for a commit that legitimately changes a measure (e.g. ζ1's new package directory).

Completed: Grammar has no method-call-with-arguments rule: obj.map(|v| ...) / .filter / .all / .any are parse errors, leaving reify-expr's method arms unreachable from .ri source
Description: Discovered while planning task #5385 (generate-of-geometry silent undef); see escalation esc-5385-1. OUT OF SCOPE for #5385, which delivers only the generate + union_all halves of its acceptance criteria.

OBSERVATION (measured on HEAD 975cbfc301 with target/debug/reify built 2026-08-21): the tree-sitter grammar has NO method-call-with-arguments rule. In tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, `member_access` (grammar.js:1583-1587) is `prec.left(11, seq(field('object', $._expression), '.', field('member', $.identifier)))` — no callTail. The only argument-taking call rules are `function_call` (grammar.js:1572, bare identifier + callTail) and `trait_method_call` (grammar.js:1642, qualified/instance-qualified callee + callTail).

Consequences measured directly:
- `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` over `let xs = [1, 2, 3]` => "Parse error: invalid let". Same for `xs.filter(|v| v > 1)`, `xs.all(|v| v > 0)`, `xs.any(...)`, and even `xs.foo(|v| v)` — so the gap is method-ARGUMENTS, not lambdas and not element type.
- `constraint all_pos: xs.all(|v| v > 0)` => "Parse error: invalid constraint" — not let-position-specific.
- Free-function forms `map(xs, |v| v)` / `filter(xs, |v| v > 1)` also fail; no free-function map/filter exists.
- `generate(3, |i| i)` and `flat_map(xs, |v| [v])` DO parse (both `function_call`); `xs.count` parses (bare `member_access`, no parens). So lambdas work and member access works — only method arguments are missing.

DEAD CODE this leaves behind: the `"map"`, `"filter"`, `"all"`, `"any"`, `"generate"` arms of `eval_method_call` in crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs (lines ~3695, ~3825, ~3714, ~3739, ~3811) are unreachable from .ri source and exercised only by Rust-level tests. crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs:3798-3810 even documents a deliberate negative-count policy divergence between the free-function and METHOD forms of `generate` — a distinction no .ri program can observe.

WORK TO DECIDE/DO (triage first, this is a design question, not a mechanical fix):
(a) add an `obj.method(args)` rule to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js plus the corresponding lowering in crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, so the existing evaluator arms become reachable; or
(b) expose the wanted combinators as free functions instead (the shape `generate` and `flat_map` already use) and delete or clearly mark the unreachable method arms; or
(c) accept the gap deliberately and document it, marking the unreachable arms so future readers do not assume surface coverage.

Files: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js, crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs, crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs.

Rationale for filing: leaving evaluator arms with no surface form is a silent-capability-gap — a design session reading the stdlib docs would reasonably write `xs.filter(...)` and get an opaque "invalid let" parse error rather than an unsupported-construct diagnostic.
Analysis: TRIAGE (the task asks for a design decision first).

PREMISE CHECK — the task text is partly stale. It was measured on 975cbfc301 (2026-08-21). Task 5495 μ landed afterwards (35e9259316 / dcc2f6a641, 2026-08-28) and added `namespaced_call: prec(12, seq(field('callee', $.member_access), callTail($)))` to tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js:2004. That rule captures EVERY `<expr>.name(args)`, so `xs.map(|v| v + 1)` now PARSES. `lower_namespaced_call` (crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs:5401) then rejects it at lowering. Measured 2026-10-01 with this lane's target/release/reify (main 107171c475):
  - `let ys = xs.map(|v| v + 1)` and `constraint xs.all(|v| v > 0)` → exit 1, "unknown qualifier `xs` in `xs.map(...)` … Reify has no method-call syntax, so this cannot be a call on a value named `xs`". So the "opaque `invalid let`" the task was filed about is GONE for identifier receivers, in let AND constraint position.

Completed: Retire 2 residual stale "ctor binding is POSITIONAL" comment claims missed by #6484's inventory
Description: Follow-up filed by task #6484 (implementer). #6484 corrected 5 comment sites that still asserted the pre-#4522 false claim that structure-ctor argument binding is POSITIONAL and `name:` labels are cosmetic. Task #4522 landed by-name ctor binding: each `name:` label is resolved against the declared params, and only UNLABELLED args fill the remaining slots in declaration order.

A corpus sweep during #6484 (`grep -rn "POSITIONAL\|positional" --include=*.ri examples/ crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/`) found 2 further sites carrying the same stale premise. Both were OUTSIDE #6484's explicit 5-site inventory, so #6484 deliberately left them untouched rather than widening its scope. Neither is covered by any automated gate (these are comments; the corpus gates only assert the files parse and compile clean).

SITE 1 — examples/fea_shell_too_thick_annotated.ri:44-49. The strongest surviving instance, and flatly false today:
  "The Reify DSL uses positional-call form exclusively — field labels like
   `shell_force: ShellForce.On` are stripped by the parser and treated as
   positional args (see crates/reify-syntax/src/ts_parser.rs).  To set
   `shell_force` (position 8) we must supply all preceding defaults explicitly"
Post-#4522 labels are NOT stripped and the "must supply all preceding defaults" consequence no longer holds — a caller can simply label `shell_force:`. The comment then enumerates 9 positional defaults justified solely by that false premise; whoever fixes this should decide whether the enumerated call is still worth keeping for review visibility (the pattern #6484 adopted elsewhere) or should be simplified to labelled form.

SITE 2 — crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/fea_multi_case.ri:514-515 (the `Gravity` structure def). Weaker but now internally inconsistent:

entry_text: Reify: a user `structure def`'s runtime Value::StructureInstance is built at FOUR independent sites, so any change to what an instance carries must cover all of them: (1) reify-expr eval_structure_instance_ctor (lowered in reify-compiler expr.rs from the authoritative template for entity-scope ctors, and from build_structure_def_skeleton templates for fn-body ctors); (2) engine_eval.rs plain-sub collapse (writes ValueCellId(parent, sub) and the "{parent}.{sub}"/__self alias); (3) engine_eval.rs keyed-sub per-key collapse; (4) unfold.rs nested-sub collapse. The three engine collapses gather fields from child_template.value_cells scoped cells only. Sub elaboration (unfold.rs elaborate_child_instance_nested) does NOT evaluate the child template's guarded_groups at all, so `Test.s.g` scoped cells never exist for where-guarded members (measured 2026-09-29, task #5935).
target_text:
Task 'Engine: project derived `let` cells off Value::StructureInstance (fn-returned/param-held) — not only the `sub` elaborate_child_instance path' completed. ROOT CAUSE (architect capability trace): derived `let` cells of a structure (e.g. upper_limit/lower_limit/tolerance_band, max_clearance/min_clearance) are materialized ONLY when the structure is instantiated as a `sub`-component. The engine's `elaborate_child_instance` computes child-scope lets — that is why `Flange.dim_tol.upper_limit` resolves correctly when reached via a `sub` (see m8_3_stdlib_integration.rs:557-615, the REFERENCE semantics that already work). A structure produced as a `Value::StructureInstance` — returned from a `.ri` free fn (`symmetric_tolerance`/`limit_tolerance`) or held in a `param` (`Fit.hole_tolerance`/`shaft_tolerance`) — carries ONLY constructor args+defaults: `eval_structure_instance_ctor` inserts only ordered_args+defaults into `fields`, never the template's let bindings (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:893-916); `eval_index_access` then projects members as fields.get(k).unwrap_or(Undef) (reify-expr/src/lib.rs:946-948). So any derived `let` member of a fn-returned or param-held struct reads as undef.

EMPIRICAL (prebuilt `reify eval`):
(1) DimensionalTolerance(...).upper_limit → undef, while .nominal (a stored param) → 0.01 m.
(2) `sub f` with derived `let max_clearance = hole_tolerance.upper_limit - ...` → f.max_clearance = undef AND f.hole_tolerance.upper_limit = undef (the param-held struct member is itself a fn/ctor-produced StructureInstance, so its lets are undef even from within an elaborated sub).
(3) `sub st = symmetric_tolerance(...)` is a PARSE ERROR (a `sub` cannot bind a function call), so the `sub` elaborate_child_instance path cannot rescue the fn-returned-struct case at all.

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL (acceptance): via `reify eval`, DimensionalTolerance(5mm, +0.02, -0.01).upper_limit must evaluate to a concrete value (not undef); and the param-held case Fit.hole_tolerance.upper_limit must likewise resolve, so derived `let` members of fn-returned and param-held struct values behave consistently with the working `sub`-child case.

DESIGN NOTE (do NOT pre-decide — weigh both in the plan): the implementer must choose between (a) EAGER evaluation of template `let` bindings inside `eval_structure_instance_ctor` (populate `fields` with the derived cells at construction), versus (b) LAZY projection at member-access time in `eval_index_access` (evaluate a requested `let` member against the template + stored fields on demand). The acceptance bar is CONSISTENCY with the existing `sub` semantics: mirror `elaborate_child_instance`'s child-scope scoping so a derived member resolves to the same value regardless of whether the struct arrived via a `sub`, a free-fn return, or a `param`. Consider cost/cycles if template lets are expensive (eager pays at every construction even when members are never read; lazy must guard against recomputation and cycles) — but keep sub-consistency as the bar, not a particular evaluation strategy.

CONSUMER (G1): task 4267 (tolerancing γ) depends on this — its RED tests (upper_limit/max_clearance read off fn-returned and param-held struct values) are the immediate consumers. More broadly, every stdlib structure with derived `let` members benefits; this is a language-semantics trap for all such structures, currently masked because most are reached via `sub`.

REFERENCES: reify-expr/src/lib.rs:893-916 (eval_structure_instance_ctor — inserts only ordered_args+defaults); reify-expr/src/lib.rs:946-948 (eval_index_access — fields.get(k).unwrap_or(Undef)); engine `elaborate_child_instance` + m8_3_stdlib_integration.rs:557-615 (the working `sub`-child reference semantics to mirror).

entry_text: Gotcha, measured 2026-09-29 for task 6029. On this host /bin/sh is dash 0.5.12, which FORKS the command for `sh -c 'sleep 30'` rather than exec'ing it. So asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(..., start_new_session=True) makes a group of the sh leader plus a sleep child. After the leader is killed and reaped, the child is orphaned to systemd --user (pid 2626) and sits in state R/Z. os.kill/os.killpg(..., 0) keeps succeeding until systemd --user reaps it. systemd --user was observed stalling for ~100s (2026-09-28 22:29:20 to 22:31:03 BST, with `systemctl --user show` timing out), so ANY bounded poll on killpg/kill(…,0) after killing a tree can false-red regardless of its timeout. That is what reddened test_proc_group's terminate tests after tasks 1081/1450 had "fixed" them with a 5s poll. Judge termination by /proc state instead (Z/X counts as exited). A deterministic zombie for tests: Popen, then SIGKILL, then os.waitid(P_PID, pid, WEXITED|WNOWAIT), which blocks until the child has exited without reaping it.
target_text: Process-group teardown tests must poll for pgid disappearance, not assert it synchronously. shared/tests/test_proc_group.py::test_terminate_process_group_reaps_grandchildren is flaky because `os.killpg(pgid, 0)` only raises ProcessLookupError after every group member is *reaped*, not just signalled. After bash leader is wait()'d, the sleep grandchildren are reparented to systemd --user (or pid 1) and only become non-zombie when that subreaper periodically calls waitpid(). The race window is non-deterministic; bounded polling (50× 100ms) is the right pattern.

entry_text:
Decompose technique that decouples commit_planning from the sidecar's landing (used 2026-10-02 for the link-healing batch 6181–6192).

Steps:
1. Generate the producers' metadata.delivered_checks AND the capability-manifest YAML sidecar from ONE Python spec. Build each check with shared.capability_manifest.DeliveredCheckMeta(name=<capability name>, ...).model_dump(), exactly as fused_memory/server/manifest_stamping.py builds its copies.
2. Set delivered_checks at submit_task.
3. After filing, write the sidecar with the real task_ids already filled in, dumped with yaml.safe_dump(sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True) — the stamper's own dumper. Assert the dump round-trips.

Result: commit_planning's stamper rewrote the sidecar byte-identically (git diff empty), re-copied identical checks, and reported stamped=all 12 labels with errors=[]. No second commit of the stamped sidecar was needed.

Why it matters: had the sidecar been absent, the stamper would have been a no-op, and the gates would still have carried their checks. That would have let commit_planning run as soon as the PRD landed, even if the manifest had to wait for a carrier.

Verification: a scripted get_task readback (a scripts/migrate_metadata_modules_to_files.py::FusedMemoryClient subclass) diffed every task's deps, before_done, delivered_checks, milestone and operational shape against the spec before and after the flip.

Gotcha: the stamper overwrites a label's metadata.delivered_checks only when that label has mechanical checks. A gate's own script check stays intact either way.
target_text: Confirmed working end-to-end 2026-07-22: commit_planning's capability-manifest sidecar stamping (task 2578 mechanism). For the stage1-entity-standing-decision batch (7 tasks, 2894-2900), one bulk commit_planning call located the YAML sidecar from metadata.prd_path, stamped all 7 Greek labels with real task ids (manifest_stamping report: stamped=[α..η], missing_labels=[], errors=[]), rewrote the file on disk (normalized YAML — comments dropped, expected), and copied only the mechanical grep checks into each producer's metadata.delivered_checks (kind=manual entries correctly excluded from the dispatch gate). Sidecar must be committed by the decompose session afterward (git commit --only). Validating the sidecar against shared.capability_manifest.CapabilityManifestDoc BEFORE committing (uv run --project shared python -c "...model_validate...") is a cheap pre-flight that prevents a stamping failure at flip time. Note: git commit --only fails on untracked files with "pathspec did not match" — git add them first, then --only works.

entry_text: Cancelling a spawned_from parent BEFORE its child raises a blocking reconciler scope_violation ('Task N orphaned: parent P cancelled') on the still-live child within seconds, even when the child is cancelled moments later. Seen 2026-09-30 as esc-6497-1 and esc-6548-1. Cancel children first. If it happens anyway, close with resolve_issue(action='close_only', resolution_class='moot-terminal-subject'). Before cancelling a parent whose child stays live, re-point the child's metadata.spawned_from at the surviving task (done for #6371: 6134 → 6934, with spawned_from_original and spawned_from_repointed keys).
target_text: Cancelling a reify task orphans every agent-followup it spawned, and each orphan surfaces as a SEPARATE blocking `scope_violation` L2 escalation asking a human to choose expand_scope vs abort_task. Measured 2026-09-11: task 7009 was cancelled as an administrative duplicate of 7308 and orphaned THREE children (7393, 7394, 7395) in one stroke. All three proved independently valid and were kept, so the cancellation was right and only the missing pre-check was wrong. Before any cancel, search for children via `search_tasks` on the parent's SUBJECT (not its id — semantic search drifts badly on "spawned from task N" and returns unrelated stranded-task records), then confirm each candidate's `metadata.spawned_from`. When a parent is cancelled ADMINISTRATIVELY (duplicate, merged elsewhere) rather than because a finding was retracted, children almost always survive — but re-verify each child's premise against current main anyway. Afterwards re-point each child's `metadata.spawned_from` at the surviving task, or the reconciler re-raises the orphan flag.

Recovering evidence of a bare xdist worker crash whose verify log was never persisted. Three sources survive:
(1) `<worktree>/orchestrator/.pytest_cache/v/cache/lastfailed` holds the nodeid xdist synthesized a FAILED report for, i.e. the crashed worker's in-flight test. The file's mtime is the controller session end, not the moment of death. The entry disappears when a later run passes that test, so read it before any retry.
(2) On the implement path, the streamed `.worktrees/<id>/.task/verify/attempt-N.<pkg>.test.log` survives the raise until a later attempt with the same N overwrites it. It carries '[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated' and "worker 'gwN' crashed while running '<nodeid>'".
(3) Merge-lane verify logs are archived unconditionally in data/verify-logs/<task>/.
With `--max-worker-restart=0` the suite keeps running on the surviving workers after a death: task 3714's worker died at 83% and the session still finished '1 failed, 19294 passed'. So detection time is not death time.

STAMPED PEER under topic `orchestrator-xdist-worker-crash-under-load` (canonical 40d1b472). A CODE-PATH finding no earlier peer records, measured task 5523 during plan revalidation at main 4ff6f032f8, 2026-09-21. It explains WHY the esc-5333-3 "only a truncated worker tail was captured" complaint happened, and corrects a natural but wrong assumption about where that evidence lives.

OBSERVED in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify.py (all line numbers at 4ff6f032f8):
- The bare-crash reclassification raises `VerifyInfraError(phase='xdist_worker_crash', errno=None)` at line 6332, inside `run_verification` (5542).
- The log-persistence block is at 6360-6394 — BELOW the raise. So on the reclassified path `_persist_attempt_logs` and `_archive_attempt_log` NEVER RUN, `worktree_log_paths` / `archive_log_paths` are both empty, and no `attempt-N.summary.json` is written.
- CONSEQUENCE: a reclassified xdist_worker_crash is never copied to the durable archive under data/verify-logs/<task_id>/. The only complete copy is the log `_run_cmd` already STREAMED to `<worktree>/.task/verify/attempt-N[.prefix].test.log`, which survives only as long as that worktree does.
- The raise also passes NO message, and `VerifyInfraError.__init__(phase, errno, message='')` then synthesises `infra OSError during verify phase='xdist_worker_crash' errno=None`. That one line is the whole of what an investigator receives. The defect is a MISSING POINTER, not missing data — but the data it should point at is the WORKTREE copy, not the archive.

WHY THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT the 2026-09-21 census peer (263aee57), which correctly says "the durable archive under data/verify-logs/<task>/attempt-N.orchestrator.test-*.log keeps the FULL log". Both are true because the reclassification is VETOED for most of these crashes: `_is_bare_xdist_worker_crash` (685) vetoes on a flat set including `^FAILED `, and a bare worker crash does emit `FAILED ... - worker 'gwN' crashed`. So the census events took the NORMAL path and were archived; the reclassified minority are the ones that vanish. Do not generalise either way — check which path a given event took before hunting for its log.

PRACTICAL: when an xdist_worker_crash infra-error is all you have and data/verify-logs/<task_id>/ holds nothing, look in the task worktree at .task/verify/attempt-N*.test.log before concluding the evidence was lost. Task 5523's plan adds that pointer to the raised message so this stops being tribal knowledge.

Today's filter is `graph_name != 'default_db' and not graph_name.endswith('_db')` (`graphiti_client.py:605`, `:2979-2982`) — it would otherwise provision all **35** probe/test/scratch graphs on every restart.

- `_indexed_graphs` is checked-and-set WITHOUT a lock today; wrap in the existing `_identity_lock_for(group_id)` pattern (`:438` — a SYNC accessor returning the Lock itself, so `async with backend._identity_lock_for(gid):`) so two concurrent first-writes don't both build.

*** INV-7 PIN — LOCK SCOPE IS LOAD-BEARING ***
Hold the per-group lock ONLY across the diff+create. Do **NOT** hold it across an `OPERATIONAL` barrier: index creation is background and takes up to **594.5 ms** to become operational, which would convert a bounded hold (statements return in 0.5-2.0 ms; a full 13-statement build at dark_factory scale is 1.93 s including background completion) into a long one blocking every concurrent write to that group. entry_text: To tell whether a `reportMissingImports` pragma on a cross-workspace-member import is load-bearing, measure under a NARROW env as well as the all-packages one. reify gotcha: running `rustfmt --edition 2024 <file>` on a crates/*/tests/<name>.rs integration test that declares `mod common;` ALSO rewrites tests/common/*.rs (rustfmt follows out-of-line `mod` declarations), silently widening a targeted format into shared helpers. Format a new test file with `rustfmt --edition 2024 --config skip_children=true` (nightly-only) or restore with `git checkout -- crates/<c>/tests/common/` afterwards, and always check `git status` before staging.
target_text: In reify, running `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops.rs` also emits a whole-file diff for `crates/reify-eval/src/geometry_ops/tests.rs`: rustfmt follows the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` child-module declaration into the separate file, and that file's contents are written indented 4 spaces (as if they were an inline `mod tests { … }` block), so rustfmt wants to dedent all ~26k lines. Per CLAUDE.md's no-rustfmt-gate invariant that diff must NOT be applied — it is an unbounded rewrite of a file you did not touch. When targeted-fmt-checking a parent module that declares child modules, expect and ignore child-file diffs; verify your own new code's formatting by eye instead.

entry_text: Reify language spec (docs/reify-language-spec.md, `where` section ~lines 1603-1621) rules that `where` blocks nest with guards composing CONJUNCTIVELY and that `else` members desugar to `where !condition`. So an else branch nested under an INACTIVE outer guard is inactive. The engine currently activates it (with on=false, Inner.ge=0.009 m) - a spec violation found by task #5935's architect (esc-5935-11). The watcher applied the spec rather than escalating: filed #7997 to fix the top-level guard composition (RED test first) and told #5935 not to mirror the bug in its new guarded-member construction paths.
target_text: Reify gotcha: the `reify eval` CLI attaches a constraint solver, so Engine::eval's post-solver guard re-eval pass re-runs every guarded group. That hides ordering bugs that a solver-less `Engine::new(checker, None)` exposes. Before task #7997 lands, guarded_groups is emitted in POST-order (nested before parent), so solver-less eval reads a nested group's parent guard cell as Undef. Test guard semantics on BOTH engine configurations.

entry_text: Counting pytest-xdist workers of a scoped run (measured 2026-10-05, task 5469; peer of 64c791bb under topic verify-resource-measurement). Under `-q` with non-tty output xdist never prints `created: N/M workers` — TerminalDistReporter.getstatus returns only "bringing up nodes..." at verbose < 0 — so a verify-shaped `-q` log cannot prove the worker count. Reading PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER from /proc/<pid>/environ UNDER-counts (read 5 of 16): that file is the process's initial environment and xdist sets the variable after the worker starts. What worked: run the command in a named scope (`systemd-run --user --scope --unit=<u>`), and from OUTSIDE the scope (so the sampler's CPU stays out of the scope's cpu.stat) poll `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/<u>.scope/cgroup.procs` every 2 s, counting processes whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains execnet's bootstrap `exec(eval(sys.stdin.readline()))` (grep -zlsF). It read exactly 16 at PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS=16, but it is an upper bound: suites that spawn their own xdist subprocesses (scripts read 2 even when run serially with -p no:xdist). pids.peak counts threads, so it is not a worker count. Scripts: plans/verify-parallelism-trial-e1-report.md §4.

entry_text: Reify gotcha: a named-leaf selector ctor (face/edge/vertex/solid_body(g, "name")) only evaluates to a Value::Selector when its first arg resolves to a named geometry cell (e.g. `let body = box(...)`); with no geometry in scope it stays Undef. So migrating an FEA .ri call site from `target: "root"` to a typed selector usually needs `let body = box(<same dims the solver uses>)` added. The BodySelector ctor is `solid_body`, not `body` (`body` is the RBD mechanism ctor).
target_text: In an FEA design loop where a box dimension is an unresolved `auto` param, the typed selector `face(body, "z_max")` evaluates to Value::Undef instead of Value::Selector, so parse_pressure_spec reads no face name and SILENTLY DROPS the PressureLoad (elastic_static.rs). Measured on examples/fea_bracket_minimize_mass.ri: the pressure cell came out as {"magnitude": Real(1000000.0), "face": Undef} and the unopposed optimiser parked thickness at 2.88e-6 m while still reporting Solved. The control is decisive: the identical spelling in examples/fea_pressure_smoke.ri, whose box dims are all concrete, mints a real Selector(Leaf{query:Named("x_max")}) — and `body` itself resolves fine (a GeometryHandle) in both, so it is the hoisted selector that fails, not the geometry. Workarounds: the legacy `face: "z_max"` String arm works but trips the ctor-field-conformance gate (PressureLoad.face is Option<FaceSelector>); PointLoad(point: "tip", force: ...) avoids both since PointLoad.point is a plain String. Tracked as tkt_0RSVYHGPGEYD2QV9MTGTXPQ86S.

Completed: Merge-gate flake suppression can launder a killed/timed-out sibling module leg: a passing re-run of another module's flake flips the joined red to PASS
Description: Follow-up found by the architect of task 5492 (merge-gate crash-truncation fix). This is OUTSIDE 5492's scope. 5492 makes the discriminator refuse suppression when the failing test_output carries an xdist worker-death marker. This is a SIBLING no-verdict hole of the same INV-1 class that 5492 does not close.

MECHANISM (by code reading at base 4e76fbd912, NOT reproduced):
- verify.py::_aggregate_results '\n'-joins per-module VerifyResults into the merge gate's single scoped result.
- Suppose one module's TEST leg was externally killed (rc<0, FailureCategory.INFRA_KILL, verdict_indeterminate) or timed out (INFRA_TIMEOUT), producing no FAILED short-summary line. Meanwhile another module completed with a genuine load flake.
- orchestrator/src/orchestrator/verify_runner.py::LocalRunner.run_merge_verify calls verify.apply_merge_flake_suppression on the joined red.
- verify.py::confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict extracts only the flake's node-id, re-runs it, sees it pass, and returns passes_in_isolation.
- The hook replace()s the whole result to passed=True / merge_flake_suppressed, so the killed module's suite lands with no verdict.
Host OOM pressure plausibly produces both at once: one pytest killed while siblings run starved.

The structured signal already exists. VerifyResult.failing_leg_categories (task 3173) carries one category per failing leg, and _aggregate_results unions it across failing children. So a discriminator precondition can refuse (unconfirmable, e.g. 'leg_without_verdict:<category>') when any failing TEST leg's category produced no verdict. Decide which categories qualify: INFRA_KILL certainly; INFRA_TIMEOUT likely.

Also decide whether a failing lint/type leg should block suppression at the merge gate. Today it deliberately does not: see confirm_isolated_rerun_verdict's requires_clean_other_legs note.

Since task 5580 landed on 2026-09-21, the merge gate's isolated re-run genuinely executes and can return passes_in_isolation, so this hole is armed, not merely latent.

- verify.py::_summarize_checks records one category per failing leg in test/lint/type order via verify_classify.classify_failure; guard 2 (timed_out -> INFRA_TIMEOUT) and guard 2.5 (is_external_kill_rc -> INFRA_KILL) fire BEFORE any output is read.

Completed: Blast-radius requeue: a failed pending write must reach the run()-exit write-failure ledger (relaxation 2), not read as an SM-2 violation
Description: Found by the independent pre-merge review of task 3542 (θ, PRD plans/task-escalation-state-graph-prd.md). The gap is NEW with 3542's tightening.

THE GAP. 3542 tightened `_OUTCOME_ALLOWED['requeued']` to {PENDING} (shared/src/shared/task_transitions.py::_OUTCOME_ALLOWED). Spec §5's relaxation 2 says a status-write failure at exit is crash-shaped: it emits ONE store-unavailable record, never a contract violation. orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._note_exit_status_write implements that ledger, but only three writers call it: _repend_for_requeue, _persist_blocked_row and the bypass reopen.

orchestrator/src/orchestrator/scheduler.py::Scheduler.handle_blast_radius_expansion swallows a failed `set_task_status(task_id, 'pending')` (the `except RuntimeError` arm after transient retries: "keeping locks held for reconcile to recover"). It returns `False`, the same value as a SUCCESSFUL conflict requeue. workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._reconcile_scope_locks passes that bool through, and TaskWorkflow._requeue_on_lock_conflict stashes a REQUEUED report. Its three callers are _plan, the escalation-resume scope-grant path in _drive, and the replan in _execute_verify_review_loop. The row is still `in-progress`, and the ledger was never set. So orchestrator/src/orchestrator/exit_contract.py::judge_exit returns VIOLATION, not STORE_UNAVAILABLE.

CONSEQUENCE.
- Log mode (shipped default): one would-violate WARNING plus a workflow_exit_contract event per affected exit during a store outage. That pollutes task μ's soak signal (3546 step 1(a), "zero would-violate").
- Enforce mode: one blocking L1 per task, which is exactly the per-task storm spec §5 forbids.
So this must land before μ flips `workflow_exit_contract_enforce`. Until it does, μ's soak criterion should read "zero violations outside store outages".

FIX SHAPE (the implementer decides). Make the scheduler's write failure visible to the workflow: return a typed result, or raise, instead of the ambiguous bool. Then call `self._note_exit_status_write('pending', exc)` on the failure arm. Update the SchedulerProtocol stub (scheduler.py, the `handle_blast_radius_expansion` protocol signature) and every test double. Check whether a failed write must still keep the locks held (it must: see the existing comment).

RED TEST. Drive a REQUEUED exit through _plan's blast-radius conflict with the scheduler's pending write raising RuntimeError. The exit must record STORE_UNAVAILABLE (exactly one record, no violation). Today it records a VIOLATION.

Not in scope: the other known would-violate producers. The sibling task filed alongside this one covers them.
