Three facts about dark_factory's scope-reconciliation machinery, all measured 2026-09-21 and all contradicting what task 4371's record had asserted since 2026-08-24.

(1) `workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._reconcile_scope_locks` is NOT "the choke point every path that re-establishes plan.files runs through". It has FIVE bypasses. `harness.py::Harness._fold_granted_files_on_repend` is a JUSTIFIED bypass (runs at re-pend when the slot has already released every lock, and writes both plan.files and metadata.files itself). `mcp/plan_tools.py::_create_plan` and `_update_plan_metadata` are LAZILY reconciled — the architect mutates plan.files mid-turn and the reconcile happens only when control returns to `_plan()`/`_replan`, so the window is the agent's whole turn. `_repair_plan` is covered only by sitting inside `_plan()`. Two are GENUINELY uncovered: `_try_narrow_plan`, which rewrites plan.json downward with no metadata write and no lock release, and the `_drive` initial_plan branch, which reconciles nothing at all. Defensible restatement: every path that re-establishes plan.files WHILE THE TASK HOLDS LOCKS IN A LIVE SLOT routes through it — and even that has the `_try_narrow_plan` exception.

(2) A REQUEUE FROM MID-EXECUTE REFILLS the iteration budget rather than forfeiting it. `metrics.execute_iterations` lives on the TaskWorkflow instance and `max_execute_iterations` (10) is re-granted in full on every dispatch; there is no durable per-task execute-iteration ledger. The worktree, branch and commits all survive (GitOps.create_worktree's reuse arm commits uncommitted work as "chore: save WIP before requeue rebase" then rebases), and redispatch resumes at STEP granularity via `artifacts.get_pending_steps()` while re-planning at phase granularity. Spend is charged and recorded via `Scheduler.record_requeue` but the agent CONTEXT is lost — agent_session.json is cleared in the invocation's finally, so `--resume` is a restart-recovery mechanism, not a requeue one. The only cross-dispatch limiter is `requeue_cap` (3). Task 4371's open design decision 3 assumed the budget is FORFEITED; the opposite is true, which removes a damper that design implicitly relied on.

(3) The conflict case has a FIFTH silent path that 4371's four-clause summary omits: alongside the acquire-failure branch (which persists widened metadata.files, writes `pending`, releases ALL the task's locks via `ModuleLockTable.release` popping the whole held set, and arms the 30s requeue cooldown), there is an `except RuntimeError` arm that returns False WITHOUT re-pending and WITHOUT releasing, deliberately, so reconcile can recover. Also: on the conflict branch `_write_module_cache` runs, `_get_modules` is cache-first, and `_phase_stale_sweep` evicts only TERMINAL or absent tasks — so a redispatched `pending` task demands the FULL widened set up front and fails at ADMISSION rather than mid-flight. Better (no spend burned) but strictly narrower.

entry_text: In reify, files under crates/*/tests/<harness_name>/ are `mod` submodules of a single harness test binary, so `cargo test --test <file_stem>` fails. Target the binary and filter by module path instead, e.g. `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_compilation_surface examples_smoke` or `cargo test -p reify-eval --test harness_auto_resolution auto_type_param_determinism_tests`. Also, `rustfmt --check` on a crate's lib.rs follows `mod` declarations into every module, so run it on the individual touched files to see only your own hunks.
target_text: In reify's crates/reify-compiler/tests/, several suites are MODULES inside a harness test binary (e.g. examples_smoke.rs and compile_api_tests.rs both live under harness_compilation_surface/), not test targets of their own. `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test examples_smoke` fails with "no test target named"; the working form is `cargo test -p reify-compiler --test harness_compilation_surface -- examples_smoke`. When citing such a file in a doc or ledger, give the full crates/<crate>/tests/<harness>/<module>.rs path plus that invocation — a bare `reify-compiler/tests/<module>.rs` citation does not resolve and sends the reader hunting.

Description: Root-caused from reify escalation esc-5665-2 (reify task 5665, filed 2026-08-03, still pending L1). Recorded plan.json provenance was rewritten so that steps 3, 5 and 7 ALL recorded the same commit 5da1f20c4d — the branch tip titled "chore: save WIP before inter-iteration rebase" — even though the branch carries three distinct commits whose messages match those steps verbatim (d4864b8371, 9b35eb20d8, 49e773e5de). workflow.py:8050-8078, inside _reconcile_done_step_commits. For each done step whose recorded commit is no longer an ancestor of HEAD, line 8054 computes orphaned_files, then line 8055 tests whether orphaned_files is a subset of wip_files (with wip_tip_sha set), and on a match line 8056 stamps the single wip_tip_sha onto the step. Only in the else branch does line 8073 call git_ops.find_equivalent_commit, stamping the precise remapped sha at line 8077.

The coarse filename-subset test at 8055 runs FIRST. It is a subset test over the union of files touched by the WIP run, so it is DEGENERATE whenever several steps touch the same file(s): every such step satisfies the subset condition and every one of them collapses onto the same WIP tip. The precise remapper (patch-id equivalence, with a unique-subject-match fallback) is thus subordinated to the imprecise one, and only ever runs when the imprecise one fails.

The comment at workflow.py:8065-8072 already documents find_equivalent_commit as fully fail-safe (returns None on any git error, an unresolvable or GC'd commit, ambiguity, or no equivalent), so promoting it to first position cannot introduce a new failure path — a miss simply falls through to today's behaviour.

SECOND SITE (same task, lower priority): workflow.py:8375 stamps post-rebase HEAD by design; confirm it is not a second route to the same collapse.

HARDENING (include if cheap): plan_tools.py:256 _mark_step_done writes any string into a step's commit field with no validation. Add a _sha_exists_on_branch check so a step can never record a sha that is not reachable on the task branch.

No merge gate or done_provenance consumes plan-step commit — done_provenance derives from _merge_sha, and .task/ is gitignored so plan.json never lands in a commit. Description: Filed by task 4481's implementer as out-of-scope follow-up work. No escalation record; discovered by inspection while executing task 4481's steps 8-10.

BACKGROUND. Task 4481 swept orchestrator/tests for tests that depend on an UNDECLARED config key's package code default, using two detectors: a committed AST ratchet (static) and a scratch adversarial-config harness (dynamic — a test green with the real yaml and red under a yaml that perturbs every undeclared key is depending on a code default by definition).

THE GAP. Both detectors are blind to a test whose assertion is NEGATIVE — "this env var is absent", "this callback did not fire", "this flag was not injected". When the root key flips, the behaviour under test is disabled, the negative assertion becomes trivially true, and the test PASSES. It passes for the wrong reason: it is no longer exercising anything. The dynamic harness cannot see it (it only reports failures), and the AST ratchet cannot see it (there is no equality-against-a-default to match).

entry_text: DESIGN GOTCHA (task 5232, measured 2026-10-02 at HEAD 13a9caaca2): never write a checked-in-corpus sweep in shared/tests asserting that every kind='path' delivered_check's paths EXIST on main. It contradicts the task-3500 authoring lint. shared/src/shared/delivered_check_polarity.py::_lint_path_check rejects an expect='present' path check as 'vacuous_present' when its paths already exist, so every correctly-authored adopter names a missing path at the moment its sidecar is committed. At HEAD, 6 of the 7 tracked kind='path' checks (owners 4681, 6181, 6184, 6185, 6188, 6190, all pending) named missing paths. The analogy to TestCheckedInScriptCheckTargets fails: a script target is the CHECKER, and a missing one is a silent ERRORED hold, while path entries are the SUBJECT. A missing path is the normal pre-delivery state and evaluates FAIL, which feeds the visible delivered_fail streak. Telling "permanently red" apart from "not yet delivered" needs owning-task status, so it belongs in a tasks.db-aware scripts/ audit, not the shared suite.
target_text: Delivered_check authoring gotcha (found at INV-12 decompose, 2026-09-18): checking a grep pattern ABSENT on main at queue time is necessary but NOT sufficient. Also ask whether a PREREQUISITE task in the same batch will write that pattern into the checked paths before the producer lands. The INV-12 sidecar had ε1/ε2 checks `governed_exceptions\(` over shared/tests/ and scripts/tests/. β's own unit tests (shared/tests) and γ2's register tests (scripts/tests, fixture sources) would contain that pattern, so the producers' checks would pass before any declaration existed. The damage is to the delivered-check consumers: the harness mark-done withhold gate would be vacuous, and landing_evidence's differential (requires FALSE at parent) degrades to no-signal. Fix: pin each check to a directory no upstream task writes (orchestrator/tests, fused-memory/tests, dashboard/tests), and mark the contaminated halves `kind: manual` with a reason.

target_text: reify: `loft(...)` is unreachable from the .ri source language and cannot be made to realize by any spelling — every profile constructor (circle/rectangle/ellipse/polygon/rounded_rect) is fixed-arity with NO plane or offset argument, so all profiles land coplanar at z=0 and bound a degenerate solid ("OCCT make_loft_with_history: TopoDS::Wire"), while wrapping one in `translate()` degrades its inferred traits and is rejected at compile time with "geometry argument 'profile' must be a 2D Surface profile (Closed, Planar)". Owned by live task #6188; the committed evidence fixture is tests/prd-gate/fixtures/pnrg_envelope_loft.ri. Do NOT plan any test that asserts a clean loft from .ri source. `crates/reify-compiler/tests/fixtures/stdlib_geometry_ops_smoke.ri`'s `loft(prof, prof2)` is an arity/registry spelling reference only, never evidence of realizability.

MERGE-LANE RATCHET, THE RAISE DIRECTION (measured on task 5342, 2026-09-14). Two existing entries cover this baseline from the γ test-seam migration angle — LOWERING a measure and splicing single `tests` lines (task 5027's 6d603eb1, task 5033's e2010717). This is the complementary case they do not address: an ordinary BUG FIX that adds production code to a cluster file, which necessarily RAISES measures.

WHAT BITES. Any edit to a `params.cluster_paths` file, and any NEW test file under orchestrator/tests/ that imports a lane module, makes test_merge_lane_ratchet.py::test_baseline_matches_a_fresh_measurement RED — it pins the committed bytes to an exact live measurement, in BOTH directions. The `tests` map has 230 entries and does include dedicated sibling files like test_merge_gates_plan_files_rename.py, so a new test file is a new key. Measured cost of that test alone: 134.85s (live AST sweep), so budget for it in any merge-lane verify.

THE README'S PROHIBITION IS NARROWER THAN IT READS. The baseline's `_README` says never regenerate it "merely to make a test pass", but the exact-match test makes regeneration MANDATORY for any cluster change. Read it as "do not regenerate to paper over an UNREVIEWED rise": regenerate, then INSPECT `git diff` of the baseline against an enumerated list of deltas you expected, and name the rise in the CHANGELOG so review sees it was deliberate.

TWO MEASURES, VERY DIFFERENT STAKES. `files[...].lines` rising is the honest, unavoidable cost of new behaviour plus docstrings. Per-FUNCTION `cognitive` rising is avoidable and is the one that actually tracks quality — and the hot lane functions sit high already (merge_gates.py::_check_post_merge_equivalence at 25, ::_check_plan_targets_in_tree at 16). TECHNIQUE THAT WORKS: put the new branching in an extracted helper and reduce the existing call site to `x = await _helper(...)` plus one `if x is None` guard. That swaps a comprehension-plus-condition for a call-plus-if, holding the host function's cognitive flat or lowering it, while the new complexity lands on a NEW baseline key. Ceilings (1500 lines/file, cognitive 15/function) apply ONLY to keys ABSENT from the baseline — see TestCeilingsApplyOnlyToNewKeys — so a new helper must clear cognitive 15, and a grandfathered file's line count is not ceiling-checked.

DO NOT "FIX" A LINE RISE BY MOVING CODE TO A NEW MODULE. `params.cluster_paths` is a literal list (only `merge_lane/**/*.py` is a glob) pinned by test_cluster_paths_has_exactly_the_appendix_a_entries, so a new orchestrator/src/orchestrator/merge_*.py sibling would escape measurement entirely. That is ratchet evasion, and it is the "splitting one unit across files stitched together with imports" that code-quality heuristic 14 forbids.

NOTHING AUTO-RUNS `--check` against main's copy of the baseline (grep confirms no hook, CI step or test invokes it), so the never-raise direction is enforced only by a human reading the baseline diff. Make that diff legible.

scripts/ IS pyright-gated (since task 3456) even though pre-commit never runs pyright for it — measured 2026-08-21 on task 4511. scripts/orchestrator.yaml declares `type_check_command: "uv run --project shared pyright scripts/"` (uv-resolved since task 4358), the root pyproject.toml [tool.pyright] extraPaths includes "scripts" and "scripts/legibility", and the tree is clean: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 0 informations at HEAD. But hooks/project-checks' PYRIGHT_PACKAGES is only (fused-memory, orchestrator, dashboard), so a scripts/ type error commits with NO output line at all and first surfaces at module verify — I committed one and only caught it by running the gate by hand. PRACTICAL RULE: after any scripts/ edit run `uv run --project shared pyright scripts/` AND `uv run --project shared ruff check scripts/` yourself; the test suite passing means nothing about either. THIS CORRECTS TWO STALE ENTRIES that still assert the opposite and would walk you straight into it: 2f1d01db-a9fc-4bba-82b7-dde37e293145 ("scripts/ ... lint-gated but NOT type-gated", plus 5 long-since-fixed digest.py errors) and 613208c1-e873-4c5b-886f-cd302f40588f ("scripts/ is knowingly not yet pyright-clean, which is why scripts/orchestrator.yaml declines to declare a type_check_command ... do NOT add scripts/ to extraPaths" — both halves now false; the extraPaths entries are load-bearing and pinned by tests/scripts/test_scripts_module_config.py::test_root_pyright_extrapaths_resolves_scripts_imports). In-place correction was refused (update_memory's content_amend arm allows only recon-stage-/curator- agents), hence this separate entry.

THE SPECIFIC TRAP in scripts/tests/: an UNANNOTATED parameter defaulting to None infers as type `None`, so a shared test helper written `def _h(..., monkeypatch=None)` reds the gate with `"setattr" is not a known attribute of "None" (reportOptionalMemberAccess)` at every use. A guard placed up front does not fix it if it narrows a DIFFERENT condition than the one reaching the use (e.g. `if branch in ('a','b') and monkeypatch is None: raise` cannot narrow inside a later `if branch == 'a':` arm). House fix, matching scripts/'s fix-don't-suppress precedent (task 3456 cleared 395 errors with zero `# type: ignore`): annotate `monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch | None = None` and `assert monkeypatch is not None, <msg>` inside each arm that uses it.

entry_text: Fused-memory completion-claim gate (task 3142, fused_memory.services.completion_claim_gate) false positive, seen 2026-10-01. An add_memory whose content said "filed as task 6155 (depends on task 5036)" was tagged unverified_claim with kind=filing_dispatch, verdict=mismatch, observed='pending'. It also opened an INFO escalation on the DARK-FACTORY ORCHESTRATOR queue named esc-unverified-claim-<task>-1 (agent_role fused-memory/completion-claim-gate). The gate apparently reads "filed as task N" as a dispatch claim, even though a freshly filed task correctly reads pending. It also matched the dependency mention (task 5036) as a second claim. Remedy used: verify the claim is true, then resolve_issue(action='close_only') with an explanation; no corpus repair is needed when the claim is true. To avoid it, phrase task filings as "task N exists, status pending, depends on M" rather than "filed as task N". Otherwise every reflection that reports follow-up filings leaves an escalation for the L2 watcher.

entry_text: Reify: to probe engine build diagnostics on real OCCT without compiling a test, run the warm lane's prebuilt `target/release/reify build <file>.ri -o <out>.step` and grep its stdout/stderr. Diagnostics print as `info: ...` / `warning: ...` lines; a file without a top-of-file `module` declaration also emits W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING, which is harmless. Example: the TopologyAttributeLocalIndexReassigned tie diagnostics for `tube(...)` with a `faces(...)` binding reproduced this way in ~seconds (task #7340 planning, 2026-10-05).
target_text: Reify: to cheaply validate a candidate .ri fixture shape during planning (no cargo build), a warm lane's prebuilt `target/debug/reify` can run `reify check <file>.ri` and `reify eval <file>.ri` on a scratch file under /tmp. It prints per-constraint OK lines, warnings and exit status. Caveat: the CLI never renders a DiagnosticCode; a code is visible only when its mnemonic is spelled into the message text (e.g. W_MODULE_DECL_MISSING). So CLI end-to-end tests (crates/reify-cli/tests/harness_cli/cli_check_*.rs) must assert stderr text, while compiler-level tests assert `d.code == Some(DiagnosticCode::…)`.

entry_text: Dashboard Tasks tab render cadence and layout cost (measured 2026-10-04, task 5116 architect). Since commit 6d5f7eedd8 the 1s wall clock lives in the app.jsx::LiveClock leaf, so TasksTab does NOT re-render every second. It re-renders on each data arrival (~20/min) and each interaction (node click, focus, filter). Any memo keyed on a per-render array (e.g. `[tasks]` from viewRows/filter/focusGroupView) still misses on all of those, and each poll replaces every row object, so only a content key hits. Measured with graph_layout.js under node on the live snapshot: one TaskGraph layout (computeTiers + partitionComponents + orderRows) costs 43.6ms for dark-factory (1,620 tasks) and 72.7ms avg / 161ms max for reify (1,657 tasks). A JSON structural signature costs ~0.45ms.

Completed: tab_tasks.jsx: TaskGraph's Sugiyama layout memos are reference-keyed on a per-render array, so computeTiers/partitionComponents/orderRows re-run for every project on every 1s clock tick
Description: Out-of-scope follow-up discovered while planning task 4137 (header count vs. focus-narrowed render array). Not filed as an escalation — it is a self-contained perf item with no blocker.

OBSERVED at base bd93e98921 by reading the source (no profiling run):

`TaskGraph` in dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx memoizes its expensive layout work with `uM_T(() => { computeTiers(tasks); partitionComponents(tasks); components.map(c => orderRows(c, tiers)) }, [tasks])`, and its highlight neighborhood with `uM_T(..., [selectedId, tasks])`.

Both dep arrays are keyed on the `tasks` REFERENCE. `tasks` originates in `TasksTab`'s `projects.map(p => ...)` callback, which computes `const projTasks = allTasks.filter(t => t.project === p.id)` and `const filtered = projTasks.filter(...)` fresh on every render — a new array instance every time. TasksTab re-renders once per second from the app-wide clock tick in app.jsx (`setInterval(() => setNow(...), 1000)`, unrelated to data polling). So these memos miss 100% of the time and the full ordering-phase layout (barycenter/transpose passes plus countCrossings inside `orderRows`, graph_layout.js) re-runs for every mounted project group every second. `PrdBox` mounts one `TaskGraph` per PRD box, multiplying this in the grouped view.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY TASK 4137: 4137 deletes two OTHER memos with the same defect (`ProjectTaskGraph`/`ProjectPrdGroups`'s `graphTasks`), but only because they were in the way of the header-count fix. It does not touch `TaskGraph`, whose memos are the expensive ones. The behaviour is identical before and after 4137.

THE FIX IDIOM ALREADY EXISTS IN THE SAME FILE: `ProjectPrdGroups` documents this exact hazard and works around it by keying its `groups`/`neighborhood`/`fullMembersByPrd` memos on the content-signature strings `filteredSig`/`allSig` rather than on the arrays. Apply the same treatment to `TaskGraph`'s two memos (a signature covering id/status/deps is sufficient for `computeTiers`/`partitionComponents`/`orderRows`/`computeNeighborhood`, which read nothing else) — or, more cheaply, memoize `projTasks`/`filtered` themselves further up so a stable reference reaches every consumer.

SUGGESTED SCOPE: dashboard/src/dashboard/static/redux/tab_tasks.jsx (+ dashboard/tests/test_tab_tasks_*.py for a structural assertion that the layout memo is signature-keyed). Note that any edit to a /static/redux asset requires bumping the shared `?v=NN` cache-buster in index.html — see dashboard/tests/_cache_buster_helpers.py::cache_buster_violation.

CAVEAT: the cost is asserted from reading the code, not measured. Confirm with a profile before investing in a large refactor; if the measured cost is negligible, closing this as won't-fix (and deleting the misleading memo comments, which claim a benefit they do not deliver) is a legitimate outcome.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, main 15634a417f): inside a trait INSTANCE assoc-fn body, every `self.member` / bare member read types as dimensionless Real, regardless of the member's declared type. Cause: crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs compile_assoc_function builds its body scope without set_template_registry, so expr.rs member_access_on_structure_like hits its registry-miss permissive fallback for the StructureRef(conformer) receiver. E.g. `fn lateral_area(self) -> Scalar<Area> { pi * diameter * length }` compiles its body to Real. Any static check on assoc-fn body types (comparison guards, body-vs-return reconciliation) will false-positive or false-negative there. Tracked as #8118; sibling #7855 is the same erase-to-Real class for trait-typed fn params.
target_text: In reify, an UNTYPED lambda param defaults to `Type::Real` (crates/reify-compiler/src/expr.rs, ExprKind::Lambda arm), so the body of the canonical `field def f : Point3 -> Scalar { source = analytical { |p| p } }` compiles to `Real` — NOT to the field's declared domain type. Any new field-body-vs-codomain type check must carve out dimensionless `Real`/`Int` bodies or it reddens ~14 existing fixtures across field_compile_tests.rs, compile_builder_smoke_tests.rs, prepass_consolidation_tests.rs, silent_defaults_tests.rs, type_alias_compile_tests.rs and reify-eval/src/test_runner.rs. Related gotcha measured at the same time: a whole-valued float literal such as `0.0` or `300.0` compiles to `Type::Int`, not `Type::Real`.

DIAGNOSING A FLAKE-DEBT TASK, host-pressure half: data/load-samples.db in the MAIN checkout keeps a time series of host pressure (table `samples(ts INTEGER unix-epoch, metric, value, window_mean, window_max)`). Its metrics include runqueue_ratio (runnable threads per CPU), psi_cpu_some_avg10, psi_cpu_full_avg10, psi_mem_some_avg10, psi_io_some_avg10, verify_concurrency, and own_cpu_some10:<orchestrator unit>.

To reconstruct the pressure a failing test actually saw, take the verify-leg window from the log filename's UTC timestamp plus the pytest duration line. Then aggregate avg/max per metric over `ts BETWEEN strftime('%s','<start>') AND strftime('%s','<end>')`.

Measured for task 6026 (merge c0d85b7082, fused-memory leg 2026-09-28 19:35–19:44): runqueue_ratio mean 6.78 / max 29.28, psi_cpu_some mean 61%, mem and io pressure below 3%. That split distinguishes a CPU-oversubscription flake, where the remedy is a CPU-time instrument such as time.thread_time, from an IO/memory one, which that remedy would not fix. flake_occurrence.psi_cpu_some10 is only a single point taken at suppression time, AFTER the leg finished.

/team routing lesson from the 2026-09-16 remediation-run investigation (fable lead; sonnet census + syslog seats; opus code-trace + skeptic): the opus/high skeptic seat run over the DRAFT report changed the decision set — it found a second orphan-recovery arm (7 remediation children cleaned by _recover_predecessor_runs, invisible to a query keyed on StaleRunRecovery), refuted a universal ("startup passes unreachable after a clean stop") with a 33-row counter-census, caught a census table that mixed failed rows into a duration distribution, and located the remediation-specific ~80 s gaps the lead had misattributed to generic context assembly. Each sonnet/medium seat produced correct numbers but one confidently mislabelled sentence, caught only by the lead re-running the query. Pattern to keep: brief the skeptic by numbered claim with the exact code path/query to attack; never let a seat's prose summary stand in for its table.

entry_text: Gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, GNU bash 5.2.21 on the dark-factory host): `bash -c 'a && b && sleep N'` execs the FINAL command of an && list in place, so `sleep N` runs as the bash pid itself, not as a child. A sleeper_spec-style test build therefore ends up as ONE process (a direct child of the verify-merge leader, leading its own session under start_new_session), not bash->sleep. Account for this when reasoning about which pid a /proc descendant walk or a pid file names.
target_text: GOTCHA (verified by direct reproduction, 2026-08-06): Python's subprocess.run(..., timeout=N) calls process.kill() on the DIRECT CHILD ONLY. If that child is a bash script currently executing a COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — `verdict="$(some_function)"` — the forked subshell SURVIVES the kill and is reparented to `systemd --user` (PPID 2036 on this host). It then runs to completion on its own, however long that takes. Reproduced twice: SIGKILLing the main shell of scripts/restart-all-orchestrators.sh left the `$(drain_await_fresh ...)` subshell alive under PPID 2036, still polling. CONSEQUENCE FOR TEST DESIGN: "the test kills the child on timeout" is NOT containment for a bash script. Spawn with start_new_session=True and os.killpg(os.getpgid(p.pid), SIGKILL) on timeout, AND structure the script so no long wait lives inside a command substitution. See [[a-wait-a-test-interrupts-must-not-live-in-a-command-substitution]].

entry_text: Counting pytest-xdist workers of a scoped run (measured 2026-10-05, task 5469; peer of 64c791bb under topic verify-resource-measurement). Under `-q` with non-tty output xdist never prints `created: N/M workers` — TerminalDistReporter.getstatus returns only "bringing up nodes..." at verbose < 0 — so a verify-shaped `-q` log cannot prove the worker count. Reading PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER from /proc/<pid>/environ UNDER-counts (read 5 of 16): that file is the process's initial environment and xdist sets the variable after the worker starts. What worked: run the command in a named scope (`systemd-run --user --scope --unit=<u>`), and from OUTSIDE the scope (so the sampler's CPU stays out of the scope's cpu.stat) poll `/sys/fs/cgroup/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/<u>.scope/cgroup.procs` every 2 s, counting processes whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains execnet's bootstrap `exec(eval(sys.stdin.readline()))` (grep -zlsF). It read exactly 16 at PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS=16, but it is an upper bound: suites that spawn their own xdist subprocesses (scripts read 2 even when run serially with -p no:xdist). pids.peak counts threads, so it is not a worker count. Scripts: plans/verify-parallelism-trial-e1-report.md §4.
target_text: pytest-xdist 3.8 spawns NO workers and prints no `created: N/M workers` header when run with `--collect-only` — measured 2026-08-03 against fused-memory/pyproject.toml via `-c`. So the cheap `--collect-only` config-probe idiom (fused-memory/tests/test_integration_marker_config.py) can prove marker deselection but CANNOT prove a worker count; a real run is required to observe the `created: N/M workers` / `N workers [K items]` header.

target_text: Root cause (jun18 /deb of reify task 4641 "orchestrator auto-deferred it"): the per-task steward (`claude-task-4641-steward`) resolved the L0 zero-output escalation (esc-4641-62) with `resolve_issue(action='park')` to stop the re-dispatch loop. The harness maps `_ACTION_TARGETS={'restart':'pending','park':'deferred','abandon':'cancelled'}` (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/harness.py:~4783), so `_action_teardown_and_set_status` force-wrote status `deferred`. The workflow had itself exited BLOCKED (correct: zero-output circuit breaker at the 10-iteration cap → `_mark_blocked(category='infra_issue')`, filing esc-4641-64), but that correct `blocked` write was suppressed by the action-teardown's `_action_teardown_tasks`/`_suppress_blocked_write` stamp (scheduler.py:~1268-1276, which absorbs racing 'blocked' writes). Hence the scheduler event `task_completed{outcome:blocked}` diverged from the final DB status `deferred`. The escalation server's `resolve_issue` docstring even documents park as passive ("stays blocked/deferred / no immediate workflow action"), but the implementation actively writes deferred AND kills the workflow — a doc/impl drift.

Lessons from authoring the INV-12 PRD under /team on 2026-09-18 (4 sonnet scout seats, an opus premise critic, a fable design critic, an opus closure check; ~1.25M subagent tokens). (1) The author's first-draft central premise — "no debt-shaped allow-list has a live owner" — was FALSE and was caught only by the adversarial premise seat. The author had checked the status of the task ids the lists CITE (all done) and concluded nothing was owned; the correct check is a read-only store query for NON-TERMINAL tasks whose title/description/details mention each list's symbol, which found live owners for five lists. A comment's cited task being done says nothing about whether a later task owns the same debt. (2) The design critic's most valuable move was measuring INFLOW (git log over 30 days) where the author had sized a mechanism from STOCK: the pressure valve looked adequate against 954 existing sites and absorbed only ~9% of the ~29/day arriving. Any gate that agents will hit daily should be sized from the rate, not the census. (3) A closure-check seat after the rewrite was worth its ~166k tokens: it confirmed the fixes and found a new filing-time blocker the rewrite introduced. (4) Seat routing: sonnet/medium was right for token-accurate measurement and substrate lookups, too light for classification judgment (its "exception list" labels were loose and had to be re-decided) and wrong on one behavioural claim ("the curator dedups by title") that an opus seat refuted from code. (5) When writing `delivered_check` grep patterns in a capability-manifest sidecar: validate the YAML with `shared.capability_manifest.CapabilityManifestDoc`, run every pattern with `git grep -E` against main to confirm it is ABSENT today (a pattern already present makes its producer read as delivered before it lands), make sure a later producer's pattern cannot be satisfied by an earlier leaf's tests in the same directory, and never start a pattern with `--` (git grep parses it as an option, rc=129). (6) `commit_planning` stamping erased the sidecar's header comment (known defect, task 5276); the decompose session restored the original text plus task_id lines.

entry_text: GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured 2026-10-03 for task 4155): to test that a spawn uses start_new_session=True, run a real child and check pid == os.getpgid(0) == os.getsid(0); see shared/tests/test_git_async.py::test_child_leads_its_own_session_with_no_controlling_terminal. An open('/dev/tty') -> ENXIO check alone cannot catch the bug in agent and verify shells. They have no controlling terminal, so the child gets ENXIO with or without the new session. target_text: GOTCHA (measured 2026-10-05, task 6346, CPython 3.13.9): asyncio.create_subprocess_exec forks and execs inline, then SUSPENDS for several loop iterations at `await waiter` in unix_events._make_subprocess_transport while it connects the child's pipes. A cancellation landing in that post-fork window is cleaned up by asyncio itself: transp.close() calls proc.kill() on the DIRECT child only, then awaits transp._wait(). So a start_new_session=True child's grandchildren survive, and the cancelled call can hang while a survivor holds the pipes. A try/except around communicate() that group-kills on cancel does NOT cover this window, because the caller never got a Process. Fix pattern: run the spawn as its own task, `await asyncio.shield(spawn)`, and on BaseException wait the spawn out (asyncio.wait, absorbing further cancels), group-kill whatever it produced, then re-raise the original exception. To reproduce deterministically in a test: yield with sleep(0) until the child appears in /proc (ppid == os.getpid()), then block the loop thread synchronously before cancel(). Do not count yields: the count changes once the spawn becomes a task.

RECIPE (task 5030, PRD merge-lane-quality γ7): how to drive the merge lane from a test through PUBLIC surfaces only — the technique every γ file migration needs, validated on four files.

SETUP. `MergeLane(git_ops, queue, verifier=FakeVerifier(...), clock=FakeClock(), escalation_queue=...)` + `asyncio.ensure_future(lane.run())`, torn down with `await asyncio.wait_for(lane.stop(), timeout=30)`. Submit with `await queue.put(request)`; observe the `MergeOutcome` future, `lane.snapshot()`, `verifier.verified`, and the escalation queue.

GOTCHA THAT SILENTLY BREAKS THE CONFLICT GRAPH: `git_ops.create_worktree(x)` PREFIXES x with `git.branch_prefix` itself. Pass the BARE task id (`create_worktree('t1')` → branch `task/t1`). Passing `'task/t1'` creates `task/task/t1`, the merge still works (it uses the worktree), but `SuffixConflictTracker.recompute()` resolves `req.branch.full_name` via `resolve_branch_sha` → None → the item is silently SKIPPED from `conflicts_with_main`, so any bounce/conflict-graph test quietly tests nothing. Measured: a bounce e2e that looked correct never bounced until the branch name was fixed.

FAULT INJECTION, all public: verify FAIL/RAISE/PARK via `FakeVerifier(scripts={task_id: VerifyScript(result=..., release=asyncio.Event())})` (`_merge_lane_fakes`; `hangs_until` parks, and a subclass overriding `run_scoped` can raise `RunnerUnavailable` once); a FROZEN PREFIX by parking the head's verify (its merge commit becomes `snapshot()['frozen_prefix']['tip_merge_commit']` while main stays behind); a second host via `_inject_two_host_allocator(lane, _gated_runner(...))` from test_merge_queue_concurrent_verify.py; operator faults via the public `operator_halt`/`unhalt_all_lanes`; abandonment via `req.result.cancel()`; a STALE VERIFY BASE by committing on main out of band while a verify is parked (yields real `two_layer_invariants()` violations); CAS-retry paths via `patch.object(git_ops, 'advance_main', ...)` (a git_ops method, not a lane internal, so the ratchet does not count it); heartbeat-timed behaviour (request-liveness escalation) by injecting `FakeClock` — its `sleep` advances time, so `_HEARTBEAT_POLL_S` carries wall-clock past the stuck threshold in a few event-loop turns.

Merge-queue observation 2026-10-02: get_merge_queue and merge_status kept showing rows as 'queued' that were not live.
- 3995 and 4237 were status done; 5671, 4920 and 5134 already had 'Merge task/<id> into main' markers.
- 5618's mr-a591011c had been finalized blocked at 09:40:22 ('real rebase conflict onto frozen tip') but still read queued at position 5–7 for hours.
- Its steward then resolved esc-5618-2 with outcome 'requeued' at 09:51:03, yet no new merge_queued event appeared for over 2 h. So 'requeued' did not by itself produce a resubmission.
- Rule: before treating a queue row as ahead of you, run a per-id marker search and check runs.db merge_queued / merge_finalized events. A solo carrier submitted behind those phantoms (mr-2d6e644a) dequeued and landed about 1h50m later.
target_text: Merge-queue ghost sighting 2026-09-16 (task 3860 class, via the _bounce_conflicting_suffix_items path in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/suffix_graph.py). mr-6e212286 and mr-0ebe3a4b (task 5185) were still listed as state=queued / waiter_alive=true in get_merge_queue, and merge_status(request_id=...) returned 'queued', for 3+ hours. Yet both had merge_finalized state=blocked rows in data/orchestrator/runs.db (08:26:44Z, 08:29:26Z). The snapshot lists queued items from _lane_buffers and _queue, and waiter_alive only checks `not req.result.cancelled()`, so a RESOLVED (not cancelled) future still reads alive. MergeWorker._request_abandoned also only drops cancelled futures. merge_cancel on such a ghost is a no-op, because it only retires PENDING futures. A fresh merge_request for the same branch (mr-2b1f4c99) was NOT coalesced onto the ghosts: it queued normally, verified and landed. So ghosts inflate queue depth but did not block a resubmit here. Discriminate ghosts by a merge_finalized row for the request_id in runs.db, never by the snapshot.

Task 'Archive remote-verify stderr on failure to data/verify-logs/<task_id>/attempt-{N}.remote-{host}-{utc_ts}.stderr.log' completed. On the REMOTE merge-verify path, a FAILED verify leaves no durable log file, so a remote-host (leo-laptop) verify failure is undiagnosable without re-running. The remote VerifyRunnerPool is built WITHOUT archive_root (merge_queue.py:894-901), unlike the local path which passes archive_root=project_root/'data'/'verify-logs' (merge_queue.py:910-920). And on a successful SSH transport (ssh_rc==0) RemoteRunner.run_merge_verify returns result_from_json(ssh_stdout) and DISCARDS ssh_stderr (verify_runner.py:781-797). Net effect: when a remote verify FAILS (passed=False, transport OK), the orchestrator-side stderr of the ssh call is lost and only the lossy block reason (VerifyResult.failure_report()) survives.

FIX: when RemoteRunner.run_merge_verify gets a VerifyResult with passed=False and non-empty ssh_stderr, persist that stderr to <project_root>/data/verify-logs/<task_id>/attempt-{N}.remote-{remote_host_name}-{utc_ts}.stderr.log — co-located with local archives for side-by-side triage, reusing the existing timestamp (%Y%m%dT%H%M%S_%fZ) + attempt-counter conventions from verify.py:_archive_merge_verify_logs (verify.py:779-856).

USER-OBSERVABLE SIGNAL: with a remote runner (leo-laptop) configured and a merge-verify that FAILS on the remote host (passed=False, transport OK), exactly one file appears at data/verify-logs/<task_id>/attempt-{N}.remote-leo-laptop-<utc_ts>.stderr.log containing the remote ssh_stderr. A PASSING remote verify writes no such file. The local-only path (no remote runner configured) is byte-identical to today.

CONSUMER: operator triaging a task that went blocked because its post-merge verify failed on the remote verify host.
Details: SCOPE / wiring (all within orchestrator/, one package):
1. verify_runner.py — RemoteRunner: thread task_id + archive_root (Path | None) into the constructor and/or run_merge_verify. After the result is parsed (verify_runner.py:797), if `not result.passed and ssh_stderr.strip() and archive_root is not None`, write the stderr file at the path above. Description: Filed by the architect of task #6875 (agent-followup) as OUT-OF-SCOPE work discovered while fixing that task's damping defect; EXTENT EXPANDED 2026-08-31 by the result-field-vacuity-closure decompose (adversary findings ADV-β-1/ADV-β-4, fixture tests/prd-gate/fixtures/adv_beta_v7_degraded_arith.ri) to cover the WHOLE fake-valued degraded construction, and designated the PVAC allowlist owner for it.

LOCUS: crates/reify-eval/src/modal_ops.rs, fn run_mechanism_modal, step (5) Mode-record construction and the surrounding ModalResult assembly. Measured 2026-08-31 on main:
- every Mode is emitted with shape = Value::List(vec![]) and participation_mass = Value::Real(0.0), unconditionally;
- the ModalResult carries a HARD-CODED boundary_conditions = Value::List(Vec::new()) — not even an echo of the caller's list;
- mass_matrix_norm / stiffness_matrix_norm = Value::Real(0.0), with the source comment naming them known-unpopulated ("the lumped generalized-coordinate model never forms the norms the FEA path reports").

Under INV-PD-2 (docs/legibility/design-invariants.md; PRD docs/prds/v0_6/result-field-vacuity-closure.md §2.3/§7) these are C2′ FAKES — empty-list-masquerading-as-computed, zero-masquerading-as-measured — not the honest Undef form, so they sit on the PVAC allowlist naming THIS task as owner until it rules and flips the form.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A BUG (and so was not folded into #6875): unlike damping, shape/participation are DECLARED as the contract in two places — the run_mechanism_modal rustdoc ("frequency-only; lumped model has no 3D shape"; boundary_conditions and reference_direction documented unused) and the stdlib signature doc in crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/modal_mechanism_fns.ri ("each Mode carries only `.frequency` (empty `.shape`, zero `participation_mass`, ...)"). The lumped generalized-coordinate model genuinely has no 3D mode shape to put in Mode.shape : List<Vector3<Dimensionless>>, and participation mass is defined as a projection onto ModalOptions.reference_direction, which the lumped model has no mesh to project against.

BUT the INV-SF-3 shape is still present: ModalOptions.reference_direction is ACCEPTED as an input on this path and silently ignored — the same "declared intent silently dropped by one producer while eval exits 0" pattern #6875 was filed for, one field over. A caller who sets reference_direction: vec3(1,0,0) gets no signal that it did nothing. (The input-side half of that is INV-PD-1/PDROP territory — trampoline-param-drop-closure.md; coordinate, don't double-land.)

entry_text: Three reify tasks carry mis-authored delivered_checks of the MODE-3 shape: a file-existence capability written as kind=grep over file contents, where the pattern is the declared file's own name. They were found by replaying dark-factory task 3500's new authoring lint on 2026-09-28. Task 5511 has pattern 'extrusion_2020' for examples/best_practices/extrusion_2020.ri. Task 6763 and task 6907 have pattern 'divergence-baseline' for a .txt baseline file, whose content will not contain its own name. Such a check goes green only if some other file happens to mention the name, so it can wedge dependents with a DEP_CAPABILITY_NOT_DELIVERED block after the producer lands. Rewrite each as kind='path' (supported since dark-factory task 4743) with the file path and expect=present. The dark-factory lint does not re-check tasks that are already filed.
target_text: Gotcha in reify capability-manifest delivered_checks: kind 'grep' runs `git grep` over file CONTENT, so a pattern that is a fixture's basename (e.g. pattern 'member_geom_let_instance' with paths [fixtures dir]) never matches unless the file body contains that string, and many .ri fixtures have no `module <basename>` line. Task 5432's 'fixtures-committed-and-probed' check is unsatisfiable for exactly this reason (measured 2026-10-01). Anchor such checks on a string that really occurs in the fixture body, or use kind: manual.

entry_text: Reify gotcha: TopologyTemplate.guarded_groups is stored child-before-parent — guards::compile_block_guard allocates the outer __guard_N first but pushes nested groups (via compile_guarded_members) BEFORE pushing the outer group, and a nested group's guard_expr is AND(ValueRef(<entity>.__guard_<parent>), inner). Any single-pass evaluator of guarded groups outside the engine must reorder parent-first (walk parent_guard). Also: when the outer guard is false, a nested group's guard is false, so the nested ELSE branch is active (engine behaviour, measured 2026-09-29).

Completed: Unblock whole-blob metadata repair on done tasks: update_task's done_provenance floor makes metadata_mode='replace' structurally unusable
Description: Split out of task 3697 (esc-3697-4) by the steward on 2026-08-06. 3697 is rescoped to ship its documentation + tested migration script; THIS task provides the write path 3697 needs, then executes the live migration 3697 could not.

OBSERVED, first-hand code reads (not inferred):

1. sqlite_task_backend.py:2575-2591 — update_task raises DoneProvenanceWriteAuthorityError
   for ANY metadata payload that parses to a dict containing 'done_provenance'. The check
   is PRESENCE-ONLY: no value-unchanged carve-out, no metadata_mode carve-out. It fires
   before _resolve_metadata_mode, before ensure_connected(), before the row SELECT.

2. _merge_metadata has no deletion sentinel (merge is shallow {**old, **new}), and there is
   no task-level metadata_delete_keys — that API exists only for MEMORIES
   (memory_service.py / update_memory). backend.set_task_status
   (sqlite_task_backend.py:1938-1947) accepts no metadata argument.

3. The privileged non-protocol seam stamp_audit_metadata (sqlite_task_backend.py:2835,
   added by task 2201) also hardcodes _merge_metadata(mode='merge'), so it cannot retire a
   key either, and it is not reachable over MCP.

4. Single enforcement point: the interceptor does NOT pre-check independently — it catches
   the backend exception at task_interceptor.py:4366 and converts via .to_error_dict().
   Task 2203 deliberately deleted the duplicate guard copies. So a fix has ONE code site,
   not several.

CONSEQUENCE (the generalization worth fixing): every done/merged task carries
done_provenance, so metadata_mode='replace' is structurally unusable on ALL of them — while
task_backend_protocol.py:209 and server/tools.py:5956 both document replace mode as
"the sanctioned repair path". That doc claim and this floor are in direct tension. Any
task needing a key RETIRED (not just added) from a done task's metadata is currently
unfixable through public API.

CANDIDATE DESIGNS (architect decides; do not assume):
  (A) Identical-passthrough carve-out — permit a payload whose done_provenance is
      byte-identical to the stored value, on the reasoning that an unchanged passthrough is
      not a write of that key. Smallest change, preserves the floor's actual intent
      (set_task_status remains the only thing that can CHANGE done_provenance), and unblocks
      whole-blob repair on every done task. Must compare against the STORED value read under
      the same txn, not trust the caller.
  (B) Task-level metadata_delete_keys on update_task, mirroring the memories API. Most
      general, largest blast radius, and needs its own write-authority thinking (deleting
      done_provenance must stay forbidden).
  (C) Widen the privileged stamp_audit_metadata seam to accept a mode/deletion argument and
      expose a narrow operator-only path. Follows the existing 2201 precedent.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, also reconcile the docstrings at task_backend_protocol.py:209 and
server/tools.py:5956 so "the sanctioned repair path" is either true or qualified.

THEN: execute the live migration 3697 was blocked on. fused-memory/scripts/
migrate_task_metadata_to_x_namespace.py lands with 3697 — it is dry-run-by-default,
requires an explicit --task-id, has a collision guard, and does a mandatory post-write
read-back (x_ keys present, old spellings gone, siblings identical, description/details
sha256 unchanged, status unchanged). Its transform is already verified in-memory against
task 3083's real blob: 6 renames, 12 keys untouched. Combined with the last_blocked_at
blessing that ships in 3697, an end-state simulation against the real blob yields
total_warnings=0. Re-running the script is cheap and safe.

TASK 3083 IS A ONE-OF-A-KIND RECORD. Its metadata is 20124 bytes / 18 keys and its
description (6269 B, sha256 0eabfa9e2a0cee74...) and details (13965 B, sha256
22590f60ff52ab4f.…[truncated, 13221 chars total]

[CONTRADICTED 2026-08-23 — READ THIS FIRST. The central claim below ("replace is structurally UNUSABLE on any done/merged task", because the write-authority floor rejects any payload containing done_provenance) DOES NOT HOLD UNIVERSALLY, and relying on it can destroy data. Mem0 6668c214-992f-4008-bede-5ffb24584502 records a first-hand probe on 2026-08-20 against task 3784 (status=done): update_task(metadata_mode='replace') was NOT refused — it returned updated=True and left metadata == {'a': 1}, destroying every other key, unrecoverably (journal.db empty; the sqlite WAL retained text columns but not the metadata BLOB). So the floor is NOT a reliable backstop on the replace path. TREAT metadata_mode='replace' AS AN UNGUARDED WHOLE-BLOB OVERWRITE: never probe it against a real task, and back the blob up before any key-retirement attempt. See also mem0 e1423e03 (2026-08-12), which frames the accurate rule as presence-keyed on done_provenance appearing in the INCOMING payload — additive writes pass, subtractive ones do not. The historical analysis below is retained as the record of what was believed on 2026-08-06.]

Gotcha (task 3697, 2026-08-06): metadata_mode='replace' is structurally UNUSABLE on any done/merged task, despite update_task's docstring calling it "the sanctioned repair path". The backend write-authority floor (sqlite_task_backend.py, ~line 2574-2591) rejects any metadata payload containing done_provenance — presence-only, no value-unchanged carve-out, evaluated BEFORE metadata_mode is resolved — and every done/merged task carries that key. This refines the older 2026-05-06 note advising migration scripts to "defensively strip done_provenance": that advice predates the three metadata modes (added 2026-06-18) and is UNSAFE under replace, where stripping the key DELETES it and only set_task_status can ever re-add it. Net effect: a whole-blob repair of a done task's metadata has no sanctioned path — merge/additive cannot delete a key (shallow {**old, **new}, no deletion sentinel) and there is no task-level metadata_delete_keys (that exists only for memories). Compounding trap: this rejection is returned as an ordinary result dict {'success': False, 'error': 'done_provenance_via_update_task'} inside a JSON-RPC SUCCESS envelope, so a client that only checks the envelope reads a refused write as an accepted one.

entry_text: ASYNCIO TEST GOTCHA (task 6079, measured on CPython 3.13.9, 20 runs per cell). To show a host stall expiring a deadline on a REAL loop, run `async with asyncio.timeout(0.05): time.sleep(0.1); await asyncio.sleep(0)`. Do not expect a TimeoutError from it: the body returns normally 20/20. The resumed task step is queued ahead of the newly-due timeout callback, so the task leaves the timeout context before the callback runs. A timed post-stall wait such as `await asyncio.sleep(0.001)` makes the loop process the overdue timer first and raises TimeoutError 20/20. Use that form whenever a test needs to discriminate real-clock from virtual-clock behaviour (see dashboard/tests/test_virtual_clock_helpers.py).
target_text: GOTCHA — `asyncio.timeout()` cannot bound a stall caused by blocking the event-loop thread, and this misleads triage. fused-memory's /health handler (server/tools.py:1234) wraps each of its two backing-store probes in `asyncio.timeout(5)`, which made ">15s /health is structurally impossible, so the loop must not be scheduling" look like a sound inference. It is sound, but the corollary people reach for next — "so a timeout will cap it" — is false: asyncio timeouts are enforced BY THE EVENT LOOP, so when the loop thread itself is blocked no timer fires and the handler is never even scheduled. Handler-level timeouts bound slow DEPENDENCIES, never a blocked loop. Corollary for reviewers: a /health (or any liveness) latency budget expressed as an in-handler `asyncio.timeout` provides no guarantee whatsoever against loop-blocking bugs; only bounded loop-thread occupancy does. Confirmed 2026-08-06 (session deb-df-4070020, task 3778).

target_text: REIFY DETERMINISM, measured manifestation (2026-09-01, task #5469 PRD2 γ): the SubProblem.auto_params HashSet axis-order leak documented on 2026-08-26 is NOT merely a latent BT5/D4 claim — it changes user-visible `reify eval` output the moment CpSatSolver occupies a registry slot. With CpSat wired into `logical` + a DiscreteFirstFallback in `fallback`, two consecutive runs of docs/prds/v0_6/fixtures/discrete_balance_lets.ri returned the two DIFFERENT balanced Bool configs, because CP-SAT's variable order IS ResolutionProblem.auto_params order and its search is fixed depth-first. DimensionalSolver was order-tolerant enough to hide it. FIX ADOPTED (5/5 runs bit-identical after): in SolverRegistry::solve_inner build sub_auto_params as `problem.auto_params.iter().filter(|ap| component.auto_params.contains(&ap.id)).cloned().collect()` — filter the caller's Vec rather than sort, because PRD2 §3 decision 10 specifies *declaration* order, and this mirrors the adjacent sub_dependent_cells discipline ("filter over the original slice, never a rebuild from a set"). It also makes the pre-existing `param_lookup` binding dead, which fails the workspace's -D warnings gate if left. A registry-level regression test CAN catch this in-process: each solve rebuilds the component HashSet with a fresh RandomState, so ~20 fresh ResolutionProblems suffice.

entry_text: In orchestrator/, a TDD RED test that imports a first-party module which does not exist yet (e.g. `from orchestrator.agents.new_leaf import X`) trips ruff I001: ruff's isort cannot find the module under src/, so it ranks it third-party, puts it in the same section as the bare-name test helper import (`from _role_splice_contract import ...`), and asks you to delete the blank line between them. Don't apply that fix. Keep the normal first-party layout; I001 clears once the GREEN step creates the module (measured, task 5970). Pre-commit passed on the RED commit regardless.
target_text: TDD gotcha in this repo: during a RED step, `ruff check` reports a SPURIOUS I001 "import block is un-sorted" on a test file importing the not-yet-created module. Ruff cannot resolve the missing module, buckets it as third-party, and `--fix` then hoists it into a separate block above the first-party fused_memory imports — producing an import order that becomes wrong the moment the module exists (GREEN). Do NOT accept that --fix during RED. Keep the natural single sorted block and re-run ruff after the implementation step, where it passes clean. Seen on task 3111 with tests/test_topic_anchor.py importing fused_memory.services.topic_anchor.

Hand-carry mechanics that worked 2026-10-04 for a BLOCKED task under an open L2 (task 5035, esc-5035-3), where Leo's ruling re-scoped the task and assigned it to the interactive session:
1. set_task_status deferred FIRST (blocked → deferred was accepted).
2. update_task the description to the ruled scope.
3. resolve_issue with action='close_only', not 'resume' ('resume' would re-dispatch the task under the carry). The L1 member esc-5035-2 was cascade-dismissed ("l2-cascade").
4. Close the cockpit DecisionRecord.
No stranded-blocked refile loop followed. After the carry, deferred → done with found_on_main was accepted directly.
Carrier walk: submit_task(planning_mode) → add_dependency on the deferred real task → commit_planning → in-progress (claimant_run_id) → merge-deferred → remove_dependency. Then `git branch task/<carrier>` plus `git worktree add .worktrees/<carrier>`; this avoids `git worktree move` and its broken venv shebangs.
A queue row whose task already had a "Merge task/<id> into main" marker was a phantom. The solo carrier went straight to verifying on the laptop and landed in about 20 min. It was NOT flipped by the lane and had to be stamped merged by hand. The orchestrator had already reaped the real task's stale .worktrees/5035 and task/5035 branch by the time of cleanup.
target_text:
Leo's hand-carry procedure (stated 2026-10-01), the contract for hand-carrying any dark_factory task outside the orchestrator: "Check task is pending and only proceed if it is. Set task to deferred. Investigate, plan, implement, review in a fresh dedicated reviewer agent, address any issues, /merge-queue, set task done."
How to apply it:
- The pending check is a hard gate. If the task is anything else, stop and report; don't continue a chain.
- Set deferred BEFORE any other write to the task, such as removing a dependency. Removing the last unmet dependency makes the task dispatchable, so the scheduler could grab it mid-carry.
- The reviewer must not have written or rebased the code, and must review the final rebased diff.
- Chained hand-carries are run as sibling /spawn sessions, each ending with /reflect.

Completed: Graphiti BM25 edge search times out on every provisioned graph: FalkorDB plans graphiti's `{uuid: rel.uuid}` join as a per-row Entity label scan
Description: Discovered 2026-10-03 (~03:40-03:50Z) by task 3711's architect (FalkorDB index provisioning ζ, PRD docs/prds/falkordb-index-provisioning.md). Task 3708 (γ, merged 2026-10-02 11:42Z) provisioned fulltext + per-property range indices on every registered graph; fused-memory.service last restarted 2026-10-02 22:51 BST. Since then Graphiti search is failing, and this blocks task 3711's primary signal.

OBSERVATIONS (all read-only: MCP search, or `docker exec docker-falkordb-1 redis-cli GRAPH.RO_QUERY / GRAPH.EXPLAIN`):
1. MCP search(stores=['graphiti'], limit=5) failed with ResponseError 'Query timed out' 3/3: dark_factory 'task 3127', dark_factory 'FalkorDB fulltext index provisioning', reify 'rustfmt gate'.
2. fused-memory.service journal since the 22:51 BST restart: 13,217 lines matching 'timed out' (graphiti_core.driver.falkordb_driver ERROR 'Error executing FalkorDB query: Query timed out').
3. GRAPH.CONFIG: TIMEOUT 1000, TIMEOUT_DEFAULT 0, TIMEOUT_MAX 0.
4. Bare `CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO','3127') YIELD relationship, score RETURN count(relationship)` on dark_factory: 3 rows in 0.72 ms. So BM25 itself serves.
5. graphiti_core's own join (graphiti_core/search/search_utils.py::edge_fulltext_search, FalkorDB branch): `CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO','3127') YIELD relationship AS rel, score MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN ['dark_factory'] RETURN e.uuid, score LIMIT 10` returned 'Query timed out' on all 3 runs. Token 'index' timed out the same way. On reify, token 'cargo' (140 fulltext rows) also timed out.
6. GRAPH.EXPLAIN of that query: ProcedureCall -> Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan [e:RELATES_TO] -> Filter -> Project -> Limit. That is a full Entity label scan per yielded row.
7. The same join with a token that yields 0 fulltext rows took 13.9 ms.
8. A rewritten join, `... YIELD relationship AS e, score WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m WHERE e.group_id IN ['dark_factory'] RETURN e.uuid, n.uuid, m.uuid, score LIMIT 10`, took 6.5 ms on dark_factory.
9. The cosine-leg shape (`MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN [...] WITH e, (2 - vec.cosineDistance(e.fact_embedding, v))/2 AS score ...`) took 736 ms on dark_factory. That is under the 1000 ms read TIMEOUT, but close to it.
10. Open L2 esc-durable-write-dead-letter-2 (root_cause 'infra-outage:fused-memory-graphiti-falkordb-query-timeout-dead-letters-add-memory', filed 2026-10-02 14:02Z) records add_memory_graphiti writes dead-lettering on 'Query timed out'.

Hypothesis: before γ, no RELATES_TO fulltext index existed, so queryRelationships yielded 0 rows and the join never ran. Now that BM25 serves, the `{uuid: rel.uuid}` property-map join runs as a per-row label scan, overruns the 1000 ms read TIMEOUT, and fails the whole Graphiti search. The same join inside add_episode's edge-dedup searches would plausibly also explain the write dead-letters.

WORK: make Graphiti's FalkorDB fulltext edge search finish well inside the read TIMEOUT. Also audit the node and community fulltext paths, and any other `{uuid: x.uuid}` re-match that follows a YIELD. graphiti_core checks `driver.search_interface` before its built-in Cypher, and fused-memory already overrides build_fulltext_query in fused-memory/src/fused_memory/backends/graphiti_client.py. entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha: every bodied trait assoc fn is a DefaultKind::Fn default that conformance/checker.rs::check_phase_resolve_assoc_fns compiles once PER CONFORMER via functions.rs::compile_assoc_function. A trait-static (no-self) default is ALSO compiled once more in compile_builder/traits_phase.rs as the namespaced `Trait::fn` through compile_function. So a diagnostic emitted from either compile path for one wrong default body repeats N (or N+1) times at the same trait span unless deduped. Task 5991 measured 7 reports for 3 bodies and fixed it with fn_return_check.rs::push_once_per_body (match on code plus label span and message). A self-taking default in a trait with no conformers is never compiled at all.
target_text: Reify trait-body checking is DEFERRED to conformance: a `trait` compiled with NO conforming structure emits ZERO error diagnostics no matter how broken its body is — dimension-mismatched constraints, references to undefined member fields, and wrong `let` type annotations all pass silently. Adding a conformer (`structure def C : T { ... }`) makes all three fire (`DimensionMismatch`, `StructureMemberNotFound`, `TypeMismatchForTraitMember` respectively). Consequence: an absence-of-diagnostic assertion (`assert_no_error_diagnostics` / `assert_no_diagnostics`) written against a bare trait body is VACUOUS — it passes regardless of what the compiler does. The vacuity condition is precisely "trait body with no conformer", NOT "trait body". Measured on main @ 6927f3c0db (task 6143); pinned in crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_traits/trait_body_deferred_check_tests.rs.

entry_text: generic-data-carrying-enums PRD decision D1 ("F-Mono erasure, to match the structure side") rests on a STALE premise. D1 was verified 2026-05-27 when generic structure references silently lost their type args; Type::Applied was added 2026-06-16 (task 4602 β) and since then STRUCTURES KEEP type args at compile time (annotations are Applied with structural Eq; couple()/gear() return Applied; substitute_type_params rebuilds Applied) and erase them only in two places: a user constructor expression `Foo(...)` is typed StructureRef, and the runtime StructureInstanceData carries no args. Shipped generic ENUMS erase EARLIER: compile_variant_construct (variant_construct.rs success exit) types the value bare Type::Enum(name) even though `final_subst` already holds the inferred args; a `let` cell always takes the initializer's result_type (entity.rs ~:3097) so even an annotated `let r : Result<..> = Ok{..}` is erased — only a `param` keeps its declared Applied. base_enum_name/enum_payload_compatible (type_compat.rs) reconcile the two spellings by NAME ONLY. Measured consequences (2026-09-29, fixtures tests/prd-gate/fixtures/getar_*.ri): `let v : String = fallback(Ok{value:5mm}, "y")` checks clean and evaluates 5mm; `Result<Force,String> = <Result<Length,String> value>` accepted; `Tree<Force>` accepts `Leaf{value:1mm}` children; the task-4031 recursive conflict never fires; `fn f(r: Result<Length,String>)` called `f(Ok{value:5mm})` fails "no matching overload for f(Enum(Result))". Reversal PRD: docs/prds/v0_6/generic-enum-type-arg-retention.md (tasks 8012-8023).
target_text: Generic data-carrying enums (PRD v0_6/generic-data-carrying-enums) use D1/F-Mono TYPE ERASURE: a constructed Value::Enum has result_type Type::Enum(name) with NO type-arg slot (resolved args live only in the compiler's per-site substitution map, §7.1). Consequence/gotcha: a nested generic construction's inferred type-arg is unrecoverable at an outer site — unify(Type::Applied{Enum,[T]}, Type::Enum(name)) binds NOTHING (type_compat.rs unify fallthrough, the documented β posture). So the PRD's illustrative conflict example Node{left:Leaf{1mm},right:Leaf{1N}}→E_ENUM_TYPE_ARG_CONFLICT is NOT detectable; the faithful, detectable conflict is a same-param-twice variant e.g. enum Pair<T>{Both{a:T,b:T}} constructed Both{a:1mm,b:1N}. Reuse type_compat::unify + TypeArgConflict (same machinery as fn-generic FnTypeArgConflict, task 4231) and type_resolution::substitute_type_params for enum construction type-arg inference.

OBSERVED (measured in lane _lane-54, 2026-09-04): neither gui/test/visual/run.ts nor gui/test/visual/lib_e2e_smoke.sh mentions REIFY_VITE_PORT or 1420 anywhere (grep: zero matches in both files), so both take scripts/run-gui-dev.sh's :1420 default. Task #7254 added a vite-port preflight that refuses (exit 1, before any build) when something already answers on that port. Consequence: two warm lanes running the e2e smoke concurrently now have the second fail fast, where it previously attached to the FIRST lane's vite and asserted against another worktree's build. The refusal is correct; the new cross-lane serialisation constraint is the cost.

REIFY_VITE_PORT is not a workaround today and scripts/run-gui-dev.sh documents it as a TEST-ONLY KNOB: gui/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json pins "devUrl": "http://localhost:1420", which tauri bakes into reify-gui at COMPILE time, and nothing under gui/src-tauri/src/ reads REIFY_VITE_PORT. So overriding it moves OUR vite off :1420 while reify-gui still loads :1420 — i.e. the foreign listener that prompted the override — and the launcher reports success anyway. REIFY_GUI_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1 bypasses the check but restores that silent-wrong-vite attach, so it is not a fix either.

Work: supply the GUI-side half so REIFY_VITE_PORT can become user-facing — either a build-time devUrl override via TAURI_CONFIG, or read the env var in the Rust shell at startup. Then drop the "TEST-ONLY KNOB" warning in scripts/run-gui-dev.sh, let gui/test/visual/run.ts and lib_e2e_smoke.sh allocate a free port per run (scripts/lib_portable.sh's allocate_free_port), and remove the serialisation caveat added to docs/debug-mcp-recipe.md section 2.

target_text: REIFY_VITE_PORT is user-facing as of task 7274 (once its branch is on main; until then the 2026-07-14 / 2026-09-10 "devUrl is baked at :1420" memories still describe main). reify-gui reads REIFY_VITE_PORT at startup (gui/src-tauri/src/dev_url.rs, called first in main()) and retargets tauri.conf.json's devUrl to that port via Context::config_mut before run(). Tauri 2 reads config.build.dev_url at runtime for both the window URL and the IPC local-origin check, so no rebuild or TAURI_CONFIG is needed and one binary serves any port. A malformed value makes reify-gui exit 2 with a message naming the variable. scripts/run-gui-dev.sh validates the value and EXPORTS it (default 1420), so vite --port, the readiness probe and the loaded page always agree. Its occupied-port refusal now offers `REIFY_VITE_PORT=<free port>` as a remedy. gui/test/visual/lib_e2e_smoke.sh (resolve_port <VAR>) and run.ts (endpoint.ts resolveVitePort) allocate a free vite port per run unless the caller set a valid one, so lanes can run e2e smokes concurrently. The old "build dist + release binary + custom REIFY_SMOKE_LAUNCHER" workaround for a held :1420 is no longer needed. And ptodo's repo-wide G-allow liveness hard gate (crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs extract_g_allow_owner_cites) flags any `#NNNN` cite of a done/cancelled task as g-allow-orphaned (High) unless a paren group containing `done`/`cancelled` directly follows the cite — write terminal cites as `#NNNN (done)`.
target_text: G-allow done-cite cleanup (CU1-CU8 family, e.g. task 4777): reify-audit's broadened g-allow grammar (prereq #4774) lives in crates/reify-audit/src/ptodo.rs. A `// G-allow:` marker citing a terminal (done/cancelled) task surfaces as advisory `g-allow-orphaned` (Severity::Medium, exit-neutral) via resolve_g_allow_owner_liveness (ptodo.rs:1043). A cite is provenance-EXEMPT iff a whole-word `done`/`cancelled` token sits in the parenthetical immediately FOLLOWING it (rule a-following, ptodo.rs:445-466) or ENCLOSING it (a-enclosing) — gold form `#NNNN (done)` (see fixture g_allow_repo_wide_advisory.rs:78). Whole-word match: "abandoned"/"undone" do NOT exempt. EVERY terminal cite occurrence in a marker body is flagged independently (ptodo.rs:1037), so multi-cite markers (e.g. `#3541/#3582` plus a repeated `#3541`) need `(done)` after EACH occurrence. Decision rule: DELETE the marker if the symbol now has a real traceable non-test caller in crates/reify-*/src (wiring landed); else ANNOTATE `(done)` (genuine in-scope orphan by design, e.g. consumer lives in gui/ outside the crates/reify-*/src audit scope). Leave markers citing pending/live tasks untouched. These are `//` line comments (not `///` doc), so edits never affect compilation.

entry_text: reify-build-utils::find() trusts any NON-EMPTY <DEP>_LIB_DIR / <DEP>_INCLUDE_DIR override without checking for the sentinel file. Pointing GMSH_LIB_DIR at a bogus path therefore does NOT force a stub (no-has_gmsh) build: it sets has_gmsh and then fails at link time. Only an empty override counts as unset. To keep stub hosts green, write cfg-safe code by construction, for example by path-qualifying has_gmsh-only calls in files that are not gated on has_gmsh, instead of relying on a local stub build to check it.
target_text: You CANNOT force a reify stub build (`cfg(not(has_occt))` / `not(has_gmsh))`) by pointing `OCCT_LIB_DIR`/`GMSH_LIB_DIR`/`OPENVDB_LIB_DIR` at a bogus path: `reify_build_utils::find_dir_with_override` (crates/reify-build-utils/src/lib.rs:162-175) returns any NON-EMPTY override verbatim with NO existence or sentinel check, so the cfg is still set and the build fails at link instead. Only an EMPTY value counts as unset. To actually exercise a stub build locally, temporarily comment out the `println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=has_<dep>");` line in that adapter crate's build.rs, run `cargo check -p <crate> --tests`, then revert and confirm `git status` is clean.

entry_text: GOTCHA (task 5669 architect, measured with `pytest --setup-show` on pytest 9.0.3): within one conftest, plain autouse fixtures set up in ALPHABETICAL name order (pytest's parsefactories walks dir(module)), not declaration order. So renaming a teardown guard in orchestrator/tests/conftest.py silently moves its teardown slot. `_drain_async_mock_coroutines` tears down AFTER _drain_leaked_tasks, _function_scoped_runner and monkeypatch only because 'a' < 'f'/'l'/'m'. A rename to e.g. `_no_unawaited_...` would drain before leaked tasks are cancelled and before patches are undone. To change a guard's name safely, make the ordering explicit by fixture request instead.

target_text:
RATIONALE RECORD for task 4809 (dark_factory, 2026-08-27) — the reasoning behind resolving the markup guard's unfilable-residue defect as a scoped fix. Written to Mem0 verbatim because the same rationale, written as decisions_and_rationale, routed to Graphiti and was distilled to the single edge "The unfilable-residue defect of the markup guard is resolved as task 4809", which preserves the conclusion and loses every reason for it.

THREE OPTIONS WERE LIVE, and the evidence genuinely pulled in different directions.

Against a durable WON'T-FIX, which the severity data alone would have supported: PRD section 4 contract C2 and boundary row B5 both promise that an unrepairable call is "rejected, and an escalation filed carrying the full raw payload so nothing is discarded even if the caller never retries." Measured over the guard's complete deployed life (2026-08-23 onward), preservation failed for 11 of 15 refusals — 73.3%. A normative contract failing three times in four is not a documentation problem, and the manifest independently scores that capability PASS on mis-bound evidence, so nothing would have caught it.

Against a PRD, which the fleet-wide blast radius would have supported: the remedy is already designed, tested and DEPLOYED at a sibling boundary. orchestrator markup_sink.make_escalation_sink already takes a last_resort= floor, documented in its own docstring as the floor for exactly "an unresolvable project root, a missing escalation package", and verdict-tools already passes one. fused-memory's install_markup_guard simply has none. Writing a PRD to re-derive a decision the fleet had already made and shipped would have been over-engineering.

WHY THE CHOSEN SCOPE IS ORDERED THE WAY IT IS. The floor is the must, because it satisfies C2 with NO trust decision at all — it never has to believe anything about the corrupted payload. Registry-validated routing is the enhancement, and it is safe specifically because a bare project_id checked against the known_projects allowlist cannot create arbitrary directories, which is the actual concern behind _resolve_project_root's refusal to trust input; that rationale is about absolute PATHS, not ids, so it is untouched.

WHY SEVERITY WAS DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED TO JUSTIFY IT. Of the 7 destroyed writes checked, ZERO were permanently lost — every one was re-landed by its own authoring agent, median under a minute. The agent retry loop, not this preservation path, is what saves the data. The fix is justified by the violated contract and by the UNMEASURED tail (callers that never retry, which is precisely the case C2 names), not by observed loss. Anyone revisiting this should not discover the low realized harm and conclude the decision was made in ignorance of it.

entry_text:
Fact, measured 2026-10-01: merge-verify peak memory is NOT systematically recorded anywhere.
- The orchestrator records nothing.
- The df-verify-*.scope units are `--collect`ed at exit, so memory.peak vanishes with them.
- The only after-the-fact source is the user-journal line systemd 255 writes at scope exit ("<scope>: Consumed … CPU time, X memory peak, Y memory swap peak"). It includes the peak for only SOME scopes: 22 of 188 DF scopes and 1 of 6 reify scopes since 2026-09-30 21:00 BST. It was missing even for some of the largest legs. Treat it as a sample, not a record.

Values on leo-laptop:
- DF full-gate test leg: 13.3–14.3 GiB, against the 24G cap.
- Other DF legs: about 4.3–4.7 GiB and about 0.7 GiB.
- reify: one record of 32.0 GiB, exactly its MemoryMax. That verify passed in its normal 15.8 min, and there were no OOM kills in the kernel log. Most likely cargo page cache filling the cgroup to the limit and being reclaimed, so it says reify runs pressed against its cap, not what its anonymous memory needs.

To get real peaks, read memory.peak and memory.stat before the scope exits (suggested for task 6106 / task 5415).
target_text: MEASURING per-run CPU-seconds and cgroup peak memory on the dark-factory workstation (measured 2026-10-05, task 5469). An agent's Bash shell runs INSIDE orchestrator-dark-factory.service's cgroup, so that cgroup's memory.peak covers the whole fleet and is useless for a single run. `systemd-run --user --wait -p MemoryAccounting=yes` prints a bogus "Memory peak: 256.0K" for a process that touched 200 MB. What works is to wrap the command in its own scope and read the counters from inside before the scope exits: `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryAccounting=yes bash -c '<cmd>; rc=$?; cg=/sys/fs/cgroup$(cut -d: -f3 /proc/self/cgroup); echo peak=$(cat $cg/memory.peak); grep usage_usec $cg/cpu.stat; exit $rc'`. Two 150 MB python children read peak=322736128 and usage_usec 430667. Production records neither metric: verify summaries, junit archives and merge_verify events carry no CPU-seconds or peak RSS (DF verify_use_cgroup_scope is off; tasks 5206/5415 own that), and no archived summary in data/verify-logs has ever had timed_out=true. A merge-gate failure's category is the `[category: X]` suffix of merge_finalized/merge_blocked data.reason.

target_text: ADDENDUM to the dark-factory carrier-task procedure for hand-carried merges from an interactive session (learned 2026-09-19, task 5668): the ORDER matters. Do NOT walk the carrier to `in-progress` before the work is done, and do NOT work in `.worktrees/<id>` on branch `task/<id>`. An `in-progress` task whose claimant_run_id is not a live orchestrator run is treated by the orchestrator's reconciler as a crashed run: within ~20 minutes it logged `[orchestrator.git_ops] Cleaned up worktree .../.worktrees/5668 and branch task/5668` and `[orchestrator.harness] Reconcile: reverted task 5668 to pending` — uncommitted work was deleted and the task became dispatchable to a factory agent. Correct sequence: file the carrier with submit_task(planning_mode=True) and LEAVE IT `deferred` for the whole working period; work in a worktree OUTSIDE `.worktrees/` (e.g. /home/leo/src/df-interactive-<slug>) on a NON-`task/` branch (interactive/<slug>); commit early; get the fresh-agent review; only when ready to submit do commit_planning → set in-progress (with claimant_run_id) → set merge-deferred back-to-back, THEN `git branch -m` to task/<id>, `git worktree move` into .worktrees/<id>, and merge_request. Related facts: `git worktree move` breaks the moved worktree's uv .venv (absolute paths) — harmless for submission because the merge lane verifies in its own _merge-* worktree, but run nothing from the moved tree; a merge commit's timestamp is when the lane BUILT the merge, not when main advanced — read the orchestrator log line `Task <id>: verify end (merge=<sha>, passed=True)` for the landing time (5668's merge commit said 19:32, main advanced at 20:00); an MCP-submitted carrier jumped from queue position 13 to the head because most older `queued` entries are ghost observability artefacts; if a carrier ever shows `pending` unexpectedly, set it `deferred` at once.

entry_text: GOTCHA (dark-factory, task 6096): any Python reader of /proc/<pid>/stat or /proc/<pid>/comm must read BYTES (read_bytes().decode('utf-8','replace')). comm is arbitrary bytes, and a strict read_text() raises UnicodeDecodeError, a ValueError that slips past `except OSError`. Since task 6029, shared/tests/test_proc_group.py::test_a_member_with_an_undecodable_comm_is_still_listed keeps a live b'\xff\xfe'-named process on the host during every verify. Any concurrent host-wide /proc walk that decodes strictly therefore crashes under load and passes in isolation; this is how verify_cancel.read_ppid_map produced the 6096 flake. Use shared/src/shared/proc_group.py::read_stat_fields as the single stat parser.
