RATIONALE RECORD for task 3500's central design call (landed 2026-08-29), written to a Mem0-backed category on purpose: the conclusion alone is useless without it, and decisions_and_rationale distils reasoning away.

THE CALL: evaluating a delivered_check against a tree yields a BIT, not a VERDICT — so the same rule cannot be both an authoring gate and a corpus sweep. 3500 split them.

WHY. "expect: present and it matches" is simultaneously (a) the SUCCESS state of a landed producer and (b) a never-fires vacuous gate on a live one. Nothing in the descriptor distinguishes them. MEASURED: applying the authoring-time 2x2 to the checked-in corpus with the reference tree set to main-today flags 313/548 descriptors (57%) — 287 present/match, 203 present/nomatch, 32 absent/match, 26 absent/nomatch. The overwhelming majority of those 313 are correctly delivered work. The fold-in (esc-4545-2) had reported 104/538 (19%) and framed the 2x2 as "checkable with nothing but the manifest and git — no commit-ordering premise"; re-running it showed the reference tree is load-bearing, and that discrepancy is methodological, not corpus growth (52 vs 50 manifest files). Filed as esc-3500-1.

THE RESOLUTION THAT MADE IT TRACTABLE: at AUTHORING time the reference tree is free. commit_planning runs BEFORE the task is implemented, so HEAD at that moment IS the pre-task tree and "already green" is decisive with no history and no status. Only the RETROACTIVE sweep cannot recover it — and there the missing input is the producer's STATUS, which turns the bit into a disposition (present+nomatch is a defect on a done task, the normal forward-looking majority on a pending one). Status lives in .taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db, which is why the sweep is scripts/audit_delivered_checks.py and not a pytest gate.

THE THIRD PLACE THE SAME QUESTION LANDS, and why it got a THIRD answer: shared/tests/test_capability_manifest.py must run in any checkout, so it can read neither tasks.db nor a status. It therefore sweeps ONLY the STRUCTURAL codes (self_referential, comment_only, filename_shaped) — statements about a descriptor's SHAPE, which stay true whatever tree they are measured against — and deliberately leaves the vacuity direction alone. It is a frozen-allowlist RATCHET, not a gate, because the measured live structural debt (5 self-reference, 5 comment-only, 1 filename-only) sits in plans/ and docs/prds/ manifests outside that task's lock scope; a hard gate there would have been permanently-red and therefore ignored.

OPTIONS REJECTED, with reasons: (1) one status-blind rule everywhere — rejected on the 57% false-positive rate above; (2) the prior plan's {pre-state, still, unchanged, old, legacy, before} NAME-TOKEN vocabulary — strictly dominated and deleted entirely, because it guessed author intent from English and needed hand-tuned exclusions (installed/stillness/threshold/preflight-state-machine) to avoid false rejects on a hard-blocking gate, whereas the non-vacuity rule MEASURES the repo and subsumes the same cases; (3) adding kind='path' for MODE 3 — deferred purely on blast radius (closed Literals plus every mechanical-kind tuple in the fleet), not merit, and filed as a follow-up.

CAVEAT DELIBERATELY NOT SUPPRESSED: the corpus ratchet's allowlist is pre-existing debt the task could not repair in-scope, and the audit sweep's exit code deliberately ignores `superseded`, `inert` and `unevaluable` rows. Both are choices to keep a detector green enough to be read, not claims that those rows are fine.

target_text:
A REBASE-LANDING DEFEATS NAIVE ANCESTRY AND SHA CHECKS. The merge lane can land a task branch by REBASING its commits onto main rather than creating a --no-ff merge commit. Rebase RE-CREATES every commit with a NEW sha, so the sha you recorded is not on main -- even though the work is.

CONSEQUENCE: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <cited-sha> main` returns rc=1 for work that DID land. Acting on that rc=1 means re-submitting already-landed work.
VERIFY CONTENT OR THE merge_status SIGNAL INSTEAD -- merge_status is the authoritative answer to "did this land". Match commit SUBJECTS, or check that the content is present, rather than testing a sha.

FOUR SUBCASES, each a stamped peer:
  - ZERO-COMMIT BRANCH: is_ancestor(HEAD, main) is TRIVIALLY True when the branch tip equals the main HEAD it was created from -- a true answer that means nothing (documented at find_task_citation_commit in git_ops.py).
  - plan.json STEP SHAs GO UNREACHABLE after an inter-iteration rebase, which breaks bisection over recorded step commits.
  - THE UNBLOCK RUNBOOK FALSE-NEGATIVE (task 3464): the runbook's ancestry test says "not landed" for a rebase-landed branch.
  - AUDITING ESCALATION-CITED SHAs (task 3624): an escalation citing shas as proof its work landed cannot be audited with merge-base; use content checks.

DERIVED NORM: NEVER PIN A DURABLE ARTIFACT REFERENCE TO A COMMIT SHA CREATED ON YOUR OWN TASK BRANCH. The lane rebases task/<id> before landing it, so any same-branch sha you record is dead on arrival. Reference by content, subject, or the post-merge sha.

ACCRETION: append here or add a stamped peer under topic `git-rebase-defeats-ancestry-check` -- do not write a new unstamped entry.

target_text: dark_factory's git_ops.py::DEFAULT_COMMIT_CITATION_PATTERN misses roughly 31% of this repo's OWN commit-citation conventions, causing validate_landing_evidence to reject genuine landings as no_citation and leave the task pending so it re-dispatches. Measured 2026-09-07 over all 64,833 subjects on main: `type(N):` / `type(N)` MATCHES 5,028; `type(N <extra>):` — e.g. impl(4369 step-8), amend(3393 review), test(1955 S7) — MISSES 2,249; `(task N, ...)` MISSES 70. Leo ruled (c) on 2026-09-07: fix the pattern AND wire delivered_checks, in that order — owners task 4862 (pattern) and task 4496 (delivered_checks). Ordering is load-bearing: wiring the second accept path alone would make genuine landings pass for the wrong reason and hide the blind spot. Widening the matcher has a false-POSITIVE direction, so the fix needs tests pinning both directions.

The fused-memory set_task_priority_override docstring overstates what pins and reserve_now do (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py). It says 'Pin this task to the front of the queue' and, for reserve_now, 'Reserve the next worker slot'.
In fact:
- A pin gives only a first try, each scheduler tick, at all-or-nothing module-lock acquisition, with no reservation.
- reserve_now installs parks once, at the task's RAW priority, and reserves no worker slot.
Operators pin expecting movement that the code does not provide. As of 2026-09-29 no task owns the docstring fix; it was deliberately kept out of 6040 to avoid adding a fused-memory file to it.

entry_text: reify check's relate-family exit behaviour depends on the phase. Compile-phase relate operand errors (ArgTypeMismatch, DatumProjectionUnavailable, DatumProjectionAmbiguous, TangentOperandsUnsupported from relation_signatures.rs) exit 1 through cmd_check's compile-diagnostics early return, with empty stdout. Engine-phase relate errors (RelateStaticViolated, AssemblyGlobalFloat, the un-consumable-member RelateExpectsRelation, and code-less conflict errors from reify-eval relate_solve.rs) exist only when an OCCT kernel is registered, because build_with_geometry_output skips solve_scopes without one. Those runs print "All constraints satisfied." and exit 1 only through #5403's check_gating_error, so CLI tests for them must skip on !reify_kernel_occt::OCCT_AVAILABLE.
target_text: `reify check` has two exit channels. A compile-phase Error returns early in cmd_check (crates/reify-cli/src/main.rs, `compiled.diagnostics.any(Error)`), before evaluation: stdout is empty and CHECK_ERROR_EXIT_ALLOWLIST is never consulted. An engine-phase Error exits through #5403's `check_gating_error` AFTER finish_check, so stdout still prints "All constraints satisfied." beside the stderr `error:` line. The presence of that summary line is a reliable test discriminator for which phase moved the exit. Relate-solve diagnostics (relate_solve::solve_scopes) are only produced when a geometry kernel is registered, so CLI tests pinning them must skip on `!reify_kernel_occt::OCCT_AVAILABLE`.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, main 15634a417f): inside a trait INSTANCE assoc-fn body, every `self.member` / bare member read types as dimensionless Real, regardless of the member's declared type. Cause: crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs compile_assoc_function builds its body scope without set_template_registry, so expr.rs member_access_on_structure_like hits its registry-miss permissive fallback for the StructureRef(conformer) receiver. E.g. `fn lateral_area(self) -> Scalar<Area> { pi * diameter * length }` compiles its body to Real. Any static check on assoc-fn body types (comparison guards, body-vs-return reconciliation) will false-positive or false-negative there. Tracked as #8118; sibling #7855 is the same erase-to-Real class for trait-typed fn params.
target_text: Reify compiler (task #5991): a fn body's result type is now reconciled against its return type by crates/reify-compiler/src/fn_return_check.rs (warn-mode FnReturnTypeMismatch / FnReturnTypeUnannotated, severity from FN_RETURN_RECONCILE_SEVERITY). Gotcha for test authors: a deliberately mismatched trivial fn fixture (e.g. `fn f(x: Real) -> Int { x }`, `-> Length { 1.0 }`, or an un-annotated `fn f() { 10mm }`) now carries a Warning, so assert Error-severity-only rather than zero total diagnostics. entry_text: reify-eval `Engine::upgrade_indeterminate_verdicts(module, values, is_candidate)` (task 6979) returns a ConstraintUpgrade for EVERY candidate whose re-check verdict is definite; it cannot know prior verdicts. Pass only the constraints that are currently Indeterminate as candidates (never `|_| true` on a module with already-definite constraints), then feed the result to `reify_eval::replace_superseded_constraint_diagnostics` to retract their stale ConstraintIndeterminate warnings. It never dispatches a geometric Conforms (explicit `actual`), whose verdict belongs to measure_gdt_conformance.
target_text: reify engine: Engine::check() (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_constraints.rs:1841) opens with a fresh self.eval(module) and checks constraints against that pure-eval value map, so calling engine.build(...) before engine.check(...) does NOT give the check pass build()'s post-processed geometry values. Geometry-derived cells such as moi_principal = eigenvalues(moment_of_inertia) are resolved only by the task-4229 post-realization constraint re-check inside build_with_geometry_output (crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs:4908-4990), which upgrades Indeterminate verdicts and drops the stale indeterminate-undefined-inputs warning. entry_text: GOTCHA (task 3096): close_only only means "no task-status change". Harness._on_escalation_resolved calls event.set() on _escalation_events[task_id] for EVERY resolution, close_only and dismiss=True included, before it dispatches the action, so any closure wakes a live workflow waiting on that task id. Also, queue.submit_resolved leaves resolution_action None, and the legacy D10 mapping reads a resolved record as 'resume' (re-pend). Stamp esc.resolution_action='close_only' before submit_resolved when you mean a no-effect closure. To suppress the wake as well, you need an explicit early return at the top of the callback, like the eval-lane guard keyed on shared.eval_lane.eval_lane_provenance.

GOTCHA (dark-factory, verified in code while planning task 4377): closing an escalation is a STATE-CHANGING ACT ON ITS SUBJECT TASK, even under `action='close_only'` whose documented task-status effect is "unchanged".

MECHANISM. `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/task_ground_truth.py::_RECOVERY` is a dict keyed on (status, live_claimant, branch_state, has_open_escalation, deploy_phase), read through `.get(_shape(report), RecoveryAction.LEAVE)`. The shape (IN_PROGRESS, live_claimant=None, EXISTS_OFF_MAIN, has_open_escalation=True, deploy_phase=None) is ABSENT from the table, so it falls through to the default and the row is PRESERVED. Close the record and the boolean flips: the shape becomes the (…, has_open_escalation=False, …) row that IS in the table, mapping to REVERT_TO_PENDING. The veto sites read `report.open_escalations` directly (harness.py ~:6185 and ~:6274).

WHY THIS IS EASY TO GET WRONG. The preservation is an EMERGENT PROPERTY OF A MISSING TABLE ROW, not a declared rule — nothing anywhere says "this record is holding this task". `resolve_issue`'s own docstring table lists `close_only` -> "task-status effect: unchanged", which is true of the call mechanically and false of its consequence. `escalation/src/escalation/pins.py::classify_pins` answers only "does this OPEN record veto recovery?" (classification at recovery time) and protects nothing from being CLOSED.

WHAT IT COST. On 2026-08-08 an L2 cascade close of the 11-member cluster esc-3237-5 dismissed esc-3371-2, the only pin preserving mu-gate validation specimen task 3371; the task reverted to pending 879.6s later and the specimen is permanently gone. The closing watcher checked for harm and reasoned correctly within what it could see — none of the eleven was `blocked`, so no stranded-blocked shield was stripped. An orphan-reaper false-positive record and a deliberate pin are indistinguishable by id, level, category, severity, agent_role or content. The sibling pin esc-3105-3 (a 15-member L2 cluster head) is still the last hold on task 3105.

PRACTICE. Before closing any pending escalation on a non-terminal task — and before designating a homogeneous cluster for a bulk/cascade close — check the subject task's status and branch state, not just whether the record looks moot. Note `escalation/src/escalation/sweep.py` is a file-RELOCATOR (moves already-terminal records to the archive), not a closer, despite the name.

Completed: Negative-assertion tests that pass for the wrong reason when a config default flips: invisible to both the AST ratchet and the adversarial-config sweep
Description: Filed by task 4481's implementer as out-of-scope follow-up work. No escalation record; discovered by inspection while executing task 4481's steps 8-10.

BACKGROUND. Task 4481 swept orchestrator/tests for tests that depend on an UNDECLARED config key's package code default, using two detectors: a committed AST ratchet (static) and a scratch adversarial-config harness (dynamic — a test green with the real yaml and red under a yaml that perturbs every undeclared key is depending on a code default by definition).

THE GAP. Both detectors are blind to a test whose assertion is NEGATIVE — "this env var is absent", "this callback did not fire", "this flag was not injected". When the root key flips, the behaviour under test is disabled, the negative assertion becomes trivially true, and the test PASSES. It passes for the wrong reason: it is no longer exercising anything. The dynamic harness cannot see it (it only reports failures), and the AST ratchet cannot see it (there is no equality-against-a-default to match).

MEASURED INSTANCES (all observed green under the adversarial config during task 4481, each in a class whose sibling POSITIVE tests went red from the same single root key, which is what makes the reading concrete rather than speculative):
- orchestrator/tests/test_verify_admission_pytest_n.py::TestPytestNWiring::test_merge_role_excluded_from_dash_n_injection and ::test_env_recovery_rerun_is_not_dash_n_injected — both assert '-n 16' is NOT present; root key verify_admission_enabled, which when false means nothing is ever injected for any role.
- orchestrator/tests/test_workflow_e2e.py::TestBuildAgentEnvCpuGovern::test_governance_disabled_by_default_no_df_agent_cpu_govern — asserts DF_AGENT_CPU_GOVERN absent; survives cpu_governance.enabled being flipped to true because the exec-path resolution then fails open.
- orchestrator/tests/test_scheduler.py::TestParkStopTrip::test_trip_does_not_re_fire_when_paused and ::test_trip_below_threshold_does_not_fire — both assert the callback did NOT fire; root key park_stop_enabled, which when false disarms the trip entirely.

WHY NOT FIXED IN 4481. Task 4481's scope was the measured failure set. Repairing tests that were passing would have meant expanding scope on a judgment call rather than a measurement, and the class is potentially much larger than the five instances listed (they are the ones that happened to sit beside a failing sibling; nothing systematically enumerated them).

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not prescriptive). The cheap, targeted version is to pin the relevant flag ON in the five sites above, exactly as task 4481 did for their failing siblings (see commits titled "class-(B) batch B/C/D" on task/4481 for the idiom — pin at the fixture or construction that builds the config, never the code_default_config hatch, since these are behaviour tests). The more general version — a mutation-style check that a negative assertion still fails when the behaviour it denies is force-enabled — is a much larger piece of work and should be scoped separately if wanted; note that a permanent dynamic gate of any kind is task 3886's still-open option (1), so check that decision before building one.

GOTCHA (dark-factory orchestrator tests, measured task 4481): a bare `OrchestratorConfig()` in a test does NOT give you code defaults. The autouse `_isolate_orch_config` fixture (orchestrator/tests/conftest.py) pins ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at the OPERATIONAL dark-factory-orchestrator.yaml, so a bare config reads whatever that file declares and falls back to the package default only for keys it does NOT declare. Measured: 390 config leaf fields exist, the operational yaml declares 41, so 349 keys are silently supplied by the code default. Any test asserting one of those 349 passes BY ACCIDENT and goes red the moment an operator declares that key — a landmine armed by an ops edit, in a file nobody thought to pre-check.

THE HATCH: `@pytest.mark.usefixtures("code_default_config")` (conftest.py) re-points ORCH_CONFIG_PATH at a guaranteed-absent file so only the package-bundled defaults.yaml loads. It runs AFTER the autouse fixture and wins. It must never be made autouse (that would strip config.yaml from ~10k tests that legitimately want it). Two ad-hoc equivalents are already widespread and count as isolation: monkeypatch.setenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', '') (154 uses) and monkeypatch.delenv('ORCH_CONFIG_PATH', raising=False) (29 uses).

TWO DISTINCT FAILURE CLASSES, needing different detection — do not assume one method finds both:
(A) STATIC — asserts a field EQUALS its code default. Found by AST scan. A committed ratchet now holds this at zero for the whole suite: orchestrator/tests/test_code_default_hatch_guard.py + _config_default_scan.py.
(B) BEHAVIOURAL — exercises default-only behaviour with no literal assertion anywhere, so NO static scan can see it. Typically a section's `enabled` flag defaulting True is what makes a code path run at all. Found ONLY dynamically: perturb every undeclared key at once (constraint-aware — several fields carry pydantic `le` bounds and model validators), swap the yaml in, run the suite, and take adversarial_failures MINUS baseline_failures. Measured over a 41-file union: baseline 0 failed / 2986 passed; adversarial 97 failed. Class (B) outnumbered class (A) roughly 3:1.

REPAIR RULE THAT HELD UP IN PRACTICE: for class (A), the one-line hatch. For class (B) where the root key is a section `enabled` flag and the test is about BEHAVIOUR rather than defaults, prefer the knob-agnostic pin (set the one flag explicitly in the fixture that builds the config) over the hatch — the test then keeps reading operational values for every other key. Where a test hard-codes a threshold literal, read it live off the config under test instead.

ALWAYS BISECT THE ROOT KEY BEFORE REPAIRING; the obvious guess is wrong often enough to matter. Measured counterexample: test_harness_deterministic_recon_sweep.py's 18 adversarial failures look like they must come from `deterministic_recon_sweep_enabled` — perturbing that key ALONE leaves the file fully green (95 passed). The actual root key was `recovery_emission.enabled`, a different config section. One root key producing 18 failures needs one decision, not 18.

TOOLING NOTE: the adversarial-config harness must `cp` the real yaml aside and restore it under a shell `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and you must verify `git status` clean and the yaml byte-identical afterwards — you are mutating a tracked, operator-owned file in the live tree.

entry_text:
Completed: Merge lane never un-stacks a train member whose predecessor leaves the queue without landing — the orphan's conflicts are then reported as the member's own
Description: MEASURED 2026-09-18 while resolving esc-4137-3/esc-4137-4 (steward). Task 4137's merge was blocked for reasons that had nothing to do with task 4137.

THE DEFECT. When a train is formed, an order>0 member is rebased onto its predecessor's branch tip rather than main (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/git_ops.py::_resolve_predecessor_tip, "train-predecessor tip or main"). That is correct at formation. But if the predecessor subsequently leaves the merge queue WITHOUT LANDING, nothing un-stacks the member. The member's branch silently keeps carrying every one of the predecessor's commits, and its next merge_request therefore reports the PREDECESSOR's conflicts against main as its own.

THE SIGHTING. task/4137 (7 own commits, all dashboard) was stacked behind task/4480 at 2026-09-08 21:49 (reflog task/4137@{0} = 'rebase (finish) onto 9788a34b13'). Task 4480 then went to status=pending and left the queue, never merged; merge_status(task_id=4480) = unknown. Ten days later 4137's merge attempt reported 15 conflicts — of which 14 were 4480's fused-memory test refactor vs main's task-3895 load_script_module migration. Replaying only 4137's own delta (`git merge-tree --merge-base=9788a34b13 main <tip>`) conflicts in exactly ONE file, its own index.html cache-buster.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A STALE BRANCH. The failure is mis-attributed by construction. The merger sees a 15-way conflict "in task 4137" and every available remedy is wrong: resolving toward main silently DROPS the absent predecessor's entire deliverable (here 786 lines of new files plus a 15-suite rewrite that exists nowhere else); combining both sides lands the predecessor's whole deliverable through the member's merge, outside the member's plan scope and file locks, and requires implementing the predecessor against a main ~2145 commits ahead. Both destructive options look locally reasonable to an agent that has not audited the branch's reflog. Only the third — un-stack — is correct, and identifying it requires noticing the stacking in the first place. Two escalation rounds were consumed on this one instance before a human-authority role took the ref rewrite.

COMPLETION CONDITION. The lane should detect, at merge_request admission time, that a branch's merge-base against main is a non-landed sibling task's branch tip, and un-stack it automatically via the operation the lane already owns — git_ops.py::materialize_member_solo(predecessor_ref=...), equivalently `git rebase --onto main <predecessor_tip> <branch>` — before attempting the merge. Escalate only if THAT rebase conflicts. Suggested shape: on dequeue, resolve the recorded train predecessor (or derive it by testing whether merge-base(branch, main) is the tip of another task's branch), check whether it is an ancestor of main, and if not, un-stack. Regression test: a member stacked on a predecessor branch that never lands merges solo on its own delta and reports only its own conflicts.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: how many other branches are currently in this state. The condition is cheap to detect in bulk (for each task branch, is merge-base(branch, main) equal to some other task/* tip that is not an ancestor of main?) and each hit is a mis-attributed merge failure waiting to happen. Task 4480 itself remains status=pending with 15 commits living only on task/4480; it is the one carrier of that work and should be scheduled before its base drifts further.

NOT A DUPLICATE (searched): 1878 (worktree-reuse rebases onto main unconditionally) is the mirror-image bug and is done; 1867/4737/4953 are merge-deferred stranding after coalescing; 4669 is a requeue rebase dropping a commit whose patch no longer applies; 2403 is a branch reset to an unrelated tip. None covers a member left stacked on a predecessor that exited the queue unlanded.
Analysis: PREMI…[truncated, 10340 chars total]
target_text: Train stacking rewrites real member refs at COALESCE time, not at merge time (verified 2026-09-11). git_ops.py::GitOps.stack_train_branches rebases each non-base member's own task/<id> branch onto its predecessor's branch, inside the member's own .worktrees/<id> worktree, via the unguarded rebase_onto_main(onto=...) primitive (the BranchResetError wipe detector is deliberately off on this path). The tip is the LAST member by sorted task id, not the FIFO anchor. There is no backup ref and no restore on any non-done outcome; the pre-stack tip survives only incidentally as `snapshot_tip` on each absorbed single's superseded merge_finalized row. Coalesce-to-train-start gaps are hours (4537: 2h15 and 6h22), so branches sit rewritten long before the status check. Rebasing a member whose previous base was newer main than the predecessor's base also REPLAYS main commits as duplicates (same subjects, new SHAs, all bearing the coalesce timestamp) — git cherry shows them as '-'.

SpeculativeMergeWorker.__init__ binds its landed outbox, <git_ops.project_root>/data/orchestrator/landed_outbox.json, onto the PROCESS-GLOBAL MergeProvenance via MergeProvenance.bind, and nothing ever unbinds it. In a test suite this means a LandedRow recorded by one test's lane answers a later test's MergeProvenance.lookup, for example inside workflow._recover_if_already_merged, in the same xdist worker.

It surfaced when task 5034 moved the workflow e2e helpers (_workflow_helpers.py::_build_workflow*) onto a production MergeLane. TestWipRecoveryNoAdvance recorded a write-ahead row for task '42' that was never consumed, and TestRecoverIfAlreadyMerged then got DONE instead of None. A -n0 repro of that pair gave 10 failing out of 12. To an observer it looked like a one-off e2e flake.

Fix: conftest.py::_isolated_merge_provenance, an autouse fixture that binds a fresh empty LandedOutbox per test (a uuid path under basetemp, never created unless something records). Six modules still carry their own older per-module `MergeProvenance._outbox = None` reset, which is now redundant.
target_text: orchestrator's MergeProvenance (orchestrator/src/orchestrator/landed_outbox.py) is a PROCESS-GLOBAL façade: `MergeProvenance.lookup(task_id)` reads a class-level `_outbox` set via `MergeProvenance.bind(outbox)`. Unbound → lookup returns None (the fail-safe/empty-journal path). Tests that bind a LandedOutbox to exercise journal-hit paths MUST reset `MergeProvenance._outbox = None` in teardown or the binding leaks across tests. On current main the write side (LandedOutbox.record) is NOT wired at any CAS-advance site (that is W1 β, a separate task), so lookup always misses in production today — the W9 α guard-collapse is behaviourally safe with an empty journal.

entry_text: Kernel linkage facts for the production `reify` binary (verified 2026-09-28 on main 5340545275): reify-cli/src/main.rs force-links OCCT, Manifold (unconditional) and OpenVDB (cfg has_openvdb) via `extern crate` so their inventory capability descriptors survive the linker. Gmsh is NOT force-linked — it reaches the CLI only FUNCTIONALLY through reify-solver-elastic's real FEA meshing calls → reify-eval → reify-cli; if the elastic solver ever drops its direct reify_kernel_gmsh calls for a pure-Rust mesher, Gmsh's GeometryKernel capability silently stops shipping with no compile error. Fidget has no path at all (see the #8010 decision). reify-config lists all five kernel crates but ONLY as [dev-dependencies] for tests/kernel_name_consistency.rs (task 3139 / esc-3123-85) — its production library is adapter-free, so a Cargo.toml grep that hits reify-config is not evidence of production linkage. Also: `sweep(profile, path)` → OCCT make_pipe is a thin BRepOffsetAPI_MakePipe with NO auto-orientation of the profile to the path's start tangent (an in-plane profile sweeps to a silent zero), whereas `pipe(path, radius)` builds an oriented circle at the start frame first — a likely source of 'sweep produced a twisted/zero solid' reports that are not kernel bugs.
target_text: PREMISE CORRECTION (verified 2026-07-14): the recurring claim that "the Manifold geometry kernel is only a DEV-dependency of reify-eval and not registered in production builds" is FALSE for the shipped binary. reify-kernel-manifold is a normal [dependencies] entry of the production CLI (crates/reify-cli/Cargo.toml:30, alongside occt/openvdb) and registers UNCONDITIONALLY (no cfg(test) gate) via inventory::submit! (crates/reify-kernel-manifold/src/register.rs:62); all four native kernels incl. manifold are prebuilt/linked (.cargo/config.toml + scripts/build-manifold-deps.sh). The dev-dep is real only WITHIN reify-eval's own crate (a dead-strip invariant so its OCCT-only registry-count tests hold). What keeps Manifold dormant is DISPATCH SELECTION, not absence: pick_lexmin_brep_kernel filters to BRep-capable kernels so OCCT wins the default pick (reify-eval/src/kernel_registry.rs:182-219), and Manifold only wins Mesh-repr booleans. Consequence: "route booleans to Manifold" is NOT a productionization/build/registration PRD (that is done) — it is a batch-op vertical slice + Mesh-repr routing. Manifold::batch_difference (near-linear n-ary CSG) is a single linked FFI call the adapter execute() (kernel.rs:343-366) simply doesn't route to yet.

entry_text: reify tests/infra/nextest_absent_lib.sh (nx_run) gives nested suites a throwaway HOME with CARGO_HOME unset, so their cargo registry cache is COLD. Any hermetic `cargo metadata --locked --offline` read inside a suite nested by test_verify_nextest_absent_suites.sh fails (measured 126 ms, 'no matching package named serde ... offline'). A bare non-offline read instead silently downloads the registry into the throwaway HOME (measured 12.6 s, ~718 MB). H7's 'HOME still small' check runs BEFORE the S-rows, so it does not catch that fetch.
target_text: CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME are asymmetric when simulating a nextest-less host in tests/infra (e.g. building a temp-HOME cargo test harness), and getting either backwards is silent. CARGO_HOME must be actively `env -u`-unset (not merely left un-exported, and NEVER exported): cargo resolves `cargo-<subcmd>` from $CARGO_HOME/bin in ADDITION to PATH, so a leaked CARGO_HOME silently un-hides cargo-nextest and flips verify.sh's plan header back to nextest=1 while the harness still appears to run normally. RUSTUP_HOME is the opposite — it must be resolved once while $HOME is still the real home and carried across, because cargo is a rustup shim that falls back to $HOME/.rustup when RUSTUP_HOME is unset; without carrying it, the shim downloads a fresh toolchain into the temp HOME (measured at task 5599: 935 MB in 12s, before `cargo --version` even returned). Carrying RUSTUP_HOME cannot weaken the simulation: cargo-nextest is a standalone binary in the cargo bin dir, not under ~/.rustup, so the nextest-absent simulation stays intact.

target_text: Three OrbitControls 0.183.2 has three camera-state traps that reify's GUI hits. (1) `_quat`/`_quatInverse` (the orbit-frame rotation) are computed ONCE in the constructor from `object.up` (OrbitControls.js:406-407) and read only at 695/784 — neither `update()` nor `reset()` re-derives them, and no public API does, so mutating `camera.up` afterwards leaves orbiting on the OLD axis while `camera.up` reads the new value. (2) `update()` clamps the orbit radius UNCONDITIONALLY via `_clampDistance` (:1072-1074, called at 771/776/814), so `minDistance` silently relocates ANY directly-assigned `camera.position`, not just dolly requests. (3) `update()` writes `camera.position` and `camera.quaternion` but NEVER `camera.matrixWorld` — only `renderer.render()` refreshes that. Since `Viewport.tsx` is render-on-demand (`controls.update()` every RAF frame, `renderer.render()` only when `needsRender`), anything reading `matrixWorld` — notably `Raycaster.setFromCamera`, which consumes `matrixWorld` + `projectionMatrixInverse` and nothing else — sees the last-RENDERED pose, not the live one, and must call `camera.updateMatrixWorld()` itself.

entry_text: In `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/workflow.py::TaskWorkflow._run_merge_phase` the Phase 1 pre-merge re-verify (`run_scoped_verification(..., role='task')`) is the only task-role verify outside `_run_scoped_verification_with_infra_retry`, and it passes no task_id or attempt_id. Whatever it returns, the loop still submits to the merge queue (with pre_rebased=False on a failure or timeout), and the queue's own merge verify is the real gate. Only a RAISED VerifyInfraError bypasses that path: it escapes run() and blocks the task as infra_issue, and the detection log says 'Task None'. This is how Task 4237 (2026-09-26) and Task 5671 (2026-09-28) blocked. Task 6039 owns the fix. Separately, the main-tip sweep (`run_main_tip_sweep`, background role) swallows the same raise as 'unexpected error ... returning the no signal sentinel' and persists nothing.
target_text: Fact (merge_queue.py, confirmed 2026-06-09): The post-merge verify is strictly more stringent than the task-phase verify. The unscoped whole-package type-check gate _run_unscoped_typechecks runs ONLY at merge phase — merge_queue.py:473 (pre-advance, block_on_timeout=True / fail-CLOSED) and :1687 / _check_post_merge_pyright (post-advance, fail-OPEN). The task-phase verify (workflow.py:1305, 3472) is a plain scoped run_scoped_verification, warm timeouts, with NO unscoped cross-package gate. This asymmetry is deliberate (the stringent final verify justifies a slimmer branch verify) and is why you cannot safely skip the merge verify by relying on the branch verify.

entry_text: Gotcha, verified 2026-10-05 for task 4701 on CPython 3.13.9 under -X dev -W error. Raising pytest.fail (a Failed, which is a BaseException) inside a monkeypatched subprocess.Popen.__init__ comes out of `await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(...)` cleanly. It emits no ResourceWarning or unraisable warning, and production `except Exception` handlers do not catch it. That makes Popen.__init__ a test seam that no name binding can bypass for 'forbid this spawn' guards. A recording-only probe over the full orchestrator suite found zero agent-CLI (claude/codex/gemini/pi) spawns in 24,267 tests: every invocation test mocks at or above asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, which shadows a Popen-level guard.
target_text: GOTCHA (measured 2026-10-05, task 6346, CPython 3.13.9): asyncio.create_subprocess_exec forks and execs inline, then SUSPENDS for several loop iterations at `await waiter` in unix_events._make_subprocess_transport while it connects the child's pipes. A cancellation landing in that post-fork window is cleaned up by asyncio itself: transp.close() calls proc.kill() on the DIRECT child only, then awaits transp._wait(). So a start_new_session=True child's grandchildren survive, and the cancelled call can hang while a survivor holds the pipes. A try/except around communicate() that group-kills on cancel does NOT cover this window, because the caller never got a Process. Fix pattern: run the spawn as its own task, `await asyncio.shield(spawn)`, and on BaseException wait the spawn out (asyncio.wait, absorbing further cancels), group-kill whatever it produced, then re-raise the original exception. To reproduce deterministically in a test: yield with sleep(0) until the child appears in /proc (ppid == os.getpid()), then block the loop thread synchronously before cancel(). Do not count yields: the count changes once the spawn becomes a task.

entry_text: When re-planning a reify task branch that already carries committed work, the orchestrator may have rebased it since its last verify, so the verify-passed tip SHA in runs.db (`workflow_verify` event `tip_sha`) no longer matches HEAD. To check that the content is still the verified diff, compare `git patch-id --stable` of `git diff $(git merge-base <old_tip> main) <old_tip>` against `git diff main HEAD`: identical ids mean the same diff. That is still not "verify passed on this exact tip", so plan with all steps pre-satisfied via mark_step_committed instead of calling report_ready_to_merge.
target_text: When a re-dispatched reify architect finds a task branch already carrying the full committed implementation, check whether the branch was REBASED into the current warm lane before considering report_ready_to_merge. Tell-tale: the escalation history names pre-rebase SHAs that no longer resolve, and `.task-meta/<lane>/verdicts/` and `reviews/` are empty while `.task/plan.json` is a dangling symlink. A rebase produces a new tree, so verify/review have NOT passed on that tip — report_ready_to_merge does not apply. Author the full plan and pre-satisfy each step with mark_step_committed instead.

entry_text: Reify compiler: when you add or widen a builtin classification family slice (e.g. in orientation_signatures.rs / units.rs), you must also do three things in crates/reify-compiler/src/unresolved_function.rs. Add the slice to the `is_known_builtin` union. Add it to the test module's `ALL_FAMILY_SLICES` table. Remove its names from `EVAL_DEFERRED_BUILTIN_NAMES`. Otherwise the name is silently double-owned (family + "unclaimed" manifest), and `eval_deferred_names_are_disjoint_from_every_registered_family` cannot detect it. Task #6082's ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES missed this; task 6306 fixes it.
target_text: Euler builtin name-family ownership in crates/reify-compiler/src/orientation_signatures.rs is SPLIT, ruled by the steward on esc-6082-8 (2026-09-20). `orient_euler` (the CONSTRUCTOR) belongs to task #5344's ORIENTATION_TYPED_FN_NAMES, which landed on main and already maps it to Type::Orientation(3) in its section-(1) producer arm. `orient_to_euler` (the DECOMPOSER) belongs to task #6082's narrower Euler family, and is unclaimed ground precisely because #5344's own test `is_orientation_typed_fn_rejects_the_four_decomposers` explicitly disclaims the four decomposers (orient_log, orient_to_euler, orient_to_axis_angle, transform_log). Task #6082's branch originally scoped ORIENTATION_EULER_FN_NAMES to BOTH names, which overlaps #5344 and breaks the units.rs family-disjointness invariants in both directions plus duplicates the expr.rs ladder arm; the ruling is to drop `orient_euler` from #6082's family and keep only `orient_to_euler`. Nothing is lost by that narrowing. GENERAL NORM this instantiates: these result-type name families must stay mutually disjoint (units.rs enforces it with forward + reciprocal tests), so a task adding a new family must first check which names main's existing families already claim — and a family that types RETURN values (orientation_signatures.rs) is a different seam from the one that types ARGUMENT slots (builtin_signatures.rs ExpectedArg), so claiming a name in one does not claim it in the other.

target_text:
GOTCHA (dark-factory, measured task 3659, 2026-09-14): renaming a markdown heading that BriefingAssembler renders silently degrades scripts/legibility/digest.py's harness-turn classifier, and nothing reports it.

MECHANISM. `is_harness_injected_turn` lowercases the turn, splits it into a SET OF STRIPPED LINES, and tests `heading in lines` — whole-line equality, not substring or prefix. So HARNESS_BRIEFING_SUBHEADINGS' '## conventions' does NOT match a rendered '## Conventions & Gotchas'. A briefing turn needs one anchor plus one corroborator (>=2 total) to be filtered out of the digest's "gold" User Corrections section; lose the corroborator and a machine-generated briefing is presented to a human as gold human input — the exact fabrication class the 07-31 confusion census (cluster 1.1(b)) found.

WHAT TO DO when you rename or retire a briefing heading: ADD the new spelling to HARNESS_BRIEFING_SUBHEADINGS and KEEP the old one. The filter reads ARCHIVED transcripts, so the retired spelling is still live data — pruning it un-classifies every historical briefing turn. Task 3659 added '## conventions & gotchas' beside the pre-3659 '## project context' / '## conventions' / '## recent decisions'.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS: digest.py lives under scripts/, is not imported by the orchestrator, and its tests (scripts/tests/test_legibility_digest.py, run via `uv run --project shared pytest scripts/tests/`) stay green on the rename because they exercise the constant's own literals rather than briefing.py's output. There is no cross-file drift guard; the coupling is prose-only. Grep scripts/legibility/digest.py for the heading literal whenever you touch a rendered '## ' heading in orchestrator/src/orchestrator/agents/briefing.py.

entry_text: dark-factory fused-memory GOTCHA (measured, task 6137 planning): never put best-effort post-write work (for example an LLM judge) inline in MemoryService._execute_graphiti_write or in a durable-queue callback. DurableWriteQueue._process_item runs _execute_write under asyncio.wait_for(write_timeout), so a slow step can time out a write that has ALREADY landed and RETRY it, minting a duplicate episode. A callback that raises also retries the item, and it holds the queue semaphore while it runs. Use a tracked background task (the task_interceptor._background_tasks idiom) submitted after the identity-lock block. Also note: result.edges from add_episode is stale after the lock, because _dedup_episode_edges deletes duplicates inside it. Re-read survivors from the graph if they matter.
target_text: Convention established/reused by task 2073: post-write cleanup sweeps in MemoryService._execute_graphiti_write (fused-memory/src/fused_memory/services/memory_service.py) follow a fixed template — guard None/empty result the same way as _dedup_episode_edges (getattr(result, 'nodes'/'edges', None) or []; return 0 if empty), and make each remediation call best-effort by wrapping in try/except that re-raises (asyncio.CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) but logs+continues on any other Exception (logger.exception with a "will retry on next episode" message), tallying success vs failed counts. This mirrors _restore_superseded_dependency_edges exactly. Any new post-write sweep added to _execute_graphiti_write should follow this same shape rather than inventing new error-handling conventions.

entry_text: Reify overload ladder gotcha: reify-expr's eval-side `find_matching_compiled_function` checks tier 1 (exact) UNSCREENED — it returns the first exact match immediately, before the head/wildcard tiers. The compile-side `resolve_function_overload`, by contrast, filters exact over the tier-3 survivors. So any widening of tier 1 must be made in BOTH resolvers, and must stay a subset of `reify_core::overload::slot_matches_wildcard_tier`; otherwise compile time and eval time pick different overloads (the esc-4231/esc-4093 drift class).
target_text: reify-expr's eval-side overload resolver `find_matching_compiled_function` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs) MUST mirror the compile-side `resolve_function_overload` in reify-compiler/src/type_compat.rs. reify-expr cannot import reify-compiler (dev-dep only), so it keeps VERBATIM local mirrors of two predicates: `type_carries_type_param` (wildcard for GENERIC fns only, gated on !type_params.is_empty()) AND `type_carries_trait_object` (wildcard for ALL fns regardless of genericity). If a param's trait-object wildcard is handled on only one side, a call like `solve_elastic_static(loads: List<Load>, supports: List<Support>)` resolves at compile time but the eval-side resolver returns None, so the @optimized ComputeNode dispatch never fires ("found targets: []"). This is the esc-4093-152 divergence class (sibling of esc-4231-120/126 for type-params). Keep both mirrors in sync.

entry_text: Bare gateway ids such as `gw0 gw2 gw3` as keys in pytest's lastfailed cache do NOT mean mass worker loss. They are minted by `xdist/scheduler/loadscope.py::LoadScopeScheduling._check_nodes_have_same_collection` (siblings in load.py and worksteal.py) when a worker's collected test list differs from the first worker's. The session then aborts with 'Different tests were collected between gwA and gwB'. No later report ever passes a gwN nodeid, so these keys persist until --cache-clear and can be days older than the other entries. Seen in task 4237's worktree (2026-09-26): 7 stale gwN keys beside the real crashed test.

How to measure account cap and auth state over time: read the orchestrator's runs.db table account_events, read-only (sqlite3 'file:/home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db?mode=ro').
- Columns: account_name, event_type, project_id, run_id, details JSON, created_at.
- Event types: cap_hit (details.reason carries 'session limit' vs 'weekly limit' and the reset time), resumed, auth_failed, auth_resumed, failover, lease_stale.
- Replay cap_hit -> resumed and auth_failed -> auth_resumed chronologically to rebuild per-account availability and compute all-capped windows.
Do NOT use journalctl for this. Grepping orchestrator-reify.service for [shared.usage_gate] over about 7 days timed out at 110 s, and the journal rotates in about 4 days. The usage_gate log strings ('All accounts capped — waiting for any to reopen', 'Account X CAPPED', 'AUTH-FAILED') are only in the journal.
Caveat: each orchestrator keeps its own gate and runs.db, so one project's table is that project's view of the shared accounts.
target_text:
To measure why orchestrator agent invocations are failing, classify by `events.invocation_end` -> `json_extract(data,'$.subtype')` in the project's OWN runs.db (reify: /home/leo/src/reify/data/orchestrator/runs.db; dark-factory's is a separate DB holding only project_id='dark_factory'). Subtypes seen: success, error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_timeout_killed_with_progress, error_empty_output. This is the only trustworthy discriminator.

THREE SIGNALS THAT LOOK RIGHT AND ARE NOT:
1. The journal's `turns=N` in "Task X [role]: success=... cost=$... turns=N" is UNRELIABLE — budget-killed runs report turns=1-2 alongside transcript_turns of 48-84, and SUCCESSES report turns above the cap (e.g. 47 against a 45 cap). The counter is per-segment for resumed sessions and cumulative elsewhere. An escalation that reasons "turns=1 at $5.11 rules out a turn cap" is reading this field. Never infer a cap from it.
2. `invocations.capped` is a DEAD COLUMN — 0 on all ~36,000 rows. It does not mark ceiling hits.
3. The systemd journal rotates fast (~4 days retained for orchestrator-reify.service), so it cannot support a 30-day window. Use runs.db.

Cost percentiles must be computed over SUCCESSES ONLY, and remember the max is CENSORED BY THE CAP — "max $9.99 against a $10 ceiling" means demand above $10 exists and is invisible, not that $10 is ample. Pair every percentile with the count of error_max_budget_usd / error_max_turns rows.

The `invocations` table (cost_usd, duration_ms, task_id, role, completed_at) is the right join for per-task spend; `events` is the right source for subtype and for routing_decision ceilings. Read-only via sqlite3 'file:<path>?mode=ro' — the orchestrator is live and counts drift by 1-2 between queries.

On a 9638-DOF P1 column (100×20×10 mm, 1 kN, sigma 0) `target/debug/reify eval` took 7.5 s at n_modes=1, 8.7 s at 2, 6.2 s at 3, 4.7 s at 4, 0.9–1.6 s at 6 and 21 s at 12. Measure before choosing n_modes for a gate-resident buckling test or fixture; do not assume fewer modes is faster.
target_text: Verified 2026-09-29 (reify esc-7260-4): shift-invert Lanczos in crates/reify-solver-elastic/src/eigensolve.rs feeds CompositeShiftInvertOp = (K - sigma*B)^-1 B to faer partial_self_adjoint_eigen, which assumes the Euclidean inner product; that is invalid whenever B is not a multiple of the identity (buckling B = -K_g, modal B = M), and `converged` only means n_modes values were returned (no residual check). Main already takes this path at sigma=0 above n = max(64, 2*n_modes), so buckling modes 2+ and modal-with-mass eigenvalues can be silently wrong (136-DOF column: lambda2 6.143e-2 vs dense 5.373e-2; lambda1 correct). The operator is self-adjoint in the K inner product for every sigma, so Cholesky symmetrisation L^T (K-sigma B)^-1 B L^-T keeps faer's Lanczos (consistent with the PRD's 'convergence diagnostic, NOT a Krylov rewrite' ruling). Owner: #7602.

entry_text: FalkorDB planner gotcha, cosine leg (measured 2026-10-03, task 6238, after γ/task 3708 provisioned per-property indices). graphiti_core edge_similarity_search's `MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO]->(m:Entity) WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH DISTINCT e,n,m, cos AS score ...` plans as Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan [e] on the RELATES_TO.group_id index. That is one index scan per Entity node: 825 ms on dark_factory (21.7k edges) and a 1000 ms 'Query timed out' on reify (26.8k edges). Edge-first with late endpoint binding avoids it: `MATCH ()-[e:RELATES_TO]->() WHERE e.group_id IN $g WITH e, cos AS score WHERE score > $min WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m WHERE n:Entity AND m:Entity ...`. It ran in 52-60 ms on dark_factory and 92-108 ms on reify. Node cosine (Node By Index Scan) was fine at 85-135 ms. Rule: in GRAPH.EXPLAIN, any *Scan operator that has children is re-executed per row.
target_text: FalkorDB planner gotcha (measured 2026-10-03, task 3711, dark_factory + reify after task 3708 provisioned indices): `CALL db.idx.fulltext.queryRelationships('RELATES_TO', $q) YIELD relationship AS rel, score MATCH (n:Entity)-[e:RELATES_TO {uuid: rel.uuid}]->(m:Entity) ...` (graphiti_core edge_fulltext_search's FalkorDB join) plans as ProcedureCall -> Node By Label Scan (n:Entity) -> Edge By Index Scan, i.e. a full Entity label scan PER yielded row, and hits the 1000 ms read TIMEOUT ('Query timed out') whenever the fulltext call yields >=1 row; the bare fulltext call takes ~1 ms. Binding the yielded relationship directly (`YIELD relationship AS e, score WITH e, score, startNode(e) AS n, endNode(e) AS m`) ran in 6.5 ms. Check GRAPH.EXPLAIN before trusting any `{uuid: x.uuid}` re-match after a YIELD.

entry_text: Reify compiler gotcha (measured 2026-10-01, main 15634a417f): inside a trait INSTANCE assoc-fn body, every `self.member` / bare member read types as dimensionless Real, regardless of the member's declared type. Cause: crates/reify-compiler/src/functions.rs compile_assoc_function builds its body scope without set_template_registry, so expr.rs member_access_on_structure_like hits its registry-miss permissive fallback for the StructureRef(conformer) receiver. E.g. `fn lateral_area(self) -> Scalar<Area> { pi * diameter * length }` compiles its body to Real. Any static check on assoc-fn body types (comparison guards, body-vs-return reconciliation) will false-positive or false-negative there. Tracked as #8118; sibling #7855 is the same erase-to-Real class for trait-typed fn params.
target_text: Reify `.ri` free-fn substrate gotcha (verified 2026-06-15 with target/debug/reify): a free `fn` that reads a member off a TRAIT-typed parameter loses dimension — e.g. `fn f(c: GeometricTolerance) { c.tolerance_value }` yields a dimensionless `Real`, so adding it to a `Length` fails with "dimension mismatch in addition: Scalar[m] vs Real". Reading the same member off a CONCRETE struct/trait-impl param (e.g. `c: Position`) preserves the declared type, and reading a DERIVED-LET member (e.g. `size.upper_limit` where size: DimensionalTolerance) off a struct fn-param materializes correctly. Workaround for generic stdlib fns: take the value as a plain `Length` param and have the caller pass `instance.member` at the call site (reading off a concrete instance preserves dimension). Also: `.ri` fns do NOT support if/match (ports_mechanical.ri:61) — fn bodies must be straight-line expressions.

entry_text:
Which fused-memory writers can hit a memory_metadata.enforce rejection, and what happens to it (traced 2026-10-02):
- Deterministic code writers set only constant keys, so they cannot produce a fatal violation. This covers the recon harness markers, scope-freshness snapshots, stall and flag markers, the cycle-summary mirror, the standing-decision and flag-suppression Mem0 mirrors (which swallow failures at DEBUG), the override audit write and the orchestrator workflow memory writes.
- add_episode extraction bypasses the vocabulary seam completely. _execute_mem0_classify_and_add calls mem0.add directly.
- Every replay path also bypasses the seam: replay_dead_letters → _execute_mem0_write, recover_mem0_intents, replay_to_graphiti. So a fatal-invalid row that was already queued would land unvalidated on replay.
- The real exposure is LLM-authored metadata: recon stages, which run as claude CLI subprocesses over MCP, plus task roles, stewards, curator sittings and interactive sessions. Each sees the rejection as a tool result on the same call. Nothing makes it retry, and if it doesn't, the memory is gone with no durable record.
- consolidate_memories already hard-rejects a malformed topic slug whatever enforce says (server/consolidation.py::validate_consolidate_args).
- Latent silent-loss path: shared/mcp_post.py::check_mcp_post_response, the orchestrator's raw MCP POST checker, inspects only the HTTP status and the JSON-RPC error member. A tool-level {'error','error_type'} dict inside a successful JSON-RPC result reads as success. Today's orchestrator payloads cannot trip enforce, but any future fatal key would be lost without an orchestrator-side log.
- sweep_toolcall_xml_leak deletes a record before re-adding it, so under enforce a rejected re-add loses the original (the script reports it as content-lost).
target_text:
How fused-memory rejects a memory write when memory_metadata.enforce=true (verified in code 2026-10-02, for Task 3626):
- Shape of the response. All three write tools (add_memory, add_system_record, update_memory) are wrapped by server/tool_errors.py::mcp_tool_errors. It catches the exception and RETURNS {'error': str(e), 'error_type': type(e).__name__}: a success-shaped dict, not a raised MCP error.
- What the message says. For invalid_topic_slug it names the offending value and the raw regex '^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\Z' plus the 100-char cap. All fatal violations are joined into one message, so one retry can fix all of them. It suggests no fix, and never says kebab-case or mentions dots.
- What is kept. Nothing. The seam runs before every journal, WAL, mem0 intent and durable-queue write, so the caller's context is the only copy.
- What the operator sees.
  - The memory_metadata.schema_warning census line is byte-identical in warn and enforce modes; only the extra '<op> error:' ERROR traceback marks a refusal.
  - A canonical_uniqueness_violation under enforce raises BEFORE _census, so it leaves no census line at all.
  - A Qdrant timeout during the canonical-uniqueness probe surfaces as a bare TimeoutError envelope.
  - There is no storm escape for fatal rejections; UnknownKeyStormDetector only sees unknown_key.
- Contrast. The near-duplicate and topic-cluster guards return a `hint` key carrying the exact retry recipe and the allow_near_duplicate override; metadata rejections have no equivalent.

entry_text: Reify gotcha for type-arg bound checks: on the generic-fn call path, T is inferred by `unify` against compiled result_types, and geometry ctors lie — `box(..)`/`sphere(..)` bind T to `Real` and `point3(..)` to `Point3<Scalar[m]>` (measured 2026-09-30 by forcing E_FN_TYPE_ARG_CONFLICT with `fn two<T>(a: T, b: T)` + `two(box(..), true)`). Since stdlib geometry marker traits (Solid/Geometry/Transformable) are meant to be satisfied by geometry values, never reject an INFERRED builtin binding against a trait bound; only WRITTEN type args (`Housing<Bool>()`, `S : Box<Bool>`, `param c : Housing<Bool>`) are trustworthy. Also `Solid`/`Geometry`/`DatumRef` written as type names resolve to `Type::Geometry`.
target_text: Reify compiler gotcha (verified task 4584): geometry constructors (box/cylinder/sweep/etc., see is_geometry_function in crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs:67) compile to a Type::dimensionless_scalar() PLACEHOLDER, not Type::Geometry. Since GHR-γ, `param body : Solid = box(...)` produces a Param ValueCellDecl whose default_expr.result_type is that scalar placeholder. So any type-only compatibility check against a Type::Geometry param (e.g. type_compatible(Geometry, default.result_type)) FALSELY rejects legitimate geometry defaults. Must gate on is_geometry_function(call_name) || Type::Geometry instead.

entry_text: Gotcha for any PRD cite-vs-status checker: even after its SHIPPED re-stamp (edd9703fae), docs/prds/kernel-seam-contracts.md still contains "Adopt existing task **#4876** (`deferred`, high)" in its frozen AS-AUTHORED §9 body, and it must not be edited. A checker that does not skip PRDs whose Status header is terminal (SHIPPED/SUPERSEDED/WITHDRAWN) therefore fires on the very doc the task requires to be silent. Capability manifests (*.capability-manifest.md) are decompose-time gate artifacts whose status words are author-time evidence, and they carried 27 of 46 raw cite-status contradictions in a 2026-09-30 survey.
target_text: Reify PRD Status-header vocabulary is ambiguous and has caused real staleness defects in both directions: "landed" was deliberately clarified in match-block-decls.md (commit e45f5419fb) to mean "the PRD DOCUMENT landed, not the feature shipped", while a stale "Status: deferred" left on a fully-shipped PRD misled readers the other way (task 6042 swept three such headers in docs/prds/v0_6/). Convention now applied: use an unambiguous state word - "SHIPPED (v0.6)" - cite the terminal-done leaf task IDs and a runnable examples/*.ri anchor, and reserve "landed" for tasks/branches where it unambiguously means merged. When flipping such a header, ALSO sweep the body for section-4/5/6 "substrate does not exist" claims and section-8 "not yet filed" headings, or the document contradicts itself within a few sections.

This amends memory a8ae43ad (which predates task #6435 and says only "pin it deliberately"): since #6435 the PG-DRIFT-GUI scenario in tests/infra/test_verify_scope.sh sed-derives every prd-gate path out of the EXPECTED_CLEAN array and asserts each one classifies RUN_GUI=1, which requires its LEAF NAME to also appear in scripts/verify.sh's _GUI_COUPLED_RI_FIXTURES. Always cite fixtures by full leaf name — a letter after the slash does not match. entry_text: Reify unit-literal scope gotcha (measured 2026-10-04, HEAD 92a94f7545): a TOP-LEVEL user `fn` body or fn-param default has NO unit registry, so the compound literal `300mm/s` errors ("compound unit expression requires a unit registry in scope") and only reify_core::units::BUILTIN_UNITS resolve there (mm cm m in deg rad kg g s K A mol cd); `200GPa`, `1N` and `5um` are "unknown unit". Compose from built-ins instead: `fn speed() -> Velocity { 300.0 * 1mm / 1s }`. Structure members (param, let, ctor args, sub blocks) and constraint defs DO have the registry, so `300mm/s` and `200GPa` work there.
target_text: Reify gotcha: stdlib fn bodies and the bootstrap scope resolve unit literals against an UNSEEDED UnitRegistry, falling through to the hardcoded `unit_to_scalar` table in crates/reify-compiler/src/units.rs via `registry.lookup(...).or_else(|| unit_to_scalar(...))` (expr.rs:770-773). So ANY unit needed inside a stdlib/bootstrap fn body MUST be in that hardcoded table (post task 4173: {mm,cm,m,in,deg,rad,kg,g,s,K,A,mol,cd}), NOT merely in si_units.rs SI_PREFIX_BASES (which emit registry-only prefixed variants invisible in that scope). This is why task α (4173) added bare A/mol/cd as factor-1.0 fallback arms, unblocking γ's electrical/molar constant bodies; the same constraint explains the deferred 'um' unrecognized-unit issue.

entry_text: Gotcha for source-scanning gates in reify-gui: the INV-GUI-2 gate's hand-rolled FnIndex (gui/src-tauri/src/tests/debug_write_tool_routing_tests.rs) ends a fn at the first column-0 `}`, which is sound only for top-level fns such as debug_server.rs's. Applied to engine.rs, every `impl EngineSession` method's span would run to the impl's end and attribute calls to the wrong fn. For per-method attribution use syn (syn 2.0.117 and proc-macro2 1.0.106 are already in Cargo.lock, so it works offline as a reify-gui dev-dep); reify-gui has no syn dependency of its own before task 5101.

EXTENDS the existing entry "Any grep/architecture test over gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs MUST strip comments before matching" (Mem0 230358ce): stripping comments is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — string LITERAL contents are a second false-GREEN path, and it was found live in task #5100's INV-GUI-2 gate (gui/src-tauri/src/tests/debug_write_tool_routing_tests.rs) after that gate had already landed its comment-stripping step. Reproduced, not reasoned about: a handler body of `run_on_engine(...)` plus `tracing::debug!("bypassing write_on_engine_and_refresh_baseline for speed")` — a real bypass — satisfied the routing check and the gate went green; symmetrically a compliant handler mentioning `.emit(` in a log string false-RED. A tracing span name, an error message, or a `json!` field naming the seam while the call is being removed is an ordinary agent edit, not a contrived one.

THE FIX IS TWO VIEWS OF THE SAME BYTES, NOT ONE WIDER STRIP, and that is the non-obvious part. A gate of this shape usually has two consumer families needing OPPOSITE things: the tool/name ENUMERATIONS read identifiers OUT of string literals (`"reify_export" =>` dispatch arms, `name: "reify_export"` registry rows), while the BEHAVIOURAL checks (does this fn call the seam / does it emit) must not see literal contents at all. One stripped view cannot serve both. Blanking must be equal-LENGTH (replace each stripped char with spaces, keep newlines) so a byte offset means the same thing in either view and fn-body slices found in one line up in the other.

This matches the design reify's awk-based gates already use (Mem0 1b0e5c7f: `_AWK_PRODUCTION_PROLOGUE` blanks string/char/raw-string CONTENTS while keeping delimiters), and crates/reify-builtins/tests/common/seed_name_scan.rs already handled literals correctly — so the hole existed only because each gate hand-rolls its own scanner. Before writing a new Rust source-scanning gate, port an existing literal-aware scanner rather than re-deriving one; the shared-primitive extraction is filed as a follow-up from #5100 (ticket tkt_0RTQ6NPHP5KR44Q1ZSJ64B5PRC).

target_text: jcodemunch identity-mode config gotcha, verified against the installed 1.108.55 on 2026-08-22 (task 4562). To force per-worktree `local/<basename>-<sha1[:8]>` index identity instead of the shared `<owner>/<repo>` one, the ONLY working levers are env `JCODEMUNCH_GIT_ROOT_IDENTITY=0` or config.jsonc `"git_root_identity": false`. `"identity_mode": "local"` is a TRAP: the shipped config template advertises it (config.py:1872/1893) but the key is absent from `CONFIG_TYPES`, so it is discarded SILENTLY and the fix looks applied while doing nothing — `CONFIG_TYPES` membership is what gates whether a key survives at all. Two further traps: (1) `git_root_identity` defaults to True (config.py:384) and `load_config()` seeds `_GLOBAL_CONFIG` from `deepcopy(DEFAULTS)`, so a `False` default at a `_config.get()` call site never applies; (2) the env-var fallback is SKIPPED for any key explicitly set in `~/.code-index/config.jsonc`, so a host-config edit can silently shadow an env-var fix with no test going red. Env-var value parsing is `value.lower() in ("true","1","yes","on")`, so `'0'` means lever ON and `'1'` means OFF — pin the literal in tests. The env var is deprecated upstream ("removed in v2.0"), so a pin bump past v2.0 must re-establish it. Source locator has MOVED since the 2026-06-11 forensics note's uv-cache path: read `~/.local/share/uv/tools/jcodemunch-mcp/lib/python3.13/site-packages/jcodemunch_mcp/` (config.py, storage/git_root.py) for the installed pin.

target_text:
Procedure that worked, 2026-10-02: landing a docs-only PRD commit into a busy merge lane via a solo merge carrier (task 6180).

Situation: two verifies were in flight and 3995 and 4237 were real queued entries, as confirmed by per-id marker search.

Steps:
1. Commit in a scratch worktree, so the main checkout is never dirtied. Pre-commit ran clean.
2. File the carrier with submit_task(planning_mode=True), carrying a temporary dependency on a pending task (3136) so the scheduler cannot dispatch it while pending.
3. Run `git worktree move` to .worktrees/<id> and `checkout -b task/<id>`, keeping the original branch as a backup ref.
4. Walk the status pending → in-progress (claimant_run_id interactive-carrier-<id>) → merge-deferred in back-to-back calls. Interactive in-progress claims get their worktree reaped within ~20 min.
5. Remove the temporary dependency.
6. merge_request(wait_secs=100, verified_green=False).

Result:
- It entered at position 1 (the docs-only footprint was disjoint) and went straight to verifying.
- It landed with a normal 'Merge task/6180 into main' marker, b3b4415805.
- The lane did NOT flip the solo carrier to done; it was stamped done by hand with kind 'merged'.
- A background `until git cat-file -e main:<path>` watcher was a cheap landing signal.

So an awaited scheduler.handle_blast_radius_expansion / update_task raises TypeError in TestSubmitToMergeQueuePlanTightening's accepted-narrow tests. target_text: Extending the pyright/Mock cross-function-narrowing gotcha (see existing entries on test_scheduler.py and test_harness_service_restart.py): when the AsyncMock is assigned onto a typed attribute (e.g. TaskWorkflow.scheduler: SchedulerFacade) inside a shared test helper function like _make_workflow(), rebinding locally in the test body doesn't work as a fix — the assertion needs to inspect calls that already happened via the helper-constructed instance, so reassigning a fresh AsyncMock right before the assert would wipe the recorded call history. entry_text: In reify-compiler, every operand in a boolean geometry position (union/difference/... args) is ALSO value-compiled before realization lowering: a top-level geometry let / geometry-list let / geometry param emits a value cell via compile_expr_with_expected over its whole initializer (entity.rs geometry-let arm, task #4954), which runs before the realization-emission third pass. So unknown-member / priv-member / collection-sub value-level diagnostics for a boolean operand are already emitted once; a geometry-position consumer that also renders MemberPathError::to_diagnostic double-reports (measured task 5425 with `reify check`).
target_text:
Reify compiler: sibling-let geometry references are NOT uniformly recoverable from RealizationDecl.operations. The #4668 sibling pre-check (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry.rs:1374-1385) emits GeomRef::Sub(name) ONLY on the Modify/Transform/Pattern/Sweep/Isosurface argument path. Boolean ops early-return before it (geometry.rs:1290-1308) into resolve_boolean_arg (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_boolean.rs:28-107), which only pre-checks the cross-sub `self.<sub>.<member>` shape and otherwise INLINES the operand's initializer, referring to it as GeomRef::Step(n). So for `param geometry : Solid = difference(body, holes)` the names "body"/"holes" appear nowhere in the template's operations. This inlining is deliberate and PINNED by crates/reify-compiler/tests/harness_langcore/let_scope_tests.rs:552-603, so "make Booleans emit GeomRef::Sub" is a cross-crate behaviour change, not a local fix. Consequence: reify_eval::deps::extract_realization_edges (crates/reify-eval/src/deps.rs:691-744) gates every arm on GeomRef::Sub and therefore registers NO edge for sibling Boolean operands — it is NOT a valid oracle for "is this realization consumed downstream".

Correct data source for geometry consumption edges: the value-cell layer. Since #4954 every geometry binding emits a ValueCellDecl alongside its realization, and its `default_expr` holds the un-inlined ValueRef(ValueCellId) operands. Walk it with the existing exhaustive reify_ir::CompiledExpr::collect_value_refs (crates/reify-ir/src/expr.rs:1008) — the repo's dependency-tracking walk; it covers every nesting variant and treats CrossSubGeometryRef as a ValueRef leaf, so no hand-rolled partial walk is needed. CRITICAL filter: only cells whose cell_type == Type::Geometry count as consumers. A `: Rigid` structure auto-derives mass/centroid/moment_of_inertia lets that all reference `geometry` but are Scalar/Point3/Tensor-typed; counting them marks the TERMINAL realization as consumed and hides the finished part. Established while resolving esc-5195-1 (task #5195, default-visibility of intermediate geometry).

entry_text: Convention (task 5158): a committed bash wrapper that runs `uv` must not hardcode a path or trust PATH. It sources scripts/lib/resolve_uv.sh, the single copy of the UV_BIN -> PATH -> $HOME/.local/bin -> /usr/local/bin ladder. Locate the lib relative to the script itself with the fork-free idiom `case "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" in */*) d="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}";; *) d=.;; esac`, never `$(dirname ...)` (unfindable under an empty PATH) or $REPO (tests point it at a fake dir, cgl hardcodes main). Use a guarded `source "$lib" || { echo "${0##*/}: ERROR: ..." >&2; exit 127; }`, then `X="$(require_uv_bin)" || exit $?` AFTER the .env source. scripts/tests/test_resolve_uv_lib.py::test_only_the_lib_defines_the_resolver fails if any other tracked .sh defines resolve_uv_bin/require_uv_bin, and its CALLERS tuple is where a new wrapper gets wiring coverage.

Adding the row would have made verify.sh assert a coupling that does not exist AND falsified the branch's own sentence one paragraph below; it would also have pulled scripts/verify.sh into the diff, which verify-pipeline-guard.sh classifies as never-trivially-config-only. The fix that landed (commit e34e0d9e01) spells the fixture's DIRECTORY and FILENAME separately in the prose so the joined path never appears in a tracked *.rs. Rule of thumb: extend the allowlist when a test genuinely READS the fixture; reword when prose merely NAMES it. Note PG-DRIFT half (a) has no escape marker today, unlike its sibling PG-DRIFT-DIR's reviewed `pg-drift-dir:allow` — a matching `pg-drift:allow` would let prose name a genuinely-uncoupled fixture by its real path.
